books.name: Genesis
chapters: In the beginning 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE) created the Shamaym and the Arath.
And the Arath (earth) was without a form, and it was void (a completely empty space); and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Ruach of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH moved upon the face of the waters.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, Let there be light: and there was light.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH saw the light, that it was tub (good): and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH divided the light from the darkness.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH called the light Yum (Day), and the darkness He called Laylah (Night). And the evening and the morning were the first Yum (day).
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH called the firmament Shamaym. And the evening and the morning were the second Yum (day).
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, Let the waters under the Shamaym be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH called the dry land Arath; and the gathering together of the waters called Yam (Seas): and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH saw that it was good.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, Let the Arath (earth) bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the Arath: and it was so.
And the Arath (earth) brought forth grass, and herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, Whose seed was in itself, after his kind: and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH saw that it was good.
And the evening and the morning were the third Yum (day).
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, Let there be lights in the firmament of the Shamaym to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:
And let them be for lights in the firmament of the Shamaym to give light upon the Arath (earth): and it was so.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH made two great lights; the greater light to rule the Yum (day), and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH set them in the firmament of the Shamaym to give light upon the Arath,
And to rule over the Yum (day) and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH saw that it was good.
And the evening and the morning were the fourth Yum.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the Arath (earth) in the open firmament of Shamaym.

And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind: and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH saw that it was good.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Baraked them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the yam (seas), and let fowl multiply in the Arath (earth).
And the evening and the morning were the fifth Yum (day).
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, Let the Arath bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the Arath after his kind: and it was so.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH made the beast of the Arath after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the Arath after his kind: and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH saw that it was good.

And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, Let us make man in our image and our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the yam (sea), and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the Arath, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the Arath.
So 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH created man in HIS own image, in the image of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH created he him; male and female 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH created.

And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Baraked them, and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the Arath (earth), and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the yam (sea), and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the Arath.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “I give you every seed-bearing plant on the face of the whole Arath and every tree that has fruit with seed in it. They will be yours for food.
And to every beast of the Arath, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the Arath, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for food: and it was so.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH saw every thing that he had made, and behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth Yum (day).
Thus the Shamaym and the Arath, and everything in the Arath were finished.
And on the seventh Yum (day), 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE) ended HIS work which He had done, and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH rested on the seventh Yum from all His work which HE had done.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Baraked the seventh Yum (day) and Qadash it (Set it Apart), because in it 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH rested from all HIS work which HE had created and made.
This is the history of the Shamaym and the Arath when they were created, in the Yum (day) that YAHUAH ALUAH made the Arath and the Shamaym,
before any plant of the field was in the Arath and before any herb of the field had grown. For 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had not caused it to rain on the Arath, and there was no man to till the ground;
But a mist went up from the Arath and watered the whole face of the ground.
And YAHUAH ALUAH formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being.
YAHUAH ALUAH planted a garden eastward in Adan (Eden), and there YAHUAH put the man whom HE had formed.

And out of the ground 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH made every tree grow that is pleasant to the sight and Tub (good) for food. The tree of life was also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of Tub (good) and Ra (evil).
Now a river went out of Àdan (Eden) to water the garden, and from there it parted and became four riverheads.
The name of the first is Pyshun; it is the one which skirts the whole land of Habilah, where there is gold.
And the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and the onyx stone are there.
The name of the second river is Gyhun; it is the one which goes around the whole land of Cush.
The name of the third river is Hyddakal; it is the one which goes toward the east of Assyria. The fourth river is the Euphrates.
Then YAHUAH ALUAH took the man and put him in the garden of Ádan (Eden) to tend and keep it.
And YAHUAH ALUAH commanded the man, saying, “Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat;
but of the tree of the knowledge of Tub (good) and Ra (evil) you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die.”
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “It is not good that man should be alone; I will make a helper suitable to him.”

Out of the ground YAHUAH formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. And whatever Adam called each living creature, that was its name.
So Adam gave names to all cattle, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a helper suitable to him.
Then YAHUAH ALUAH caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, and he slept; and He took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
Then the rib which YAHUAH ALUAH had taken from man, ALUAH made into a woman, and ALUAH brought her to the man.
And Adam said: “This is now bone of my bones And flesh of my flesh She shall be called Woman, Because she was taken out of Man.”
Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.
Now the serpent was more cunning than any beast of the field which YAHUAH ALUAH had made. And the serpent said to the woman, “Has ALUAH indeed said, ‘You shall not eat of every tree of the garden’?”
And the woman said to the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden;
but of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has Dabar, ‘You shall not eat it, nor shall you touch it, lest you die.’ ”
Then the serpent said to the woman, “You will not surely die.
For 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH knows that in the day you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, knowing Tub (good) and Ra (evil).”

So when the woman saw that the tree was Tub (good) for food, that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree desirable to make one wise, she took of its fruit and ate. She also gave to her husband with her, and he ate.
Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together and made themselves coverings.
And they heard the Dabar of YAHUAH ALUAH walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of YAHUAH ALUAH among the trees of the garden.
Then YAHUAH ALUAH called to Adam and said to him, “Where are you?”
So Adam said, “I heard Your voice in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked; and I hid myself.”
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree of which I commanded you that you should not eat?”
Then the man said, “The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.”
And ALUAH Dabar to the woman, “What is this you have done?” The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

Then ALUAH Dabar to the serpent: “Because you have done this, you are cursed more than all cattle, and more than every beast of the field; on your belly you shall go, and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.
And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her Seed; the woman's seed shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.”
To the woman 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your conception; in pain you shall bring forth children; Your desire shall be for your husband, and he shall rule over you.”
Then to Adam, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “Because you have heeded the voice of your wife, and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you, saying, ‘You shall not eat of it’:
Both thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you, and you shall eat the herb of the field.
In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread till you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
And Adam called his wife’s name Chayah (Eve), because she was the mother of all living.
Also for Adam and his wife YAHUAH ALUAH made tunics of skin, and clothed them.
Then YAHUAH ALUAH Dabar, “Behold, the man has become like one of Us, to know tub (good) and Ra (evil). And now, lest he put out his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever”—
Therefore YAHUAH ALUAH sent Adam out of the garden of Àdan (Eden) to till the ground from which he was taken.
So 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH drove out the man; and He placed karu (charubim) at the east of the garden of Àdan (Eden), and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.
Adam made love to his wife Chayah (Eve), and she became pregnant and gave birth to Qayn (Cain). She said, “With the help of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH I have brought forth a man.”
Later she gave birth to his brother Habal (Abel). Now Habal kept flocks, and Qayn worked the soil.
In the course of time Qayn brought some of the fruits of the soil as an offering to YAHUAH.
And Habal also brought an offering fat portions from some of the firstborn of his flock. YAHUAH looked with favor on Habal and his offering,
but on Qayn and his offering 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH did not look with favor. So Qayn was very angry, and his face was downcast.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Qayn, “Why are you angry? Why is your face downcast?
If you do what is right, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at your door; it desires to have you, but you must rule over it.”
Now Qayn said to his brother Habal, “Let’s go out to the field.” While they were in the field, Qayn attacked his brother Habal and killed Habal.
Then YAHUAH Dabar to Qayn, “Where is your brother Habal? “I don’t know,” Qayn replied to YAHUAH. “am I, my brother’s keeper?”
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “What have you done? Listen! Your brother’s blood cries out to ME from the ground.
Now you are cursed and banished from the ground, which has swallowed your brother’s blood.
When you work the ground, it will no longer yield good crops for you again. You will be a restless wanderer on the Arath (earth).”
Qayn said to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH “My punishment is more than I can bear.
Today you are driving me from the land, and I will be hidden from your presence; I will be a restless wanderer on the Arath (earth), and whoever finds me will kill me.”
But YAHUAH Dabar to him, “Not so; anyone who kills Qayn will suffer vengeance seven times over.” Then YAHUAH put a mark on Qayn so that no one who found him would kill him.
So Qayn went out from YAHUAH's presence and lived in the land of Nud, east of Adan (Eden).
Qayn made love to his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Anuch. Qayn was then building a city, and he named it after his son Anuch.
To Anuch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mahujaal, and Mahujaal was the father of Mathushaal, and Mathushaal was the father of Lamach.
Lamach married two women, one named Adah and the other Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Yabal; he was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock.
His brother’s name was Yubal; he was the father of all who play stringed instruments and pipes.
Zillah also had a son, Tubal-Qayn, who forged all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-Qayn’s sister was Naamah.
Lamach said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, listen to me; wives of Lamach, hear my words. I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for injuring me.
If Qayn is avenged seven times, then Lamach seventy-seven times.”
Adam made love to his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Shath (Seth), saying, ALUAH has granted me another child in place of Habal (Abel), since Qayn killed him.”
Shath (Seth) also had a son, and he named him Anush. At that time people began to call on the name of YAHUAH.
This is the written account of Adam’s family line. When 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH created mankind, He made them in the likeness of ALUAH, to be Aluahym.
For 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH created them male and female and baraked them. And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH named them “Mankind” when they were created.
When Adam had lived one hundred and thirty years, he had a son in his own likeness, in his own image; and he named him Shath (Seth).
After Shath was born, Adam lived eight hundred years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died.
When Shath had lived one hundred and five years, he became the father of Anush (Enosh).
After he became the father of Anush, Shath lived eight hundred and seven years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Shath lived a total of nine hundred and twelve (912) years, and then he died.
When Anush (Enosh) had lived 90 years, he became the father of Kanan.
After he became the father of Kanan, Anush (Enosh) lived 815 years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Anush lived a total of 905 years, and then he died.
When Kanan had lived 70 years, he became the father of Mahalalal.
After he became the father of Mahalalal, Kanan lived 840 years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Kanan lived a total of 910 years, and then he died.
When Mahalalal had lived 65 years, he became the father of Yarad.
After he became the father of Yarad, Mahalalal lived 830 years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Mahalalel lived a total of 895 years, and then he died.
When Yarad had lived 162 years, he became the father of Chanuk (Enoch).
After he became the father of Chanuk, Yarad lived 800 years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Jarad lived a total of 962 years, and then he died.
When Chanuk had lived 65 years, he became the father of Mathusalah.
After he became the father of Mathusalah, Chanuk walked in Amunah (faithfully) with ALUAH 300 years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Chanuk lived a total of 365 years.
Chanuk walked in Amunah (faithfully) with ALUAH; then Chanuk was no more, because ALUAH took him away.
When Mathusalah had lived 187 years, he became the father of Lamach.
After he became the father of Lamach, Mathusalah lived 782 years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Mathusalah lived a total of 969 years, and then he died.
When Lamach had lived 182 years, he had a son.
He named him Nuah and said, “He will comfort us in the labor and painful toil of our hands caused by the ground YAHUAH ALUAH has cursed.”
After Nuah was born, Lamach lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
Altogether, Lamach lived a total of 777 years, and then he died.
After Nuah was 500 years old, he became the father of Sham, Ham and Yaphath.
Now it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the Arath (earth), and daughters were born to them,
The rebellious fallen Malakym saw the daughters of men, that they were beautiful; and they took wives for themselves of all whom they chose.
And ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE) Dabar, “My RUACH shall not strive with man forever, for man is indeed flesh; yet his days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”

There were giants on the Arath (earth) in those days, and also afterward, when the rebellious fallen Malak came in to the daughters of men and they bore children to them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, men of renown.
Then YAHUAH ALUAH saw that the wickedness of man was great in the Arath (earth), and that every intent of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
And YAHUAH was sorry that HE had made man on the Arath, and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was grieved in HIS heart.
So YAHUAH Dabar, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the Arath (earth), both man and beast, creeping thing and birds of the air, for I am sorry that I have made them.”
But Nuah found Favour in the eyes of YAHUAH.
This is the genealogy of Nuah. Nuah was a just man, perfect in his generations. Nuah walked with ALUAH.
And Nuah begot three sons: Sham, Ham, and Yaphath.
The Arath (earth) also was corrupt before ALUAH, and the Arath was filled with violence.
So ALUAH looked upon the Arath (earth), and indeed it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted their way on the Arath.
And ALUAH Dabar to Nuah, “The end of all flesh has come before ME, for the Arath (earth) is filled with violence through them; and behold, I will destroy them with the Arath.
“Build a large boat from cypress wood and waterproof it with tar, inside and out. Then construct decks and stalls throughout its interior.
Make the boat 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high.
Leave an 18-inch opening below the roof all the way around the boat. Put the door on the side, and build three decks inside the boat—lower, middle, and upper.
“Look! I am about to cover the Arath (earth) with a flood that will destroy every living thing that breathes. Everything on Arath will die.
But I will establish My covenant with you; and you shall go into the Ark; you, your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives with you.
And of every living thing of all flesh you shall bring two of every sort into the ark, to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female.
Of the birds after their kind, of animals after their kind, and of every creeping thing of the Arath (earth) after its kind, two of every kind will come to you to keep them alive.
And you shall take for yourself of all food that is eaten, and you shall gather it to yourself; and it shall be food for you and for them.”
Thus Nuah did; according to all that YAHUAH ALUAH commanded him, so he did.
YAHUAH ALUAH Dabar to Nuah, “Come into the ark, you and all your household, because I have seen that you are righteous before Me in this generation.
You shall take with you seven each of every clean animal, a male and his female; two each of animals that are unclean, a male and his female;
Also seven each of birds of the air, male and female, to keep the species alive on the face of all the Arath (earth).
For after seven more days I will cause it to rain on the Arath forty days and forty nights, and I will destroy from the face of the Arath all living things that I have made.”
And Nuah did according to all that YAHUAH commanded him.
Nuah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters were on the Arath.
So Nuah, with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives, went into the ark because of the waters of the flood.
Of clean animals, of animals that are unclean, of birds, and of everything that creeps on the Arath (earth),
Two by two they went into the ark to Nuah, male and female, as 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had commanded Nuah.
And it came to pass after seven Yum (days) that the waters of the flood were on the Arath.

In the six hundredth year of Nuah’s life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, on that Yum (day) all the fountains of the great deep were broken up, and the windows of Shamaym were opened.
And the rain was on the Arath (earth) forty Yum (days) and forty nights.
On the very same Yum (day) Nuah and Nuah’s sons, Sham, Ham, and Yaphath, and Nuah’s wife and the three wives of his sons with them, entered the ark
They and every beast after its kind, all cattle after their kind, every creeping thing that creeps on the Arath after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.
And they went into the ark to Nuah, two by two, of all flesh in which is the breath of life.
So those that entered, male and female of all flesh, went in as 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had commanded him; and YAHUAH ALUAH shut Nuah in the Ark.
Now the flood was on the Arath (earth) forty days. The waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose high above the Arath (earth).
The waters prevailed and greatly increased on the Arath, and the ark moved about on the surface of the waters.
And the waters prevailed exceedingly on the Arath (earth), and all the high hills under the whole Shamaym were covered.
The waters prevailed fifteen cubits upward, and the mountains were covered.
And all flesh died that moved on the Arath: birds and cattle and beasts and every creeping thing that creeps on the Arath, and every man.
All in whose nostrils was the breath of the Ruach of life, all that was on the dry land, died.

So 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH destroyed all living things which were on the face of the ground: both man and cattle, creeping thing and bird of the air. They were destroyed from the Arath. Only Nuah and those who were with him in the ark remained alive.
And the waters prevailed on the Arath one hundred and fifty days.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH remembered Nuah, and every living thing, and all the animals that were with him in the ark. And ALUAH made a wind to pass over the Arath (earth), and the waters subsided.
The fountains of the deep and the windows of Shamaym were also stopped, and the rain from Shamaym was restrained.
And the waters receded continually from the Arath (earth). At the end of the hundred and fifty days the waters decreased.
Then the ark rested in the seventh month (7 moon cycle), the seventeenth day of the month, on the mountains of Ararat.
And the waters decreased continually until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
So it came to pass, at the end of forty days, that Nuah opened the window of the ark which he had made.
Then he sent out a raven, which kept going to and fro until the waters had dried up from the Arath.
He also sent out from himself a dove, to see if the waters had receded from the face of the ground.

But the dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, and she returned into the ark to Nuah, for the waters were on the face of the whole Arath. So Nuah put out his hand and took the dove, and drew her into the ark to himself.
And Nuah waited yet another seven days, and again he sent the dove out from the ark.
Then the dove came to him in the evening, and behold, a freshly plucked olive leaf was in her mouth; and Nuah knew that the waters had receded from the Arath.
So Nuah waited yet another seven days and sent out the dove, which did not return again to him anymore.

And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, that the waters were dried up from the Arath; and Nuah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and indeed the surface of the ground was dry.
And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the Arath (earth) was dried.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Nuah, saying,
“Go out of the ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons’ wives with you.

Bring out with you every living thing of all flesh that is with you: birds and cattle and every creeping thing that creeps on the Arath (earth), so that they may abound on the Arath, and be fruitful and multiply on the Arath.”
So Nuah went out, and his sons and his wife and his sons’ wives with him.
Every animal, every creeping thing, every bird, and whatever creeps on the Arath, according to their families, went out of the ark.
Then Nuah built an altar to YAHUAH, and took of every clean animal and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

And YAHUAH smelled a soothing aroma. Then YAHUAH Dabar in His heart, “I will never again curse the ground for man’s sake, although the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; nor will I again destroy every living thing as I have done.
“While the Arath (earth) remains, Seedtime and harvest, Cold and heat, Winter and summer, And day and night Shall not cease.”
So 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Baraked Nuah and his sons, and said to them: “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the Arath (earth).

And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be on every beast of the Arath, on every bird of the air, on all that move on the Arath (earth), and on all the fish of the Yam (sea). They are given to your hand.
Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you. I have given you all things, even as the green herbs.
But you must never eat any meat that still has the lifeblood in it.
“And I will require the blood of anyone who takes another person’s life. If a wild animal kills a person, it must die. And anyone who murders his fellow man must die.
If anyone takes a man's life, that person’s life will also be taken by a man's hands. For 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH made man in HIS own image.
And as for you, be fruitful and multiply; Bring forth abundantly in the Arath And multiply in it.”
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄 ALUAH Dabar to Nuah and to his sons with him, saying:
“Behold I establish My covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
And with every living creature that is with you: the birds, the cattle, and every beast of the Arath with you, of all that go out of the ark, every beast of the Arath.
Thus I establish My covenant with you: Never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood; never again shall there be a flood to destroy the Arath.”
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar: “This is the sign of the covenant which I make between Me and you, and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
I set My rainbow in the cloud, and it shall be for the sign of the covenant between Me and the Arath.
It shall be, when I bring a cloud over the Arath, that the rainbow shall be seen in the cloud;
And I will remember My covenant which is between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh; the waters shall never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.
The rainbow shall be in the cloud, and I will look on it to remember the everlasting covenant between 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and every living creature of all flesh that is on the Arath.”
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Nuah, “This is the sign of the covenant which I have established between Me and all flesh that's on the Arath.”
Now the sons of Nuah who went out of the ark were Sham, Ham, and Yaphath. And Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were the sons of Nuah, and from these the whole Arath was populated.
And Nuah began to be a farmer, and he planted a vineyard.
Then he drank of the wine and was drunk, and became uncovered in his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brothers outside.

But Sham and Yaphath took a garment, laid it on both their shoulders, and went backward and covered the nakedness of their father. Their faces were turned away, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.
So Nuah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done to him.
Then he said: “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants he shall be to his brethren.”
And he said: Baraked be YAHUAH, The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Sham, and may Canaan be his servant.
May 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH enlarge Yaphath, and may 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH dwell in the tents of Sham; and may Canaan be his servant.”
And Nuah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
So all the days of Nuah were nine hundred and fifty years; and he died.
This is the account of the families of Sham, Ham, and Yaphath, the three sons of Nuah. Many children were born to them after the great flood.
The descendants of Yaphath were Gamar, Magag, Madai, Yaban, Tubal, Mashach, and Tiras.
The descendants of Gamar were Ashkanaz, Riphath, and Tugarmah.
The descendants of Yaban were Alishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rudanim.
Their descendants became the seafaring peoples that spread out to various lands, each identified by its own language, clan, and national identity.
The descendants of Ham were Cush, Mitzraym, Put, and Canaan.
The descendants of Cush were Saba, Habilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabtaca. The descendants of Raamah were Shaba and Dadan.
Cush was also the ancestor of Nimrud, who was the first heroic warrior on the Arath.
Since he was the greatest hunter in the world, his name became proverbial. People would say, “This man is like Nimrud, the greatest hunter in the world.”
He built his kingdom in the land of Babylunia, with the cities of Babylun, Arach, Akkad, and Calnah.
From there he expanded his territory to Assyria, building the cities of Ninabah, Rahubuth-ir, Calah,
And Rasan (the great city located between Ninabah and Calah).
Mitzraym was the ancestor of the Ludites, Anamites, Lahabites, Naphtuhites,
Pathrusites, Casluhites, and the Caphturites, from whom the Philistines came.
Canaan’s oldest son was Sidun, the ancestor of the Sidunians. Canaan was also the ancestor of the Hittites,
Yabusites, Amyrites, Girgashites,
Hibites, Arkites, Sinites,
Arbadites, Zamarites, and Hamathites. The Canaanite clans eventually spread out,
and the territory of Canaan extended from Sidun in the north to Garar and Gaza in the south, and east as far as Sudum, Gumurrah, Admah, and Zabuiim, near Lasha.
These were the descendants of Ham, identified by clan, language, territory, and national identity.
Sons were also born to Sham, the older brother of Yaphath. Sham was the ancestor of all the descendants of Abar.
The descendants of Sham were Alam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
The descendants of Aram were Uz, Hul, Gathar, and Mash.
Arphaxad was the father of Shalah, and Shalah was the father of Abar.
Abar had two sons, the first was named Palag (which means “division”), for during his lifetime the people of the world were divided into different language groups. His brother’s name was Yuktan.
Yuktan was the ancestor of Almudad, Shalaph, Hazarmabath, Yarah,
Haduram, Uzal, Diklah,
Ubal, Abimaal, Shaba,
Uphir, Habilah, and Yubab. All these were descendants of Yuktan.
The territory they occupied extended from Masha all the way to Saphar in the eastern mountains.
These were the descendants of Sham, identified by clan, language, territory, and national identity.
These are the clans that descended from Nuah’s sons, arranged by nation according to their lines of descent. All the nations of the Arath descended from these clans after the great flood.
At one time all the people of the Arath spoke the same language and used the same words.
As the people migrated to the east, they found a plain in the land of Babylunia and settled there.
They began saying to each other, “Let’s make bricks and harden them with fire.” (In this region bricks were used instead of stone, and tar was used for mortar.)
Then they said, “Come, let’s build a great city for ourselves with a tower that reaches into the sky. This will make us famous and keep us from being scattered all over the world.”
Then YAHUAH came down to look at the city and the tower the people were building.
And YAHUAH said, the people are united, and they all speak the same language, with this, nothing they set out to do will be impossible for them!
Come, let’s go down and confuse the people with different languages. Then they won’t be able to understand each other.”
In that way, YAHUAH scattered them all over the world, and they stopped building the city.
That is why the city was called Babaal, because that is where YAHUAH confused the people with different languages. In this way YAHUAH scattered them all over the world.
This is the account of Sham’s family. Two years after the great flood, when Sham was 100 years old, he became the father of Arphaxad.
After the birth of Arphaxad, Sham lived another 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he became the father of Shalah.
After the birth of Shalah, Arphaxad lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Shalah was 30 years old, he became the father of Abar.
After the birth of Abar, Shalah lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Aber was 34 years old, he became the father of Palag.
After the birth of Palag, Abar lived another 430 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Palag was 30 years old, he became the father of Rau.
After the birth of Rau, Palag lived another 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Rau was 32 years old, he became the father of Sarug.
After the birth of Sarug, Rau lived another 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Sarug was 30 years old, he became the father of Nahur.
After the birth of Nahur, Sarug lived another 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
When Nahur was 29 years old, he became the father of Tarah.
After the birth of Tarah, Nahur lived another 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
After Tarah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahur, and Haran.
This is the account of Tarah’s family. Tarah was the father of Abram, Nahur, and Haran; and Haran was the father of Lut.
But Haran died in Ur of the Chaldaans, the land of his birth, while his father, Tarah, was still living.
Meanwhile, Abram and Nahur both married. The name of Abram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nahur’s wife was Milcah. (Milcah and her sister Iscah were daughters of Nahur’s brother Haran.)
But Sarai was unable to become pregnant and had no children.

One day Tarah took his son Abram, his daughter-in-law Sarai (his son Abram’s wife), and his grandson Lut (his son Haran’s child) and moved away from Ur of the Chaldaans. He was headed for the land of Canaan, but they stopped at Haran and settled there.
Tarah lived for two hundred and five years and died while still in Haran.
Then YAHUAH Dabar to Abram, “Leave your native country, your relatives, and your father’s family, and go to the land that I will show you.
I will make you into a great nation. I will Barak you and make you great, and you will be a Barakah to others.
I will Barak those who barak you and curse those who curse you. All the families on the Arath (earth) will be Baraked through you.”
So Abram departed as YAHUAH had instructed, and Lut went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
He took his wife, Sarai, his nephew Lut, and all his wealth his livestock and all the people he had taken into his household at Haran and headed for the land of Canaan. When they arrived in Canaan,
Abram traveled through the land as far as Shacham. There he set up camp beside the oak of Murah. At that time, the area was inhabited by Canaanites.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH appeared to Abram and Dabar to him, “I will give this land to your descendants.” And Abram built an altar there and dedicated it to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who had appeared to him.

After that, Abram traveled south and set up camp in the hill country, with Bathal to the west and Ai to the east. There he built another altar and dedicated it to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and he worshiped 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Then Abram continued traveling south by stages toward the Nagab.
At that time a severe famine struck the land of Canaan, forcing Abram to go down to Mitzrayim, where he lived as a foreigner.
As Abram was approaching the border of Mitzrayim, Abram said to his wife, Sarai, “Look, you are a very beautiful woman.
When the Mitzrayim see you, they will say, ‘This is his wife. Let’s kill him; then we can have her!’
So please tell them you are my sister. Then they will spare my life and treat me well because of their interest in you.”
And sure enough, when Abram arrived in Mitzraym, everyone noticed Sarai’s beauty.
When the palace officials saw her, they sang her praises to Pharuh, their king, and Sarai was taken into his palace.
Then Pharuh gave Abram many gifts, sheep, goats, cattle, male and female donkeys, male and female servants, and camels.
Then YAHUAH sent terrible plagues upon Pharuh and his household because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
So Pharuh summoned Abram and accused him sharply. “What have you done to me?” he demanded. “Why didn’t you tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ and allow me to take her as my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and get out of here!”
Pharauh ordered some of his men to escort them, and he sent Abram out of the country, along with his wife and all his possessions.
Abram traveled from Mitzraym, along with his wife and everyone who belonged to his household including Lut to the Nagab.
Now Abram had become quite wealthy in livestock, silver, and gold.
He journeyed by stages from the Nagab to Bathal, the place where his tent had formerly been, between Bathal and Ai,
where he had first built an altar. There Abram called on the Name of ALUAH.
Lut, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks of sheep, herds, and tents.
But the land could not support them living together, because they had so many livestock that they could not stay together.
There was strife between the herdsmen in charge of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen in charge of Lut’s livestock. Also, at that time the Canaanites and the Parizzites were living in the land.
So Abram told Lut, “Please, let’s not have strife between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen, since we are relatives.
Is the whole land not available to you? Let’s separate: If you go to the left, then I will go to the right; if you go to the right, then I will go to the left.”

Lut looked around and noticed that the whole Yurdan plain as far as Zuar was well-watered like the garden of YAHUAH or like the land of Mitzraym. (This was before YAHUAH destroyed Sudum and Gumurrah.)
So Lut chose for himself all the Yurdan plain. Then Lut traveled eastward, and they separated from each other.
So Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lut settled in the cities of the plain, setting up his tent in the vicinity of Sudum.
Now the men of Sudum were particularly evil and sinful in their defiance of YAHUAH.
After Lut had separated from Abram, YAHUAH told Abram, “Look off to the north, south, east, and west from where you’re living,
Because I’m going to give you and your descendants all of the land that you see forever!
I’ll make your descendants as plentiful as the dust of the Arath, so that if one could count the specks of dust of the Arath, then your descendants could also be counted.
Get up! Walk throughout the length and breadth of the land, because I’m going to give it to you.”
So Abram moved his tent and settled beside the oaks of Mamra that are by Habrun, where he built an altar to YAHUAH ALUAH.
And it came to pass in the days of Amraphal king of Shinar, Ariuch king of Allasar, Chadurlaumar king of Alam, and Tidal king of nations,
That they made war with Bara king of Sudum, Birsha king of Gumurrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shamamabar king of Zabuim, and the king of Bala (that is, Zuar).
All these joined together in the Valley of Siddim (that is, the Salt Sea).
Twelve years they served Chadurlaumar, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
In the fourteenth year Chadurlaumar and the kings that were with him came and attacked the Raphaim in Ashtaruth Karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, the Amim in Shaba Kiriathaim,
And the Hurites in their mountain of Sair, as far as Al Paran, which is by the wilderness.
Then they turned back and came to An Mishpat (that is, Kadash), and attacked all the country of the Amalakites, and also the Amurites who dwelt in Hazazun Tamar.
And the king of Sudum, the king of Gumurrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zabuiim, and the king of Bala (that is, Zuar) went out and joined together in battle in the Valley of Siddim
Against Chadurlaumar king of Alam, Tidal king of nations, Amraphal king of Shinar, and Ariuch king of Allasar, four kings against five.
Now the Valley of Siddim was full of asphalt pits; and the kings of Sudum and Gumurrah fled; some fell there, and the remainder fled to the mountains.
Then they took all the goods of Sudum and Gumurrah, and all their provisions, and went their way.
They also took Lut, Abram’s brother’s son who dwelt in Sudum, and his goods, and departed.
Then one who had escaped came and told Abram the Abryt (Hebrew), for he dwelt by the tarabinth trees of Mamrala the Amyrite, brother of Ashcul and brother of Anar; and they were allies with Abram.
Now when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his three hundred and eighteen trained servants who were born in his own house, and went in pursuit as far as Dan.
Abram divided his forces against them by night, and he and his servants attacked them and pursued them as far as Hubah, which is north of Damascus.
So Abram brought back all the goods, and also brought back his brother's son Lut and his goods, as well as the women and the people.
And the king of Sudum went out to meet Abram at the Valley of Shaba (that is, the King’s Valley), after his return from the defeat of Chadurlaumar and the kings who were with him.
Then Mal'kizadak king of Shalam brought out bread and wine; he was the Kuhan of AL'ALYUN (𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH the Most High).
Mal'kizadak Barak Abram and said, Barak be Abram of AL'ALYUN, Maker of Shamaym and Arath;
And Barak be AL'ALYUN, Who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” And Abram gave Mal'kizadak a tithe of all he got from rescuing Lut his brother's son.
Now the king of Sudum said to Abram, “Give me the persons, and take the goods for yourself.”
But Abram said to the king of Sudum, “I have raised my hand to AL'ALYUN, (𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Most High), the Maker of Shamaym and Arath (earth),
That I will take nothing, from a thread to a sandal strap, and that I will not take anything that is yours, lest you should say, ‘I have made Abram rich’
Except only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me: Anar, Ashcul, and Mamra; let them take their portion.”
After these things the Dabar of YAHUAH came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield and your exceedingly great reward.”
But Abram said, “𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, what will You give me, seeing I go childless, and the heir of my house is Aliazar of Damascus?”
Then Abram said, “Look, You have given me no offspring; indeed one born in my house is my heir!”
Then Dabar of YAHUAH came to Abram, saying, “This one shall not be your heir, but one who will come from your own body shall be your heir.”
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH brought Abram outside and Dabar to him, “Look now toward Shamaym , and count the stars if you are able to number them.” And ALUAH said to Abram, “So shall your descendants be.”
And Abram believed in 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and YAHUAH accounted it to Abram for righteousness.
Then YAHUAH Dabar to Abram, “I am 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who brought you out of Urh of the Chaldaans, to give you this land to inherit it.”
And Abram said, “𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, how shall I know that I will inherit it?”
So YAHUAH Dabar to Abram, “Bring ME a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”
Then Abram brought all these to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and cut them in two, down the middle, and placed each piece opposite the other; but Abram did not cut the birds in two.
And when the vultures came down on the carcasses, Abram drove them away.
Now when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and behold, horror and great darkness fell upon him.
Then YAHUAH Dabar to Abram: “Know certainly that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them, and they will afflict them four hundred years.
And also the nation whom they serve, I will judge; afterward they shall come out with great possessions.
Now as for you, you shall go to your fathers in Shalum; you shall be buried at a good old age.
But in the fourth generation they shall return here, for the iniquity of the Amurites is not yet complete.”
And it came to pass, when the sun went down and it was dark, that behold, there appeared a smoking oven and a burning torch that passed between those pieces.
On the same day YAHUAH made a covenant with Abram, saying: To your descendants I have given this land, from the river of Mitzraym to the great river, the River Euphrates
The Kanites, the Kanazzites, the Kadmunites,
The Hittites, the Parizzites, the Raphaim,
The Amurites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Yabusites.”
Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children. And she had a Mitzraym maidservant whose name was Hagar.
So Sarai said to Abram, “See now, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has restrained me from bearing children. Please, go in to my maid; perhaps I shall obtain children by her.” And Abram heeded the voice of Sarai.
Then Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hagar her maid, the Mitzraym, and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan.
So Abram had sexual relations with Hagar, and she became pregnant. But when Hagar knew she was pregnant, she began to treat her mistress, Sarai, with contempt.
Then Sarai said to Abram, “This is all your fault! I put my servant into your arms, but now that she’s pregnant she treats me with contempt. 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will show who’s wrong you or me!
So Abram said to Sarai, “Indeed your maid is in your hand; do to her as you please.” And when Sarai dealt harshly with Hagar, she fled from her presence.
Now the Malak of YAHUAH found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur.
And the Malak said, “Hagar, Sarai’s maid, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She said, “I am fleeing from the presence of my mistress Sarai.”
The Malak of YAHUAH Dabar to her, “Return to your mistress, and submit yourself under her hand.”
Then the Malak of YAHUAH Dabar to her, “I will multiply your descendants exceedingly, so that they shall not be counted for multitude.”
And the Malak of YAHUAH Dabar to her: “Behold, you are with child, And you shall bear a son. You shall call his name Ishma'al, Because YAHUAH has heard your affliction.
Ishma'al shall be a wild man; His hand shall be against every man, And every man’s hand against him, and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brethren.”
Then she called the name of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who spoke to her, AL RU'Y (You Are ALUAH Who Sees) for she said, “Have I now sees the One who sees me?”
Therefore the well was called Baar Lahay Ru'y; observe, it is between Kadash and Barad.
So Hagar bore Abram a son; and Abram named his son, whom Hagar bore, Ishma'al.
Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishma'al to Abram.
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, YAHUAH appeared to him and said, “I am AL-Shaddah (𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄 ALUAH the AL'Mighty ONE) Serve me in Amunah (faithfully) and live a blameless life.
I will make a covenant with you, by which I will guarantee to give you countless descendants.”
At this, Abram fell face down on the ground. Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to him,
“This is my covenant with you: I will make you the father of a multitude of nations!
YAHUAH Dabar to Abram, I am changing your name. It will no longer be Abram. Instead, you will be called Abraham, for you will be the father of many nations.
I will make you extremely fruitful. Your descendants will become many nations, and kings will be among them!

“I will confirm my covenant with you and your descendants after you, from generation to generation. This is the everlasting covenant: I will always be your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE) and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your descendants after you.
And I will give the entire land of Canaan, where you now live as a foreigner, to you and your descendants. It will be their possession forever, and I will be their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.”
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Abraham, “Your responsibility is to obey the terms of the covenant. You and all your descendants have this continual responsibility.
This is the covenant that you and your descendants must keep: Each male among you must be circumcised.
You must cut off the flesh of your foreskin as a sign of the covenant between me and you.

From generation to generation, every male child must be circumcised on the eighth day after his birth. This applies not only to members of your family but also to the servants born in your household and the foreign-born servants whom you have purchased.
All must be circumcised. Your bodies will bear the mark of my everlasting covenant.
Any male who fails to be circumcised will be cut off from the covenant family for breaking the covenant.”
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Abraham, “Regarding Sarai, your wife her name will no longer be Sarai. From now on her name will be Sharah.
And I will barak her and give you a son from her! Yes, I will barak her richly, and she will become the mother of many nations. Kings of nations will be among her descendants.”

Then Abraham bowed down to the ground, but he laughed to himself in disbelief. “How could I become a father at the age of 100?” he thought. “And how can Sharah have a baby when she is ninety years old?”
So Abraham said to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, “May Ishma'al live under your special Barakah!”
But 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “No Sharah, your wife, will give birth to a son for you. You will name him Yachaq, and I will confirm my covenant with him and his descendants as an everlasting covenant.

As for Ishma'al, I will Barak him also, just as you have asked. I will make him extremely fruitful and multiply his descendants, he will become the father of twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.
But my covenant will be confirmed with Yachaq, who will be born to you and Sharah about this time next year.”
When 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had finished speaking, he left Abraham.

On that very day Abraham took his son, Ishma'al, and every male in his household, including those born there and those he had bought. Then he circumcised them, cutting off their foreskins, just as 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had told him.
Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised,
And Ishma'al, his son, was thirteen.
Both Abraham and his son, Ishma'al, were circumcised on that same day,
Along with all the other men and boys of the household, whether they were born there or bought as servants. All were circumcised with him.
Then YAHUAH appeared to Abraham by the terebinth trees of Mamra, as he was sitting in the tent door in the heat of the day.
So Abraham lifted his eyes and looked, and behold, three men were standing by him; and when he saw them, he ran from the tent door to meet them, and bowed himself to the ground,
And said, “My Master, if I have now found favor in Your sight, do not pass on by Your servant.
Please let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
And I will bring a morsel of bread, that you may refresh your hearts. After that you may pass by, inasmuch as you have come to your servant.”, The Men said, “Do as you have said.”
So Abraham hurried into the tent to Sharah and said, “Quickly, make ready three measures of fine meal; knead it and make cakes.”
And Abraham ran to the herd, took a tender and good calf, gave it to a young man, and he hastened to prepare it.
So Abraham took butter and milk and the calf which he had prepared, and set it before them; and he stood by them under the tree as they ate.
Then they said to him, “Where is Sharah your wife?” Abraham said, “Here, in the tent.”

And the Malak of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄 ALUAH said, “I will certainly return to you according to this time of life, and behold, Sharah your wife shall have a son.” (Sharah was listening in the tent door which was behind him.)
Now Abraham and Sharah were old, well advanced in age; and Sharah had passed the age of childbearing.
Therefore Sharah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old, shall I have pleasure, my master being old also?”
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Abraham, “Why did Sharah laugh, saying, ‘Shall I surely bear a child, since I am old?’
Is anything too hard for 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH? At the appointed time I will return to you, according to this time of life, and Sharah shall have a son.”
But Sharah denied it, saying, “I did not laugh,” for she was afraid. And the Malak 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said, “No, but you did laugh!”
Then the men rose from there and looked toward Sudum, and Abraham went with them to send them on the way.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am doing,
since Abraham shall surely become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations of the Arath shall be Barak in him?

For I have known him, in order that Abraham may command his children and his household after him, that they keep the ways of YAHUAH, to do righteousness and justice, that YAHUAH may bring to Abraham what He has spoken to him.”
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “Because the outcry against Sudum and Gumurrah is great, and because their sin is very grave,
I will go down now and see whether they have done altogether according to the outcry against it that has come to ME; and if not, I will know.”
Then the men turned away from there and went toward Sudum, but Abraham still stood before the Malak of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH
And Abraham came near and said, “Would You also destroy the righteous with the wicked?
Suppose there were fifty righteous within the city; would You also destroy the place and not spare it for the fifty righteous that were in it?

Far be it from You to do such a thing as this, to slay the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous should be as the wicked; far be it from You! Shouldn't the Judge of all the Arath do what's right?”
So 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “If I find in Sudum fifty righteous within the city, then I will spare all the place for their sakes.”
Then Abraham answered and said, “Indeed now, who am I but dust and ashes have taken it upon myself to speak to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH:
Suppose there were five less than the fifty righteous; would You destroy all of the city for lack of five?” So 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “If I find there forty-five, I will not destroy it.”
And Abraham spoke to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH yet again and said, “Suppose there should be forty found there?” and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said, “I will not do it for the sake of forty.”
Then Abraham said, “Let not 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be angry, and I will speak: Suppose thirty should be found there?” and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said, “I will not do it if I find thirty there.”
And Abraham said, “Indeed now, I have taken it upon myself to speak to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH: Suppose twenty should be found there?” and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.”
Then Abraham said, “Let not 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be angry, and I will speak but once more: Suppose ten should be found there?” And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said, “I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.”
So YAHUAH went His way as soon as He had finished speaking with Abraham; and Abraham returned to his place.
Now the two Malak came to Sudum in the evening, and Lut was sitting in the gate of Sudum. When Lut saw them, he rose to meet them, and Lut bowed himself with his face toward the ground.

And Lut said, “Here now, my Masters, please turn in to your servant’s house and spend the night, and wash your feet; then you may rise early and go on your way.” And they said, “No, but we will spend the night in the open square.”
But he insisted strongly; so they turned in to him and entered his house. Then he made them a feast, and baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
Now before they lay down, the men of the city, the men of Sudum, both old and young, all the people from every quarter, surrounded the house.
And they called to Lut and said to him, “Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us, so we can have sex with them!”
So Lut went out to them through the doorway, shut the door behind him,
And said, “Please, my brethren, do not do so wickedly!

See now, I have two daughters who have not known a man; please, let me bring them out to you, and you may do to them as you wish; only do nothing to these men, since this is the reason they have come under the shadow of my roof.”

And they said, “Stand back!” Then they said, “This one came in to stay here, and he keeps acting as a judge; now we will deal worse with you than with them.” So they pressed hard against the man Lut, and came near to break down the door.
But the men reached out their hands and pulled Lut into the house with them, and shut the door.
And they struck the men who were at the doorway of the house with blindness, both small and great, so that they became weary trying to find the door.
Then the Malakym said to Lut, “Have you anyone else here? Son-in-law, your sons, your daughters, and whomever you have in the city take them out of this place!
For we will destroy this place, because the outcry against them has grown great before the face of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has sent us to destroy it.”

So Lut went out and spoke to his sons-in-laws, who had married his daughters, and said, “Get up, get out of this place; for 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will destroy this city!” But to his sons-in-laws he seemed to be joking.
When the morning dawned, the Malak urged Lut to hurry, saying, “Arise, take your wife and your two daughters who are here, lest you be consumed in the punishment of the city.”
And while he lingered, the men took hold of his hand, his wife’s hand, and the hands of his two daughters, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH being merciful to him, and they brought him out and set him outside the city.
So it came to pass, when they had brought them outside, the Malak said, “Escape for your life! Do not look behind you nor stay anywhere in the plain. Escape to the mountains, lest you be destroyed.”
Then Lut said to them, “Please my Masters!

Indeed now, your servant has found favor in your sight, and you have increased your mercy which you have shown me by saving my life; but I cannot escape to the mountains, lest some evil overtake me and I die.
See now, this city is near enough to flee to, and it is a little one; please let me escape there and my soul shall live.”
And he said to him, “See, I have favored you concerning this thing also, in that I will not overthrow this city for which you have spoken.
Hurry, escape there. For I cannot do anything until you arrive there.” Therefore the name of the city was called Zuar.
The sun had risen upon the Arath when Lut entered Zuar.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄 ALUAH rained brimstone and fire on Sudum and Gumurrah from the Shamaym.
So HE overthrew those cities, all the plain, all the inhabitants of the cities, and what grew on the ground.
But Lut wife looked back behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham went early in the morning to the place where he had stood before 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Then he looked toward Sudum and Gumurrah, and toward all the land of the plain; and he saw, and behold, the smoke of the land which went up like the smoke of a furnace.

And it came to pass, when 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH destroyed the cities of the plain, that 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH remembered Abraham, and sent Lut out of the midst of the overthrow, when He overthrew the cities in which Lut had dwelt.
Then Lut went up out of Zuar and dwelt in the mountains, and his two daughters were with him; for he was afraid to dwell in Zuar. And he and his two daughters dwelt in a cave.
Now the firstborn said to the younger, “Our father is old, and there is no man on the Arath to come in to us as is the custom of all the Arath.
Come, let us make our father drink wine, and we will lie with him, that we may preserve the lineage of our father.”
So they made their father drink wine that night. And the firstborn went in and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down or when she arose.

It happened on the next day that the firstborn said to the younger, “Indeed I lay with my father last night; let us make him drink wine tonight also, and you go in and lie with him, that we may preserve the lineage of our father.”
Then they made their father drink wine that night also. And the younger arose and lay with him, and Lut did not know when she lay down or when she arose.
Thus both the daughters of Lut were with child by their father.
The firstborn bore a son and called his name Muab; he is the father of the Muabites to this day.
And the younger, she also bore a son and called his name Ban-Ammy; he is the father of the people of Ammun to this day.
Abraham moved south to the Nagab and lived for a while between Kadash and Shur, and then he moved on to Garar. While living there as a foreigner,
Abraham introduced his wife, Sharah, by saying, “She is my sister.” So King Abimalach of Garar sent for Sharah and had her brought to him at his palace.
But that night 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH came to Abimalach in a dream and said to him, “You are a dead man, for that woman you have taken is already married!”
But Abimalach had not slept with her yet, so he said, “𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, will you destroy an innocent nation?
Abraham told me, ‘She is my sister’? And Sharah herself said, ‘Yes, he is my brother.’ I acted in complete innocence! My hands are clean.”
In the dream 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar, “Yes, I know you are innocent. That’s why I kept you from sinning against me, and why I did not let you touch her.

Now return the woman to her husband, and he will pray for you, for he is a Nabym (Prophet). Then you will live. But if you don’t return her to Abraham, you can be sure that you and all your people will die.”
Abimalach got up early the next morning and quickly called all his servants together. When he told them what had happened, his men were terrified.

Then Abimalach called for Abraham. “What have you done to us?” he demanded. “What crime have I committed that deserves treatment like this, making me and my kingdom guilty of this great sin? No one should ever do what you have done!
Abimalach asked Abraham what have you been thinking for you to do such a thing?”
“I thought that there’s no fear of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in this place,” Abraham replied, “and that they would kill me because of my wife.
Besides, she really is my sister she’s my father’s daughter, but not my mother’s daughter so she could become my wife.
When 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH caused me to journey from my father’s house, I asked her to do me this favor and say, ‘He’s my brother.’”
So Abimalach took some sheep and oxen, and some male and female servants, gave them to Abraham, returned his wife Sharah to him,
Abimalach said, “Look! My land is available to you, so settle wherever you please.”
Abimalach also told Sharah, “Look! I am giving your brother 1,000 pieces of silver to vindicate you in the eyes of all who are with you. As a result, you will be completely vindicated.”
Then Abraham interceded with 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH healed Abimalach, his wife, and his female servants so they could bear children,
Since 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had made all the women barren in Abimalach’s household on account of Abraham’s wife Sharah.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH visited Sharah as He had said, and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH did for Sharah as He had Dabar.
For Sharah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had said to Abraham.
And Abraham called the name of his son who was born to him by Sharah Yachaq.
Then Abraham circumcised his son Yachaq when he was eight days old, as 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had commanded him.
Now Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Yachaq was born to him.
And Sharah said, “𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has made me laugh, and all who hear will laugh with me.”
She also said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sharah would nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”
So the child grew and was weaned. And Abraham made a great feast on the same day that Yachaq was weaned.
And Sharah saw the son of Hagar the Mitzraym, whom she had borne to Abraham, scoffing.
Therefore she said to Abraham, “Cast out this bondwoman and her son; for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, namely with Yachaq.”
And the matter was very displeasing in Abraham’s sight because of his son.

But 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Abraham, “Do not let it be displeasing in your sight because of the lad or because of your bondwoman. Whatever Sarah has said to you, listen to her voice; for in Yachaq your seed shall be called.
Yet I will also make a nation of the son of the bondwoman, because he is your seed.”

So Abraham rose early in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water; and putting it on her shoulder, Abraham sent her away with their son. Then she departed and wandered in the Wilderness of Baarshaba.
And the water in the skin was used up, and she placed the boy under one of the shrubs.
Then she went and sat down across from him at a distance of about a bowshot; for she said to herself, “Let me not see the death of the boy.” So she sat opposite him, and lifted her voice and wept.

And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH heard the voice of the lad. Then the Malak of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH called to Hagar out of Shamaym, and said to her, “What ails you Hagar? Fear not, for 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has heard the voice of the lad where he is.
Arise, lift up the lad and hold him with your hand, for I will make him a great nation.”
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled the skin with water, and gave the lad a drink.
So 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was with the lad; and he grew and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer.
He dwelt in the Wilderness of Paran; and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Mitzraym.
And it came to pass at that time that Abimalach and Phichul, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham, saying, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is with you in all that you do.

Now therefore, swear to me by 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH that you will not deal falsely with me, with my offspring, or with my posterity; but that according to the kindness that I have done to you, you will do to me and to the land in which you have dwelt.”
And Abraham said, “I will swear.”
Then Abraham rebuked Abimalach because of a well of water which Abimalach’s servants had seized.
And Abimalach said, “I do not know who has done this thing; you did not tell me, nor had I heard of it until today.”
So Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimalach, and the two of them made a covenant.
And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.
Then Abimalach asked Abraham, “What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?”
And Abraham said, “You will take these seven ewe lambs from my hand, that they may be my witness that I have dug this well.”
Therefore he called that place Baarshaba, because the two of them swore an oath there.
Thus they made a covenant at Baarshaba. So Abimalach rose with Phichul, the commander of his army, and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
Then Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Baarshaba, and there called on the name of YAHUAH, the Everlasting 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
And Abraham stayed in the land of the Philistines many days.
Some time later, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH tested Abraham’s Amunah (Faith). “Abraham!” 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH called. “Yes,” Abraham replied. “Here I am.”
“Take your son, your only son—yes, Yachaq, whom you Ahaba (love) so much and go to the land of Muryah. Go and sacrifice him as a burnt offering on one of the mountains, which I will show you.”

The next morning Abraham got up early, he saddled his donkey and took two of his servants with him, along with his son, Yachaq. Then he chopped wood for a fire for a burnt offering and set out for the place 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had told him about.
On the third day of their journey, Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
“Stay here with the donkey,” Abraham told the servants. “The boy and I will travel a little farther. We will worship there, and then we will come right back.”
So Abraham placed the wood for the burnt offering on Yachaq’s shoulders, while he himself carried the fire and the knife. As the two of them walked on together,
Yachaq turned to Abraham and said, “Father?” Yes, my son?” Abraham replied. “We have the fire and the wood,” the boy said, “but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?”
“ALUAH will provide a sheep for the burnt offering, my son,” Abraham answered. And they both walked on together.
When they arrived at the place where 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had told him to go, Abraham built an altar and arranged the wood on it. Then he tied his son, Yachaq, and laid him on the altar on top of the wood.
And Abraham picked up the knife to kill his son as a sacrifice.
At that moment the Malak of YAHUAH Dabar to Abraham from Shamaym, “Abraham! Abraham! “Yes,” Abraham replied. “Here I am!”
“Don’t lay a hand on the boy!” the Malak said. “Do not hurt him in any way, for now I know that you truly fear 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. You have not withheld from me even your son, your only son.”
Then Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. So he took the ram and sacrificed it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
Abraham named the place YAHUAH-Yhirah (which means “YAHUAH will provide”). To this day, people still use that name as a proverb: “On the mountain of YAHUAH, it will be provided.”
Then the Malak of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH called again to Abraham from Shamaym.
“This is what 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar: Because you have obeyed ME and have not withheld even your son, your only son, I swear by my own Name that
I will certainly Barak you. I will multiply your descendants beyond number, like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will conquer the cities of their enemies.
And through your descendants all the nations of the Arath will be Barak, all because you have obeyed me.”
Then they returned to the servants and traveled back to Baarshaba, where Abraham continued to live.
Soon after this, Abraham heard that Milcah, his brother Nahur’s wife, had borne Nahur eight sons.
The oldest was named Uz, the next oldest was Buz, followed by Kamual (the ancestor of the Arameans),
Kasad, Hazo, Pildash, Yidlaph, and Bathual.
(Bathual became the father of Rabakah.) In addition to these eight sons from Milcah,
Nahor had four other children from his concubine Raumah. Their names were Tabah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
Sharah lived for one hundred and twenty seven years. That’s how long Sharah’s life was.
She died in Kiriath-arba (that is, in Habrun) in the land of Canaan. Abraham went in to mourn for Sharah and to weep for her.
Then Abraham stood up from beside his dead wife and addressed the Hittites. Abraham said,
““I am a foreigner and a visitor among you. Give me property for a burial place among you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
The Hittites responded to Abraham,
“Listen to us, sir. You are a mighty prince among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our burial tombs. None of us would refuse you his tomb for burying your dead.”
Abraham rose and bowed before the Hittites, the people of the land,
And addressed them, “If you are willing that I should bury my dead out of my sight, listen to me and make a request of Zuhar’s son Aphrun on my behalf.
Give me the cave of Machpalah that belongs to him, at the end of his field. He should sell it to me in your presence at full price for a burial site.”
Now since Aphrun the Hittite had taken a seat there among the Hittites, he responded publicly to Abraham where the Hittites and everyone who was entering the gate of his city could hear him:
“No, sir. Listen to me! I will give you the field, and I will give you the cave that’s in it. I give it to you publicly, in the sight of my people. Bury your dead.”
Abraham bowed before the people of the land
And then addressed Aphrun so all the people of the land could hear him: “Please listen to me! I am willing to pay the price of the field. Accept it from me, so I may bury my dead there.”
So Aphrun answered Abraham,
“Sir, listen to me! The land is worth 400 shakals of silver, but what’s that between us? You may bury your dead.”
Abraham agreed with Aphrun, so he weighed out to Aphrun the money to which he had agreed publicly while the Hittites were listening: 400 shakals of silver at the current merchant rate.
That’s how Aphrun’s field in Machpalah, east of Mamra the field, the cave that was in it, and all the trees that were within the boundaries of the field came to be deeded
To Abraham in the presence of all the Hittites and everyone who was entering the city gate.
After this, Abraham buried his wife Sharah in the cave at the field of Machpalah, east of Mamra (that is, in Habrun) in the land of Canaan.
And so the field with its cave was deeded by the Hittites to Abraham as a burial site.
Now Abraham was old, well advanced in age; and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had Barak Abraham in all things.
So Abraham said to the oldest servant of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Please, put your hand under my thigh,
And I will make you swear by 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Arath, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell;
But you will go to my country and to my family, and take a wife for my son Yachaq.”
And the servant said to him, “Perhaps the woman will not be willing to follow me to this land. Must I take your son back to the land from which you came?”
But Abraham said to him, “Beware that you do not take my son back there.

The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my family, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, ‘To your descendants I give this land,’ 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will send His Malak before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there.
And if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you will be released from this oath; only do not take my son back there.”
So the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter.
Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels and departed, for all his master’s goods were in his hand. And he arose and went to Masuputamia, to the city of Nahur.
And he made his camels kneel down outside the city by a well of water at evening time, the time when women go out to draw water.
Then he said, “O 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of my master Abraham, please give me success this day, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
Behold, here I stand by the well of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.

Now let it be that the young woman to whom I say, ‘Please let down your pitcher that I may drink,’ and she says, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink’—let her be the one You have appointed for Your servant Yachaq. And by this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.”
And it happened, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rabakah, who was born to Bathual, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahur, Abraham’s brother, came out with her pitcher on her shoulder.
Now the young woman was very beautiful to behold, a virgin; no man had known her. And she went down to the well, filled her pitcher, and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please let me drink a little water from your pitcher.”
So she said, “Drink, my master.” Then she quickly let her pitcher down to her hand, and gave him a drink.
And when she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will draw water for your camels also, until they have finished drinking.”
Then she quickly emptied her pitcher into the trough, ran back to the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels.
And the man, wondering at her, remained silent so as to know whether 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had made his journey prosperous or not.
So it was, when the camels had finished drinking, that the man took a golden nose ring weighing half a shakal, and two bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shakals of gold,
and said, “Whose daughter are you? Tell me, please, is there room in your father’s house for us to lodge?”
So she said to him, “I am the daughter of Bathual, Milcah’s son, whom she bore to Nahur.”
Moreover she said to him, “We have both straw and feed enough, and room to lodge.”
Then the man bowed down his head and worshiped 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

And he said, “Baraked be the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken His mercy and His truth toward my master. As for me, being on the way, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH led me to the house of my master’s brethren.”
So the young woman ran and told her mother’s household these things.
Now Rabakah had a brother whose name was Laban, and Laban ran out to the man by the well.

So it came to pass, when he saw the nose ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s wrists, and when he heard the words of his sister Rabakah, saying, “Thus the man spoke to me,” that he went to the man. And there he stood by the camels at the well.
And he said, “Come in, O Baraked of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH! Why do you stand outside? For I have prepared the house, and a place for the camels.”
Then the man came to the house. And he unloaded the camels, and provided straw and feed for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
Food was set before him to eat, but he said, “I will not eat until I have told you about my errand.” and he said, “Speak on.”
So he said, “I am Abraham’s servant.
The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of my master has Baraked my master greatly, and he has become great; and he has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
And Sharah my master’s wife bore a son to my master when she was old; and to him he has given all that he has.
Now my master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell;
But you shall go to my father’s house and to my family, and take a wife for my son.’
And I said to my master, ‘Perhaps the woman will not follow me.’
But he said to me, ‘𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH before whom I walk, will send His Malak with you and prosper your way; and you shall take a wife for my son from my family and from my father’s house.
You will be clear from this oath when you arrive among my family; for if they will not give her to you, then you will be released from my oath.’
“And this day I came to the well and said, ‘O 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of my master Abraham, if You Will, now prosper the way in which I go,
Behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass that when the virgin comes out to draw water, and I say to her, “Please give me a little water from your pitcher to drink,”
And she says to me, “Drink, and I will draw for your camels also,”—let her be the woman whom 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has appointed for my master’s son.’

“But before I had finished speaking in my heart, there was Rabakah, coming out with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down to the well and drew water. And I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’
And she made haste and let her pitcher down from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will give your camels a drink also.’ So I drank, and she gave the camels a drink also.
