And people from all around came to Mitzraym to buy grain from Ya'asaf because the famine was severe throughout the world.
When Ya'aqub heard that grain was available in Mitzraym, he said to his sons, “Why are you standing around looking at one another?
I have heard there is grain in Mitzraym. Go down there, and buy enough grain to keep us alive. Otherwise we will die.”
So Ya'asaf’s ten older brothers went down to Mitzraym to buy grain.
But Ya'aqub wouldn’t let Ya'asaf’s younger brother, Banyamyn, go with them, for fear some harm might come to him.
So Ya'aqub’s sons arrived in Mitzraym along with others to buy food, for the famine was in Canaan as well.

Since Ya'asaf was governor of all Mitzraym and in charge of selling grain to all the people, it was to him that his brothers came. When they arrived, they bowed before him with their faces to the ground.

Ya'asaf recognized his brothers instantly, but he pretended to be a stranger and spoke harshly to them. “Where are you from?” he demanded. “From the land of Canaan,” they replied. “We have come to buy food.”
Although Ya'asaf recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.
And Ya'asaf remembered the dreams he’d had about them many years before, he said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see how vulnerable our land has become.”
“No, my master!” they exclaimed. “Your servants have simply come to buy food.
We are all brothers, members of the same family. We are honest men, sir! We are not spies!”
“Yes, you are!” Ya'asaf insisted. “You have come to see how vulnerable our land has become.”

“Sir,” they said, “there are actually twelve of us. We, your servants, are all brothers, sons of a man living in the land of Canaan. Our youngest brother is back there with our father right now, and one of our brothers is no longer with us.”
But Ya'asaf insisted, “As I said, you are spies!
This is how I will test your story. I swear by the life of Phar'uh that you will never leave Mitzraym unless your youngest brother comes here!

One of you must go and get your brother. I will keep the rest of you here in prison. Then we will find out whether or not your story is true. By the life of Phar'uh, if it turns out that you don’t have a younger brother, then I will know you are spies.”
So Ya'asaf put them all in prison for three days.
On the third day Ya'asaf said to them, “I am an 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH-fearing man. If you do as I say, you will live.
If you really are honest men, choose one of your brothers to remain in prison. The rest of you may go home with grain for your starving families.
But you must bring your youngest brother back to me. This will prove that you are telling the truth, and you will not die.” To this they agreed.

Speaking among themselves, they said, “Clearly we are being punished because of what we did to Ya'asaf long ago. We saw his anguish when he pleaded for his life, but we wouldn’t listen. That’s why we are in this trouble.”
“Did I not tell you not to sin against the boy?” Rauban asked. “But you wouldn’t listen. And now we have to answer for his blood!”
Of course, they did not know that Ya'asaf understood them, for he had been speaking to them through an interpreter.
Now he turned away from them and began to weep. When he regained his composure, he spoke to them again. Then he chose Simaun from among them and had him tied up right before their eyes.

Ya'asaf then ordered his servants to fill the men’s sacks with grain, but he also gave secret instructions to return each brother’s payment at the top of his sack. He also gave them supplies for their journey home.
So the brothers loaded their donkeys with the grain and headed for home.
But when they stopped for the night and one of them opened his sack to get grain for his donkey, he found his money in the top of his sack.
“Look!” he exclaimed to his brothers. “My money has been returned; it’s here in my sack!” Then their hearts sank. Trembling, they said to each other, “What has 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH done to us?”
When the brothers came to their father, Ya'aqub, in the land of Canaan, they told him everything that had happened to them.
“The man who is governor of the land spoke very harshly to us,” they told him. “He accused us of being spies scouting the land.
But we said, ‘We are honest men, not spies.
We are twelve brothers, sons of one father. One brother is no longer with us, and the youngest is at home with our father in the land of Canaan.’

“Then the man who is governor of the land told us, ‘This is how I will find out if you are honest men. Leave one of your brothers here with me, and take grain for your starving families and go on home.
But you must bring your youngest brother back to me. Then I will know you are honest men and not spies. Then I will give you back your brother, and you may trade freely in the land.’”
As they emptied out their sacks, there in each man’s sack was the bag of money he had paid for the grain! The brothers and their father were terrified when they saw the bags of money.
Ya'aqub exclaimed, “You are robbing me of my children! Ya'asaf is gone! Simaun is gone! And now you want to take Banyamyn, too. Everything is going against me!”
Then Rauban said to his father, “You may kill my two sons if I do not bring Banyamyn back to you. I will be responsible for him, and I promise to bring him back.”

But Ya'aqub replied, “My son will not go down with you. His brother Ya'asaf is dead, and he is all I have left. If anything should happen to him on your journey, you would send this grieving, white-haired man to his grave.”
But the famine continued to ravage the land of Canaan.
When the grain they had brought from Mitzraym was almost gone, Ya'aqub said to his sons, “Go back and buy us a little more food.”
But Yahudah said, “The man was serious when he warned us, ‘You won’t see my face again unless your brother is with you.’
If you send Banyamyn with us, we will go down and buy more food.
But if you don’t let Banyamyn go, we won’t go either. Remember, the man said, ‘You won’t see my face again unless your brother is with you.’”
“Why were you so cruel to me?” Ya'aqub moaned. “Why did you tell him you had another brother?”

“The man kept asking us questions about our family,” they replied. “He asked, ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?’ So we answered his questions. How could we know he would say, ‘Bring your brother down here’?”
Yahudah said to his father, “Send the boy with me, and we will be on our way. Otherwise we will all die of starvation and not only we, but you and our little ones.
I personally guarantee his safety. You may hold me responsible if I do not bring him back to you, let me bear the blame forever.
If we had not wasted all this time, we could have gone and returned twice by now.”

So their father, Ya'aqub, finally said to them, “If it can’t be avoided, then at least do this. Pack your bags with the best products of this land. Take them down to the man as gifts—balm, honey, gum, aromatic resin, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
Also take double the money that was put back in your sacks, as it was probably someone’s mistake.
Then take your brother, and go back to the man.
May 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH give you mercy as you go before the man, so that he will release Simaun and let Banyamyn return. But if I must lose my children, so be it.”
So the men packed Ya'aqub’s gifts and double the money and headed off with Banyamyn. They finally arrived in Mitzraym and presented themselves to Ya'asaf.

When Ya'asaf saw Banyamyn with them, he said to the manager of his household, “These men will eat with me this noon. Take them inside the palace. Then go slaughter an animal, and prepare a big feast.”
So the man did as Ya'asaf told him and took them into Ya'asaf’s palace.

The brothers were terrified when they saw that they were being taken into Ya'asaf’s house. “It’s because of the money someone put in our sacks last time we were here,” they said. “He plans to pretend that we stole it. Then he will seize us, make us slaves, and take our donkeys.”
The brothers approached the manager of Ya'asaf’s household and spoke to him at the entrance to the palace.
“Sir,” they said, “we came to Mitzraym once before to buy food.

But as we were returning home, we stopped for the night and opened our sacks. Then we discovered that each man’s money, the exact amount paid was in the top of his sack! Here it is; we have brought it back with us.
We also have additional money to buy more food. We have no idea who put our money in our sacks.”

“Relax. Do not t be afraid,” the household manager told them. “Your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your father, must have put this treasure into your sacks. I know I received your payment.” Then he released Simaun and brought him out to them.
The manager then led the men into Ya'asaf’s palace, he gave them water to wash their feet and provided food for their donkeys.
They were told they would be eating there, so they prepared their gifts for Ya'asaf’s arrival at noon.
When Ya'asaf came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought him, then bowed low to the ground before him.
After greeting them, he asked, “How is your father, the old man you spoke about? Is he still alive?”
“Yes,” they replied. “Our father, your servant, is alive and well.” And they bowed low again.
Then Ya'asaf looked at his brother Banyamyn, the son of his own mother. “Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?” Ya'asaf asked. “May 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be merciful to you, my son.”
Then Ya'asaf hurried from the room because he was overcome with emotion for his brother, he went into his private room, where he broke down and wept.
After washing his face, he came back out, keeping himself under control. Then he ordered, “Bring out the food!”

The waiters served Ya'asaf at his own table, and his brothers were served at a separate table. The Mitzraym who ate with Ya'asaf sat at their own table, because Mitzraym despise Abarym (Hebrews) and refuse to eat with them.
Ya'asaf told each of his brothers where to sit, and to their amazement, he seated them according to age, from oldest to youngest.
And Ya'asaf filled their plates with food from his own table, giving Banyamyn five times as much as he gave the others. So they feasted and drank freely with him.

When his brothers were ready to leave, Ya'asaf gave these instructions to his palace manager: “Fill each of their sacks with as much grain as they can carry, and put each man’s money back into his sack.
And put my personal silver cup at the top of the youngest brother’s sack, along with the money for his grain.” So the manager did as Ya'asaf instructed him.
The brothers were up at dawn and were sent on their journey with their loaded donkeys.

But when they had gone only a short distance and were barely out of the city, Ya'asaf said to his palace manager, “Chase after them and stop them. When you catch up with them, ask them, ‘Why have you repaid my kindness with such evil?
Why have you stolen my master’s silver cup, which he uses to predict the future? What a wicked thing you have done!’”
When the palace manager caught up with the men, he spoke to them as he had been instructed.
“What are you talking about?” the brothers responded. “We are your servants and would never do such a thing!
Did we not return the money we found in our sacks? We brought it back all the way from the land of Canaan. Why would we steal silver or gold from your master’s house?
If you find his cup with any one of us, let that man die. And all the rest of us, will be your slaves.”
“That’s fair,” the man replied. “But only the one who stole the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may go free.”
They all quickly took their sacks from the backs of their donkeys and opened them.
The palace manager searched the brothers’ sacks, from the oldest to the youngest. And the cup was found in Banyamyn's sack!
When the brothers saw this, they tore their clothing in despair. Then they loaded their donkeys again and returned to the city.
Ya'asaf was still in his palace when Yahudah and his brothers arrived, and they fell to the ground before him.
“What have you done?” Ya'asaf demanded. “Don’t you know that a man like me can predict the future?”

Yahudah answered, “Oh, my master, what can we say to you? How can we explain this? How can we prove our innocence? 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is punishing us for our sins. My master, we have all returned to be your slaves all of us, not just our brother who had your cup in his sack.”
“No,” Ya'asaf said. “I would never do such a thing! Only the man who stole the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may go back to your father in Shalum.”
Then Yahudah stepped forward and said, “Please, my master, let your servant say just one word to you. Please, do not be angry with me, even though you are as powerful as Phar'uh himself.
“My master, previously you asked us, your servants, ‘Do you have a father or a brother?’

And we responded, ‘Yes, my master, we have a father who is an old man, and his youngest son is a child of his old age. His full brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother’s children, and his father loves him very much.’
“And you said to us, ‘Bring him here so I can see him with my own eyes.’
But we said to you, ‘My master, the boy cannot leave his father, for his father would die.’
But you told us, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes with you, you will never see my face again.’
“So we returned to your servant, our father, and told him what you had said.
Later, when he said, ‘Go back again and buy us more food,’
We replied, ‘We can’t go unless you let our youngest brother go with us. We will never get to see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’
“Then my father said to us, ‘As you know, my wife had two sons,
And one of them went away and never returned. Doubtless he was torn to pieces by some wild animal. I have never seen him since.
Now if you take his brother away from me, and any harm comes to him, you will send this grieving, white-haired man to his grave.’
“And now, my master, I cannot go back to my father without the boy. Our father’s life is bound up in the boy’s life.
If he sees that the boy is not with us, our father will die. We, your servants, will indeed be responsible for sending that grieving, white-haired man to his grave.
My master, I guaranteed to my father that I would take care of the boy. I told him, ‘If I don’t bring him back to you, I will bear the blame forever.’
“So please, my master, let me stay here as a slave instead of the boy, and let the boy return with his brothers.
For how can I return to my father if the boy is not with me? I couldn’t bear to see the anguish this would cause my father!”
Ya'asaf could not stand it no longer. There were many people in the room, and he said to his attendants, “Out, all of you!” So he was alone with his brothers when he told them who he was.
Then Ya'asaf broke down and wept. He wept so loudly the Mitzraym could hear him, and word of it quickly carried to Phar'uh’s palace.
“I am Ya'asaf!” he said to his brothers. “Is my father still alive?” But his brothers were speechless! They were stunned to realize that Ya'asaf was standing there in front of them.
“Please, come closer,” he said to them. So they came closer. And he said again, “I am Ya'asaf, your brother, whom you sold into slavery in Mitzraym.
But do not be upset, and don’t be angry with yourselves for selling me to this place. It was 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who sent me here ahead of you to preserve your lives.
This famine that has ravaged the land for two years will last five more years, and there will be neither plowing nor harvesting.
Our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has sent me ahead of you to keep you and your families alive and to preserve many survivors.
So it was 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who sent me here, not you! And he is the one who made me an adviser to Phar'uh, the manager of his entire palace and the governor of all Mitzraym.
“Now hurry back to my father and tell him, ‘This is what your son Ya'asaf says: 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has made me master over all the land of Mitzraym. So come down to me immediately!
You can live in the region of Gushan, where you can be near me with all your children and grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and everything you own.
I will take care of you there, for there are still five years of famine ahead of us. Otherwise you, your household, and all your animals will starve.’”
Then Ya'asaf added, “Look! You can see for yourselves, and so can my brother Banyamyn, that I really am Ya'asaf!
Go tell my father of my honored position here in Mitzraym. Describe for him everything you have seen, and then bring my father here quickly.”
Weeping with joy, he embraced Banyamyn, and Banyamyn did the same.
Then Ya'asaf kissed each of his brothers and wept over them, and after that they began talking freely with him.
The news soon reached Phar'uh’s palace: Ya'asaf brothers have arrived!” Phar'uh and his officials were all delighted to hear this.
Phar'uh said to Ya'asaf, “Tell your brothers, ‘This is what you must do: Load your pack animals, and hurry back to the land of Canaan.
Then get your father and all of your families, and return here to me. I will give you the very best land in Mitzraym, and you will eat from the best that the land produces.’”
Then Phar'uh said to Ya'asaf, “Tell your brothers, ‘Take wagons from the land of Mitzraym to carry your little children and your wives, and bring your father here.
Do not worry about your personal belongings, for the best of all the land of Mitzraym is yours.’”
So the sons of Ya'aqub did as they were told. Ya'asaf provided them with wagons, as Phar'uh had commanded, and he gave them supplies for the journey.
And he gave each of them new clothes, but to Banyamyn he gave five changes of clothes and 300 pieces of silver.
He also sent his father ten male donkeys loaded with the finest products of Mitzraym, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other supplies he would need on his journey.
So Ya'asaf sent his brothers off, and as they left, he called after them, “Don’t quarrel about all this along the way!”
And they left Mitzraym and returned to their father, Ya'aqub, in the land of Canaan.
Ya'asaf is still alive!” they told him. “And he is the governor of all the land of Mitzraym!” Ya'aqub was stunned at the news, he could not believe it.
But when they repeated to Ya'aqub everything Ya'asaf had told them, and when he saw the wagons Ya'asaf had sent to carry him, their father’s spirits revived.
Then Ya'aqub exclaimed, “It must be true! My son Ya'asaf is alive! I must go and see him before I die.”
So Ya'aqub set out for Mitzraym with all his possessions. And when he came to Baarshaba, he offered sacrifices to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of his father, Yachaq.
During the night 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Ya'aqub in a vision. Ya'aqub! Ya'aqub!” 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH called. “Here I am,” Ya'aqub replied.
“I AM 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your father,” the voice said. “Do not be afraid to go down to Mitzraym, for there I will make your family into a great nation.
I will go with you down to Mitzraym, and I will bring you back again. You will die in Mitzraym, but Ya'asaf will be with you to close your eyes.”
So Ya'aqub left Baarshaba, and his sons took him to Mitzraym. They carried him and their little ones and their wives in the wagons Phar'uh had provided for them.
They also took all their livestock and all the personal belongings they had acquired in the land of Canaan. So Ya'aqub and his entire family went to Mitzraym,
Sons and grandsons, daughters and granddaughters—all his descendants.
These are the names of the descendants of YASHAR'AL (the sons of Ya'aqub) who went to Mitzraym: Rauban was Ya'aqub’s oldest son.
The sons of Rauban were Hanuch, Pallu, Hazrun, and Carmi.
The sons of Simaun were Yamual, Yamin, Uhad, Yakin, Zuhar, and Shaul. (Shaul’s mother was a Canaanite woman.)
The sons of Lauy were Garshun, Kuhath, and Marari.
The sons of Yahudah were Ar, Unan, Shalah, Paraz, and Zarah (though Ar and Unan had died in the land of Canaan). The sons of Paraz were Hazrun and Hamul.
The sons of Issachar were Tula, Puah, Yashub, and Shimrun.
The sons of Zabulun were Sarad, Alun, and Yahlaal.
These were the sons of La'ah and Ya'aqub who were born in Paddan-aram, in addition to their daughter, Dinah. The number of Ya'aqub’s descendants (male and female) through La'ah was thirty-three.
The sons of Gad were Zaphun, Haggi, Shuni, Azbun, Ari, Arudi, and Arali.
The sons of Ashar were Imnah, Ishbah, Ishbi, and Baryah. Their sister was Sharah. Baryah’s sons were Habar and Malkial.
These were the sons of Zilpah, the servant given to La'ah by her father, Laban. The number of Ya'aqub’s descendants through Zilpah was sixteen.
The sons of Ya'aqub’s wife Rachal were Ya'asaf and Banyamyn.
Ya'asaf’s sons, born in the land of Mitzraym, were Manassah and Aphraim. Their mother was Asanath, daughter of Putiphara, the priest of Un.
Banyamyn’s sons were Bala, Bakar, Ashbal, Gara, Naaman, Ahi, Rush, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.
These were the sons of Rachal and Ya'aqub. The number of Ya'aqub’s descendants through Rachal was fourteen.
The son of Dan was Hushim.
The sons of Naphtali were Yahzaal, Guni, Yazar, and Shillam.
These were the sons of Bilhah, the servant given to Rachal by her father, Laban. The number of Ya'aqub’s descendants through Bilhah was seven.
The total number of Ya'aqub’s direct descendants who went with him to Mitzraym, not counting his sons’ wives, was sixty-six.
In addition, Ya'asaf had two sons who were born in Mitzraym. So altogether, there were seventy members of Ya'aqub’s family in the land of Mitzraym.
As they neared their destination, Ya'aqub sent Yahudah ahead to meet Ya'asaf and get directions to the region of Gushan. And when they finally arrived there,
Ya'asaf prepared his chariot and traveled to Gushan to meet his father Ya'aqub, when Ya'asaf arrived, he embraced his father and wept, holding him for a long time.
Finally, Ya'aqub said to Ya'asaf, “Now I am ready to die, since I have seen your face again and know you are still alive.”
And Ya'asaf said to his brothers and to his father’s entire family, “I will go to Phar'uh and tell him, ‘My brothers and my father’s entire family have come to me from the land of Canaan.
These men are shepherds, and they raise livestock. They have brought with them their flocks and herds and everything they own.’”
Then he said, “When Phar'uh calls for you and asks you about your occupation,

You must tell him, ‘We, your servants, have raised livestock all our lives, as our ancestors have always done.’ When you tell him this, he will let you live here in the region of Gushan, for the Mitzraym despise shepherds.”

Then Ya'asaf went to see Phar'uh and told him, “My father and my brothers have arrived from the land of Canaan. They have come with all their flocks and herds and possessions, and they are now in the region of Gushan.”
Ya'asaf took five of his brothers with him and presented them to Phar'uh.
And Phar'uh asked the brothers, “What is your occupation?” They replied, “We, your servants, are shepherds, just like our ancestors.

We have come to live here in Mitzraym for a while, for there is no pasture for our flocks in Canaan. The famine is very severe there. So please, we request permission to live in the region of Gushan.”
Then Phar'uh said to Ya'asaf, “Now that your father and brothers have joined you here,

Choose any place in the entire land of Mitzraym for them to live. Give them the best land of Mitzraym. Let them live in the region of Gushan. And if any of them have special skills, put them in charge of my livestock, too.”
Then Ya'asaf brought in his father, Ya'aqub, and presented him to Phar'uh. And Ya'aqub Baraked Phar'uh.
“How old are you?” Phar'uh asked him.
Ya'aqub replied, “I have traveled this Arath for 130 hard years. But my life has been short compared to the lives of my Fathers.”
Then Ya'aqub Baraked Phar'uh again before leaving his court.
So Ya'asaf assigned the best land of Mitzraym, the region of Ramasas to his father and his brothers, and he settled them there, just as Phar'uh had commanded.
And Ya'asaf provided food for his father and his brothers in amounts appropriate to the number of their dependents, including the smallest children.
Meanwhile, the famine became so severe that all the food was used up, and people were starving throughout the lands of Mitzraym and Canaan.
By selling grain to the people, Ya'asaf eventually collected all the money in Mitzraym and Canaan, and he put the money in Phar'uh’s treasury.
When the people of Mitzraym and Canaan ran out of money, all the Mitzraym came to Ya'asaf. “Our money is gone!” they cried. “But please give us food, or we will die before your very eyes!”
Ya'asaf replied, “Since your money is gone, bring me your livestock. I will give you food in exchange for your livestock.”

So they brought their livestock to Ya'asaf in exchange for food. In exchange for their horses, flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and donkeys, Ya'asaf provided them with food for another year.

But that year ended, and the next year they came again and said, “We cannot hide the truth from you, my master. Our money is gone, and all our livestock and cattle are yours. We have nothing left to give but our bodies and our land.

Why should we die before your very eyes? Buy us and our land in exchange for food; we offer our land and ourselves as slaves to Phar'uh. Just give us grain so we may live and not die, and so the land does not become empty and desolate.”
So Ya'asaf bought all the land of Mitzraym for Phar'uh. All the Mitzraym sold him their fields because the famine was so severe, and soon all the land belonged to Phar'uh.
As for the people, he made them all slaves, from one end of Mitzraym to the other.
The only land he did not buy was the land belonging to the priests. They received an allotment of food directly from Phar'uh, so they didn’t need to sell their land.
Then Ya'asaf said to the people, “Look, today I have bought you and your land for Phar'uh. I will provide you with seed so you can plant the fields.
Then when you harvest it, one-fifth of your crop will belong to Phar'uh. You may keep the remaining four-fifths as seed for your fields and as food for you, your households, and your little ones.”
“You have saved our lives!” they exclaimed. “May it please you, my master, to let us be Phar'uh’s servants.”

Ya'asaf then issued a decree still in effect in the land of Mitzraym, that Phar'uh should receive one-fifth of all the crops grown on his land. Only the land belonging to the priests was not given to Phar'uh.
Meanwhile, the people of YASHAR'AL settled in the region of Gushan in Mitzraym. There they acquired property, and they were fruitful, and their population grew rapidly.
Ya'aqub lived for seventeen years after his arrival in Mitzraym, so he lived 147 years in all.

As the time of his death drew near, Ya'aqub called for his son Ya'asaf and said to him, “Please do me this favor. Put your hand under my thigh and swear that you will treat me with unfailing love by honoring this last request: Do not bury me in Mitzraym.
When I die, please take my body out of Mitzraym and bury me with my Fathers.” So Ya'asaf promised, “I will do as you ask.”
“Swear that you will do it,” Ya'aqub insisted. So Ya'asaf gave his oath, and Ya'aqub bowed humbly at the head of his bed.
One day not long after this, word came to Ya'asaf, “Your father is failing rapidly.” So Ya'asaf went to visit his father, and he took with him his two sons, Manassah and Alphraim.
When Ya'asaf arrived, Ya'aqub was told, “Your son Ya'asaf has come to see you.” So Ya'aqub gathered his strength and sat up in his bed.
Ya'aqub said to Ya'asaf, “𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE) appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and Baraked me.

He said to me, ‘I will make you fruitful, and I will multiply your descendants. I will make you a multitude of nations. And I will give this land of Canaan to your descendants after you as an everlasting possession.’
“Now I am claiming as my own sons these two boys of yours, Alphraim and Manassah, who were born here in the land of Mitzraym before I arrived. They will be my sons, just as Rauban and Simaun are.
But any children born to you in the future will be your own, and they will inherit land within the territories of their brothers Alphraim and Manassah.

“Long ago, as I was returning from Paddan-aram, Rachal died in the land of Canaan. We were still on the way, some distance from Aphrath (that is, Bathlaham). So with great sorrow I buried her there beside the road to Aphrath.”
Then Ya'aqub looked over at the two boys. “Are these your sons?” he asked.
“Yes,” Ya'asaf told him, “these are the sons 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given me here in Mitzraym.” And Ya'aqub said, “Bring them closer to me, so I can Barak them.”
Ya'aqub was half blind because of his age and could hardly see. So Ya'asaf brought the boys close to him, and Ya'aqub kissed and embraced them.
Then Ya'aqub said to Ya'asaf, “I never thought I would see your face again, but now 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has let me see your children, too!”
Ya'asaf moved the boys, who were at their grandfather’s knees, and he bowed with his face to the ground.
Then he positioned the boys in front of Ya'aqub. With his right hand he directed Alphraim toward Ya'aqub’s left hand, and with his left hand he put Manassah at Ya'aqub’s right hand.

But Ya'aqub crossed his arms as he reached out to lay his hands on the boys’ heads. He put his right hand on the head of Alphraim, though he was the younger boy, and his left hand on the head of Manassah, though he was the firstborn.
Then he Baraked Ya'asaf and said, “May the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH before whom my grandfather Abraham and my father, Yachaq, walked, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who has been my shepherd all my life, to this very day,
The Malak who has redeemed me from all harm, may he barak these boys. May they preserve my name and the names of Abraham and Yachaq. And may their descendants multiply greatly throughout the Arath.”
But Ya'asaf was upset when he saw that his father placed his right hand on Alphraim’s head. So Ya'asaf lifted it to move it from Alphraim’s head to Manassah’s head.
“No, my father,” he said. “This one is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head.”

But his father refused. “I know, my son; I know,” he replied. “Manassah will also become a great people, but his younger brother will become even greater. And his descendants will become a multitude of nations.”

So Ya'aqub Baraked the boys that day with this Barakah: “The people of YASHAR'AL will use your names when they give a Barakah. They will say, ‘May 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH make you as prosperous as Alphraim and Manassah.’” In this way, Ya'aqub put Alphraim ahead of Manassah.
Then Ya'aqub said to Ya'asaf, “Look, I am about to die, but 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will be with you and will take you back to Canaan, the land of your ancestors.
And beyond what I have given your brothers, I am giving you an extra portion of the land that I took from the Amurites with my sword and bow.”
Then Ya'aqub called together all his sons and said, “Gather around me, and I will tell you what will happen to each of you in the days to come.
“Come and listen, you sons of Ya'aqub; listen to YASHAR'AL, your father.
“Rauban, you are my firstborn, my strength, the child of my vigorous youth. You are first in rank and first in power.
But you are as unruly as a flood, and you will be first no longer. For you went to bed with my wife; you defiled my marriage couch.
“Simaun and Lauy are two of a kind; their weapons are instruments of violence.
May I never join in their meetings; may I never be a party to their plans. For in their anger they murdered men, and they crippled oxen just for sport.
A curse on their anger, for it is fierce; a curse on their wrath, for it is cruel. I will scatter them among the descendants of Ya'aqub; I will disperse them throughout YASHAR'AL.
“Yahudah, your brothers will yadah you. You will grasp your enemies by the neck. All your relatives will bow before you.
Yahudah, my son, is a young lion that has finished eating its prey. Like a lion he crouches and lies down; like a lioness—who dares to rouse him?
The scepter will not depart from Yahudah, nor the ruler’s staff from his descendants, until the coming of the one to whom it belongs, the one whom all nations will honor.
He ties his foal to a grapevine, the colt of his donkey to a choice vine. He washes his clothes in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
“Zabulun will settle by the seashore and will be a harbor for ships; his borders will extend to Sidun.
“Issachar is a sturdy donkey, resting between two saddlepacks.
When he sees how good the countryside is and how pleasant the land, he will bend his shoulder to the load and submit himself to hard labor.
“Dan will govern his people, like any other tribe in YASHAR'AL.
Dan will be a snake beside the road, a poisonous viper along the path that bites the horse’s hooves so its rider is thrown off.
I trust in you for salvation, O 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH!
“Gad will be attacked by marauding bands, but he will attack them when they retreat.
“Ashar will dine on rich foods and produce food fit for kings.
“Naphtali is a doe set free that bears beautiful fawns.
Ya'asaf is the foal of a wild donkey, the foal of a wild donkey at a spring, one of the wild donkeys on the ridge.
Archers attacked him savagely; they shot at him and harassed him.
But his bow remained taut, and his arms were strengthened by the hands of the Mighty One of Ya'aqub, by the Shepherd, the Rock of YASHAR'AL.
May the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your father help you; may the AL'Mighty ONE Barak you with the Barakah of the Shamaym above, and Barakah of the watery depths below, and Barakah of the breasts and womb.
May my fatherly Barakah on you surpass the Barakah of my Fathers, reaching to the heights of the eternal hills. May these Barakah rest on the head of Ya'asaf, who is a prince among his brothers.
Banyamyn is a ravenous wolf, devouring his enemies in the morning and dividing his plunder in the evening.”
These are the twelve tribes of YASHAR'AL, and this is what their father said as he told his sons good-bye. He Baraked each one with an appropriate message.
Then Ya'aqub instructed them, “Soon I will die and join my ancestors. Bury me with my father and grandfather in the cave in the field of Aphrun the Hittite.
This is the cave in the field of Machpalah, near Mamra in Canaan, that Abraham bought from Aphrun the Hittite as a permanent burial site.
There Abraham and his wife Sarah are buried. There Yachaq and his wife, Rabakah, are buried. And there I buried La'ah.
It is the plot of land and the cave that my grandfather Abraham bought from the Hittites.”
When Ya'aqub had finished this charge to his sons, he drew his feet into the bed, breathed his last, and joined his fathers in death.
Ya'asaf threw himself on his father and wept over him and kissed him.
Then Ya'asaf told the physicians who served him to embalm his father’s body; so Ya'aqub was embalmed.
The embalming process took the usual forty days. And the Mitzraym mourned Ya'aqub‘s death for seventy days.
When the period of mourning was over, Ya'asaf approached Phar'uh’s advisers and said, “Please do me this favor and speak to Phar'uh on my behalf.

Tell him that my father made me swear an oath. He said to me, ‘Listen, I am about to die. Take my body back to the land of Canaan, and bury me in the tomb I prepared for myself.’ So please allow me to go and bury my father. After his burial, I will return without delay.”
Phar'uh agreed to Ya'asaf’s request. “Go and bury your father, as he made you promise,” Phar'uh said.
So Ya'asaf went up to bury his father, he was accompanied by all of Phar'uh’s officials, all the senior members of Phar'uh’s household, and all the senior officers of Mitzraym.
Ya'asaf also took his entire household and his brothers and their households. But they left their little children and flocks and herds in the land of Gushan.
A great number of chariots and charioteers accompanied Ya'asaf.
When they arrived at the threshing floor of Atad, near the Yurdan River, they held a very great and solemn memorial service, with a seven-day period of mourning for Ya'asaf’s father.

The local residents, the Canaanites, watched them mourning at the threshing floor of Atad. Then they renamed that place (which is near the Yurdan) Abal-mitzraym, for they said, “This is a place of deep mourning for these Mitzraym.”
So Ya'aqub’s sons did as he had commanded them.

They carried his body to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpalah, near Mamra. This is the cave that Abraham had bought as a permanent burial site from Aphrun the Hittite.
After burying Ya'aqub, Ya'asaf returned to Mitzraym with his brothers and all who had accompanied him to his father’s burial.
But now that their father was dead, Ya'asaf’s brothers became fearful. “Now Ya'asaf will show his anger and pay us back for all the wrong we did to him,” they said.
So they sent this message to Ya'asaf: “Before your father died, he instructed us

To say to you: ‘Please forgive your brothers for the great wrong they did to you—for their sin in treating you so cruelly.’ So we, the servants of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your father, beg you to forgive our sin.” When Ya'asaf received the message, he broke down and wept.
Then his brothers came and threw themselves down before Ya'asaf. “Look, we are your slaves!” they said.
But Ya'asaf replied, “Don’t be afraid of me. Am I 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, that I can punish you?
You intended to harm me, but 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH intended it all for good. 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH brought me to this position so I could save the lives of many people.
No, don’t be afraid. I will continue to take care of you and your children.” So Ya'asaf reassured his brothers by speaking kindly to them.
So Ya'asaf and his brothers and their families continued to live in Mitzraym. Ya'asaf lived to the age of one hundred and ten years.
He lived to see three generations of descendants of his son Alphraim, and he lived to see the birth of the children of Manassah’s son Makir, whom he claimed as his own.

“Soon I will die,” Ya'asaf told his brothers, “but 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will surely come to help you and lead you out of this land of Mitzraym. 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will bring you back to the land He solemnly promised to give to Abraham, to Yachaq, and to Ya'aqub.”
Then Ya'asaf made the sons of YASHAR'AL swear an oath, and he said, “When 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH comes to help you and lead you back, you must take my bones with you.”
So Ya'asaf died at the age of 110 years. The Mitzraym embalmed him, and his body was placed in a coffin in Mitzraym.

books.name: Exodus
chapters: These are the names of the sons of Yashar'AL (that is, Ya'aqub) who moved to Mitzraym with their father, each with his family:
Rauban, Simaun, La'uy, Yahudah,
Issachar, Zabulun, Banyamyn,
Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Ashar.
In all, Ya'aqub had seventy descendants in Mitzraym, including Ya'asaf, who was already there.
In time, Ya'asaf and all of his brothers died, ending that entire generation.
But their descendants, the Yasharalym had many children and grandchildren, infact they multiplied so greatly that they became extremely powerful and filled the land.
Eventually, a new king came to power in Mitzraym who knew nothing about Ya'asaf or what he had done.
He said to his people, “Look, the people of Yashar'AL now outnumber us and are stronger than we are.
We must make a plan to keep them from growing even more. If we don’t and if war breaks out, they will join our enemies and fight against us. Then they will escape from the country.”

So the Mitzraym made the Yasharalym their slaves, they appointed brutal slave drivers over them, hoping to wear them down with crushing labor, they forced them to build the cities of Pithum and Ramasas as supply centers for Phar'uh.
But the more the Mitzraym oppressed them, the more the Yasharalym multiplied and spread and the more alarmed the Mitzraym became.
So the Mitzraym put the people of Yashar'AL to worked without mercy.
They made their lives bitter, forcing them to mix mortar and make bricks and do all the work in the fields. They were ruthless in all their demands.
Then Phar'uh the king of Mitzraym, gave this order to the Abarym (Hebrew) midwives, Shiphrah and Puah:
“When you help the Abarym women as they give birth, watch as they deliver, if the baby is a boy kill him; if it is a girl let her live.”
But because the midwives feared 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, they refused to obey the king’s orders. They allowed the boys to live, too.
So the king of Mitzraym called for the midwives. “Why have you done this?” he demanded. “Why have you allowed the boys to live?”
“The Abarym (Hebrew) women are not like the Mitzraym women,” the midwives replied. “They are more vigorous and have their babies so quickly that we cannot get there in time.”
So 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was good to the midwives, and the Yasharalym continued to multiply, growing more and more powerful.
And because the midwives feared 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, He gave them families of their own.
Then Phar'uh gave this order to all his people: “Throw every newborn Abarym (Hebrew) boy into the Nile River. But you may let the girls live.”
About this time, a man and woman from the tribe of La'uy got married.
The woman became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She saw that he was a special baby and kept him hidden for three months.

But when she could no longer hide him, she got a basket made of papyrus reeds and waterproofed it with tar and pitch. She put the baby in the basket and laid it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile River.
The baby’s sister then stood at a distance, watching to see what would happen to him.
Soon Phar'uh’s daughter came down to bathe in the river and her attendants walked along the riverbank. When the princess saw the basket among the reeds, she sent her maid to get it for her.
When the Mitzrayim princess opened it, she saw the baby, the little boy was crying and she felt sorry for him. “This must be one of the Abarym (Hebrew) children,” she said.
Then the baby’s sister approached the Mitzraym princess. “Should I go and find one of the Abarym (Hebrew) women to nurse the baby for you?” she asked.
“Yes, do!” the princess replied. So the girl went and called the baby’s mother.
“Take this baby and nurse him for me,” the Mitzraym princess told the baby’s mother. “I will pay you for your help.” So the woman took her baby home and nursed him.

Later, when the boy was older, his mother brought him back to Phar'uh’s daughter, who adopted him as her own son. The Mitzraym princess named him Musha, for she explained, “I lifted him out of the water.”

Many years later, when Musha had grown up, he went out to visit his own people, the Abarym (Hebrews), and he saw how hard they were forced to work. During his visit, he saw a Mitzraym beating one of his fellow Abarym.
After looking in all directions to make sure no one was watching, Musha killed the Mitzraym and hid the body in the sand.
The next time, when Musha went out to visit his people again, he saw two Abarym (Hebrew) men fighting. “Why are you beating up your friend?” Musha said to the one who had started the fight.
The man replied, “Who appointed you to be our prince and judge? Are you going to kill me as you killed that Mitzraym yesterday?” Then Musha was afraid, thinking everyone knows what he did.”

And sure enough, Phar'uh heard what had happened and Phar'uh tried to kill Musha. But Musha fled from Pharuh and went to live in the land of Midian; When Musha arrived in Midian, he sat down beside a well.
Now the Kuhan (priest) of Midian had seven daughters who came as usual to draw water and fill the water troughs for their father’s flocks.
But some other shepherds came and chased them away, so Musha jumped up and rescued the girls from the shepherds, then he drew water for their flocks.
When the girls returned to Raual their father, he asked why are you back so soon today?”
“A Mitzraym man rescued us from the shepherds,” they answered, “and then he drew water for us and watered our flocks.”
“Then where is he?” their father asked. “Why did you leave him there? Invite him to come and eat with us.”
Musha accepted the invitation and he settled there with him. In time, Raual gave Musha his daughter Zippurah to be his wife.
Later she gave birth to a son and Musha named him Garshum, for he explained, “I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.”
Years passed and the king of Mitzraym died. But the Yasharalym continued to groan under their burden of slavery. They cried out for help and their cry rose up to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant promise to Abraham, Yachaq and Ya'aqub.
He looked down on the people of Yashar'AL and knew it was time to act.
One day Musha was tending the flock of his father-in-law Yathru the Kuhan of Midian, Musha led the flock far into the wilderness and came to Sinai, the mountain of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
There the Malak of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH appeared to Musha in a blazing fire from the middle of a bush. Musha stared in amazement. Though the bush was engulfed in flames, it didn’t burn up.
“This is amazing,” Musha said to himself. “Why isn’t that bush burning up? I must go see it.”
When 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH saw Musha coming to take a closer look, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Musha from the middle of the bush, “Musha! Musha! “Here I am!” Musha replied.
“Do not come any closer,” 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH warned. “Take off your sandals, for you are standing on Qadash ground.

I AM the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your father, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yachaq and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Ya'aqub.” When Musha heard this, he covered his face because he was afraid to look at 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH told Musha, “I have certainly seen the oppression of my people in Mitzraym, I have heard their cries of distress because of their harsh slave drivers. Yes, I AM aware of their suffering.

So I have come down to rescue them from the power of the Mitzraym and lead them out of Mitzraym into their own fertile and spacious land. It is a land flowing with milk and honey, the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amurites, Parizzites, Hiuites, and Yabusites now live.
Look! The cry of the people of Yashar'AL has reached me and I have seen how harshly the Mitzraym abuse them.
Now go, for I AM sending you to Phar'uh. You must lead my people the Yasharalym out of Mitzraym.”
But Musha protested to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, “Who am I to appear before Phar'uh? Who am I to lead the people of Yashar'AL out of Mitzraym?”

And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH answered, “I will be with you. And this is your sign that I am the one who has sent you: When you have brought the people out of Mitzraym, you will worship 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH at this very mountain.”
But Musha protested, “If I go to the people of Yashar'AL and tell them, ‘The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your ancestors has sent me to you,’ they will ask me, ‘What is his Name?’ Then what should I tell them?”
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH replied to Musha, “Ahayah (I AM who I AM). Say this to the people of Yashar'AL: Ahayah (I AM) has sent me to you.”

And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH also Dabar to Musha, “Say this to the people of Yashar'AL: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your ancestors, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yachaq and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Ya'aqub has sent me to you. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is my eternal NAME, my NAME to be remembered for all generations.

“Now go and call together all the elders of Yashar'AL, tell them 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your ancestors, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, Yachaq, and Ya'aqub has appeared to me. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told me, “I have been watching closely and I see how the Mitzraym are treating you.

I have promised to rescue you from your oppression in Mitzraym. I will lead you to a land flowing with milk and honey, the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amurites, Perizzites, Hibites, and Yabusites now live.”’

“The elders of Yashar'AL will accept your message. Then you and the elders must go to the king of Mitzraym and tell him, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Abarym (Hebrews), has met with us. So please let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.’
“But I know that the king of Mitzraym will not let you go unless a mighty hand forces him.
So I will raise my hand and strike the Mitzraym, performing all kinds of miracles among them. Then at last he will let you go.
And I will cause the Mitzraym to look favorably on you. They will give you gifts when you go so you will not leave empty-handed.

Every Yashar'AL woman will ask for articles of silver and gold and fine clothing from her Mitzraym neighbors and from the foreign women in their houses. You will dress your sons and daughters with these, stripping the Mitzraym of their wealth.”
But Musha protested again, “What if they won’t believe me or listen to me? What if they say, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH never appeared to you’?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH asked Musha, “What is that in your hand?” A shepherd’s staff,” Musha replied.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha throw the staff on the ground, So Musha threw down the staff and it turned into a snake! Musha jumped back.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told Musha, “Reach out and grab its tail.” So Musha reached out and grabbed it, and it turned back into a shepherd’s staff (Rod) in his hand.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha. with this sign “they will believe that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their ancestors, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yachaq and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Ya'aqub really has appeared to you.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to Musha, “Now put your hand inside your cloak.” So Musha put his hand inside his cloak, and when he took it out again, his hand was white as snow with a severe skin disease.
“Now put your hand back into your cloak,” So Musha put his hand back in and when he took it out again it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “If they do not believe you and are not convinced by the first miraculous sign, they will be convinced by the second sign.

And if they don’t believe you or listen to you even after these two signs, then take some water from the Nila River and pour it out on the dry ground. When you do, the water from the Nila will turn to blood on the ground.”
But Musha pleaded with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, I am not very good with words. I never have been and I am not now, even though you have spoken to me. I get tongue-tied and my words get tangled.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH asked Musha, “Who makes a man’s mouth? Who decides whether people speak or do not speak, who decides if someone to hear or not hear and to see or not see? Is it not I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?
Now go! I will be with you as you speak, and I will instruct you in what to say.”
But Musha again pleaded, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH please! Send anyone else.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH became angry with Musha. “All right, “What about your brother, Aarun the Lauym? I know he speaks well, and look! He is on his way to meet you now. He will be delighted to see you.
Talk to him and put the words in his mouth. I will be with both of you as you speak and I will instruct you both in what to do.
Aarun will be your spokesman to the people, he will be your mouthpiece and you Musha will stand in the place of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for him, telling him what to say.
And take your shepherd’s staff with you, and use it to perform the miraculous signs I have shown you.”
So Musha went back home to Yathru, his father-in-law. “Please let me return to my relatives in Mitzraym,” Musha said. “I don’t even know if they are still alive.” Go in Shalum,” Yathru replied.
Before Musha left Midian, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to him, “Return to Mitzraym, for all those who wanted to kill you have died.”
So Musha took his wife and sons, put them on a donkey and headed back to the land of Mitzraym. In his hand he carried the staff of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “When you arrive back in Mitzraym, go to Phar'uh and perform all the miracles I have empowered you to do, but I will harden his heart so he will refuse to let the people go.
Then you will tell him, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says: Yashar'AL is my firstborn son.
I commanded you, “Let my son go, so he can worship me.” But since you have refused, I will now kill your firstborn son!’”
On the way to Mitzraym, at a place where Musha and his family had stopped for the night, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH confronted him and was about to kill him.
But Musha’s wife, Zippurah, took a flint knife and circumcised her son. She touched his feet with the foreskin and said, “Now you are a bridegroom of blood to me.”
(When she said “a bridegroom of blood,” she was referring to the circumcision.) After that, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH left him alone.
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said to Aarun, “Go out into the wilderness to meet Musha.” So Aarun went and met Musha at the mountain of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and he embraced him.
Musha then told Aarun everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him to say. And he told him about the miraculous signs 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him to perform.
Then Musha and Aarun returned to Mitzraym and called all the elders of Yashar'AL together.
Aarun told them everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had told Musha and Musha performed the miraculous signs as they watched.

Then the people of Yashar'AL were convinced that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had sent Musha and Aarun. When they heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was concerned about them and had seen their misery, they bowed down and worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

After this presentation to Yasharalym leaders, Musha and Aarun went and spoke to Pharuh. They told him, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE) of Yashar'AL says: Let my people go so they may hold a festival in my honor in the wilderness.”
“Is that so?” retorted Phar'uh. “And who is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? Why should I listen to Him and let Yashar'AL go? I don’t know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and I will not let Yashar'AL go.”

But Aarun and Musha persisted. “The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Abarym (Hebrews) has met with us,” they declared. “So let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness so we can offer sacrifices to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. If we don’t, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will kill us with a plague or with the sword.”
Pharuh replied, “Musha and Aarun, why are you distracting the people from their tasks? Get back to work!
Look, there are many of your people in the land, and you are stopping them from their work.”
That same day Phar'uh sent this order to the Mitzraym slave drivers and the Yasharalym foremen:
“Do not supply any more straw for making bricks. Make the people get it themselves!
But still require them to make the same number of bricks as before. Don’t reduce the quota. They are lazy. That’s why they are crying out, ‘Let us go and offer sacrifices to our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.’
Load them down with more work. Make them sweat! That will teach them to not listen to the lies of Musha!”
So the slave drivers and foremen went out and told the people: “This is what Phar'uh says: I will not provide any more straw for you.
Go and get it yourselves. Find it wherever you can. But you must produce just as many bricks as before!”
So the people scattered throughout the land of Mitzraym in search of stubble to use as straw.
Meanwhile, the Mitzraym slave drivers continued to push hard. “Meet your daily quota of bricks, just as you did when we provided you with straw!” they demanded.
Then they whipped the Yasharalym foremen they had put in charge of the work crews. “Why haven’t you met your quotas either yesterday or today?” they demanded.
So the Yasharalym foremen went to Pharuh and pleaded with him. “Please don’t treat your servants like this,” they begged.
“We are given no straw, but the slave drivers still demand, ‘Make bricks!’ We are being beaten, but it is not our fault! Your own people are to blame!”
But Phar'uh shouted, “You are just lazy! Lazy! That’s why you are saying, ‘Let us go and offer sacrifices to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.’
Now get back to work! No straw will be given to you, but you must still produce the full quota of bricks.”
The Yasharalym foremen could see that they were in serious trouble when they were told, “You must not reduce the number of bricks you make each day.”
As they left Pharuh’s court, they confronted Musha and Aarun, who were waiting outside for them.
The foremen said to them, “May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH judge and punish you for making us stink before Phar'uh and his officials. You have put a sword into their hands, an excuse to kill us!”
Then Musha went back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and protested, “Why have you brought all this trouble on your own people? Why did you send me?
Ever since I came to Phar'uh as your spokesman, he has been even more brutal to your people, and you have done nothing to rescue them!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Now you will see what I will do to Phar'uh. When he feels the force of my strong hand, he will let the people go. In fact, he will force them to leave his land!”
And 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Musha, “I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’
I appeared to Abraham, to Yachaq and to Ya'aqub as AL-Shaddah, ‘𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE)’ but I did not reveal my Name 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 YAHUAH to them.
And I reaffirmed my covenant with them. Under its terms, I promised to give them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
You can be sure that I have heard the groans of the people of Yashar'AL, who are now slaves to the Mitzraym and I am well aware of my covenant with them.

“Therefore, say to the people of Yashar'AL: ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. I will free you from your oppression and will rescue you from your slavery in Mitzraym. I will redeem you with a powerful arm and great acts of judgment.
I will claim you as my own people and I will be your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Then you will know that I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who has freed you from your oppression in Mitzraym.
I will bring you into the land I swore to give to Abraham, Yachaq, and Ya'aqub. I will give it to you as your very own possession, I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH
So Musha told the people of Yashar'AL what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar, but they refused to listen anymore, They had become too discouraged by the brutality of their slavery.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Go back to Pharuh, the king of Mitzraym, and tell him to let the people of Yashar'AL leave his country.”
“But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!” Musha objected. “My own people won’t listen to me anymore. How can I expect Phar'uh to listen? I am such a clumsy speaker!”

But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH spoke to Musha and Aarun and gave them orders for the Yasharalym and for Pharuh, the king of Mitzraym, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded Musha and Aarun to lead the people of Yashar'AL out of Mitzraym.
These are the ancestors of some of the clans of Yashar'AL: The sons of Rauban, Yashar'AL’s oldest son, were Hanuch, Pallu, Hazrun and Carmi. Their descendants became the clans of Rauban.
The sons of Simaun were Yamual, Yamin, Uhad, Yakin, Zuhar and Shaul. (Shaul’s mother was a Canaanite woman.) Their descendants became the clans of Simaun.
These are the descendants of La'uy, as listed in their family records: The sons of La'uy were Garshum, Kuhath and Marari. (La'uy lived to be 137 years old.)
The descendants of Garshum included Libni and Shimai, each of whom became the ancestor of a clan.
The descendants of Kuhath included Amram, Izhar, Habrun and Uzzial. (Kuhath lived to be 133 years old.)
The descendants of Marari included Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Lauym, as listed in their family records.
Amram married his father’s sister Yuchabad and she gave birth to his sons, Aarun and Musha. (Amram lived to be 137 years old.)
The sons of Izhar were Kurah, Naphag and Zicri.
The sons of Uzzial were Mishaal, Alzaphan, and Sithri.
Aarun married Alishaba, the daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshun and she gave birth to his sons, Nadab, Abihu, Aleazar, and Ithamar.
The sons of Kurah were Assir, Alkanah and Abiasaph. Their descendants became the clans of Kurah.
Aleazar son of Aarun married one of the daughters of Putial, and she gave birth to his son, Phinahas. These are the ancestors of the Lauym (Levite) families, listed according to their clans.
The Aarun and Musha named in this list are the same ones to whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said, Lead the people of Yashar'AL out of the land of Mitzraym like an army.”
It was Musha and Aarun who spoke to Phar'uh, the king of Mitzraym, about leading the people of Yashar'AL out of Mitzraym.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH spoke to Musha in the land of Mitzraym,
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to Musha, “I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! Tell Phar'uh the king of Mitzraym everything I AM telling you.”
But Musha argued with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, saying, “I can’t do it! I am such a clumsy speaker! Why should Phar'uh listen to me?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Pay close attention to this. I will make you seem like Aluah to Pharuh, and your brother, Aarun, will be your Nabym (prophet).
Tell Aarun everything I command you, and Aarun must command Phar'uh to let the people of Yashar'AL leave his country.
But I will make Pharuh’s heart stubborn so I can multiply my miraculous signs and wonders in the land of Mitzraym.
Even then Phar'uh will refuse to listen to you. So I will bring down my fist on Mitzraym. Then I will rescue my people, the Yasharalym from the land of Mitzraym with great acts of judgment.
When I raise my powerful hand and bring out the Yasharalym, the Mitzraym will know that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So Musha and Aarun did just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded them.
Musha was eighty years old and Aarun was eighty-three when they made their demands to Phar'uh.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha and Aarun,
“Pharuh will demand, ‘Show me a miracle.’ When he does this, say to Aarun, ‘Take your staff and throw it down in front of Phar'uh, and it will become a serpent.’”
So Musha and Aarun went to Phar'uh and did what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded them. Aarun threw down his staff before Phar'uh and his officials and it became a serpent!
Then Phar'uh called in his own wise men and sorcerers and these Mitzraym magicians did the same thing with their magic.
They threw down their staffs, which also became serpents! But then Aarun’s staff swallowed up their staffs.
Pharuh’s heart, however remained hard, he still refused to listen, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Pharuh’s heart is stubborn and he still refuses to let the people go.
So go to Pharuh in the morning as he goes down to the river, stand on the bank of the Nile and meet him there. Be sure to take along the staff that turned into a snake.

Then announce to Pharuh, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Abarym (Hebrews), has sent me to tell you, “Let my people go, so they can worship me in the wilderness.” Until now, you have refused to listen to him.
So this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says: “I will show you that I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” Look! I will strike the water of the Nile with this staff in my hand and the river will turn to blood.
The fish in it will die, and the river will stink. The Mitzraym will not be able to drink any water from the Nile.’”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha: “Tell Aarun, ‘Take your staff and raise your hand over the waters of Mitzraym all its rivers, canals, ponds, and all the reservoirs. Turn all the water to blood. Everywhere in Mitzraym the water will turn to blood, even the water stored in wooden bowls and stone pots.’”

So Musha and Aarun did just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded them. As Phar'uh and all of his officials watched, Aarun raised his staff and struck the water of the Nile. Suddenly the whole river turned to blood!
The fish in the river died and the water became so foul that the Mitzraym could not drink it. There was blood everywhere throughout the land of Mitzraym.
But again the magicians of Mitzraym used their magic and they too turned water into blood. So Pharuh’s heart remained hard, he refused to listen to Musha and Aarun, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said.
Phar'uh returned to his palace and put the whole thing out of his mind.
Then all the Mitzraym dug along the riverbank to find drinking water, for they couldn’t drink the water from the Nile.
Seven days passed from the time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck the Nile.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Go back to Phar'uh and announce to him, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says: Let my people go, so they can worship me.
If you refuse to let them go, I will send a plague of frogs across your entire land.

The Nila River will swarm with frogs. They will come up out of the river and into your palace, even into your bedroom and onto your bed! They will enter the houses of your officials and your people. They will even jump into your ovens and your kneading bowls.
Frogs will jump on you, your people and all your officials.’”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Tell Aarun, ‘Raise the staff in your hand over all the rivers, canals and ponds of Mitzraym and bring up frogs over all the land.’”
So Aarun raised his hand over the waters of Mitzraym and frogs came up and covered the whole land!
But the magicians were able to do the same thing with their magic. They too, caused frogs to come up on the land of Mitzraym.
Then Phar'uh summoned Musha and Aarun and begged, “Plead with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to take the frogs away from me and my people. I will let your people go, so they can offer sacrifices to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”

“You set the time!” Musha replied. “Tell me when you want me to pray for you, your officials and your people. Then you and your houses will be rid of the frogs. They will remain only in the Nila River.”
“And Phar'uh said Do it tomorrow, “All right,” Musha replied, “it will be as you have said. Then you will know that there is no one like 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
The frogs will leave you and your houses, your officials and your people. They will remain only in the Nila River.”
So Musha and Aarun left Pharuh’s palace, and Musha cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH about the frogs he had inflicted on Pharuh.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did just what Musha had said. The frogs in the houses, the courtyards and the fields all died.
The Mitzraym piled them into great heaps, and a terrible stench filled the land.
But when Pharuh saw that relief had come, he became stubborn, he refused to listen to Musha and Aarun, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Tell Aarun, ‘Raise your staff and strike the ground. The dust will turn into swarms of gnats throughout the land of Mitzraym.’”

So Musha and Aarun did just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded them. When Aarun raised his hand and struck the ground with his staff, gnats infested the entire land, covering the Mitzraym and their animals. All the dust in the land of Mitzraym turned into gnats.
Pharuh’s magicians tried to do the same thing with their secret arts, but this time they failed, and the gnats covered everyone, people and animals alike.
“This is the finger of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE)!” the magicians exclaimed to Phar'uh. But Pharuh’s heart remained hard. He wouldn’t listen to them, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said to Musha.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Get up early in the morning and stand in Pharuh’s way as he goes down to the river. Say to him, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says: Let my people go, so they can worship me.
If you refuse, then I will send swarms of flies on you, your officials, your people, and all the houses. The Mitzraym homes will be filled with flies and the ground will be covered with them.
But this time I will spare the region of Gushan, where my people live. No flies will be found there. Then you will know that I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and that I AM present even in the heart of your land.
I will make a clear distinction between My people and your people. This miraculous sign will happen tomorrow.’”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did just as He had said. A thick swarm of flies filled Pharuh’s palace and the houses of his officials. The whole land of Mitzraym was thrown into chaos by the flies.
Phar'uh called for Musha and Aarun. “All right! Go ahead and offer sacrifices to your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, “But do it here in this land.”

But Musha replied, “That would not be right. The Mitzraym detest the sacrifices that we offer to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Look, if we offer our sacrifices here where the Mitzraym can see us, they will stone us.
We must take a three-day trip into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, just as He has commanded us.”
“All right, go ahead,” Phar'uh replied. “I will let you go into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. But don’t go too far away. Now hurry and pray for me.”

Musha answered, “As soon as I leave you, I will pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and tomorrow the swarms of flies will disappear from you and your officials and all your people. But I am warning you Pharuh, don’t lie to us again and refuse to let the people go to sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So Musha left Pharuh’s palace and pleaded with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to remove all the flies.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did as Musha asked and caused the swarms of flies to disappear from Pharuh, his officials, and his people. Not a single fly remained.
But Pharuh again became stubborn and refused to let the people go.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded Musha. “ go tell Phar'uh, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Abarym (Hebrews), Dabar: Let my people go, so they can worship me.
If you continue to hold them and refuse to let them go,
The hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will strike all your livestock, your horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, sheep and goats with a deadly plague.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will again make a distinction between the livestock of the Yasharalym and that of the Mitzraym. Not a single one of Yashar'AL’s animals will die!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has already set the time for the plague to begin. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has declared that HE will strike the land tomorrow.’”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did just as HE had said. The next morning all the livestock of the Mitzraym died, but the Yasharalym didn’t lose a single animal.

Phar'uh sent his officials to investigate and they discovered that the Yasharalym had not lost a single animal! But even so, Pharuh’s heart remained stubborn and he still refused to let the people go.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha and Aarun, “Take handfuls of soot from a brick kiln and have Musha toss it into the air while Pharuh watches.
The ashes will spread like fine dust over the whole land of Mitzraym, causing festering boils to break out on people and animals throughout the land.”
So Musha and Aarun took soot from a brick kiln and went and stood before Pharuh. As Pharuh watched, Musha threw the soot into the air and boils broke out on people and animals alike.
Even the magicians were unable to stand before Musha, because the boils had broken out on them and all the Mitzraym.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH hardened Pharuh’s heart and just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar to Musha, Pharuh refused to listen.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Get up early in the morning and stand before Phar'uh tell him, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Abarym (Hebrews), says: Let my people go, so they can worship me.
If you do not, I will send more plagues on you and your officials and your people, then you will know that there is no one like me in all the Arath (earth).
By now I could have lifted my hand and struck you and your people with a plague to wipe you off the face of the Arath.
But I have spared you for a purpose, to show you my power and to spread my fame throughout the Arath.
But you still ruling over my people and refuse to let them go.
So tomorrow at this time I will send a hailstorm more devastating than any in all the history of Mitzraym.
Quick! Order your livestock and servants to come in from the fields to find shelter, any person or animal left outside will die when the hail falls.’”
Some of Pharuh’s officials were afraid because of what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar. They quickly brought their servants and livestock in from the fields.
But those who paid no attention to the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH left theirs out in the open.
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Dabar to Musha, “Lift your hand toward the sky so hail may fall on the people, the livestock, and all the plants throughout the land of Mitzraym.”
So Musha lifted his staff toward the sky, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent thunder and hail, and lightning flashed toward the Arath, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent a tremendous hailstorm against all the land of Mitzraym.
Never in all the history of Mitzraym had there been a storm like that, with such devastating hail and continuous lightning.
It left all of Mitzraym in ruins. The hail struck down everything in the open field, people, animals and plants alike. Even the trees were destroyed.
The only place without hail was the region of Gushan, where the people of Yashar'AL lived.
Then Phar'uh quickly summoned Musha and Aarun. “This time I have sinned,” he confessed. “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the righteous one and my people and I are wrong.
Please beg 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to end this terrifying thunder and hail, we have had enough, I will let you go; you do not need to stay any longer.”
“And Musha said all right, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my hands and pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, then the thunder and hail will stop and you will know that the Arath belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
But I know that you and your officials still do not fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.”
(All the flax and barley were ruined by the hail, because the barley had formed heads and the flax was budding.
But the wheat and the emmer wheat were spared, because they had not yet sprouted from the ground.)
So Musha left Pharuh’s court and went out of the city, when he lifted his hands to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the thunder and hail stopped, and the downpour ceased.
But when Pharuh saw that the rain, hail, and thunder had stopped, he and his officials sinned again and Pharuh again became stubborn.
Because his heart was hard, Phar'uh refused to let the people leave, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar to Musha.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Return to Phar'uh and make your demands again. I have made him and his officials stubborn so I can display my miraculous signs among them.
I have also done it so you can tell your children and grandchildren about how I made a mockery of the Mitzraym and about the signs I displayed among them and so you will know that I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”

So Musha and Aarun went to Phar'uh and said, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Abarym (Hebrews), Dabar: How long will you refuse to submit to me? Let my people go, so they can worship me.
If you refuse, watch out! For tomorrow I will bring a swarm of locusts on your country.
They will cover the land so that you won’t be able to see the ground. They will devour what little is left of your crops after the hailstorm, including all the trees growing in the fields.

They will overrun your palaces and the homes of your officials and all the houses in Mitzraym. Never in the history of Mitzraym have your ancestors seen a plague like this one!” And with that, Musha turned and left Phar'uh.
So Musha and Aarun were brought back to Phar'uh. “All right,” he told them, “go and worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, But who exactly will be going with you?”
Musha replied, “We will all go—young and old, our sons and daughters and our flocks and herds. We must all join together in celebrating a festival to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Pharuh retorted, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will certainly need to be with you if I let you take your little ones! I can see through your evil plan.
Never! Only the men may go and worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, since that is what you requested.” And Phar'uh threw them out of the palace.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Raise your hand over the land of Mitzraym to bring on the locusts. Let them cover the land and devour every plant that survived the hailstorm.”
So Musha raised his staff over Mitzraym, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH caused an east wind to blow over the land all that day and through the night. When morning arrived, the east wind had brought the locusts.

And the locusts swarmed over the whole land of Mitzraym, settling in dense swarms from one end of the country to the other. It was the worst locust plague in Mitzraym history and there has never been another one like it.

For the locusts covered the whole country and darkened the land. They devoured every plant in the fields and all the fruit on the trees that had survived the hailstorm. Not a single leaf was left on the trees and plants throughout the land of Mitzraym.
Phar'uh quickly summoned Musha and Aarun. “I have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and against you,” he confessed.
“Forgive my sin, just this once and plead with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH to take away this death from me.”
So Musha left Pharuh’s court and pleaded with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH responded by shifting the wind and the strong west wind blew the locusts into the Red Sea. Not a single locust remained in all the land of Mitzraym.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH hardened Pharuh’s heart again, so he refused to let the people go.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to Musha, “Lift your hand toward Shamaym, and the land of Mitzraym will be covered with a darkness so thick you can feel it.”
So Musha lifted his hand to the sky, and a deep darkness covered the entire land of Mitzraym for three days.
During all that time the people could not see each other and no one moved. But there was light as usual where the people of Yashar'AL lived.
Finally, Pharuh called for Musha. “Go and worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,” he said. “But leave your flocks and herds here. You may even take your little ones with you.”
“No,” Musha said, “you must provide us with animals for sacrifices and burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

All our livestock must go with us, too; not a hoof can be left behind. We must choose our sacrifices for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH from among these animals. And we won’t know how we are to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH until we get there.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH hardened Pharuh’s heart once more and he would not let them go.
“Get out of here!” Phar'uh shouted at Musha. “I’m warning you. Never come back to see me again! The day you see my face, you will die!”
“Very well,” Musha replied. “I will never see your face again.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “I will strike Phar'uh and the land of Mitzraym with one more blow. After that, Phar'uh will let you leave this country. In fact, he will be so eager to get rid of you that he will force you all to leave.
Tell all the Yasharalym men and women to ask their Mitzraym neighbors for articles of silver and gold.”

Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had caused the Mitzraym to look favorably on the people of Yashar'AL. And Musha was considered a very great man in the land of Mitzraym, respected by Pharuh’s officials and the Mitzraym people alike.
Musha had announced to Pharuh, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: At midnight tonight I will pass through the heart of Mitzraym.

All the firstborn sons will die in every family in Mitzraym, from the oldest son of Pharuh, who sits on his throne, to the oldest son of his lowliest maidservant who grinds the flour. Even the firstborn of all the livestock will die.
Then a loud wail will rise throughout the land of Mitzraym, a wail like no one has heard before or will ever hear again.
But among the Yasharalym it will be of Shalum that not even a dog will bark. Then you will know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH makes a distinction between the Mitzraym and the Yasharalym.

All the officials of Mitzraym will run to me and fall to the ground before me. ‘Please leave!’ they will beg. ‘Hurry! And take all your followers with you.’ Only then will I go!” Then, burning with anger, Musha left Phar'uh.
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had told Musha earlier, “Pharuh will not listen to you, but then I will do even more mighty miracles in the land of Mitzraym.”
Musha and Aarun performed these miracles in Pharuh’s presence, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH hardened Pharuh’s heart, and he wouldn’t let the Yasharalym leave the country.
While the Yasharalym were still in the land of Mitzraym, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar the following instructions to Musha and Aarun:
“From now on, this Moon (month) will be the first Moon (month) of the year for you.
