Announce to the whole community of Yashar'AL that on the tenth day of this Moon each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for a sacrifice, one animal for each household.
If a family is too small to eat a whole animal, let them share with another family in the neighborhood. Divide the animal according to the size of each family and how much they can eat.
The animal you select must be a one-year-old male, either a sheep or a goat, with no defects.

“Take special care of this chosen animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of this first Moon (month). Then the whole assembly of the community of Yashar'AL must slaughter their lamb or young goat in evening.
They are to take some of the blood and smear it on the sides and top of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the animal.
That same night they must roast the meat over a fire and eat it along with bitter salad greens and bread made without yeast.
Do not eat any of the meat raw or boiled in water. The whole animal including the head, legs, and internal organs must be roasted over a fire.
Do not leave any of it until the next morning. Burn whatever is not eaten before morning.

“These are your instructions for eating this meal: Be fully dressed, wear your sandals, and carry your walking stick in your hand. Eat the meal with urgency, for this is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Passak (Passover).

On that night I will pass through the land of Mitzraym and strike down every firstborn son and firstborn male animal in the land of Mitzraym. I will execute judgment against all the idols of Mitzraym, for I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH

But the blood on your doorposts will serve as a sign, marking the houses where you are staying. When I see the blood, I will pass over you. This plague of death will not touch you when I strike the land of Mitzraym.
“This is a day to remember. Each year, from generation to generation, you must celebrate it as a special festival to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. This is a law for all time.

For seven days the bread you eat must be made without yeast. On the first day of the festival, remove every trace of yeast from your homes. Anyone who eats bread made with yeast during the seven days of the festival will be cut off from the community of Yashar'AL.

On the first day of the festival and again on the seventh day, all the people must observe an official day for Qadash assembly. No work of any kind may be done on these days except in the preparation of food.

“Celebrate this Festival of Unleavened Bread, for it will remind you that I brought your forces out of the land of Mitzraym on this very day. This festival will be a permanent law for you; celebrate this day from generation to generation.
The bread you eat must be made without yeast from the evening of the fourteenth day of the first Moon (month) until the evening of the twenty-first day of that Moon (month).

During those seven days, there must be no trace of yeast in your homes. Anyone who eats anything made with yeast during this week will be cut off from the community of Yashar'AL. These regulations apply both to the foreigners living among you and to the native-born Yashar'AL.
During those days you must not eat anything made with yeast. Wherever you live, eat only bread made without yeast.”
Then Musha called all the elders of Yashar'AL together and said to them, “Go, pick out a lamb or young goat for each of your families and slaughter the Pasakh (Passover) animal.

Drain the blood into a basin. Then take a bundle of hyssop branches and dip it into the blood. Brush the hyssop across the top and sides of the doorframes of your houses. And no one may go out through the door until morning.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will pass through the land to strike down the Mitzraym. But when He sees the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will pass over your home. He will not permit the Malak of death to enter your house and strike you down.
“Remember, these instructions are a permanent law that you and your descendants must observe forever.
When you enter the land 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has promised to give you, you will continue to observe this ceremony.
Then your children will ask, ‘What does this ceremony mean?’

And you will reply, ‘It is the Pasakh (Passover) sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for HE passed over the houses of the Yasharalym in Mitzraym. And though HE struck the Mitzraym, HE spared our families.’” When Musha had finished speaking, all the people bowed down to the ground and worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE)
So the people of Yashar'AL did just as 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had commanded through Musha and Aarun.

And that night at midnight 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck down all the firstborn sons in the land of Mitzraym, from the firstborn son of Pharuh, who sat on his throne, to the firstborn son of the prisoner in the dungeon. Even the firstborn of their livestock were killed.

Pharuh and all his officials and all the people of Mitzraym woke up during the night, and loud wailing was heard throughout the land of Mitzraym. There was not a single house where someone had not died.
Pharuh sent for Musha and Aarun during the night. “Get out!” he ordered. “Leave my people and take the rest of the Yasharalym with you! Go and worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as you have requested.
Take your flocks and herds, as you said and be gone. Go, but Barak me as you leave.”
All the Mitzraym urged the people of Yashar'AL to get out of the land as quickly as possible, for they thought, “We will all die!”
The Yasharalym took their bread dough without yeast, they wrapped their kneading boards in their cloaks and carried them on their shoulders.
And the people of Yashar'AL did as Musha had instructed; they asked the Mitzraym for clothing and articles of silver and gold.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH caused the Mitzraym to look favorably on the Yasharalym and they gave the Yasharalym whatever they asked for. So they stripped the Mitzraym of their wealth!
That night the people of Yashar'AL left Ramasas and started for Succuth. There were about 600,000 men, plus all the women and children.
A mix multitude of non-Yashar'AL went with them, along with great flocks and herds of livestock.

For bread they baked flat cakes from the dough without yeast they had brought from Mitzraym. It was made without yeast because the people were driven out of Mitzraym in such a hurry that they had no time to prepare the bread or other food.
The people of Yashar'AL had lived in Mitzraym for 430 years.
In fact, it was on the last day of the 430th year that all 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s forces left the land.

On this night 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH kept HIS promise to bring HIS people out of the land of Mitzraym. So this night belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and it must be commemorated every year by all the Yasharalym, from generation to generation.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha and Aarun, “These are the instructions for the festival of Passak (Passover). No outsiders are allowed to eat the Passak meal.
But any slave who has been purchased may eat it if he has been circumcised.
Temporary residents and hired servants may not eat it.
Each Passak lamb must be eaten in one house. Do not carry any of its meat outside, and do not break any of its bones.
The whole community of Yashar'AL must celebrate this Passak (Passover) festival.

“If there are foreigners living among you who want to celebrate 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Passak, let all their males be circumcised. Only then may they celebrate the Passak with you like any native-born Yashar'AL. But no uncircumcised male may ever eat the Passak meal.
This instruction applies to everyone, whether a native-born Yasharalym or a foreigner living among you.”
So all the people of Yashar'AL followed all 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s commands to Musha and Aarun.
On that very day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought the people of Yashar'AL out of the land of Mitzraym like an army.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Dedicate to me every firstborn among the Yasharalym. The first offspring to be born, of both man and animals belongs to me.”

So Musha said to the people, “This is a day to remember forever, the day you left Mitzraym the place of your slavery. Today 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought you out by the power of His mighty hand. (Remember, eat no food containing yeast.)
On this day in early spring, in the month of Abib, you have been set free.

You must celebrate this event in this month each year after 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amurites, Hibites, and Yabusites. (𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH swore to your ancestors that HE would give you this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.)
For seven days the bread you eat must be made without yeast. Then on the seventh day, celebrate a feast to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Eat bread without yeast during those seven days. In fact, there must be no yeast bread or any yeast at all found within the borders of your land during this time.
“On the seventh day you must explain to your children, ‘I am celebrating what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did for me when I left Mitzraym.’

This annual festival will be a visible sign to you, like a mark branded on your hand or your forehead. Let it remind you always to recite this teaching of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘With a strong hand, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rescued you from Mitzraym.’
So observe the decree of this festival at the appointed time each year.
“This is what you must do when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH fulfills the promise HE swore to you and to your ancestors. When HE gives you the land where the Canaanites now live,
you must present all firstborn sons and firstborn male animals to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for they belong to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

A firstborn donkey may be bought back from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by presenting a lamb or young goat in its place. But if you do not buy it back, you must break its neck. However you must buy back every firstborn son.

“And in the future, your children will ask you, ‘What does all this mean?’ Then you will tell them, ‘With the power of ALUAH's mighty hand, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought us out of Mitzraym, the place of our slavery.

Phar'uh stubbornly refused to let us go, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH killed all the firstborn males throughout the land of Mitzraym, both people and animals. That is why I now sacrifice all the firstborn males to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, except that the firstborn sons are always bought back.’
This ceremony will be like a mark branded on your hand or your forehead. It is a reminder that the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s mighty hand brought us out of Mitzraym.”

When Pharuh finally let the people go, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did not lead them along the main road that runs through Philistine territory, even though that was the shortest route to the Promised Land. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said, “If the people are faced with a battle, they might change their minds and return to Mitzraym.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH led them in a roundabout way through the wilderness toward the Red Sea. Thus the Yasharalym left Mitzraym like an army ready for battle.

Musha took the bones of Ya'asaf with him, for Ya'asaf had made the sons of Yashar'AL swear to do this. He said, “𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will certainly come to help you. When he does, you must take my bones with you from this place.”
The Yasharalym left Succuth and camped at Atham on the edge of the wilderness.
For 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH went ahead of them. HE guided them during the day with a pillar of cloud and HE provided light at night with a pillar of fire. This allowed them to travel by day or by night.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did not remove the pillar of cloud or pillar of fire from its place in front of the people.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave these instructions to Musha:
“Order the Yasharalym to turn back and camp by Pi-hahiruth between Migdul and the sea. Camp there along the shore, across from Baal-zaphun.
Then Pharuh will think, ‘The Yasharalym are confused. They are trapped in the wilderness!’

And once again I will harden Pharuh’s heart, and he will chase after you. I have planned this in order to display my Kabad (Esteemed) through Pharuh and his whole army. After this the Mitzraym will know that I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!” So the Yasharalym camped there as they were told.
When word reached the king of Mitzraym that the Yasharalym had fled, Phar'uh and his officials changed their minds. “What have we done, letting all those Yasharalym slaves get away?” they asked.
So Pharuh harnessed his chariot and called up his troops.
He took with him 600 of Mitzraym best chariots, along with the rest of the chariots of Mitzraym, each with its commander.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH hardened the heart of Pharuh the king of Mitzraym, so he chased after the people of Yashar'AL, who had left with fists raised in defiance.

The Mitzraym chased after them with all the forces in Pharuh’s army all his horses and chariots, his charioteers and his troops. The Mitzraym caught up with the people of Yashar'AL as they were camped beside the shore near Pi-hahiruth, across from Baal-zaphun.
As Pharuh approached, the people of Yashar'AL looked up and panicked when they saw the Mitzraym overtaking them. They cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
And they said to Musha, “Why did you bring us out here to die in the wilderness? Weren’t there enough graves for us in Mitzraym? What have you done to us? Why did you make us leave Mitzraym?

Did we not tell you this would happen while we were still in Mitzraym? We said, ‘Leave us alone! Let us be slaves to the Mitzraym. It is better to be a slave in Mitzraym than a corpse in the wilderness!’
But Musha told the people, “Do not be afraid. Just stand still and watch 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rescue you today. The Mitzraym you see today, you will never see them again.
See 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH himself will fight for you. Just stay calm.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Why are you crying out to me? Tell the people to get moving!
Pick up your staff and raise your hand over the sea. Divide the water so the Yashar'AL can walk through the middle of the sea on dry ground.
And I will harden the hearts of the Mitzraym and they will charge in after the Yasharalym. My great Kabad will be displayed through Phar'uh and his troops, his chariots, and his charioteers.
When my Kabad is displayed through them, all Mitzraym will see my Kabad and know that I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
Then the Malak of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who had been leading the people of Yashar'AL, moved to the rear of the camp. The pillar of cloud also moved from the front and stood behind them.
The cloud settled between the Mitzraym and Yasharalym camps. As darkness fell, the cloud turned to fire, lighting up the night. But the Mitzraym and Yasharalym did not approach each other all night.
Then Musha raised his hand over the sea, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH opened up a path through the water with a strong east wind. The wind blew all that night, turning the Yam (sea) into dry land.
So the people of Yashar'AL walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on each side!
Then the Mitzraym all of Pharuh’s horses, chariots and charioteers chased them into the middle of the sea.
But just before dawn 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH looked down on the Mitzraym army from the pillar of fire and cloud and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH threw their forces into total confusion.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH twisted their chariot wheels, making their chariots difficult to drive. “Let’s get out of here away from these Yasharalym!” the Mitzraym shouted. “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is fighting for them against Mitzraym!”

When all the Yasharalym had reached the other side, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Raise your hand over the sea again. Then the waters will rush back and cover the Mitzraym and their chariots and charioteers.”
So as the sun began to rise, Musha raised his hand over the sea and the water rushed back into its usual place. The Mitzraym tried to escape, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH swept them into the sea.
Then the waters returned and covered all the chariots and charioteers the entire army of Pharuh. Of all the Mitzraym who had chased the Yasharalym into the sea, not a single one survived.
But the people of Yashar'AL had walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground, as the water stood up like a wall on both sides.
That is how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rescued Yashar'AL from the hand of the Mitzraym that day. And the Yasharalym saw the bodies of the Mitzraym washed up on the seashore.

When the people of Yashar'AL saw the mighty power that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had unleashed against the Mitzraym, they were filled with awe before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. They put their Amunah (faith) in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and in HIS servant Musha.

Then Musha and the people of Yashar'AL sang this song to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: “I will sing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has triumphed Wonderfully, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has hurled both horse and rider into the Yam (sea).

The AL'Mighty 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is my strength and my song; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given me victory. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and I will Yadah (Praise) 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my father’s 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and I will exalt 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
AL'Mighty 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is a warrior; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is HIS NAME!
Pharuh’s chariots and army 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has hurled into the Yam (sea). The finest of Pharuh’s officers are drowned in the Red Sea.
The deep waters gushed over them; they sank to the bottom like a stone.
“Your right hand, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is Wonderful in power. Your right hand, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH smashes the enemy.
In the greatness of your majesty, You overthrow those who rise against You. For You unleash your blazing fury; it consumes them like straw.
At the blast of your breath, the waters piled up! The surging waters stood straight like a wall; in the heart of the Yam (sea) the deep waters became hard.
“The enemy boasted, ‘I will chase them and catch up with them. I will plunder them and consume them. I will flash my sword; my powerful hand will destroy them.’
But You blew with your breath and the Yam (sea) covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
No one is like You in the Shamaym and in the Arath, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, You are wonderful and Qadash, awesome in splendor, performing great wonders?
You raised your right hand and the Arath (earth) swallowed our enemies.
“With your unfailing love You lead the people You have redeemed. In your Might, you guide them to your sacred home.
The peoples hear and tremble; anguish grips those who live in Philistia.
The leaders of Adum are terrified; the nobles of Muab tremble. All who live in Canaan melt away;
Terror and dread fall upon them. The power of your arm makes them lifeless as stone until your people pass by, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, until the people you purchased pass by.
You will bring them in and plant them on your own mountain the place, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, reserved for your own dwelling the sanctuary, AL'Mighty 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, that your hands have established.
AL'Mighty 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will reign forever and ever!”

When Pharuh’s horses, chariots and charioteers rushed into the sea, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought the water crashing down on them. But the people of Yashar'AL had walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground!
Then Miryam the Nabym, Aarun’s sister, took a tambourine and led all the women as they played their tambourines and danced.
And Miryam sang this song: “Sing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has triumphed Wonderfully He has hurled both horse and rider into the sea.”
Then Musha led the people of Yashar'AL away from the Red Sea, and they moved out into the desert of Shur. They traveled in this desert for three days without finding any water.
When they came to the oasis of Marah, the water was too bitter to drink. So they called the place Marah (which means “bitter”).
Then the people complained and turned against Musha. “What are we going to drink?” they demanded.

So Musha cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for help and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH showed him a piece of wood. Musha threw it into the water and this made the water good to drink. It was there at Marah that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH set before them the following decree as a standard to test their Amunah (faithfulness) to Him.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said, “If you will listen carefully to the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and do what is right in His sight, obeying HIS commands and keeping all HIS decrees, then I will not make you suffer any of the diseases I sent on the Mitzraym; for I AM the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who heals you.”
After leaving Marah, the Yasharalym traveled on to the oasis of Alim, where they found twelve springs and seventy palm trees. They camped there beside the water.

Then the whole community of Yashar'AL set out from Alim and journeyed into the wilderness of Sin, between Alim and Mount Sinai. They arrived there on the fifteenth day of the second month, one month after leaving the land of Mitzraym.
There too, the whole community of Yashar'AL complained about Musha and Aarun.

“If only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had killed us back in Mitzraym,” they moaned. “There we sat around pots filled with meat and ate all the bread we wanted. But now you have brought us into this wilderness to starve us all to death.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Look, I AM going to rain down food from Shamaym for you. Each day the people can go out and pick up as much food as they need for that day. I will test them in this to see whether or not they will follow my instructions.
On the sixth day they will gather food and when they prepare it, there will be twice as much as usual.”
So Musha and Aaron said to all the people of Yashar'AL, “By evening you will realize it was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who brought you out of the land of Mitzraym.
In the morning you will see the Kabad of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has heard your complaints which are against Him, not against us. What have we done that you should complain about us?”

Then Musha added, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give you meat to eat in the evening and bread to satisfy you in the morning, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has heard all your complaints against Him. What have we done? Yes your complaints are against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, not against us.”
Then Musha said to Aarun, “Announce this to the entire community of Yashar'AL: ‘Present yourselves before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has heard your complaining.’”
And as Aarun spoke to the whole community of Yashar'AL, they looked out toward the wilderness. There they could see the awesome Kabad of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the cloud.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,

“I have heard the Yasharalym’ complaints. Now tell them, ‘In the evening you will have meat to eat and in the morning you will have all the bread you want. Then you will know that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
That evening vast numbers of quail flew in and covered the camp. And the next morning the area around the camp was wet with dew.
When the dew evaporated, a flaky substance as fine as frost blanketed the ground.
The Yasharalym were puzzled when they saw it. “What is it?” they asked each other. They had no idea what it was. And Musha told them, “It is the food 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you to eat.
These are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s instructions: Each household should gather as much as it needs. Pick up two quarts for each person in your tent.”
So the people of Yashar'AL did as they were told. Some gathered a lot, some only a little.
But when they measured it out, everyone had just enough. Those who gathered a lot had nothing left over and those who gathered only a little had enough. Each family had just what it needed.
Then Musha told them, “Do not keep any of it until morning.”
But some of them did not listen and kept some of it until morning. But by then it was full of maggots and had a terrible smell. Musha was very angry with them.
After this the people gathered the food morning by morning, each family according to its need. And as the sun became hot, the flakes they had not picked up melted and disappeared.
On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much as usual, four quarts for each person instead of two. Then all the leaders of the community came and asked Musha for an explanation.

Musha told the Yasharalym, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded: Tomorrow will be a day of complete rest, a Qadash Shabbat day set apart for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. So bake or boil as much as you want today, and set aside what is left for tomorrow.”
So they put some aside until morning, just as Musha had commanded. And in the morning the leftover food was wholesome and good, without maggots or odor.
Musha said, “Eat this food today, for today is a Shabbat day dedicated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, There will be no food on the ground today.
You may gather the food for six days, but the seventh day is the Shabbat. There will be no food on the ground that day.”
Some of the people went out anyway on the seventh day, but they found no food.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH asked Musha, “How long will these people refuse to obey my commands and instructions?

They must realize that the Shabbat is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s gift to you. That is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives you a two-day supply on the sixth day, so there will be enough for two days. On the Shabbat day you must each stay in your place. Do not go out to pick up food on the seventh day.”
So the people did not gather any food on the seventh day.
The Yasharalym called the food manna. It was white like coriander seed and it tasted like honey wafers.

Then Musha said, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded: Fill a two-quart container with manna to preserve it for your descendants. Then later generations will be able to see the food I gave you in the wilderness when I set you free from Mitzraym.”
Musha said to Aarun, “Get a jar and fill it with two quarts of manna. Then put it in a sacred place before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to preserve it for all future generations.”
Aarun did just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha. He eventually placed it in the Ark of the Covenant in front of the stone tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant.
So the people of Yashar'AL ate manna for forty years until they arrived at the land where they would settle. They ate manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.
The container used to measure the manna was an omer, which was one-tenth of an ephah; it held about two quarts.

At 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command, the whole community of Yashar'AL left the wilderness of Sin and moved from place to place. Eventually they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water there for the people to drink.
So once more the people complained against Musha. “Give us water to drink!” they demanded. Musha replied, “Why are you complaining against me? And why are you testing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?”
But tormented by thirst, they continued to argue with Musha. “Why did you bring us out of Mitzraym? Are you trying to kill us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?”
Then Musha cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “What should I do with these people? They are ready to stone me!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Walk out in front of the people. Take your staff, the one you used when you struck the water of the Nile and call some of the elders of Yashar'AL to join you.

I will stand before you on the rock at Mount Sinai. Strike the rock and water will come gushing out. Then the people will be able to drink.” So Musha struck the rock as he was told, and water gushed out as the elders looked on.

Musha named the place Massah (which means “test”) and Maribah (which means “arguing”) because the people of Yashar'AL argued with Musha and tested 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by saying, Is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH here with us or not?”
While the people of Yashar'AL were still at Raphidim, the warriors of Amalak attacked them.
Musha commanded Yahusha Ba'Nun , “Choose some men to go out and fight the army of Amalak for us. Tomorrow, I will stand at the top of the hill, holding the staff of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in my hand.”
So Yahusha Ba'Nun did what Musha had commanded and fought the army of Amalak. Meanwhile, Musha, Aarun, and Hur climbed to the top of a nearby hill.
As long as Musha held up the staff in his hand, the Yasharalym had the advantage. But whenever he dropped his hand, the Amalakites gained the advantage.

Musha's arms soon became so tired he could no longer hold them up. So Aarun and Hur found a stone for him to sit on. Then they stood on each side of Musha, holding up his hands. So his hands held steady until sunset.
As a result, Yahusha Ba'Nun overwhelmed the army of Amalak in battle.
After the victory, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH instructed Musha, “Write this down on a scroll as a permanent reminder, and read it aloud to Yahusha Ba'Nun: I will erase the memory of Amalak from under Shamaym.”
Musha built an altar there and named it 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH-Nissi (which means “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is my banner”).
He said, “They have raised their fist against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s throne, so now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be at war with Amalak generation after generation.”

Musha father-in-law Yathru, the Cuhan of Midian, heard about everything 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had done for Musha and his people, the Yasharalym. He heard especially about how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had rescued them from Mitzraym.
Earlier, Musha had sent his wife, Zippurah, and his two sons back to Yathru, who had taken them in.
Musha first son was named Garshum, for Musha had said when the boy was born, “I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.”
His second son was named Aliazar, for Musha had said, “The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of my ancestors was my helper; he rescued me from the sword of Pharuh.”

Yathru, Musha's father-in-law, now came to visit Musha in the wilderness. He brought Musha's wife and two sons with him and they arrived while Musha and the people were camped near the mountain of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Yathru had sent a message to Musha, saying, “I, Yathru your father-in-law, am coming to see you with your wife and your two sons.”
So Musha went out to meet his father-in-law, he bowed low and kissed him. They asked about each other’s welfare and then went into Musha’s tent.

Musha told his father-in-law everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done to Pharuh and Mitzraym on behalf of Yashar'AL. Musha also told about all the hardships they had experienced along the way and how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had rescued his people from all their troubles.
Yathru was delighted when he heard about all the good things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done for Yashar'AL as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rescued them from the hand of the Mitzraym.
“Yadah (Praise) 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,” Yathru said, “for He has rescued you from the Mitzraym and from Pharuh. Yes, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has rescued Yashar'AL from the powerful hand of Mitzraym!
I know now that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is greater than all, because He rescued his people from the oppression of the proud Mitzraym.”

Then Yathru, Musha’s father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Aarun and all the elders of Yashar'AL came out and joined him in a sacrificial meal in 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH’s presence.
The next day, Musha took his seat to hear the people’s disputes against each other. They waited before him from morning till evening.

When Musha’s father-in-law saw all that Musha was doing for the people, he asked, “What are you really accomplishing here? Why are you trying to do all this alone while everyone stands around you from morning till evening?”
Musha replied, “Because the people come to me to get a ruling from 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

When a dispute arises, they come to me, and I am the one who settles the case between the quarreling parties. I inform the people of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH’s decrees and give them the instructions of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
“This is not good!” Musha’s father-in-law exclaimed.
“You are going to wear yourself out and the people too. This job is too heavy a burden for you to handle all by yourself.
Now listen to me and let me give you a word of advice and may 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be with you. You should continue to be the people’s representative before 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, bringing their disputes to Him.
Teach them 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH’s decrees and give them HIS instructions. Show them how to conduct their lives.
But select from all the people some capable, honest men who fear 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and hate bribes. Appoint them as leaders over groups of one thousand, one hundred, fifty, and ten.

They should always be available to solve the people’s common disputes, but have them bring the major cases to you. Let the leaders decide the smaller matters themselves. They will help you carry the load, making the task easier for you.
If you follow this advice and if 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH command's you to do so, then you will be able to endure the pressures and all these people will go home in Shalum.”
Musha listened to his father-in-law’s advice and followed his suggestions.
He chose capable men from all over Yashar'AL and appointed them as leaders over the people. He put them in charge of groups of one thousand, one hundred, fifty, and ten.
These men were always available to solve the people’s common disputes. They brought the major cases to Musha, but they took care of the smaller matters themselves.
Soon after this, Musha said good-bye to his father-in-law, who returned to his own land.
Exactly two Moons (months) after the Yasharalym left Mitzraym, they arrived in the wilderness of Sinai.
After breaking camp at Raphidim, they came to the wilderness of Sinai and set up camp there at the base of Mount Sinai.

Then Musha climbed the mountain to appear before 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH called to Musha from the mountain and Dabar, “Give these instructions to the family of Ya'aqub; announce it to the descendants of Yashar'AL:
‘You have seen what I did to the Mitzraym. You know how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself.
Now if you will obey ME and keep My covenant, you will be my own special treasure from among all the people on the Arath (earth); for all the Arath belongs to ME.
And you shall be to Me a kingdom of Kuhan (priest) and a Qadash (Set Apart) nation.’ These are the words which you shall speak to the children of YASHAR'AL.”
So Musha returned from the mountain and called together the elders of the people and told them everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him.
And all the people responded together, “We will do everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded.” So Musha brought the people’s answer back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “I will come to you in a thick cloud, so the people themselves can hear me when I speak with you, then they will always trust you.” Musha told 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what the people had said.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Go down and prepare the people for my arrival. Consecrate them today and tomorrow and have them wash their clothing.
Be sure they are ready on the third day, for on that day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will come down on Mount Sinai as all the people watch.
Mark off a boundary all around the mountain. Warn the people, ‘Be careful! Do not go up on the mountain or even touch its boundaries. Anyone who touches the mountain will certainly be put to death.

No hand may touch the person or animal that crosses the boundary; instead stone them or shoot them with arrows. They must be put to death.’ However when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast, then the people may go up on the mountain.”
So Musha went down to the people, he consecrated them for worship and they washed their clothes.
Musha told them, “Get ready for the third day and until then abstain from having sexual intercourse.”
On the morning of the third day, thunder roared and lightning flashed and a dense cloud came down on the mountain. There was a long, loud blast from a ram’s horn and all the people trembled.
Musha led them out from the camp to meet with 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE), and they stood at the foot of the mountain.

All of Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had descended on it in the form of fire. The smoke billowed into the sky like smoke from a brick kiln, and the whole mountain shook violently.
As the blast of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Musha spoke and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH thundered His reply.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came down on the top of Mount Sinai and called Musha to the top of the mountain. So Musha climbed the mountain.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told Musha, “Go back down and warn the people not to break through the boundaries to see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or they will die.
Even the Kuhan (priests) who regularly come near to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH must purify themselves so that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH does not break out and destroy them.”
“But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,” Musha protested, “the people cannot come up to Mount Sinai. You already warned us. You told me, ‘Mark off a boundary all around the mountain to set it apart as Qadash.’”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “Go down and bring Aarun back up with you. In the meantime, do not let the Kuhan or the people break through to approach 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, or He will break out and destroy them.”
So Musha went down to the people and told them what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar directly to the Yasharalym saying:

“I AM 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (ALMIGHTY ONE), who brought you out of the land of Mitzraym, out of the house of bondage. 3 “You must not have and serve any other Aluahym (which means Mighty ones, idols/deities) but me 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your only 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (ALMighty ONE).

“You must not make for yourself an idol of any kind or an image of anything in the Shamaym or on the Arath (earth) or in the Yam (sea). 5 You must not bow down to them or worship them, for I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, I AM a jealous 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄 ALUAH who will not tolerate your affection for any other Aluahym (mighty ones/idols deities). I lay the sins of the parents upon their children; the entire family is affected, even children in the third and fourth generations of those who reject ME. 6 But I lavish unfailing love for a thousand generations on those who love ME and obey my commandments.
“You must not misuse the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄 ALUAH, For I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will not let you go unpunished if you misuse My Name.

“Remember to observe the Shabbat Yum (day) by keeping it Qadash (Set Apart). 9 You have six Yum (days) each week for your ordinary work, 10 but the seventh day is a Shabbat day of rest dedicated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. On that day no one in your household may do any work. This includes you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, your livestock and any foreigners living among you. 11 For in six days 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made the Shamaym, the Arath, the Yam (sea), and everything in them; but on the seventh day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rested. That is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Baraked the Shabbat Yum (day) and set it apart as Qadash.
“Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long upon the Arath (earth) which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has giving you.
“You must not murder.
“You must not commit adultery.
“You must not steal.
“You must not testify falsely against your neighbor.
“You must not covet your neighbor’s house. You must not covet your neighbor’s wife, male or female servant, ox or donkey, or anything else that belongs to your neighbor.”

When the people heard the thunder and the loud blast of the ram’s horn and when they saw the flashes of lightning and the smoke billowing from the mountain, they stood at a distance, trembling with fear.
And they said to Musha, “You" speak to us and we will listen. But don’t let our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH speak directly to us, or we will die!”
“Do not be afraid,” Musha answered them, “for 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has come in this way to test you and so that your fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will keep you from sinning!”
As the people stood in the distance, Musha approached the dark cloud where 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Say this to the people of Yashar'AL: You saw for yourselves that I spoke to you from Shamaym.
Remember, you must not make any idols of silver or gold to rival me.

“Build for me an altar made of Arath (earth), and offer your sacrifices to me, your burnt offerings and Shalum offerings, your sheep and goats, and your cattle. Build my altar wherever I cause my Name to be remembered and I will come to you and barak you.
If you use stones to build my altar, use only natural, uncut stones. Do not shape the stones with a tool, for that would make the altar unfit for Qadash use.
And do not approach my altar by going up steps. If you do, someone might look up under your clothing and see your nakedness.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, These are the regulations you must present to Yashar'AL.
“If you buy an Abarym (Hebrew) slave, he may serve for no more than six years. Set him free in the seventh year and he will owe you nothing for his freedom.
If he was single when he became your slave, he shall leave single. But if he was married before he became a slave, then his wife must be freed with him.
“If his master gave him a wife while he was a slave and they had sons or daughters, then only the man will be free in the seventh year, but his wife and children will still belong to his master.
But the slave may declare, ‘I love my master, my wife and my children. I don’t want to go free.’

If he does this, his master must present him before 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Then his master must take him to the door or doorpost and publicly pierce his ear with an awl. After that, the slave will serve his master for life.
“When a man sells his daughter as a slave, she will not be freed at the end of six years as the men are.
If she does not satisfy her owner, he must allow her to be bought back again. But he is not allowed to sell her to foreigners, since he is the one who broke the contract with her.
But if the slave’s owner arranges for her to marry his son, he may no longer treat her as a slave but as a daughter.
“If a man who has married, takes another wife for himself, he must not neglect the rights of the first wife to food, clothing, and sexual intimacy.
If he fails in any of these three obligations, she may leave as a free woman without making any payment.
“Anyone who assaults and kills another person must be put to death.
But if it was simply an accident permitted by 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, I will appoint a place of refuge where the slayer can run for safety.
However, if someone deliberately murdered another person, then the slayer must be dragged even from my altar and be put to death.
“Anyone who strikes father or mother must be put to death.
“Kidnappers must be put to death, whether they are caught in possession of their victims or have already sold them as slaves.
“Anyone who dishonors father or mother must be put to death.
“Now suppose two men quarrel and one hits the other with a stone or fist and the injured person did not die but is confined to bed.
If he is later able to walk outside again, even with a crutch, the assailant will not be punished but must compensate his victim for lost wages and provide for his full recovery.
“If a man beats his male or female slave with a club and the slave dies as a result, the owner must be punished.
But if the slave recovers within a day or two, then the owner shall not be punished, since the slave is his property.

“Now suppose two men are fighting, and in the process they accidentally strike a pregnant woman so she gives birth prematurely. If no further injury results, the man who struck the woman must pay the amount of compensation the woman’s husband demands and the judges approve.
But if there is further injury, the punishment must match the injury: a life for a life,
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot,
A burn for a burn, a wound for a wound, a bruise for a bruise.
“If a man hits his male or female slave in the eye and the eye is blinded, he must let the slave go free to compensate for the eye.
And if a man knocks out the tooth of his male or female slave, he must let the slave go free to compensate for the tooth.
“If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must be stoned and its flesh may not be eaten. In such a case, however, the owner will not be held liable.

But suppose the ox had a reputation for goring and the owner had been informed but failed to keep it under control. If the ox then kills someone, it must be stoned and the owner must also be put to death.
However, the dead person’s relatives may accept payment to compensate for the loss of life. The owner of the ox may redeem his life by paying whatever is demanded.
“The same regulation applies if the ox gores a boy or a girl.
But if the ox gores a slave, either male or female, the animal’s owner must pay the slave’s owner thirty silver coins and the ox must be stoned.
“Suppose someone digs or uncovers a pit and fails to cover it and then an ox or a donkey falls into it.
The owner of the pit must pay full compensation to the owner of the animal, but then he gets to keep the dead animal.
“If someone’s ox injures a neighbor’s ox and the injured ox dies, then the two owners must sell the live ox and divide the price equally between them. They must also divide the dead animal.
But if the ox had a reputation for goring, yet its owner failed to keep it under control, he must pay full compensation—a live ox for the dead one, but he may keep the dead ox.
“If someone steals an ox or sheep and then kills or sells it, the thief must pay back five oxen for each ox stolen and four sheep for each sheep stolen.
“If a thief is caught in the act of breaking into a house and is struck and killed in the process, the person who killed the thief is not guilty of murder.

But if it happens in daylight, the one who killed the thief is guilty of murder. “A thief who is caught must pay in full for everything he stole. If he cannot pay, he must be sold as a slave to pay for his theft.
If someone steals an ox or a donkey or a sheep and it is found in the thief’s possession, then the thief must pay double the value of the stolen animal.
“If an animal is grazing in a field or vineyard and the owner lets it stray into someone else’s field to graze, then the animal’s owner must pay compensation from the best of his own grain or grapes.

“If you are burning thornbushes and the fire gets out of control and spreads into another person’s field, destroying the sheaves or the uncut grain or the whole crop, the one who started the fire must pay for the lost crop.
“Suppose someone leaves money or goods with a neighbor for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house. If the thief is caught, the compensation is double the value of what was stolen.
But if the thief is not caught, the neighbor must appear before 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who will determine if he stole the property.

“Suppose there is a dispute between two people who both claim to own a particular ox, donkey, sheep, article of clothing, or any lost property. Both parties must come before 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and the person whom 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH declares guilty must pay double compensation to the other.
“Now suppose someone leaves a donkey, ox, sheep, or any other animal with a neighbor for safekeeping, but it dies or is injured or is taken away and no one sees what happened.

The neighbor must then take an oath in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH confirms that the neighbor did not steal the property, the owner must accept the verdict and no payment will be required.
But if the animal was indeed stolen, the guilty person must pay compensation to the owner.
If it was torn to pieces by a wild animal, the remains of the carcass must be shown as evidence and no compensation will be required.
“If someone borrows an animal from a neighbor and it is injured or dies when the owner is absent, the person who borrowed it must pay full compensation.
But if the owner was present, no compensation is required. And no compensation is required if the animal was rented, for this loss is covered by the rental fee.
“If a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged to anyone and has sex with her, he must pay the customary bride price and marry her.
But if her father refuses to let him marry her, the man must still pay him an amount equal to the bride price of a virgin.
“You must not allow a sorceress to live.
“Anyone who has sexual relations with an animal must certainly be put to death.
“Anyone who sacrifices to any idols other than 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH must be destroyed.
“You must not mistreat or oppress foreigners in any way. Remember, you yourselves were once foreigners in the land of Mitzraym.
“You must not exploit a widow or an orphan.
If you exploit them in any way and they cry out to Me, then I will certainly hear their cry.
My anger will blaze against you and I will kill you with the sword. Then your wives will be widows and your children fatherless.
“If you lend money to any of my people who are in need, do not charge interest as a money lender would.
If you take your neighbor’s cloak as security for a loan, you must return it before sunset.
This coat may be the only blanket your neighbor has. How can a person sleep without it? If you do not return it and your neighbor cries out to me for help, then I will hear, for I AM merciful.
“You must not dishonor your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH or curse any of your rulers.
“You must not hold anything back when you give ME offerings from your crops and your wine. “You must give me your firstborn sons.
“You must also give ME the firstborn of your cattle, sheep and goats. But leave the newborn animal with its mother for seven days; then give it to me on the eighth day.
“You must be my Qadash (Set Apart) people. Therefore, do not eat any animal that has been torn up and killed by wild animals. Throw it to the dogs.
“You must not pass along false rumors. You must not cooperate with evil people by lying on the witness stand.
“You must not follow the crowd in doing wrong. When you are called to testify in a dispute, do not be swayed by the crowd to twist justice.
And do not slant your testimony in favor of a person just because that person is poor.
“If you come upon your enemy’s ox or donkey that has strayed away, take it back to its owner.
If you see that the donkey of someone who hates you has collapsed under its load, do not walk by. Instead, stop and help.
“In a lawsuit, you must not deny justice to the poor.
“Be sure never to charge anyone falsely with evil. Never sentence an innocent or blameless person to death, for I will never declare a guilty person to be innocent.
“Take no bribes, for a bribe makes you ignore something that you clearly see. A bribe makes even a righteous person twist the truth.
“You must not oppress foreigners. You know what it’s like to be a foreigner, for you yourselves were once foreigners in the land of Mitzraym.
“Plant and harvest your crops for six years,

But let the land be renewed and lie uncultivated during the seventh year. Then let the poor among you harvest whatever grows on its own. Leave the rest for wild animals to eat. The same applies to your vineyards and olive groves.

“You have six days each week for your ordinary work, but on the seventh day you must stop working. This gives your ox and your donkey a chance to rest. It also allows your slaves and the foreigners living among you to be refreshed.
“Pay close attention to all my instructions. You must not call on the name of any other Aluahym (mighty ones, idols and Deities) . Do not even speak their names.
“Each year you must celebrate three festivals in my honor.

First, celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days the bread you eat must be made without yeast, just as I commanded you. Celebrate this festival annually at the appointed time in early spring, in the Moon (month) of Abib, for that is the anniversary of your departure from Mitzraym. No one may appear before me without an offering.

“Second, celebrate the Festival of Harvest, when you bring me the first crops of your harvest. “Finally, celebrate the Festival of the Final Harvest at the end of the harvest season, when you have harvested all the crops from your fields.
At these three times each year, every man in Yashar'AL must appear before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
“You must not offer the blood of my sacrificial offerings together with any baked goods containing yeast. And do not leave the fat from the festival offerings until the next morning.
“As you harvest your crops, bring the very best of the first harvest to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. “You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
“See, I AM sending a Malak before you to protect you on your journey and lead you safely to the place I have prepared for you.
Pay close attention to him and obey his instructions. Do not rebel against him, for he is my representative and he will not forgive your rebellion.
But if you are careful to obey him, following all My instructions, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and I will oppose those who oppose you.
For my Malak will go before you and bring you into the land of the Amurites, Hittites, Parizzites, Canaanites, Hibites, and Yabusites, so you may live there. And I will destroy them completely.
You must not worship the idols of these nations or serve them in any way or imitate their evil practices. Instead, you must utterly destroy them and smash their sacred pillars.
“You must serve only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. If you do, I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will barak you with food and water and I will protect you from illness.
There will be no miscarriages or infertility in your land and I will give you long, full lives.
“I will send my terror ahead of you and create panic among all the people whose lands you invade. I will make all your enemies turn and run.
I will send terror ahead of you to drive out the Hibites, Canaanites and Hittites.
But I will not drive them out in a single year, because the land would become desolate and the wild animals would multiply and threaten you.
I will drive them out a little at a time until your population has increased enough to take possession of the land.

And I will fix your boundaries from the Red Sea to the Maditarranean Sea and from the eastern wilderness to the Euphrates River. I will hand over to you the people now living in the land and you will drive them out ahead of you.
“Make no treaties with them or their idols.
They must not live in your land, or they will cause you to sin against me. If you serve their idols, you will be caught in the trap of idolatry.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH instructed Musha: “Come up here to me and bring along Aarun, Nadab, Abihu and seventy of Yashar'AL’s elders. All of you must worship from a distance.
Only Musha is allowed to come near to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. The others must not come near and none of the other people are allowed to climb up the mountain with Musha.”

Then Musha went down to the people and repeated all the instructions and regulations 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given him. All the people answered with one voice, We will do everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded.

Then Musha carefully wrote down all 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s instructions. Early the next morning Musha got up and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, Musha also set up twelve pillars, one for each of the twelve tribes of Yashar'AL.
Then Musha sent some of the young Yasharalym men to present burnt offerings and to sacrifice bulls as Shalum offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Musha drained half the blood from these animals into basins. The other half he splattered against the altar.
Then Musha took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud to the people. Again they all responded, “We will do everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded. We will obey.”
Then Musha took the blood from the basins and splattered it over the people, declaring, “Look, this blood confirms the covenant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has made with you in giving you these instructions.”
Then Musha, Aarun, Nadab, Abihu and the seventy elders of Yashar'AL climbed up the mountain.
There they saw the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL. Under His feet there seemed to be a surface of brilliant blue lapis lazuli, as clear as the sky itself.
And though these nobles of Yashar'AL gazed upon 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH., he did not destroy them. In fact, they ate a covenant meal, eating and drinking in HIS presence!

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Come up to me on the mountain. Stay there, and I will give you the tablets of stone on which I have inscribed the instructions and Commandments so you can teach the people.”
So Musha and his assistant Yahusha Ba'Nun set out and Musha climbed up the mountain of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Musha told the elders, “Stay here and wait for us until we come back. Aarun and Hur are here with you. If anyone has a dispute while I am gone, consult with them.”
Then Musha climbed up the mountain and the cloud covered it.
And the Kabad of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH settled down on Mount Sinai and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH called to Musha from inside the cloud.
To the Yasharalym at the foot of the mountain, the Kabad of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared at the summit like a consuming fire.
Then Musha disappeared into the cloud as he climbed higher up the mountain. Musha remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Tell the people of Yashar'AL to bring me their sacred offerings. Accept the contributions from all whose hearts are moved to offer them.
Here is a list of sacred offerings you may accept from them: gold, silver and bronze;
Blue, purple and scarlet thread; fine linen and goat hair for cloth;
Tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather; acacia wood;
olive oil for the lamps; spices for the anointing oil and the fragrant incense;
Onyx stones and other gemstones to be set in the ephod and the Kuhan’s chestpiece.
“Have the people of Yashar'AL build me a Qadash (Set Apart) sanctuary so I can live among them.
You must build this Tabernacle and its furnishings exactly according to the pattern I will show you.
“Have the people make an Ark of acacia wood, a sacred chest 45 inches long, 27 inches wide and 27 inches high.
Overlay it inside and outside with pure gold, and run a molding of gold all around it.
Cast four gold rings and attach them to its four feet, two rings on each side.
Make poles from acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Insert the poles into the rings at the sides of the Ark to carry it.
These carrying poles must stay inside the rings; never remove them.
When the Ark is finished, place inside it the stone tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant, which I will give to you.
“Then make the Ark’s cover, the place of atonement from pure gold. It must be 45 inches long and 27 inches wide.
Then make two charubim from hammered gold and place them on the two ends of the atonement cover.
Mold the charubim on each end of the atonement cover, making it all of one piece of gold.
The charubim will face each other and look down on the atonement cover. With their wings spread above it, they will protect it.
Place inside the Ark the stone tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant, which I will give to you. Then put the atonement cover on top of the Ark.

I will meet with you there and talk to you from above the atonement cover between the gold charubim that hover over the Ark of the Covenant. From there I will give you my commands for the people of Yashar'AL.
“You shall also make a table of acacia wood; two cubits shall be its length, a cubit its width and a cubit and a half its height.
Overlay it with pure gold and run a gold molding around the edge.
Decorate it with a 3-inch border all around, and run a gold molding along the border.
Make four gold rings for the table and attach them at the four corners next to the four legs.
Attach the rings near the border to hold the poles that are used to carry the table.
Make these poles from acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.
Make special containers of pure gold for the table bowls, ladles, pitchers, and jars, to be used in pouring out liquid offerings.
Place the Bread of the Presence on the table to remain before me at all times.
“Make a lampstand of pure, hammered gold. Make the entire lampstand and its decorations of one piece, the base, center stem, lamp cups, buds, and petals.
Make it with six branches going out from the center stem, three on each side.
Each of the six branches will have three lamp cups shaped like almond blossoms, complete with buds and petals.
Craft the center stem of the lampstand with four lamp cups shaped like almond blossoms, complete with buds and petals.
There will also be an almond bud beneath each pair of branches where the six branches extend from the center stem.
The almond buds and branches must all be of one piece with the center stem and they must be hammered from pure gold.
Then make the seven lamps for the lampstand and set them so they reflect their light forward.
The lamp snuffers and trays must also be made of pure gold.
You will need 75 pounds of pure gold for the lampstand and its accessories.
“Be sure that you make everything according to the pattern I have shown you here on the mountain.
“Moreover you shall make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine woven linen and blue, purple and scarlet thread; with artistic designs of charubim you shall weave them.
The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits and the width of each curtain four cubits. And every one of the curtains shall have the same measurements.
Five curtains shall be coupled to one another and the other five curtains shall be coupled to one another.
And you shall make loops of blue yarn on the edge of the curtain on the selvedge of one set, and likewise you shall do on the outer edge of the other curtain of the second set.
Fifty loops you shall make in the one curtain, and fifty loops you shall make on the edge of the curtain that is on the end of the second set, that the loops may be clasped to one another.
And you shall make fifty clasps of gold and couple the curtains together with the clasps, so that it may be one tabernacle.
“You shall also make curtains of goats’ hair, to be a tent over the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits and the width of each curtain four cubits; and the eleven curtains shall all have the same measurements.
And you shall couple five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves, and you shall double over the sixth curtain at the forefront of the tent.
You shall make fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that is outermost in one set and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain of the second set.
And you shall make fifty bronze clasps, put the clasps into the loops and couple the tent together, that it may be one.
The remnant that remains of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remains, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.

And a cubit on one side and a cubit on the other side, of what remains of the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on this side and on that side, to cover it.
“You shall also make a covering of ram skins dyed red for the tent and a covering of badger skins above that.
“And for the tabernacle you shall make the boards of acacia wood, standing upright.
Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and a cubit and a half shall be the width of each board.
Two tenons shall be in each board for binding one to another. Thus you shall make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
And you shall make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side.
You shall make forty sockets of silver under the twenty boards: two sockets under each of the boards for its two tenons.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, there shall be twenty boards
And their forty sockets of silver: two sockets under each of the boards.
For the far side of the tabernacle, westward, you shall make six boards.
And you shall also make two boards for the two back corners of the tabernacle.
They shall be coupled together at the bottom and they shall be coupled together at the top by one ring. Thus it shall be for both of them. They shall be for the two corners.
So there shall be eight boards with their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets, two sockets under each of the boards.
“And you shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the boards on one side of the tabernacle,
five bars for the boards on the other side of the tabernacle and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the far side westward.
The middle bar shall pass through the midst of the boards from end to end.
You shall overlay the boards with gold, make their rings of gold as holders for the bars and overlay the bars with gold.
And you shall raise up the tabernacle according to its pattern which you were shown on the mountain.
“You shall make a veil woven of blue, purple and scarlet thread and fine woven linen. It shall be woven with an artistic design of charubim.
You shall hang it upon the four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold. Their hooks shall be gold, upon four sockets of silver.

And you shall hang the veil from the clasps. Then you shall bring the ark of the Testimony in there, behind the veil. The veil shall be a divider for you between the Qadash place and the Most Qadash (Set Apart).
You shall put the mercy seat upon the ark of the Testimony in the Most Qadash.
You shall set the table outside the veil and the lampstand across from the table on the side of the tabernacle toward the south; and you shall put the table on the north side.
“You shall make a screen for the door of the tabernacle, woven of blue, purple and scarlet thread and fine woven linen, made by a weaver.
And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia wood and overlay them with gold; their hooks shall be gold and you shall cast five sockets of bronze for them.
“You shall make an altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide the altar shall be square and its height shall be three cubits.
You shall make its horns on its four corners; its horns shall be of one piece with it. And you shall overlay it with bronze.
Also you shall make its pans to receive its ashes and its shovels and its basins and its forks and its firepans; you shall make all its utensils of bronze.
You shall make a grate for it, a network of bronze; and on the network you shall make four bronze rings at its four corners.
You shall put it under the rim of the altar beneath, that the network may be midway up the altar.
And you shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood and overlay them with bronze.
The poles shall be put in the rings and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar to bear it.
You shall make it hollow with boards; as it was shown you on the mountain, so shall they make it.
“You shall also make the court of the tabernacle. For the south side there shall be hangings for the court made of fine woven linen, one hundred cubits long for one side.
And its twenty pillars and their twenty sockets shall be bronze. The hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be silver.

Likewise along the length of the north side there shall be hangings one hundred cubits long, with its twenty pillars and their twenty sockets of bronze and the hooks of the pillars and their bands of silver.
“And along the width of the court on the west side shall be hangings of fifty cubits, with their ten pillars and their ten sockets.
The width of the court on the east side shall be fifty cubits.
The hangings on one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
And on the other side shall be hangings of fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
“For the gate of the court there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, woven of blue, purple and scarlet thread and fine woven linen, made by a weaver. It shall have four pillars and four sockets.
All the pillars around the court shall have bands of silver; their hooks shall be of silver and their sockets of bronze.
The length of the court shall be one hundred cubits, the width fifty throughout and the height five cubits, made of fine woven linen and its sockets of bronze.
All the utensils of the tabernacle for all its service, all its pegs and all the pegs of the court, shall be of bronze.
“And you shall command the children of YASHAR'AL that they bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to cause the lamp to burn continually.

In the tabernacle of meeting, outside the veil which is before the Testimony, Aarun and his sons shall tend it from evening until morning before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. It shall be a statute forever to their generations on behalf of the children of YASHAR'AL.
“Now take Aarun your brother and his sons with him, from among the children of YASHAR'AL, that he may minister to Me as Kuhan (priest), Aarun and Aarun’s sons: Nadab, Abihu, Alaazar and Ithamar.
And you shall make Qadash garments for Aarun your brother, for Kabad and for beauty.
So you shall speak to all who are gifted artisans, whom I have filled with the Ruach of wisdom, that they may make Aarun’s garments, to consecrate him, that he may minister to Me as Kuhan (priest).

And these are the garments which they shall make: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a skillfully woven tunic, a turban and a sash. So they shall make Qadash garments for Aarun your brother and his sons, that he may minister to Me as Kuhan.
“They shall take the gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread and the fine linen,
And they shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple and scarlet thread and fine woven linen, artistically worked.
It shall have two shoulder straps joined at its two edges and so it shall be joined together.
And the intricately woven band of the ephod, which is on it, shall be of the same workmanship, made of gold, blue, purple and scarlet thread and fine woven linen.
“Then you shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Yashar'AL:
Six of their names on one stone and six names on the other stone, in order of their birth.
With the work of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Yashar'AL. You shall set them in settings of gold.
And you shall put the two stones on the shoulders of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Yashar'AL. So Aarun shall bear their names before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH on his two shoulders as a memorial.
You shall also make settings of gold,
and you shall make two chains of pure gold like braided cords, and fasten the braided chains to the settings.

“You shall make the breastplate of judgment. Artistically woven according to the workmanship of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine woven linen, you shall make it.
It shall be doubled into a square: a span shall be its length and a span shall be its width.
And you shall put settings of stones in it, four rows of stones: The first row shall be a sardius, a topaz and an emerald; this shall be the first row;
The second row shall be a turquoise, a sapphire and a diamond;
The third row, a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst;
And the fourth row, a beryl, an onyx and a jasper. They shall be set in gold settings.

And the stones shall have the names of the sons of Yashar'AL, twelve according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, each one with its own name; they shall be according to the twelve tribes.
“You shall make chains for the breastplate at the end, like braided cords of pure gold.
And you shall make two rings of gold for the breastplate and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
Then you shall put the two braided chains of gold in the two rings which are on the ends of the breastplate;
And the other two ends of the two braided chains you shall fasten to the two settings and put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod in the front.
“You shall make two rings of gold and put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on the edge of it, which is on the inner side of the ephod.
And two other rings of gold you shall make, and put them on the two shoulder straps, underneath the ephod toward its front, right at the seam above the intricately woven band of the ephod.

They shall bind the breastplate by means of its rings to the rings of the ephod, using a blue cord, so that it is above the intricately woven band of the ephod and so that the breastplate does not come loose from the ephod.
“So Aarun shall bear the names of the sons of Yashar'AL on the breastplate of judgment over his heart, when he goes into the Qadash place, as a memorial before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH continually.

And you shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim and they shall be over Aarun’s heart when he goes in before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. So Aarun shall bear the judgment of the children of YASHAR'AL over his heart before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH continually.
“You shall make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
There shall be an opening for his head in the middle of it; it shall have a woven binding all around its opening, like the opening in a coat of mail, so that it does not tear.
And upon its hem you shall make pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet, all around its hem and bells of gold between them all around:
A golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the hem of the robe all around.
And it shall be upon Aarun when he ministers and its sound will be heard when he goes into the Qadash place before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and when he comes out, that he may not die.
“You shall also make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like the engraving of a signet: QADASHYM TO 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And you shall put it on a blue cord, that it may be on the turban; it shall be on the front of the turban.

So it shall be on Aarun’s forehead, that Aarun may bear the iniquity of the Qadash things which the children of YASHAR'AL set apart in all their Qadash gifts and it shall always be on his forehead, that they may be accepted before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“You shall skillfully weave the tunic of fine linen thread, you shall make the turban of fine linen, and you shall make the sash of woven work.
“For Aarun’s sons you shall make tunics, and you shall make sashes for them. And you shall make hats for them, for Kabad and beauty.
So you shall put them on Aarun your brother and on his sons with him. You shall anoint them, consecrate them and sanctify them, that they may minister to Me as Kuhan.
And you shall make for them linen trousers to cover their nakedness; they shall reach from the waist to the thighs.

They shall be on Aarun and on his sons when they come into the tabernacle of meeting, or when they come near the altar to minister in the Qadash place, that they do not incur iniquity and die. It shall be a statute forever to Aarun and his descendants after him.
“And this is what you shall do to Aarun and his sons to Set them Apart for ministering to Me as Kuhan: Take one young bull and two rams without blemish,
and unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil and unleavened wafers anointed with oil (you shall make them of wheat flour).
You shall put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, with the bull and the two rams.
“And Aarun and his sons you shall bring to the door of the tabernacle of meeting and you shall wash them with water.
Then you shall take the garments, put the tunic on Aarun and the robe of the ephod, the ephod and the breastplate and gird him with the intricately woven band of the ephod.
You shall put the turban on the head of Aarun and put the Qadash crown on the turban.
And you shall take the anointing oil, pour it on his head and anoint him.
Then you shall bring his sons and put tunics on them.
And you shall gird them with sashes, for Aarun and his sons and put the hats on them. The Kuhanym shall be theirs for a perpetual statute. So you shall consecrate Aarun and his sons.
“You shall also have the bull brought before the tabernacle of meeting, then Aarun and his sons shall put their hands on the head of the bull.
Then you shall kill the bull before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, by the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
You shall take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger and pour all the blood beside the base of the altar.
And you shall take all the fat that covers the entrails, the fatty lobe attached to the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them and burn them on the altar.
But the flesh of the bull, with its skin and its offal, you shall burn with fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
“You shall also take one ram and Aarun and his sons shall put their hands on the head of the ram;
and you shall kill the ram and you shall take its blood and sprinkle it all around on the altar.
Then you shall cut the ram in pieces, wash its entrails and its legs and put them with its pieces and with its head.
And you shall burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; it is a sweet aroma, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“You shall also take the other ram, and Aarun and his sons shall put their hands on the head of the ram.

Then you shall kill the ram and take some of its blood and put it on the tip of the right ear of Aarun and on the tip of the right ear of his sons, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot and sprinkle the blood all around on the altar.

And you shall take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aarun and on his garments, on his sons and on the garments of his sons with him; and Aarun and his garments shall be Qadash and his sons garments with him.

“Also you shall take the fat of the ram, the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the fatty lobe attached to the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, the right thigh (for it is a ram of consecration),
One loaf of bread, one cake made with oil and one wafer from the basket of the unleavened bread that is before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH;
And you shall put all these in the hands of Aarun and in the hands of his sons and you shall wave them as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
You shall receive them back from their hands and burn them on the altar as a burnt offering, as a sweet aroma before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. It is an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Then you shall take the breast of the ram of Aarun’s consecration and wave it as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and it shall be your portion.

And from the ram of the consecration you shall consecrate the breast of the wave offering which is waved, and the thigh of the heave offering which is raised, of that which is for Aarun and of that which is for his sons.

It shall be from the children of YASHAR'AL for Aarun and his sons by a statute forever. For it is a heave offering; it shall be a heave offering from the children of YASHAR'AL from the sacrifices of their Shalum offerings, that is, their heave offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“And the Qadash garments of Aarun shall be his sons’ after him, to be anointed in them and to be consecrated in them.
That son who becomes Kuhan in his place shall put them on for seven days, when he enters the tabernacle of meeting to minister in the Qadash place.
“And you shall take the ram of the consecration and boil its flesh in the Qadash (Set Apart) place.
Then Aarun and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket, by the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
They shall eat those things with which the atonement was made, to consecrate and to sanctify them; but an outsider shall not eat them, because they are Qadash.
And if any of the flesh of the consecration offerings, or of the bread, remains until the morning, then you shall burn the remainder with fire. It shall not be eaten, because it is Qadash.
“Thus you shall do to Aarun and his sons, according to all that I have commanded you. Seven days you shall consecrate them.
And you shall offer a bull every day as a sin offering for atonement. You shall cleanse the altar when you make atonement for it and you shall anoint it to Qadash it.
Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and Qadash it. And the altar shall be most Qadash. Whatever touches the altar must be Qadash.
“Now this is what you shall offer on the altar: two lambs of the first year, day by day continually.
One lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the other lamb you shall offer at twilight.
With the one lamb shall be one-tenth of an ephah of flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of pressed oil and one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering.
And the other lamb you shall offer at twilight; and you shall offer with it the grain offering and the drink offering, as in the morning, for a sweet aroma, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
