This shall be a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the door of the tabernacle of meeting before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, where I will meet you to speak with you.
And there I will meet with the children of Yashar'AL and the tabernacle shall be Qadash (Set Apart) by My Kabad.
So I will consecrate the tabernacle of meeting and the altar. I will also consecrate both Aarun and his sons to minister to Me as Kuhanym.
I will dwell among the children of Yashar'AL and will be their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
And they shall know that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who brought them out of the land of Mitzraym, that I may dwell among them. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
“You are to make an altar for burning incense. You are to make it of acacia wood.
It is to be a square, one cubit long and one cubit wide and it is to be two cubits high, with its horns of one piece with it.
Overlay the top, the sides and horns of the altar with pure gold and run a gold molding around the entire altar.
Make two gold rings and attach them on opposite sides of the altar below the gold molding to hold the carrying poles.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.

Place the incense altar just outside the inner curtain that shields the Ark of the Covenant, in front of the Ark’s cover, the place of atonement, that covers the tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant. I will meet with you there.
“Every morning when Aarun maintains the lamps, he must burn fragrant incense on the altar.
And each evening when he lights the lamps, Aarun must again burn incense in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. This must be done from generation to generation.
Do not offer any Unqadash incense on this altar, or any burnt offerings, grain offerings, or liquid offerings.

“Once a year Aarun must purify the altar by smearing its horns with blood from the offering made to purify the people from their sin. This will be a regular annual event from generation to generation, for this is the most Qadash altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Whenever you take a census of the people of Yashar'AL, each man who is counted must pay a ransom for himself to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then no plague will strike the people as you count them.
Each person who is counted must give a small piece of silver as a sacred offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. (This payment is half a shekel, based on the sanctuary shekel, which equals twenty gerahs.)
All who have reached their twentieth birthday must give this sacred offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
When this offering is given to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to purify your lives, making you right with Him, the rich must not give more than the specified amount and the poor must not give less.
Receive this ransom money from the Yasharalym and use it for the care of the Tabernacle. It will bring the Yasharalym to the attention of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and it will purify your lives.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Make a bronze washbasin with a bronze stand. Place it between the Tabernacle and the altar and fill it with water.
Aarun and his sons will wash their hands and feet there.
They must wash with water whenever they go into the Tabernacle to appear before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and when they approach the altar to burn up their special gifts to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or they will die!
They must always wash their hands and feet, or they will die. This is a permanent law for Aarun and his descendants, to be observed from generation to generation.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Collect choice spices, 12 1⁄2 pounds of pure myrrh, 6 1⁄4 pounds of fragrant cinnamon, 6 1⁄4 pounds of fragrant calamus,
and 12 1⁄2 pounds of cassia, as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel, also get one gallon of olive oil.
Like a skilled incense maker, blend these ingredients to make a Qadash anointing oil.
Use this sacred oil to anoint the Tabernacle, the Ark of the Covenant,
The table and all its utensils, the lampstand and all its accessories, the incense altar,
The altar of burnt offering and all its utensils and the washbasin with its stand.
Consecrate them to make them absolutely Qadash. After this, whatever touches them will also become Qadash.
“Anoint Aarun and his sons also, consecrating them to serve me as Kuhanym (priests).
And say to the people of Yashar'AL, ‘This Qadash anointing oil is reserved for me from generation to generation.
It must never be used to anoint anyone else and you must never make any blend like it for yourselves. It is Qadash and you must treat it as Qadash.
Anyone who makes a blend like it or anoints someone other than a Kuhan (priest) will be cut off from the community.’”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Gather fragrant spices, resin droplets, mollusk shell and galbanum, mix these fragrant spices with pure frankincense, weighed out in equal amounts.
Using the usual techniques of the incense maker, blend the spices together and sprinkle them with salt to produce a pure and Qadash incense.
Grind some of the mixture into a very fine powder and put it in front of the Ark of the Covenant, where I will meet with you in the Tabernacle. You must treat this incense as most Qadash.
Never use this formula to make this incense for yourselves. It is reserved for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and you must treat it as Qadash.
Anyone who makes incense like this for personal use will be cut off from the community of Yashar'AL.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Look, I have called Uri’s son Bazalal, grandson of Hur from Yahudah’s tribe,
And I have filled him with the Ruach of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge and all kinds of craftsmanship,
To create plans for work in gold, silver, and bronze,
and for cutting stones to set them, for carving wood and for doing all kinds of craftsmanship.
Along with him I am appointing Ahisamach’s son Uhuliab from the tribe of Dan and I have given wisdom to all who are skilled so they can make everything that I have commanded you,
Including the Tent of Meeting, the Ark of the Testimony, the Mercy Seat that is on it, all the furnishings of the tent
The table and its furnishings, the lamp stand of pure gold, all its furnishings, the altar of incense,
The altar for burnt offerings, its furnishings, the basin, its base,
The woven garments, the Qadash garments of Aarun the Kuhan (priest), the garments of his sons as they serve as Kuhanym,
the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the Qadash Place, they are to make them in accordance with everything that I commanded you.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,

“You are to tell the Yasharalym: that surely, ‘You are to certainly observe my Shabbat because it is a sign between me and you from generation to generation, so you may know that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who Qadash (Set Apart) you.

You are to observe the Shabbat, because it’s Qadash (Set Apart) for you. Whoever profanes the Shabbat is certainly to die; indeed, whoever does work on the Shabbat Yum (day) is to be cut off from among his people.
Work may be done for six days, but the seventh day is a Shabbat of complete rest, Qadash (Set Apart) to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Whoever does work on the Shabbath is certainly to die.
The Yasharalym are to keep the Shabbat and to make the Shabbat observance a perpetual covenant from generation to generation.
It is a sign forever between me and the Yashar'AL, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made the Shamaym and the Arath in six days, but on the seventh day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rested and was refreshed.’”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH finished Dabarym with Musha on Mount Sinai, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave Musha the two Tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone written by the finger of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

Now when the people saw that Musha delayed coming down from the mountain, the people gathered together to Aarun and said to him, “Come, make us idols that shall go before us; for as for this Musha, the man who brought us up out of the land of Mitzraym, we do not know what has become of him.”
And Aarun said to them, “Break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters and bring them to me.”
So all the people broke off the golden earrings which were in their ears and brought them to Aarun.
And Aarun received the gold from their hand, and he fashioned it with an engraving tool and made a molded calf.
So when Aarun saw it, he built an altar before it. And Aarun made a proclamation and said, “Tomorrow is a feast.”
Then they rose early on the next day, offered burnt offerings and brought Shalum offerings; and the people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Go down from the mountain! For your people whom you brought out of the land of Mitzraym have corrupted themselves.

They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them. They have made themselves a molded calf and worshiped it and they sacrificed to it and said, ‘This is your idol, O Yashar'AL, that brought you out of the land of Mitzraym!’
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “I have seen this people and indeed they are stiff-necked people!
Now therefore, let Me alone, that My wrath may burn hot against them and I may consume them, and I will make of you a great nation.

Then Musha pleaded with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and said, Oh 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, why does Your wrath burn hot against Your people whom You have brought out of the land of Mitzraym with great power and with a mighty hand?

What should the Mitzraym speak and say, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought them out to harm them, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them from the face of the Arath’? Turn from Your fierce wrath and relent from destroying Your people.

Remember Abraham, Yachaq, and Yashar'AL your servants, to whom You swore by Your own self and said to them, ‘I will multiply your descendants as the stars of Shamaym; and all this land that I have spoken of, I give to your descendants and they shall inherit it forever.’ ”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH relented from the harm which He said He would do to His people.
And Musha turned and went down from the mountain and the two tablets of the Testimony were in Musha's hand. The tablets were written on both sides; on the one side and on the other they were written.
Now the tablets were the work of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and the writing was the writing of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH engraved on the tablets.
And when Yahusha Ba'Nun heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said to Musha, There is a noise of war in the camp.”
But Musha said: “It is not the noise of the shout of victory, Nor the noise of the cry of defeat, But the sound of singing I hear.”
So it was, as soon as Musha came near the camp, he saw the calf and the dancing. So Musha anger became hot and he cast the tablets out of his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain.
Then Musha took the gold calf which they had made, burned it in the fire and ground it to powder; and he scattered it on the water and made the children of Yashar'AL drink it.
And Musha said to Aarun, “What did this people do to you that you have brought so great a sin upon them?
Do not get so upset, my master,” Aarun replied. “You yourself know how evil these people are.
For they said to me, ‘Make us idols that shall go before us; as for this Musha, the man who brought us out of the land of Mitzraym, we do not know what has become of him.’
And I said to them, ‘Whoever has any gold, let them break it off. So they gave it to me and I cast it into the fire and this goldcalf came out.
Now when Musha saw that the people were unrestrained (for Aarun had not restrained them, to their shame among their enemies),
Then Musha stood in the entrance of the camp and said, Whoever is on the side of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH come to me!” And all the sons of La'uy gathered themselves together to Musha.

And he said to them, “Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL: ‘Let every man put his sword on his side and go in and out from entrance to entrance throughout the camp and let every man kill his brother, every man his companion, and every man his neighbor.
So the sons of La'uy did according to the word of Musha. And about three thousand men of the people fell that day.
Then Musha said, Consecrate yourselves today to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that He may bestow on you a Baraka this day, for every man has opposed his son and his brother.”
Now it came to pass on the next day that Musha said to the people, “You have committed a great sin. So now I will go up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin.”
Then Musha returned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and said, Oh 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, these people have committed a great sin and have made for themselves an idol of gold!
Yet now, if You will forgive their sin, but if not, I pray, blot me out of Your book which You have written.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, Whoever has sinned against Me, I will blot him out of My book.

Now therefore, go, lead the people to the place of which I have spoken to you. Behold, My Malak shall go before you. Nevertheless, in the day when I visit for punishment, I will visit punishment upon them for their sin.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH plagued the people because of what they did with the calf which Aarun made.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Depart and go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought out of the land of Mitzraym, to the land of which I swore to Abraham, Yachaq, and Ya'aqub, saying, ‘To your descendants I will give it.’
And I will send My Malak before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite and the Amurite and the Hittite and the Parizzite and the Hibite and the Yabusite.
Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey; for I will not go up in your midst, lest I consume you on the way, for you are a stiff-necked people.”
And when the people heard this bad news, they mourned and no one put on his ornaments.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said to Musha, “Say to the children of Yashar'AL, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. I could come up into your midst in one moment and consume you. Now therefore, take off your ornaments, that I may know what to do to you.’ ”
So the children of Yashar'AL stripped themselves of their ornaments by Mount Hurab.

Musha took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and called it the tabernacle of meeting. And it came to pass that everyone who sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH went out to the tabernacle of meeting which was outside the camp.
So it was, whenever Musha went out to the tabernacle, that all the people rose, and each man stood at his tent door and watched Musha until he had gone into the tabernacle.
And it came to pass, when Musha entered the tabernacle, that the pillar of cloud descended and stood at the door of the tabernacle and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH talked with Musha.
All the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the tabernacle door and all the people rose and worshiped, each man in his tent door.

So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha face to face, as a man speaks to his friend, and Musha would return to the camp, but his servant Yahusha Ba'Nun (the son of Nun), a young man, did not depart from the tabernacle.

Then Musha said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “See, You say to me, ‘Bring up this people.’ But You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name and you have also found favour in My sight.
Now therefore, I pray, if I have found favour in Your sight, show me now Your way, that I may know You and that I may find favour in Your sight, and consider that this nation is Your people.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “My Presence will go with you and I will give you rest.”
Then Musha said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “If Your Presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here.

For how then will it be known that Your people and I have found Favour in Your sight, except You go with us? So we shall be separate, Your people and I, from all the people who are upon the face of the Arath.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “I will also do this thing that you have spoken; for you have found favour in My sight and I know you by name.”
And Musha said, “Please, show me Your Kabad.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “I will make all My goodness pass before you and I will proclaim My Name before you. I will be merciful to whomever I will be merciful to, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “You cannot see My face; for no man shall see Me and live.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “Look, stand near ME on this rock.
So it shall be, while My Kabad passes by, that I will put you in the cleft of the rock and will cover you with My hand while I pass by.
Then I will take away My hand and you shall see My back; but My face shall not be seen.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones. I will write on them the same words that were on the tablets you smashed.
Be ready in the morning to climb up Mount Sinai and present yourself to me on the top of the mountain.
No one else may come with you. In fact, no one is to appear anywhere on the mountain, do not even let the flocks or herds graze near the mountain.”
So Musha chiseled out two tablets of stone like the first ones. Early in the morning he climbed Mount Sinai as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him and he carried the two stone tablets in his hands.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came down in a cloud and stood there with Musha; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH called out His Own Name, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH passed in front of Musha, calling out, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of compassion and mercy! I AM slow to anger and filled with unfailing Ahabah (love) and Amunah (faithfulness).

I lavish unfailing Ahabah (love) to a thousand generations. I forgive iniquity, rebellion and sin. But I do not excuse the guilty. I lay the sins of the parents upon their children and grandchildren; the entire family is affected, even children in the third and fourth generations.”
Musha immediately threw himself to the ground and worshiped.

And Musha said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, if it is true that I have found favor with you, then please travel with us. Yes, this is a stubborn and rebellious people, but please forgive our iniquity and our sins. Claim us as your own special possession.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied, “Listen, I am making a covenant with you in the presence of all your people. I will perform miracles that have never been performed anywhere in all the Arath or in any nation. And all the people around you will see the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the awesome power I will display for you.
But listen carefully to everything I command you today. Then I will go ahead of you and drive out the Amurites, Canaanites, Hittites, Parizzites, Hibites, and Yabusites.
“Be very careful never to make a treaty with the people who live in the land where you are going. If you do, you will follow their evil ways and be trapped.
Instead, you must break down their pagan altars, smash their sacred pillars and cut down their Asharah poles.
You must worship no idols, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, whose very Name is Jealous, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty ONE) who is jealous about his relationship with you.

“You must not make a treaty of any kind with the people living in the land. They lust after their idols, offering sacrifices to them. They will invite you to join them in their sacrificial meals and you will go with them.

Then you will accept their daughters, who they have sacrifice to idols as wives for your sons and they will seduce your sons to commit adultery against me by worshiping other Aluahym (mighty ones/idols).
You must not make any idols of molten metal for yourselves.

“You must celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days the bread you eat must be made without yeast, just as I commanded you. Celebrate this festival annually at the appointed time in early spring, in the Moon (month) of Abib, for that is the anniversary of your departure from Mitzraym.
“The firstborn of every animal belongs to me, including the firstborn males from your herds of cattle and your flocks of sheep and goats.

A firstborn donkey may be bought back from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by presenting a lamb or young goat in its place. But if you do not buy it back, you must break its neck. However, you must buy back every firstborn son. “No one may appear before me without an offering.
“You have six days each week for your ordinary work, but on the seventh day you must stop working, even during the seasons of plowing and harvest.
“You must celebrate the Festival of Harvest with the first crop of the wheat harvest and celebrate the Festival of the Final Harvest at the end of the harvest season.
Three times each year every man in Yashar'AL must appear before ME 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
I will drive out the other nations ahead of you and expand your territory, so no one will covet and conquer your land while you appear before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH three times each year.
“You must not offer the blood of my sacrificial offerings together with any baked goods containing yeast. And none of the meat of the Passover sacrifice may be kept over until the next morning.
“As you harvest your crops, bring the very best of the first harvest to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, “Write down all these instructions, for they represent the terms of the covenant I AM making with you and with Yashar'AL.”

Musha remained there on the mountain with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH forty days and forty nights. In all that time he ate no bread and drank no water. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH wrote the terms of the covenant, the Ten Commandments on the stone tablets.
When Musha came down Mount Sinai carrying the two stone tablets inscribed with the terms of the covenant, he wasn’t aware that his face had become radiant because he had spoken to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
So when Aarun and the people of Yashar'AL saw the radiance of Musha's face, they were afraid to come near him.
But Musha called out to them and asked Aarun and all the leaders of the community to come over and he talked with them.
Then all the people of Yashar'AL approached him and Musha gave them all the instructions 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given him on Mount Sinai.
When Musha finished speaking with them, he covered his face with a veil.

But whenever he went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he would remove the veil until he came out again. Then he would give the people whatever instructions 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given him,
And the people of Yashar'AL would see the radiant glow of his face. So Musha would put the veil over his face until he returned to speak with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then Musha called together the whole community of Yashar'AL and told them, “These are the instructions 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded you to follow.

You have six days each week for your ordinary work, but the seventh day must be a Shabbat day of complete rest, a Qadash (Set Apart) day dedicated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Anyone who works on that day must be put to death.
You must not even light a fire in any of your homes on the Shabbat.
Then Musha said to the whole community of Yashar'AL, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded:
Take a sacred offering for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Let those with generous hearts present the following gifts to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: gold, silver, and bronze;
Blue, purple and scarlet thread; fine linen and goat hair for cloth;
Tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather; acacia wood;
Olive oil for the lamps; spices for the anointing oil and the fragrant incense;
Onyx stones and other gemstones to be set in the ephod and the kuhan’s chestpiece.
“Come, all of you who are gifted craftsmen. Construct everything that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded:
The Tabernacle and its sacred tent, its covering, clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
The Ark and its carrying poles; the Ark’s cover, the place of atonement and the inner curtain to shield the Ark;
The table, its carrying poles, and all its utensils; the Bread of the Presence;
For light, the lampstand, its accessories, the lamp cups and the olive oil for lighting;
The incense altar and its carrying poles; the anointing oil and fragrant incense; the curtain for the entrance of the Tabernacle;
The altar of burnt offering; the bronze grating of the altar and its carrying poles and utensils; the washbasin with its stand;
The curtains for the walls of the courtyard; the posts and their bases; the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard;
The tent pegs of the Tabernacle and courtyard and their ropes;

The beautifully stitched garments for the Kuhanym to wear while ministering in the Qadash Place the sacred garments for Aarun the Kuhan (priest), and the garments for his sons to wear as they minister as Kuhanym.”
So the whole community of Yashar'AL left Musha and returned to their tents.

All whose hearts were stirred and whose spirits were moved came and brought their Qadash offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. They brought all the materials needed for the Tabernacle, for the performance of its rituals, and for the sacred garments.

Both men and women came, all whose hearts were willing. They brought to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their offerings of gold—brooches, earrings, rings from their fingers, and necklaces. They presented gold objects of every kind as a special offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
All those who owned the following items willingly brought them: blue, purple, and scarlet thread; fine linen and goat hair for cloth; and tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather.
And all who had silver and bronze objects gave them as a sacred offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And those who had acacia wood brought it for use in the project.
All the women who were skilled in sewing and spinning prepared blue, purple and scarlet thread and fine linen cloth.
All the women who were willing used their skills to spin the goat hair into yarn.
The leaders brought onyx stones and the special gemstones to be set in the ephod and the Kuhan’s chestpiece.
They also brought spices and olive oil for the light, the anointing and the fragrant incense.
So the people of Yashar'AL every man and woman who was eager to help in the work 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 YAHUAH had given them through Musha, brought their gifts and gave them freely to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 YAHUAH.
Then Musha told the people of Yashar'AL, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has specifically chosen Bazalal son of Uri, grandson of Hur, of the tribe of Yahudah.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has filled Bazalal with the Ruach of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, giving him great wisdom, ability and expertise in all kinds of crafts.
He is a master craftsman, expert in working with gold, silver and bronze.
He is skilled in engraving and mounting gemstones and in carving wood, he is a master at every craft.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given both him and Uhuliab son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach their skills to others.
Also 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 YAHUAH has given them special skills as engravers, designers, embroiderers in blue, purple, and scarlet thread on fine linen cloth and weavers, they excel as craftsmen and as designers.

“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has gifted Bazalal, Uhuliab and the other skilled craftsmen with wisdom and ability to perform any task involved in building the sanctuary, let them construct and furnish the Tabernacle, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded.”
So Musha summoned Bazalal and Uhuliab and all the others who were specially gifted by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and were eager to get to work.
Musha gave them the materials donated by the people of Yashar'AL as sacred offerings for the completion of the sanctuary, but the people continued to bring additional gifts each morning.
Finally the craftsmen who were working on the sanctuary left their work.
They went to Musha and reported, “The people have given more than enough materials to complete the job our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has commanded us to do!”

So Musha gave the command and this message was sent throughout the camp: “Men and women, do not prepare any more gifts for the sanctuary, we have enough!” So the people stopped bringing their sacred offerings.
Their contributions were more than enough to complete the whole project.
The skilled craftsmen made ten curtains of finely woven linen for the Tabernacle, then Bazalal decorated the curtains with blue, purple and scarlet thread and with skillfully embroidered charubim.
All ten curtains were exactly the same size, 42 feet long and 6 feet wide.
Five of these curtains were joined together to make one long curtain and the other five were joined to make a second long curtain.
Bazalal made fifty loops of blue yarn and put them along the edge of the last curtain in each set.
The fifty loops along the edge of one curtain matched the fifty loops along the edge of the other curtain.
Then Bazalal made fifty gold clasps and fastened the long curtains together with the clasps. In this way, the Tabernacle was made of one continuous piece.
Bazalal made eleven curtains of goat-hair cloth to serve as a tent covering for the Tabernacle.
These eleven curtains were all exactly the same size—45 feet long and 6 feet wide.
Bazalal joined five of these curtains together to make one long curtain and the other six were joined to make a second long curtain.
He made fifty loops for the edge of each large curtain.
He also made fifty bronze clasps to fasten the long curtains together. In this way, the tent covering was made of one continuous piece.
Bazalal completed the tent covering with a layer of tanned ram skins and a layer of fine goatskin leather.
For the framework of the Tabernacle, Bezalal constructed frames of acacia wood.
Each frame was 15 feet high and 27 inches wide,
with two pegs under each frame. All the frames were identical.
He made twenty of these frames to support the curtains on the south side of the Tabernacle.
He also made forty silver bases, two bases under each frame, with the pegs fitting securely into the bases.
For the north side of the Tabernacle, he made another twenty frames,
with their forty silver bases, two bases under each frame.
Bazalal made six frames for the rear, the west side of the Tabernacle
Along with two additional frames to reinforce the rear corners of the Tabernacle.
These corner frames were matched at the bottom and firmly attached at the top with a single ring, forming a single corner unit, both of these corner units were made the same way.
So there were eight frames at the rear of the Tabernacle, set in sixteen silver bases, two bases under each frame.
Then Bazalal made crossbars of acacia wood to link the frames, five crossbars for the north side of the Tabernacle
And five for the south side, he also made five crossbars for the rear of the Tabernacle, which faced west.
He made the middle crossbar to attach halfway up the frames; it ran all the way from one end of the Tabernacle to the other.
Bazalal also overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. Then he overlaid the crossbars with gold as well.
For the inside of the Tabernacle, Bazalal made a special curtain of finely woven linen, he decorated it with blue, purple and scarlet thread, with skillfully embroidered Karubim.
For the curtain, Bazalal made four posts of acacia wood and four gold hooks, he overlaid the posts with gold and set them in four silver bases.
Then Bazalal made another curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent, he made it of finely woven linen and embroidered it with exquisite designs using blue, purple and scarlet thread.
This curtain was hung on gold hooks attached to five posts, the posts with their decorated tops and hooks were overlaid with gold and the five bases were cast from bronze.
Then Bazalal made the ark of acacia wood; two and a half cubits was its length, a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold all around it.
And he cast for it four rings of gold to be set in its four corners: two rings on one side, and two rings on the other side of it.
He made poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
And he put the poles into the rings at the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
He also made the mercy seat of pure gold; two and a half cubits was its length and a cubit and a half its width.
Bazalal also made two charubim of beaten gold; he made them of one piece at the two ends of the mercy seat:
One charub at one end on this side, and the other charub at the other end on that side, he made the charubim at the two ends of one piece with the mercy seat.
The charubim spread out their wings above, and covered the mercy seat with their wings. They faced one another; the faces of the charubim were toward the mercy seat.
Bazalal made the table of acacia wood; two cubits was its length, a cubit its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made a molding of gold all around it.
Also he made a frame of a handbreadth all around it, and made a molding of gold for the frame all around it.
And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings on the four corners that were at its four legs.
The rings were close to the frame, as holders for the poles to bear the table.
And he made the poles of acacia wood to bear the table, and overlaid them with gold.
He made of pure gold the utensils which were on the table: its dishes, its cups, its bowls, and its pitchers for pouring.
Then Bazalal made the lampstand of pure, hammered gold, he made the entire lampstand and its decorations of one piece, the base, center stem, lamp cups, buds, and petals.
The lampstand had six branches going out from the center stem, three on each side.
Each of the six branches had three lamp cups shaped like almond blossoms, complete with buds and petals.
The center stem of the lampstand was crafted with four lamp cups shaped like almond blossoms, complete with buds and petals.
There was an almond bud beneath each pair of branches where the six branches extended from the center stem, all made of one piece.
The almond buds and branches were all of one piece with the center stem, and they were hammered from pure gold.
He also made seven lamps for the lampstand, lamp snuffers, and trays, all of pure gold.
The entire lampstand, along with its accessories, was made from 75 pounds of pure gold.
He made the incense altar of acacia wood. Its length was a cubit and its width a cubit, it was square and two cubits was its height. Its horns were of one piece with it.
And Bazalal overlaid it with pure gold: its top, its sides all around, and its horns, he also made for it a molding of gold all around it.
He made two rings of gold for it under its molding, by its two corners on both sides, as holders for the poles with which to bear it.
And Bazalal also made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
Then he made the sacred anointing oil and the fragrant incense, using the techniques of a skilled incense maker.
Bazalal made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood; five cubits was its length and five cubits its width, it was square and its height was three cubits.
He made its horns on its four corners; the horns were of one piece with it. And he overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the utensils for the altar: the pans, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the firepans; all its utensils he made of bronze.
And he made a grate of bronze network for the altar, under its rim, midway from the bottom.
He cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles.
And he made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with bronze.
Then he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, with which to bear it. He made the altar hollow with boards.
He made the laver of bronze and its base of bronze, from the bronze mirrors of the serving women who assembled at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
Then he made the court on the south side; the hangings of the court were of fine woven linen, one hundred cubits long.
There were twenty pillars for them, with twenty bronze sockets. The hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
On the north side the hangings were one hundred cubits long, with twenty pillars and their twenty bronze sockets. The hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
And on the west side there were hangings of fifty cubits, with ten pillars and their ten sockets. The hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
For the east side the hangings were fifty cubits.
The hangings of one side of the gate were fifteen cubits long, with their three pillars and their three sockets,
And the same for the other side of the court gate; on this side and that were hangings of fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
All the hangings of the court all around were of fine woven linen.
The sockets for the pillars were bronze, the hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver, and the overlay of their capitals was silver; and all the pillars of the court had bands of silver.

The screen for the gate of the court was woven of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and of fine woven linen. The length was twenty cubits, and the height along its width was five cubits, corresponding to the hangings of the court.
And there were four pillars with their four sockets of bronze; their hooks were silver, and the overlay of their capitals and their bands was silver.
All the pegs of the tabernacle, and of the court all around, were bronze.

This is the inventory of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the Testimony, which was counted according to the instructions of Musha, for the service of the La'uym, by the hand of Ithamar, son of Aarun the Kuhan (priest).
Bazalal the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Yahudah, made all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
And with Bazalal was Ahuliab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and designer, a weaver of blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and of fine linen.

All the gold that was used in all the work of the Qadash place, that is, the gold of the offering, was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.
And the silver from those who were numbered of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary:

A bekah for each man (that is, half a shekel, according to the shekel of the sanctuary), for everyone included in the numbering from twenty years old and above, for six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty men.
And from the hundred talents of silver were cast the sockets of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil: one hundred sockets from the hundred talents, one talent for each socket.
Then from the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their capitals, and made bands for them.
The offering of bronze was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
And with it he made the sockets for the door of the tabernacle of meeting, the bronze altar, the bronze grating for it, and all the utensils for the altar,
The sockets for the court all around, the bases for the court gate, all the pegs for the tabernacle, and all the pegs for the court all around.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet thread they made garments of ministry, for ministering in the Qadash place, and made the Qadash garments for Aarun, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
They made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and of fine woven linen.
And they beat the gold into thin sheets and cut it into threads, to work it in with the blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and the fine linen, into artistic designs.
They made shoulder straps for it to couple it together; it was coupled together at its two edges.
And the intricately woven band of his ephod that was on it was of the same workmanship, woven of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and of fine woven linen, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
And they set onyx stones, enclosed in settings of gold; they were engraved, as signets are engraved, with the names of the sons of Yashar'AL.
Bazalal put them on the shoulders of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Yashar'AL, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
And they made the breastplate, artistically woven like the workmanship of the ephod, of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and of fine woven linen.
They made the breastplate square by doubling it; a span was its length and a span its width when doubled.
And they set in it four rows of stones: a row with a sardius, a topaz, and an emerald was the first row;
The second row, a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
The fourth row, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. They were enclosed in settings of gold in their mountings.
There were twelve stones according to the names of the sons of Yashar'AL: according to their names, engraved like a signet, each one with its own name according to the twelve tribes.
And they made chains for the breastplate at the ends, like braided cords of pure gold.
They also made two settings of gold and two gold rings, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
And they put the two braided chains of gold in the two rings on the ends of the breastplate.
The two ends of the two braided chains they fastened in the two settings, and put them on the shoulder straps of the ephod in the front.
And they made two rings of gold and put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on the edge of it, which was on the inward side of the ephod.
They made two other gold rings and put them on the two shoulder straps, underneath the ephod toward its front, right at the seam above the intricately woven band of the ephod.

And they bound the breastplate by means of its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it would be above the intricately woven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate would not come loose from the ephod, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
Bazalal made the robe of the ephod of woven work, all of blue.
And there was an opening in the middle of the robe, like the opening in a coat of mail, with a woven binding all around the opening, so that it would not tear.
They made on the hem of the robe pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet, and of fine woven linen.
And they made bells of pure gold, and put the bells between the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around between the pomegranates:
A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe to minister in, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
They made tunics, artistically woven of fine linen, for Aarun and his sons,
A turban of fine linen, exquisite hats of fine linen, short trousers of fine woven linen,
And a sash of fine woven linen with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, made by a weaver, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
Then they made the plate of the Qadash crown of pure gold, and wrote on it an inscription like the engraving of a signet:
And they tied to it a blue cord, to fasten it above on the turban, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded Musha.
Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was finished, and the children of Yashar'AL did according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha; so they did.
And they brought the tabernacle to Musha, the tent and all its furnishings: its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;
The covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of badger skins, and the veil of the covering;
The ark of the Testimony with its poles, and the mercy seat;
the table, all its utensils, and the showbread;
The pure gold lampstand with its lamps (the lamps set in order), all its utensils, and the oil for light;
The gold altar, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense; the screen for the tabernacle door;
The bronze altar, its grate of bronze, its poles, and all its utensils; the laver with its base;
The hangings of the court, its pillars and its sockets, the screen for the court gate, its cords, and its pegs; all the utensils for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
And the garments of ministry, to minister in the Qadash place: the Qadash garments for Aarun the Kuhan, and his sons’ garments, to minister as Kuhanym (priests).
According to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha, so the children of Yashar'AL did all the work.
Then Musha looked over all the work, and indeed they had done it; as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded, just so they had done it. And Musha Baraked them.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, saying:
“On the first day of the first month you shall set up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
You shall put in it the ark of the Testimony, and partition off the ark with the veil.
You shall bring in the table and arrange the things that are to be set in order on it; and you shall bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.
You shall also set the altar of gold for the incense before the ark of the Testimony, and put up the screen for the door of the tabernacle.
Then you shall set the altar of the burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
And you shall set the laver between the tabernacle of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
You shall set up the court all around, and hang up the screen at the court gate.
“And you shall take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle and all that is in it; and you shall Qadash it and all its utensils, and it shall be Qadash.
You shall anoint the altar of the burnt offering and all its utensils, and consecrate the altar. The altar shall be most Qadash.
And you shall anoint the laver and its base, and consecrate it.
“Then you shall bring Aarun and his sons to the door of the tabernacle of meeting and wash them with water.
You shall put the Qadash garments on Aarun, and anoint him and consecrate him, that he may minister to Me as Kuhan (priest).
And you shall bring his sons and clothe them with tunics.
You shall anoint them, as you anointed their father, that they may minister to Me as Kuhanym; for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting Kuhanhood throughout their generations.”
Thus Musha did; according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him, so he did.
And it came to pass in the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was raised up.
So Musha raised up the tabernacle, fastened its sockets, set up its boards, put in its bars, and raised up its pillars.
And he spread out the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering of the tent on top of it, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
He took the Testimony and put it into the ark, inserted the poles through the rings of the ark, and put the mercy seat on top of the ark.
And he brought the ark into the tabernacle, hung up the veil of the covering, and partitioned off the ark of the Testimony, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
He put the table in the tabernacle of meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil;
And he set the bread in order upon it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
He put the lampstand in the tabernacle of meeting, across from the table, on the south side of the tabernacle;
And he lit the lamps before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him.
Musha put the gold altar in the tabernacle of meeting in front of the veil;
And Musha burned sweet incense on it, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him.
He hung up the screen at the door of the tabernacle.
And he put the altar of burnt offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered upon it the burnt offering and the grain offering, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
He set the laver between the tabernacle of meeting and the altar, and put water there for washing;
And Musha, Aarun, and his sons would wash their hands and their feet with water from it.
Whenever they went into the tabernacle of meeting, and when they came near the altar, they washed, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
And he raised up the court all around the tabernacle and the altar, and hung up the screen of the court gate. So Musha finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tabernacle of meeting, and the Kabad of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH filled the tabernacle.
For Musha was not able to enter the tabernacle of meeting, because the cloud rested above it, and the Kabad of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud was taken up from above the tabernacle, the children of Yashar'AL would go onward in all their journeys.
But if the cloud was not taken up, then they did not journey till the day that it was taken up.
For the cloud of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was above the tabernacle by day, and fire was over it by night, in the sight of all the house of Yashar'AL, throughout all their journeys.

books.name: Leviticus
chapters: Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH called to Musha, and Dabar to him from the tabernacle of meeting, saying,
“Speak to the children of Yashar'AL, and say to them: ‘When any one of you brings an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you shall bring your offering of the livestock of the herd and of the flock.
‘If his offering is a burnt sacrifice of the herd, let him offer a male without blemish; he shall offer it of his own free will at the door of the tabernacle of meeting before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then he shall put his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.

He shall kill the bull before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and the Kuhanym (priests), Aarun’s sons, shall bring the blood and sprinkle the blood all around on the altar that is by the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
And he shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces.
The sons of Aarun the Kuhan shall put fire on the altar, and lay the wood in order on the fire.
Then the Kuhanym, Aarun’s sons, shall lay the parts, the head, and the fat in order on the wood that is on the fire upon the altar;
But he shall wash its entrails and its legs with water. And the Kuhan shall burn all on the altar as a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
‘If his offering is of the flocks—of the sheep or of the goats—as a burnt sacrifice, he shall bring a male without blemish.
He shall kill it on the north side of the altar before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and the Kuhanym, Aarun’s sons, shall sprinkle its blood all around on the altar.
And he shall cut it into its pieces, with its head and its fat; and the Kuhan shall lay them in order on the wood that is on the fire upon the altar;
But he shall wash the entrails and the legs with water. Then the Kuhan shall bring it all and burn it on the altar; it is a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
‘And if the burnt sacrifice of his offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is of birds, then he shall bring his offering of turtledoves or young pigeons.
The Kuhan shall bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood shall be drained out at the side of the altar.
And he shall remove its crop with its feathers and cast it beside the altar on the east side, into the place for ashes.

Then he shall split it at its wings, but shall not divide it completely; and the Kuhan shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt sacrifice, an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
‘When anyone offers a grain offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, his offering shall be of fine flour, and he shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it.

He shall bring it to Aarun’s sons, the Kuhanym, one of whom shall take from it his handful of fine flour and oil with all the frankincense, and the Kuhan shall burn it as a memorial on the altar, an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The rest of the grain offering shall be Aarun’s and his sons’. It is most Qadash of the offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made by fire.
‘And if you bring as an offering a grain offering baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
But if your offering is a grain offering baked in a pan, it shall be of fine flour, unleavened, mixed with oil.
You shall break it in pieces and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
If your offering is a grain offering baked in a covered pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall bring the grain offering that is made of these things to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and when it is presented to the Kuhan, he shall bring it to the altar.
Then the Kuhan shall take from the grain offering a memorial portion, and burn it on the altar. It is an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And what is left of the grain offering shall be Aarun’s and his sons’. It is most Qadash of the offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made by fire.
‘No grain offering which you bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH shall be made with leaven, for you shall burn no leaven nor any honey in any offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made by fire.
As for the offering of the firstfruits, you shall offer them to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but they shall not be burned on the altar for a sweet aroma.

And every offering of your grain offering you shall season with salt; you shall not allow the salt of the covenant of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH to be lacking from your grain offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.
‘If you offer a grain offering of your firstfruits to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you shall offer for the grain offering of your firstfruits green heads of grain roasted on the fire, grain beaten from full heads.
And you shall put oil on it, and lay frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
Then the Kuhan shall burn the memorial portion: part of its beaten grain and part of its oil, with all the frankincense, as an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
When a Yashar'AL is offering a sacrifice of a Shalum offering, if he offers it of the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without blemish before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the tabernacle of meeting; and Aarun’s sons, the Kuhanym, shall sprinkle the blood all around on the altar.
Then he shall offer from the sacrifice of the Shalum offering an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. The fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
The two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the flanks, and the fatty lobe attached to the liver above the kidneys, he shall remove;
And Aarun’s sons shall burn it on the altar upon the burnt sacrifice, which is on the wood that is on the fire, as an offering made by fire, a sweet aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
If his offering as a sacrifice of a Shalum offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is of the flock, whether male or female, he shall offer it without blemish.
If he offers a lamb as his offering, then he shall offer it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it before the tabernacle of meeting; and Aarun’s sons shall sprinkle its blood all around on the altar.

‘Then he shall offer from the sacrifice of the Shalum offering, as an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, its fat and the whole fat tail which he shall remove close to the backbone, and the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
The two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the flanks, and the fatty lobe attached to the liver above the kidneys, he shall remove;
And the Kuhan shall burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
‘And if his offering is a goat, then he shall offer it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
He shall lay his hand on its head and kill it before the tabernacle of meeting; and the sons of Aarun shall sprinkle its blood all around on the altar.
Then he shall offer from it his offering, as an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. The fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
The two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the flanks, and the fatty lobe attached to the liver above the kidneys, he shall remove;
And the Kuhan shall burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire for a sweet aroma; all the fat is for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
‘This shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings: you shall not eat neither fat nor blood.’
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Give the following instructions to the people of Yashar'AL. This is how you are to deal with those who sin unintentionally by doing anything that violates one of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s commands.
“If the high Kuhan sins, bringing guilt upon the entire community, he must give a sin offering for the sin he has committed, he must present to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH a young bull with no defects.
He must bring the bull to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at the entrance of the Tabernacle, lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The high Kuhan will then take some of the bull’s blood into the Tabernacle,
Dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in front of the inner curtain of the sanctuary.

The Kuhan will then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar for fragrant incense that stands in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH inside the Tabernacle, he will pour out the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar for burnt offerings at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
Then the Kuhan must remove all the fat of the bull to be offered as a sin offering. This includes all the fat around the internal organs,
The two kidneys and the fat around them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver. He must remove these along with the kidneys,
Just as he does with cattle offered as a Shalum offering, and burn them on the altar of burnt offerings.
But he must take whatever is left of the bull, its hide, meat, head, legs, internal organs, and dung,
And carry it away to a place outside the camp that is ceremonially clean, the place where the ashes are dumped. There on the ash heap, he will burn it on a wood fire.
“If the entire Yasharalym community sins by violating one of the Commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but the people do not realize it, they are still guilty.
When they become aware of their sin, the people must bring a young bull as an offering for their sin and present it before the Tabernacle.
The elders of the community must then lay their hands on the bull’s head and slaughter it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The high Kuhan will then take some of the bull’s blood into the Tabernacle,
Dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in front of the inner curtain.

He will then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar for fragrant incense that stands in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH inside the Tabernacle, he will pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar for burnt offerings at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
Then the Kuhan must remove all the animal’s fat and burn it on the altar,
Just as he does with the bull offered as a sin offering for the high Kuhan. Through this process, the Kuhan will purify the people, making them right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and they will be forgiven.

Then the Kuhan must take what is left of the bull and carry it outside the camp and burn it there, just as is done with the sin offering for the high Kuhan. This offering is for the sin of the entire congregation of Yashar'AL.
“If one of Yashar'AL leaders sins by violating one of the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH but does not realize it, he is still guilty.
When he becomes aware of his sin, he must bring as his offering a male goat with no defects.
He must lay his hand on the goat’s head and slaughter it at the place where burnt offerings are slaughtered before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. This is an offering for his sin.
Then the Kuhan will dip his finger in the blood of the sin offering and put it on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings. He will pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

Then he must burn all the goat’s fat on the altar, just as he does with the Shalum offering. Through this process, the Kuhan will purify the leader from his sin, making him right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and he will be forgiven.
“If any of the common people sin by violating one of the Commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but they don’t realize it, they are still guilty.
When they become aware of their sin, they must bring as an offering for their sin a female goat with no defects.
They must lay a hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place where burnt offerings are slaughtered.
Then the Kuhan will dip his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings, he will pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

Then he must remove all the goat’s fat, just as he does with the fat of the Shalum offering. He will burn the fat on the altar, and it will be a pleasing aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Through this process, the Kuhan will purify the people, making them right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and they will be forgiven.
“If the people bring a sheep as their sin offering, it must be a female with no defects.
They must lay a hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place where burnt offerings are slaughtered.
Then the Kuhan will dip his finger in the blood of the sin offering and put it on the horns of the altar for burnt offerings. He will pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

Then he must remove all the sheep’s fat, just as he does with the fat of a sheep presented as a Shalum offering. He will burn the fat on the altar on top of the special gifts presented to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Through this process, the Kuhan will purify the people from their sin, making them right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and they will be forgiven.
“If you are called to testify about something you have seen or that you know about, it is sinful to refuse to testify, and you will be punished for your sin.

“Or suppose you unknowingly touch something that is ceremonially unclean, such as the carcass of an unclean animal. When you realize what you have done, you must admit your defilement and your guilt, this is true whether it is a wild animal, a domestic animal, or an animal that scurries along the ground.
“Or suppose you unknowingly touch something that makes a person unclean. When you realize what you have done, you must admit your guilt.
“Or suppose you make a foolish vow of any kind, whether its purpose is for good or for bad. When you realize its foolishness, you must admit your guilt.
“When you become aware of your guilt in any of these ways, you must confess your sin.

Then you must bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as the penalty for your sin a female from the flock, either a sheep or a goat. This is a sin offering with which the Kuhan will purify you from your sin, making you right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

“But if you cannot afford to bring a sheep, you may bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH two turtledoves or two young pigeons as the penalty for your sin. One of the birds will be for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.
You must bring them to the Kuhan, who will present the first bird as the sin offering, he will wring its neck but without severing its head from the body.
Then he will sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering against the sides of the altar, and the rest of the blood will be drained out at the base of the altar. This is an offering for sin.

The Kuhan will then prepare the second bird as a burnt offering, following all the procedures that have been prescribed. Through this process the Kuhan will purify you from your sin, making you right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and you will be forgiven.

“If you cannot afford to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, you may bring two quarts of choice flour for your sin offering. Since it is an offering for sin, you must not moisten it with olive oil or put any frankincense on it.
Take the flour to the Kuhan, who will scoop out a handful as a representative portion. He will burn it on the altar on top of the special gifts presented to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. It is an offering for sin.

Through this process, the Kuhan will purify those who are guilty of any of these sins, making them right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and they will be forgiven, the rest of the flour will belong to the Kuhan, just as with the grain offering.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,

“If one of you commits a sin by unintentionally defiling the sacred property of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you must bring a guilt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. The offering must be your own ram with no defects, or you may buy one of equal value with silver, as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel.

You must make restitution for the sacred property you have harmed by paying for the loss, plus an additional 20 percent, when you give the payment to the Kuhan, he will purify you with the ram sacrificed as a guilt offering, making you right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and you will be forgiven.
“Suppose you sin by violating one of the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Even if you are unaware of what you have done, you are guilty and will be punished for your sin.

For a guilt offering, you must bring to the Kuhan your own ram with no defects, or you may buy one of equal value, through this process the Kuhan will purify you from your unintentional sin, making you right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and you will be forgiven.
This is a guilt offering, for you have been guilty of an offense against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Suppose one of you sins against your associate and is unfaithful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Suppose you cheat in a deal involving a security deposit, or you steal or commit fraud,
Or you find lost property and lie about it, or you lie while swearing to tell the truth, or you commit any other such sin.
If you have sinned in any of these ways, you are guilty. You must give back whatever you stole, or the money you took by extortion, or the security deposit, or the lost property you found,

Or anything obtained by swearing falsely. You must make restitution by paying the full price plus an additional 20 percent to the person you have harmed. On the same day you must present a guilt offering.
As a guilt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you must bring to the Kuhan your own ram with no defects, or you may buy one of equal value.
Through this process, the Kuhan will purify you before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, making you right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and you will be forgiven for any of these sins you have committed.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,

“Give Aarun and his sons the following instructions regarding the burnt offering, the burnt offering must be left on top of the altar until the next morning, and the fire on the altar must be kept burning all night.
In the morning, after the Kuhan on duty has put on his official linen clothing and linen undergarments, he must clean out the ashes of the burnt offering and put them beside the altar.
Then he must take off these garments, change back into his regular clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a place that is ceremonially clean.

Meanwhile, the fire on the altar must be kept burning; it must never go out. Each morning the Kuhan will add fresh wood to the fire and arrange the burnt offering on it. He will then burn the fat of the Shalum offerings on it.
Remember, the fire must be kept burning on the altar at all times. It must never go out.
“These are the instructions regarding the grain offering. Aarun’s sons must present this offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in front of the altar.

The Kuhan on duty will take from the grain offering a handful of the choice flour moistened with olive oil, together with all the frankincense he will burn this representative portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Aarun and his sons may eat the rest of the flour, but it must be baked without yeast and eaten in a sacred place within the courtyard of the Tabernacle.
Remember, it must never be prepared with yeast. I have given it to the Kuhanym as their share of the special gifts presented to me. Like the sin offering and the guilt offering, it is most Qadash.

Any of Aarun’s male descendants may eat from the special gifts presented to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. This is their permanent right from generation to generation. Anyone or anything that touches these offerings will become Qadash.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,

“On the day Aarun and his sons are anointed, they must present to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the standard grain offering of two quarts of choice flour, half to be offered in the morning and half to be offered in the evening.
It must be carefully mixed with olive oil and cooked on a griddle, then slice this grain offering and present it as a pleasing aroma to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
In each generation, the high Kuhan who succeeds Aarun must prepare this same offering. It belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and must be burned up completely, this is a permanent law.
All such grain offerings of a Kuhan must be burned up entirely. None of it may be eaten.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,

“Give Aarun and his sons the following instructions regarding the sin offering. The animal given as an offering for sin is a most Qadash offering, and it must be slaughtered in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.
The Kuhan who offers the sacrifice as a sin offering must eat his portion in a sacred place within the courtyard of the Tabernacle.
Anyone or anything that touches the sacrificial meat will become Qadash. If any of the sacrificial blood spatters on a person’s clothing, the soiled garment must be washed in a sacred place.
If a clay pot is used to boil the sacrificial meat, it must then be broken. If a bronze pot is used, it must be scoured and thoroughly rinsed with water.
Any male from a Kuhan’s family may eat from this offering; it is most Qadash.
But the offering for sin may not be eaten if its blood was brought into the Tabernacle as an offering for purification in the Qadash Place. It must be completely burned with fire.
These are the instructions for the guilt offering. It is most Qadash.
The animal sacrificed as a guilt offering must be slaughtered at the place where the burnt offerings are slaughtered, and its blood must be splattered against all sides of the altar.
The Kuhan will then offer all its fat on the altar, including the fat of the broad tail, the fat around the internal organs,
The two kidneys and the fat around them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver. These are to be removed with the kidneys,
And the Kuhanym will burn them on the altar as a special gift presented to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. This is the guilt offering.
Any male from a Kuhan’s family may eat the meat. It must be eaten in a sacred place, for it is most Qadash.
“The same instructions apply to both the guilt offering and the sin offering, both belong to the Kuhan who uses them to purify someone, making that person right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
In the case of the burnt offering, the Kuhan may keep the skin of the sacrificed animal.
Any grain offering that has been baked in an oven, prepared in a pan, or cooked on a griddle belongs to the Kuhan who presents it.
All other grain offerings, whether made of dry flour or flour moistened with olive oil, are to be shared equally among all the Kuhanym, the descendants of Aarun.
“These are the instructions regarding the different kinds of Shalum offerings that may be presented to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

If you present your Shalum offering as an expression of thanksgiving, the usual animal sacrifice must be accompanied by various kinds of bread made without yeast—thin cakes mixed with olive oil, wafers spread with oil, and cakes made of choice flour mixed with olive oil.
This Shalum offering of thanksgiving must also be accompanied by loaves of bread made with yeast.
One of each kind of bread must be presented as a gift to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. It will then belong to the Kuhan who splatters the blood of the Shalum offering against the altar.
The meat of the Shalum offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the same day it is offered. None of it may be saved for the next morning.
“If you bring an offering to fulfill a vow or as a voluntary offering, the meat must be eaten on the same day the sacrifice is offered, but whatever is left over may be eaten on the second day.
Any meat left over until the third day must be completely burned up.

If any of the meat from the Shalum offering is eaten on the third day, the person who presented it will not be accepted by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. You will receive no credit for offering it. By then the meat will be contaminated; if you eat it, you will be punished for your sin.
“Meat that touches anything ceremonially unclean may not be eaten; it must be completely burned up. The rest of the meat may be eaten, but only by people who are ceremonially clean.
If you are ceremonially unclean and you eat meat from a Shalum offering that was presented to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you will be cut off from the community.

If you touch anything that is unclean, whether it is man's defilement or an unclean animal or any other unclean, detestable thing and then eat meat from a Shalum offering presented to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you will be cut off from the community.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Give the following instructions to the people of Yashar'AL. You must never eat fat, whether from cattle, sheep, or goats.
The fat of an animal found dead or torn to pieces by wild animals must never be eaten, though it may be used for any other purpose.
Anyone who eats fat from an animal presented as a special gift to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, will be cut off from the community.
No matter where you live, you must never consume the blood of any bird or animal.
Anyone who consumes blood will be cut off from the community.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha,
“Give the following instructions to the people of Yashar'AL. When you present a Shalum offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, bring part of it as a gift to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Present it to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 YAHUAH with your own hands as a special gift to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Bring the fat of the animal, together with the breast, and lift up the breast as a special offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then the Kuhan will burn the fat on the altar, but the breast will belong to Aarun and his descendants.
Give the right thigh of your Shalum offering to the Kuhan as a gift.
The right thigh must always be given to the Kuhan who offers the blood and the fat of the Shalum offering.

For I have reserved the breast of the special offering and the right thigh of the sacred offering for the Kuhanym. It is the permanent right of Aarun and his descendants to share in the Shalum offerings brought by the people of Yashar'AL.
This is their rightful share. The special gifts presented to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have been reserved for Aarun and his descendants from the time they were set apart to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as Kuhanym.
On the day they were anointed, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded the Yasharalym to give these portions to the Kuhanym as their permanent share from generation to generation.”
These are the instructions for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, as well as the ordination offering and the Shalum offering.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave these instructions to Musha on Mount Sinai when he commanded the Yasharalym to present their offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the wilderness of Sinai.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, saying:
Take Aarun and his sons with him, and the garments, the anointing oil, a bull as the sin offering, two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread;
And gather all the congregation together at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.”
So Musha did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded him, and the congregation was gathered together at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
And Musha said to the congregation, this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded to be done.”
Then Musha brought Aarun and his sons and washed them with water.

And Musha put the tunic on Aarun, girded him with the sash, clothed him with the robe, and put the ephod on him; and he girded him with the intricately woven band of the ephod, and with it tied the ephod on him.
Then Musha put the breastplate on Aarun, and he put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastplate.
And Musha put the turban on the head of Aarun, also on the turban, on its front, he put the golden plate, the Qadash crown, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
Also Musha took the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle and all that was in it, and consecrated them.
He sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times, anointed the altar and all its utensils, and the laver and its base, to consecrate them.
And Musha poured some of the anointing oil on Aarun’s head and anointed him, to consecrate him.
Then Musha brought Aarun’s sons and put tunics on them, girded them with sashes, and put hats on them, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him.
And Musha brought the bull for the sin offering, then Aarun and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull for the sin offering,

And Musha killed it. Then he took the blood, and put some on the horns of the altar all around with his finger, and purified the altar. And he poured the blood at the base of the altar, and consecrated it, to make atonement for it.
Then Musha took all the fat that was on the entrails, the fatty lobe attached to the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and Musha burned them on the altar.
But the bull, its hide, its flesh, and its offal, he burned with fire outside the camp, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
Then he brought the ram as the burnt offering, and Aarun and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram,
And Musha killed it. Then he sprinkled the blood all around on the altar.
And he cut the ram into pieces; and Musha burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.

Then he washed the entrails and the legs in water, and Musha burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt sacrifice for a sweet aroma, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.
And he brought the second ram, the ram of consecration. Then Aarun and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram,
And Musha killed it. Also he took some of its blood and put it on the tip of Aarun’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

Then Musha brought Aarun’s sons and he put some of the blood on the tips of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet, and Musha sprinkled the blood all around on the altar.
Then he took the fat and the fat tail, all the fat that was on the entrails, the fatty lobe attached to the liver, the two kidneys and their fat, and the right thigh;

On top of these he placed a thin cake of bread made without yeast, a cake of bread mixed with olive oil, and a wafer spread with olive oil. All these were taken from the basket of bread made without yeast that was placed in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s presence.
And Musha put all these in Aarun’s hands and in his sons’ hands, and waved them as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then Musha took them from their hands and burned them on the altar, on the burnt offering. They were consecration offerings for a sweet aroma. That was an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And Musha took the breast and waved it as a wave offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. It was Musha's part of the ram of consecration, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded him.

Then Musha took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood which was on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aarun, on his garments, and on the garments of his sons with him; and Musha consecrated Aarun, his garments, his sons, and the garments of his sons with him.

And Musha said to Aarun and his sons, “Boil the flesh at the door of the tabernacle of meeting, and eat it there with the bread that is in the basket of consecration offerings, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded, saying, ‘Aarun and his sons shall eat it.’
What remains of the flesh and of the bread you shall burn with fire.
And you shall not go outside the door of the tabernacle of meeting for seven days, until the days of your consecration are ended. For seven days Musha shall consecrate you Aarun.
As he has done this day, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded to do, to make atonement for you.
