For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent him to perform all the miraculous signs and wonders in the land of Mitzraym against Phar'uh, and all his servants, and his entire land.
With mighty power, Musha performed terrifying acts in the sight of all Yashar'AL.

books.name: Joshua
chapters: After the death of Musha the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, it came to pass that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha Ba'Nun (son of Nun), Musha's assistant.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, Musha my servant is dead. Therefore, the time has come for you Yahusha Ba'Nun to lead these people, the Yasharalym, across the Yurdan River into the land I am giving them.
Every place that the sole of your foot will tread upon I have given you, as I Dabar to Musha.
from the Nagab wilderness in the south to the Labanun mountains in the north, from the Euphratas River in the east to the Maditerranaan Sea in the west, including all the land of the Hittites.’
No one will be able to stand against you as long as you live. For I will be with you as I was with Musha. I will not fail you or abandon you.
“Be strong and courageous, for you are the one who will lead these people to possess all the land I swore to their ancestors I would give them.

Only be strong and very courageous, that you may observe to do according to all the law which Musha My servant commanded you, do not turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may prosper wherever you go.
Study this Book of the Laws and Instruction continually. Meditate on it day and night so you will be sure to obey everything written in it. Only then will you prosper and succeed in all you do.
This is my command to you, be strong and courageous! Do not be afraid or discouraged. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is with you wherever you go.”
Yahusha then commanded the officers of Yashar'AL,
“Go through the camp and tell the people to get their provisions ready. In three days you will cross the Yurdan River and take possession of the land 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given you.”
Then Yahusha called together the tribes of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah. He told them,
“Remember what Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, commanded you: ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has giving you a place of rest. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you this land.’

Your wives, children, and livestock may remain here in the land Musha assigned to you on the east side of the Yurdan River. But your strong warriors, fully armed, must lead the other tribes across the Yurdan to help them conquer their territory. Stay with them

until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives them rest, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you rest, and until they have possess the land 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has giving them. Only then may you return and settle here on the east side of the Yurdan River in the land that Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, assigned to you.”
They answered Yahusha, “We will do whatever you command us, and we will go wherever you send us.
We will obey you just as we obeyed Musha. And may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be with you as he was with Musha.
Anyone who rebels against your orders and does not obey your words and everything you command will be put to death. So be strong and courageous!”

Then Yahusha Ba'Nun secretly sent out two spies from the Yasharalym camp at Acacia Grove, he instructed them, “Scout out the land on the other side of the Yurdan River, especially around Yarichu.” So the two men set out and came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there that night.
But someone told the king of Yarichu, “Some Yasharalym have come here tonight to spy out the land.”
So the king of Yarichu sent orders to Rahab: “Bring out the men who have come into your house, for they have come here to spy out the whole land.”
Rahab had hidden the two men, but she replied, “Yes, the men were here earlier, but I did not know where they were from.
They left the town at dusk, as the gates were about to close. I do not know where they went. If you hurry, you can probably catch up with them.”
Actually, she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them beneath bundles of flax she had laid out.
So the king’s men went looking for the spies along the road leading to the shallow crossings of the Yurdan river, and as soon as the king’s men had left, the gate of Yarichu was shut.
Before the spies went to sleep that night, Rahab went up on the roof to talk with them.
“I know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you this land,” she told them. “We are all afraid of you. Everyone in the land is living in terror.

For we have heard how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made a dry path for you through the Red Sea when you left Mitzraym, and we know what you did to Sihun and Ug, the two Amurite kings east of the Yurdan River, whose people you completely destroyed.

No wonder our hearts have melted in fear! No one has the courage to fight after hearing such things. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is the supreme 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Shamaym above and the Arath below.
“Now swear to me by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that you will be kind to me and my family since I have helped you, give me some guarantee that
when Yarichu is conquered, you will let me live, along with my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all their families.”
“We offer our own lives as a guarantee for your safety,” the men agreed. “If you do not betray us, we will keep our promise and be kind to you when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives us the land.
Then, since Rahab’s house was built into the town wall, she let them down by a rope through the window.
“Escape to the hill country,” she told them. “Hide there for three days from the men searching for you. Then, when they have returned, you can go on your way.”
Before they left, the men told her, “We will be bound by the oath we have taken only if you follow these instructions.

When we come into the land, you must leave this scarlet rope hanging from the window through which you let us down, and all your family members, your father, mother, brothers, and all your relatives must be here inside the house.
If they go out into the street and are killed, it will not be our fault. But if anyone lays a hand on people inside this house, we will accept the responsibility for their death.
If you betray us, however, we are not bound by this oath in any way.”
“I accept your terms,” she replied, and she sent them on their way, leaving the scarlet rope hanging from the window.
The spies went up into the hill country and stayed there three days. The men who were chasing them searched everywhere along the road, but they finally returned without success.
Then the two spies came down from the hill country, crossed the Yurdan River, and reported to Yahusha Ba'Nun all that had happened to them.
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given us the whole land,” they said, “for all the people in the land are terrified of us.”
Early the next morning Yahusha Ba'Nun and all the Yasharalym left Acacia Grove and arrived at the banks of the Yurdan River, where they camped before crossing.
Three days later the Yasharalym officers went through the camp,
giving these instructions to the people: “When you see the Lauym and Kuhanym (priests) carrying the Ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, move out from your positions and follow them.
Since you have never traveled this way before, they will guide you. Stay about half a mile behind them, keeping a clear distance between you and the Ark. Make sure you do not come any closer.”
Then Yahusha told the people, “Purify yourselves, for tomorrow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will do great wonders among you.”
In the morning Yahusha Ba'Nun said to the Kuhanym, “Lift up the Ark of the Covenant and lead the people across the river.” And so they started out and went ahead of the people.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha, “Today I will begin to make you a great leader in the eyes of all the Yasharalym. They will know that I am with you, just as I was with Musha.
Give this command to the Kuhanym who carry the Ark of the Covenant: ‘When you reach the banks of the Yurdan River, take a few steps into the river and stop there.’”
So Yahusha told the Yasharalym, “Come and listen to what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has said.
Today you will know that the living 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is among you. He will surely drive out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hibites, Parizzites, Girgashites, Amurites, and Yabusites ahead of you.
Look, the Ark of the Covenant, which belongs to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the whole Arath, will lead you across the Yurdan River!
Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Yashar'AL, one from each tribe.

The Kuhanym will carry the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of all the Arath. As soon as their feet touch the water, the flow of water will be cut off upstream, and the river will stand up like a wall.”
So the people left their camp to cross the Yurdan, and the Kuhanym who were carrying the Ark of the Covenant went ahead of them.
It was the harvest season, and the Yurdan river was overflowing its banks. But as soon as the feet of the Kuhanym who were carrying the Ark touched the water at the river’s edge,

the water above that point began backing up a great distance away at a town called Adam, which is near Zarathan, and the water below that point flowed on to the Dead Sea until the river channel was dry. Then all the people crossed over near the town of Yarichu.

Meanwhile, the Kuhanym who were carrying the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant stood on dry ground in the middle of the river channel as the people passed by. They waited there until the whole nation of Yashar'AL had crossed the Yurdan on dry ground.
When all the people had crossed the Yurdan, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha Ba'Nun,
“Now choose twelve men, one from each tribe.
Tell them, ‘Take twelve stones from the very place where the Kuhanym are standing in the middle of the Yurdan. Carry them out and pile them up at the place where you will camp tonight.’”
So Yahusha Ba'Nun called together the twelve men he had chosen one from each of the tribes of Yashar'AL.

He told them, “Go into the middle of the Yurdan, in front of the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Each of you must pick up one stone and carry it out on your shoulder twelve stones in all, one for each of the twelve tribes of Yashar'AL.
We will use these stones to build a memorial. In the future your children will ask you, ‘What do these stones mean?’

Then you can tell them, ‘They remind us that the Yurdan River stopped flowing when the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant went across.’ These stones will stand as a memorial among the people of Yashar'AL forever.”

So the men did as Yahusha had commanded them. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Yurdan River, one for each tribe, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had told Yahusha. They carried them to the place where they camped for the night and constructed the memorial there.
Yahusha Ba'Nun also set up another pile of twelve stones in the middle of the Yurdan, at the place where the Kuhanym who carried the Ark of the Covenant were standing, and they are there to this day.

The Kuhanym who were carrying the Ark stood in the middle of the river until all of the commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that Musha had given to Yahusha Ba'Nun were carried out. Meanwhile, the people hurried across the river channel.
And when everyone was safely on the other side, the Kuhanym crossed over with the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as the people watched.
The armed warriors from the tribes of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah led the Yasharalym across the Yurdan, just as Musha had directed.
These armed men about 40,000 strong were ready for battle, For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with them as they crossed over to the plains of Yarichu.
That day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made Yahusha Ba'Nun a great leader in the eyes of all the Yasharalym, and for the rest of his life they revered him as much as they had revered Musha.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha,
“Command the Kuhanym carrying the Ark of the Covenant to come up out of the river Yurdan.”
So Yahusha gave the command.

As soon as the Kuhanym carrying the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant came up out of the river Yurdan and their feet were on high ground, the water of the Yurdan returned and overflowed its banks as before.
The people crossed the Yurdan on the tenth day of the first month. Then they camped at Gilgal, just east of Yarichu.
It was there at Gilgal that Yahusha Ba'Nun piled up the twelve stones taken from the Yurdan River.
Then Yahusha said to the Yasharalym, “In the future your children will ask, ‘What do these stones mean?’
Then you can tell them, ‘This is where the Yasharalym crossed the Yurdan on dry ground.’

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH dried up the river right before your eyes, and he kept it dry until you were all across, just as he did at the Red Sea when he dried it up until we had all crossed over.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did this so all the nations of the Arath might know that His hand is powerful, and so you might fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH forever.”

When all the Amurite kings west of the Yurdan and all the Canaanite kings who lived along the Mediterranean coast heard how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had dried up the Yurdan River so the people of Yashar'AL could cross, they lost heart and were paralyzed with fear because of them.
At that time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha Ba'Nun, “Make flint knives and circumcise this second generation of Yasharalym.
So Yahusha made flint knives and circumcised the entire male population of Yashar'AL at Gibaath-haaraluth.
Yahusha had to circumcise them because all the men who were old enough to fight in battle when they left Mitzraym had died in the wilderness.
Those who left Mitzraym had all been circumcised, but none of those born after the Shamuth (Exodus), during the years in the wilderness, had been circumcised.

The Yasharalym had traveled in the wilderness for forty years until all the men who were old enough to fight in battle when they left Mitzraym had died. For they had disobeyed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH vowed He would not let them enter the land He had sworn to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
So Yahusha Ba'Nun circumcised their sons those who had grown up to take their fathers’ places for they had not been circumcised on the way to the Promised Land.
After all the males had been circumcised, they rested in the camp until they were healed.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha, “Today I have rolled away the shame of your slavery in Mitzraym.” So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.
While the Yasharalym were camped at Gilgal on the plains of Yarichu, they celebrated Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month.
The very next day they began to eat unleavened bread and roasted grain harvested from the land.
No manna appeared on the day they first ate from the crops of the land, and it was never seen again. So from that time on the Yasharalym ate from the crops of Canaan.
When Yahusha was near the town of Yarichu, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with sword in his hand. Yahusha Ba'Nun went up to him and demanded, “Are you friend or foe?”

“Neither one,” he replied. “I am the commander of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s army.” At this, Yahusha Ba'Nun fell with his face to the ground in reverence. “I am at your command,” Yahusha said. “What do you want your servant to do?”
The commander of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s army replied, “Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is Qadash.” And Yahusha Ba'Nun did as he was told.
Now the gates of Yarichu were tightly shut because the people were afraid of the Yasharalym. No one was allowed to go out or in.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha Ba'Nun, “I have given you Yarichu, its king, and all its strong warriors.
You and your fighting men should march around the town once a day for six days.
Seven Kuhanym will walk ahead of the Ark, each carrying a ram’s horn. On the seventh day you are to march around the town seven times, with the Kuhanym blowing the horns.

When you hear the Kuhanym give one long blast on the rams’ horns, have all the people shout as loud as they can. Then the walls of the town will collapse, and the people can charge straight into the town.”
So Yahusha called together the Kuhanym and said, “Take up the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant, and assign seven Kuhanym to walk in front of it, each carrying a ram’s horn.”
Then Yahusha gave orders to the people: “March around the town, and the armed men will lead the way in front of the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”

After Yahusha Ba'Nun spoke to the people, the seven Kuhanym with the rams’ horns started marching in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, blowing the horns as they marched, and the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant followed behind them.
Some of the armed men marched in front of the Kuhanym with the horns and some behind the Ark, with the Kuhanym continually blowing the horns.
“Do not shout; do not even talk,” Yahusha commanded. “Not a single word from any of you until I tell you to shout. Then shout!”
So the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was carried around the town once that day, and then everyone returned to spend the night in the camp.
Yahusha Ba'Nun got up early the next morning, and the Kuhanym again carried the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

The seven Kuhanym with the rams’ horns marched in front of the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, blowing their horns, and the armed men marched both in front of the Kuhanym with the horns and behind the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. All this time the Kuhanym were blowing their horns.
On the second day they marched around the town once and returned to the camp, they followed this pattern for six days.
On the seventh day the Yasharalym got up at dawn and marched around the town as they had done before. But this time they went around the town seven times.
At the seventh time, the Kuhanym sounded the long blast on their horns, and Yahusha Ba'Nun commanded the people, “Shout! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you the town!
Yarichu and everything in it must be completely destroyed as an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Only Rahab the prostitute and the others in her house will be spared, for she protected our spies.
“Do not take any of the things set apart for destruction, or you yourselves will be completely destroyed, and you will bring trouble on the camp of Yashar'AL.
Everything made from silver, gold, bronze, or iron is Qadash to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and must be brought into his treasury.

When the people heard the sound of the rams’ horns, they shouted as loud as they could. Suddenly, the walls of Yarichu collapsed down, and the Yasharalym charged straight into the town and captured it.
They completely destroyed everything in it with their swords men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep, goats, and donkeys.
Meanwhile, Yahusha Ba'Nun said to the two spies, “Keep your promise. Go to the prostitute’s house and bring her out, along with all her family.”

The men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father, mother, brothers, and all the other relatives who were with her. They moved her whole family to a safe place near the camp of Yashar'AL.
Then the Yasharalym burned the town and everything in it. Only the things made from silver, gold, bronze, or iron were kept for the treasury of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s house.
So Yahusha spared Rahab the prostitute and her relatives who were with her in the house, because she had hidden the spies Yahusha sent to Yarichu. And she lives among the Yasharalym to this day.

At that time Yahusha Ba'Nun invoked this curse: “May the curse of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH fall on anyone who tries to rebuild the town of Yarichu. At the cost of his firstborn son, he will lay its foundation. At the cost of his youngest son, he will set up its gates.”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with Yahusha Ba'Nun, and his reputation spread throughout the land.

Yashar'AL violated the instructions about the things set apart for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, a man named Achan had stolen some of these dedicated things, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was very angry with the Yasharalym. Achan was the son of Carmi, a descendant of Zimri son of Zarah, of the tribe of Yahudah.
Yahusha Ba'Nun sent some of his men from Yarichu to spy out the town of Ah, east of Bathal, near Bath-aban.

When they returned, they told Yahusha, “There’s no need for all of us to go up there; it won’t take more than two or three thousand men to attack Ah. Since there are so few of them, do not make all our people struggle to go up there.”
So approximately three thousand warriors were sent, but they were soundly defeated, the men of Ah

chased the Yasharalym from the town gate as far as the quarries, and they killed about thirty-six who were retreating down the slope. The Yasharalym were paralyzed with fear at this turn of events, and their courage melted away.
Yahusha Ba'Nun and the elders of Yashar'AL tore their clothing in dismay, threw dust on their heads, and bowed face down to the ground before the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH until evening.

Then Yahusha Ba'Nun cried out, “Oh, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, why did you bring us across the Yurdan River if you are going to let the Amurites kill us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side!
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, what can I say now that Yashar'AL has fled from its enemies?

For when the Canaanites and all the other people living in the land hear about it, they will surround us and wipe our name off the face of the Arath, and then what will happen to the honor of your great Name?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha, “Get up! Why are you lying on your face like this?

Yashar'AL has sinned and broken my covenant! They have stolen some of the things that I commanded must be set apart for me. And they have not only stolen them but have lied about it and hidden the things among their own belongings.

That is why the Yasharalym are running from their enemies in defeat. For now Yashar'AL itself has been set apart for destruction. I will not remain with you any longer unless you destroy the things among you that were set apart for destruction.

“Get up! Command the people to purify themselves in preparation for tomorrow. For this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, says: Hidden among you, O Yashar'AL, are things set apart for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. You will never defeat your enemies until you remove these things from among you.

“In the morning you must present yourselves by tribes, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will point out the tribe to which the guilty man belongs. That tribe must come forward with its clans, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will point out the guilty clan. That clan will then come forward, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will point out the guilty family. Finally, each member of the guilty family must come forward one by one.

The one who has stolen what was set apart for destruction will himself be burned with fire, along with everything he has, for he has broken the covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and has done a horrible thing in Yashar'AL.”
Early the next morning Yahusha Ba'Nun brought the tribes of Yashar'AL before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the tribe of Yahudah was singled out.
Then the clans of Yahudah came forward, and the clan of Zarah was singled out. Then the families of Zarah came forward, and the family of Zimri was singled out.
Every member of Zimri’s family was brought forward person by person, and Achan was singled out.
Then Yahusha said to Achan, “My son, give Kabad to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, by telling the truth. Make your confession and tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me.”
Achan replied, “It is true! I have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.

Among the plunder I saw a beautiful robe from Babylun, 200 silver coins, and a bar of gold weighing more than a pound. I wanted them so much that I took them. They are hidden in the ground beneath my tent, with the silver buried deeper than the rest.”
So Yahusha sent some men to make a search. They ran to the tent and found the stolen goods hidden there, just as Achan had said, with the silver buried beneath the rest.
They took the things from the tent and brought them to Yahusha and all the Yasharalym. Then they laid them on the ground in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then Yahusha and all the Yasharalym took Achan, the silver, the robe, the bar of gold, his sons, daughters, cattle, donkeys, sheep, goats, tent, and everything he had, and they brought them to the valley of Achur.
Then Yahusha said to Achan, “Why have you brought trouble on us? 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will now bring trouble on you.” And all the Yasharalym stoned Achan and his family and burned their bodies.
They piled a great heap of stones over Achan, which remains to this day. That is why the place has been called the Valley of Trouble ever since. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was no longer angry.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha Ba'Nun, “Do not be afraid or discouraged. Take all your fighting men and attack Ah, for I have given you the king of Ah, his people, his town, and his land.
You will destroy them as you destroyed Yarichu and its king. But this time you may keep the plunder and the livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the town.”
So Yahusha and all the fighting men set out to attack Ah. Yahusha chose thirty thousand of his best warriors and sent them out at night
with these orders: “Hide in ambush close behind the town and be ready for action.
When our main army attacks, the men of Ah will come out to fight as they did before, and we will run away from them.
We will let them chase us until we have drawn them away from the town. For they will say, ‘The Yasharalym are running away from us as they did before.’ Then, while we are running from them,
you will jump up from your ambush and take possession of the town, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will give it to you.
Set the town on fire, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded. You have your orders.”
So they left and went to the place of ambush between Bathal and the west side of Ah. But Yahusha remained among the people in the camp that night.
Early the next morning Yahusha roused his men and started toward Ah, accompanied by the elders of Yashar'AL.
All the fighting men who were with Yahusha marched in front of the town and camped on the north side of Ah, with a valley between them and the town.
That night Yahusha sent about five thousand men to lie in ambush between Bathal and Ah, on the west side of the town.
So they stationed the main army north of the town and the ambush west of the town. Yahusha himself spent that night in the valley.

When the king of Ah saw the Yasharalym across the valley, he and all his army hurried out early in the morning and attacked the Yasharalym at a place overlooking the Yurdan Valley. But he did not realize there was an ambush behind the town.
Yahusha and the Yasharalym army fled toward the wilderness as though they were badly beaten.
Then all the men in the town were called out to chase after them. In this way, they were lured away from the town.
There was not a man left in Ah or Bathal who did not chase after the Yasharalym, and the town was left wide open.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha, “Point the spear in your hand toward Ah, for I will hand the town over to you.” Yahusha did as he was commanded.
As soon as Yahusha gave this signal, all the men in ambush jumped up from their position and poured into the town. They quickly captured it and set it on fire.

When the men of Ah looked behind them, smoke from the town was filling the sky, and they had nowhere to go. For the Yasharalym who had fled in the direction of the wilderness now turned on their pursuers.
When Yahusha and all the other Yasharalym saw that the ambush had succeeded and that smoke was rising from the town, they turned and attacked the men of Ah.

Meanwhile, the Yasharalym who were inside the town came out and attacked the enemy from the rear. So the men of Ah were caught in the middle, with Yasharalym fighters on both sides. Yashar'AL attacked them, and not a single person survived or escaped.
Only the king of Ah was taken alive and brought to Yahusha.
When the Yasharalym army finished chasing and killing all the men of Ah in the open fields, they went back and finished off everyone inside.
So the entire population of Ah, including men and women, was wiped out that day, twelve thousand in all.
For Yahusha Ba'Nun kept holding out his spear until everyone who had lived in Ah was completely destroyed.
Only the livestock and the treasures of the town were not destroyed, for the Yasharalym kept these as plunder for themselves, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Yahusha.
So Yahusha Ba'Nun burned the town of Ah, and it became a permanent mound of ruins, desolate to this very day.

Yahusha impaled the king of Ah on a sharpened pole and left him there until evening. At sunset the Yasharalym took down the body, as Yahusha commanded, and threw it in front of the town gate. They piled a great heap of stones over him that can still be seen today.
Then Yahusha built an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, on Mount Albal.

He followed the commands that Musha 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s servant had written in the Book of Instruction: “Make me an altar from stones that are uncut and have not been shaped with iron tools.” Then on the altar they presented burnt offerings and Shalum offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And as the Yasharalym watched, Yahusha copied onto the stones of the altar the instructions Musha had given them.

Then all the Yasharalym, foreigners and native-born alike, along with the elders, officers, and judges, were divided into two groups. One group stood in front of Mount Garizim, the other in front of Mount Albal. Each group faced the other, and between them stood the Lauym and Kuhanym carrying the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant. This was all done according to the commands that Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, had previously given for Barakah on the people of Yashar'AL.
Yahusha then read to them all the Barakah and curses Musha had written in the Book of Instruction.
Every word of every command that Musha had ever given was read to the entire assembly of Yashar'AL, including the women and children and the foreigners who lived among them.

Now all the kings west of the Yurdan River heard about what had happened. These were the kings of the Hittites, Amurites, Canaanites, Parizzites, Hibites, and Yabusites, who lived in the hill country, in the western foothills, and along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea as far north as the Labanun mountains.
These kings combined their armies to fight as one against Yahusha and the Yasharalym.
But when the people of Gybaun heard what Yahusha had done to Yarichu and Ah,
they resorted to deception to save themselves. They sent ambassadors to Yahusha, loading their donkeys with weathered saddlebags and old, patched wineskins.
They put on worn-out, patched sandals and ragged clothes. And the bread they took with them was dry and moldy.
When they arrived at the camp of Yashar'AL at Gilgal, they told Yahusha and the men of Yashar'AL, “We have come from a distant land to ask you to make a Shalum treaty with us.”
The Yasharalym replied to these Hibites, “How do we know you do not live nearby? For if you do, we cannot make a treaty with you.”
They replied, “We are your servants. “But who are you?” Yahusha demanded. “Where do you come from?”
They answered, Your servants have come from a very distant country. We have heard of the might of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and of all 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did in Mitzraym.
We have also heard what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did to the two Amurite kings east of the Yurdan River, King Sihun of Hashbun and King Ug of Bashan (who lived in Ashtaruth).
So our elders and all our people instructed us, ‘Take supplies for a long journey. Go meet with the people of Yashar'AL and tell them, “We are your servants; please make a treaty with us.
“This bread was hot from the ovens when we left our homes. But now, as you can see, it is dry and moldy.
These wineskins were new when we filled them, but now they are old and split open, and our clothing and sandals are worn out from our very long journey.”
So the Yasharalym examined their food, but they did not consult 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then Yahusha made a Shalum treaty with them and guaranteed their safety, and the leaders of the community ratified their agreement with a binding oath.
Three days after making the treaty, they learned that these people actually lived nearby!
The Yasharalym set out at once to investigate and reached their towns in three days. The names of these towns were Gybaun, Kaphirah, Baaruth, and Kiriath-Yaarim.

But the Yasharalym did not attack the towns, for the Yasharalym leaders had made a vow to them in the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL. The people of Yashar'AL grumbled against their leaders because of the treaty.
But the leaders replied, “Since we have sworn an oath in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, we cannot touch them.
This is what we must do. We must let them live, for divine anger would come upon us if we broke our oath.
Let them live.” So they made them woodcutters and water carriers for the entire community, as the Yasharalym leaders directed.
Yahusha called together the Gybaunites and said, “Why did you lie to us? Why did you say that you live in a distant land when you live right here among us?
May you be cursed! From now on you will always be servants who cut wood and carry water for the house of my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

They replied, “We did it because we your servants were clearly told that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH commanded his servant Musha to give you this entire land and to destroy all the people living in it. So we feared greatly for our lives because of you. That is why we have done this.
Now we are at your mercy do to us whatever you think is right.”
So Yahusha did not allow the people of Yashar'AL to kill them.

But that day he made the Gybaunites the woodcutters and water carriers for the community of Yashar'AL and for the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH wherever 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH would choose to build it. And that is what they do to this day.

Aduny-zadak, king of Yahushalam heard that Yahusha had captured and completely destroyed Ah and killed its king, just as he had destroyed the town of Yarichu and killed its king. He also learned that the Gybaunites had made Shalum with Yashar'AL and were now their allies.
He and his people became very afraid when they heard all this because Gybaun was a large town, as large as the royal cities and larger than Ah. And the Gybaunite men were strong warriors.
So King Aduny-zadak of Yahushalam sent messengers to several other kings: Huham of Habrun, Piram of Yarmuth, Yaphia of Lachish, and Daabir of Aglun.
“Come and help me destroy Gybaun,” he urged them, “for they have made Shalum with Yahusha and the people of Yashar'AL.”
So these five Amurite kings combined their armies for a united attack. They moved all their troops into place and attacked Gybaun.

The men of Gybaun quickly sent messengers to Yahusha at his camp in Gilgal. “Do not abandon your servants now!” they pleaded. “Come at once! Save us! Help us! For all the Amurite kings who live in the hill country have joined forces to attack us.”
So Yahusha and his entire army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal and set out for Gybaun.
“And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha, Do not be afraid of them, “for I have given you victory over them. Not a single one of them will be able to stand up to you.”
Yahusha Ba'Nun traveled all night from Gilgal and took the Amurite armies by surprise.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH threw them into a panic, and the Yasharalym slaughtered great numbers of them at Gybaun. Then the Yasharalym chased the enemy along the road to Bath-hurun, killing them all along the way to Azakah and Makkadah.

As the Amurites retreated down the road from Bath-hurun, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH destroyed them with a terrible hailstorm from Shamaym that continued until they reached Azakah. The hail killed more of the enemy than the Yasharalym killed with the sword.

On the day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave the Yasharalym victory over the Amurites, Yahusha Ba'Nun prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in front of all the people of Yashar'AL. He said, “Let the sun stand still over Gybaun, and the moon over the valley of Aiyalun.”

So the sun stood still and the moon stayed in place until the nation of Yashar'AL had defeated its enemies. Is this not recorded in The Book of Yashar? The sun stayed in the middle of the sky, and it did not set as on a normal day.
There has never been a day like this one before or since, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH answered such a prayer. Surely 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH fought for Yashar'AL that day!
Then Yahusha Ba'Nun and the Yasharalym army returned to their camp at Gilgal.
During the battle the five kings escaped and hid in a cave at Makkadah.
When Yahusha heard that they had been found,
he issued this command: “Cover the opening of the cave with large rocks, and place guards at the entrance to keep the kings inside.
The rest of you continue chasing the enemy and cut them down from the rear. Do not give them a chance to get back to their towns, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given you victory over them.”

So Yahusha and the Yasharalym army continued the slaughter and completely crushed the enemy. They totally wiped out the five armies except for a tiny remnant that managed to reach their fortified towns.
Then the Yasharalym returned safely to Yahusha in the camp at Makkadah. After that, no one dared to speak even a word against Yashar'AL.
Then Yahusha said, “Remove the rocks covering the opening of the cave, and bring the five kings to me.”
So they brought the five kings out of the cave, the kings of Yahushalam, Habrun, Yarmuth, Lachish, and Aglun.
When they brought them out, Yahusha told the commanders of his army, “Come and put your feet on the kings’ necks.” And they did as they were told.
“Do not ever be afraid or discouraged,” Yahusha told his men. “Be strong and courageous, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is going to do this to all of your enemies.”
Then Yahusha killed each of the five kings and impaled them on five sharpened poles, where they hung until evening.

As the sun was going down, Yahusha gave instructions for the bodies of the kings to be taken down from the poles and thrown into the cave where they had been hiding. Then they covered the opening of the cave with a pile of large rocks, which remains to this very day.

That same day Yahusha captured and destroyed the town of Makkadah. He killed everyone in it, including the king, leaving no survivors, he destroyed them all, and he killed the king of Makkadah as he had killed the king of Yarichu.
Then Yahusha and the Yasharalym went to Libnah and attacked it.
There, too, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them the town and its king, he killed everyone in it, leaving no survivors. Then Yahusha killed the king of Libnah as he had killed the king of Yarichu.
From Libnah, Yahusha and the Yasharalym went to Lachish and attacked it.
Here again, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them Lachish. Yahusha took it on the second day and killed everyone in it, just as he had done at Libnah.
During the attack on Lachish, King Huram of Gazar arrived with his army to help defend the town. But Yahusha’s men killed him and his army, leaving no survivors.
Then Yahusha and the Yasharalym army went on to Aglun and attacked it.
They captured it that day and killed everyone in it, he completely destroyed everyone, just as he had done at Lachish.
From Aglun, Yahusha and the Yasharalym army went up to Habrun and attacked it.

They captured the town and killed everyone in it, including its king, leaving no survivors. They did the same thing to all of its surrounding villages. And just as he had done at Aglun, he completely destroyed the entire population.
Then Yahusha and the Yasharalym turned back and attacked Dabir.

He captured the town, its king, and all of its surrounding villages, he completely destroyed everyone in it, leaving no survivors, he did to Dabir and its king just what he had done to Habrun and to Libnah and its king.

So Yahusha conquered the whole region, the kings and people of the hill country, the Nagab, the western foothills, and the mountain slopes. He completely destroyed everyone in the land, leaving no survivors, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, had commanded.
Yahusha slaughtered them from Kadash-barnaa to Gaza and from the region around the town of Gushan up to Gybaun.
Yahusha conquered all these kings and their land in a single campaign, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, was fighting for HIS people.
Then Yahusha Ba'Nun and the Yasharalym army returned to their camp at Gilgal.
When King Yabin of Hazur heard what had happened, he sent messages to the following kings: King Yubab of Madun; the king of Shimrun; the king of Acshaph;
all the kings of the northern hill country; the kings in the Yurdan Valley south of Galilee; the kings in the Galilaan foothills; the kings of Naphuth-dur on the west;

the kings of Canaan, both east and west; the kings of the Amurites, the Hittites, the Parizzites, the Yabusites in the hill country, and the Hibites in the towns on the slopes of Mount Harmun in the land of Mizpah.
All these kings came out to fight. Their combined armies formed a vast horde. And with all their horses and chariots, they covered the landscape like the sand on the seashore.
The kings joined forces and established their camp around the water near Marum to fight against Yashar'AL.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha, “Do not be afraid of them. By this time tomorrow I will hand all of them over to Yashar'AL as dead men. Then you must cripple their horses and burn their chariots.”
So Yahusha and all his fighting men traveled to the water near Marum and attacked suddenly.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them victory over their enemies. The Yasharalym chased them as far as Greater Sidun and Misraphuth-maim, and eastward into the valley of Mizpah, until not one enemy warrior was left alive.
Then Yahusha crippled the horses and burned all the chariots, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had instructed.
Yahusha then turned back and captured Hazur and killed its king. (Hazur had at one time been the capital of all these kingdoms.)
The Yasharalym completely destroyed every living thing in the city, leaving no survivors. Not a single person was spared. And then Yahusha burned the city.
Yahusha slaughtered all the other kings and their people, completely destroying them, just as Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, had commanded.
But the Yasharalym did not burn any of the towns built on mounds except Hazur, which Yahusha burned.
And the Yasharalym took all the plunder and livestock of the ravaged towns for themselves. But they killed all the people, leaving no survivors.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded his servant Musha, so Musha commanded Yahusha Ba'Nun. And Yahusha did as he was told, carefully obeying all the commandments that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given to Musha.

So Yahusha conquered the entire region of the hill country, the entire Nagab, the whole area around the town of Gushan, the western foothills, the Yurdan Valley, the mountains of Yashar'AL, and the Galilyan foothills.

The Yasharalym territory now extended all the way from Mount Halak, which leads up to Sair in the south, as far north as Baal-gad at the foot of Mount Harmun in the valley of Labanun. Yahusha killed all the kings of those territories,
waging war for a long time to accomplish this.
No one in this region made Shalum with the Yasharalym except the Hibites of Gibaun. All the others were defeated.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH hardened their hearts and caused them to fight the Yasharalym. So they were completely destroyed without mercy, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Musha.

During this period Yahusha Ba'Nun destroyed all the descendants of Anak, who lived in the hill country of Habrun, Dabir, Anab, and the entire hill country of Yahudah and Yashar'AL. He killed them all and completely destroyed their towns.
None of the descendants of Anak were left in all the land of Yashar'AL, though some still remained in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdud.

So Yahusha took control of the entire land, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had instructed Musha. He gave it to the people of Yashar'AL as their special possession, dividing the land among the tribes. So the land finally had rest from war.

These are the kings of the land whom the children of Yashar'AL defeated, and whose land they possessed on the other side of the Yurdan toward the rising of the sun, from the River Arnun to Mount Harmun, and all the eastern Yurdan plain:

One king was Sihun king of the Amurites, who dwelt in Hashbun and ruled half of Gilaad, from Aruar, which is on the bank of the River Arnun, from the middle of that river, even as far as the River Yabbuk, which is the border of the Ammunites,
and the eastern Yurdan plain from the Sea of Chinnaruth as far as the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea), the road to Bath Yashimuth, and southward below the slopes of Pisgah.
The other king was Ug king of Bashan and his territory, who was of the remnant of the giants, who dwelt at Ashtaruth and at Adray,
and reigned over Mount Harmun, over Salcah, over all Bashan, as far as the border of the Gashurites and the Maachathites, and over half of Gilaad to the border of Sihun king of Hashbun.

Musha the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the children of Yashar'AL had conquered; and Musha the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given it as a possession to the Raubanites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manassah.

And these are the kings of the country which Yahusha Ba'Nun and the children of Yashar'AL conquered on this side of the Yurdan, on the west, from Baal Gad in the Valley of Labanun as far as Mount Halak and the ascent to Sair, which Yahusha gave to the tribes of Yashar'AL as a possession according to their divisions,

in the mountain country, in the lowlands, in the Yurdan plain, in the slopes, in the wilderness, and in the South—the Hittites, the Amurites, the Canaanites, the Parizzites, the Hibites, and the Yabusites:
the king of Yarichu, one; the king of Ah, which is beside Bathal, one;
the king of Yahushalam, one; the king of Habrun, one;
the king of Yarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Aglun, one; the king of Gazar, one;
the king of Dabir, one; the king of Gadar, one;
the king of Harmah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkadah, one; the king of Bathal, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Haphar, one;
the king of Aphak, one; the king of Lasharun, one;
the king of Madun, one; the king of Hazur, one;
the king of Shimrun Marun, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Magiddu, one;
the king of Kadash, one; the king of Yuknaam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dur in the heights of Dur, one; the king of the people of Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one—all the kings, thirty-one.
When Yahusha Ba'Nun was an old man, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to him, “You are growing old, and much land remains to be conquered.
This is the territory that remains: all the regions of the Philistines and the Gashurites,

and the larger territory of the Canaanites, extending from the stream of Shihur on the border of Mitzraym, northward to the boundary of Akrun. It includes the territory of the five Philistine rulers of Gaza, Ashdud, Ashkalun, Gath, and Akrun. The land of the Abbites

in the south also remains to be conquered. In the north, the following area has not yet been conquered: all the land of the Canaanites, including Maarah (which belongs to the Sidunians), stretching northward to Aphak on the border of the Amurites;
the land of the Gabalites and all of the Labanun mountain area to the east, from Baal-gad below Mount Harmun to Labu-hamath;

and all the hill country from Labanun to Misraphuth-maim, including all the land of the Sidunians. “I myself will drive these people out of the land ahead of the Yasharalym. So be sure to give this land to Yashar'AL as a special possession, just as I have commanded you.
Include all this territory as Yashar'AL’s possession when you divide this land among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manassah.”

Half the tribe of Manassah and the tribes of Rauban and Gad had already received their grants of land on the east side of the Yurdan, for Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, had previously assigned this land to them.
Their territory extended from Aruar on the edge of the Arnun Gurge (including the town in the middle of the gurge) to the plain beyond Madaba, as far as Dibun.
It also included all the towns of King Sihun of the Amurites, who had reigned in Hashbun, and extended as far as the borders of Ammun.
It included Gilaad, the territory of the kingdoms of Gashur and Maacah, all of Mount Harmun, all of Bashan as far as Salacah,
and all the territory of King Ug of Bashan, who had reigned in Ashtaruth and Adray. King Ug was the last of the Raphaites, for Musha had attacked them and driven them out.
But the Yasharalym failed to drive out the people of Gashur and Maacah, so they continue to live among the Yasharalym to this day.

Musha did not assign any allotment of land to the tribe of Lauy. Instead, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised them, their allotment came from the offerings burned on the altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
Musha had assigned the following area to the clans of the tribe of Rauban.
Their territory extended from Aruar on the edge of the Arnun Gurge (including the town in the middle of the gurge) to the plain beyond Madaba.
It included Hashbun and the other towns on the plain Dibun, Bamuth-baal, Bath-baal-maun,
Yahaz, Kadamuth, Maphaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zarath-shahar on the hill above the valley,
Bath-paur, the slopes of Pisgah, and Bath-Yashimuth.

The land of Rauban also included all the towns of the plain and the entire kingdom of Sihun. Sihun was the Amurite king who had reigned in Hashbun and was killed by Musha along with the leaders of Midian Aby, Rakam, Zur, Hur, and Raba princes living in the region who were allied with Sihun.
The Yasharalym had also killed Balaam son of Baur, who used magic to tell the future.
The Yurdan River marked the western boundary for the tribe of Rauban. The towns and their surrounding villages in this area were given as a homeland to the clans of the tribe of Rauban.
Musha had assigned the following area to the clans of the tribe of Gad.
Their territory included Yazar, all the towns of Gilaad, and half of the land of Ammun, as far as the town of Aruar just west of Rabbah.
It extended from Hashbun to Ramath-mizpah and Betunim, and from Mahanaim to the territory of Lu-dabar.

In the valley were Bath-haram, Bath-nimrah, Succuth, Zaphun, and the rest of the kingdom of King Sihun of Hashbun. The western boundary ran along the Yurdan River, extended as far north as the tip of the Sea of Galily, and then turned eastward.
The towns and their surrounding villages in this area were given as a homeland to the clans of the tribe of Gad.
Musha had assigned the following area to the clans of the half-tribe of Manassah.
Their territory extended from Mahanaim, including all of Bashan, all the former kingdom of King Ug, and the sixty towns of Yair in Bashan.
It also included half of Gilaad and King Ug’s royal cities of Ashtaruth and Adray. All this was given to the clans of the descendants of Makir, who was Manassah’s son.
These are the allotments Musha had made while he was on the plains of Muab, across the Yurdan River, east of Yarichu.
But Musha gave no allotment of land to the tribe of Lauy, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, had promised that HE Himself would be their allotment.
The remaining tribes of Yashar'AL received land in Canaan as allotted by Alaazar the Kuhan, Yahusha Ba'Nun, and the tribal leaders.
These nine and a half tribes received their grants of land by means of sacred lots, in accordance with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command through Musha.
Musha had already given a grant of land to the two and a half tribes on the east side of the Yurdan River, but he had given the Lauym no such allotment.

The descendants of Ya'asaf had become two separate tribes, Manassah and Aphraim. And the Lauym were given no land at all, only towns to live in with surrounding pasturelands for their livestock and all their possessions.
So the land was distributed in strict accordance with the commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to Musha.

A delegation from the tribe of Yahudah, led by Calab son of Yaphunnah the Kanizzite, came to Yahusha Ba'Nun at Gilgal. Calab said to Yahusha, “Remember what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH about you and me when we were at Kadash-barnaa.
I was forty years old when Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, sent me from Kadash-barnaa to explore the land of Canaan. I returned and gave an honest report,
but my brothers who went with me frightened the people from entering the Promised Land. For my part, I wholeheartedly followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

So that day Musha solemnly promised me, ‘The land of Canaan on which you were just walking will be your grant of land and that of your descendants forever, because you wholeheartedly followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

“Now, as you can see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has kept me alive and well as he promised for all these forty-five years since Musha made this promise, even while Yashar'AL wandered in the wilderness. Today I am eighty-five years old.
I am as strong now as I was when Musha sent me on that journey, and I can still travel and fight as well as I could then.

So give me the hill country that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH promised me. You will remember that as scouts we found the descendants of Anak living there in great, walled towns. But if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with me, I will drive them out of the land, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said.
So Yahusha Ba'Nun Baraked Calab son of Yaphunnah and gave Habrun to him as his portion of land.
Habrun still belongs to the descendants of Calab son of Yaphunnah the Kanizzite because he wholeheartedly followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
Previously Habrun had been called Kiriath-arba. It had been named after Arba, a great hero of the descendants of Anak, and the land had rest from war.
The allotment for the clans of the tribe of Yahudah reached southward to the border of Adum, as far south as the wilderness of Zin.
The southern boundary began at the south bay of the Dead Sea,
Then it went out to the south of Scorpion Pass into the wilderness of Zin, and then went south of Kadash-barnaa to Hazrun. Then it went up to Addar, where it turned toward Karka.
From there it passed to Azmun until it finally reached the Brook of Mitzraym, which it followed to the Mediterranean Sea. This was their southern boundary.
The eastern boundary extended along the Dead Sea to the mouth of the Yurdan river. The northern boundary began at the bay where the Yurdan river empties into the Dead Sea,
went up from there to Bath-huglah, then proceeded north of Bath-arabah to the Stone of Buhan. (Buhan was Rauban’s son.)

From that point it went through the valley of Achur to Dabir, turning north toward Gilgal, which is across from the slopes of Adummim on the south side of the valley. From there the boundary extended to the springs at An-shamash and on to An-rugal.

The boundary then passed through the valley of Ban-Hinnum, along the southern slopes of the Yabusites, where the city of Yahushalam is located. Then it went west to the top of the mountain above the valley of Hinnum, and on up to the northern end of the valley of Raphaim.

From there the boundary extended from the top of the mountain to the spring at the waters of Naphtuah, and from there to the towns on Mount Aphrun. Then it turned toward Baalah (that is, Kiriath-Yaarim).
The boundary circled west of Baalah to Mount Sair, passed along to the town of Kasalun on the northern slope of Mount Yaarim, and went down to Bath-shamash and on to Timnah.
The boundary then proceeded to the slope of the hill north of Akrun, where it turned toward Shikkarun and Mount Baalah. It passed Yabnaal and ended at the Maditarranaan Sea.
The western boundary was the shoreline of the Maditarranaan Sea.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded Yahusha Ba'Nun to assign some of Yahudah’s territory to Calab son of Yaphunnah. So Calab was given the town of Kiriath-arba (that is, Habrun), which had been named after Anak’s ancestor.
Calab drove out the three groups of Anakites, the descendants of Shashai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the sons of Anak.
From there he went to fight against the people living in the town of Dabir (formerly called Kiriath-saphar).
Calab said, “I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage to the one who attacks and captures Kiriath-saphar.”
Uthnial, the son of Calab’s brother Kanaz, was the one who conquered it, so Acsah became Uthnial’s wife.
When Acsah married Uthnial, she urged him to ask her father for a field. As she got down off her donkey, Calab asked her, “What’s the matter?”
She said, “Give me another gift. You have already given me land in the Nagab; now please give me springs of water, too.” So Calab gave her the upper and lower springs.
This was the homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Yahudah.
The towns of Yahudah situated along the borders of Adum in the extreme south were Kabzaal, Adar, Yagur,
Kinah, Dimunah, Adadah,
Kadash, Hazur, Ithnan,
Ziph, Talam, Ba'aluth,
Hazur-hadattah, Kariuth-hazrun (that is, Hazur),
Amam, Shama, Muladah,
Hazar-gaddah, Hashmun, Bath-palat,
Hazar-shual, Baarshaba, Biziuthiah,
Baalah, Iym, Azam,
Altulad, Kasil, Hurmah,
Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Labauth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmun, twenty-nine towns with their surrounding villages.
The following towns situated in the western foothills were also given to Yahudah: Ashtaul, Zurah, Ashnah,
Zanuah, An-gannim, Tappuah, Anam,
Yarmuth, Adullam, Sucuh, Azakah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gadarah, and Gadaruthaim, fourteen towns with their surrounding villages.
Also included were Zanan, Hadashah, Migdal-gad,
Dilaan, Mizpah, Yukthaal,
Lachish, Buzkath, Aglun,
Cabbun, Lahmam, Kitlish,
Gadaryth, Bath-dagun, Naamah, and Makkadah, sixteen towns with their surrounding villages.
Besides these, there were Libnah, Athar, Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah, Nazib,
Keilah, Aczib, and Marashah, nine towns with their surrounding villages.
The territory of the tribe of Yahudah also included Akrun and its surrounding settlements and villages.
From Akrun the boundary extended west and included the towns near Ashdud with their surrounding villages.
It also included Ashdud with its surrounding settlements and villages and Gaza with its settlements and villages, as far as the Brook of Mitzraym and along the coast of the Maditarranaan Sea.
Yahudah also received the following towns in the hill country: Shamir, Yattir, Sucuh,
Dannah, Kiriath-sannah (that is, Dabir),
Anab, Ashtamuh, Anim,
Gushan, Hulun, and Giluh, eleven towns with their surrounding villages.
Also included were the towns of Arab, Dumah, Ashan,
Yanim, Bath-tappuah, Aphakah,
Humtah, Kiriath-arba (that is, Habrun), and Ziur, nine towns with their surrounding villages.
Besides these, there were Maun, Carmal, Ziph, Yuttah,
Yazraal, Jukdaam, Zanuah,
Kain, Gibaah, and Timnah, ten towns with their surrounding villages.
In addition, there were Halhul, Bath-zur, Gadur,
Maarath, Bath-anuth, and Altakun, six towns with their surrounding villages.
There were also Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-Yaarim) and Rabbah two towns with their surrounding villages.
In the wilderness there were the towns of Bath-arabah, Middin, Sacacah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and An-gadi, six towns with their surrounding villages.
But the tribe of Yahudah could not drive out the Yabusites, who lived in the city of Yahushalam, so the Yabusites live there among the people of Yahudah to this day.
The allotment for the descendants of Ya'asaf extended from the Yurdan River near Yarichu, east of the springs of Yarichu, through the wilderness and into the hill country of Bathal.
From Bathal (that is, Luz) it ran over to Ataruth in the territory of the Arkites.
Then it descended westward to the territory of the Yaphlatites as far as Lower Bath-hurun, then to Gazar and over to the Maditarranaan Sea.
This was the homeland allocated to the families of Ya'asaf’s sons, Manassah and Aphraim.
The following territory was given to the clans of the tribe of Aphraim.
then on to the Mediterranean Sea. From Micmethath on the north, the boundary curved eastward past Taanath-shiluh to the east of Yanuah.
From Yanuah it turned southward to Ataruth and Naarah, touched Yarichu, and ended at the Yurdan River.
From Tappuah the boundary extended westward, following the Kanah Ravine to the Mediterranean Sea. This is the homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Aphraim.
In addition, some towns with their surrounding villages in the territory allocated to the half-tribe of Manassah were set aside for the tribe of Aphraim.
They did not drive the Canaanites out of Gazar, so the people of Gazar live as slaves among the people of Aphraim to this day.

The next allotment of land was given to the half-tribe of Manassah, the descendants of Ya'asaf’s older son. Makir, the firstborn son of Manassah, was the father of Gilaad. Because his descendants were experienced soldiers, the regions of Gilaad and Bashan on the east side of the Yurdan had already been given to them.

So the allotment on the west side of the Yurdan was for the remaining families within the clans of the tribe of Manassah: Abiazar, Halak, Asrial, Shacham, Haphar, and Shamida. These clans represent the male descendants of Manassah son of Ya'asaf.
However, Zaluphahad, a descendant of Haphar son of Gilaad, son of Makir, son of Manassah, had no sons. He had only daughters, whose names were Mahlah, Nuah, Huglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

These women came to Alaazar the Kuhan, Yahusha Ba'Nun, and the Yasharalym leaders and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded Musha to give us a grant of land along with the men of our tribe.” So Yahusha gave them a grant of land along with their uncles, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded.
As a result, Manassah’s total allocation came to ten parcels of land, in addition to the land of Gilaad and Bashan across the Yurdan River,
because the female descendants of Manassah received a grant of land along with the male descendants. The land of Gilaad was given to the rest of the male descendants of Manassah.
The boundary of the tribe of Manassah extended from the border of Ashar to Micmathath, near Shacham. Then the boundary went south from Micmathath to the settlement near the spring of Tappuah.
The land surrounding Tappuah belonged to Manassah, but the town of Tappuah itself, on the border of Manassah’s territory, belonged to the tribe of Aphraim.

From the spring of Tappuah, the boundary of Manassah followed the Kanah Ravine to the Mediterranean Sea. Several towns south of the ravine were inside Manassah’s territory, but they actually belonged to the tribe of Aphraim.

In general, however, the land south of the ravine belonged to Aphraim, and the land north of the ravine belonged to Manassah. Manassah’s boundary ran along the northern side of the ravine and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. North of Manassah was the territory of Ashar, and to the east was the territory of Issachar.

The following towns within the territory of Issachar and Ashar, however, were given to Manassah: Bath-shan, Iblaam, Dur (that is, Naphuth-dur), Andur, Taanach, and Magiddu, each with their surrounding settlements.
But the descendants of Manassah were unable to occupy these towns because the Canaanites were determined to stay in that region.
Later, however, when the Yasharalym became strong enough, they forced the Canaanites to work as slaves. But they did not drive them out of the land.
The descendants of Ya'asaf came to Yahusha and asked, “Why have you given us only one portion of land as our homeland when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has Baraked us with so many people?”
Yahusha replied, “If there are so many of you, and if the hill country of Aphraim is not large enough for you, clear out land for yourselves in the forest where the Parizzites and Raphaites live.”

The descendants of Ya'asaf responded, “It’s true that the hill country is not large enough for us. But all the Canaanites in the lowlands have iron chariots, both those in Bath-shan and its surrounding settlements and those in the valley of Yazraal. They are too strong for us.”
Then Yahusha Ba'Nun said to the tribes of Aphraim and Manassah, the descendants of Ya'asaf, “Since you are so large and strong, you will be given more than one portion.

The forests of the hill country will be yours as well. Clear as much of the land as you wish, and take possession of its farthest corners. And you will drive out the Canaanites from the valleys, too, even though they are strong and have iron chariots.”
Now that the land was under Yasharalym control, the entire community of Yashar'AL gathered at Shiluh and set up the Tabernacle.
But there remained seven tribes who had not yet been allotted their grants of land.
Then Yahusha asked them, “How long are you going to wait before taking possession of the remaining land 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your ancestors, has given to you?
Select three men from each tribe, and I will send them out to explore the land and map it out. They will then return to me with a written report of their proposed divisions of their new homeland.
Let them divide the land into seven sections, excluding Yahudah’s territory in the south and Ya'asaf’s territory in the north.
And when you record the seven divisions of the land and bring them to me, I will cast sacred lots in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH to assign land to each tribe.

“The Lauym, however, will not receive any allotment of land. Their role as Kuhanym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is their allotment. And the tribes of Gad, Rauban, and the half-tribe of Manassah won’t receive any more land, for they have already received their grant of land, which Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, gave them on the east side of the Yurdan River.”

As the men started on their way to map out the land, Yahusha Ba'Nun commanded them, “Go and explore the land and write a description of it. Then return to me, and I will assign the land to the tribes by casting sacred lots here in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at Shiluh.”
The men did as they were told and mapped the entire territory into seven sections, listing the towns in each section. They made a written record and then returned to Yahusha in the camp at Shiluh.
And there at Shiluh, Yahusha cast sacred lots in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to determine which tribe should have each section.
The first allotment of land went to the clans of the tribe of Banyamin. It lay between the territory assigned to the tribes of Yahudah and Ya'asaf.
The northern boundary of Banyamin’s land began at the Yurdan River, went north of the slope of Yarichu, then west through the hill country and the wilderness of Bath-aban.
From there the boundary went south to Luz (that is, Bathal) and proceeded down to Ataruth-addar on the hill that lies south of Lower Bath-hurun.

The boundary then made a turn and swung south along the western edge of the hill facing Bath-hurun, ending at the village of Kiriath-baal (that is, Kiriath-Yaarim), a town belonging to the tribe of Yahudah. This was the western boundary.
The southern boundary began at the outskirts of Kiriath-yaarim. From that western point it ran to the spring at the waters of Naphtuah,

and down to the base of the mountain beside the valley of Ban-Hinnum, at the northern end of the valley of Raphaim. From there it went down the valley of Hinnum, crossing south of the slope where the Yabusites lived, and continued down to An-rugal.

From An-rugal the boundary proceeded in a northerly direction and came to An-shamash and on to Galiluth (which is across from the slopes of Adummim). Then it went down to the Stone of Buhan. (Buhan was Rauban’s son.)
From there it passed along the north side of the slope overlooking the Yurdan Valley. The border then went down into the valley,
ran past the north slope of Bath-huglah, and ended at the north bay of the Dead Sea, which is the southern end of the Yurdan River. This was the southern boundary.
The eastern boundary was the Yurdan River. These were the boundaries of the homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Banyamin.
These were the towns given to the clans of the tribe of Banyamin. Yarichu, Bath-huglah, Amak-kaziz,
Bath-arabah, Zamaraim, Bathal,
Abbim, Parah, Uphrah,
Kaphar-ammuni, Uphni, and Gaba, twelve towns with their surrounding villages.
Also Gibaun, Ramah, Baaruth,
Mizpah, Kaphirah, Muzah,
Rakam, Irpaal, Taralah,

Zala, Haalaph, the Yabusite town (that is, Yahushalam), Gibaah, and Kiriath-Yaarim, fourteen towns with their surrounding villages. This was the homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Banyamin.
The second allotment of land went to the clans of the tribe of Simaun. Their homeland was surrounded by Yahudah’s territory.
Simaun’s homeland included Baarshaba, Shaba, Muladah,
Hazar-shual, Balah, Azam,
Altulad, Bathul, Hurmah,
Ziklag, Bath-marcabuth, Hazar-susah,
Bath-labauth, and Sharuhan, thirteen towns with their surrounding villages.
It also included Ain, Rimmun, Athar, and Ashan, four towns with their villages,
including all the surrounding villages as far south as Baalath-baar (also known as Ramah of the Nagab). This was the homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Simaun.

Their allocation of land came from part of what had been given to Yahudah because Yahudah’s territory was too large for them. So the tribe of Simaun received an allocation within the territory of Yahudah.
The third allotment of land went to the clans of the tribe of Zabulun. The boundary of Zabulun’s homeland started at Sarid.
From there it went west, going past Maralah, touching Dabbashath, and proceeding to the brook east of Yuknaam.
In the other direction, the boundary went east from Sarid to the border of Kisluth-tabur, and from there to Dabarath and up to Yaphia.
Then it continued east to Gath-haphar, Ath-kazin, and Rimmun and turned toward Naah.
The northern boundary of Zabulun passed Hannathun and ended at the valley of Iphtah-al.
The towns in these areas included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimrun, Idalah, and Bathlaham, twelve towns with their surrounding villages.
The homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Zabulun included these towns and their surrounding villages.
The fourth allotment of land went to the clans of the tribe of Issachar.
Its boundaries included the following towns: Yazraal, Kasulluth, Shunam,
Hapharaim, Shiun, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishiun, Abaz,
Ramath, An-gannim, An-haddah, and Bath-pazzaz.
The boundary also touched Tabur, Shahazumah, and Bath-shamash, ending at the Yurdan River, sixteen towns with their surrounding villages.
The homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Issachar included these towns and their surrounding villages.
The fifth allotment of land went to the clans of the tribe of Ashar.
Its boundaries included these towns: Halkath, Hali, Batan, Acshaph,
Allammalach, Amad, and Mishal. The boundary on the west touched Carmal and Shihur-libnath,
then it turned east toward Bath-dagun, and ran as far as Zabulun in the valley of Iphtah-al, going north to Bath-amak and Nayal. It then continued north to Cabul,
Abdun, Rahub, Hammun, Kanah, and as far as Greater Sidun.
Then the boundary turned toward Ramah and the fortress of Tyra, where it turned toward Husah and came to the Mediterranean Sea. The territory also included Mahabal, Aczib,
Ummah, Aphak, and Rahub, twenty-two towns with their surrounding villages.
The homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Ashar included these towns and their surrounding villages.
The sixth allotment of land went to the clans of the tribe of Naphtali.
Its boundary ran from Halaph, from the Uak at Zaanannim, and extended across to Adami-nakab, Yabnaal, and as far as Lakkum, ending at the Yurdan River.
The western boundary ran past Aznuth-tabur, then to Hukkuk, and touched the border of Zabulun in the south, the border of Ashar on the west, and the Yurdan River on the east.
The fortified towns included in this territory were Ziddim, Zar, Hammath, Rakkath, Kinnarath,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazur,
Kadash, Adrai, An-hazur,
Yirun, Migdal-al, Huram, Bath-anath, and Bath-shamash, nineteen towns with their surrounding villages.
The homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Naphtali included these towns and their surrounding villages.
The seventh allotment of land went to the clans of the tribe of Dan.
The land allocated as their homeland included the following towns: Zurah, Ashtaul, Ir-shamash,
Shaalabbin, Aiyalun, Ithlah,
Alun, Timnah, Akrun,
Altakah, Gibbathun, Baalath,
Yahud, Bana-barak, Gath-rimmun,
Ma-yarkun, Rakkun, and the territory across from Yuppa.

But the tribe of Dan had trouble taking possession of their land, so they attacked the town of Laish. They captured it, slaughtered its people, and settled there. They renamed the town Dan after their ancestor.
The homeland allocated to the clans of the tribe of Dan included these towns and their surrounding villages.
After all the land was divided among the tribes, the Yasharalym gave a piece of land to Yahusha Ba'Nun as his allocation.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said he could have any town he wanted, he chose Timnath-sarah in the hill country of Aphraim, he rebuilt the town and lived there.

These are the territories that Alaazar the Kuhan, Yahusha Ba'Nun, and the tribal leaders allocated as grants of land to the tribes of Yashar'AL by casting sacred lots in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at the entrance of the Tabernacle at Shiluh. So the division of the land was completed.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahusha Ba'Nun,
“Now tell the Yasharalym to designate the cities of refuge, as I instructed Musha.
Anyone who kills another person accidentally and unintentionally can run to one of these cities; they will be places of refuge from relatives seeking revenge for the person who was killed.

“Upon reaching one of these cities, the one who caused the death will appear before the elders at the city gate and present his case. They must allow him to enter the city and give him a place to live among them.
If the relatives of the victim come to avenge the killing, the leaders must not release the slayer to them, for he killed the other person unintentionally and without previous hostility.

But the slayer must stay in that city and be tried by the local assembly, which will render a judgment, and he must continue to live in that city until the death of the high Kuhan who was in office at the time of the accident. After that, he is free to return to his own home in the town from which he fled.”

The following cities were designated as cities of refuge: Kadash of Galilyan, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shacham, in the hill country of Aphraim; and Kiriath-arba (that is, Habrun), in the hill country of Yahudah.

On the east side of the Yurdan River, across from Yarichu, the following cities were designated: Bazar, in the wilderness plain of the tribe of Rauban; Ramuth in Gilaad, in the territory of the tribe of Gad; and Gulan in Bashan, in the land of the tribe of Manassah.

These cities were set apart for all the Yasharalym as well as the foreigners living among them. Anyone who accidentally killed another person could take refuge in one of these cities. In this way, they could escape being killed in revenge prior to standing trial before the local assembly.
Then the leaders of the tribe of Lauy came to consult with Alaazar the Kuhan, Yahusha Ba'Nun (son of Nun), and the leaders of the other tribes of Yashar'AL.
They came to them at Shiluh in the land of Canaan and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded Musha to give us towns to live in and pasturelands for our livestock.”
So by the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the people of Yashar'AL gave the Lauym the following towns and pasturelands out of their own grants of land.
The descendants of Aarun, who were members of the Kuhathite clan within the tribe of Lauy, were allotted thirteen towns that were originally assigned to the tribes of Yahudah, Simaun, and Banyamin.
The other families of the Kuhathite clan were allotted ten towns from the tribes of Aphraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manassah.
The clan of Garshun was allotted thirteen towns from the tribes of Issachar, Ashar, Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manassah in Bashan.
The clan of Marari was allotted twelve towns from the tribes of Rauban, Gad, and Zabulun.
So the Yasharalym obeyed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command to Musha and assigned these towns and pasturelands to the Lauym by casting sacred lots.
The Yasharalym gave the following towns from the tribes of Yahudah and Simaun
to the descendants of Aarun, who were members of the Kuhathite clan within the tribe of Lauy, since the sacred lot fell to them first:
Kiriath-arba (that is, Habrun), in the hill country of Yahudah, along with its surrounding pasturelands. (Arba was an ancestor of Anak.)
But the open fields beyond the town and the surrounding villages were given to Calab son of Yaphunnah as his possession.
The following towns with their pasturelands were given to the descendants of Aarun the Kuhan: Habrun (a city of refuge for those who accidentally killed someone), Libnah,
Yattir, Ashtamua,
Hulun, Dabir,
Ain, Yuttah, and Bath-shamash, nine towns from these two tribes.
From the tribe of Banyamin the Kuhanym were given the following towns with their pasturelands: Gibaun, Gaba,
Anathuth, and Almun four towns.
So in all, thirteen towns with their pasturelands were given to the Kuhanym, the descendants of Aarun.
The rest of the Kuhathite clan from the tribe of Lauy was allotted the following towns and pasturelands from the tribe of Aphraim:
Shechem in the hill country of Aphraim (a city of refuge for those who accidentally killed someone), Gazar,
Kibzaim, and Bath-harun, four towns.
The following towns and pasturelands were allotted to the Kuhanym from the tribe of Dan: Altakah, Gibbathun,
Aiyalun, and Gath-rimmun, four towns.
The half-tribe of Manassah allotted the following towns with their pasturelands to the Kuhanym: Taanach and Gath-rimmun, two towns.
So in all, ten towns with their pasturelands were given to the rest of the Kuhathite clan.

The descendants of Garshun, another clan within the tribe of Lauy, received the following towns with their pasturelands from the half-tribe of Manassah: Gulan in Bashan (a city of refuge for those who accidentally killed someone) and Be-ashtarah—two towns.
From the tribe of Issachar they received the following towns with their pasturelands: Kishiun, Dabarath,
Yarmuth, and An-gannim, four towns.
From the tribe of Ashar they received the following towns with their pasturelands: Mishal, Abdun,
Halkath, and Rahub, four towns.

From the tribe of Naphtali they received the following towns with their pasturelands: Kadash in Galily (a city of refuge for those who accidentally killed someone), Hammuth-dur, and Kartan, three towns.
So in all, thirteen towns with their pasturelands were allotted to the clan of Garshun.
The rest of the Lauym the Marari clan were given the following towns with their pasturelands from the tribe of Zabulun: Yuknaam, Kartah,
Dimnah, and Nahalal, four towns.
From the tribe of Rauban they received the following towns with their pasturelands: Bazar, Yahaz,
Kadamuth, and Maphaath, four towns.
From the tribe of Gad they received the following towns with their pasturelands: Ramuth in Gilaad (a city of refuge for those who accidentally killed someone), Mahanaim,
Hashbun, and Yazar, four towns.
So in all, twelve towns were allotted to the clan of Marari.
The total number of towns and pasturelands within Yasharalym territory given to the Lauym came to forty-eight.
Every one of these towns had pasturelands surrounding it.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave to Yashar'AL all the land he had sworn to give their ancestors, and they took possession of it and settled there.
