And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them rest on every side, just as he had solemnly promised their ancestors. None of their enemies could stand against them, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH helped them conquer all their enemies.
Not a single one of all the good promises 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given to the family of Yashar'AL was left unfulfilled; everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had spoken about, happened the way He said it.
Then Yahusha Ba'Nun called together the tribes of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah.
He told them, “You have done as Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, commanded you, and you have obeyed every order I have given you.
During all this time you have not deserted the other tribes. You have been careful to obey the commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH right up to the present day.

And now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given the other tribes rest, as He promised them. So go back home to the land that Musha, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, gave you as your possession on the east side of the Yurdan River.

But be very careful to obey all the commands and the instructions that Musha gave to you. Love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, walk in all his ways, obey his commandments, hold firmly to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and serve Him with all your heart and all your soul.”
So Yahusha Ba'Nun Baraked them and sent them away, and they went home.

Musha had given the land of Bashan, east of the Yurdan River, to the half-tribe of Manassah. (The other half of the tribe was given land west of the Yurdan.) As Yahusha sent them away and Baraked them,

he said to them, “Go back to your homes with the great wealth you have taken from your enemies, the vast herds of livestock, the silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and the large supply of clothing. Share the plunder with your relatives.”

So the men of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah left the rest of Yashar'AL at Shiluh in the land of Canaan. They started the journey back to their own land of Gilaad, the territory that belonged to them according to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command through Musha.

But while they were still in Canaan, and when they came to a place called Galiluth near the Yurdan River, the men of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah stopped to build a large and imposing altar.
The rest of Yashar'AL heard that the people of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah had built an altar at Galiluth at the edge of the land of Canaan, on the west side of the Yurdan River.
So the whole community of Yashar'AL gathered at Shiluh and prepared to go to war against them.
First, however, they sent a delegation led by Phinahas son of Alaazar, the Kuhan, to talk with the tribes of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah.
In this delegation were ten leaders of Yashar'AL, one from each of the ten tribes, and each the head of his family within the clans of Yashar'AL.
When they arrived in the land of Gilaad, they said to the tribes of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah,

“The whole community of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH demands to know why you are betraying the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL. How could you turn away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and build an altar for yourselves in rebellion against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?
Was our sin at Paur not enough? To this day we are not fully cleansed of it, even after the plague that struck the entire community of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And yet today you are turning away from following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. If you rebel against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH today, He will be angry with all of us tomorrow.

“If you need the altar because the land you possess is defiled, then join us in land where the Tabernacle of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is situated, and share our land with us. But do not rebel against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or against us by building an altar other than the one true altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

The divine anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH fell on the entire community of Yashar'AL when Achan, a member of the clan of Zarah, sinned by stealing the things set apart for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Achan was not the only one who died because of his sin.”
Then the people of Rauben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manassah answered the heads of the clans of Yashar'AL:

“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the only 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, is the only 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH!! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH knows the truth, and may Yashar'AL know it, too! We have not built the altar in treacherous rebellion against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. If we have done so, do not spare our lives this day.
If we have built an altar for ourselves to turn away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings or Shalum offerings, may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH himself punish us.
“The truth is, we have built this altar because we fear that in the future your descendants will say to ours, ‘What right do you have to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL?

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has placed the Yurdan River as a barrier between our people and you people of Rauban and Gad. You have no claim to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’ So your descendants may prevent our descendants from worshiping 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“So we decided to build the altar, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices,

but as a memorial. It will remind our descendants and your descendants that we, too, have the right to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at his sanctuary with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and Shalum offerings. Then your descendants will not be able to say to ours, ‘You have no claim to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’

“If they say this, our descendants can reply, ‘Look at this copy of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s altar that our ancestors made. It is not for burnt offerings or sacrifices; it is a reminder of the relationship both of us have with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’

Far be it from us to rebel against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or turn away from Him by building our own altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices. Only the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH that stands in front of the Tabernacle may be used for that purpose.”
When Phinahas the Kuhan and the leaders of the community the heads of the clans of Yashar'AL heard this from the tribes of Rauban, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, they were satisfied.

Phinahas son of Alaazar, the Kuhan, replied to them, “Today we know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is among us because you have not committed this treachery against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as we thought. Instead, you have rescued Yashar'AL from being destroyed by the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then Phinahas son of Alaazar, the Kuhan, and the other leaders left the tribes of Rauban and Gad in Gilaad and returned to the land of Canaan to tell the Yasharalym what had happened.
And all the Yasharalym were satisfied and Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and spoke no more of war against Rauban and Gad.
The people of Rauban and Gad named the altar “Witness,” for they said, “It is a witness between us and them that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, too.”
The years passed, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given the people of Yashar'AL rest from all their enemies. Yahusha Ba'Nun, who was now very old,
called together all the elders, leaders, judges, and officers of Yashar'AL, he said to them, “I am now a very old man.
You have seen everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has done for you during my lifetime. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has fought for you against your enemies.
I have allotted to you as your homeland all the land of the nations yet unconquered, as well as the land of those we have already conquered from the Yurdan River to the Maditarranaan Sea in the west.

This land will be yours, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will himself drive out all the people living there now. You will take possession of their land, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH promised you.
“So be very careful to follow everything Musha wrote in the Book of Instruction. Do not deviate from it, turning either to the right or to the left.
Make sure you do not associate with the other people still remaining in the land. Do not even mention the names of their mighty ones, much less swear by them or serve them or worship them.
Rather, cling tightly to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH as you have done until now.
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has driven out great and powerful nations for you, and no one has yet been able to defeat you.
Each one of you will put to flight a thousand of the enemy, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH fights for you, just as He has promised.
So you must be very careful, and love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, with all your heart
“But if you turn away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and cling to the customs of the survivors of these nations remaining among you, and if you intermarry with them,

then know for certain that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will no longer drive them out of your land. Instead, they will be a snare and a trap to you, a whip for your backs and thorny brambles in your eyes, and you will vanish from this good land 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given you.
“Soon I will die, going the way of everything on Arath. Deep in your hearts you know that every promise of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has come true. Not a single one has failed!

But as surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given you the good things he promised, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will also bring disaster on you if you disobey Him. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will completely destroy you from this good land He has given you.

If you break the covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH by worshiping and serving other nations idols, His anger will burn against you, and you will quickly vanish from the good land 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you.”
Then Yahusha Ba'Nun summoned all the tribes of Yashar'AL to Shacham, including their elders, leaders, judges, and officers. So they came and presented themselves to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

Yahusha said to the people, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, says: Long ago your ancestors, including Tarah, the father of Abraham and Nahur, lived beyond the Auphrates River, and they worshiped idols.
But I took your ancestor Abraham from the land beyond the Auphrates and led him into the land of Canaan. I gave him many descendants through his son Yachaq.
To Yachaq I gave Ya'aqub and Asau. To Asau I gave the mountains of Sair, while Ya'aqub and his children went down into Mitzraym.
“Then I sent Musha and Aarun, and I brought terrible plagues on Mitzraym; and afterward I brought you out as a free people.
But when your ancestors arrived at the Red Sea, the Mitzraym chased after you with chariots and charioteers.

When your ancestors cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, I put darkness between you and the Mitzraym. I brought the sea crashing down on the Mitzraym, drowning them. With your very own eyes you saw what I did. Then you lived in the wilderness for many years.

“Finally, I brought you into the land of the Amurites on the east side of the Yurdan. They fought against you, but I destroyed them before you. I gave you victory over them, and you took possession of their land.
Then Balak son of Zippur, king of Muab, started a war against Yashar'AL, he summoned Balaam son of Baur to curse you,
but I would not listen to him. Instead, I made Balaam barak you, and so I rescued you from Balak.

“When you crossed the Yurdan River and came to Yarichu, the men of Yarichu fought against you, same way the Amurites, the Parizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hibites, and the Yabusites. But I gave you victory over them.
And I sent terror ahead of you to drive out the two kings of the Amurites. It was not your swords or bows that brought you victory.
I gave you land you had not worked on, and I gave you towns you did not build, the towns where you are now living. I gave you vineyards and olive groves for food, though you did not plant them.
“So fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and serve Him wholeheartedly. Put away forever the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived beyond the Auphrates River and in Mitzraym. Serve only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

But if you refuse to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, then choose today whom you will serve. Would you prefer the idols your ancestors served beyond the Auphrates? Or will it be the idols of the Amurites in whose land you now live? But as for me and my family, we will serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
The people replied, “We would never abandon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and serve other nations pagan idols.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is the one who rescued us and our ancestors from slavery in the land of Mitzraym. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH performed mighty miracles before our very eyes. As we traveled through the wilderness among our enemies, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH preserved us.
It was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who drove out the Amurites and the other nations living here in the land. So we will only serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH alone is our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.”
Then Yahusha warned the people, “You are not able to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is Qadash and jealous 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. He will not forgive your rebellion and your sins.
If you abandon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and serve other nations idols, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will turn against you and destroy you, even though He has been so good to you.”
But the people answered Yahusha, “No, we will serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
“You are a witness to your own decision,” Yahusha said. “You have chosen to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. “Yes,” they replied, “we are witnesses to what we have said.”
“All right then,” Yahusha said, “destroy the idols among you, and turn your hearts to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.”
The people said to Yahusha, “We will serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. We will obey 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH alone.”
So Yahusha made a covenant with the people that day at Shacham, committing them to follow the decrees and regulations of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Yahusha wrote these things in the Book of the law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. As a reminder of their agreement, he took a huge stone and rolled it beneath the terebinth tree beside the Tabernacle of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Yahusha said to all the people, “This stone has heard everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to us. It will be a witness to testify against you if you go back on your word to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.”
Then Yahusha sent all the people away to their own homelands.
After this, Yahusha Ba'Nun (son of Nun), the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, died at the age of one hundred and ten years.
They buried Yahusha in the land he had been allocated, at Timnath-sarah in the hill country of Aphraim, north of Mount Gaash.
The people of Yashar'AL served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH throughout the lifetime of Yahusha and of the elders who outlived him, those who had personally experienced all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done for Yashar'AL.

The bones of Ya'asaf, which the Yasharalym had brought along with them when they left Mitzraym, were buried at Shacham, in the parcel of ground Ya'aqub had bought from the sons of Hamur for 100 pieces of silver. This land was located in the territory allotted to the descendants of Ya'asaf.
Alaazar son of Aarun also died. He was buried in the hill country of Aphraim, in the town of Gibaah, which had been given to his son Phinahas.

books.name: Judges
chapters: After the death of Yahusha Ba'Nun, the Yasharalym asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Which tribe should go first to attack the Canaanites?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH answered, “Yahudah, for I have given them victory over the land.”

The men of Yahudah said to their relatives from the tribe of Simaun, “Join with us to fight against the Canaanites living in the territory allotted to us. Then we will help you conquer your territory.” So the men of Simaun went with Yahudah.
When the men of Yahudah attacked, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them victory over the Canaanites and Parizzites, and they killed ten thousand enemy warriors at the town of Bazak.
While at Bazak they encountered King Aduni-bazak and fought against him, and the Canaanites and Parizzites were defeated.
Aduni-bazak escaped, but the Yasharalym soon captured him and cut off his thumbs and big toes.

Aduni-bazak said, “I once had seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off, eating scraps from under my table. Now 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has paid me back for what I did to them.” They took him to Yahushalam, and he died there.
The men of Yahudah attacked Yahushalam and captured it, killing all its people and setting the city on fire.
Then they went down to fight the Canaanites living in the hill country, the Nagab, and the western foothills.
Yahudah marched against the Canaanites in Habrun (formerly called Kiriath-arba), defeating the forces of Shashai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there they went to fight against the people living in the town of Dabir (formerly called Kiriath-saphar).
Calab said, “I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage to the one who attacks and captures Kiriath-saphar.”
Uthnial, the son of Calab’s younger brother, Kanaz, was the one who conquered it, so Acsah became Uthnial’s wife.
When Acsah married Uthnial, she urged him to ask her father for a field. As she got down off her donkey, Calab asked her, “What’s the matter?”
She said, “Let me have another gift. You have already given me land in the Nagab; now please give me springs of water, too.” So Calab gave her the upper and lower springs.

When the tribe of Yahudah left Yarichu the city of palms, the Kanites, who were descendants of Musha’s father-in-law, traveled with them into the wilderness of Yahudah. They settled among the people there, near the town of Arad in the Nagab.
Then Yahudah joined with Simaun to fight against the Canaanites living in Zaphath, and they completely destroyed the town. So the town was named Hurmah.
In addition, Yahudah captured the towns of Gaza, Ashkalun, and Akrun, along with their surrounding territories.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with the people of Yahudah, and they took possession of the hill country. But they failed to drive out the people living in the plains, who had iron chariots.
The town of Habrun was given to Calab as Musha had promised, and Calab drove out the people living there, who were descendants of the three sons of Anak.
The tribe of Banyamin, however, failed to drive out the Yabusites, who were living in Yahushalam. So to this day the Yabusites live in Yahushalam among the people of Banyamin
The descendants of Ya'asaf attacked the town of Bathal, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with them.
They sent men to scout out Bathal (formerly known as Luz).
They confronted a man coming out of the town and said to him, “Show us a way into the town, and we will have mercy on you.”
So he showed them a way in, and they killed everyone in the town except that man and his family.
Later the man moved to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town, he named it Luz, which is its name to this day.

The tribe of Manassah failed to drive out the people living in Bath-shan, Taanach, Dur, Iblaam, Magiddu, and all their surrounding settlements, because the Canaanites were determined to stay in that region.
When the Yasharalym grew stronger, they forced the Canaanites to work as slaves, but they never did drive them completely out of the land.
The tribe of Aphraim failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Gazar, so the Canaanites continued to live there among them.

The tribe of Zabulun failed to drive out the residents of Kitrun and Nahalul, so the Canaanites continued to live among them. But the Canaanites were forced to work as slaves for the people of Zabulun.
The tribe of Ashar failed to drive out the residents of Accu, Sidun, Ahlab, Aczib, Halbah, Aphik, and Rahub.
Instead, the people of Asher moved in among the Canaanites, who controlled the land, for they failed to drive them out.

Likewise, the tribe of Naphtali failed to drive out the residents of Bath-shamash and Bath-anath. Instead, they moved in among the Canaanites, who controlled the land. Nevertheless, the people of Bath-shamash and Bath-anath were forced to work as slaves for the people of Naphtali.
As for the tribe of Dan, the Amurites forced them back into the hill country and would not let them come down into the plains.
The Amurites were determined to stay in Mount Haras, Aijalun, and Shaalbim, but when the descendants of Ya'asaf became stronger, they forced the Amurites to work as slaves.
The boundary of the Amurites ran from Scurpiun Pass to Sala and continued upward from there.

The Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH went up from Gilgal to Bukim and said to the Yasharalym, “I brought you out of Mitzraym into this land that I swore to give your ancestors, and I said, I would never break my covenant with you.
For your part, you were not to make any covenants with the people living in this land; instead, you were to destroy their altars. But you disobeyed my command. Why did you do this?
So now I declare that I will no longer drive out the people living in your land. They will be thorns in your sides, and their idols will be a constant temptation to you.”
When the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH finished speaking to all the Yasharalym, the people wept loudly.
So they called the place Bukim (which means “weeping”), and they offered sacrifices there to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
After Yahusha Ba'Nun sent the people away, each of the tribes left to take possession of the land allotted to them.
And the Yasharalym served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH throughout the lifetime of Yahusha and the leaders who outlived him, those who had seen all the great things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done for Yashar'AL.
Yahusha Ba'Nun (son of Nun), the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, died at the age of one hundred and ten years.
They buried him in the land he had been allocated, at Timnath-sarah in the hill country of Aphraim, north of Mount Gaash.
After that generation died, another generation grew up who did not acknowledge 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or remember the mighty things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done for Yashar'AL.
The Yasharalym did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and served the images of Baal.

They abandoned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their ancestors, who had brought them out of Mitzraym. They went after other nations idols, worshiping the idols of the people around them, and they angered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
They abandoned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to serve Baal and the images of Ashturath.

This made 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH burn with anger against Yashar'AL, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH handed them over to raiders who stole their possessions, he turned them over to their enemies all around, and they were no longer able to resist them.
Every time Yashar'AL went out to battle, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH fought against them, causing them to be defeated, just as he had warned, and the people were in great distress.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised up Shuphatym (judges) to rescue the Yasharalym from their attackers.

Yet Yashar'AL did not listen to the judges but prostituted themselves by worshiping other nations idols. How quickly they turned away from the path of their ancestors, who had walked in obedience to the commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Whenever 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised up a Shuphatym (judge) over Yashar'AL, he was with that shuphatym and rescued the people from their enemies throughout the judge’s lifetime. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH took pity on his people, who were burdened by oppression and suffering.

But when the judge died, the people returned to their corrupt ways, behaving worse than those who had lived before them. They went after other nations pagan idols, serving and worshiping them, and they refused to give up their evil practices and stubborn ways.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH burned with anger against Yashar'AL. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “Because these people have violated my covenant, which I made with their ancestors, and have ignored my commands,
I will no longer drive out the nations that Yahusha Ba'Nun left unconquered when he died.
I did this to test Yashar'AL, to see whether or not they would follow the ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as their ancestors did.”
That is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH left those nations in place. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did not quickly drive them out or allow Yahusha Ba'Nun to conquer them all.
These are the nations that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH left in the land to test those Yasharalym who had not experienced the wars of Canaan.
He did this to teach warfare to generations of Yashar'AL who had no experience in battle.

These are the nations: the Philistines (those living under the five Philistine rulers), all the Canaanites, the Sidunians, and the Hibites living in the mountains of Labanun from Mount Baal-harmun to Labu-hamath.
These people were left to test the Yasharalym to see whether they would obey the commands 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given to their ancestors through Musha.
So the people of Yashar'AL lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amurites, Parizzites, Hibites, and Yabusites,
and they intermarried with them. Yasharalym sons married their daughters, and Yasharalym daughters were given in marriage to their sons, and the Yasharalym served their idols.
The Yasharalym did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they forgot about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and they served the images of Baal and the Asharah poles.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH burned with anger against Yashar'AL, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH turned them over to King Cushan-rishathaim of Aram-naharaim. And the Yasharalym served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years.
But when the people of Yashar'AL cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for help, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised up a rescuer to save them. His name was Uthnial, the son of Calab’s younger brother, Kanaz.
The Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came upon him, and he became Yashar'AL’s judge, he went to war against King Cushan-rishathaim of Aram, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave Uthnial victory over him.
So there was peace in the land for forty years. Then Uthnial son of Kanaz died.
Once again the Yasharalym did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave King Aglun of Muab control over Yashar'AL because of their evil.
Aglun enlisted the Ammunites and Amalakites as allies, and then he went out and defeated Yashar'AL, taking possession of Yarichu, the city of palms.
And the Yasharalym served Aglun of Muab for eighteen years.

But when the people of Yashar'AL cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for help, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH again raised up a rescuer to save them, his name was Ahud son of Gara, a left-handed man of the tribe of Banyamin, the Yasharalym sent Ahud to deliver their tribute money to King Aglun of Muab.
So Ahud made a double-edged dagger that was about a foot long, and he strapped it to his right thigh, keeping it hidden under his clothing.
He brought the tribute money to Aglun, who was very fat.
After delivering the payment, Ahud started home with those who had helped carry the tribute.

But when Ahud reached the stone idols near Gilgal, he turned back, he came to Aglun and said, “I have a secret message for you.” So the king commanded his servants, “Be quiet!” and he sent them all out of the room.
Ahud walked over to Aglun, who was sitting alone in a cool upstairs room, and Ahud said, “I have a message from 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for you!” As King Aglun rose from his seat,
Ahud reached with his left hand, pulled out the dagger strapped to his right thigh, and plunged it into the king’s belly.
The dagger went so deep that the handle disappeared beneath the king’s fat. So Ahud did not pull out the dagger, and the king’s bowels emptied.
Then Ahud closed and locked the doors of the room and escaped down the latrine.
After Ahud was gone, the king’s servants returned and found the doors to the upstairs room locked. They thought he might be using the latrine in the room,
so they waited. But when the king did not come out after a long delay, they became concerned and got a key, and when they opened the doors, they found their master dead on the floor.
While the servants were waiting, Ahud escaped, passing the stone idols on his way to Sairah.
When he arrived in the hill country of Aphraim, Ahud sounded a call to arms, then he led a band of Yashar'AL down from the hills.

“Follow me,” he said, “for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you victory over Muab your enemy.” So they followed him, and the Yasharalym took control of the shallow crossings of the Yurdan River across from Muab, preventing anyone from crossing.
They attacked the Muabites and killed about ten thousand of their strongest and most able-bodied warriors. Not one of them escaped.
So Muab was conquered by Yashar'AL that day, and there was peace in the land for eighty years.
After Ahud, Shamgar son of Anath rescued Yashar'AL, he once killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad.
After Ahud’s death, the Yasharalym again did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH turned them over to King Yabin of Hazur, a Canaanite king. The commander of his army was Sisara, who lived in Harushath-hagguyim.
Sisara, who had nine hundred iron chariots, ruthlessly oppressed the Yasharalym for twenty years. Then the people of Yashar'AL cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for help.
Daburah, the wife of Lappiduth, was a Nabym who was judging Yashar'AL at that time.
She would sit under the Palm of Daburah, between Ramah and Bathal in the hill country of Aphraim, and the Yasharalym would go to her for judgment.

One day she sent for Barak son of Abinuam, who lived in Kadash in the land of Naphtali. She said to him, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, commands you: Call out ten thousand warriors from the tribes of Naphtali and Zabulun at Mount Tabur.
And I will call out Sisara, commander of Yabin’s army, along with his chariots and warriors, to the Kishun River, there I will give you victory over him.”
Barak told her, “I will go, but only if you go with me.”

“Very well,” she replied, “I will go with you. But you will receive no honor in this venture, for the victory of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH over Sisara will be at the hands of a woman.” So Daburah went with Barak to Kadash.
At Kadash, Barak called together the tribes of Zabulun and Naphtali, and ten thousand warriors went up with him. Daburah also went with him.
Now Habar the Kanite, a descendant of Musha’s brother-in-law Hubab, had moved away from the other members of his tribe and pitched his tent by the oak of Zaanannim near Kadash.
When Sisara was told that Barak son of Abinuam had gone up to Mount Tabur,
he called for all nine hundred of his iron chariots and all of his warriors, and they marched from Harushath-hagguyim to the Kishun River.

Then Daburah said to Barak, “Get ready! This is the day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give you victory over Sisara, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is marching ahead of you.” So Barak led his ten thousand warriors down the slopes of Mount Tabur into battle.
When Barak attacked, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH threw Sisara and all his chariots and warriors into a panic. Sisara leaped down from his chariot and escaped on foot.
Then Barak chased the chariots and the enemy army all the way to Harushath-hagguyim, killing all of Sisera’s warriors. Not a single one was left alive.
Meanwhile, Sisara ran to the tent of Ya'al, the wife of Habar the Kanite, because Habar’s family was on friendly terms with King Yabin of Hazur.
Ya'al went out to meet Sisara and said to him, “Come into my tent, sir. Come in. Don’t be afraid.” So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
“Please give me some water,” he said. “I’m thirsty.” So she gave him some milk from a leather bag and covered him again.
“Stand at the door of the tent,” he told her. “If anybody comes and asks you if there is anyone here, say no.”
But when Sisara fell asleep from exhaustion, Ya'al quietly crept up to him with a hammer and tent peg in her hand. Then she drove the tent peg through his temple and into the ground, and so he died.

When Barak came looking for Sisara, Ya'al went out to meet him. She said, “Come, and I will show you the man you are looking for.” So he followed her into the tent and found Sisara lying there dead, with the tent peg through his temple.
So on that day Yashar'AL saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH defeat Yabin, the Canaanite king.
And from that time on Yashar'AL became stronger and stronger against King Yabin until they finally destroyed him.
On that day Daburah and Barak son of Abinuam sang this song:
Yashar'AL’s leaders took charge, and the people gladly followed. Yadah (Praise) 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
“Listen, you kings! Pay attention, you mighty rulers! For I will sing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. I will make music to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
For when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, set out from Seir and marched across the fields of Adum, the Arath trembled, and the cloudy skies poured down rain.
The mountains quaked in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Mount Sinai, in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
“In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, and in the days of Yaal, people avoided the main roads, and travelers stayed on winding pathways.
There were few people left in the villages of Yashar'AL until Daburah arose as a mother for Yashar'AL.
When Yashar'AL chose new idols, war erupted at the city gates. Yet not a shield or spear could be seen among forty thousand warriors in Yashar'AL!
My heart is with the commanders of Yashar'AL, with those who volunteered for war. Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
“Consider this, you who ride on fine donkeys, you who sit on fancy saddle blankets, and you who walk along the road.

Listen to the village musicians gathered at the watering holes. They recount the righteous victories of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the victories of his villagers in Yashar'AL. Then the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH marched down to the city gates.
“Wake up, Daburah, wake up! Wake up, wake up, and sing a song! Arise, Barak! Lead your captives away, son of Abinuam!
Down from Tabur marched the few against the nobles, the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH marched down against mighty warriors.

They came down from Aphraim a land that once belonged to the Amalakites; they followed you, Banyamin, with your troops. From Makir the commanders marched down; from Zabulun came those who carry a commander’s staff.
The princes of Issachar were with Daburah and Barak. They followed Barak, rushing into the valley. But in the tribe of Rauban there was great indecision.
Why did you sit at home among the sheepfolds to hear the shepherds whistle for their flocks? Yes, in the tribe of Rauban there was great indecision.
Gilaad remained east of the Yurdan, and why did Dan stay home? Ashar sat unmoved at the seashore, remaining in his harbors.
But Zabulun risked his life, as did Naphtali, on the heights of the battlefield.
“The kings of Canaan came and fought, at Taanach near Magiddu’s springs, but they carried off no silver treasures.
The stars fought from Shamaym. The stars in their orbits fought against Sisara.
The Kishun River swept them away that ancient torrent, the Kishun. March on with courage, my soul!
Then the horses’ hooves hammered the ground, the galloping of Sisara’s mighty steeds.
‘Let the people of Maruz be cursed,’ said the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. ‘Let them be utterly cursed, because they did not come to help 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH against the mighty warriors.’
“Most Baraked among women is Yaal, the wife of Habar the Kanite. May she be Baraked above all women who live in tents.
Sisara asked for water, and she gave him milk. In a bowl fit for nobles, she brought him yogurt.

Then with her left hand she reached for a tent peg, and with her right hand for the workman’s hammer. She struck Sisara with the hammer, crushing his head. With a shattering blow, she pierced his temples.
He sank, he fell, he lay still at her feet, and where he sank, there he died.
“From the window Sisara’s mother looked out. Through the window she watched for his return, saying, ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? To Why don’t we hear the sound of chariot wheels?’
“Her wise women answer, and she repeats these words to herself:

‘They must be dividing the captured plunder with a woman or two for every man. There will be colorful robes for Sisara, and colorful, embroidered robes for me. Yes, the plunder will include colorful robes embroidered on both sides.’
“O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, may all your enemies die like Sisara! But may those who love you rise like the sun in all its power!”
The Yasharalym did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH handed them over to the Midianites for seven years.
The Midianites were so cruel that the Yasharalym made hiding places for themselves in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.
Whenever the Yasharalym planted their crops, marauders from Midian, Amalak, and the people of the east would attack Yashar'AL,
camping in the land and destroying crops as far away as Gaza. They left the Yasharalym with nothing to eat, taking all the sheep, goats, cattle, and donkeys.
These enemy hordes, coming with their livestock and tents, were as thick as locusts; they arrived on droves of camels too numerous to count. And they stayed until the land was stripped bare.
So Yashar'AL was reduced to starvation by the Midianites. Then the Yasharalym cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for help.
When they cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH because of Midian,
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent a Nabym to the Yasharalym, he said, “this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL says: I brought you up out of slavery in Mitzraym.
I rescued you from the Mitzraym and from all who oppressed you. I drove out your enemies and gave you their land.
I told you, ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. You must not worship the image idols of the Amurites, in whose land you now live.’ But you have not listened to me.”

Then the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came and sat beneath the great tree at Uphrah, which belonged to Yuash of the clan of Abiazer. Gydaun son of Yuash was threshing wheat at the bottom of a winepress to hide the grain from the Midianites.
The Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared to him and said, “Mighty hero, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with you!”

“Gydaun replied, Sir if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with us, why has all this happened to us? And where are all the miracles our ancestors told us about? Did they not say, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought us up out of Mitzraym’? But now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has abandoned us and handed us over to the Midianites.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH turned to him and Dabar, “Go with the strength you have, and rescue Yashar'AL from the Midianites. I am sending you!”
“Gydaun replied, “how can I rescue Yashar'AL? My clan is the weakest in the whole tribe of Manassah, and I am the least in my entire family!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Gydaun, I will be with you, and you will destroy the Midianites as if you were fighting against one man.”
Gydaun replied, “If you are truly going to help me, show me a sign to prove that it is really 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH speaking to me.
Do not go away until I come back and bring my offering to you.” and He answered, “I will stay here until you return.”

Gydaun hurried home, he cooked a young goat, and with a basket of flour he baked some bread without yeast. Then, carrying the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, he brought them out and presented them to the Malak, who was under the great tree.
The Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Gydaun, “Place the meat and the unleavened bread on this rock, and pour the broth over it.” And Gydaun did as he was told.

Then the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH touched the meat and bread with the tip of the staff in his hand, and fire flamed up from the rock and consumed all he had brought, and the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH disappeared.
When Gydaun realized that it was the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he cried out, “Oh, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, I’m doomed! I have seen the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH face to face!”
“It is all right,” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied. “Do not be afraid. You will not die.”
And Gydaun built an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH there and named it 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH-Shalum (which means “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is peace”). The altar remains in Uphrah in the land of the clan of Abiazar to this day.

That night 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Gydaun, Take the second bull from your father’s herd, the one that is seven years old. Pull down your father’s altar to Baal, and cut down the Asharah pole standing beside it.

Then build an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH here on this hilltop sanctuary, laying the stones carefully. Sacrifice the bull as a burnt offering on the altar, using as fuel the wood of the Asharah pole you cut down.”
So Gydaun took ten of his servants and did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded. But he did it at night because he was afraid of the other members of his father’s household and the people of the town.

Early the next morning, as the people of the town began to stir, someone discovered that the altar of Baal had been broken down and that the Asharah pole beside it had been cut down. In their place a new altar had been built, and on it were the remains of the bull that had been sacrificed.
The people said to each other, “Who did this?” And after asking around and making a careful search, they learned that it was Gydaun, the son of Yuash.
“Bring out your son,” the men of the town demanded of Yuash. “He must die for destroying the altar of Baal and for cutting down the Asharah pole.”

But Yuash shouted to the mob that confronted him, “Why are you defending Baal? Will you argue his case? Whoever pleads his case will be put to death by morning! If Baal truly is mighty, let him defend himself and destroy the one who broke down his altar!”
From then on Gydaun was called Yarub-baal, which means “Let Baal defend himself,” because he broke down Baal’s altar.
Soon afterward the armies of Midian, Amalak, and the people of the east formed an alliance against Yashar'AL and crossed the Yurdan, camping in the valley of Yazraal.
Then the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH clothed Gydaun with power. Gydaun blew a ram’s horn as a call to arms, and the men of the clan of Abiazar came to him.
He also sent messengers throughout Manassah, Ashar, Zabulun, and Naphtali, summoning their warriors, and all of them responded.
Then Gydaun said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “If you are truly going to use me to rescue Yashar'AL as you promised,

prove it to me in this way. I will put a wool fleece on the threshing floor tonight. If the fleece is wet with dew in the morning but the ground is dry, then I will know that you are going to help me rescue Yashar'AL as you promised.”
And that is just what happened. When Gydaun got up early the next morning, he squeezed the fleece and wrung out a whole bowlful of water.

Then Gydaun said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Please don’t be angry with me, but let me make one more request. Let me use the fleece for one more test. This time let the fleece remain dry while the ground around it is wet with dew.”
So that night 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did as Gydaun asked. The fleece was dry in the morning, but the ground was covered with dew.
So Yarub-baal (that is, Gydaun) and his army got up early and went as far as the spring of Harud. The armies of Midian were camped north of them in the valley near the hill of Murah.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Gydaun, “You have too many warriors with you. If I let all of you fight the Midianites, the Yasharalym will boast to me that they saved themselves by their own strength.
Therefore, tell the people, ‘Whoever is timid or afraid may leave this mountain and go home.’” So twenty two thousand of them went home, leaving only ten thousand who were willing to fight.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Gydaun, “There are still too many! Bring them down to the spring, and I will test them to determine who will go with you and who will not.”

When Gydaun took his warriors down to the water, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told him, “Divide the men into two groups. In one group put all those who cup water in their hands and lap it up with their tongues like dogs. In the other group put all those who kneel down and drink with their mouths in the stream.”
Only three hundred of the men drank from their hands. All the others got down on their knees and drank with their mouths in the stream.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Gydaun, “With these three hundred men I will rescue you and give you victory over the Midianites. Send all the others home.”
So Gydaun collected the provisions and rams’ horns of the other warriors and sent them home. But he kept the three hundred men with him. The Midianite camp was in the valley just below Gydaun.
That night 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “Get up! Go down into the Midianite camp, for I have given you victory over them!
But if you are afraid to attack, go down to the camp with your servant Purah.
Listen to what the Midianites are saying, and you will be greatly encouraged. Then you will be eager to attack.” So Gydaun took Purah and went down to the edge of the enemy camp.
The armies of Midian, Amalak, and the people of the east had settled in the valley like a swarm of locusts. Their camels were like grains of sand on the seashore, too many to count!

Gydaun crept up just as a man was telling his companion about a dream, the man said, “I had this dream, and in my dream a loaf of barley bread came tumbling down into the Midianite camp. It hit a tent, turned it over, and knocked it flat!”
His companion answered, “Your dream can mean only one thing 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given Gydaun son of Yuash, the Yasharalym, victory over Midian and all its allies!”

When Gydaun heard the dream and its interpretation, he bowed in worship before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then he returned to the Yasharalym camp and shouted, “Get up! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you victory over the Midianite hordes!”
He divided the 300 men into three groups and gave each man a ram’s horn and a clay jar with a torch in it.
Then he said to them, “Keep your eyes on me. When I come to the edge of the camp, do just as I do.
As soon as I and those with me blow the rams’ horns, blow your horns, too, all around the entire camp, and shout, ‘For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and for Gydaun!’”

It was just after midnight, after the changing of the guard, when Gydaun and the one hundred men with him reached the edge of the Midianite camp. Suddenly, they blew the rams’ horns and broke their clay jars.

Then all three groups blew their horns and broke their jars. They held the blazing torches in their left hands and the horns in their right hands, and they all shouted, “A sword for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and for Gydaun!”
Each man stood at his position around the camp and watched as all the Midianites rushed around in a panic, shouting as they ran to escape.

When the three hundred Yasharalym blew their rams’ horns, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH caused the warriors in the camp to fight against each other with their swords, those who were not killed fled to places as far away as Bath-shittah near Zararah and to the border of Abal-mahulah near Tabbath.
Then Gydaun sent for the warriors of Naphtali, Ashar, and Manassah, who joined in chasing the army of Midian.

Gydaun also sent messengers throughout the hill country of Aphraim, saying, “Come down to attack the Midianites. Cut them off at the shallow crossings of the Yurdan River at Bath-barah.” So all the men of Aphraim did as they were told.

They captured Urab and Zaab, the two Midianite commanders, killing Urab at the rock of Urab, and Zaab at the winepress of Zaab. And they continued to chase the Midianites. Afterward the Yasharalym brought the heads of Urab and Zaab to Gydaun, who was by the Yurdan River.
Then the people of Aphraim asked Gydaun, “Why have you treated us this way? Why did you not send for us when you first went out to fight the Midianites?” And they argued heatedly with Gydaun.
But Gydaun replied, “What have I accomplished compared to you? even the leftover grapes of Aphraim’s harvest is better than the entire crop of my little clan of Abiazar?

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave you victory over Urab and Zaab, the commanders of the Midianite army. What have I accomplished compared to that?” When the men of Aphraim heard Gydaun’s answer, their anger subsided.
Gydaun then crossed the Yurdan River with his three hundred men, and though exhausted, they continued to chase the enemy.
When they reached Succuth, Gydaun asked the leaders of the town, “Please give my warriors some food. They are very tired. I am chasing Zabah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
But the officials of Succuth replied, “Catch Zabah and Zalmunna first, and then we will feed your army.”
So Gydaun said, “After 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives me victory over Zabah and Zalmunna, I will return and tear your flesh with the thorns and briers from the wilderness.”
From there Gydaun went up to Panial and again asked for food, but he got the same answer.
So he said to the people of Panial, “After I return in victory, I will tear down this tower.”
By this time Zabah and Zalmunna were in Karkur with about fifteen thousand warriors, all that remained of the allied armies of the east, for one hundred and twenty thousand had already been killed.
Gydaun circled around by the caravan route east of Nubah and Yugbahah, taking the Midianite army by surprise.
Zabah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings, fled, but Gydaun chased them down and captured all their warriors.
After this, Gydaun returned from the battle by way of Haras Pass.
There he captured a young man from Succuth and demanded that he write down the names of all the seventy-seven officials and elders in the town.

Gydaun then returned to Succuth and said to the leaders, “Here are Zabah and Zalmunna. When we were here before, you taunted me, saying, ‘Catch Zabah and Zalmunna first, and then we will feed your exhausted army.’”
Then Gydaun took the elders of the town and taught them a lesson, punishing them with thorns and briers from the wilderness.
He also tore down the tower of Panial and killed all the men in the town.
Then Gydaun asked Zabah and Zalmunna, “The men you killed at Tabur, what were they like? “Like you,” they replied. “They all had the look of a king’s son.”
“They were my brothers, the sons of my own mother!” Gydaun exclaimed. “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, I wouldn’t kill you if you hadn’t killed them.”
Turning to Yathar, his oldest son, he said, “Kill them!” But Yathar did not draw his sword, for he was only a boy and was afraid.
Then Zabah and Zalmunna said to Gydaun, “Be a man! Kill us yourself!” So Gydaun killed them both and took the royal ornaments from the necks of their camels.
Then the Yasharalym said to Gydaun, “Be our ruler! You and your son and your grandson will be our rulers, for you have rescued us from Midian.”
But Gydaun replied, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will rule over you!
However, I do have one request, that each of you give me an earring from the plunder you collected from your fallen enemies.” (The enemies, being Ishmaalites, all wore gold earrings.)
“Gladly!” they replied. They spread out a cloak, and each one threw in a gold earring he had gathered from the plunder.

The weight of the gold earrings was forty-three pounds, not including the royal ornaments and pendants, the purple clothing worn by the kings of Midian, or the chains around the necks of their camels.
Gydaun made a sacred ephod from the gold and put it in Uphrah, his hometown. But soon all the Yasharalym prostituted themselves by worshiping it, and it became a trap for Gydaun and his family.
That is the story of how the people of Yashar'AL defeated Midian, which never recovered. Throughout the rest of Gydaun’s lifetime, about forty years, there was peace in the land.
Then Gydaun son of Yuash returned home.
He had seventy sons born to him, for he had many wives.
He also had a concubine in Shacham, who gave birth to a son, whom he named Abimalach.
Gydaun died when he was very old, and he was buried in the grave of his father Yuash, at Uphrah in the land of the clan of Abiazar.
As soon as Gydaun died, the Yasharalym prostituted themselves by worshiping the images of Baal, making Baal-barith their deities.
They forgot 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who had rescued them from all their enemies surrounding them.
Nor did they show any loyalty to the family of Yarub-baal (that is, Gydaun), despite all the good he had done for Yashar'AL.
One day Gydaun’s son Abimalach went to Shacham to visit his uncles, his mother’s brothers, he said to them and to the rest of his mother’s family,
“Ask the leading citizens of Shacham whether they want to be ruled by all seventy of Gydaun’s sons or by one man. And remember that I am your own flesh and blood!”

So Abimalach’s uncles gave his message to all the citizens of Shacham on his behalf, and after listening to this proposal, the people of Shacham decided in favor of Abimalach because he was their relative.
They gave him seventy silver coins from the temple of Baal-barith, which he used to hire some reckless troublemakers who agreed to follow him.
He went to his father’s home at Uphrah, and there, on one stone, they killed all seventy of his half brothers, the sons of Gydaun. But the youngest brother, Yutham, escaped and hid.
Then all the leading citizens of Shacham and Bath-millu called a meeting under the oak beside the pillar at Shacham and made Abimalach their king.
When Yutham heard about this, he climbed to the top of Mount Garizim and shouted, “Listen to me, citizens of Shacham! Listen to me if you want 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH to listen to you!
Once upon a time the trees decided to choose a king. First they said to the olive tree, ‘Be our king!’
But the olive tree refused, saying, ‘Should I quit producing the olive oil that barak both 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and people, just to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“Then they said to the fig tree, You be our king!’
But the fig tree also refused, saying, ‘Should I quit producing my sweet fruit just to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“Then they said to the grapevine, You be our king!’
But the grapevine also refused, saying, Should I quit producing the wine that cheers both 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and people, just to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“Then all the trees finally turned to the thornbush and said, Come, you be our king!’
And the thornbush replied to the trees, ‘If you truly want to make me your king, come and take shelter in my shade. If not, let fire come out from me and devour the cedars of Labanun.’”

Yutham continued, “Now make sure you have acted honorably and in good faith by making Abimalach your king, and that you have done right by Gydaun and all of his descendants. Have you treated him with the honor he deserves for all he accomplished?
For he fought for you and risked his life when he rescued you from the Midianites.

But today you have revolted against my father and his descendants, killing his seventy sons on one stone. And you have chosen his slave woman’s son, Abimalach, to be your king just because he is your relative.
“If you have acted honorably and in good faith toward Gydaun and his descendants today, then may you find joy in Abimalach, and may he find joy in you.

But if you have not acted in good faith, then may fire come out from Abimalach and devour the leading citizens of Shachem and Bath-millu; and may fire come out from the citizens of Shacham and Bath-millu and devour Abimalach!”
Then Yutham escaped and lived in Baar because he was afraid of his brother Abimalach.
After Abimalach had ruled over Yashar'AL for three years,
(AL'Mighty ONE) 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH sent a ruach (spirit) that stirred up trouble between Abimalach and the leading citizens of Shacham, and they revolted.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was punishing Abimalach for murdering Gydaun’s seventy sons, and the citizens of Shacham for supporting him in this treachery of murdering his brothers.
The citizens of Shacham set an ambush for Abimalach on the hilltops and robbed everyone who passed that way. But someone warned Abimalach about their plot.
One day Gaal son of Abad moved to Shacham with his brothers and gained the confidence of the leading citizens of Shacham.
During the annual harvest festival at Shacham, held in the temple of the local idol, the wine flowed freely, and everyone began cursing Abimalach.

“Who is Abimalach?” Gaal shouted. “He’s not a true son of Shacham, so why should we be his servants? He’s merely the son of Gydaun, and this Zabul is merely his deputy. Serve the true sons of Hamur, the founder of Shacham. Why should we serve Abimalach?
If I were in charge here, I would get rid of Abimalach. I would say to him, ‘Get some soldiers, and come out and fight!’”
But when Zabul, the leader of the city, heard what Gaal was saying, he was furious.
He sent messengers to Abimalach in Arumah, telling him, “Gaal son of Abad and his brothers have come to live in Shacham, and now they are inciting the city to rebel against you.
Come by night with an army and hide out in the fields.
In the morning, as soon as it is daylight, attack the city. When Gaal and those who are with him come out against you, you can do with them as you wish.”
So Abimelech and all his men went by night and split into four groups, stationing themselves around Shacham.
Gaal was standing at the city gates when Abimalach and his army came out of hiding.
When Gaal saw them, he said to Zabul, “Look, there are people coming down from the hilltops!” Zabul replied, “It’s just the shadows on the hills that look like men.”
But again Gaal said, “No, people are coming down from the hills. And another group is coming down the road past the Diviners’ Oak.”

Then Zabul turned on him and asked, “Now where is that big mouth of yours? Wasn’t it you that said, ‘Who is Abimalach, and why should we be his servants?’ The men you mocked are right outside the city! Go out and fight them!”
So Gaal led the leading citizens of Shacham into battle against Abimalach.
But Abimalach chased him, and many of Shacham’s men were wounded and fell along the road as they retreated to the city gate.
Abimelech returned to Arumah, and Zabul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shacham.
The next day the people of Shacham went out into the fields to battle. When Abimalach heard about it,
he divided his men into three groups and set an ambush in the fields. When Abimalach saw the people coming out of the city, he and his men jumped up from their hiding places and attacked them.
Abimalach and his group stormed the city gate to keep the men of Shacham from getting back in, while the other two groups of Abimalach cut them down in the fields.
The battle went on all day before Abimalach finally captured the city. He killed the people, leveled the city, and scattered salt all over the ground.
When the leading citizens who lived in the tower of Shacham heard what had happened, they ran and hid in the temple of Baal-barith.
Someone reported to Abimalach that the citizens had gathered in the temple,
so he led his forces to Mount Zalmun, he took an ax and chopped some branches from a tree, then put them on his shoulder. “Quick, do as I have done!” he told his men.

So each of them cut down some branches, following Abimalach’s example. They piled the branches against the walls of the temple and set them on fire. So all the people who had lived in the tower of Shacham died, about one thousand men and women.
Then Abimalach attacked the town of Thabaz and captured it.
But there was a strong tower inside the town, and all the men and women, the entire population fled to it. They barricaded themselves in and climbed up to the roof of the tower.
Abimalach followed them to attack the tower. But as he prepared to set fire to the entrance,
a woman on the roof dropped a millstone that landed on Abimalach’s head and crushed his skull.
He quickly said to his young armor bearer, “Draw your sword and kill me! Do not let it be said that a woman killed Abimalach!” So the young man ran him through with his sword, and he died.
When Abimalach’s men saw that he was dead, they disbanded and returned to their homes.
In this way, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH punished Abimalach for the evil he had done against his father by murdering his seventy brothers.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH also punished the men of Shacham for all their evil. So the curse of Yutham son of Gydaun was fulfilled.
After Abimalach died, Tula son of Puah, son of Dudu, was the next person to rescue Yashar'AL, he was from the tribe of Issachar but lived in the town of Shamir in the hill country of Aphraim.
He judged Yashar'AL for twenty-three years. When he died, he was buried in Shamir.
After Tula died, Yair from Gilaad judged Yashar'AL for twenty-two years.
His thirty sons rode around on thirty donkeys, and they owned thirty towns in the land of Gilaad, which are still called the Towns of Yair.
When Yair died, he was buried in Kamun.

Again the Yasharalym did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. They served the images of Baal and Ashturath, and the idols of Aram, Sidun, Muab, Ammun, and Philistia. They abandoned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and no longer served him at all.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH burned with anger against Yashar'AL, and he turned them over to the Philistines and the Ammunites,
who began to oppress them that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the Yasharalym east of the Yurdan River in the land of the Amurites (that is, in Gilaad).
The Ammunites also crossed to the west side of the Yurdan and attacked Yahudah, Banyamin, and Aphraim. The Yasharalym were in great distress.
Finally, they cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for help, saying, “We have sinned against you because we have abandoned you as our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and have served the images of Baal.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied, “Did I not rescue you from the Mitzraym, the Amurites, the Ammunites, the Philistines,
the Sidunians, the Amalekites, and the Maunites? When they oppressed you, you cried out to me for help, and I rescued you.
Yet you have abandoned me and served other nations pagan idols. So I will not rescue you anymore.
Go and cry out to the idols you have chosen! Let them rescue you in your hour of distress!”
But the Yasharalym pleaded with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and said, “We have sinned. Punish us as you see fit, only rescue us today from our enemies.”
Then the Yasharalym put aside their foreign idols and served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was grieved by their misery.
At that time the armies of Ammun had gathered for war and were camped in Gilaad, and the people of Yashar'AL assembled and camped at Mizpah.
The leaders of Gilaad said to each other, “Whoever attacks the Ammunites first will become ruler over all the people of Gilaad.”
Now Yaphthah of Gilaad was a great warrior. He was the son of Gilaad, but his mother was a prostitute.

Gilaad’s wife also had several sons, and when these half brothers grew up, they chased Yaphthah off the land. “You will not get any of our father’s inheritance,” they said, “for you are the son of a prostitute.”
So Yaphthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tub. Soon he had a band of worthless rebels following him.
At about this time, the Ammunites began their war against Yashar'AL.
When the Ammunites attacked, the elders of Gilaad sent for Yaphthah in the land of Tub.
The elders said, “Come and be our commander! Help us fight the Ammunites!”
But Yaphthah said to them, “Aren’t you the ones who hated me and drove me from my father’s house? Why do you come to me now when you’re in trouble?”
“The elders said to Yaphthah; Because we need you, “If you lead us in battle against the Ammunites, we will make you ruler over all the people of Gilaad.”
Yaphthah said to the elders, “Let me get this straight. If I come with you and if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives me victory over the Ammunites, will you really make me ruler over all the people?”
The elders replied and said to him, let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH be our witness, “We promise to do whatever you say.”
So Yaphthah went with the elders of Gilaad, and the people made him their ruler and commander of the army. At Mizpah, in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Yaphthah repeated what he had said to the elders.
Then Yaphthah sent messengers to the king of Ammun, asking, “Why have you come out to fight against my land?”

The king of Ammun answered Yaphthah’s messengers, “When the Yasharalym came out of Mitzraym, they stole my land from the Arnun River to the Yabbuk River and all the way to the Yurdan. Now then, give back the land peaceably.”
Yaphthah sent this message back to the Ammunites king:
“This is what Yaphthah says: Yashar'AL did not steal any land from Muab or Ammun.
When the people of Yashar'AL arrived at Kadash on their journey from Mitzraym after crossing the Red Sea,

they sent messengers to the king of Adum asking for permission to pass through his land. But their request was denied. Then they asked the king of Muab for similar permission, but he would not let them pass through either. So the people of Yashar'AL stayed in Kadash.

“Finally, they went around Adum and Muab through the wilderness. They traveled along Muab’s eastern border and camped on the other side of the Arnun River. But they never once crossed the Arnun River into Muab, for the Arnun was the border of Muab.
“Then Yashar'AL sent messengers to King Sihun of the Amurites, who ruled from Hashbun, asking for permission to cross through his land to get to their destination.
But King Sihun did not trust Yashar'AL to pass through his land. Instead, he mobilized his army at Yahaz and attacked them.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, gave his people victory over King Sihun. So Yashar'AL took control of all the land of the Amurites, who lived in that region,
from the Arnun River to the Yabbuk River, and from the eastern wilderness to the Yurdan.
“So you see, it was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, who took away the land from the Amurites and gave it to Yashar'AL. Why then, should we give it back to you?
You keep whatever your pagan idol Chamush gives you, and we will keep whatever 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH gives us.
Are you any better than Balak son of Zippur, king of Muab? Did he try to make a case against Yashar'AL for disputed land? Did he go to war against them?

Yashar'AL has been living here for three hundred years, inhabiting Hashbun and its surrounding settlements, all the way to Aruar and its settlements, and in all the towns along the Arnun River. Why have you made no effort to recover it before now?
Therefore, I have not sinned against you. Rather, you have wronged me by attacking me. Let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who is judge, decide today which of us is right Yashar'AL or Ammun.”
But the king of Ammun paid no attention to Yaphthah’s message.
At that time the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came upon Yaphthah, and he went throughout the land of Gilaad and Manassah, including Mizpah in Gilaad, and from there he led an army against the Ammunites.
And Yaphthah made a vow to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Yaphthah said, “If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH give me victory over the Ammunites,
I will give to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH whatever comes out of my house to meet me when I return in triumph. I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering.”
So Yaphthah led his army against the Ammunites, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave him victory.
He crushed the Ammunites, devastating about twenty towns from Aruar to an area near Minnith and as far away as Abal-karamim. In this way Yashar'AL defeated the Ammunites.
When Yaphthah returned home to Mizpah, his daughter came out to meet him, playing on a tambourine and dancing for joy. She was his one and only child; he had no other sons or daughters.

When he saw her, he tore his clothes in anguish. “Oh, my daughter!” he cried out. “You have completely destroyed me! You’ve brought disaster on me! For I have made a vow to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and I cannot take it back.”
And she said, “Father, if you have made a vow to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you must do to me what you have vowed, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given you a great victory over your enemies, the Ammunites.
But first let me do this one thing: Let me go up and roam in the hills and weep with my friends for two months, because I will die a virgin.”
“You may go,” Yaphthah said. And he sent her away for two months. She and her friends went into the hills and wept because she would never have children.
When she returned home, her father kept the vow he had made, and she died a virgin. So it has become a custom in Yashar'AL
for young Yasharalym women to go away for four days each year to lament the fate of Yaphthah’s daughter.

Then the people of Aphraim mobilized an army and crossed over the Yurdan River to Zaphun. They sent this message to Yaphthah: “Why didn’t you call for us to help you fight against the Ammunites? We are going to burn down your house with you in it!”
Yaphthah replied, “I summoned you at the beginning of the dispute, but you refused to come! You failed to help us in our struggle against Ammun.
So when I realized you were not coming, I risked my life and went to battle without you, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave me victory over the Ammunites. So why have you now come to fight me?”

The people of Aphraim responded, “You men of Gilaad are nothing more than fugitives from Aphraim and Manassah.” So Yaphthah gathered all the men of Gilaad and attacked the men of Aphraim and defeated them.

Yaphthah captured the shallow crossings of the Yurdan River, and whenever a fugitive from Aphraim tried to go back across, the men of Gilaad would challenge him. “Are you a member of the tribe of Aphraim?” they would ask. If the man said, “No, I’m not,”

they would tell him to say “Sibbulath.” If he was from Aphraim, he would say “Sibbulath,” because people from Aphraim cannot pronounce the word correctly. Then they would take him and kill him at the shallow crossings of the Yurdan. In all, forty two thousand Aphraimites were killed at that time.
Yaphthah judged Yashar'AL for six years. When he died, he was buried in one of the towns of Gilaad.
After Yaphthah died, Ibzan from Bathlaham judged Yashar'AL.

He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He sent his daughters to marry men outside his clan, and he brought in thirty young women from outside his clan to marry his sons. Ibzan judged Yashar'AL for seven years.
When he died, he was buried at Bathlaham.
After Ibzan died, Alun from the tribe of Zabulun judged Yashar'AL for ten years.
When he died, he was buried at Aijalun in Zabulun.
After Alun died, Abdun son of Hillal, from Pirathon, judged Yashar'AL.
He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He judged Yashar'AL for eight years.
When he died, he was buried at Pirathon in Aphraim, in the hill country of the Amalakites.
Again the Yasharalym did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH handed them over to the Philistines, who oppressed them for forty years.
In those days a man named Manuah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zurah. His wife was unable to become pregnant, and they had no children.
The Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared to Manuah’s wife and said, “Even though you have been unable to have children, you will soon become pregnant and give birth to a son.
So be careful; you must not drink wine or any other alcoholic drink nor eat any forbidden food.

You will become pregnant and give birth to a son, and his hair must never be cut. For he will be dedicated to 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH as a Nazirite from birth, he will begin to rescue Yashar'AL from the Philistines.”

The woman ran and told her husband, “A man of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH appeared to me! He looked like one of the Malakym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, terrifying to see. I did not ask where he was from, and He did not tell me his name.

But he told me, ‘You will become pregnant and give birth to a son. You must not drink wine or any other alcoholic drink nor eat any forbidden food. For your son will be dedicated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as a Nazarite from the moment of his birth until the day of his death.’”
Then Manuah prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, saying, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, please let the man of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH come back to us again and give us more instructions about this son who is to be born.”
Then 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH answered Manuah’s prayer, and the Malak of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH appeared once again to his wife as she was sitting in the field. But her husband, Manuah, was not with her.
So she quickly ran and told her husband, “The man who appeared to me the other day is here again!”
Manuah ran back with his wife and asked, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife the other day? “Yes,” he replied, “I am.”
So Manuah asked him, “When your words come true, what kind of rules should govern the boy’s life and work?”
The Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied, “Be sure your wife follows the instructions I gave her.
She must not eat grapes or raisins, drink wine or any other alcoholic drink, or eat any forbidden food.”
Then Manuah said to the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Please stay here until we can prepare a young goat for you to eat.”

“I will stay,” the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied, “but I will not eat anything. However, you may prepare a burnt offering as a sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” (Manuah didn’t realize it was the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.)
Then Manuah asked the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “What is your name? For when all this comes true, we want to honor you.”
“Why do you ask my name?” the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied. “It is too wonderful for you to understand.”
Then Manuah took a young goat and a grain offering and offered it on a rock as a sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And as Manuah and his wife watched, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did an amazing thing.
As the flames from the altar shot up toward the sky, the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH ascended in the fire. When Manuah and his wife saw this, they fell with their faces to the ground.
The Malak did not appear again to Manuah and his wife. Manuah finally realized it was the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
and he said to his wife, “We will certainly die, for we have seen 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH!”

But his wife said, “If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was going to kill us, he would not have accepted our burnt offering and grain offering. He would not have appeared to us and told us this wonderful thing and done these miracles.”
When her son was born, she named him Shamsun, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Baraked him as he grew up.
And the RUACH of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH began to stir him while he lived in Mahanah-dan, which is located between the towns of Zurah and Ashtaul.
One day when Shamsun was in Timnah, one of the Philistine women caught his eye.
When he returned home, he told his father and mother, “A young Philistine woman in Timnah caught my eye. I want to marry her. Get her for me.”
His father and mother objected. “Is there not even one woman in our tribe or among all the Yasharalym you could marry?” they asked. “Why must you go to the pagan Philistines to find a wife?”
His father and mother had not realized that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was at work in this, creating an opportunity to work against the Philistines, who ruled over Yashar'AL at that time.
As Shamsun and his parents were going down to Timnah, a young lion suddenly attacked Shamsun near the vineyards of Timnah.

At that moment the RUACH of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came powerfully upon him, and he ripped the lion’s jaws apart with his bare hands, he did it as easily as if it were a young goat. But he did not tell his father or mother about it.
When Shamsun arrived in Timnah, he talked with the woman and was very pleased with her.
Later, when he returned to Timnah for the wedding, he turned off the path to look at the carcass of the lion, and he found that a swarm of bees had made some honey in the carcass.

He scooped some of the honey into his hands and ate it along the way, Shamsun also gave some to his father and mother, and they ate it. But he did not tell them he had taken the honey from the carcass of the lion.
As his father was making final arrangements for the marriage, Shamsun threw a party at Timnah, as was the custom for elite young men.
When the bride’s parents saw him, they selected thirty young men from the town to be his companions.
Shamsun said to them, “Let me tell you a riddle. If you solve my riddle during these seven days of the celebration, I will give you thirty fine linen robes and thirty sets of festive clothing.
But if you cannot solve it, then you must give me thirty fine linen robes and thirty sets of festive clothing.” All right,” they agreed, “let’s hear your riddle.”
So he said: Out of the one who eats came something to eat; out of the strong came something sweet.” Three days later they were still trying to figure it out.

On the fourth day they said to Shamsun’s wife, “Entice your husband to explain the riddle for us, or we will burn down your father’s house with you in it. Did you invite us to this party just to make us poor?”

So Shamsun’s wife came to him in tears and said, “You do not love me; you hate me! You have given my people a riddle, but you have not told me the answer." Shamsun said to her, I have not even given the answer to my father or mother, “Why should I tell you?”

So she cried whenever she was with him and kept it up for the rest of the celebration. At last, on the seventh day he told her the answer because she was tormenting him with her nagging. Then she explained the riddle to the young men.

So before sunset of the seventh day, the men of the town came to Shamsun with their answer: What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?” Shamsun replied, “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you wouldn’t have solved my riddle!”

Then the RUACH of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came powerfully upon Shamsun, and he went down to the town of Ashkalun, killed thirty men, took their belongings, and gave their clothing to the men who had solved his riddle. But Shamsun was furious about what had happened, and he went back home to live with his father and mother.
So his wife was given in marriage to the man who had been Shamsun’s best man at the marriage.
Later on, during the wheat harvest, Shamsun took a young goat as a present to his wife. He said, “I’m going into my wife’s room to sleep with her,” but her father did not let him in.
“I truly thought you must hate her,” her father explained, “so I gave her in marriage to your best man. But look, her younger sister is even more beautiful than she is. Marry her instead.”
Shamsun said, “This time I cannot be blamed for everything I am going to do to you Philistines.”
Then he went out and caught 300 foxes, he tied their tails together in pairs, and he fastened a fire torch to each pair of tails.

Then Shamsun lit the torches and let the foxes run through the grain fields of the Philistines, he burned all their grain to the ground, including the sheaves and the uncut grain, he also destroyed their vineyards and olive groves.

“When the Philistines asked who had done this, they learned Shamsun had done this, “because his father-in-law from Timnah gave Shamsun’s wife to be married to his best man.” So the Philistines went and got the woman and her father and burned them to death.
And Shamsun vowed, because you did this, “I will not rest until I take my revenge on you!”
So Shamsun attacked the Philistines with great fury and killed many of them, then he went to live in a cave in the rock of Atam.
The Philistines retaliated by setting up camp in Yahudah and spreading out near the town of Lahi.
The men of Yahudah asked the Philistines, “Why are you attacking us?” The Philistines replied, “We have come to capture Shamsun. We have come to pay him back for what he did to us.”
