So the assembly sent twelve thousand of their best warriors to Yabash-gilaad with orders to kill everyone there, including women and children.
“This is what you are to do,” they said. “Completely destroy all the males and every woman who is not a virgin.”
Among the residents of Yabash-gilaad they found four hundred young virgins who had never slept with a man, and they brought them to the camp at Shiluh in the land of Canaan.
The Yasharalym assembly sent a peace delegation to the remaining people of Banyamin who were living at the rock of Rimmun.
Then the men of Banyamin returned to their homes, and the four hundred women of Yabash-gilaad who had been spared were given to them as wives. But there were not enough women for all of them.
The people felt sorry for Banyamin because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had made this gap among the tribes of Yashar'AL.
So the elders of the assembly asked, “How can we find wives for the few who remain, since the women of the tribe of Banyamin are dead?
There must be heirs for the survivors so that an entire tribe of Yashar'AL is not wiped out.
But we cannot give them our own daughters in marriage because we have sworn with a solemn oath that anyone who does this will fall under the curse of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then they thought of the annual festival of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH held in Shiluh, south of Lebunah and north of Bathal, along the east side of the road that goes from Bathal to Shacham.
They told the men of Banyamin who still needed wives, “Go and hide in the vineyards.
When you see the young women of Shiluh come out for their dances, rush out from the vineyards, and each of you can take one of them home to the land of Banyamin to be your wife!

And when their fathers and brothers come to us in protest, we will tell them, ‘Please be sympathetic. Let them have your daughters, for we did not find wives for all of them when we destroyed Yabash-gilaad. And you are not guilty of breaking the vow since you did not actually give your daughters to them in marriage.’”

So the men of Banyamin did as they were told. Each man caught one of the women as she danced in the celebration and carried her off to be his wife. They returned to their own land, and they rebuilt their towns and lived in them.
Then the people of Yashar'AL departed by tribes and families, and they returned to their own homes.
In those days Yashar'AL had no king; all the people did whatever seemed right in their own eyes.

books.name: Ruth
chapters: In the days when the judges ruled in Yashar'AL, a severe famine came upon the land. So a man from Bathlaham in Yahudah left his home and went to live in the country of Muab, taking his wife and two sons with him.

The man’s name was Alimalach, and his wife was Naumi, their two sons were Mahlun and Kiliun, they were Aphrathites from Bethlaham in the land of Yahudah, and when they reached Muab, they settled there.
Then Alimalach died, and Naumi was left with her two sons.
The two sons married Muabite women. One married a woman named Urpah, and the other a woman named Ruth. But about ten years later,
both Mahlun and Kiliun died, this left Naumi alone, without her two sons or her husband.
Then Naumi heard in Muab that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Baraked his people in Yahudah by giving them good crops again. So Naumi and her daughters-in-law got ready to leave Muab to return to her homeland.
With her two daughters-in-law she set out from the place where she had been living, and they took the road that would lead them back to Yahudah.
But on the way, Naumi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back to your mothers’ homes, and may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH reward you for your kindness to your husbands and to me.
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH barak you with the security of another marriage.” Then she kissed them good-bye, and they all broke down and wept.
“No,” they said. “We want to go with you to your people.”
But Naumi replied, “Why should you go on with me? Can I still give birth to other sons who could grow up to be your husbands?
No, my daughters, return to your parents’ homes, for I am too old to marry again, and even if it were possible, and I were to get married tonight and bear sons, then what?

Would you wait for them to grow up and refuse to marry someone else? No, of course not, my daughters! Things are far more bitter for me than for you, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH himself has raised his fist against me.”
And again they wept together, and Urpah kissed her mother-in-law good-bye. But Ruth clung tightly to Naumi.
“Look,” Naumi said to her, “your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her idols, you should do the same.”
But Ruth replied, “Do not ask me to leave you and turn back. Wherever you go, I will go; wherever you live, I will live. Your people will be my people, and your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will be my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Wherever you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH punish me severely if I allow anything but death to separate us!”
When Naumi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she said nothing more.
So the two of them continued on their journey. When they came to Bathlaham, the entire town was excited by their arrival. “Is it really Naumi?” the women asked.
“She said to them, do not call me Naumi, “Instead, call me Mara, for the Almighty has made life very bitter for me.
I went away full, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought me home empty, why call me Naumi when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has caused me to suffer and the Almighty has sent such tragedy upon me?”
So Naumi returned from Muab, accompanied by her daughter-in-law Ruth, the young Muabite woman. They arrived in Bathlaham in late spring, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
Now there was a wealthy and influential man in Bathlaham named Buaz, who was a relative of Naumi’s husband, Alimalach.

One day Ruth the Muabite said to Naumi, “Let me go out into the harvest fields to pick up the stalks of grain left behind by anyone who is kind enough to let me do it.” Naumi replied, “All right, my daughter, go ahead.”
So Ruth went out to gather grain behind the harvesters, and as it happened, she found herself working in a field that belonged to Buaz, the relative of her father-in-law, Alimalach.
While she was there, Buaz arrived from Bathlaham and greeted the harvesters. “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH be with you!” he said, and the harvest replied to Buaz; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH barak you.
Then Buaz asked his foreman, “Who is that young woman over there? Who does she belong to?”
And the foreman replied, “She is the young woman from Muab who came back with Naumi.
She asked me this morning if she could gather grain behind the harvesters. She has been hard at work ever since, except for a few minutes’ rest in the shelter.”
Buaz went over and said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Stay right here with us when you gather grain; do not go to any other fields. Stay right behind the young women working in my field.

See which part of the field they are harvesting, and then follow them. I have warned the young men not to treat you roughly, and when you are thirsty, help yourself to the water they have drawn from the well.”
Ruth fell at his feet and thanked him warmly. “What have I done to deserve such kindness?” she asked. “I am only a foreigner.”

“Yes, I know,” Buaz replied. “But I also know about everything you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, I have heard how you left your father and mother and your own land to live here among complete strangers.
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, under whose wings you have come to take refuge, reward you fully for what you have done.”
“And Ruth said to Buaz; I hope, I continue to please you, sir, “you have comforted me by speaking so kindly to me, even though I am not one of your workers.”

At mealtime Buaz called to her, “Come over here, and help yourself to some food, you can dip your bread in the sour wine.” So she sat with his harvesters, and Buaz gave her some roasted grain to eat, she ate all she wanted and still had some left over.
When Ruth went back to work again, Buaz ordered his young men, “Let her gather grain right among the sheaves without stopping her.
And pull out some heads of barley from the bundles and drop them on purpose for her. Let her pick them up, and do not give her a hard time!”
So Ruth gathered barley there all day, and when she beat out the grain that evening, it filled an entire basket.
She carried it back into town and showed it to her mother-in-law, Ruth also gave her the roasted grain that was left over from her meal.

“Where did you gather all this grain today?” Naumi asked. “Where did you work? May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH barak the one who helped you!” So Ruth told her mother-in-law about the man in whose field she had worked, she said, “The man I worked with today is named Buaz.”
“May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH barak him!” Naumi told her daughter-in-law. “He is showing his kindness to us as well as to your dead husband, that man is one of our closest relatives, one of our family redeemers.”
Then Ruth said, “What’s more, Buaz even told me to come back and stay with his harvesters until the entire harvest is completed.”
Naumi said to Ruth. “Do as he said, my daughter. Stay with his young women right through the whole harvest, you might be harassed in other fields, but you will be safe with him.”

So Ruth worked alongside the women in Buaz’s fields and gathered grain with them until the end of the barley harvest, then she continued working with them through the wheat harvest in early summer, and all the while she lived with her mother-in-law.
One day Naumi said to Ruth, “My daughter, it’s time that I found a permanent home for you, so that you will be provided for.
Buaz is a close relative of ours, and he’s been very kind by letting you gather grain with his young women, tonight he will be winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
Now do as I tell you, take a bath and put on perfume and dress in your nicest clothes. Then go to the threshing floor, but do not let Buaz see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
Be sure to notice where he lies down; then go and uncover his feet and lie down there, he will tell you what to do.”
“I will do everything you say,” Ruth replied.
So she went down to the threshing floor that night and followed the instructions of her mother-in-law.
After Buaz had finished eating and drinking and was in good spirits, he lay down at the far end of the pile of grain and went to sleep. Then Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
Around midnight Buaz suddenly woke up and turned over, he was surprised to find a woman lying at his feet!
“And Buaz asked, who are you?” Ruth replied him; “I am your servant Ruth, “Spread the corner of your covering over me, for you are my family redeemer.”
Let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH barak you, my daughter!” Buaz exclaimed. “You are showing even more family loyalty now than you did before, for you have not gone after a younger man, whether rich or poor.
Now do not worry about a thing, my daughter. I will do what is necessary, for everyone in town knows you are a virtuous woman.
I know it is true that I am one of your family redeemers, there is another man who is more closely related to you than I am.

Stay here tonight, and in the morning I will talk to him. If he is willing to redeem you, very well. Let him marry you, but if he is not willing, then as surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, I will redeem you myself! Now lie down here until morning.”

So Ruth lay at Buaz’s feet until the morning, but she got up before it was light enough for people to recognize each other, for Buaz had said, “No one must know that a woman was here at the threshing floor.”
Then Buaz said to her, “Bring your cloak and spread it out.” He measured six scoops of barley into the cloak and placed it on her back. Then he returned to the town.
When Ruth went back to her mother-in-law, Naumi asked, “What happened, my daughter?” Ruth told Naumi everything Buaz had done for her,
and she added, “He gave me these six scoops of barley and said, do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’”
Then Naumi said to her, “Just be patient, my daughter, until we hear what happens, the man will not rest until he has settled things today.”
Now Buaz went up to the gate and sat down there; and behold, the close relative of whom Buaz had spoken came by. So Buaz said, Come aside, friend, sit down here.” So he came aside and sat down.
And Buaz took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, “Sit down here.” So they sat down.
Then Buaz said to the close relative, “Naumi, who has come back from the country of Muab, sold the piece of land which belonged to our brother Alimalach.

And I thought to inform you, saying, ‘Buy it back in the presence of the inhabitants and the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it; but if you will not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know; for there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am next after you.’ and he said, “I will redeem it.”
Then Buaz said, “On the day you buy the field from the hand of Naumi, you must also buy it from Ruth the Muabitess, the wife of the dead, to perpetuate the name of the dead through his inheritance.”
And the close relative said, “I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. You redeem my right of redemption for yourself, for I cannot redeem it.”

Now this was the custom in former times in Yashar'AL concerning redeeming and exchanging, to confirm anything: one man took off his sandal and gave it to the other, and this was a confirmation in Yashar'AL.
Therefore the close relative said to Buaz, “Buy it for yourself.” So he took off his sandal.
And Buaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses this day that I have bought all that was Alimalach’s, and all that was Chiliun’s and Mahlun’s, from the hand of Naumi.

Moreover, Ruth the Muabitess, the widow of Mahlun, I have acquired as my wife, to perpetuate the name of the dead through his inheritance, that the name of the dead may not be cut off from among his brethren and from his position at the gate. You are witnesses this day.”

And all the people who were at the gate, and the elders, said, “We are witnesses. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make the woman who is coming to your house like Rachal and Laah, the two who built the house of Yashar'AL; and may you prosper in Aphrathah and be famous in Bathlaham.
May your house be like the house of Paraz, whom Tamar bore to Yahudah, because of the offspring which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give you from this young woman.”
So Buaz took Ruth and she became his wife; and when he went in to her, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave her conception, and she bore a son.
Then the women said to Naumi, “baraked be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who has not left you this day without a close relative; and may the child's name be famous in Yashar'AL!
And may the child be to you a restorer of life and a nourisher of your old age; for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has borne him.”
Then Naumi took the child and laid him on her bosom, and became a nurse to him.
Also the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, “There is a son born to Naumi.” And they called his name Ubad, he is the father of Yassa, the father of Daud.
Now this is the genealogy of Paraz: Paraz begot Hazrun;
Hezrun begot Ram, and Ram begot Amminadab;
Amminadab begot Nahshun, and Nahshun begot Salmun;
Salmun begot Buaz, and Buaz begot Ubad;
Ubad begot Yassa, and Yassa begot Daud.

books.name: I Samuel
chapters: There was a man named Alkanah who lived in Ramah in the region of Zuph in the hill country of Aphraim, he was the son of Yaruham, son of Alihu, son of Tuhu, son of Zuph in the Tribe of Aphraim.
Alkanah had two wives, Hannah and Paninnah. Paninnah had children, but Hannah did not.
Each year Alkanah would travel to Shiluh to worship and sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at the Tabernacle. The Kuhan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at that time were the two sons of Ali-Huphni and Phinahas.
On the day Alkanah presented his sacrifice, he would give portions of the meat to Paninnah and each of her children.
And though he loved Hannah, he would give her only one choice portion because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given her no children.
So Paninnah would taunt Hannah and make fun of her because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had kept her from having children.
Year after year it was the same, Paninnah would taunt Hannah as they went to the Tabernacle. Each time, Hannah would be reduced to tears and would not even eat.
“Why are you crying, Hannah? Alkanah would ask. “Why are you not eating? Why are you downhearted just because you have no children? You have me is that not better than having ten sons?”
After eating a sacrificial meal at Shiluh, Hannah got up and went to pray. Ali the Kuhan was sitting at his customary place beside the entrance of the Tabernacle.
Hannah was in deep anguish, crying bitterly as she prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

And she made this vow: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, if you will look upon my sorrow and answer my prayer and give me a son, then I will give him back to you, he will be yours for his entire lifetime, and as a sign that he has been dedicated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, his hair will never be cut.”
As she was praying to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Ali watched her.
Seeing her lips moving but hearing no sound, he thought she had been drinking.
“Must you come here drunk?” he demanded. “Throw away your wine!”
“Oh no, sir!” she replied. “I have not been drinking wine or anything stronger, but I am very discouraged, and I was pouring out my heart to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Do not think I am a wicked woman! For I have been praying out of great anguish and sorrow.”
“In that case,” Ali the Kuhan said, “go in Shalum! May the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL grant the request you have asked of Him.”
“Oh, thank you, sir!” she exclaimed. Then she went back and began to eat again, and she was no longer sad.
The entire family got up early the next morning and went to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH once more, then they returned home to Ramah, then Alkanah slept with Hannah, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH remembered her plea,
and in due time she gave birth to a son. She named him Shamu'AL, for she said, “I asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for him.
The next year Alkanah and his family went on their annual trip to offer a sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and to keep his vow.
But Hannah did not go. She told her husband, “Wait until the boy is weaned. Then I will take him to the Tabernacle and leave him there with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH permanently.”
“Whatever you think is best,” Alkanah agreed. “Stay here for now, and may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH help you keep your promise.” So she stayed home and nursed the boy until he was weaned.
When the child was weaned, Hannah took him to the Tabernacle in Shiluh. They brought along a three-year-old bull for the sacrifice and a basket of flour and some wine.
After sacrificing the bull, they brought the boy to Ali the Kuhan.
“Sir, do you remember me?” Hannah asked. “I am the very woman who stood here several years ago praying to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
I asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to give me this boy, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has granted my request.
Now I am giving him to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and he will belong to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his whole life.” And they worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH there.
And Hannah prayed and said: “My heart rejoices in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; My horn is exalted in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. I smile at my enemies, Because I rejoice in Your salvation.
“No one is Qadash like 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, For there is none besides You, Nor is there any rock like our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Stop acting so very proudly; Let no arrogance come from your mouth, For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of knowledge; And by Him actions are weighed.
“The bows of the mighty men are broken, And those who stumbled are girded with strength.
Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, And the hungry have ceased to hunger. Even the barren has borne seven, and she who has many children has become feeble.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH kills and makes alive; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brings down to the grave and brings up.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH makes poor and makes rich; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brings low and lifts up.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raises the poor from the dust And lifts the beggar from the ash heap, to set them among princes and make them inherit the throne of Kabad. For the pillars of the Arath belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has set the world upon them.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will guard the feet of His Qadash ones, But the wicked shall be silent in darkness. For by strength no man shall prevail.

The adversaries of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH shall be broken in pieces; From Shamaym He will thunder against them. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will judge the ends of the Arath. “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give strength to His king, and exalt the horn of His anointed.”
Then Alkanah went to his house at Ramah. But the child ministered to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH before Ali the Kuhan.
Now the sons of Ali were corrupt; they did not know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And the Kuhanym’ custom with the people was that when any man offered a sacrifice, the Kuhan’s servant would come with a three-pronged fleshhook in his hand while the meat was boiling.

Then he would thrust it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; and the Kuhan would take for himself all that the fleshhook brought up. So they did in Shiluh to all the Yasharalym who came there.
Also, before they burned the fat, the Kuhan’s servant would come and say to the man who sacrificed, “Give meat for roasting to the Kuhan, for he will not take boiled meat from you, but raw.”

And if the man said to him, “They should really burn the fat first; then you may take as much as your heart desires,” he would then answer him, “No, but you must give it now; and if not, I will take it by force.”
Therefore the sin of the young men was very great before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for men abhorred the offering of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
But Shamu'AL ministered before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, even as a child, wearing a linen ephod.
Moreover his mother used to make him a little robe, and bring it to him year by year when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
And Ali would barak Alkanah and his wife, and say, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH give you descendants from this woman for the loan that was given to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” Then they would go to their own home.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH visited Hannah, so that she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile the child Shamu'AL grew before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Now Ali the Kuhan was very old; and he heard everything his sons did to all Yashar'AL, and how they lay with the women who assembled at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
So he said to them, “Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all the people.
No, my sons! For it is not a good report that I hear, you make the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to transgress.

If one man sins against another, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will judge him, but if a man sins against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who will intercede for him?” Nevertheless they did not heed the voice of their father, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH desired to kill them.
And the child Shamu'AL grew in stature, and in favor both with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and with men.
Then a servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to Ali and said to him, “Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘Did I not clearly reveal Myself to the house of your father when they were in Mitzraym in Pharuh’s house?

Did I not choose him out of all the tribes of Yashar'AL to be My Kuhan, to offer upon My altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod before Me? And did I not give to the house of your father all the offerings of the children of Yashar'AL made by fire?

Why do you kick at My sacrifice and My offering which I have commanded in My dwelling place, and honor your sons more than Me, to make yourselves fat with the best of all the offerings of Yashar'AL My people?’

Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar: ‘I said indeed that your house and the house of your father would walk before Me forever.’ But now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: ‘Far be it from Me; for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed.
Behold, the days are coming that I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father’s house, so that there will not be an old man in your house.
And you will see an enemy in My dwelling place, despite all the good which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH does for Yashar'AL. And there shall not be an old man in your house forever.
But any of your men whom I do not cut off from My altar shall consume your eyes and grieve your heart. And all the descendants of your house shall die in the flower of their age.
Now this shall be a sign to you that will come upon your two sons, on Huphni and Phinehas: in one day they shall die, both of them.
Then I will raise up for Myself a faithful Kuhan who shall do according to what is in My heart and in My mind. I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before My anointed forever.

And it shall come to pass that everyone who is left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread, and say, “Please, put me in one of the Kuhanym positions, that I may eat a piece of bread.
Meanwhile, the boy Shamu'AL served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by assisting Ali the Kuhan. Now in those days messages from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH were very rare, and visions were quite uncommon.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH called out again, Shamu'AL!” Again Shamu'AL got up and went to Ali. “Here I am. Did you call me?” I did not call you, my son,” Ali said. “Go back to bed.”
Shamu'AL did not yet know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH because he had never had a message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH before.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH called a third time, and once more Shamu'AL got up and went to Ali. “Here I am. Did you call me? Then Ali realized it was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who was calling the boy.
So Ali the Kuhan said to Shamu'AL, “Go and lie down again, and if someone calls again, say, ‘Speak to me 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, your servant is listening.’” So Shamu'AL went back to bed.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Shamu'AL, I am about to do a shocking thing in Yashar'AL.
I am going to carry out all my threats against Ali and his family, from beginning to end.

So I have vowed that the sins of Ali and his sons will never be forgiven by sacrifices or offerings.”
Shamu'AL stayed in bed until morning, then got up and opened the doors of the Tabernacle as usual, he was afraid to tell Ali what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said to him.
But Ali called out to him, Shamu'AL, my son.” Here I am,” Shamu'AL replied.

So Shamu'AL told Ali everything; he didn’t hold anything back. “It is the Will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,” Ali replied. “Let Him do what he thinks best.”
As Shamu'AL grew up, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with him, and everything Shamu'AL said proved to be reliable.
And all Yashar'AL, from Dan in the north to Baarshaba in the south, knew that Shamu'AL was confirmed as a Nabym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH continued to appear at Shiluh and gave messages to Shamu'AL there at the Tabernacle.
And Shamu'AL’s word came to all Yashar'AL. Now the Yasharalym went out to fight against the Philistines. The Yasharalym camped at Abanazar, and the Philistines at Aphak.
The Philistines deployed their forces to meet Yashar'AL, and as the battle spread, Yashar'AL was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand of them on the battlefield.

When the soldiers returned to camp, the elders of Yashar'AL asked, “Why did 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH bring defeat on us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s covenant from Shiluh, so that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH may go with us and save us from the hand of our enemies.”

So the people sent men to Shiluh, and they brought back the ark of the covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, who is enthroned between the charubim. And Ali’s two sons, Huphni and Phinahas, were there with the ark of the covenant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
When the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s covenant came into the camp, all Yashar'AL raised such a great shout that the ground shook.
Hearing the uproar, the Philistines asked, “What’s all this shouting in the Abarym (Hebrew) camp?” When they learned that the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had come into the camp,
the Philistines were afraid. “A Super power has come into the camp,” they said. “Oh no! Nothing like this has happened before.

Be strong, Philistines! Be men, or you will be subject to the Abarym (Hebrews), as they have been to you. Be men, and fight!”
So the Philistines fought, and the Yasharalym were defeated and every man fled to his tent. The slaughter was very great; Yashar'AL lost thirty thousand foot soldiers.
The ark of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was captured, and Ali’s two sons, Huphni and Phinahas, died.
That same day a Banyamyn ran from the battle line and went to Shiluh with his clothes torn and dust on his head.

When he arrived, there was Ali sitting on his chair by the side of the road, watching, because his heart feared for the ark of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. When the man entered the town and told what had happened, there was a loud cry in the whole town.
Ali heard the outcry and asked, “What is the meaning of this uproar?” The man hurried over to Ali,
who was ninety-eight years old and whose eyes had failed so that he could not see.
He told Ali, “I have just come from the battle line; I fled from it this very day.” Ali asked, “What happened, my son?”

The man who brought the news replied, Yashar'AL fled before the Philistines, and the army has suffered heavy losses. Also your two sons, Huphni and Phinahas, are dead, and the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has been captured.”

When he mentioned the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Ali fell backward off his chair by the side of the gate, his neck was broken and he died, for he was an old man, and he was heavy, he had led Yashar'AL forty years.

His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinahas, was pregnant and near the time of delivery. When she heard the news that the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she went into labor and gave birth, but was overcome by her labor pains.
As she was dying, the women attending her said, “Do not despair; you have given birth to a son.” But she did not respond or pay any attention.
She named the boy Ichabud, saying, “The Kabad has departed from Yashar'AL because of the capture of the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband.
She said, “The Kabad has departed from Yashar'AL, for the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has been captured.”
After the Philistines captured the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they took it from the battleground at Abanazar to the town of Ashdud.
They carried the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH into the temple of Dagun and placed it beside an idol of Dagun.
But when the citizens of Ashdud went to see it the next morning, Dagun had fallen with his face to the ground in front of the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! So they took Dagun and put him in his place again.

But the next morning the same thing happened, Dagun had fallen face down before the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH again. This time his head and hands had broken off and were lying in the doorway. Only the trunk of his body was left intact.
That is why to this day neither the priests of Dagun nor anyone who enters the temple of Dagun in Ashdud will step on its threshold.
Then the heavy hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck the people of Ashdud and the nearby villages with a plague of tumors.

So they called together the rulers of the Philistine towns and asked, “What should we do with the Ark of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL?” The rulers discussed it and replied, “Move it to the town of Gath.” So they moved the Ark of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL to Gath.

So they sent the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to the town of Akrun, but when the people of Akrun saw it coming they cried out, “They are bringing the Ark of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL here to kill us, too!”

The people summoned the Philistine rulers again and begged them, “Please send the Ark of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL back to its own country, or it will kill us all.” For the deadly plague from 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had already begun, and great fear was sweeping across the town.

The Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH remained in Philistine territory seven months in all.
Then the Philistines called in their priests and diviners and asked them, “What should we do about the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? Tell us how to return it to its own country.”

“Send the Ark of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL back with a gift,” they were told. “Send a guilt offering so the plague will stop. Then, if you are healed, you will know it was the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that caused the plague.”

“What sort of guilt offering should we send?” they asked. And they were told, “Since the plague has struck both you and your five rulers, make five gold tumors and five gold rats, just like those that have ravaged your land.

“Now build a new cart, and find two cows that have just given birth to calves. Make sure the cows have never been yoked to a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but shut their calves away from them in a pen.
Put the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH on the cart, and beside it place a chest containing the gold rats and gold tumors you are sending as a guilt offering. Then let the cows go wherever they want.

So these instructions were carried out, two cows were hitched to the cart, and their newborn calves were shut up in a pen.
Then the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the chest containing the gold rats and gold tumors were placed on the cart.

And sure enough, without veering off in other directions, the cows went straight along the road toward Bath-shamash, lowing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them as far as the border of Bath-shamash.
The people of Bath-shamash were harvesting wheat in the valley, and when they saw the Ark, they were overjoyed!

Several men of the tribe of Lauym lifted the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the chest containing the gold rats and gold tumors from the cart and placed them on the large rock. Many sacrifices and burnt offerings were offered to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that day by the people of Bath-shamash.
The five Philistine rulers watched all this and then returned to Akrun that same day.
The five gold tumors sent by the Philistines as a guilt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH were gifts from the rulers of Ashdud, Gaza, Ashkalun, Gath, and Akrun.

The five gold rats represented the five Philistine towns and their surrounding villages, which were controlled by the five rulers. The large rock at Bath-shamash, where they set the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, still stands in the field of Husha as a witness to what happened there.

“Who is able to stand in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, this Qadash 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH? they cried out. “Where can we send the Ark from here?”

Shamu'AL then took a large stone and placed it between the towns of Mizpah and Yashanah, Shamu'AL named it Abanazar (which means “the stone of help”), for he said, “Up to this point 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has helped us!”

Shamu'AL continued as Yashar'AL’s judge for the rest of his life.
Each year he traveled around, setting up his court first at Bathal, then at Gilgal, and then at Mizpah, he judged the people of Yashar'AL at each of these places.
Then he would return to his home at Ramah, and he would hear cases there, too, and Shamu'AL built an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at Ramah.
As Shamu'AL grew old, he appointed his sons to be judges over Yashar'AL.
Yual and Abiyah, his oldest sons, held court in Baarshaba.
But they were not like their father, for they were greedy for money. They accepted bribes and perverted justice.
Finally, all the elders of Yashar'AL met at Ramah to discuss the matter with Shamu'AL.
“Look,” they told him, “you are now old, and your sons are not like you. Give us a king to judge us like all the other nations have.”
Shamu'AL was displeased with their request and went to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for guidance.
“And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Shamu'AL, do everything they want, for they are rejecting me, not you. They do not want me to be their Ruler any longer.

So Shamu'AL passed on the warning of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to the people who were asking him for a king.

He will take away the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his own officials.

He will take your male and female slaves and demand the finest of your cattle and donkeys for his own use.

So Shamu'AL repeated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what the people had said,
and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “Do as they say, and give them a king.” Then Shamu'AL agreed and sent the people home.
There was a wealthy, influential man named Kish from the tribe of Banyamin. He was the son of Abial, son of Zarur, son of Bacurath, son of Aphiah, of the tribe of Banyamin.
His son Shaul was the most handsome man in Yashar'AL, head and shoulders taller than anyone else in the land.
One day Kish’s donkeys strayed away, and he told Shaul, “Take a servant with you, and go look for the donkeys.”

So Shaul took one of the servants and traveled through the hill country of Aphraim, the land of Shalishah, the Shaalim area, and the entire land of Banyamin, but they could not find the donkeys anywhere.
Finally, they entered the region of Zuph, and Shaul said to his servant, “Let us go home, by now my father will be more worried about us than about the donkeys!”

But the servant said, “I have just thought of something! There is a servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who lives here in this town, he is held in high honor by all the people because everything he says comes true. Let us go find him. Perhaps he can tell us which way to go.”
“Shaul replied; But we do not have anything to offer him, “Even our food is gone, and we do not have a thing to give him.”
“Well,” the servant said, “I have one small silver piece. We can at least offer it to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and see what happens!”
(In those days if people wanted a message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they would say, “Let’s go and ask the seer,” for Nabym used to be called seers.)
“All right,” Shaul agreed, “let’s try it!” So they started into the town where the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH lived.
As they were climbing the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to draw water. So Shaul and his servant asked, “Is the seer here today?”
“Yes,” they replied. “Stay right on this road he is at the town gates, he has just arrived to take part in a public sacrifice up at the place of worship.
Hurry and catch him before he goes up there to eat, the guests must wait for Shamu'AL to Barak the food before they will start eating.”
So they entered the town, and as they passed through the gates, Shamu'AL was coming out toward them to go up to the place of worship.
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar to Shamu'AL the previous day,

“About this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Banyamin. Anoint him to be the leader of my people, Yashar'AL, he will rescue them from the Philistines, for I have looked down on my people in mercy and have heard their cry.”
When Shamu'AL saw Shaul, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “That’s the man I told you about! He will rule my people.”
Just then Shaul approached Shamu'AL at the gateway and asked, “Can you please tell me where the seer’s house is?”
“I am the seer!” Shamu'AL replied. “Go up to the place of worship ahead of me. We will eat there together, and in the morning I’ll tell you what you want to know and send you on your way.
And do not worry about those donkeys that were lost three days ago, for they have been found. And I am here to tell you that you and your family are the focus of all Yashar'AL’s hopes.”

Shaul replied, “But I am only from the tribe of Banyamin, the smallest tribe in Yashar'AL, and my family is the least important of all the families of that tribe! Why are you talking like this to me?”
Then Shamu'AL brought Shaul and his servant into the hall and placed them at the head of the table, honoring them above the thirty special guests.
Shamu'AL then instructed the cook to bring Shaul the finest cut of meat, the piece that had been set aside for the guest of honor.
So the cook brought in the meat and placed it before Shaul. “Go ahead and eat it,” Shamu'AL said. “I was saving it for you even before I invited these others!” So Shaul ate with Shamu'AL that day.
When they came down from the place of worship and returned to town, Shamu'AL took Shaul up to the roof of the house and prepared a bed for him there.
At daybreak the next morning, Shamu'AL called to Shaul, “Get up! It’s time you were on your way.” So Shaul got ready, and he left the house with Shamu'AL.

When they reached the edge of town, Shamu'AL told Shaul to send his servant on ahead. After the servant was gone, Shamu'AL said, “Stay here, for I have received a special message for you from our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

Then Shamu'AL took a flask of olive oil and poured it over Shaul’s head, and he kissed Shaul and said, “I am doing this because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has appointed you to be the ruler over Yashar'AL, his special possession.

When you leave me today, you will see two men beside Rachal’s tomb at Zalzah, on the border of Banyamin. They will tell you that the donkeys have been found and that your father has stopped worrying about them and is now worried about you, and asking, ‘have you seen my son?’

“When you get to the oak of Tabur, you will see three men coming toward you who are on their way to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at Bathal. One will be bringing three young goats, another will have three loaves of bread, and the third will be carrying a wineskin full of wine.
They will greet you and offer you two of the loaves, which you are to accept.

“When you arrive at Hill of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, where the garrison of the Philistines is located, you will meet a band of Nabym coming down from the place of worship, they will be playing a harp, a tambourine, a flute, and a lyre, and they will be prophesying.
At that time the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will come powerfully upon you, and you will prophesy with them. You will be changed into a different person. .
After these signs take place, do what must be done, for the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL is with you.
Then go down to Gilgal ahead of me. I will join you there to sacrifice burnt offerings and Shalum offerings. You must wait for seven days until I arrive and give you further instructions.”
As Shaul turned and started to leave, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave him a new heart, and all Shamu'AL’s signs were fulfilled that day.
When Shaul and his servant arrived at Gibaah, they saw a group of Nabym coming toward them. Then the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came powerfully upon Shaul, and he, too, began to prophesy.
When those who knew Shaul heard about it, they exclaimed, “What? Is Shaul a Nabym? How did the son of Kish become a Nabym?”
And one of those standing there said, “Can anyone become a Nabym, no matter who his father is?” So that is the origin of the saying “Is Shaul a Nabym?”
When Shaul had finished prophesying, he went up to the place of worship.
“Where have you been?” Shaul’s uncle asked him and his servant. “We were looking for the donkeys,” Shaul replied, “but we could not find them. So we went to Shamu'AL to ask him where they were.”
“Oh? And what did he say?” his uncle asked.
“And Shaul replied; he told us that the donkeys had already been found,” But Shaul did not tell his uncle what Shamu'AL said about the kingdom.
Later Shamu'AL called all the people of Yashar'AL to meet before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at Mizpah.
And he said, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, has declared: I brought you from Mitzraym and rescued you from the Mitzraym and from all of the nations that were oppressing you.

But though I have rescued you from your misery and distress, you have rejected your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH today and have said, ‘No, we want a king instead!’ Now, therefore, present yourselves before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by tribes and clans.”
So Shamu'AL brought all the tribes of Yashar'AL before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the tribe of Banyamin was chosen by lot.

Then he brought each family of the tribe of Banyamin before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the family of the Matrites was chosen, and finally Shaul son of Kish was chosen from among them. But when they looked for him, he had disappeared!
So they asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Where is he?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied, “He is hiding among the baggage.”
So they found him and brought him out, and he stood head and shoulders above anyone else.
Then Shamu'AL said to all the people, “This is the man 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has chosen as your king. No one in all Yashar'AL is like him!” And all the people shouted, “Long live the king!”
Then Shamu'AL told the people what the rights and duties of a king were. He wrote them down on a scroll and placed it before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then Shamu'AL sent the people home again.
When Shaul returned to his home at Gibaah, a group of men whose hearts 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had touched went with him.

But there were some scoundrels who complained, “How can this man save us?” And they scorned him and refused to bring him gifts. But Shaul ignored them. [Nahash, king of the Ammunites, had been grievously oppressing the people of Gad and Rauban who lived east of the Yurdan River, he gouged out the right eye of each of the Yasharalym living there, and he didn’t allow anyone to come and rescue them. In fact, of all the Yasharalym east of the Yurdan, there was not a single one whose right eye Nahash had not gouged out. But there were 7,000 men who had escaped from the Ammunites, and they had settled in Yabash-gilaad.]

About a month later, King Nahash of Ammun led his army against the Yasharalym town of Yabash-gilaad. But all the citizens of Yabash asked for Shalum. “Make a treaty with us, and we will be your servants,” they pleaded.
“All right,” Nahash said, “but only on one condition. I will gouge out the right eye of every one of you as a shame to all Yashar'AL!”
“The elders of Yabash replied; Give us seven days to send messengers throughout Yashar'AL! “If no one comes to save us, we will agree to your terms.”
When the messengers came to where Shaul live in Gibaah and told the people about their plight, everyone broke into tears.
Shaul had been plowing a field with his oxen, and when he returned to town, he asked, “What’s the matter? Why is everyone crying?” So they told him about the message from Yabash-gilaad.
Then the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came powerfully upon Shaul, and he became very angry.

He took two oxen and cut them into pieces and sent the messengers to carry them throughout Yashar'AL with this message: “This is what will happen to the oxen of anyone who refuses to follow Shaul and Shamu'AL into battle!” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made the people afraid of Shaul’s anger, and all of them came out together as one.
When Shaul mobilized them at Bazak, he found that there were 300,000 men from Yashar'AL and 30,000 men from Yahudah.
So Shaul sent the messengers back to Yabash-gilaad to say, “We will rescue you by noontime tomorrow!” There was great joy throughout the town when that message arrived!
The men of Yabash then told their enemies, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you can do to us whatever you wish.”

But before dawn the next morning, Shaul arrived, having divided his army into three detachments. He launched a surprise attack against the Ammunites and slaughtered them the whole morning. The remnant of their army was so badly scattered that no two of them were left together.
Then the people exclaimed to Shamu'AL, “Now where are those men who said, ‘Why should Shaul rule over us?’ Bring them here, and we will kill them!”
But Shaul replied, “No one will be executed today, for today 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has rescued Yashar'AL!”
Then Shamu'AL said to the people, “Come, let us all go to Gilgal to renew the kingdom.”
So they all went to Gilgal, and in a solemn ceremony before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH they made Shaul king. Then they offered Shalum offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and Shaul and all the Yasharalym were filled with joy.
Then Shamu'AL addressed all Yashar'AL: “I have done as you asked and given you a king.
Your king is now your leader. I stand here before you an old, gray-haired man, and my sons serve you. I have served as your leader from the time I was a boy to this very day. .

Now testify against me in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and before his anointed one. Whose ox or donkey have I stolen? Have I ever cheated any of you? Have I ever oppressed you? Have I ever taken a bribe and perverted justice? Tell me and I will make right whatever I have done wrong.”
“No,” they replied, “you have never cheated or oppressed us, and you have never taken even a single bribe.”
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and his anointed one are my witnesses today,” Shamu'AL declared, that my hands are clean. Yes, He is a witness,” they replied.
“Shamu'AL continued; It was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who appointed Musha and Aarun, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought your ancestors out of the land of Mitzraym.
Now stand here quietly before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as I remind you of all the great things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done for you and your ancestors.
“When the Yasharalym were in Mitzraym and cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he sent Musha and Aarun to rescue them from Mitzraym and to bring them into this land.

But the people soon forgot about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH handed them over to Sisara, the commander of Hazur’s army, and also to the Philistines and to the king of Muab, who fought against them.

“Then they cried to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH again and confessed, ‘We have sinned by turning away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and worshiping the images of Baal and Ashturath. But we will worship you 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and you alone if you will rescue us from our enemies.’
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent Gidaun, Badan, Yaphthah, and Shamu'AL to save you, and you lived in safety.
“But when you were afraid of Nahash, the king of Ammun, you came to me and said that you wanted a king to reign over you, even though 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was already your Ruler.
All right, here is the king you have chosen. You asked for him, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has granted your request.

“Now if you fear and worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and listen to his voice, and if you do not rebel against the commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, then both you and your king will show that you recognize 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
But if you rebel against the commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and refuse to listen to Him, then His hand will be as heavy upon you as it was upon your ancestors.
“Now stand here and see the great thing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is about to do.

You know that it does not rain at this time of the year during the wheat harvest. I will ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to send thunder and rain today, then you will realize how wicked you have been in asking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for a king!”
So Shamu'AL called to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent thunder and rain that day. And all the people were terrified of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and of Shamu'AL.
Then they all said to Shamu'AL; Pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for us, or we will die! “For now we have added to our sins by asking for a king.”
“Shamu'AL reassured them, Do not be afraid, “You have certainly done wrong, but make sure now that you worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all your heart, and do not turn your back on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Do not go back to worshiping worthless idols that cannot help or rescue you, they are totally useless!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will not abandon His people, because that would dishonor His great Name. For it has pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to make you His very own people.
“As for me, I will certainly not sin against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by ending my prayers for you. And I will continue to teach you what is good and right.
But be sure to fear and serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Truth. Think of all the wonderful things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done for you.
But if you continue to sin, you and your king will be swept away.”
Shaul was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned for forty-two years.

Shaul selected three thousand special troops from the army of Yashar'AL and sent the rest of the men home. He took two thousand of the chosen men with him to Micmash and the hill country of Bathal, the other one thousand went with Shaul’s son Yunathan to Gibaah in the land of Banyamin.

Soon after this, Yunathan attacked and defeated the garrison of Philistines at Gaba. The news spread quickly among the Philistines. So Shaul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land, saying, Abarym (Hebrews), hear this! Rise up in revolt!”

All Yashar'AL heard the news that Shaul had destroyed the Philistine garrison at Gaba and that the Philistines now hated the Yasharalym more than ever. So the entire Yasharalym army was summoned to join Shaul at Gilgal.
The Philistines mustered a mighty army of three thousand chariots, six thousand charioteers, and as many warriors as the grains of sand on the seashore! They camped at Micmash east of Bath-aban.
The men of Yashar'AL saw what a tight spot they were in; and because they were hard pressed by the enemy, they tried to hide in caves, thickets, rocks, holes, and cisterns.
Some of them crossed the Yurdan River and escaped into the land of Gad and Gilaad.
Shaul waited there seven days for Shamu'AL, as Shamu'AL had instructed him earlier, but Shamu'AL still did not come. Shaul realized that his troops were rapidly slipping away.
So he demanded, “Bring me the burnt offering and the Shalum offerings!” And Shaul sacrificed the burnt offering himself.
Just as Shaul was finishing with the burnt offering, Shamu'AL arrived. Shaul went out to meet and welcome him,

but Shamu'AL said, “What is this you have done?” and Shaul replied, “I saw my men scattering from me, and you did not arrive when you said you would, and the Philistines are at Micmash ready for battle.
‘The Philistines are ready to march against us at Gilgal, and I have not even asked for help of𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!’ So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering myself before you came.”

” Shamu'AL exclaimed. You have done foolishly, you have not kept the command 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH gave you. If you Had kept it, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH would have established your kingdom over Yashar'AL forever.

But now your kingdom must end, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sought out a man after His own heart. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has already appointed him to be the leader of His people, because you have not kept the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”

Shamu'AL then left Gilgal and went on his way, but the rest of the troops went with Shaul to meet the army. They went up from Gilgal to Gibaah in the land of Banyamin. When Shaul counted the men who were still with him, he found only six hundred were left!
Shaul and Yunathan and the troops with them were staying at Gaba in the land of Banyamin. The Philistines set up their camp at Micmash.
Three raiding parties soon left the camp of the Philistines. One went north toward Uphrah in the land of Shual,
another went west to Bath-hurun, and the third moved toward the border above the valley of Zabuim near the wilderness.
There were no blacksmiths in the land of Yashar'AL in those days. The Philistines would not allow them for fear they would make swords and spears for the Abarym (Hebrews).
So whenever the Yasharalym needed to sharpen their plowshares, picks, axes, or sickles, they had to take them to a Philistine blacksmith.
The charges were as follows: a quarter of an ounce of silver for sharpening a plowshare or a pick, and an eighth of an ounce for sharpening an ax or making the point of an ox goad.
So on the day of the battle none of the people of Yashar'AL had a sword or spear, except for Shaul and Yunathan.
The pass at Micmash had meanwhile been secured by a contingent of the Philistine army.
One day Yunathan said to his armor bearer, “Come on, let’s go over to where the Philistines have their outpost.” But Yunathan did not tell his father what he was doing.
Meanwhile, Shaul and his six hundred men were camped on the outskirts of Gibaah, around the pomegranate tree at Migrun.

Among Shaul’s men was Ahijah the Kuhan, who was wearing the ephod, the Kuhan vest. Ahijah was the son of Ichabud’s brother Ahitub, son of Phinahas, son of Ali, the Kuhan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who had served at Shiluh. No one realized that Yunathan had left the Yasharalym camp.
To reach the Philistine outpost, Yunathan had to go down between two rocky cliffs that were called Buzaz and Sanah.
The cliff on the north was in front of Micmash, and the one on the south was in front of Gaba.

“Let us go across to the outpost of those pagans,” Yunathan said to his armor bearer. “Perhaps 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will help us, for nothing can hinder 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. He can win a battle whether He has many warriors or only a few!”
“Do what you think is best,” the armor bearer replied. “I’m with you completely, whatever you decide.”
“Yunathan said to him; All right then, “We will cross over and let them see us.
If they say to us, ‘Stay where you are or we will kill you,’ then we will stop and not go up to them.
But if they say, ‘Come on up and fight,’ then we will go up. That will be sign of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that He will help us defeat them.”
When the Philistines saw them coming, they shouted, “Look! The Abarym (Hebrews) are crawling out of their holes!”

Then the men from the outpost shouted to Yunathan, “Come on up here, and we’ll teach you a lesson!” Come on, ”Yunathan said to his armor bearer; climb right behind me, “for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will help us defeat them!”
So they climbed up using both hands and feet, and the Philistines fell before Yunathan, and his armor bearer killed those who came behind them.
They killed some twenty men in all, and their bodies were scattered over about half an acre.
Suddenly, panic broke out in the Philistine army, both in the camp and in the field, including even the outposts and raiding parties. And just then an earthquake struck, and everyone was terrified.
Shaul’s lookouts in Gibaah of Banyamin saw a strange sight, the vast army of Philistines began to melt away in every direction.
“Call the roll and find out who’s missing,” Shaul ordered. And when they checked, they found that Yunathan and his armor bearer were gone.
Then Shaul shouted to Ahijah, “Bring the aphod here!” For at that time Ahijah was wearing the aphod in front of the Yasharalym.
But while Shaul was talking to the Kuhan, the confusion in the Philistine camp grew louder and louder. So Shaul said to the Kuhan, “Never mind; let’s get going!”
Then Shaul and all his men rushed out to the battle and found the Philistines killing each other. There was terrible confusion everywhere.
Even the Abarym (Hebrews) who had previously gone over to the Philistine army revolted and joined in with Shaul, Yunathan, and the rest of the Yasharalym.
Likewise, the men of Yashar'AL who were hiding in the hill country of Aphraim joined the chase when they saw the Philistines running away.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH saved Yashar'AL that day, and the battle continued to rage even beyond Bath-aban.

Now the men of Yashar'AL were pressed to exhaustion that day, because Shaul had placed them under an oath, saying, “Let a curse fall on anyone who eats before evening, before I have full revenge on my enemies.” So no one ate anything all day,
even though they had all found honeycomb on the ground in the forest.
They did not dare touch the honey because they all feared the oath they had taken.
But Yunathan had not heard his father’s command, and he dipped the end of his stick into a piece of honeycomb and ate the honey. After he had eaten it, he felt refreshed.
But one of the men saw him and said, “Your father made the army take a strict oath that anyone who eats food today will be cursed. That is why everyone is weary and faint.”
“My father has made trouble for us all!” Yunathan exclaimed. “A command like that only hurts us. See how refreshed I am now that I have eaten this little bit of honey.
If the men had been allowed to eat freely from the food they found among our enemies, think how many more Philistines we could have killed!”
They chased and killed the Philistines all day from Micmash to Aiyalun, growing more and more faint.
That evening they rushed for the battle plunder and butchered the sheep, goats, cattle, and calves, but they ate them without draining the blood.
Someone reported to Shaul, “Look, the men are sinning against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by eating meat that still has blood in it.” That is very wrong,” Shaul said. “Find a large stone and roll it over here.

Then go out among the troops and tell them, ‘Bring the cattle, sheep, and goats here to me. Kill them here, and drain the blood before you eat them. Do not sin against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by eating meat with the blood still in it.’ So that night all the troops brought their animals and slaughtered them there.
Then Shaul built an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH it was the first of the altars he built to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then Shaul said, “Let’s chase the Philistines all night and plunder them until sunrise. Let’s destroy every last one of them.” and his men replied, “We’ll do whatever you think is best.” But the Kuhan said, “Let’s ask our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH first.”
So Shaul asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Should we go after the Philistines? Will you help us defeat them?” But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made no reply that day.
Then Shaul said to the leaders, Something is wrong! I want all my army commanders to come here. We must find out what sin was committed today.
I vow by the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who rescued Yashar'AL that the sinner will surely die, even if it is my own son Yunathan!” But no one would tell him what the trouble was.
Then Shaul said, “Yunathan and I will stand over here, and all of you stand over there.” And the people responded to Shaul, “Whatever you think is best.”

Then Shaul prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, please show us who is guilty and who is innocent.” Then they cast sacred lots, and Yunathan and Shaul were chosen as the guilty ones, and the people were declared innocent.
Then Shaul said, “Now cast lots again and choose between me and Yunathan.” And Yunathan was shown to be the guilty one.
“Tell me what you have done,” Shaul demanded of Yunathan. “I tasted a little honey,” Yunathan admitted. “It was only a little bit on the end of my stick. Does that deserve death?”
“Shaul replied to Yunathan; Yes, “you must die! May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH strike me and even kill me if you do not die for this.”

But the people broke in and said to Shaul, “Yunathan has won this great victory for Yashar'AL. Should he die? Far from it! As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, not one hair on his head will be touched, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH helped him do a great deed today.” So the people rescued Yunathan, and he was not put to death.
Then Shaul called back the army from chasing the Philistines, and the Philistines returned home.

Now when Shaul had secured his grasp on Yashar'AL’s throne, he fought against his enemies in every direction, against Muab, Ammun, Adum, the kings of Zubah, and the Philistines, and wherever he turned, he was victorious.
He performed great deeds and conquered the Amalakites, saving Yashar'AL from all those who had plundered them.
Shaul’s sons included Yunathan, Ishbushath, and Malkishua, king Shaul also had two daughters: Marab, who was older, and Michal.
Shaul’s wife was Ahinuam, the daughter of Ahimaaz. The commander of Shaul’s army was Abner, the son of Shaul’s uncle Nar.
Shaul’s father, Kish, and Abnar’s father, Ner, were both sons of Abial.
The Yasharalym fought constantly with the Philistines throughout Shaul’s lifetime. So whenever Shaul observed a young man who was brave and strong, he drafted him into his army.
One day the Shamu'AL said to King Shaul, “It was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who told me to anoint you as king of his people, Yashar'AL. Now listen to this message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has declared: I have decided to settle accounts with the nation of Amalak for opposing Yashar'AL when they came from Mitzraym.
Now go and completely destroy the entire Amalak nation, men, women, children, babies, cattle, sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys.”
So Shaul mobilized his army at Talaim. There were two hundred thousand soldiers from Yashar'AL and ten thousand men from Yahudah.
Then Shaul and his army went to a town of the Amalak and lay in wait in the valley.

Shaul sent this warning to the Kanites: “Move away from where the Amalak live, or you will die with them. For you showed kindness to all the people of Yashar'AL when they came up from Mitzraym.” So the Kanites packed up and left.
Then Shaul slaughtered the Amalak nation from Habilah all the way to Shur, east of Mitzraym.
Shaul captured Agag, the Amalak king, but completely destroyed everyone else.

Shaul and his men spared Agag’s life and kept the best of the sheep and goats, the cattle, the fat calves, and the lambs everything that appealed to them. They destroyed only what was worthless or of poor quality.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Shamu'AL,

“I greatly regret that I ever made Shaul king, for he has not been loyal to me and has refused to obey my command.” Shamu'AL was so deeply moved when he heard this that he cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH all night.
Early the next morning Shamu'AL went to find Shaul. Someone told him, “Shaul went to the town of Carmel to set up a monument to himself; then he went on to Gilgal.”
When Shamu'AL finally found him, king Shaul greeted Shamu'AL cheerfully. “May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH barak you, “I have carried out the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
“Then what is all the bleating of sheep and goats and the lowing of cattle I hear?” Shamu'AL demanded.

Then Yunathan said, “Tomorrow we celebrate the new moon festival. You will be missed when your place at the table is empty.
The day after tomorrow, toward evening, go to the place where you hid before, and wait there by the stone pile.
I will come out and shoot three arrows to the side of the stone pile as though I were shooting at a target.
Then I will send a boy to bring the arrows back. If you hear me tell him, ‘They are on this side,’ then you will know, as surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, that all is well, and there is no trouble.
But if I tell him, ‘Go farther, the arrows are still ahead of you,’ then it will mean that you must leave immediately, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is sending you away.
And may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH make us keep our promises to each other, for he has witnessed them.”
So Daud hid himself in the field, and when the new moon festival began, the king sat down to eat.
He sat at his usual place against the wall, with Yunathan sitting opposite him and Abner beside him. But Daud’s place was empty.
Shaul didn’t say anything about it that day, for he said to himself, “Something must have made Daud ceremonially unclean.”
But when Daud’s place was empty again the next day, Shaul asked Yunathan, “Why not the son of Yassa been here for the meal either yesterday or today?”
Yunathan replied, “Daud earnestly asked me if he could go to Bathlaham.
He said, ‘Please let me go, for we are having a family sacrifice. My brother demanded that I be there. So please let me get away to see my brothers.’ That’s why he is not here at the king’s table.”
Saul boiled with rage at Yunathan. “You stupid son of a whore!” he swore at him. “Do you think I do not know that you want him to be king in your place, shaming yourself and your mother?
As long as that son of Yassa is alive, you will never be king, now go and get him so I can kill him!”
“But why should he be put to death?” Yunathan asked his father. “What has he done?”
Then Shaul hurled his spear at Yunathan, intending to kill him. So at last Yunathan realized that his father was really determined to kill Daud.
Yunathan left the table in fierce anger and refused to eat on that second day of the festival, for he was crushed by his father’s shameful behavior toward Daud.
The next morning, as agreed, Yunathan went out into the field and took a young boy with him to gather his arrows.
“Start running,” he told the boy, “so you can find the arrows as I shoot them.” So the boy ran, and Yunathan shot an arrow beyond him.
When the boy had almost reached the arrow, Yunathan shouted, “The arrow is still ahead of you.
Hurry, hurry, do not wait.” So the boy quickly gathered up the arrows and ran back to his master.
He suspected nothing; only Yunathan and Daud understood the signal.
Then Yunathan gave his bow and arrows to the boy and told him to take them back to town.

As soon as the boy was gone, Daud came out from where he had been hiding near the stone pile. Then Daud bowed three times to Yunathan with his face to the ground. Both of them were in tears as they embraced each other and said good-bye, especially Daud.

At last Yunathan said to Daud, “Go in Shalum, for we have sworn loyalty to each other in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the witness of the bond between us and our children forever.” Then Daud left, and Yunathan returned to the town.
Daud went to the town of Nub to see Ahimalach the Kuhan. Ahimalach trembled when he saw him. “Why are you alone?” he asked. “Why is no one with you?”
“The king has sent me on a private matter,” Daud said. “He told me not to tell anyone why I am here. I have told my men where to meet me later.
Now, what is there to eat? Give me five loaves of bread or anything else you have.”
“We do not have any regular bread,” the Kuhan replied. “But there is the Qadash bread, which you can have if your young men have not slept with any women recently.”
“Do not worry,” Daud replied. “I never allow my men to be with women when we are on a campaign. And since they stay clean even on ordinary trips, how much more on this one!”

Since there was no other food available, the Kuhan gave him the Qadash bread, the Bread of the Presence that was placed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the Tabernacle. It had just been replaced that day with fresh bread.
Now Duag the Adumite, Saul’s chief herdsman, was there that day, having been detained before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Daud asked Ahimalach, “Do you have a spear or sword? The king’s business was so urgent that I did not even have time to grab a weapon!”

“I only have the sword of Guliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the valley of Alah,” the Kuhan replied. “It is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. Take that if you want it, for there is nothing else here.” There is nothing like it!” Daud replied. “Give it to me!”
So Daud escaped from Shaul and went to King Achish of Gath.

But the officers of Achish were unhappy about his being there. “Is not this Daud, the king of the land?” they asked. “Is not he the one the people honor with dances, singing, ‘Shaul has killed his thousands, and Daud has killed his ten thousands’?”
Daud heard these comments and was very afraid of what King Achish of Gath might do to him.
So he pretended to be insane, scratching on doors and drooling down his beard.
Finally, King Achish said to his men, “Must you bring me a madman?
We already have enough of them around here! Why should I let someone like this be my guest?”
So Daud left Gath and escaped to the cave of Adullam. Soon his brothers and all his other relatives joined him there.
Then others began coming, men who were in trouble or in debt or who were just discontented, until Daud was the captain of about four hundred men.
Later Daud went to Mizpah in Muab, where he asked the king, “Please allow my father and mother to live here with you until I know what 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is going to do for me.”
So Daud’s parents stayed in Muab with the king during the entire time Daud was living in his stronghold.
One day the Nabym Gad told Daud, “Leave the stronghold and return to the land of Yahudah.” So Daud went to the forest of Harath.
The news of his arrival in Yahudah soon reached Shaul. At the time, the king was sitting beneath the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibaah, holding his spear and surrounded by his officers.

“Listen here, you men of Banyamin!” Shaul shouted to his officers when he heard the news. “Has that son of Yassa promised every one of you fields and vineyards? Has he promised to make you all generals and captains in his army?

Is that why you have conspired against me? For not one of you told me when my own son made a solemn pact with the son of Yassa. You are not even sorry for me. Think of it! My own son, encouraging him to kill me, as he is trying to do this very day!”
Then Duag the Adumite, who was standing there with Shaul’s men, spoke up. “When I was at Nub,” he said, “I saw the son of Yassa talking to the Kuhan, Ahimalach son of Ahitub.
Ahimalach consulted 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for him. Then he gave him food and the sword of Guliath the Philistine.”
King Shaul immediately sent for Ahimalach and all his family, who served as Kuhanym at Nub.
When they arrived, Shaul shouted at him, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub! “What is it, my king?” Ahimalach asked.

“Why have you and the son of Yassa conspired against me?” Shaul demanded. “Why did you give him food and a sword? Why have you consulted 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for him? Why have you encouraged him to kill me, as he is trying to do this very day?”
“But sir,” Ahimalach replied, “is anyone among all your servants as faithful as Daud, your son-in-law? Why, he is the captain of your bodyguard and a highly honored member of your household!
This was certainly not the first time I had consulted 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for him! May the king not accuse me and my family in this matter, for I knew nothing at all of any plot against you.”
“You will surely die, Ahimalach, along with your entire family!” the king shouted.

And he ordered his bodyguards, “Kill these Kuhanym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for they are allies and conspirators with Daud! They knew he was running away from me, but they did not tell me!” But Shaul’s men refused to kill 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Kuhanym.
Then the king said to Duag, “You do it.” So Duag the Adumite turned on them and killed them that day, eighty-five Kuhanym in all, still wearing their Kuhanym garments.
Then he went to Nub, the town of the Kuhanym, and killed the Kuhanym’ families, men and women, children and babies, and all the cattle, donkeys, sheep, and goats.
Only Abiathar, one of the sons of Ahimalach, escaped and fled to Daud.
When he told Daud that Shaul had killed the Kuhanym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
Daud exclaimed, “I knew it! When I saw Duag the Adumite there that day, I knew he was sure to tell Shaul. Now I have caused the death of all your father’s family.
Stay here with me, and do not be afraid. I will protect you with my own life, for the same person wants to kill us both.”
One day news came to Daud that the Philistines were at Kailah stealing grain from the threshing floors.
Daud asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Should I go and attack them? Yes, go and save Keilah,” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told him.
But Daud’s men said, “We are afraid even here in Yahudah. We certainly do not want to go to Kailah to fight the whole Philistine army!”
So Daud asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH again, and again 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied, “Go down to Kailah, for I will help you conquer the Philistines.”
So Daud and his men went to Kailah. They slaughtered the Philistines and took all their livestock and rescued the people of Kailah.
Now when Abiathar son of Ahimalach fled to Daud at Kailah, he brought the ephod with him.
Shaul soon learned that Daud was at Kailah. “Good! “We have got him now! 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has handed him over to me, for he has trapped himself in a walled town!”
So Shaul mobilized his entire army to march to Kailah and besiege Daud and his men.
But Daud learned of Shaul’s plan and told Abiathar the Kuhan to bring the ephod and ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what he should do.
Then Daud prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, I have heard that Shaul is planning to come and destroy Kailah because I am here.
Will the leaders of Kailah betray me to him? And will Shaul actually come as I have heard? O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, please tell me. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Daud, “He will come.”
Again Daud asked, “Will the leaders of Kailah betray me and my men to Shaul?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied, “Yes, they will betray you.”
So Daud and his men, about six hundred of them left Keilah and began roaming the countryside. Word soon reached Shaul that Daud had escaped, so he did not go to Kailah after all.
Daud now stayed in the strongholds of the wilderness and in the hill country of Ziph. Shaul hunted him day after day, but 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH did not let Shaul find him.
One day near Hurash, Daud received the news that Shaul was on the way to Ziph to search for him and kill him.
Yunathan went to find Daud and encouraged him to stay strong in his Amunah in 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
“Do not be afraid,” Yunathan reassured Daud. “My father will never find you! You are going to be the king of Yashar'AL, and I will be next to you, as my father, Shaul, is well aware.”
So the two of them renewed their solemn pact before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then Yunathan returned home, while Daud stayed at Hurash.

But now the men of Ziph went to Shaul in Gibaah and betrayed Daud to him. “We know where Daud is hiding,” they said. “He is in the strongholds of Hurash on the hill of Hakilah, which is in the southern part of Yashimun.
Come down whenever you are ready, O king, and we will catch him and hand him over to you!”
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH barak you,” Shaul said. “At last someone is concerned about me!
Go and check again to be sure of where he is staying and who has seen him there, for I know that he is very crafty.
Discover his hiding places, and come back when you are sure, then I will go with you, and if he is in the area at all, I will track him down, even if I have to search every hiding place in Yahudah!”
So the men of Ziph returned home ahead of Shaul. Meanwhile, Daud and his men had moved into the wilderness of Maun in the Arabah Valley south of Yashimun.

When Daud heard that King Shaul and his men were searching for him, he went even farther into the wilderness to the great rock, and he remained there in the wilderness of Maun. But Shaul kept after him in the wilderness.
Shaul and Daud were now on opposite sides of a mountain. Just as Shaul and his men began to close in on Daud and his men,
an urgent message reached Shaul that the Philistines were raiding Yashar'AL again.
So Shaul quit chasing Daud and returned to fight the Philistines. Ever since that time, the place where Daud was camped has been called the Rock of Escape.
Daud then went to live in the strongholds of An-gady.
After Shaul returned from fighting the Philistines, he was told that Daud had gone into the wilderness of An-gady.
So Shaul chose three thousand elite troops from all Yashar'AL and went to search for Daud and his men near the rocks of the wild goats.
At the place where the road passes some sheepfolds, Shaul went into a cave to relieve himself. But as it happened, Daud and his men were hiding farther back in that very cave!

“Daud’s men whispered to him; this is your opportunity “Today 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is telling you, ‘I will certainly put your enemy into your power, to do with as you wish.’” So Daud crept forward and cut off a piece of the hem of Shaul’s robe.
But then Daud’s conscience began bothering him because he had cut Shaul’s robe.
He said to his men, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH forbid that I should do this to my master the king. I can not attack the anointed one of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH himself has chosen him.”
So Daud restrained his men and did not let them kill Shaul. After Shaul had left the cave and gone on his way,
Daud came out and shouted after him, “My master the king!” And when Shaul looked around, Daud bowed low before him.
Then Daud shouted to Shaul, “Why do you listen to the people who say I am trying to harm you?

This very day you can see with your own eyes it is not true. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH placed you at my mercy back there in the cave. Some of my men told me to kill you, but I spared you. For I said, ‘I will never harm the king, he is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anointed one.’

Look, my father, at what I have in my hand. It is a piece of the hem of your robe! I cut it off, but I did not kill you. This proves that I am not trying to harm you and that I have not sinned against you, even though you have been hunting for me to kill me.
“May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH judge between us. Perhaps 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will punish you for what you are trying to do to me, but I will never harm you.
As that old proverb says, ‘From evil people come evil deeds.’ So you can be sure I will never harm you.
Who is the king of Yashar'AL trying to catch anyway? Should he spend his time chasing one who is as worthless as a dead dog or a single flea?
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH therefore judge which of us is right and punish the guilty one, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is my advocate, and he will rescue me from your power!”
