When Daud had finished speaking, Shaul called back, “Is that really you, my son Daud?” Then Shaul began to cry.
And he said to Daud, “You are a better man than I am, for you have repaid me good for evil.
Yes, you have been amazingly kind to me today, for when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH put me in a place where you could have killed me, you did not do it.
Who else would let his enemy get away when he had him in his power? May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH reward you well for the kindness you have shown me today.
And now I realize that you are surely going to be king, and that the kingdom of Yashar'AL will flourish under your rule.
Now swear to me by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that when that happens you will not kill my family and destroy my line of descendants!”
So Daud promised this to Shaul with an oath. Then Shaul went home, but Daud and his men went back to their stronghold.
Now Shamu'AL died, and all Yashar'AL gathered for his funeral. They buried him at his house in Ramah. Then Daud moved down to the wilderness of Maun.
There was a wealthy man from Maun who owned property near the town of Carmel. He had three thousand sheep and one thousand goats, and it was sheep-shearing time.
This man’s name was Nabal, and his wife, Abigail, she was a sensible and beautiful woman. But Nabal, a descendant of Calab, was crude and mean in all his dealings.
When Daud heard that Nabal was shearing his sheep,
he sent ten of his young men to Carmel with this message for Nabal:
“Shalum and prosperity to you, your family, and everything you own!
I am told that it is sheep-shearing time. While your shepherds stayed among us near Carmel, we never harmed them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.

Ask your own men, and they will tell you this is true. So would you be kind to us, since we have come at a time of celebration? Please share any provisions you might have in hand with us and with your friend Daud.”
Daud’s young men gave this message to Nabal in Daud’s name, and they waited for a reply.
“Who is this fellow Daud?” Nabal sneered to the young men. “Who does this son of Yassa think he is? There are lots of servants these days who run away from their masters.
Should I take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers and give it to a band of outlaws who come from who knows where?”
So Daud’s young men returned and told him what Nabal had said.
“Daud said to his men; Get your swords!” as he strapped on his own sword, then four hundred men started off with Daud, and two hundred men remained behind to guard their equipment.
Meanwhile, one of Nabal’s servants went to Abigail and told her, “Daud sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he screamed insults at them.
These men have been very good to us, and we never suffered any harm from them. Nothing was stolen from us the whole time they were with us.
In fact, day and night they were like a wall of protection to us and the sheep.
You need to know this and figure out what to do, for there is going to be trouble for our master and his whole family, he is so ill-tempered that no one can even talk to him!”

Abigail wasted no time. She quickly gathered 200 loaves of bread, two wineskins full of wine, five sheep that had been slaughtered, nearly a bushel of roasted grain, one hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred fig cakes. She packed them on donkeys
and said to her servants, “Go on ahead. I will follow you shortly.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
As she was riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, she saw Daud and his men coming toward her.
Daud had just been saying, “A lot of good it did to help this fellow. We protected his flocks in the wilderness, and nothing he owned was lost or stolen. But he has repaid me evil for good.
May 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH strike me and kill me if even one man of his household is still alive tomorrow morning!”
When Abigail saw Daud, she quickly got off her donkey and bowed low before him.
She fell at his feet and said, “I accept all blame in this matter, my master. Please listen to what I have to say.
I know Nabal is a wicked and ill-tempered man; please do not pay any attention to him, he is a fool, just as his name suggests. But I never even saw the young men you sent.

“Now, my master, as surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives and you yourself live, since 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has kept you from murdering and taking vengeance into your own hands, let all your enemies and those who try to harm you be as cursed as Nabal is.
And here is a present that I, your servant, have brought to you and your young men.

Please forgive me if I have offended you in any way. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will surely reward you with a lasting dynasty, for you are fighting 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s battles. And you have not done wrong throughout your entire life.

“Even when you are chased by those who seek to kill you, your life is safe in the care of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, secure in his treasure pouch! But the lives of your enemies will disappear like stones shot from a sling!
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done all he promised and has made you leader of Yashar'AL,

do not let this be a blemish on your record. Then your conscience will not have to bear the staggering burden of needless bloodshed and vengeance. And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done these great things for you, please remember me, your servant!”
Daud replied to Abigail, “Yadah (Praise) 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, who has sent you to meet me today!
Tudah (Thank) 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for your good sense! Barak you for keeping me from murder and from carrying out vengeance with my own hands.
For I swear by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, who has kept me from hurting you, that if you had not hurried out to meet me, not one of Nabal’s men would still be alive tomorrow morning.”
Then Daud accepted her present and told her, “Return home in Shalum. I have heard what you said. We will not kill your husband.”

When Abigail arrived home, she found that Nabal was throwing a big party and was celebrating like a king, he was very drunk, so she did not tell him anything about her meeting with Daud until dawn the next day.
In the morning when Nabal was sober, his wife told him what had happened. As a result he had a stroke, and he lay paralyzed on his bed like a stone.
About ten days later, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck him, and he died.

When Daud heard that Nabal was dead, he said, “Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who has avenged the insult I received from Nabal and has kept me from doing it myself. Nabal has received the punishment for his sin.” Then Daud sent messengers to Abigail to ask her to become his wife.
When the messengers arrived at Carmel, they told Abigail, “Daud has sent us to take you back to marry him.”
She bowed low to the ground and responded, “I, your servant, would be happy to marry Daud. I would even be willing to become a slave, washing the feet of his servants!”
Quickly getting ready, she took along five of her servant girls as attendants, mounted her donkey, and went with Daud’s messengers. And so she became his wife.
Daud also married Ahinuam from Yazraal, making both of them his wives.
King Shaul, meanwhile, had given his daughter Michal, Daud’s wife, to a man from Gallim named Palti son of Laish.
Now some men from Ziph came to king Shaul at Gibaah to tell him, “Daud is hiding on the hill of Hakilah, which overlooks Yashimun.”
So Shaul took three thousand of Yashar'AL’s elite troops and went to hunt Daud down in the wilderness of Ziph.
Shaul camped along the road beside the hill of Hakilah, near Yashimun, where Daud was hiding. When Daud learned that Shaul had come after him into the wilderness,
he sent out spies to verify the report of Shaul’s arrival.
Daud slipped over to Shaul’s camp one night to look around. Shaul and Abnar son of Nar, the commander of his army, were sleeping inside a ring formed by the slumbering warriors.
“Who will volunteer to go in there with me?” Daud asked Ahimalach the Hittite and Abishai son of Zaruyahu, Yuab’s brother. I will go with you,” Abishai replied.
So Daud and Abishai went right into Shaul’s camp and found him asleep, with his spear stuck in the ground beside his head. Abnar and the soldiers were lying asleep around him.
Your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has surely handed your enemy over to you this time!” Abishai whispered to Daud. “Let me pin him to the ground with one thrust of the spear; I will not need to strike twice!”
“Daud said. No “Don’t kill him. For who can remain innocent after attacking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anointed one?
Surely 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will strike Shaul down someday, or he will die of old age or in battle.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH forbid that I should kill the one he has anointed, take his spear and that jug of water beside his head, and then let’s get out of here!”

So Daud took the spear and jug of water that were near Shaul’s head. Then he and Abishai got away without anyone seeing them or even waking up, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had put Shaul’s men into a deep sleep.
Daud climbed the hill opposite the camp until he was at a safe distance.
Then Daud shouted down to the soldiers and to Abnar son of Nar, “Wake up, Abnar! “Who is it?” Abnar demanded.
“Well, Abnar, you are a great man, are you not?” Daud taunted. “Where in all Yashar'AL is there anyone as mighty? So why have you not guarded your master the king when someone came to kill him?

This is not good at all! I swear by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that you and your men deserve to die, because you failed to protect your master, the anointed of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! Look around! Where are the king’s spear and the jug of water that were beside his head?”
Shaul recognized Daud’s voice and called out, “Is that you, my son Daud?” And Daud replied, “Yes, my master the king.
Why are you chasing me? What have I done? What is my crime?

But now let my master the king listen to his servant. If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has stirred you up against me, then let him accept my offering. But if this is simply a human scheme, then may those involved be cursed by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. For they have driven me from my home, so I can no longer live among 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s people, and they have said, ‘Go, worship pagan idols.’
Must I die on foreign soil, far from the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? Why has the king of Yashar'AL come out to search for a single flea? Why does he hunt me down like a partridge on the mountains?”
Then Shaul confessed, “I have sinned. Come back home, my son, and I will no longer try to harm you, for you valued my life today. I have been a fool and very, very wrong.”
“Here is your spear, O king,” Daud replied. “Let one of your young men come over and get it.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives his own reward for doing good and for being loyal, and I refused to kill you even when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH placed you in my power, for you are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anointed one.
Now may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH value my life, even as I have valued yours today. May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rescue me from all my troubles.”
And Shaul said to Daud, “Barakah on you, my son Daud. You will do many heroic deeds, and you will surely succeed.” Then Daud went away, and Shaul returned home.

But Daud kept thinking to himself, “Someday Shaul is going to get me. The best thing I can do is escape to the Philistines. Then Shaul will stop hunting for me in Yashar'AL territory, and I will finally be safe.”
So Daud took his six hundred men and went over and joined Achish son of Mauch, the king of Gath.
Daud and his men and their families settled there with Achish at Gath. Daud brought his two wives along with him, Ahinuam from Yazraal and Abigail, Nabal’s widow from Carmel.
Word soon reached Shaul that Daud had fled to Gath, so he stopped hunting for him.
One day Daud said to Achish, “If it is all right with you, we would rather live in one of the country towns instead of here in the royal city.”
So Achish gave him the town of Ziklag (which still belongs to the kings of Yahudah to this day),
and they lived there among the Philistines for a year and four months.
Daud and his men spent their time raiding the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalakites people who had lived near Shur, toward the land of Mitzraym, since ancient times.
Daud did not leave one person alive in the villages he attacked. He took the sheep, goats, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing before returning home to see King Achish.
“Where did you make your raid today?” Achish would ask. And Daud would reply, “Against the south of Yahudah, the Yarahmalites, and the Kanites.”
No one was left alive to come to Gath and tell where he had really been. This happened again and again while he was living among the Philistines.
Achish believed Daud and thought to himself, “By now the people of Yashar'AL must hate him bitterly. Now he will have to stay here and serve me forever!”
About that time the Philistines mustered their armies for another war with Yashar'AL. King Achish told Daud, “You and your men will be expected to join me in battle.”
“Very well!” Daud agreed. “Now you will see for yourself what we can do.” Then Achish told Daud, “I will make you my personal bodyguard for life.”

Meanwhile, Shamu'AL had died, and all Yashar'AL had mourned for him. He was buried in Ramah, his hometown. And Shaul had banned from the land of Yashar'AL all mediums and those who consult the spirits of the dead.
The Philistines set up their camp at Shunam, and Shaul gathered all the army of Yashar'AL and camped at Gilbua.
When Shaul saw the vast Philistine army, he became frantic with fear.
Shaul asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what he should do, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH refused to answer him, either by dreams or by sacred lots or by the Nabym.
Shaul then said to his advisers, “Find a woman who is a medium, so I can go and ask her what to do. His advisers replied, “There is a medium at Andur.”

So Shaul disguised himself by wearing ordinary clothing instead of his royal robes. Then he went to the woman’s home at night, accompanied by two of his men. “I have to talk to a man who has died, “Will you call up his spirit for me?”
“Are you trying to get me killed?” the woman demanded. “You know that Shaul has outlawed all the mediums and all who consult the spirits of the dead. Why are you setting a trap for me?”
But Shaul took an oath in the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and promised, “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, nothing bad will happen to you for doing this.”
Finally, the woman said, “Well, whose spirit do you want me to call up? Call up Shamu'AL, Shaul replied.
When the woman saw Shamu'AL, she screamed, “You have deceived me! You are Shaul!”
“Do not be afraid!” the king told her. “What do you see?” I see a deity coming up out of the earth,” she said.
“What does he look like?” Shaul asked. “He is an old man wrapped in a robe,” she replied. Shaul realized it was Shamu'AL, and he fell to the ground before him.

“Why have you disturbed me by calling me back?” Shamu'AL asked Shaul. Because I am in deep trouble,” Shaul replied. “The Philistines are at war with me, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has left me and will not reply by Nabym or dreams. So I have called for you to tell me what to do.”
But Shamu'AL replied, “Why ask me, since 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has left you and has become your enemy?
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done just as he said he would. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has torn the kingdom from you and given it to your rival, Daud.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done this to you today because you refused to carry out his fierce anger against the Amalakites.

What’s more, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will hand you and the army of Yashar'AL over to the Philistines tomorrow, and you and your sons will be here with me. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will bring down the entire army of Yashar'AL in defeat.”
Shaul fell full length on the ground, paralyzed with fright because of Shamu'AL’s words, he was also faint with hunger, for he had eaten nothing all day and all night.
When the woman saw how distraught he was, she said, “Sir, I obeyed your command at the risk of my life.
Now do what I say, and let me give you a little something to eat so you can regain your strength for the trip back.”
But Shaul refused to eat anything. Then his advisers joined the woman in urging him to eat, so he finally yielded and got up from the ground and sat on the couch.
The woman had been fattening a calf, so she hurried out and killed it. She took some flour, kneaded it into dough and baked unleavened bread.
She brought the meal to king Shaul and his advisers, and they ate it. Then they went out into the night.
The entire Philistine army now mobilized at Aphak, and the Yasharalym camped at the spring in Yazraal.
As the Philistine rulers were leading out their troops in groups of hundreds and thousands, Daud and his men marched at the rear with King Achish.

But the Philistine commanders demanded, “What are these Abarym (Hebrews) doing here?” And Achish told them, “This is Daud, the servant of King Shaul of Yashar'AL, he is been with me for years, and I have never found a single fault in him from the day he arrived until today.”

But the Philistine commanders were angry. “Send him back to the town you have given him!” they demanded, “he can not go into the battle with us. What if he turns against us in battle and becomes our adversary? Is there any better way for him to reconcile himself with his master than by handing our heads over to him?
Is this not the same Daud about whom the women of Yashar'AL sing in their dances, ‘Shaul has killed his thousands, and Daud has killed his ten thousands’?”

So Achish finally summoned Daud and said to him, “I swear by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that you have been a trustworthy ally. I think you should go with me into battle, for I have never found a single flaw in you from the day you arrived until today. But the other Philistine rulers won’t hear of it.
Please do not upset them, but go back quietly.”
“And Daud said; What have I done to deserve this treatment? “What have you ever found in your servant, that I can not go and fight the enemies of my master the king?”
But Achish insisted, “As far as I am concerned, you are as perfect as a Malak of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. But the Philistine commanders are afraid to have you with them in the battle.
Now get up early in the morning, and leave with your men as soon as it gets light.”
So Daud and his men headed back into the land of the Philistines, while the Philistine army went on to Yazraal.

Three days later, when Daud and his men arrived home at their town of Ziklag, they found that the Amalakites had made a raid into the Nagab and Ziklag; they had crushed Ziklag and burned it to the ground.
They had carried off the women and children and everyone else but without killing anyone.
When Daud and his men saw the ruins and realized what had happened to their families,
they wept until they could weep no more.
Daud’s two wives, Ahinuam from Yazraal and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel, were among those captured.
Daud was now in great danger because all his men were very bitter about losing their sons and daughters, and they began to talk of stoning him. But Daud found strength in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Then he said to Abiathar the Kuhan, “Bring me the ephod!” So Abiathar brought it.

Then Daud asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Should I chase after this band of raiders? Will I catch them?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Daud, “Yes, go after them. You will surely recover everything that was taken from you!”
So Daud and his six hundred men set out, and they came to the brook Basur.
But two hundred of the men were too exhausted to cross the brook, so Daud continued the pursuit with four hundred men.
Along the way they found a Mitzraym man in a field and brought him to Daud, they gave him some bread to eat and water to drink.
They also gave him part of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins, for he had nothing to eat or drink for three days and nights. Before long his strength returned.
“To whom do you belong, and where do you come from?” Daud asked him. “I am a Mitzraym the slave of an Amalakite,” he replied. “My master abandoned me three days ago because I was sick.
We were on our way back from raiding the Karathites in the Nagab, the territory of Yahudah, and the land of Calab, and we had just burned Ziklag.”

“And Daud asked him; Will you lead me to this band of raiders?” The young man replied, “If you take an oath in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that you will not kill me or give me back to my master, then I will guide you to them.”

So he led Daud to them, and they found the Amalakites spread out across the fields, eating and drinking and dancing with joy because of the vast amount of plunder they had taken from the Philistines and the land of Yahudah.

Daud and his men rushed in among them and slaughtered them throughout that night and the entire next day until evening. None of the Amalakites escaped except four hundred young men who fled on camels.
Daud got back everything the Amalakites had taken, and he rescued his two wives.
Nothing was missing: small or great, son or daughter, nor anything else that had been taken. Daud brought everything back.
Daud also recovered all the flocks and herds, and his men drove them ahead of the other livestock. “This plunder belongs to Daud!” they said.

Then Daud returned to the brook Basur and met up with the two hundred men who had been left behind because they were too exhausted to go with him. They went out to meet Daud and his men, and Daud greeted them joyfully.
But some evil troublemakers among Daud’s men said, “They did not go with us, so they can not have any of the plunder we recovered. Give them their wives and children, and tell them to be gone.”
But Daud said, “No, my brothers! Do not be selfish with what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given us, For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has kept us safe and helped us defeat the band of raiders that attacked us.
Who will listen when you talk like this? We share and share alike, those who go to battle and those who guard the equipment.”
From then on Daud made this a decree and regulation for Yashar'AL, and it is still followed today.
When Daud arrived at Ziklag, he sent part of the plunder to the elders of Yahudah, who were his friends. “Here is a present for you, taken from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s enemies,” he said.
The gifts were sent to the people of the following towns Daud had visited: Bathal, Ramuth-nagab, Yattir,
Aruer, Siphmuth, Ashtemua,
Racal, the towns of the Yarahmaalites, the towns of the Kanites,
Hurmah, Bur-ashan, Athach,
Habrun, and all the other places Daud and his men had visited.
Now the Philistines fought against Yashar'AL; and the men of Yashar'AL fled from before the Philistines, Many were slaughtered on the slopes of Mount Gilbua.
Then the Philistines followed hard after Shaul and his sons. And the Philistines killed Yunathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, Shaul’s sons.
The battle became fierce against Shaul. The archers hit him, and he was severely wounded by the archers.

Then Shaul said to his armorbearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and thrust me through and abuse me.” But his armorbearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. Therefore Shaul took a sword and fell on it.
And when his armorbearer saw that Shaul was dead, he also fell on his sword, and died with him.
So Shaul, his three sons, his armorbearer, and all his men died together that same day.

And when the men of Yashar'AL who were on the other side of the valley, and those who were on the other side of the Yurdan, saw that the men of Yashar'AL had fled and that Shaul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
So it happened the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Shaul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilbua.
And they cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and sent word throughout the land of the Philistines, to proclaim it in the temple of their idols and among the people.
Then they put his armor in the temple of the Ashturaths, and they fastened his body to the wall of Bath Shan.
Now when the inhabitants of Yabash Gilaad heard what the Philistines had done to Shaul,
all the valiant men arose and traveled all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Bath Shan; and they came to Yabash and burned them there.
Then they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Yabash, and fasted seven days.

books.name: II Samuel
chapters: After the death of Shaul, Daud returned from his victory over the Amalakites and spent two days in Ziklag.
On the third day a man arrived from Shaul’s army camp, he had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show that he was in mourning, he fell to the ground before Daud in deep respect.
“And Daud asked him; Where have you come from? "he replied; “I escaped from the Yasharalym camp,”
“Daud asked him. “Tell me how the battle went.” The man replied, “Our entire army fled from the battle. Many of the men are dead, and Shaul and his son Yunathan are also dead.”
“How do you know Shaul and Yunathan are dead?” Daud demanded of the young man.
The man answered, “I happened to be on Mount Gilbua, and there was Shaul leaning on his spear with the enemy chariots and charioteers closing in on him.
When he turned and saw me, he cried out for me to come to him. ‘How can I help?’ I asked him.
“He responded, ‘Who are you?’ I told him that ‘I am an Amalakite,’.
“Then he begged me, ‘Come over here and put me out of my misery, for I am in terrible pain and want to die.’
“So I killed him,” the Amalakite told Daud, “for I knew he could not live. Then I took his crown and his armband, and I have brought them here to you, my master.”
Daud and his men tore their clothes in sorrow when they heard the news.
They mourned and wept and fasted all day for Shaul and his son Yunathan, and for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s army and the nation of Yashar'AL, because they had died by the sword that day.
Then Daud said to the young man who had brought the news, “Where are you from?” And he replied, “I am a foreigner, an Amalakites, who lives in your land.”
“And Daud asked him; Why were you not afraid to kill 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anointed one?”.
Then Daud said to one of his men, “Kill him!” So the man thrust his sword into the Amalakite and killed him.
“You have condemned yourself,” Daud said, “for you yourself confessed that you killed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anointed one.”
Then Daud composed a funeral song for Shaul and Yunathan,
and he commanded that it be taught to the people of Yahudah. It is known as the Song of the Bow, and it is recorded in The Book of Yashar.
Your pride and joy, O Yashar'AL, lies dead on the hills! Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen!
Do not announce the news in Gath, do not proclaim it in the streets of Ashkalun, or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice and the pagans will laugh in triumph.

O mountains of Gilbua, let there be no dew or rain upon you, nor fruitful fields producing offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty heroes was defiled; the shield of Shaul will no longer be anointed with oil.
The bow of Yunathan was powerful, and the sword of Shaul did its mighty work.They shed the blood of their enemies and pierced the bodies of mighty heroes.
How beloved and kind were Shaul and Yunathan! They were together in life and in death. They were swifter than eagles, stronger than lions.
O women of Yashar'AL, weep for Shaul, for he dressed you in luxurious scarlet clothing, in garments decorated with gold.
Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen in battle! Yunathan lies dead on the hills.
How I weep for you, my brother Yunathan! Oh, how much I loved you! And your love for me was deep, deeper than the love of women!
Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen! Stripped of their weapons, they lie dead.

After this, Daud asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Should I move back to one of the towns of Yahudah? “Yes,”And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to him, Yes, "Then Daud asked, “Which town should I go to?” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said. Go to Habrun
So Daud left for Habrun with his two wives Ahinuam from Yazraal and Abigail the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
and his men and their families all moved to Yahudah, and they settled in the villages near Habrun.
Then the men of Yahudah came to Daud and anointed him king over the people of Yahudah. When Daud heard that the men of Yabash-gilaad had buried Shaul,
he sent them this message: “May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH barak you for being so loyal to your master Shaul and giving him a decent burial.
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH reward you in return with His unfailing love! And I, too, will reward you for what you have done.
Now that Shaul is dead, I ask you to be my strong and loyal subjects like the people of Yahudah, who have anointed me as their new king.”
But Abner son of Nar, the commander of Shaul’s army, had already gone to Mahanaim with Shaul’s son Ishbushath.
There he proclaimed Ishbushath king over Gilaad, Yazraal, Aphraim, Banyamin, the land of the Ashurites, and all the rest of Yashar'AL.
Ishbushath, Shaul’s son, was forty years old when he became king, and he ruled from Mahanaim for two years. Meanwhile, the people of Yahudah remained loyal to Daud.
Daud made Habrun his capital, and he ruled as king of Yahudah for seven and a half years.
One day Abnar led Ishbushath’s troops from Mahanaim to Gibaun.
About the same time, Yuab son of Zaruiah led Daud’s troops out and met them at the pool of Gibaun. The two groups sat down there, facing each other from opposite sides of the pool.
Then Abnar suggested to Yuab, “Let’s have a few of our warriors fight hand to hand here in front of us.” All right,” Yuab agreed.
So twelve men were chosen to fight from each side—twelve men of Banyamin representing Ishbushath son of Shaul, and twelve representing Daud.
Each one grabbed his opponent by the hair and thrust his sword into the other’s side so that all of them died. So this place at Gibaun has been known ever since as the Field of Swords.
A fierce battle followed that day, and Abner and the men of Yashar'AL were defeated by the forces of Daud.
Yuab, Abishai, and Asahal, the three sons of Zaruyahu were among Daud’s forces that day. Asahal could run like a gazelle,
and he began chasing Abnar, he pursued him relentlessly, not stopping for anything.
When Abnar looked back and saw him coming, he called out, “Is that you, Asahal?” he replied “Yes, it is,”
“Go fight someone else!” Abnar warned. “Take on one of the younger men, and strip him of his weapons.” But Asahal kept right on chasing Abnar.
Again Abnar shouted to him, “Get away from here! I don’t want to kill you. How could I ever face your brother Yuab again?”

But Asahal refused to turn back, so Abnar thrust the butt end of his spear through Asahal’s stomach, and the spear came out through his back. He stumbled to the ground and died there. And everyone who came by that spot stopped and stood still when they saw Asahal lying there.
When Yuab and Abishai found out what had happened, they set out after Abnar. The sun was just going down as they arrived at the hill of Ammah near Giah, along the road to the wilderness of Gibaun.
Abnar’s troops from the tribe of Banyamin regrouped there at the top of the hill to take a stand.
Abnar shouted down to Yuab, “Must we always be killing each other? Do you not realize that bitterness is the only result? When will you call off your men from chasing their Yasharalym brothers?”
Then Yuab said, “𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH only knows what would have happened if you had not spoken, for we would have chased you all night if necessary.”
So Yuab blew the ram’s horn, and his men stopped chasing the troops of Yashar'AL.
All that night Abnar and his men retreated through the Yurdan Valley. They crossed the Yurdan River, traveling all through the morning, and did not stop until they arrived at Mahanaim.
Meanwhile, Yuab and his men also returned home. When Yuab counted his casualties, he discovered that only nineteen men were missing in addition to Asahal.
But three hundred and sixty of Abner’s men had been killed, all from the tribe of Banyamin.
Yuab and his men took Asahal’s body to Bathlaham and buried him there in his father’s tomb. Then they traveled all night and reached Habrun at daybreak.
This was the beginning of a long war between those who were loyal to Shaul and those loyal to Daud. As time passed Daud became stronger and stronger, while Shaul’s dynasty became weaker and weaker.
These are the sons who were born to Daud in Habrun: The oldest was Amnun, whose mother was Ahinuam from Yazraal.
The second was Danial, whose mother was Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel.The third was Absalum, whose mother was Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Gashur.
The fourth was Aduniyah, whose mother was Haggith.The fifth was Shaphatiah, whose mother was Abital.
The sixth was Ithraam, whose mother was Aglah, Daud’s wife.
As the war between the house of Shaul and the house of Daud went on, Abnar became a powerful leader among those loyal to Shaul.
One day Ishbushath, Shaul’s son, accused Abnar of sleeping with one of his father’s concubines, a woman named Rizpah, daughter of Aiah.

Abnar was furious. “Am I a dog in Yahudah to be kicked around like this?” he shouted. “After all I have done for your father, Shaul, and his family and friends by not handing you over to Daud, is this my reward that you find fault with me about this woman?
May 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH strike me and even kill me if I don’t do everything I can to help Daud get what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has promised him!
I am going to take Shaul’s kingdom and give it to Daud. I will establish the throne of Daud over Yashar'AL as well as Yahudah, all the way from Dan in the north to Baarshaba in the south.”
Ishbushath did not dare say another word because he was afraid of what Abnar might do.
Then Abnar sent messengers to Daud, saying, “Doesn’t the entire land belong to you? Make a solemn pact with me, and I will help turn over all of Yashar'AL to you.”
“Daud replied, okay “but I will not negotiate with you unless you bring back my wife Michal, Shaul’s daughter, when you come.”
Daud then sent this message to Ishbushath, Shaul’s son: “Give me back my wife Michal, for I bought her with the lives of one hundred Philistines.”
So Ishbushath took Michal away from her husband, Palti son of Laish.
Palti followed along behind her as far as Bahurim, weeping as he went. Then Abnar told him, “Go back home!” So Palti returned.
Meanwhile, Abnar had consulted with the elders of Yashar'AL. “For some time now,” he told them, “you have wanted to make Daud your king.
Now is the time! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has said, ‘I have chosen Daud to save my people Yashar'AL from the hands of the Philistines and from all their other enemies.’”
Abnar also spoke with the men of Banyamin. Then he went to Habrun to tell Daud that all the people of Yashar'AL and Banyamin had agreed to support him.
When Abnar and twenty of his men came to Habrun, Daud entertained them with a great feast.

Then Abnar said to Daud, “Let me go and call an assembly of all Yashar'AL to support my master the king. They will make a covenant with you to make you their king, and you will rule over everything your heart desires.” So Daud sent Abnar safely on his way.
But just after Daud had sent Abner away in safety, Yuab and some of Daud’s troops returned from a raid, bringing much plunder with them.
When Yuab arrived, he was told that Abnar had just been there visiting the king and had been sent away in safety.
Yuab rushed to the king and demanded, “What have you done? What do you mean by letting Abnar get away?
You know perfectly well that he came to spy on you and find out everything you are doing!”
Yuab then left Daud and sent messengers to catch up with Abnar, asking him to return. They found him at the well of Sirah and brought him back, though Daud knew nothing about it.

When Abnar arrived back at Habrun, Yuab took him aside at the gateway as if to speak with him privately. But then he stabbed Abnar in the stomach and killed him in revenge for killing his brother Asahal.
When Daud heard about it, he declared, “I vow by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that I and my kingdom are forever innocent of this crime against Abnar son of Nar.
Yuab and his family are the guilty ones. May the family of Yuab be cursed in every generation with a man who has open sores or leprosy or who walks on crutches or dies by the sword or begs for food!”
So Yuab and his brother Abishai killed Abnar because Abnar had killed their brother Asahal at the battle of Gibaun.
Then Daud said to Yuab and all those who were with him, “Tear your clothes and put on burlap. Mourn for Abnar.” And King Daud himself walked behind the procession to the grave.
They buried Abnar in Hebrun, and the king and all the people wept at his graveside.
Then the king sang this funeral song for Abnar: “Should Abner have died as fools die?
Your hands were not bound; your feet were not chained. No, you were murdered the victim of a wicked plot.” All the people wept again for Abnar.

Daud had refused to eat anything on the day of the funeral, and now everyone begged him to eat. But Daud had made a vow, saying, “May 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH strike me and even kill me if I eat anything before sundown.”
This pleased the people very much. In fact, everything the king did pleased them!
So everyone in Yahudah and all Yashar'AL understood that Daud was not responsible for Abnar’s murder.
Then King Daud said to his officials, “Do you not realize that a great commander has fallen today in Yashar'AL?
And even though I am the anointed king, these two sons of Zaruyahu, Yuab and Abishai are too strong for me to control. So may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH repay these evil men for their evil deeds.”
When Ishbushath, Shaul’s son, heard about Abnar’s death at Habrun, he lost all courage, and all Yashar'AL became paralyzed with fear.

Now there were two brothers, Baanah and Racab, who were captains of Ishbushath’s raiding parties. They were sons of Rimmun, a member of the tribe of Banyamin who lived in Baaruth. The town of Baaruth is now part of Banyamin’s territory
because the original people of Baaruth fled to Gittaim, where they still live as foreigners.

(Shaul’s son Yunathan had a son named Maphibushath, who was crippled as a child. He was five years old when the report came from Yazraal that Shaul and Yunathan had been killed in battle. When the child’s nurse heard the news, she picked him up and fled. But as she hurried away, she dropped him, and he became crippled.)
One day Racab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmun from Baaruth, went to Ishbushath’s house around noon as he was taking his midday rest.
The doorkeeper, who had been sifting wheat, became drowsy and fell asleep. So Racab and Baanah slipped past her.

They went into the house and found Ishbushath sleeping on his bed. They struck and killed him and cut off his head. Then, taking his head with them, they fled across the Yurdan Valley through the night.

When they arrived at Habrun, they presented Ishbushath’s head to Daud. Look!” they exclaimed to the king. “Here is the head of Ishbushath, the son of your enemy Shaul who tried to kill you. Today 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given my master the king revenge on Shaul and his entire family!”
But Daud said to Racab and Baanah, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who saves me from all my enemies, is my witness.
Someone once told me, ‘Shaul is dead,’ thinking he was bringing me good news. But I seized him and killed him at Ziklag. That’s the reward I gave him for his news!
How much more should I reward evil men who have killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed? Should I not hold you responsible for his blood and rid the Arath of you?”

So Daud ordered his young men to kill them, and they did. They cut off their hands and feet and hung their bodies beside the pool in Habrun. Then they took Ishbushath’s head and buried it in Abnar’s tomb in Habrun.
Then all the tribes of Yashar'AL went to Daud at Habrun and told him, “We are your own flesh and blood.

In the past, when Shaul was our king, you were the one who really led the forces of Yashar'AL. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told you, ‘You will be the shepherd of my people Yashar'AL. You will be Yashar'AL’s leader.’”
So there at Habrun, King Daud made a covenant before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all the elders of Yashar'AL. And they anointed him king of Yashar'AL.
Daud was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in all.
He had reigned over Yahudah from Habrun for seven years and six months, and from Yahushalam he reigned over all Yashar'AL and Yahudah for thirty-three years.

Daud then led his men to Yahushalam to fight against the Yabusites, the original inhabitants of the land who were living there. The Yabusites taunted Daud, saying, “You’ll never get in here! Even the blind and lame could keep you out!” For the Yabusites thought they were safe.
But Daud captured the fortress of Ziun, which is now called the City of Daud.

On the day of the attack, Daud said to his troops, “I hate those ‘lame’ and ‘blind’ Yabusites. Whoever attacks them should strike by going into the city through the water tunnel.” That is the origin of the saying, “The blind and the lame may not enter the house.”
So Daud made the fortress his home, and he called it the City of Daud. He extended the city, starting at the supporting terraces and working inward.
And Daud became more and more powerful, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut was with him.
Then King Hiram of Tyre sent messengers to Daud, along with cedar timber and carpenters and stonemasons, and they built Daud a palace.
And Daud realized that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had confirmed him as king over Yashar'AL and had Baraked his kingdom for the sake of his people Yashar'AL.
After moving from Habrun to Yahushalam, Daud married more concubines and wives, and they had more sons and daughters.
These are the names of Daud’s sons who were born in Yahushalam: Shammua, Shubab, Nathan, Shaluma,
Ibhar, Alishua, Naphag, Yaphia,
Alishama, Aliada, and Aliphalat.
When the Philistines heard that Daud had been anointed king of Yashar'AL, they mobilized all their forces to capture him. But Daud was told they were coming, so he went into the stronghold.
The Philistines arrived and spread out across the valley of Raphaim.
So Daud asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Should I go out to fight the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH replied to Daud, “Yes, go ahead. I will certainly hand them over to you.”

So Daud went to Baal-parazim and defeated the Philistines there. And Daud said “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did it! “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH burst through my enemies like a raging flood!” So Daud named that place Parazim (which means “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who bursts through”).
The Philistines had abandoned their idols there, so Daud and his men confiscated them.
But after a while the Philistines returned and again spread out across the valley of Raphaim.
And again Daud asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what to do. “and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Daud; do not attack them straight on, “Instead, circle around behind and attack them near the poplar trees.
When you hear a sound like marching feet in the tops of the poplar trees, be on the alert! That will be the signal that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is moving ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army.”
So Daud did what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Gibaun to Gazar.
Then Daud again gathered all the elite troops in Yashar'AL, thirty thousand in all.
Daud led them to Baalah of Yahudah to bring back the Ark of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, which bears the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, who is enthroned between the charubim.
They placed the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH on a new cart and brought it from Abinadab’s house, which was on a hill. Uzzah and Ahiu, Abinadab’s sons, were guiding the cart
that carried the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Ahiu walked in front of the Ark.
Daud and all the people of Yashar'AL were celebrating before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, singing songs and playing all kinds of musical instruments lyres, harps, tambourines, castanets, and cymbals.
But when they arrived at the threshing floor of Nacun, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out his hand and steadied the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH aroused against Uzzah, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck him dead because of this. So Uzzah died right there beside the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Daud was angry because the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had burst out against Uzzah, and Daud named that place Paraz-uzzah (which means “to burst out against Uzzah”), as it is still called today.
Daud was now afraid of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and he asked, “How can I ever bring the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH back into my care?”
So Daud decided not to move the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH into the City of Daud. Instead, he took it to the house of Ubad-Adum of Gath.
The Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH remained there in Ubad-adum’s house for three months, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Baraked Ubad-Adum and his entire household.

Then King Daud was told, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has Baraked Ubad-adum’s household and everything he has because of the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” So Daud went there and brought the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH from the house of Ubad-Adum to the City of Daud with a great celebration.
After the men who were carrying the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had gone six steps, Daud sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.
And Daud danced before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all his might, wearing a Kuhan garment.
So Daud and all the people of Yashar'AL brought up the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with shouts of joy and the blowing of rams’ horns.

But as the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH entered the City of Daud, Michal, the daughter of Shaul, looked down from her window. When she saw King Daud leaping and dancing before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, she was filled with contempt for him.
They brought the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and set it in its place inside the special tent Daud had prepared for it. And Daud sacrificed burnt offerings and Shalum offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
When he had finished his sacrifices, Daud Baraked the people in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
Then he gave to every Yasharalym man and woman in the crowd a loaf of bread, a cake of dates, and a cake of raisins. Then all the people returned to their homes.

When Daud returned home to barak his own family, Michal, the daughter of Shaul, came out to meet him. She said in disgust, “How distinguished the king of Yashar'AL looked today, shamelessly exposing himself to the servant girls like any vulgar person might do!”

Daud retorted to Michal, “I was dancing before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who chose me above your father and all his family! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appointed me as the leader of Yashar'AL, the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, so I celebrate before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Yes, and I am willing to look even more foolish than this, even to be humiliated in my own eyes! But those servant girls you mentioned will indeed think I am distinguished!”
So Michal, the daughter of Shaul, remained childless throughout her entire life.
When King Daud was settled in his palace and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given him rest from all the surrounding enemies,
the king Daud summoned Nathan the Nabym. “and said him, “I am living in a beautiful cedar palace, but the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is out there in a tent!”
Nathan replied to the king, “Go ahead and do whatever you have in mind, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with you.”
But that same night 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Nathan the Nabym,
“Go and tell my servant Daud, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has declared: Are you the one to build a house for me to live in?
I have never lived in a house, from the day I brought the Yasharalym out of Mitzraym until this very day. I have always moved from one place to another with a tent and a Tabernacle as my dwelling.

Yet no matter where I have gone with the Yasharalym, I have never once complained to Yashar'AL’s tribal leaders, the shepherds of my people Yashar'AL. I have never asked them, “Why have you not built me a beautiful cedar house?”’
“Now go and say to my servant Daud, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has declared: I took you from tending sheep in the pasture and selected you to be the leader of my people Yashar'AL.
I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have destroyed all your enemies before your eyes. Now I will make your name as famous as anyone who has ever lived on the Arath!
And I will provide a homeland for my people Yashar'AL, planting them in a secure place where they will never be disturbed. Evil nations will not oppress them as they have done in the past,

starting from the time I appointed judges to rule my people Yashar'AL. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. ‘Furthermore, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH declares that he will make a house for you, a dynasty of kings!
For when you die and are buried with your ancestors, I will raise up one of your descendants, your own offspring, and I will make his kingdom strong.
He is the one who will build a house, a temple for my Name. And I will secure his royal throne forever.
I will be his father, and he will be my son. If he sins, I will correct and discipline him with the rod, like any father would do.
But my favor will not be taken from him as I took it from Shaul, whom I removed from your sight.
Your house and your kingdom will continue before me for all time, and your throne will be secure forever.’”
So Nathan went back to Daud and told him everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar in this vision.
Then King Daud went in and sat before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and prayed, “Who am I, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far?
And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, in addition to everything else, you speak of giving your servant a lasting dynasty! Do you deal with everyone this way, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut?
“What more can I say to you? You know all about me Daud your servant,.
Because of your promise and according to your will, you have done all these great things and have made them known to your servant.
“How great you are, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut! There is no one like you. We have never even heard of another 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH like you!

What other nation on the Arath is like your people Yashar'AL? What other nation, have You redeemed from slavery to be your own people? You made a great Name for yourself when you redeemed your people from Mitzraym. You performed awesome miracles and drove out the nations and deities that stood in their way.
You made Yashar'AL your very own people forever, and you, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH became their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, I am your servant; do as you have promised concerning me and my family. Confirm it as a promise that will last forever.
And may your Name be honored forever so that everyone will say, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut is 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH over Yashar'AL!’ And may the house of your servant Daud continue before you forever.

“O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, I have been bold enough to pray this prayer to you because you have revealed all this to your servant, saying, ‘I will build a house for you a dynasty of kings!’
For you are 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, Your words are truth, and you have promised these good things to your servant.

And now, may it please you to barak the house of your servant, so that it may continue forever before you. For you have spoken, and when you grant a Barakah to your servant, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, it is an eternal Barakah!”
After this, Daud defeated and subdued the Philistines by conquering Gath, their largest town.

Daud also conquered the land of Muab, he made the people lie down on the ground in a row, and he measured them off in groups with a length of rope, he measured off two groups to be executed for every one group to be spared. The Muabites who were spared became Daud’s subjects and paid him tribute money.
Daud also destroyed the forces of Hadadazar son of Rahub, king of Zubah, when Hadadazar marched out to strengthen his control along the Auphrates River.
Daud captured one thousand chariots, seven thousand charioteers, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. Daud crippled all the chariot horses except enough for one hundred chariots.
When Aramaans from Damascus arrived to help King Hadadazar, Daud killed twenty two thousand of them.
Then he placed several army garrisons in Damascus, the Aramaan capital, and the Aramaans became Daud’s subjects and paid him tribute money. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made Daud victorious wherever he went.
Daud brought the gold shields of Hadadazar’s officers to Yahushalam,
along with a large amount of bronze from Hadadazar’s towns of Tabah and Baruthai.
When King Tuy of Hamath heard that Daud had destroyed the entire army of Hadadazar,

he sent his son Yuram to congratulate King Daud for his successful campaign. Hadadazar and Tuy had been enemies and were often at war. Yuram presented Daud with many gifts of silver, gold, and bronze.
King Daud dedicated all these gifts to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as he did with the silver and gold from the other nations he had defeated.
from Adum, Muab, Ammun, Philistia, and Amalak and from Hadadazar son of Rahub, king of Zubah.
So Daud became even more famous when he returned from destroying eighteen thousand Adumites in the Valley of Salt.
Daud placed army garrisons throughout Adum, and all the Adumites became Daud’s subjects. In fact, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made Daud victorious wherever he went.
So Daud reigned over all Yashar'AL and did what was just and right for all his people.
Yuab son of Zaruyahu was commander of the army. Yahushaphat son of Ahilud was the royal historian.
Zaduk son of Ahitub and Ahimalach son of Abiathar were the Kuhan. Sarayahu was the court secretary.
Banayahu son of Yahuada was captain of the king’s bodyguard. And Daud’s sons served as chief ministers.
One day king Daud asked, “Is anyone in Shaul’s family still alive anyone to whom I can show kindness for Yunathan’s sake?”
Daud summoned a man named Ziba, who had been one of Shaul’s servants, and the king asked him “Are you Ziba? “Yes sir, I am,” Ziba replied.

The king then asked him, “Is anyone still alive from Shaul’s family? If so, I want to show 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH’s kindness to them.” Ziba replied, “Yes, one of Yunathan’s sons is still alive. He is crippled in both feet.”
“Where is he?” the king asked. “In Lu-dabar Ziba told King Daud, “at the home of Makir son of Ammial.”
So Daud sent for him and brought him from Makir’s home.

His name was Maphibushath; he was Yunathan’s son and Shaul’s grandson. When he came to Daud, he bowed low to the ground in deep respect. Daud said, Greetings, Maphibushath." And Maphibushath replied, “I am your servant.”

“King Daud said to him; Do not be afraid! “I intend to show kindness to you because of my promise to your father, Yunathan. I will give you all the property that once belonged to your grandfather Shaul, and you will eat here with me at the king’s table!”
Maphibushath bowed respectfully and exclaimed, “Who is your servant, that you should show such kindness to a dead dog like me?”
Then the king summoned Shaul’s servant Ziba and said, “I have given your master’s grandson everything that belonged to Shaul and his family.

You and your sons and servants are to farm the land for him to produce food for your master’s household. But Maphibushath, your master’s grandson, will eat here at my table.” (Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.)

Ziba replied, “Yes, my master the king; I am your servant, and I will do all that you have commanded.” And from that time on, Maphibushath ate regularly at Daud’s table, like one of the king’s own sons.
Maphibushath had a young son named Mica. From then on, all the members of Ziba’s household were Maphibushath’s servants.
And Maphibushath who was crippled in both feet, lived in Yahushalam and ate regularly at the king’s table.
Some time after this, King Nahash of the Ammunites died, and his son Hanun became king.

Daud said, “I am going to show loyalty to Hanun just as his father, Nahash, was always loyal to me.” So Daud sent ambassadors to express sympathy to Hanun about his father’s death. But when Daud’s ambassadors arrived in the land of Ammun,

the Ammunites commanders said to Hanun, their master, “Do you really think these men are coming here to honor your father? No! Daud has sent them to spy out the city so they can come in and conquer it!”
So Hanun seized Daud’s ambassadors and shaved off half of each man’s beard, cut off their robes at the buttocks, and sent them back to Daud in shame.
When king Daud heard what had happened, he sent messengers to tell the men, “Stay at Yarichu until your beards grow out, and then come back.” For they felt deep shame because of their appearance.

When the people of Ammun realized how seriously they had angered Daud, they sent and hired twenty thousand Aramaan foot soldiers from the lands of Bath-rahub and Zubah, one thousand from the king of Maacah, and twelve thousand from the land of Tub.
When Daud heard about this, he sent Yuab and all his warriors to fight them.

The Ammunite troops came out and drew up their battle lines at the entrance of the city gate, while the Aramaans from Zubah and Rahub and the men from Tub and Maacah positioned themselves to fight in the open fields.
When Yuab saw that he would have to fight on both the front and the rear, he chose some of Yashar'AL elite troops and placed them under his personal command to fight the Aramaans in the fields.
He left the rest of the army under the command of his brother Abishai, who was to attack the Ammunites.
“If the Aramaans are too strong for me, then come over and help me,” Yuab told his brother. “And if the Ammunites are too strong for you, I will come and help you.
Be courageous! Let us fight bravely for our people and the cities of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s will be done.”
When Yuab and his troops attacked, the Aramaans began to run away.
And when the Ammunites saw the Aramaans running, they ran from Abishai and retreated into the city. After the battle was over, Yuab returned to Yahushalam.
The Aramaans now realized that they were no match for Yashar'AL. So when they regrouped,

they were joined by additional Aramaan troops summoned by Hadadazar from the other side of the Euphrates River. These troops arrived at Halam under the command of Shubach, the commander of Hadadazar’s forces.
When Daud heard what was happening, he mobilized all Yashar'AL, crossed the Yurdan River, and led the army to Halam. The Aramaans positioned themselves in battle formation and fought against Daud.
But again the Aramaans fled from the Yasharalym. This time Daud’s forces killed seven hundred charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers, including Shubach, the commander of their army.

When all the kings allied with Hadadazar saw that they had been defeated by Yashar'AL, they surrendered to Yashar'AL and became their subjects. After that, the Aramaans were afraid to help the Ammunites.

In the spring of the year, when kings normally go out to war, Daud sent Yuab and the Yasharalym army to fight the Ammunites. They destroyed the Ammunite army and laid siege to the city of Rabbah. However, Daud stayed behind in Yahushalam.
Late one afternoon, after his midday rest, Daud got out of bed and was walking on the roof of the palace. As he looked out over the city, he noticed a woman of unusual beauty taking a bath.
Daud sent someone to find out who she was, and he was told, “She is Bathshaba, the daughter of Aliam and the wife of Uryahu the Hittite.”
Then Daud sent messengers to get her; and when she came to the palace, Daud slept with her. She had just completed the purification rites after having her menstrual period. Then she returned home.
Later, when Bathshaba discovered that she was pregnant, she sent king Daud a message, saying, “I’m pregnant.”
Then Daud sent word to Yuab: “Send me Uryahu the Hittite.” So Yuab sent him to Daud.
When Uryahu arrived, Daud asked him how Yuab and the army were getting along and how the war was progressing.
Then King Daud told Uryahu, “Go on home and relax.” the king even sent a gift to Uryahu after he had left the palace.
But Uryahu did not go home, he slept at the palace entrance with the king’s palace guard.
When Daud heard that Uryahu had not gone home, he summoned him and asked, “What’s the matter? Why did you not go home last night after being away for so long?”

Uryahu replied, “The Ark and the armies of Yashar'AL and Yahudah are living in tents, and Yuab and my master’s men are camping in the open fields. How could I go home to wine and dine and sleep with my wife? I swear that I would never do such a thing.”
“Well, stay here today,” Daud told him, “and tomorrow you may return to the army.” So Uryahu stayed in Yahushalam that day and the next.
Then Daud invited him to dinner and got him drunk. But even then he could not get Uryahu to go home to his wife. Again Uryahu slept at the palace entrance with the king’s palace guard.
So the next morning Daud wrote a letter to Yuab and gave it to Uryahu to deliver.
The letter instructed Yuab, “Station Uryahu on the front lines where the battle is fiercest. Then pull back so that he will be killed.”
So Yuab assigned Uryahu to a spot close to the city wall where he knew the enemy’s strongest men were fighting.
And when the enemy soldiers came out of the city to fight, Uryahu the Hittite was killed along with several other Yasharalym soldiers.
Then Yuab sent a battle report to Daud.
He told his messenger, “Report all the news of the battle to the king.
But he might get angry and ask, ‘Why did the troops go so close to the city? Did they not know there would be shooting from the walls?

Was it not a woman who killed Abimalach son of Gidaun at Thabaz, by casting a millstone down on him from the wall? Why would you get so close to the wall?’ Then tell him, ‘Uryahu the Hittite was killed, too.’”
So the messenger went to Yahushalam and gave a complete report to Daud.
“The enemy came out against us in the open fields,” he said. “And as we chased them back to the city gate,
the archers on the wall shot arrows at us. Some of the king’s men were killed, including Uryahu the Hittite.”
“Well, tell Yuab not to be discouraged,” Daud said. “The sword devours this one today and that one tomorrow! Fight harder next time, and conquer the city!”
When Uryahu’s wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.

When the period of mourning was over, Daud sent for her and brought her to the palace, and she became one of his wives. Then she gave birth to a son. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was displeased with what Daud had done.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent Nathan the Nabym to tell Daud this story: “There were two men in a certain town. One was rich, and one was poor.
The rich man owned a great many sheep and cattle.

The poor man owned nothing but one little lamb he had bought, he raised that little lamb, and it grew up with his children. It ate from the man’s own plate and drank from his cup, he cuddled it in his arms like a baby daughter.
One day a guest arrived at the home of the rich man. But instead of killing an animal from his own flock or herd, he took the poor man’s lamb and killed it and prepared it for his guest.”
Daud was furious. “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives,” Daud vowed, “any man who would do such a thing deserves to die!
He must repay four lambs to the poor man for the one he stole and for having no pity.”
Then Nathan said to Daud, “You are that man! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, says: I anointed you king of Yashar'AL and saved you from the power of Shaul.
I gave you your master’s house and his wives and the kingdoms of Yashar'AL and Yahudah. And if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
Why, then, have you despised the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and done this horrible deed? For you have murdered Uryahu the Hittite with the sword of the Ammunites and stolen his wife.
From this time on, your family will live by the sword because you have despised me by taking Uryahu’s wife to be your own.

“This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Because of what you have done, I will raise up adversity from your own household to rebel against you. I will give your wives to another man before your very eyes, and he will go to bed with them in public view.
What you did secretly, "I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make this happen to you openly in the sight of all Yashar'AL, under the sun.”
Then Daud confessed to Nathan, “I have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” Nathan replied, “Yes, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has forgiven you, and you will not die for this sin.
Nevertheless, because you have shown utter contempt for the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by doing this, your child will die.”
After Nathan returned to his home, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent a deadly illness to the child of Daud and Uryahu’s wife.
Daud begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to spare the child, he went without food and lay all night on the bare ground.
The elders of his household pleaded with him to get up and eat with them, but he refused.

Then on the seventh day the child died. Daud’s advisers were afraid to tell him, “he will not listen to reason while the child was ill,” they said. “What drastic thing will he do when we tell him the child is dead?”
When Daud saw them whispering, he realized what had happened. And Daud asked “Is the child dead?” they replied him Yes,” he is dead.”

Then Daud got up from the ground, washed himself, put on lotions, and changed his clothes, he went to the Tabernacle and worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. After that, he returned to the palace and was served food and ate.

His advisers were amazed. “We do not understand you,” they told him. “While the child was still living, you wept and refused to eat. But now that the child is dead, you have stopped your mourning and start eating again.”
Daud replied, “I fasted and wept while the child was alive, for I said, ‘Perhaps 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be merciful to me and let the child live.’
But why should I fast when the child is dead? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him one day, but he cannot return to me.”
Then Daud comforted Bathshaba, his wife, and slept with her. She became pregnant and gave birth to a son, and Daud named him Shalumah. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH loved the child
and sent word through Nathan the Nabym that they should name him Yadidyahu (which means “beloved of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH”), as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded.
Meanwhile, Yuab was fighting against Rabbah, the capital of Ammun, and he captured the royal fortifications.
Yuab sent messengers to tell Daud, “I have fought against Rabbah and captured its water supply.
Now bring the rest of the army and capture the city. Otherwise, I will capture it and get credit for the victory.”
So Daud gathered the rest of the army and went to Rabbah, and he fought against it and captured it.

Daud removed the crown from the king’s head, and it was placed on his own head. The crown was made of gold and set with gems, and it weighed seventy-five pounds. Daud took a vast amount of plunder from the city.

He also made slaves of the people of Rabbah and forced them to labor with saws, iron picks, and iron axes, and to work in the brick kilns. That is how he dealt with the people of all the Ammunite towns. Then Daud and all the army returned to Yahushalam.
Now Daud’s son Absalum had a beautiful sister named Tamar. And Amnun, her half brother, fell desperately in love with her.
Amnun became so obsessed with Tamar that he became ill. She was a virgin, and Amnun thought he could never have her.
But Amnun had a very crafty friend, his cousin Yunadab, he was the son of Daud’s brother Shimaa.
One day Yunadab said to Amnun, “What’s the trouble? Why should the son of a king look so dejected morning after morning?” So Amnun told him, “I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalum’s sister.”

“So Yunadab said to Ammun, “I will tell you what to do. Go back to bed and pretend you are ill. When your father comes to see you, ask him to let Tamar come and prepare some food for you. Tell him you’ll feel better if she prepares it as you watch and feeds you with her own hands.”

So Amnun lay down and pretended to be sick. And when the king came to see him, Amnun asked him, “Please let my sister Tamar come and cook my favorite dish as I watch. Then I can eat it from her own hands.”
So Daud agreed and sent Tamar to Amnun’s house to prepare some food for him.
When Tamar arrived at Amnun’s house, she went to the place where he was lying down so he could watch her mix some dough. Then she baked his favorite dish for him.
But when she set the serving tray before him, he refused to eat. “Everyone get out of here,” Amnun told his servants. So they all left.
Then he said to Tamar, “Now bring the food into my bedroom and feed it to me here.” So Tamar took his favorite dish to him.
But as Tamar was feeding Amnun, he grabbed her and demanded, “Come to bed with me, my darling sister.”
“No, my brother!” she cried. “Do not be foolish! Do not do this to me! Such wicked things are not done in Yashar'AL.
Where could I go in my shame? And you would be called one of the greatest fools in Yashar'AL. Please, just speak to the king about it, and he will let you marry me.”
But Amnun did not listen to her, and since he was stronger than her, he succeeded in raping her.
Then suddenly Amnun’s love turned to hate, and he hated her even more than he had loved her. “Get out of here!” he snarled at her.
“No, no!” Tamar cried. “Sending me away now is worse than what you’ve already done to me.” But Amnun would not listen to her.
Amnun shouted for his servant and demanded, “Throw this woman out, and lock the door behind her!”
So the servant put her out and locked the door behind her. She was wearing a long, beautiful robe, as was the custom in those days for the king’s virgin daughters.
But now Tamar tore her robe and put ashes on her head. And then, with her face in her hands, she went away crying.

Her brother Absalum saw her and asked, “Is it true that Amnun has been with you? Well, my sister, keep quiet for now, since he’s your brother. Do not worry about it.” So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in her brother Absalum’s house.
When King Daud heard what had happened, he was very angry.
And though Absalum never spoke to Amnun about this, he hated Amnun deeply because of what he had done to his sister.
Two years later, when Absalum’s sheep were being sheared at Baal-hazur near Aphraim, Absalum invited all the king’s sons to come to a feast.
He went to the king and said, “My sheep-shearers are now at work. Would the king and his servants please come to celebrate the occasion with me?”
The king replied, “No, my son. If we all go with you, we would be too much of a burden on you.” Absalum pressed him, but the king would not come, though he gave Absalum his Barakah.
“Well, then,” Absalum said, “if you can not come, how about sending my brother Amnun with us? “Why Amnun?” the king asked.
But Absalum kept on pressing the king until he finally agreed to let all his sons attend, including Amnun. So Absalum prepared a feast fit for a king.
Absalum told his men, “Wait until Amnun gets drunk; then at my signal, kill him! Do not be afraid. I am the one who has given the command. Take courage and do it!”
So at Absalum’s signal they murdered Amnun. Then the other sons of the king jumped on their mules and fled.
As they were on the way back to Yahushalam, this report reached Daud: “Absalum has killed all the king’s sons; not one is left alive!”
The king got up, tore his robe, and threw himself on the ground. His advisers also tore their clothes in horror and sorrow.

But just then Yunadab, the son of Daud’s brother Shimaa, arrived and said, “No, do not believe that all the king’s sons have been killed! It was only Amnun! Absalum has been plotting this ever since Amnun raped his sister Tamar.
No, my master the king, your sons are not all dead! It was only Amnun.”

Meanwhile Absalum escaped. Then the watchman on the Yahushalam wall saw a great crowd coming down the hill on the road from the west, he ran to tell the king, “I see a crowd of people coming from the Hurunaim road along the side of the hill.”
“Look!” Yunadab told the king. “There they are now! The king’s sons are coming, just as I said.”
They soon arrived, weeping and sobbing, and the king and all his servants wept bitterly with them.
And Daud mourned many days for his son Amnun. Absalum fled to his grandfather, Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Gashur.
He stayed there in Gashur for three years.
And King Daud, now reconciled to Amnun’s death, longed to be reunited with his son Absalum.
Yuab realized how much the king longed to see Absalum.

So he sent for a woman from Takua who had a reputation for great wisdom, he said to her, “Pretend you are in mourning; wear mourning clothes and do not put on lotions. Act like a woman who has been mourning for the dead for a long time.
Then go to the king and tell him the story I am about to tell you.” Then Yuab told her what to say.
When the woman from Takua approached the king, she bowed with her face to the ground in deep respect and cried out, “O king! Help me!”
“And the king asked her; What is the trouble? She replied “Alas, I am a widow! “My husband is dead.
My two sons had a fight out in the field. And since no one was there to stop it, one of them was killed.

Now the rest of the family is demanding, ‘Let us have your son. We will execute him for murdering his brother, he did not deserve to inherit his family’s property.’ They want to extinguish the only coal I have left, and my husband’s name and family will disappear from the face of the Arath.”
“Leave it to me,” the king told her. “Go home, and I’ll see to it that no one touches him.”

“Oh, thank you, my master the king,” the woman from Takua replied. “If you are criticized for helping me, let the blame fall on me and on my father’s house, and let the king and his throne be innocent.”
“the king said; If anyone objects, “bring him to me. I can assure you he will never harm you again!”

Then she said, “Please swear to me by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH that you will not let anyone take vengeance against my son. I want no more bloodshed. And king Daud replied her“ As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, “not a hair on your son’s head will be disturbed!”
“Please allow me to ask one more thing of my master the king,” she said. Daud said to her “Go ahead and speak,”.

And she said, “Why do you not do as much for the people of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH as you have promised to do for me? You have convicted yourself in making this decision, because you have refused to bring home your own banished son.

All of us must die eventually. Our lives are like water spilled out on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. But our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH does not just sweep life away; instead, he devises ways to bring us back when we have been separated from him.
“I have come to plead with my master the king because people have threatened me. I said to myself, ‘Perhaps the king will listen to me
and rescue us from those who would cut us off from the inheritance 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given us.
Yes, my master the king will give us Shalum of mind again.’ I know that you are like a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in discerning good from evil. May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be with you.”
“And the king said to her; I must know one thing, tell me the truth.” she replied; Yes, my master the king,”
“King Daud asked her; Did Yuab put you up to this?” And the woman replied, “My master the king, how can I deny it? Nobody can hide anything from you. Yes, Yuab sent me and told me what to say.
He did it to place the matter before you in a different light. But you are as wise as a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and you understand everything that happens among us!”
So the king sent for Yuab and told him, “All right, go and bring back the young man Absalum.”
Yuab bowed with his face to the ground in deep respect and said, “At last I know that I have gained your approval, my master the king, for you have granted me this request!”
Then Yuab went to Gashur and brought Absalum back to Yahushalam.
But the king gave this order: “Absalum may go to his own house, but he must never come into my presence.” So Absalum did not see the king.
Now Absalum was praised as the most handsome man in all Yashar'AL, he was flawless from head to foot.
He cut his hair only once a year, and then only because it was so heavy. When he weighed it out, it came to five pounds!
He had three sons and one daughter, his daughter’s name was Tamar, and she was very beautiful.
Absalum lived in Yahushalam for two years, but he never got to see the king.
Then Absalum sent for Yuab to ask him to intercede for him, but Yuab refused to come. Absalum sent for him a second time, but again Yuab refused to come.
So Absalum said to his servants, “Go and set fire to Yuab’s barley field, the field next to mine.” So they set his field on fire, as Absalum had commanded.
Then Yuab came to Absalum at his house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”

And Absalum replied, “Because I wanted you to ask the king why he brought me back from Gashur if he did not intend to see me. I might as well have stayed there. Let me see the king; if he finds me guilty of anything, then let him kill me.”
So Yuab told the king what Absalum had said. Then at last Daud summoned Absalum, who came and bowed low before the king, and the king kissed him.
After this, Absalum bought a chariot and horses, and he hired fifty bodyguards to run ahead of him.

He got up early every morning and went out to the gate of the city. When people brought a case to the king for judgment, Absalum would ask where in Yashar'AL they were from, and they would tell him their tribe.
Then Absalum would say, “You have really got a strong case here! It’s too bad the king does not have anyone to hear it.
I wish I were the judge. Then everyone could bring their cases to me for judgment, and I would give them justice!”
When people tried to bow before him, Absalum would not let them. Instead, he took them by the hand and kissed them.
Absalum did this with everyone who came to the king for judgment, and so he stole the hearts of all the people of Yashar'AL.
After four years, Absalum said to the king, “Let me go to Habrun to offer a sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and fulfill a vow I made to him.
For while your servant was at Gashur in Aram, I promised to sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Habrun if he would bring me back to Yahushalam.”
“All right,” the king told him. “Go and fulfill your vow.” So Absalum went to Habrun.

But while he was there, he sent secret messengers to all the tribes of Yashar'AL to stir up a rebellion against the king. “As soon as you hear the ram’s horn,” his message read, “you are to say, ‘Absalum has been crowned king in Habrun.’”
He took two hundred men from Yahushalam with him as guests, but they knew nothing of his intentions.
While Absalum was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithuphal, one of Daud’s counselors who lived in Giluh. Soon many others also joined Absalum, and the conspiracy gained momentum.
A messenger soon arrived in Yahushalam to tell Daud, “All Yashar'AL has joined Absalum in a conspiracy against you!”
“Then we must flee at once, or it will be too late!” Daud urged his men. “Hurry! If we get out of the city before Absalum arrives, both we and the city of Yahushalam will be spared from disaster.”
“We are with you,” his advisers replied. “Do what you think is best.”
So the king and all his household set out at once, he left no one behind except ten of his concubines to look after the palace.
The king and all his people set out on foot, pausing at the last house
to let all the king’s men move past to lead the way. There were 600 men from Gath who had come with Daud, along with the king’s bodyguard.
Then the king turned and said to Ittai, a leader of the men from Gath, “Why are you coming with us? Go on back to King Absalum, for you are a guest in Yashar'AL, a foreigner in exile.

You arrived only recently, and should I force you today to wander with us? I do not even know where we are going. Go on back and take your kinsmen with you, and may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH show you his unfailing love and faithfulness.”
But Ittai said to the king, “I vow by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and by your own life that I will go wherever my master the king goes, no matter what happens, whether it means life or death.”
Daud replied, “All right, come with us.” So Ittai and all his men and their families went along.
