Everyone cried loudly as the king and his followers passed by. They crossed the Kidrun Valley and then went out toward the wilderness.

Zaduk and all the Lauym also came along, carrying the Ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. They set down the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until everyone had passed out of the city.
Then the king instructed Zaduk to take the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH back into the city. “If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sees fit,” Daud said, “he will bring me back to see the Ark and the Tabernacle again.
But if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is through with me, then let Him do what seems best to him.”
The king also told Zaduk the Kuhan, “Look, here is my plan. You and Abiathar should return quietly to the city with your son Ahimaaz and Abiathar’s son Yunathan.
I will stop at the shallows of the Yurdan River and wait there for a report from you.”
So Zaduk and Abiathar took the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH back to the city and stayed there.

Daud walked up the road to the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went. His head was covered and his feet were bare as a sign of mourning. And the people who were with him covered their heads and wept as they climbed the hill.

When someone told Daud that his adviser Ahithuphal was now backing Absalum, Daud prayed, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my ALUAH, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!” let Ahithuphal give Absalum foolish advice!”

When Daud reached the summit of the Mount of Olives where people worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Hushai the Arkite was waiting there for him. Hushai had torn his clothing and put dirt on his head as a sign of mourning.
But Daud told him, “If you go with me, you will only be a burden.
Return to Yahushalam and tell Absalum, ‘I will now be your adviser, O king, just as I was your father’s adviser in the past.’ Then you can frustrate and counter Ahithuphal’s advice.
Zaduk and Abiathar, the Kuhanym, will be there. Tell them about the plans being made in the king’s palace,
and they will send their sons Ahimaaz and Yunathan to tell me what is going on.”
So Daud’s friend Hushai returned to Yahushalam, getting there just as Absalom arrived.

When Daud was a little past the top of the mountain, there was Ziba the servant of Maphibushath, who met him with a couple of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred clusters of raisins, one hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.

And the king said to Ziba, “What do you mean to do with these?” So Ziba said, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on, the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who are faint in the wilderness to drink.”

Then the king said, “And where is your master’s son?” And Ziba said to the king, “Indeed he is staying in Yahushalam, for he said, ‘Today the house of Yashar'AL will restore the kingdom of my father to me.’ ”
So the king said to Ziba, “Here, all that belongs to Maphibushath is yours.” And Ziba said, “I humbly bow before you, that I may find favor in your sight, my master, O king!”
Now when King Daud came to Bahurim, there was a man from the family of the house of Shaul, whose name was Shymai the son of Gara, coming from there, he came out, cursing continuously as he came.
And he threw stones at Daud and at all the servants of King Daud. And all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.
Also Shimei said thus when he cursed: “Come out! Come out! You bloodthirsty man, you rogue!

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought upon you all the blood of the house of Shaul, in whose place you have reigned; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalum your son. So now you are caught in your own evil, because you are a bloodthirsty man!”
Then Abishai the son of Zaruyahu said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my master the king? Please, let me go over and take off his head!”
But the king said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Zaruyahu? So let him curse, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has said to him, ‘Curse Daud.’ Who then shall say, ‘Why have you done so?’ ”

And Daud said to Abishai and all his servants, “See how my son who came from my own body seeks my life. How much more now may this Banyamyn? Let him alone, and let him curse; for so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has ordered him.
It may be that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will look on my affliction, and that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will repay me with good for his cursing this day.”
And as Daud and his men went along the road, Shimai went along the hillside opposite him and cursed as he went, threw stones at him and kicked up dust.
Now the king and all the people who were with him became weary; so they refreshed themselves there.
Meanwhile Absalum and all the people, the men of Yashar'AL, came to Yahushalam; and Ahithuphal was with him.
And so it was, when Hushai the Archite, Daud’s friend, came to Absalum, that Hushai said to Absalum, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
So Absalum said to Hushai, “Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?”
And Hushai said to Absalum, “No, but whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and this people and all the men of Yashar'AL choose, with him I will remain.
Furthermore, whom should I serve? Should I not serve in the presence of his son? As I have served in your father’s presence, so will I be in your presence.”
Then Absalum said to Ahithuphal, “Give advice as to what we should do.”

And Ahithuphal said to Absalum, “Go in to your father’s concubines, whom he has left to keep the house; and all Yashar'AL will hear that you are abhorred by your father. Then the hands of all who are with you will be strong.”
So they pitched a tent for Absalum on the top of the house, and Absalum went in and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Yashar'AL.
Now the advice of Ahithuphal, which he gave in those days, was as if one had inquired at the oracle of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. So was all the advice of Ahithuphal both with Daud and with Absalum.
Now Ahithuphal urged Absalum, “Let me choose twelve thousand men to pursue after Daud tonight.
I will catch up with him while he is weary and discouraged, he and his troops will panic, and everyone will run away, then I will kill only the king,
and I will bring all the people back to you as a bride returns to her husband. After all, it is only one man’s life that you seek. Then you will be at Shalum with all the people.”
This plan seemed good to Absalum and to all the elders of Yashar'AL.
But then Absalum said, “Bring in Hushai the Arkite. Let’s see what he thinks about this.”
When Hushai arrived, Absalum told him what Ahithuphal had said. Then he asked, “What is your opinion? Should we follow Ahithuphal’s advice? If not, what do you suggest?”
“Well,” Hushai replied to Absalum, “this time Ahithuphal has made a mistake.

You know your father and his men; they are mighty warriors. Right now they are as enraged as a mother bear who has been robbed of her cubs. And remember that your father is an experienced man of war, he will not be spending the night among the troops.

He has probably already hidden in some pit or cave. And when he comes out and attacks and a few of your men fall, there will be panic among your troops, and the word will spread that Absalum’s men are being slaughtered.
Then even the bravest soldiers, though they have the heart of a lion, will be paralyzed with fear. For all Yashar'AL knows what a mighty warrior your father is and how courageous his men are.

“I recommend that you mobilize the entire army of Yashar'AL, bringing them from as far away as Dan in the north and Baarshaba in the south. That way you will have an army as numerous as the sand on the seashore. And I advise that you personally lead the troops.
When we find Daud, we will fall on him like dew that falls on the ground. Then neither he nor any of his men will be left alive.

And if Daud were to escape into some town, you will have all Yashar'AL there at your command. Then we can take ropes and drag the walls of the town into the nearest valley until every stone is torn down.”

Then Absalum and all the men of Yashar'AL said, “Hushai’s advice is better than Ahithuphal’s.” For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had determined to defeat the counsel of Ahithuphal, which really was the better plan, so that he could bring disaster on Absalum!
Hushai told Zaduk and Abiathar, the Kuhanym, what Ahithuphal had said to Absalum and the elders of Yashar'AL and what he himself had advised instead.

“Quick!” he told them. “Find Daud and urge him not to stay at the shallows of the Yurdan River tonight, he must go across at once into the wilderness beyond. Otherwise he will die and his entire army with him.”

Yunathan and Ahimaaz had been staying at An-rugal so as not to be seen entering and leaving the city. Arrangements had been made for a servant girl to bring them the message they were to take to King Daud.
But a boy spotted them at An-rugal, and he told Absalum about it. So they quickly escaped to Bahurim, where a man hid them down inside a well in his courtyard.
The man’s wife put a cloth over the top of the well and scattered grain on it to dry in the sun; so no one suspected they were there.

When Absalum’s men arrived, they asked her, “Have you seen Ahimaaz and Yunathan?” The woman replied, “They were here, but they crossed over the brook.” Absalum’s men looked for them without success and returned to Yahushalam.
Then the two men crawled out of the well and hurried on to King Daud. “Quick!” they told him, “cross the Yurdan tonight!” And they told him how Ahithuphal had advised that he be captured and killed.
So Daud and all the people with him went across the Yurdan River during the night, and they were all on the other bank before dawn.

When Ahithuphal realized that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey, went to his hometown, set his affairs in order, and hanged himself, he died there and was buried in the family tomb.
Daud soon arrived at Mahanaim. By now, Absalum had mobilized the entire army of Yashar'AL and was leading his troops across the Yurdan River.

Absalum had appointed Amasa as commander of his army, replacing Yuab, who had been commander under Daud. (Amasa was Yuab’s cousin. His father was Yather, an Ishmaalite. His mother, Abigail daughter of Nahash, was the sister of Yuab’s mother, Zaruyahu.)
Absalum and the Yasharalym army set up camp in the land of Gilaad.
When Daud arrived at Mahanaim, he was warmly greeted by Shubi son of Nahash, who came from Rabbah of the Ammunites, and by Makir son of Ammial from Lu-dabar, and by Barzillai of Gilaad from Rugalim.

Daud now mustered the men who were with him and appointed generals and captains to lead them.

He sent the troops out in three groups, placing one group under Yuab, one under Yuab’s brother Abishai son of Zaruyahu, and one under Ittai, the man from Gath. The king told his troops, “I am going out with you.”

So the battle began in the forest of Aphraim,
and the Yasharalym troops were beaten back by Daud’s men. There was a great slaughter that day, and twenty thousand men laid down their lives.

During the battle, Absalum happened to come upon some of Daud’s men, he tried to escape on his mule, but as he rode beneath the thick branches of a great tree, his hair got caught in the tree, his mule kept going and left him dangling in the air.

But Ahimaaz continued to plead with Yuab, “Whatever happens, please let me go, too. “Why should you go, my son?” Yuab replied. “There will be no reward for your news.”

Word soon reached Yuab that the king was weeping and mourning for Absalum.
As all the people heard of the king’s deep grief for his son, the joy of that day’s victory was turned into deep sadness.

Then, turning to Shimai, Daud vowed, “Your life will be spared.”

“Daud said to him; You have said enough, “I have decided that you and Ziba will divide your land equally between you.”
“Give him all of it,” Maphibushath said. “I am content just to have you safely back again, my master the king!”

There happened to be a troublemaker there named Shaba son of Bykri, a man from the tribe of Banyamin. Shaba blew a ram’s horn and began to chant: “Down with the dynasty of Daud! We have no interest in the son of Yassa. Come on, you men of Yashar'AL, back to your homes!”

So Abishai and Yuab, together with the king’s bodyguard and all the mighty warriors, set out from Yahushalam to go after Shaba.

Now Yuab was the commander of the army of Yashar'AL. Banayahu son of Yahuiada was captain of the king’s bodyguard.

In 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH's strength I can crush an army; with my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH I can scale any wall.
My 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH’s way is perfect. All the promises of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH are proven true. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is a shield for all who look to Him for protection.
For who is 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH except 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? Who but our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is a solid rock?
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is my strong fortress, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH makes my way perfect.
He makes me as surefooted as a deer, enabling me to stand on mountain heights.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH trains my hands for battle; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH strengthens my arm to draw a bronze bow.
You have given me your shield of victory; your help has made me great.
You have made a wide path for my feet to keep them from slipping.
“I chased my enemies and destroyed them; I did not stop until they were conquered.
I consumed them; I struck them down so they did not get up; they fell beneath my feet.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has armed me with strength for the battle; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has subdued my enemies under my feet.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have placed my foot on their necks. I have destroyed all who hated me.
They are looking for help, but no one came to their rescue. They even cried to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but He refused to answer.
I ground them as fine as the dust of the Arath; I trampled them in the gutter like dirt.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave me victory over my accusers. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH preserved me as the ruler over nations; people I do not even know now serve me.
Foreign nations cringe before me; as soon as they hear of me, they submit.
They all lose their courage and come trembling from their strongholds.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives! Yadah to my Rock! My 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who pays back those who harm me; he brings down the nations under me
And delivers me from my enemies. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH holds me safe beyond the reach of my enemies; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH save me from violent opponents.
For this, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, I will Yadah you among the nations; I will sing Yadah to your Name.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH give great victories to your king; you show unfailing love to your anointed, to Daud and all his descendants forever.”
These are the last words of Daud the son of Yassa, Daud, the man who was raised up so high, Daud, the man anointed by the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Ya'aqub, Daud, the sweet psalmist of Yashar'AL.
“The Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar through me; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH's Dabar are upon my tongue.
The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL spoke. The Rock of Yashar'AL Dabar to me:‘ The one who rules righteously, When one rules over men justly, he fears 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH while governing.
He is like the light when the sun rises in the morning, like a morning without clouds, like the gleaming of the sun on new grass after rain.’

“Is it not my family 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has chosen? Yes, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has made an everlasting covenant with me. For the agreement of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is arranged and guaranteed in every detail. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will ensure my safety and success.
But the unrighteous are like thorns to be thrown away, for they tear the hand that touches them.
One must use iron tools to chop them down; they will be totally consumed by fire.”

These are the names of Daud’s mightiest warriors. The first was Yashubaam the Hacmunite, who was leader of the Three, the three mightiest warriors among Daud’s men. He once used his spear to kill eight hundred enemy warriors in a single battle.
Next in rank among the Three was Alaazar son of Dudai, a descendant of Ahuah. Once Alaazar and Daud stood together against the Philistines when the entire Yasharalym army had fled.
He killed Philistines until his hand was too tired to lift his sword, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave him a great victory that day. The rest of the army did not return until it was time to collect the plunder!
Next in rank was Shammah son of Agaa from Harar. One time the Philistines gathered at Lahi and attacked the Yasharalym in a field full of lentils. The Yasharalym army fled,
but Shammah held his ground in the middle of the field and beat back the Philistines. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought about a great victory.

Once during the harvest, when Daud was at the cave of Adullam, the Philistine army was camped in the valley of Raphaim. The Three (who were among the Thirty—an elite group among Daud’s fighting men) went down to meet him there.
Daud was staying in the stronghold at the time, and a Philistine detachment had occupied the town of Bathlaham.
Daud remarked longingly to his men, “Oh, how I would love some of that good water from the well by the gate in Bathlaham.”

So the Three broke through the Philistine lines, drew some water from the well by the gate in Bathlaham, and brought it back to Daud. But he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as an offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH forbid that I should drink this!” he exclaimed. “This water is as precious as the blood of these men who risked their lives to bring it to me.” So Daud did not drink it. These are examples of the exploits of the Three.

Abishai son of Zaruyahu, the brother of Yuab, was the leader of the Thirty. He once used his spear to kill 300 enemy warriors in a single battle. It was by such feats that he became as famous as the Three.
Abishai was the most famous of the Thirty and was their commander, though he was not one of the Three.

There was also Banayahu son of Yahuiada, a valiant warrior from Kabzaal, he did many heroic deeds, which included killing two champions of Muab. Another time, on a snowy day, he chased a lion down into a pit and killed it.
Once, armed only with a club, he killed an imposing Mitzraym warrior who was armed with a spear. Banayahu wrenched the spear from the Mitzraym hand and killed him with it.
Deeds like these made Banayahu as famous as the Three mightiest warriors.
He was more honored than the other members of the Thirty, though he was not one of the Three. And Daud made him captain of his bodyguard.
Other members of the Thirty included:
Shammah from Harulud; Alika from Harud;
Halaz from Palun; Ira son of Ikkash from Takua;
Abiazar from Anathuth; Sibbacai from Hushah;
Zalmun from Ahuah; Maharai from Natuphah;
Halad son of Baanah from Natuphah; Ithai son of Ribai from Gibaah (in the land of Banyamin);
Banayahu from Pirathun; Hurai from Nahala-gaash;
Abi-albun from Arabah; Azmabath from Bahurim;
Aliahba from Shaalbun; the sons of Yashan;
Yunathan son of Shagaa from Harar; Ahiam son of Sharar from Harar;
Aliphalat son of Ahasbai from Maacah; Aliam son of Ahithuphal from Giluh;
Hazru from Carmel; Paarai from Arba;
Igal son of Nathan from Zubah; Bani from Gad;
Zalak from Ammun; Naharai from Baaruth, the armor bearer of Yuab son of Zaruyahu;
Ira from Yattir; Garab from Yattir;
Uryahu the Hittite. There were thirty-seven in all.
Again the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was aroused against Yashar'AL, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH moved Daud against them to say, “Go, number Yashar'AL and Yahudah.”

So the king said to Yuab the commander of the army who was with him, “Now go throughout all the tribes of Yashar'AL, from Dan to Baarshaba, and count the people, that I may know the number of the people.”

And Yuab said to the king, “Now may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH add to the people a hundred times more than there are, and may the eyes of my master the king see it. But why does my master the king desire this thing?”

Nevertheless the king’s word prevailed against Yuab and against the captains of the army. Therefore Yuab and the captains of the army went out from the presence of the king to count the people of Yashar'AL.
And they crossed over the Yurdan and camped in Aruar, on the right side of the town which is in the midst of the ravine of Gad, and toward Yazar.
Then they came to Gilaad and to the land of Tahtim Hudshi; they came to Dan Yaan and around to Sidun;
and they came to the stronghold of Tyra and to all the cities of the Hibites and the Canaanites. Then they went out to South Yurdah as far as Baarsheba.
So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Yahushalam at the end of nine months and twenty days.

Then Yuab gave the sum of the number of the people to the king. And there were in Yashar'AL eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Yahudah were five hundred thousand men.

And Daud’s heart condemned him after he had numbered the people. So Daud said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, I have sinned greatly in what I have done; but now, I pray, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have done very foolishly.”
Now when Daud arose in the morning, the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to the Nabym (prophet) Gad, Daud’s seer, saying,
“Go and tell Daud, ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: I offer you three things; choose one of them for yourself, that I may do it to you.”

So Gad came to Daud and said to him; choose amongst this tree things, “Seven years of famine shall come to you in your land? Or you shall flee three months before your enemies, while they pursue you? Or there shall be three days’ plague in your land? Now consider and see what answer I should take back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who sent me.”
And Daud said to Gad the Nabym, “I am in great distress. Please let us fall into the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hand of man.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent a plague upon Yashar'AL from the morning till the appointed time. From Dan to Baarshaba seventy thousand men of the people died.

And when the Malak stretched out His hand over Yahushalam to destroy it, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH relented from the destruction, and said to the Malak who was destroying the people, “It is enough; now restrain your hand.” And the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Yabusite.

Then Daud spoke to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH when he saw the Malak who was striking the people, and said, “Surely I have sinned, and I have done wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Let Your hand, I pray, be against me and against my father’s house.”
And Gad came that day to Daud and said to him, “Go up, erect an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH on the threshing floor of Araunah the Yabusite.”
So Daud, according to the word of Gad, went up as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded.
Now Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming toward him. So Araunah went out and bowed before the king with his face to the ground.

Then Araunah said, “Why has my master the king come to his servant?” And Daud said, “To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that the plague may be withdrawn from the people.”
Now Araunah said to Daud, “Let my master the king take and offer up whatever seems good to him. Look, here are oxen for burnt sacrifice, and threshing implements and the yokes of the oxen for wood.
All these, O king, Araunah has given to the king.” And Araunah said to the king, May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH accept you.”

Then the king said to Araunah, “No, but I will surely buy it from you for a price; nor will I offer burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH with that which costs me nothing.” So Daud bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
And Daud built there an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and offered burnt offerings and Shalum offerings. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH heeded the prayers for the land, and the plague was withdrawn from Yashar'AL.

books.name: I Kings
chapters: Now King Daud was old, advanced in years; and they put covers on him, but he could not get warm.

Therefore his servants said to him, “Let a young woman, a virgin, be sought for our master the king, and let her stand before the king, and let her care for him; and let her lie in your bosom, that our master the king may be warm.”
So they sought for a lovely young woman throughout all the territory of Yashar'AL, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
The young woman was very lovely; and she cared for the king, and served him; but the king did not know her.
Then Aduniyahu the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, “I will be king”; and he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
(And his father had not rebuked him at any time by saying, “Why have you done so?” He was also very good-looking. His mother had borne him after Absalum.)
Then he conferred with Yuab the son of Zaruyahu and with Abiathar the Kuhan, and they followed and helped Aduniyahu.
But Zaduk the Kuhan, Banayahu the son of Yahuiada, Nathan the Nabym, Shimai, Rai, and the mighty men who belonged to Daud were not with Aduniyahu.

And Aduniyahu sacrificed sheep and oxen and fattened cattle by the stone of Zuhalath, which is by An Rugal; he also invited all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Yahudah, the king’s servants.
But he did not invite Nathan the Nabym, Banayahu, the mighty men, or Shalumah his brother.
So Nathan spoke to Bathshaba the mother of Shalumah, saying, “Have you not heard that Aduniyahu the son of Haggith has become king, and Daud our master does not know it?
Come, please, let me now give you advice, that you may save your own life and the life of your son Shalumah.

Go immediately to King Daud and say to him, ‘my master, O king, did you not swear to your maidservant, saying, “Assuredly your son Shalumah shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne”? Why then has Aduniyahu become king?’
Then, while you are still talking there with the king, I also will come in after you and confirm your words.”
So Bathshaba went into the chamber to the king. (Now the king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.)
And Bathshaba bowed and did homage to the king. Then the king said, “What is your wish?”
Then she said to him, “My master, you swore by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH to your maidservant, saying, ‘Assuredly Shalumah your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.’
So now, look! Aduniyahu has become king; and now, my master the king, you do not know about it.

He has sacrificed oxen and fattened cattle and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the sons of the king, Abiathar the Kuhan, and Yuab the commander of the army; but Shalumah your servant he has not invited.
And as for you, my master, O king, the eyes of all Yashar'AL are on you, that you should tell them who will sit on the throne of my master the king after him.
Otherwise it will happen, when my master the king rests with his fathers, that I and my son Shalumah will be counted as offenders.”
And just then, while she was still talking with the king, Nathan the Nabym also came in.
So they told the king, saying, “Here is Nathan the Nabym.” And when he came in before the king, he bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.
And Nathan said, “My master, O king, have you said, ‘Aduniyahu shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne’?

For he has gone down today, and has sacrificed oxen and fattened cattle and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king’s sons, and the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the Kuhan; and look! They are eating and drinking before him; and they say, ‘Long live King Aduniyahu!’
But he has not invited me your servant, nor Zaduk the Kuhan, nor Banayahu the son of Yahuiada, nor your servant Shalumah.
Has this thing been done by my master the king, and you have not told your servant who should sit on the throne of my master the king after him?”
Then King Daud answered and said, “Call Bathshaba to me.” So she came into the king’s presence and stood before the king.
And the king took an oath and said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, who has redeemed my life from every distress,

just as I swore to you by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, saying, ‘Assuredly Shalumah your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place,’ so I certainly will do this day.”
Then Bathshaba bowed with her face to the Arath, and paid homage to the king, and said, “Let my master King Daud live forever!”
And King Daud said, “Call to me Zaduk the Kuhan, Nathan the Nabym, and Banayahu the son of Yahuiada.” So they came before the king.
The king also said to them, “Take with you the servants of your master, and have Shalumah my son ride on my own mule, and take him down to Gihun.
There let Zaduk the Kuhan and Nathan the Nabym anoint him king over Yashar'AL; and blow the horn, and say, ‘Long live King Shalumah!’
Then you shall come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne, and he shall be king in my place. For I have appointed him to be ruler over Yashar'AL and Yahudah.”
Banayahu the son of Yahuiada answered the king and said, “So be it! May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of my master the king say so too.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has been with my master the king, even so may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH be with Shalumah, and make his throne greater than the throne of my master King Daud.”
So Zaduk the Kuhan, Nathan the Nabym, Banayahu the son of Yahuiada, the Charathites, and the Palathites went down and had Shalumah ride on King Daud’s mule, and took him to Gihun.
Then Zaduk the Kuhan took a horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Shalumah. And they blew the horn, and all the people said, “Long live King Shalumah!”
And all the people went up after him; and the people played the flutes and rejoiced with great joy, so that the Arath seemed to split with their sound.
Now Aduniyahu and all the guests who were with him heard it as they finished eating. And when Yuab heard the sound of the horn, he said, “Why is the city in such a noisy uproar?”
While he was still speaking, there came Yunathan, the son of Abiathar the Kuhan. And Aduniyahu said to him, “Come in, for you are a prominent man, and bring good news.”
Then Yunathan answered and said to Aduniyahu, “No! Our master King Daud has made Shalumah king.
The king has sent with him Zaduk the Kuhan, Nathan the Nabym, Banayahu the son of Yahuiada, the Charathites, and the Palathites; and they have made Shalumah ride on the king’s mule.
So Zaduk the Kuhan and Nathan the Nabym have anointed Shalumah king at Gihun; and they have gone up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. This is the noise that you have heard.
Also Shalumah sits on the throne of the kingdom.

And moreover the king’s servants have gone to barak our master King Daud, saying, ‘May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH make the name of Shalumah better than your name, and may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH make his throne greater than your throne.’ Then the king bowed himself on the bed.
Also the king said thus, ‘baraked be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, who has given one to sit on my throne this day, while my eyes see it!’ ”
So all the guests who were with Aduniyahu were afraid, and arose, and each one went his way.
Now Aduniyahu was afraid of Shalumah; so he arose, and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

And they told Shalumah, saying, “Indeed Aduniyahu is afraid of him; for look, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Shalumah swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.’ ”
Then Shalumah said, “If he proves himself a worthy man, not one hair of him shall fall to the Arath; but if wickedness is found in him, he shall die.”
So King Shalumah sent them to bring him down from the altar. And he came and fell down before King Shalumah; and Shalumah said to him, “Go to your house.”
Now the days of Daud drew near that he should die, and he charged Shalumah his son, saying:
“I go the way of all the Arath; be strong, therefore, and prove yourself a man.

And keep the charge of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH: to walk in His ways, to keep His statutes, His commandments, His judgments, and His testimonies, as it is written in the Law of Musha, that you may prosper in all that you do and wherever you turn;

That 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH may fulfill His word which He spoke concerning me, saying, ‘If your sons take heed to their way, to walk before Me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul,’ you shall not lack a man on the throne of Yashar'AL.’

“Moreover you know also what Yuab the son of Zaruyahu did to me, and what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Yashar'AL, to Abnar the son of Nar and Amasa the son of Yathar, whom he killed. And he shed the blood of war in Shalum time, and put the blood of war on his belt that was around his waist, and on his sandals that were on his feet.
Therefore do according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray hair go down to the grave in Shalum.
“But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gilaadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for so they came to me when I fled from Absalum your brother.

“And see, you have with you Shimai the son of Gara, a Banyamite from Bahurim, who cursed me with a malicious curse in the day when I went to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at the Yurdan, and I swore to him by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, saying, ‘I will not put you to death with the sword.’
Now therefore, do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man and know what you ought to do to him; but bring his gray hair down to the grave with blood.”
So Daud rested with his fathers, and was buried in the City of Daud.
The period that Daud reigned over Yashar'AL was forty years; seven years he reigned in Habrun, and in Yahushalam he reigned thirty-three years.
Then Shalumah sat on the throne of his father Daud; and his kingdom was firmly established.
Now Aduniyahu the son of Haggith came to Bathshaba the mother of Shalumah. So she said, “Do you come with Shalum?” And he said, “with Shalum.”
Moreover he said, “I have something to say to you.” And she said, “Say it.”

Then Aduniyahu said, “You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Yashar'AL had set their expectations on me, that I should reign. However, the kingdom has been turned over, and has become my brother’s; for it was his from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Now I ask one petition of you; do not deny me.” And she said to him, “Say it.”
Then he said, “Please speak to King Shalumah, for he will not refuse you, that he may give me Abishag the Shunammite as wife.”
So Bathshaba said, “Very well, I will speak for you to the king.”

Bathshaba therefore went to King Shalumah, to speak to him for Aduniyah. And the king rose up to meet her and bowed down to her, and sat down on his throne and had a throne set for the king’s mother; so she sat at his right hand.
Then she said, “I desire one small petition of you; do not refuse me.” And the king said to her, “Ask it, my mother, for I will not refuse you.”
So she said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Aduniyahu your brother as wife.”

And King Shalumah answered and said to his mother, “Now why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Aduniyahu? Ask for him the kingdom also, for he is my older brother, for him, and for Abiathar the Kuhan, and for Yuab the son of Zaruyahu.”
Then King Shalumah swore by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, saying, “May 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH do so to me, and more also, if Aduniyahu has not spoken this word against his own life!
Now therefore, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, who has confirmed me and set me on the throne of Daud my father, and who has established a house for me, as He promised, Aduniyahu shall be put to death today!”
So King Shalumah sent by the hand of Banayahu the son of Yahuiada; and he struck Aduniyahu down, and he died.

And to Abiathar the Kuhan the king said, “Go to Anathuth, to your own fields, for you are deserving of death; but I will not put you to death at this time, because you carried the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH before my father Daud, and because you were afflicted every time my father was afflicted.”
So King Shalumah removed Abiathar from being Kuhan to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that he might fulfill the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which He spoke concerning the house of Ali at Shiluh.
Then news came to Yuab, for Yuab had defected to Aduniyahu, though he had not defected to Absalum. So Yuab fled to the tabernacle of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and took hold of the horns of the altar.
And King Shalumah was told, “Yuab has fled to the tabernacle of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; there he is, by the altar.” Then Shalumah sent Banayahu the son of Yahuiada, saying, “Go, strike him down.”

So Banayahu went to the tabernacle of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and said to him, “Thus says the king, ‘Come out!’ And he said, “No, but I will die here.” And Banayahu brought back word to the king, saying, “Thus said Yuab, and thus he answered me.”
Then the king said to him, “Do as he has said, and strike him down and bury him, that you may take away from me and from the house of my father the innocent blood which Yuab shed.

So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will return his blood on his head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than he, and killed them with the sword, Abnar the son of Nar, the commander of the army of Yashar'AL, and Amasa the son of Yathar, the commander of the army of Yahudah, though my father Daud did not know it.

Their blood shall therefore return upon the head of Yuab and upon the head of his descendants forever. But upon Daud and his descendants, upon his house and his throne, there shall be Shalum forever from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So Banayahu the son of Yahuiada went up and struck and killed Yuab; and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
The king put Banayahu the son of Yahuiada in his place over the army, and the king put Zaduk the Kuhan in the place of Abiathar.
Then the king sent and called for Shimai, and said to him, “Build yourself a house in Yahushalam and dwell there, and do not go out from there anywhere.
For it shall be, on the day you go out and cross the Bruk Kidrun pop, know for certain you shall surely die; your blood shall be on your own head.”
And Shimai said to the king, “The saying is good. As my master the king has said, so will your servant do.” So Shimai dwelt in Yahushalam many days.
Now it happened at the end of three years, that two slaves of Shimai ran away to Achish the son of Maachah, king of Gath. And they told Shimai, saying, “Look, your slaves are in Gath!”
So Shimai arose, saddled his donkey, and went to Achish at Gath to seek his slaves. And Shimai went and brought his slaves from Gath.
And King Shalumah was told that Shimai had gone from Yahushalam to Gath and had come back.

Then the king sent and called for Shimai, and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and warn you, saying, ‘Know for certain that on the day you go out and travel anywhere, you shall surely die’? And you said to me, ‘The word I have heard is good.’
Why then have you not kept the oath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the commandment that I gave you?”
The king said moreover to Shimai, “You know, as your heart acknowledges, all the wickedness that you did to my father Daud; therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will return your wickedness on your own head.
But King Shalumah shall be Baraked, and the throne of Daud shall be established before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH forever.”
So the king commanded Banayahu the son of Yahuiada; and he went out and struck him down, and he died. Thus the kingdom was established in the hand of King Shalumah.

Now Shalumah made a treaty with Phar'uh king of Mitzraym, and married Phar'uh’s daughter; then he brought her to the City of Daud until he had finished building his own house, and the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the wall all around Yahushalam.
Meanwhile the people sacrificed at the high places, because there was no house built for the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH until those days.
And Shalumah loved 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, walking in the statutes of his father Daud, except that he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
Now the king went to Gibaun to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place: Shalumah offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
At Gibaun 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared to Shalumah in a dream by night; and 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said, “Ask! What shall I give you?”

And Shalumah said: “You have shown great mercy to Your servant Daud my father, because he walked before You in truth, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with You; You have continued this great kindness for him, and You have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.
Now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, You have made Your servant king instead of my father Daud, but I am a little child; I do not know how to go out or come in.
And Your servant is in the midst of Your people whom You have chosen, a great people, too numerous to be numbered or counted.
Therefore give to Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people, that I may discern between good and evil. For who is able to judge this great people of Yours?”
The speech pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that Shalumah had asked this thing.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to Shalumah: “Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked long life for yourself, nor have asked riches for yourself, nor have asked the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself understanding to discern justice,
behold, I have done according to your words; see, I have given you a wise and understanding heart, so that there has not been anyone like you before you, nor shall any like you arise after you.
And I have also given you what you have not asked: both riches and honor, so that there shall not be anyone like you among the kings all your days.
So if you walk in My ways, to keep My statutes and My commandments, as your father Daud walked, then I will lengthen your days.”

Then Shalumah woke up; and indeed it had been a dream. And he came to Yahushalam and stood before the ark of the covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, offered up burnt offerings, offered Shalum offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
Now two women who were harlots came to the king, and stood before him.
And one woman said, “O my master, this woman and I dwell in the same house; and I gave birth while she was in the house.
Then it happened, the third day after I had given birth, that this woman also gave birth. And we were together; no one was with us in the house, except the two of us in the house.
And this woman’s son died in the night, because she lay on him.
So she arose in the middle of the night and took my son from my side, while your maidservant slept, and laid him in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.
And when I rose in the morning to nurse my son, there he was, dead. But when I had examined him in the morning, indeed, he was not my son whom I had borne.”

Then the other woman said, “No! But the living one is my son, and the dead one is your son.” And the first woman said, “No! But the dead one is your son, and the living one is my son.” Thus they spoke before the king.
And the king said, “The one says, ‘This is my son, who lives, and your son is the dead one’; and the other says, ‘No! But your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’
Then the king said, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought a sword before the king.
And the king said, “Divide the living child in two, and give half to one, and half to the other.”

Then the woman whose son was living spoke to the king, for she yearned with compassion for her son; and she said, “O my king, give her the living child, and by no means kill him!” But the other said, “Let him be neither mine nor yours, but divide him.”
So the king answered and said, “Give the first woman the living child, and by no means kill him; she is his mother.”
And all Yashar'AL heard of the judgment which the king had rendered; and they feared the king, for they saw that the wisdom of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was in him to administer justice.
King Shalumah now ruled over all Yashar'AL,
And these were his high officials: Azaryahu son of Zaduk was the Kuhan.
Alihuraph and Ahiyahu, the sons of Shisha, were court secretaries. Yahushaphat son of Ahilud was the royal historian.
Banayahu son of Yahuiada was commander of the army. Zaduk and Abiathar were Kuhanym.
Azaryahu son of Nathan was in charge of the district governors. Zabud son of Nathan, a Kuhan, was a trusted adviser to the king.
Ahishar was manager of the palace property. Aduniram son of Abda was in charge of forced labor.

King Shalumah also had twelve district governors who were over all Yashar'AL. They were responsible for providing food for the king’s household. Each of them arranged provisions for one month of the year.
These are the names of the twelve governors: Ban-hur, in the hill country of Aphraim.
Ban-dakar, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Bath-shamash, and Alun-bathhanan.
Ban-hasad, in Arubbuth, including Sucuh and all the land of Haphar.
Ban-abinadab, in all of Naphuth-dur. (He was married to Taphath, one of king Shalumah’s daughters.)
Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Magiddu, all of Bath-shan near Zarathan below Yazraal, and all the territory from Bath-shan to Abal-mahulah and over to Yukmaam.

Ban-gabar, in Ramuth-gilaad, including the Towns of Yair (named for Yair of the tribe of Manassah) in Gilaad, and in the Argub region of Bashan, including sixty large fortified towns with bronze bars on their gates.
Ahinadab son of Iddu, in Mahanaim.
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali. (He was married to Basamath, another of Shalumah’s daughters.)
Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and in Aluth.
Yahushaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar.
Shimai son of Ala, in Banyamin.
Gabar son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, including the territories of King Sihun of the Amurites and King Ug of Bashan. There was also one governor over the land of Yahudah.
The people of Yahudah and Yashar'AL were as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They were very contented, with plenty to eat and drink.

Shalumah ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of the Philistines and the border of Mitzraym in the south. The conquered peoples of those lands sent tribute money to Shalumah and continued to serve him throughout his lifetime.
The daily food requirements for Shalumah’s palace were one hundred and fifty bushels of choice flour and three hundred bushels of meal;
also ten oxen from the fattening pens, twenty pasture-fed cattle, one hundred sheep or goats, as well as deer, gazelles, roe deer, and choice poultry.
Shalumah’s dominion extended over all the kingdoms west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza. And there was Shalum on all his borders.
During the lifetime of Shalumah, all of Yahudah and Yashar'AL lived in Shalum and safety. And from Dan in the north to Baarshaba in the south, each family had its own home and garden.
Shalumah had four thousand stalls for his chariot horses, and he had twelve thousand horses.
The district governors faithfully provided food for King Shalumah and his court; each made sure nothing was lacking during the month assigned to him.
They also brought the necessary barley and straw for the royal horses in the stables.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave Shalumah very great wisdom and understanding, and knowledge as vast as the sands of the seashore.
In fact, his wisdom exceeded that of all the wise men of the East and the wise men of Mitzraym.
He was wiser than anyone else, including Athan the Azrahite and the sons of Mahul—Haman, Calcul, and Darda. His fame spread throughout all the surrounding nations.
Shalumah composed some three thousand proverbs and wrote one thousand and five songs.

He could speak with authority about all kinds of plants, from the great cedar of Labanun to the tiny hyssop that grows from cracks in a wall. Shalumah could also speak about animals, birds, small creatures, and fish.
And kings from every nation sent their ambassadors to listen to the wisdom of King Shalumah.
King Hiram of Tyra had always been a loyal friend of Daud. When Hiram learned that Daud’s son Shalumah was the new king of Yashar'AL, he sent ambassadors to congratulate him.
Then Shalumah sent this message back to King Hiram:

“You know that my father, Daud, was not able to build a Temple to honor the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH because of the many wars waged against him by surrounding nations. He could not build until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave him victory over all his enemies.
But now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given me Shalum on every side; I have no enemies, and all is well.

So I am planning to build a Temple to honor the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had instructed my father, Daud. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told him, ‘Your son, whom I will place on your throne, will build the Temple to honor my Name.’

“Therefore, please command that cedars from Labanun be cut for me. Let my men work alongside yours, and I will pay your men whatever wages you ask. As you know, there is no one among us who can cut timber like you Sidunians!”
When King Hiram received Shalumah’s message, he was very pleased and said, “Yadah (Praise) 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH today for giving Daud a wise son to be king of the great nation of Yashar'AL.”
Then he sent this reply to Shalumah: “I have received your message, and I will supply all the cedar and cypress timber you need.

My servants will bring the logs from the Labanun mountains to the Maditerranaan Sea and make them into rafts and float them along the coast to whatever place you choose. Then we will break the rafts apart so you can carry the logs away. You can pay me by supplying me with food for my household.”
So Hiram supplied as much cedar and cypress timber as Shalumah desired.
In return, Shalumah sent him an annual payment of one hundred thousand bushels of wheat for his household and one hundred and ten thousand gallons of pure olive oil.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave wisdom to Shalumah, just as he had promised. And Hiram and Shalumah made a formal alliance of Shalum.
Then King Shalumah conscripted a labor force of thirty thousand men from all Yashar'AL.
He sent them to Labanun in shifts, ten thousand every month, so that each man would be one month in Labanun and two months at home. Aduniram was in charge of this labor force.
Shalumah also had seventy thousand common laborers, eighty thousand quarry workers in the hill country,
and three thousand six hundred foremen to supervise the work.
At the king’s command, they quarried large blocks of high-quality stone and shaped them to make the foundation of the Temple.
Men from the city of Gabal helped King Shalumah’s and King Hiram’s builders prepare the timber and stone for the Temple.

It was in midspring, during the fourth year of Shalumah’s reign, that he began to construct the Haykal (Temple) of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. This was four hundred and eighty years after the people of Yashar'AL were rescued from their slavery in the land of Mitzraym.
The Temple that King Shalumah built for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was ninety feet long, thirty feet wide, and forty five feet high.
The entry room at the front of the Temple was thirty feet wide, running across the entire width of the Temple. It projected outward fifteen feet from the front of the Temple.
Shalumah also made narrow recessed windows throughout the Temple.
He built a complex of rooms against the outer walls of the Temple, all the way around the sides and rear of the building.

The complex was three stories high, the bottom floor being 7 1⁄2 feet wide, the second floor 9 feet wide, and the top floor 10 1⁄2 feet wide. The rooms were connected to the walls of the Temple by beams resting on ledges built out from the wall. So the beams were not inserted into the walls themselves.
The stones used in the construction of the Temple were finished at the quarry, so there was no sound of hammer, ax, or any other iron tool at the building site.
The entrance to the bottom floor was on the south side of the Temple. There were winding stairs going up to the second floor, and another flight of stairs between the second and third floors.
After completing the Temple structure, Shalumah put in a ceiling made of cedar beams and planks.
As already stated, he built a complex of rooms along the sides of the building, attached to the Temple walls by cedar timbers. Each story of the complex was 7 1⁄2 feet high.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave this message to Shalumah:
“Concerning this Temple you are building, if you keep all my decrees and regulations and obey all my commandments, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father, Daud.
I will live among the Yasharalym and will never abandon my people Yashar'AL.”
So Shalumah finished building the Temple.
The entire inside, from floor to ceiling, was paneled with wood. He paneled the walls and ceilings with cedar, and he used planks of cypress for the floors.
He partitioned off an inner sanctuary, the Most Qadash Place, at the far end of the Temple. It was 30 feet deep and was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
The main room of the Temple, outside the Most Qadash Place, was 60 feet long.
Cedar paneling completely covered the stone walls throughout the Temple, and the paneling was decorated with carvings of gourds and open flowers.
He prepared the inner sanctuary at the far end of the Temple, where the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant would be placed.
This inner sanctuary was 30 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 30 feet high. He overlaid the inside with solid gold. He also overlaid the altar made of cedar.
Then Shalumah overlaid the rest of the Temple’s interior with solid gold, and he made gold chains to protect the entrance to the Most Qadash Place.
So he finished overlaying the entire Temple with gold, including the altar that belonged to the Most Qadash Place.
He made two charubim of wild olive wood, each 15 feet tall, and placed them in the inner sanctuary.
The wingspan of each of the charubim was 15 feet, each wing being 7 1⁄2 feet long.
The two charubim were identical in shape and size;
each was 15 feet tall.
He placed them side by side in the inner sanctuary of the Temple. Their outspread wings reached from wall to wall, while their inner wings touched at the center of the room.
He overlaid the two charubim with gold.
He decorated all the walls of the inner sanctuary and the main room with carvings of charubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
He overlaid the floor in both rooms with gold.
For the entrance to the inner sanctuary, he made double doors of wild olive wood with five-sided doorposts.
These double doors were decorated with carvings of charubim, palm trees, and open flowers. The doors, including the decorations of charubim and palm trees, were overlaid with gold.
Then he made four-sided doorposts of wild olive wood for the entrance to the Temple.
There were two folding doors of cypress wood, and each door was hinged to fold back upon itself.
These doors were decorated with carvings of charubim, palm trees, and open flowers, all overlaid evenly with gold.
The walls of the inner courtyard were built so that there was one layer of cedar beams between every three layers of finished stone.
The foundation of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple was laid in midspring, during the fourth year of Shalumah’s reign.
The entire building was completed in every detail by midautumn, during the eleventh year of his reign. So it took seven years to build the Temple.
King Shalumah also built a palace for himself, and it took him thirteen years to complete the construction.

One of Shalumah’s buildings was called the Palace of the Forest of Labanun. It was 150 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 45 feet high. There were four rows of cedar pillars, and great cedar beams rested on the pillars.
The hall had a cedar roof. Above the beams on the pillars were forty-five side rooms, arranged in three tiers of fifteen each.
On each end of the long hall were three rows of windows facing each other.
All the doorways and doorposts had rectangular frames and were arranged in sets of three, facing each other.
Shalumah also built the Hall of Pillars, which was 75 feet long and 45 feet wide. There was a porch in front, along with a canopy supported by pillars.
Shalumah also built the throne room, known as the Hall of Justice, where he sat to hear legal matters. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
Shalumah’s living quarters surrounded a courtyard behind this hall, and they were constructed the same way. He also built similar living quarters for Phar'uh’s daughter, whom he had married.
From foundation to eaves, all these buildings were built from huge blocks of high-quality stone, cut with saws and trimmed to exact measure on all sides.
Some of the huge foundation stones were 15 feet long, and some were 12 feet long.
The blocks of high-quality stone used in the walls were also cut to measure, and cedar beams were also used.

The walls of the great courtyard were built so that there was one layer of cedar beams between every three layers of finished stone, just like the walls of the inner courtyard of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple with its entry room.
King Shalumah then asked for a man named Huram to come from Tyra.

He was half Yasharalym, since his mother was a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father had been a craftsman in bronze from Tyra. Huram was extremely skillful and talented in any work in bronze, and he came to do all the metal work for King Shalumah.
Huram cast two bronze pillars, each 27 feet tall and 18 feet in circumference.
For the tops of the pillars he cast bronze capitals, each 7 1⁄2 feet tall.
Each capital was decorated with seven sets of latticework and interwoven chains.
He also encircled the latticework with two rows of pomegranates to decorate the capitals over the pillars.
The capitals on the columns inside the entry room were shaped like water lilies, and they were six feet tall.
The capitals on the two pillars had 200 pomegranates in two rows around them, beside the rounded surface next to the latticework.
Huram set the pillars at the entrance of the Temple, one toward the south and one toward the north, he named the one on the south Yakin, and the one on the north Buaz.
The capitals on the pillars were shaped like water lilies. And so the work on the pillars was finished.
Then Huram cast a great round basin, 15 feet across from rim to rim, called the Sea. It was 7 1⁄2 feet deep and about 45 feet in circumference.
It was encircled just below its rim by two rows of decorative gourds. There were about six gourds per foot all the way around, and they were cast as part of the basin.
The Sea was placed on a base of twelve bronze oxen, all facing outward. Three faced north, three faced west, three faced south, and three faced east, and the Sea rested on them.
The walls of the Sea were about three inches thick, and its rim flared out like a cup and resembled a water lily blossom. It could hold about 11,000 gallons of water.
Huram also made ten bronze water carts, each 6 feet long, 6 feet wide, and 4 1⁄2 feet tall.
They were constructed with side panels braced with crossbars.
Both the panels and the crossbars were decorated with carved lions, oxen, and charubim. Above and below the lions and oxen were wreath decorations.

Each of these carts had four bronze wheels and bronze axles. There were supporting posts for the bronze basins at the corners of the carts; these supports were decorated on each side with carvings of wreaths.

The top of each cart had a rounded frame for the basin. It projected 1 1⁄2 feet above the cart’s top like a round pedestal, and its opening was 2 1⁄4 feet across; it was decorated on the outside with carvings of wreaths. The panels of the carts were square, not round.
Under the panels were four wheels that were connected to axles that had been cast as one unit with the cart. The wheels were 2 1⁄4 feet in diameter
and were similar to chariot wheels. The axles, spokes, rims, and hubs were all cast from molten bronze.
There were handles at each of the four corners of the carts, and these, too, were cast as one unit with the cart.
Around the top of each cart was a rim nine inches wide. The corner supports and side panels were cast as one unit with the cart.
Carvings of charubim, lions, and palm trees decorated the panels and corner supports wherever there was room, and there were wreaths all around.
All ten water carts were the same size and were made alike, for each was cast from the same mold.
Huram also made ten smaller bronze basins, one for each cart. Each basin was six feet across and could hold 220 gallons of water.
He set five water carts on the south side of the Temple and five on the north side. The great bronze basin called the Sea was placed near the southeast corner of the Temple.
He also made the necessary washbasins, shovels, and bowls. So at last Huram completed everything King Shalumah had assigned him to make for the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH:
the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two networks of interwoven chains that decorated the capitals;
the 400 pomegranates that hung from the chains on the capitals (two rows of pomegranates for each of the chain networks that decorated the capitals on top of the pillars);
the ten water carts holding the ten basins;
the Sea and the twelve oxen under it;
the ash buckets, the shovels, and the bowls. Huram made all these things of burnished bronze for the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, just as King Shalumah had directed.
The king had them cast in clay molds in the Yurdan Valley between Succuth and Zarathan.
Shalumah did not weigh all these things because there were so many; the weight of the bronze could not be measured.
Shalumah also made all the furnishings of the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: the gold altar; the gold table for the Bread of the Presence;
the lampstands of solid gold, five on the south and five on the north, in front of the Most Qadash Place; the flower decorations, lamps, and tongs, all of gold;

the small bowls, lamp snuffers, bowls, ladles, and incense burners, all of solid gold; the doors for the entrances to the Most Qadash Place and the main room of the Temple, with their fronts overlaid with gold.

So King Shalumah finished all his work on the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then he brought all the gifts his father, Daud, had dedicated, the silver, the gold, and the various articles, and he stored them in the treasuries of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple.

King Shalumah then summoned to Yahushalam the elders of Yashar'AL and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral families of the Yasharalym. They were to bring the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant to the Temple from its location in the City of Daud, also known as Ziun.
So all the men of Yashar'AL assembled before King Shalumah at the annual Festival of Shelters, which is held in early autumn.
When all the elders of Yashar'AL arrived, the Kuhanym picked up the Ark.
The Kuhanym and Lauym brought up the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH along with the special tent and all the sacred items that had been in it.
There, before the Ark, King Shalumah and the entire community of Yashar'AL sacrificed so many sheep, goats, and cattle that no one could keep count!
Then the Kuhanym carried the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Covenant into the inner sanctuary of the Temple the Most Qadash Place, and placed it beneath the wings of the charubim.
The charubim spread their wings over the Ark, forming a canopy over the Ark and its carrying poles.
These poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Qadash Place, which is in front of the Most Qadash Place, but not from the outside. They are still there to this day.
Nothing was in the Ark except the two stone tablets that Musha had placed in it at Mount Sinai, where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made a covenant with the children of Yashar'AL when they left the land of Mitzraym.
When the Kuhanym came out of the Qadash Place, a thick cloud filled the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The Kuhanym could not continue their service because of the cloud, for the Kabad presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH filled the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then Shalumah prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you have said that you would live in a thick cloud of darkness.
Now I have built a Qadash Temple for you, a place where you can live forever!”
Then the king turned around to the entire community of Yashar'AL standing before him and gave this Barakah:
“Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, who has kept the promise he made to my father Daud. For he told my father,

‘From the day I brought my people Yashar'AL out of Mitzraym, I have never chosen a city among any of the tribes of Yashar'AL as the place where a Temple should be built to honor my name. But I have chosen Daud to be king over my people Yashar'AL.’”
Then Shalumah said, “My father Daud, wanted to build this Temple to honor the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told him, ‘You wanted to build the Temple to honor my Name. Your intention is good,
but you are not the one to do it. One of your own sons will build the Temple to honor me.’

“And now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has fulfilled the promise he made, for I have become king in my father’s place, and now I sit on the throne of Yashar'AL, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH promised, I have built this Temple to honor the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
And I have prepared a place there for the Ark, which contains the covenant that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made with our ancestors when he brought them out of Mitzraym.”
Then Shalumah stood before the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in front of the entire community of Yashar'AL. He lifted his hands toward Shamaym,

and he prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you are the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, there is no 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH like you in all of Shamaym above or on the Arath below. You keep your covenant and show unfailing love to all who walk before you in wholehearted devotion.
You have kept your promise to your servant Daud, my father. You made that promise with your own mouth, and with your own hands you have fulfilled it today.

And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, carry out the additional promise you made to your servant Daud, my father. For you said to him, ‘If your descendants guard their behavior and faithfully follow me as you have done, one of them will always sit on the throne of Yashar'AL.’
Now, O 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, fulfill this promise to your servant Daud, my father.
“But will 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH really live on Arath? Why, even the highest Shamaym cannot contain you. How much less this Temple I have built!
Nevertheless, listen to my prayer and my plea, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Hear the cry and the prayer that your servant is making to you today.
May you watch over this Temple night and day, this place where you have said, ‘My Name will be there.’ May you always hear the prayers I make toward this place.
May you hear the humble and earnest requests from me and your people Yashar'AL when we pray toward this place. Yes, hear us from Shamaym where you live, and when you hear, forgive.
“If someone wrongs another person and is required to take an oath of innocence in front of your altar in this Haykal (Temple),
then hear from Shamaym and judge between your servants, the accuser and the accused. Punish the guilty as they deserve, and Acquit the innocent because of their innocence.
“If your people Yashar'AL are defeated by their enemies because they have sinned against you, and if they turn to you and acknowledge your name and pray to you here in this Temple,
then hear from Shamaym and forgive the sin of your people Yashar'AL and return them to this land you gave their ancestors.

“If the skies are shut up and there is no rain because your people have sinned against you, and if they pray toward this Temple and acknowledge your Name and turn from their sins because you have punished them,

then hear from Shamaym and forgive the sins of your servants, your people Yashar'AL. Teach them to follow the right path, and send rain on your land that you have given to your people as their special possession.

“If there is a famine in the land or a plague or crop disease or attacks of locusts or caterpillars, or if the enemies of your people are in the land besieging their towns, whatever disaster or disease there is,
and if your people Yashar'AL pray about their troubles, raising their hands toward this Temple,
then hear from Shamaym where you live, and forgive. Give your people what their actions deserve, for you alone knows the heart of each man.
Then they will fear you as long as they live in the land you gave to our ancestors.
“In the future, foreigners who do not belong to your people Yashar'AL will hear of you. They will come from distant lands because of your Name,
for they will hear of your great Name and your strong hand and your powerful arm. And when they pray toward this Temple,

then hear from Shamaym where you live, and grant what they ask of you. In this way, all the people of the Arath will come to know and fear you, just as your own people Yashar'AL do. They too, will know that this Temple I have built, honors your name.
“If your people go out where you send them to fight their enemies, and if they pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by turning toward this city you have chosen and toward this Temple I have built to honor your Name,
then hear their prayers from Shamaym and uphold their cause.
“If they sin against You and who has never sinned? you might become angry with them and let their enemies conquer them and take them captive to their land far away or near.
But in that land of exile, they might turn to you in repentance and pray, ‘We have sinned, done evil, and acted wickedly.’

If they turn to you with their whole heart and soul in the land of their enemies and pray toward the land you gave to their ancestors, toward this city you have chosen, and toward this Temple I have built to honor your name,
then hear their prayers and their petition from Shamaym where you live, and uphold their cause.
Forgive your people who have sinned against you. Forgive all the offenses they have committed against you. Make their captors merciful to them,
for they are your people, your special possession whom you brought out of the iron-smelting furnace of Mitzraym.
“May your eyes be open to my requests and to the requests of your people Yashar'AL. May you hear and answer them whenever they cry out to you.

For when you brought our ancestors out of Mitzraym, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, you told your servant Musha that you had set Yashar'AL apart from all the nations of the Arath to be your own special possession.”
When Shalumah finished making these prayers and petitions to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he stood up in front of the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, where he had been kneeling with his hands raised toward Shamaym.
He stood and in a loud voice Baraked the entire congregation of Yashar'AL:
“Yadah (Praise) 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who has given rest to his people Yashar'AL, just as he promised. Not one word has failed of all the wonderful promises he gave through his servant Musha.
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be with us as he was with our ancestors; may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH never leave us or abandon us.
May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH give us the desire to do His will in everything and to obey all the commandments, decrees, and regulations that He gave our ancestors.

And may these words that I have prayed in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH be before him constantly day and night, so that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH may give justice to me and to his people Yashar'AL, according to each day’s needs.
Then people all over the Arath will know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH alone is 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and there is no other.
And may you be completely faithful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. May you always obey his decrees and commands, just as you are doing today.”
Then the king and all Yashar'AL with him offered sacrifices to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Shalumah offered to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH a Shalum offering of 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep and goats. And so the king and all the people of Yashar'AL dedicated the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

That same day the king consecrated the central area of the courtyard in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple. He offered burnt offerings, grain offerings, and the fat of Shalum offerings there, because the bronze altar in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s presence was too small to hold all the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and the fat of the Shalum offerings.

Then Shalumah and all Yashar'AL celebrated the Festival of Shelters in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. A large congregation had gathered from as far away as Labu-hamath in the north and the Brook of Mitzraym in the south. The celebration went on for fourteen days in all, seven days for the dedication of the altar and seven days for the Festival of Shelters.

After the festival was over, Shalumah sent the people home. They Baraked the king and went to their homes joyful and glad because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had been good to his servant Daud and to his people Yashar'AL.
So Shalumah finished building the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as well as the royal palace. He completed everything he had planned to do.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared to Shalumah a second time, as he had done before at Gibaun.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Shalumah, “I have heard your prayer and your petition. I have set this Temple apart to be Qadash, this place you have built where my Name will be honored forever. I will always watch over it, for it is dear to my heart.
“As for you, if you will follow me with integrity and righteousness, as Daud your father did, obeying all my commandments, decrees, and regulations,
then I will establish the throne of your dynasty over Yashar'AL forever. For I made this promise to your father, Daud: ‘One of your descendants will always sit on the throne of Yashar'AL.’
“But if you or your descendants abandon me and disobey the commandments and decrees I have given you, and if you serve and worship other nations pagan idols,

then I will uproot Yashar'AL from this land that I have given them. I will reject this Temple that I have made Qadash to honor my Name. I will make Yashar'AL an object of mockery and ridicule among the nations.
And though this Temple is impressive now, all who pass by will be appalled and will gasp in horror. They will ask, ‘Why did 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH do such terrible things to this land and to this Temple?’

“And the answer will be, ‘Because his people abandoned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who brought their ancestors out of Mitzraym, and they worshiped other nations idols instead and bowed down to them. That is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought all these disasters on them.’”
It took Shalumah twenty years to build 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple and his own royal palace. At the end of that time,
he gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to King Hiram of Tyra. (Hiram had previously provided all the cedar and cypress timber and gold that Shalumah had requested.)
But when Hiram came from Tyra to see the towns Shalumah had given him, he was not at all pleased with them.
“What kind of towns are these, my brother? he asked. So Hiram called that area Cabul (which means “worthless”), as it is still known today.
Nevertheless, Hiram paid Shalumah 9,000 pounds of gold.

This is the account of the forced labor that King Shalumah conscripted to build 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple, the royal palace, the supporting terraces, the wall of Yahushalam, and the cities of Hazur, Magiddu, and Gazar.

(Phar'uh, the king of Mitzraym, had attacked and captured Gazar, killing the Canaanite population and burning it down, Phar'uh gave the city to his daughter as a wedding gift when she married Shalumah.
So Shalumah rebuilt the city of Gazar.) He also built up the towns of Lower Bath-hurun,
Baalath, and Tamar in the wilderness within his land.
He built towns as supply centers and constructed towns where his chariots and horses could be stationed, he built everything he desired in Yahushalam and Labanun and throughout his entire realm.
There were still some people living in the land who were not Yasharalym, including Amurites, Hittites, Parizzites, Hibites, and Yabusites.
These were descendants of the nations whom the people of Yashar'AL had not completely destroyed. So Shalumah conscripted them as slaves, and they serve as forced laborers to this day.

But Shalumah did not conscript any of the Yasharalym for forced labor. Instead, he assigned them to serve as fighting men, government officials, officers and captains in his army, commanders of his chariots, and charioteers.
Shalumah appointed 550 of them to supervise the people working on his various projects.
Shalumah moved his wife, Phar'uh’s daughter, from the City of Daud to the new palace he had built for her. Then he constructed the supporting terraces.

Three times each year Shalumah presented burnt offerings and Shalum offerings on the altar he had built for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he also burned incense to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And so he finished the work of building the Temple.
King Shalumah also built a fleet of ships at Aziun-gabar, a port near Alath in the land of Adum, along the shore of the Red Sea.
Hiram sent experienced crews of sailors to sail the ships with Shalumah’s men.
They sailed to Uphir and brought back to Shalumah some sixteen tons of gold.
When the queen of Shaba heard of Shalumah’s fame, which brought honor to the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, she came to test him with hard questions.

She arrived in Yahushalam with a large group of attendants and a great caravan of camels loaded with spices, large quantities of gold, and precious jewels. When she met with Shalumah, she talked with him about everything she had on her mind.
Shalumah had answers for all her questions; nothing was too hard for the king to explain to her.
When the queen of Shaba realized how very wise Shalumah was, and when she saw the palace he had built,

she was overwhelmed. She was also amazed at the food on his tables, the organization of his officials and their splendid clothing, the cup-bearers, and the burnt offerings Shalumah made at the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
She exclaimed to the king, “Everything I heard in my country about your achievements and wisdom is true!
I did not believe what was said until I arrived here and saw it with my own eyes. In fact, I had not heard the half of it! Your wisdom and prosperity are far beyond what I was told.
How happy your people must be! What a privilege for your officials to stand here day after day, listening to your wisdom!

Yadah (Praise) 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who delights in you and has placed you on the throne of Yashar'AL. Because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s eternal love for Yashar'AL, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has made you king so you can rule with justice and righteousness.”
Then she gave the king a gift of 9,000 pounds of gold, great quantities of spices, and precious jewels. Never again were so many spices brought in as those the queen of Shaba gave to King Shalumah.
(In addition, Hiram’s ships brought gold from Uphir, and they also brought rich cargoes of red sandalwood and precious jewels.

The king used the sandalwood to make railings for the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the royal palace, and to construct lyres and harps for the musicians. Never before or since has there been such a supply of sandalwood.)
King Shalumah gave the queen of Shaba whatever she asked for, besides all the customary gifts he had so generously given. Then she and all her attendants returned to their own land.
Each year Shalumah received about 25 tons of gold.
This did not include the additional revenue he received from merchants and traders, all the kings of Arabia, and the governors of the land.
King Shalumah made 200 large shields of hammered gold, each weighing more than fifteen pounds.
He also made 300 smaller shields of hammered gold, each weighing nearly four pounds. The king placed these shields in the Palace of the Forest of Labanun.
Then the king made a huge throne, decorated with ivory and overlaid with fine gold.
The throne had six steps and a rounded back. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, and the figure of a lion stood on each side of the throne.
There were also twelve other lions, one standing on each end of the six steps. No other throne in all the world could be compared with it!
