All of King Shalumah’s drinking cups were solid gold, as were all the utensils in the Palace of the Forest of Labanun. They were not made of silver, for silver was considered worthless in Shalumah’s day!
The king had a fleet of trading ships of Tarshish that sailed with Hiram’s fleet. Once every three years the ships returned, loaded with gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
So King Shalumah became richer and wiser than any other king on Arath.
People from every nation came to consult him and to hear the wisdom 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had given him.
Year after year everyone who visited brought him gifts of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
Shalumah built up a huge force of chariots and horses, he had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, he stationed some of them in the chariot cities and some near him in Yahushalam.
The king made silver as plentiful in Yahushalam as stone. And valuable cedar timber was as common as the sycamore-fig trees that grow in the foothills of Yahudah.
Shalumah’s horses were imported from Mitzraym and from Cilicia; the king’s traders acquired them from Cilicia at the standard price.
At that time chariots from Mitzraym could be purchased for 600 pieces of silver, and horses for 150 pieces of silver. They were then exported to the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
Now King Shalumah loved many foreign women. Besides Phar'uh’s daughter, he married women from Muab, Ammun, Adum, Sidun, and from among the Hittites.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had clearly instructed the people of Yashar'AL, “You must not marry them, because they will turn your hearts to their nations pagan idols.” Yet Shalumah insisted on loving them anyway.
He had 700 wives of royal birth and 300 concubines. And in fact, they did turn his heart away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
In Shalumah's old age, they turned his heart to worship their nations idols instead of being completely faithful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, as his father Daud, had been.
Shalumah worshiped Ashturath, the female idol of the Sidunians, and Mulach, the detestable idol of the Ammunites.
In this way, Shalumah did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; he refused to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH completely, as his father Daud, had done.
On the Mount of Olives, east of Yahushalam, Shalumah even built a pagan shrine for Chamush, the detestable idol of Muab, and another for Mulach, the detestable idol of the Ammunites.
Shalumah built such shrines for all his foreign wives to use for burning incense and sacrificing to their idols.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was very angry with Shalumah, for his heart had turned away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, who had appeared to him twice.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had warned Shalumah specifically about worshiping other nations pagan idols, but Shalumah did not listen to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command.
So now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Shalumah, “Since you have not kept my covenant and have disobeyed my decrees, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to one of your servants.
But for the sake of your father Daud, I will not do this while you are still alive. I will take the kingdom away from your son.
And even so, I will not take away the entire kingdom; I will let him be king of one tribe, for the sake of my servant Daud and for the sake of Yahushalam, my chosen city.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised up Hadad the Adumite, a member of Adum’s royal family, to be Shalumah’s adversary.
Years before, Daud had defeated Adum. Yuab, his army commander, had stayed to bury some of the Yasharalym soldiers who had died in battle. While there, they killed every male in Adum.
Yuab and the army of Yashar'AL had stayed there for six months, killing them.
But Hadad and a few of his father’s royal officials escaped and headed for Mitzraym. (Hadad was just a boy at the time.)
They set out from Midian and went to Paran, where others joined them. Then they traveled to Mitzraym and went to Phar'uh, who gave them a home, food, and some land.
Phar'uh grew very fond of Hadad, and he gave him his wife’s sister in marriage, the sister of Queen Tahpanas.
She bore him a son named Ganubath. Tahpanas raised him in Phar'uh’s palace among Phar'uh’s own sons.
When the news reached Hadad in Mitzraym that Daud and his commander Yuab were both dead, he said to Phar'uh, “Let me return to my own country.”
“Why?” Phar'uh asked him. “What do you lack here that makes you want to go home?” “Nothing,” he replied. “But even so, please let me return home.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH also raised up Razun son of Aliada as Shalumah’s adversary. Razun had fled from his master, King Hadadazar of Zubah,
and had become the leader of a gang of rebels. After Daud conquered Hadadazar, Razun and his men fled to Damascus, where he became king.
Razun was Yashar'AL’s bitter adversary for the rest of Shalumah reign, and he made trouble, just as Hadad did. Razun hated Yashar'AL intensely and continued to reign in Aram.
Another rebel leader was Yarubuam son of Nabat, one of Shalumah’s own officials, he came from the town of Zaradah in Aphraim, and his mother was Zaruah, a widow.
This is the story behind his rebellion. Shalumah was rebuilding the supporting terraces and repairing the walls of the city of his father, Daud.
Yarubuam was a very capable young man, and when Shalumah saw how industrious he was, he put him in charge of the labor force from the tribes of Aphraim and Manasseh, the descendants of Ya'asaf.
One day as Yarubuam was leaving Yahushalam, the Nabym Ahiyahu from Shiluh met him along the way. Ahiyahu was wearing a new cloak. The two of them were alone in a field,
and Ahiyahu took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.

Then he said to Yarubuam, “Take ten of these pieces, for this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, says: ‘I am about to tear the kingdom from the hand of Shalumah, and I will give ten of the tribes to you!
But I will leave him one tribe for the sake of my servant Daud and for the sake of Yahushalam, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Yashar'AL.

For Shalumah has abandoned me and worshiped Ashturath, the female calve idol of the Sidunians; Chamush, the idol of Muab; and Mulach, the idol of the Ammunites. Shalumah has not followed my ways and done what is pleasing in my sight, he has not obeyed my decrees and regulations as Daud his father did.

“‘But I will not take the entire kingdom from Shalumah at this time. For the sake of my servant Daud, the one whom I chose and who obeyed my commands and decrees, I will keep Shalumah as leader for the rest of his life.
But I will take the kingdom away from his son and give ten of the tribes to you.
His son will have one tribe so that the descendants of Daud my servant will continue to reign, shining like a lamp in Yahushalam, the city I have chosen to be the place for my Name.
And I will place you on the throne of Yashar'AL, and you will rule over all that your heart desires.

If you listen to what I tell you and follow my ways and do whatever I consider to be right, and if you obey my decrees and commands, as my servant Daud did, then I will always be with you. I will establish an enduring dynasty for you as I did for Daud, and I will give Yashar'AL to you.
Because of Shalumah’s sin I will punish the descendants of Daud, though not forever.’”
Shalumah tried to kill Yarubuam, but he fled to King Shishak of Mitzraym and stayed there until Shalumah died.
The rest of the events in Shalumah’s reign, including all his deeds and his wisdom, are recorded in The Book of the Acts of Shalumah.
Shalumah ruled in Yahushalam over all Yashar'AL for forty years.
When he died, he was buried in the City of Daud his father. Then his son Rahubuam became the next king.
Rahubuam went to Shacham, where all Yashar'AL had gathered to make him king.
When Yarubuam son of Nabat heard of this, he returned from Mitzraym, for he had fled to Mitzraym to escape from King Shalumah.
The leaders of Yashar'AL summoned him, and Yarubuam and the whole assembly of Yashar'AL went to speak with Rahubuam.
“Your father was a hard master,” they said. “Lighten the harsh labor demands and heavy taxes that your father imposed on us. Then we will be your loyal subjects.”
Rahubuam replied, “Give me three days to think this over. Then come back for my answer.” So the people went away.
Then King Rahubuam discussed the matter with the older men who had counseled his father, Shalumah. And he asked them “What is your advice? “How should I answer these people?”
The older counselors replied, “If you are willing to be a servant to these people today and give them a favorable answer, they will always be your loyal subjects.”
But Rahubuam rejected the advice of the older men and instead asked the opinion of the young men who had grown up with him and were now his advisers.
“And he asked them; What is your advice? “How should I answer these people who want me to lighten the burdens imposed by my father?”
The young men replied, “This is what you should tell those complainers who want a lighter burden: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
Yes, my father laid heavy burdens on you, but I am going to make them even heavier! My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions!’”
Three days later Yarubuam and all the people returned to hear Rahubuam’s decision, just as the king had ordered.
But Rahubuam spoke harshly to the people, for he rejected the advice of the older counselors

and followed the counsel of his younger advisers, he told the people, “My father laid heavy burdens on you, but I’m going to make them even heavier! My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions!”

So the king paid no attention to the people. This turn of events was the will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for it fulfilled the message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to Yarubuam son of Nabat through the Nabym (prophet) Ahiyahu from Shiluh.

When all Yashar'AL realized that the king had refused to listen to them, they responded, “Down with the dynasty of Daud! We have no interest in the son of Yassa. Back to your homes, O Yashar'AL! Look out for your own house, So the people of Yashar'AL returned home.
But Rahubuam continued to rule over the Yasharalym who lived in the towns of Yahudah.

King Rahubuam sent Aduniram, who was in charge of forced labor, to restore order, but the people of Yashar'AL stoned him to death. When this news reached King Rahubuam, he quickly jumped into his chariot and fled to Yahushalam.
And to this day the northern tribes of Yashar'AL have refused to be ruled by a descendant of Daud.

When the people of Yashar'AL learned of Yarubuam’s return from Mitzraym, they called an assembly and made him king over all Yashar'AL. So only the tribe of Yahudah remained loyal to the family of Daud.
When Rahubuam arrived at Yahushalam, he mobilized the men of Yahudah and the tribe of Banyamin 180,000 select troops—to fight against the men of Yashar'AL and to restore the kingdom to himself.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Shamayahu, the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
“Say to Rahubuam son of Shalumah, king of Yahudah, and to all the people of Yahudah and Banyamin, and to the rest of the people,

‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Do not fight against your relatives, the Yasharalym. Go back home, for what has happened is my doing!’” So they obeyed the message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and went home, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded.
Yarubuam then built up the city of Shacham in the hill country of Aphraim, and it became his capital. Later he went and built up the town of Panial.
Yarubuam thought to himself, “Unless I am careful, the kingdom will return to the dynasty of Daud.

When these people go to Yahushalam to offer sacrifices at the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they will again give their allegiance to King Rahubuam of Yahudah. They will kill me and make him their king instead.”

So on the advice of his counselors, the king made two gold calves, and he said to the people, “It is too much trouble for you to worship in Yahushalam. Look, O Yashar'AL, these are the idols who brought you out of Mitzraym!”
Yarubuam placed these calf idols in Bathal and in Dan, at either end of his kingdom.
But this became a great sin, for the people worshiped the idols, traveling as far north as Dan to worship the one there.
Yarubuam also erected buildings at the pagan shrines and ordained priests from the common people, those who were not from the Kuhanym (priestly) tribe of Lauym.

And Yarubuam instituted a religious festival in Bathal, held on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in imitation of the annual Festival of Shelters in Yahudah. There at Bathal he himself offered sacrifices to the calves idols he had made, and he appointed priests for the pagan shrines he had made.

So on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a day that he himself had designated, Yarubuam offered sacrifices on the altar at Bathal, he instituted a religious festival for Yashar'AL, and he went up to the altar to burn incense.
At 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command, a servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH from Yahudah went to Bathal, arriving there just as Yarubuam was approaching the altar to burn incense.

Then at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command, he shouted, “O altar, altar! This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: A child named Yusyahu will be born into the dynasty of Daud. On you he will sacrifice the priests from the pagan shrines who come here to burn incense, and men's bone will be burned.”

That same day the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH gave a sign to prove his message, he said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has promised to give this sign: This altar will split apart, and its ashes will be poured out on the ground.”

When King Yarubuam heard the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH speaking against the altar at Bathal, he pointed at him and shouted, “Seize that man!” But instantly the king’s hand became paralyzed in that position, and he couldn’t pull it back.
At the same time a wide crack appeared in the altar, and the ashes poured out, just as the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had predicted in his message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

The king cried out to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, “Please ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH to restore my hand again!” So the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the king’s hand was restored and he could move it again.
Then the king said to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, “Come to the palace with me and have something to eat, and I will give you a gift.”
But the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said to the king, “Even if you gave me half of everything you own, I would not go with you. I would not eat or drink anything in this place.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave me this command: ‘You must not eat or drink anything while you are there, and do not return to Yahudah by the same way you came.’”
So he left Bathal and went home another way.

As it happened, there was an old Nabym (prophet) living in Bathal, and his sons came home and told him what the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had done in Bathal that day. They also told their father what the man had said to the king.
The old Nabym asked them, “Which way did he go?” So they showed their father which road the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had taken.
“Quick, saddle the donkey,” the old man said. So they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.
Then he rode after the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and found him sitting under a great tree. The old Nabym asked him, “Are you the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who came from Yahudah? “Yes, I am,” he replied.
Then he said to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, “Come home with me and eat some food.”
“He replied, No I cannot, “I am not allowed to eat or drink anything here in this place.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave me this command: ‘You must not eat or drink anything while you are there, and do not return to Yahudah by the same way you came.’”

But the old Nabym answered, “I am a Nabym too, just as you are. And a Malak gave me this command from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘Bring him home with you so he can have something to eat and drink.’” But the old man was lying to him.
So they went back together, and the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH ate and drank at the Nabym’s home.
Then while they were sitting at the table, a command from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to the old Nabym.
He cried out to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH from Yahudah, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says: You have defied the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and have disobeyed the command 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH gave you.
You came back to this place and ate and drank where he told you not to eat or drink. Because of this, your body will not be buried in the grave of your ancestors.”
After the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had finished eating and drinking, the old Nabym saddled his own donkey for him,
and the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH started off again. But as he was traveling along, a lion came out and killed him, his body lay there on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it.
People who passed by saw the body lying in the road and the lion standing beside it, and they went and reported it in Bathal, where the old Nabym lived.
When the Nabym heard the report, he said, “It is the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who disobeyed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has fulfilled his word by causing the lion to attack and kill him.”
Then the Nabym said to his sons, “Saddle a donkey for me.” So they saddled a donkey,
and he went out and found the body lying in the road. The donkey and lion were still standing there beside it, for the lion had not eaten the body nor attacked the donkey.
So the Nabym laid the body of the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH on the donkey and took it back to the town to mourn over him and bury him.
He laid the body in his own grave, crying out in grief, “Oh, my brother!”
Afterward the Nabym said to his sons, “When I die, bury me in the grave where the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.
For the message 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told him to proclaim against the altar in Bathal and against the pagan shrines in the towns of Samaria will certainly come true.”
But even after this, Yarubuam did not turn from his evil ways, he continued to choose priests from the common people, he appointed anyone who wanted to become a priest for the pagan shrines.
This became a great sin and resulted in the utter destruction of Yarybuam’s dynasty from the face of the Arath.
At that time Yarubuam’s son Abiyahu became very sick.
So Yarubuam told his wife, “Disguise yourself so that no one will recognize you as my wife. Then go to the Nabym Ahiyahu at Shiluh, the man who told me I would become king.
Take him a gift of ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and ask him what will happen to the boy.”
So Yarubuam’s wife went to Ahiyahu’s home at Shiluh, he was an old man now and could no longer see.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had told Ahiyahu, Yarubuam’s wife will come here, pretending to be someone else. She will ask you about her son, for he is very sick. Give her the answer I give you.”
So when Ahiyahu heard her footsteps at the door, he called out, “Come in, wife of Yarubuam! Why are you pretending to be someone else?” Then he told her, “I have bad news for you.
Give your husband, Yarubuam, this message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL: ‘I promoted you from the ranks of the common man and made you ruler over my people Yashar'AL.

I ripped the kingdom away from the family of Daud and gave it to you. But you have not been like my servant Daud, who obeyed my commands and followed me with all his heart and always did whatever I wanted.
You have done more evil than all who lived before you. You have made other nations pagan idols for yourself and have made me furious with your gold calves. And since you have turned your back on me,

I will bring disaster on your dynasty and will destroy every one of your male descendants, slave and free alike, anywhere in Yashar'AL. I will burn up your royal dynasty as one burns up trash until it is all gone.
The members of Yarubuam’s family who die in the city will be eaten by dogs, and those who die in the field will be eaten by vultures. I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, have spoken.’
Then Ahiyahu said to Yarubuam’s wife, “Go on home, and when you enter the city, the child will die.

All Yashar'AL will mourn for him and bury him, he is the only member of your family who will have a proper burial, for this child is the only good thing that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, sees in the entire family of Yarubuam.
“In addition, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will raise up a king over Yashar'AL who will destroy the family of Yarubuam. This will happen today, even now!

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will shake Yashar'AL like a reed whipped about in a stream. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will uproot the people of Yashar'AL from this good land that he gave their ancestors and will scatter them beyond the Euphrates River, for they have angered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with the Asharah poles they have set up for worship.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will abandon Yashar'AL because Yarubuam sinned and made Yashar'AL sin along with him.”
So Yarubuam’s wife returned to Tirzah, and the child died just as she walked through the door of her home.
And all Yashar'AL buried him and mourned for him, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised through the Nabym Ahiyahu.
The rest of the events in Yarubuam’s reign, including all his wars and how he ruled, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
Yarubuam reigned in Yashar'AL twenty-two years. When Yarubuam died, his son Nadab became the next king.

Meanwhile, Rahubuam son of Shalumah was king in Yahudah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Yahushalam, the city 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had chosen from among all the tribes of Yashar'AL as the place to honor His Name. Rahubuam’s mother was Naamah, an Ammunite woman.
During Rahubuam’s reign, the people of Yahudah did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, provoking His anger with their sin, for it was even worse than that of their ancestors.
For they also built for themselves pagan shrines and set up sacred pillars and Asharah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
There were even male and female shrine prostitutes throughout the land. The people imitated the detestable practices of the pagan nations 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had driven from the land ahead of the Yasharalym.
In the fifth year of King Rahubuam’s reign, King Shishak of Mitzraym came up and attacked Yahushalam.
He ransacked the treasuries of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple and the royal palace; he stole everything, including all the gold shields Shalumah had made.
King Rahubuam later replaced them with bronze shields as substitutes, and he entrusted them to the care of the commanders of the guard who protected the entrance to the royal palace.
Whenever the king went to the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the guards would also take the shields and then return them to the guardroom.
The rest of the events in Rahubuam’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
There was constant war between Rahubuam and Yarubuam.
When Rahubuam died, he was buried among his ancestors in the City of Daud, his mother was Naamah, an Ammunite woman. Then his son Abiyam became the next king.
Abiyam began to rule over Yahudah in the eighteenth year of Yarubuam’s reign in Yashar'AL.
He reigned in Yahushalam three years, his mother was Maacah, the granddaughter of Absalum.
He committed the same sins as his father before him, and he was not faithful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, as his ancestor Daud had been.
But for Daud’s sake, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH allowed his descendants to continue ruling, shining like a lamp, and he gave Abiyam a son to rule after him in Yahushalam.
For Daud had done what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and had obeyed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s commands throughout his life, except in the affair concerning Uryahu the Hittite.
There was war between Abiyam and Yarubuam throughout Abiyam’s reign.
The rest of the events in Abiyam’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah. There was constant war between Abiyam and Yarubuam.
When Abiyam died, he was buried in the City of Daud. Then his son Asa became the next king.
Asa began to rule over Yahudah in the twentieth year of Yahrubuam’s reign in Yashar'AL.
Asa reigned in Yahushalam forty-one years. His grandmother was Maacah, the granddaughter of Absalum.
Asa did what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as his ancestor Daud had done.
He banished the male and female shrine prostitutes from the land and got rid of all the idols his ancestors had made.
He even deposed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made an obscene Asharah pole, he cut down her obscene pole and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
Although the pagan shrines were not removed, Asa’s heart remained completely faithful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH throughout his life.
He brought into the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the silver and gold and the various items that he and his father had dedicated.
There was constant war between King Asa of Yahudah and King Baasha of Yashar'AL.
King Baasha of Yashar'AL invaded Yahudah and fortified Ramah in order to prevent anyone from entering or leaving King Asa’s territory in Yahudah.

Asa responded by removing all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the royal palace, he sent it with some of his officials to Ban-hadad son of Tabrimmun, son of Haziun, the king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus, along with this message:

“Let there be a treaty between you and me like the one between your father and my father. See, I am sending you a gift of silver and gold. Break your treaty with King Baasha of Yashar'AL so that he will leave me alone.”

Ban-hadad agreed to King Asa’s request and sent the commanders of his army to attack the towns of Yashar'AL. They conquered the towns of Iyun, Dan, Abal-bath-maacah, and all Kinnarath, and all the land of Naphtali.
As soon as Baasha of Yashar'AL heard what was happening, he abandoned his project of fortifying Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.

Then King Asa sent an order throughout Yahudah, requiring that everyone, without exception, help to carry away the building stones and timbers that Baasha had been using to fortify Ramah. Asa used these materials to fortify the town of Gaba in Banyamin and the town of Mizpah.

The rest of the events in Asa’s reign, the extent of his power, everything he did, and the names of the cities he built, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah. In his old age his feet became diseased.
When Asa died, he was buried with his ancestors in the City of Daud. Then Yahushaphat, Asa’s son, became the next king.
Nadab son of Yarubuam began to rule over Yashar'AL in the second year of King Asa’s reign in Yahudah. He reigned in Yashar'AL two years.
But he did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and followed the example of his father, continuing the sins that Yarubuam had led Yashar'AL to commit.
Then Baasha son of Ahiyahu, from the tribe of Issachar, plotted against Nadab and assassinated him while he and the Yasharalym army were laying siege to the Philistine town of Gibbathun.
Baasha killed Nadab in the third year of King Asa’s reign in Yahudah, and he became the next king of Yashar'AL.
He immediately slaughtered all the descendants of King Yarubuam, so that not one of the royal family was left, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar concerning Yarubuam by the Nabym Ahiyahu from Shiluh.
This was done because Yarubuam had provoked the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, by the sins he had committed and the sins he had led Yashar'AL to commit.
The rest of the events in Nadab’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
There was constant war between King Asa of Yahudah and King Baasha of Yashar'AL.
Baasha son of Ahiyahu began to rule over all Yashar'AL in the third year of King Asa’s reign in Yahudah. Baasha reigned in Tirzah twenty-four years.
But he did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and followed the example of Yarubuam, continuing the sins that Yarubuam had led Yashar'AL to commit.
This message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was delivered to King Baasha by the Nabym (prophet) Yahu son of Hanani:
“I lifted you out of the dust to make you ruler of my people Yashar'AL, but you have followed the evil example of Yarubuam, you have provoked my anger by causing my people Yashar'AL to sin.
So now I will destroy you and your family, just as I destroyed the descendants of Yarubuam son of Nabat.
The members of Baasha’s family who die in the city will be eaten by dogs, and those who die in the field will be eaten by vultures.”
The rest of the events in Baasha’s reign and the extent of his power are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When Baasha died, he was buried in Tirzah. Then his son Alah became the next king.

The message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH against Baasha and his family came through the Nabym Yahu son of Hanani. It was delivered because Baasha had done what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH (just as the family of Yarubuam had done), and also because Baasha had destroyed the family of Yarubuam, the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was provoked by Baasha’s sins.
Alah son of Baasha began to rule over Yashar'AL in the twenty-sixth year of King Asa’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in the city of Tirzah for two years.
Then Zimri, who commanded half of the royal chariots, made plans to kill him. One day in Tirzah, Alah was getting drunk at the home of Arza, the supervisor of the palace.
Zimri walked in and struck him down and killed him. This happened in the twenty-seventh year of King Asa’s reign in Yahudah. Then Zimri became the next king.
Zimri immediately killed the entire royal family of Baasha, leaving him not even a single male child, he even destroyed distant relatives and friends.
So Zimri destroyed the dynasty of Baasha as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar through the Nabym Yahu.

This happened because of all the sins Baasha and his son Alah had committed, and because of the sins they led Yashar'AL to commit. They provoked the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, with their worthless idols.
The rest of the events in Alah’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.

Zimri began to rule over Yashar'AL in the twenty-seventh year of King Asa’s reign in Yahudah, but his reign in Tirzah lasted only seven days. The army of Yashar'AL was then attacking the Philistine town of Gibbathun.
When they heard that Zimri had committed treason and had assassinated the king, that very day they chose Umri, commander of the army, as the new king of Yashar'AL.
So Umri led the entire army of Yashar'AL up from Gibbathun to attack Tirzah, Yashar'AL’s capital.
When Zimri saw that the city had been taken, he went into the citadel of the palace and burned it down over himself and died in the flames.
For he, too, had done what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he followed the example of Yarubuam in all the sins he had committed and led Yashar'AL to commit.
The rest of the events in Zimri’s reign and his conspiracy are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
But now the people of Yashar'AL were split into two factions. Half the people tried to make Tibni son of Ginath their king, while the other half supported Umri.
But Umri’s supporters defeated the supporters of Tibni. So Tibni was killed, and Umri became the next king.
Umri began to rule over Yashar'AL in the thirty-first year of King Asa’s reign in Yahudah. He reigned twelve years in all, six of them in Tirzah.
Then Umri bought the hill now known as Samaria from its owner, Shamar, for one hundred and fifty pounds of silver. He built a city on it and called the city Samaria in honor of Shamar.
But Umri did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, even more than any of the kings before him.

He followed the example of Yarubuam son of Nabat in all the sins he had committed and led Yashar'AL to commit. The people provoked the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, with their worthless idols.
The rest of the events in Umri’s reign, the extent of his power, and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When Umri died, and he was buried in Samaria. Then his son Ahab became the next king.
Ahab son of Umri began to rule over Yashar'AL in the thirty-eighth year of King Asa’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria twenty-two years.
But Ahab son of Umri did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, even more than any of the kings before him.
And as though it were not enough to follow the sinful example of Yarubuam, he married Yazabaal, the daughter of King Athbaal of the Sidunians, and he began to bow down in worship of Baal.
First Ahab built a temple and an altar for Baal in Samaria.
Then he set up an Asharah pole, he did more to provoke the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, than any of the other kings of Yashar'AL before him.

It was during his reign that Hial, a man from Bathal, rebuilt Yarichu. When he laid its foundations, it cost him the life of his oldest son, Abiram. And when he completed it and set up its gates, it cost him the life of his youngest son, Sagub. This all happened according to the message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH concerning Yarichu spoken by Yahusha Ba'Nun (son of Nun).

Now AliYahu, who was from Tishba in Gilaad, told King Ahab, “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL lives, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH I serve, there will be no dew or rain during the next few years until I give the word!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to AliYahu,
“Go to the east and hide by Karith Brook, near where it enters the Yurdan River.
Drink from the brook and eat what the ravens bring you, for I have commanded them to bring you food.”
So AliYahu did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told him and camped beside Karith Brook, east of the Yurdan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat each morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.
But after a while the brook dried up, for there was no rainfall anywhere in the land.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to AliYahu,
“Go and live in the village of Zaraphath, near the city of Sidun. I have instructed a widow there to feed you.”
So he went to Zaraphath. As he arrived at the gates of the village, he saw a widow gathering sticks, and he asked her, “Would you please bring me a little water in a cup?”
As she was going to get it, he called to her, “Bring me a bite of bread, too.”

But she said, “I swear by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH that I do not have a single piece of bread in the house. And I have only a handful of flour left in the jar and a little cooking oil in the bottom of the jug. I was just gathering a few sticks to cook this last meal, and then my son and I will die.”
But AliYahu said to her, “Do not be afraid! Go ahead and do just what you have said, but make a little bread for me first, then use what is left to prepare a meal for yourself and your son.
For this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, says: There will always be flour and olive oil left in your containers until the time when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sends rain and the crops grow again!”
So she did as AliYahu said, and she and AliYahu and her family continued to eat for many days.
There was always enough flour and olive oil left in the containers, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said through AliYahu.
Some time later the woman’s son became sick, he grew worse and worse, and finally he died.
Then she said to AliYahu, “O servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, what have you done to me? Have you come here to point out my sins and kill my son?”
But AliYahu replied, “Give me your son.” And he took the child’s body from her arms, carried him up the stairs to the room where he was staying, and laid the body on his bed.
Then AliYahu cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, why have you brought tragedy to this widow who has opened her home to me, causing her son to die?”
And he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, please let this child’s life return to him.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH heard AliYahu’s prayer, and the life of the child returned, and he revived!
Then AliYahu brought him down from the upper room and gave him to his mother. “Look! “Your son is alive!”
Then the woman told AliYahu, “Now I know for sure that you are a servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH truly speaks through you.”
Later on, in the third year of the drought, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to AliYahu, “Go and present yourself to King Ahab, and tell him that I will soon send rain!”
So AliYahu went to appear before Ahab. Meanwhile, the famine had become very severe in Samaria.
So Ahab summoned Ubadyahu, who was in charge of the palace. (Ubadyahu was a devoted follower of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Once when Yazabaal had tried to kill all 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Nabym, Ubadyahu had hidden one hundred of them in two caves, he put fifty Nabym in each cave and supplied them with food and water.)
Ahab said to Ubadyahu, “We must check every spring and valley in the land to see if we can find enough grass to save at least some of my horses and mules.”
So they divided the land between them. Ahab went one way by himself, and Ubadyahu went another way by himself.
As Ubadyahu was walking along, he suddenly saw AliYahu coming toward him. Ubadyahu recognized him at once and bowed low to the ground before him. “Is it really you, my master AliYahu?” he asked.
“Yes, it is,” AliYahu replied. “Now go and tell your master Ahab, AliYahu is here.’”
“Oh, sir,” Ubadyahu protested, “what harm have I done to you that you are sending me to my death at the hands of Ahab?

For I swear by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH that the king has searched every nation and kingdom on Arath from end to end to find you. And each time he was told, AliYahu is not here,’ King Ahab forced the king of that nation to swear to the truth of his claim.
And now you say, ‘Go and tell your master, AliYahu is here.”’

But as soon as I leave you, the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will carry you away to who knows where. When Ahab comes and cannot find you, he will kill me. Yet I have been a true servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH all my life.
Has no one told you, my master, about the time when Yazabaal was trying to kill 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Nabym? I hid one hundred of them in two caves and supplied them with food and water.
And now you say, ‘Go and tell your master, AliYahu is here.’ Sir, if I do that, Ahab will certainly kill me.”
But AliYahu said, “I swear by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, in whose presence I stand, that I will present myself to Ahab this very day.”
So Ubadyahu went to tell Ahab that AliYahu had come, and Ahab went out to meet AliYahu.
When Ahab saw AliYahu, he exclaimed, “So, is it really you, you troublemaker of Yashar'AL?”

“I have made no trouble for Yashar'AL,” AliYahu replied. “You and your family are the troublemakers, for you have refused to obey the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and have worshiped the images of Baal instead.
Now summon all Yashar'AL to join me at Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asharah who are supported by Yazabaal.”
So Ahab summoned all the people of Yashar'AL and the prophets to Mount Carmel.

Then AliYahu stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you waver, hobbling between two opinions? If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, follow Him! But if Baal is mighty, then follow him!” But the people were completely silent.
Then AliYahu said to them, “I am the only Nabym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who is left, but Baal has four hundred and fifty prophets.

Now bring two bulls. The prophets of Baal may choose whichever one they wish and cut it into pieces and lay it on the wood of their altar, but without setting fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and lay it on the wood on the altar, I will not set fire to it.
Then call on the name of your Baal idol, and I will call on the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who answers by fire, He is the only 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH!” And all the people agreed.
Then AliYahu said to the prophets of Baal, “You go first, for there are many of you. Choose one of the bulls, and prepare it and call on the name of your Baal idol. But do not set fire to the wood.”

So they prepared one of the bulls and placed it on the altar. Then they called on the name of Baal from morning until noontime, shouting, “O Baal, answer us!” But there was no reply of any kind. Then they danced, hobbling around the altar they had made.

About noontime AliYahu began mocking them. “You’ll have to shout louder,” he scoffed, “for surely he is a idol! Perhaps he is daydreaming, or is relieving himself. Or maybe he is away on a trip, or is asleep and needs to be wakened!”
So they shouted louder, and following their normal custom, they cut themselves with knives and swords until the blood gushed out.
They raved all afternoon until the time of the evening sacrifice, but still there was no sound, no reply, no response.
Then AliYahu called to the people, “Come over here!” They all crowded around him as he repaired the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that had been torn down.
AliYahu took twelve stones, one to represent each of the tribes of Yashar'AL,
and AliYahu used the stones to rebuild the altar in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then he dug a trench around the altar large enough to hold about three gallons.
He piled wood on the altar, cut the bull into pieces, and laid the pieces on the wood. Then AliYahu said, “Fill four large jars with water, and pour the water over the offering and the wood.”
After they had done this, he said, “Do the same thing again!” And when they were finished, he said, “Now do it a third time!” So they did as he said,
and the water ran around the altar and even filled the trench.

At the usual time for offering the evening sacrifice, AliYahu the Nabym walked up to the altar and prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, Yachaq and Ya'aqub, prove today that you are 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in Yashar'AL and that I am your servant. Prove that I have done all this at your command.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, answer me! Answer me so these people will know that you, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, are their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and that you have brought them back to yourself.”
Immediately the fire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH flashed down from Shamaym and burned up the young bull, the wood, the stones, and the dust. It even licked up all the water in the trench!
And when all the people saw it, they fell face down on the ground and cried out, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, He is 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH! Yes, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH!”
Then AliYahu commanded, “Seize all the prophets of Baal. Do not let a single one escape!” So the people seized them all, and AliYahu took them down to the Kishun Valley and killed them there.
Then AliYahu said to Ahab, “Go get something to eat and drink, for I hear a mighty rainstorm coming!”
So Ahab went to eat and drink. But AliYahu climbed to the top of Mount Carmel and bowed low to the ground and prayed with his face between his knees.
Then he said to his servant, “Go and look out toward the sea.” The servant went and looked, then returned to AliYahu and said, “I did not see anything.”
Finally the seventh time, his servant told him, “I saw a little cloud about the size of a man’s hand rising from the sea.”
And soon the sky was black with clouds. A heavy wind brought a terrific rainstorm, and Ahab left quickly for Yazraal.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave special strength to AliYahu, he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab’s chariot all the way to the entrance of Yazraal.
When Ahab got home, he told Yazabaal everything AliYahu had done, including the way he had killed all the prophets of Baal.
So Yazabaal sent this message to AliYahu: “May the idols strike me and even kill me if by this time tomorrow I have not killed you just as you killed them.”
AliYahu was afraid and fled for his life, he went to Baarshaba, a town in Yahudah, and he left his servant there.

Then he went on alone into the wilderness, traveling all day, he sat down under a solitary broom tree and prayed that he might die, he said “I have had enough, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Take my life, for I am no better than my ancestors who have already died.”
Then he lay down and slept under the broom tree. But as he was sleeping, a Malak touched him and told him, “Get up and eat!”
AliYahu looked around and there beside his head was some bread baked on hot stones and a jar of water! So he ate and drank and lay down again.
Then the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came again and touched him and said, “Get up and eat some more, or the journey ahead will be too much for you.”
So he got up and ate and drank, and the food gave him enough strength to travel forty days and forty nights to Mount Sinai, the mountain of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
There he came to a cave, where he spent the night. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to AliYahu, “What are you doing here?”

AliYahu replied, “I have zealously served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. But the people of Yashar'AL have broken their covenant with you, torn down your altars, and killed every one of your Nabym. I am the only one left, and now they are trying to kill me, too.”

“And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to AliYahu; Go out and stand before me on the mountain, and as AliYahu stood there, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH passed by, and a mighty windstorm hit the mountain. It was such a terrible blast that the rocks were torn loose, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was not in the earthquake.
And after the earthquake there was a fire, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was not in the fire, and after the fire there was the sound of a gentle whisper.
When AliYahu heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the entrance of the cave, and a voice said, “What are you doing here, AliYahu?”

And AliYahu replied again, “I have zealously served 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. But the people of Yashar'AL have broken their covenant with you, torn down your altars, and killed every one of your Nabym. I am the only one left, and now they are trying to kill me, too.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to AliYahu, “Go back the same way you came, and travel to the wilderness of Damascus. When you arrive there, anoint Hazaal to be king of Aram.
Then anoint Yahu grandson of Nimshi to be king of Yashar'AL, and anoint Alysha son of Shaphat from the town of Abal-mahulah to replace you as my Nabym (prophet).
Anyone who escapes from Hazaal will be killed by Yahu, and those who escape Yahu will be killed by Alysha!
Yet I will preserve 7,000 others in Yashar'AL who have never bowed down to Baal or kissed him!”

So AliYahu went and found Alysha son of Shaphat plowing a field. There were twelve teams of oxen in the field, and Alysha was plowing with the twelfth team, and AliYahu went over to Alysha and threw his cloak across his shoulders and then walked away.

Alysha left the oxen standing there, ran after AliYahu, and said to him, “First let me go and kiss my father and mother good-bye, and then I will go with you!” AliYahu replied, “Go on back, but think about what I have done to you.”

So Alysha returned to his oxen and slaughtered them, he used the wood from the plow to build a fire to roast their flesh, he passed around the meat to the people of his town, and they all ate, then Alysha went with AliYahu as his assistant.

About that time King Ban-hadad of Aram mobilized his army, supported by the chariots and horses of thirty-two allied kings. They went to besiege Samaria, the capital of Yashar'AL, and launched attacks against it.
Ban-hadad sent messengers into the city to relay this message to King Ahab of Yashar'AL: “This is what Ban-hadad says:
‘Your silver and gold are mine, and so are your wives and the best of your children!’”
“And king Ahab said to him; All right, my master the king, “All that I have is yours!”
Soon Ban-hadad’s messengers returned again and said, “This is what Ban-hadad says: ‘I have already demanded that you give me your silver, gold, wives, and children.
But about this time tomorrow I will send my officials to search your palace and the homes of your officials. They will take away everything you consider valuable!’”
Then Ahab summoned all the elders of the land and said to them, “Look how this man is stirring up trouble! I already agreed with his demand that I give him my wives and children and silver and gold.”
“Do not give in to any more demands,” all the elders and the people advised.

So Ahab told the messengers from Ban-hadad, “Say this to my master the king: ‘I will give you everything you asked for the first time, but I cannot accept this last demand of yours.’” So the messengers returned to Ban-hadad with that response.
Then Ban-hadad sent this message to Ahab: “May the idols strike me and even kill me if there remains enough dust from Samaria to provide even a handful for each of my soldiers.”
The king of Yashar'AL sent back this answer: “A warrior putting on his sword for battle should not boast like a warrior who has already won.”
Ahab’s reply reached Ban-hadad and the other kings as they were drinking in their tents. “Prepare to attack!” Ban-hadad commanded his officers. So they prepared to attack the city.

Then a certain Nabym (prophet) came to see King Ahab of Yashar'AL and told him, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Do you see all these enemy forces? Today I will hand them all over to you. Then you will know that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”

Ahab asked, “How will 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH do it?” And the Nabym replied, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: The troops of the provincial commanders will do it. “Should we attack first?” Ahab asked. “Yes,” the Nabym answered.
So Ahab mustered the troops of the 232 provincial commanders. Then he called out the rest of the army of Yashar'AL, some 7,000 men.
About noontime, as Ban-hadad and the thirty-two allied kings were still in their tents drinking themselves into a stupor,
the troops of the provincial commanders marched out of the city as the first contingent. As they approached, Ban-hadad’s scouts reported to him, “Some troops are coming from Samaria.”
“Take them alive,” Ban-hadad commanded, “whether they have come for Shalum or for war.”
But Ahab’s provincial commanders and the entire army had now come out to fight.

Each Yasharalym soldier killed his Aramaan opponent, and suddenly the entire Aramaan army panicked and fled. The Yasharalym chased them, but King Ban-hadad and a few of his charioteers escaped on horses.
However, the king of Yashar'AL destroyed the other horses and chariots and slaughtered the Aramaans.
Afterward the Nabym said to King Ahab, “Get ready for another attack. Begin making plans now, for the king of Aram will come back next spring.”
After their defeat, Ban-hadad’s officers said to him, “The Yasharalym are of the hills; that is why they won. But we can beat them easily on the plains.
Only this time replace the kings with field commanders!

Recruit another army like the one you lost. Give us the same number of horses, chariots, and men, and we will fight against them on the plains. There’s no doubt that we will beat them.” So King Ban-hadad did as they suggested.
The following spring he called up the Aramaan army and marched out against Yashar'AL, this time at Aphak.

Yashar'AL then mustered its army, set up supply lines, and marched out for battle. But the Yasharalym army looked like two little flocks of goats in comparison to the vast Aramaan forces that filled the countryside!

Then the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH went to the king of Yashar'AL and said, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: The Aramaans have said, ‘the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is of the hills and not of the plains.’ So I will defeat this vast army for you. Then you will know that I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
The two armies camped opposite each other for seven days, and on the seventh day the battle began. The Yasharalym killed 100,000 Aramaan foot soldiers in one day.
The rest fled into the town of Aphak, but the wall fell on them and killed another 27,000. Ban-hadad fled into the town and hid in a secret room.

Ban-hadad’s officers said to him, “Sir, we have heard that the kings of Yashar'AL are merciful. So let’s humble ourselves by wearing burlap around our waists and putting ropes on our heads, and surrender to the king of Yashar'AL. Then perhaps he will let you live.”

So they put on burlap and ropes, and they went to the king of Yashar'AL and begged, “Your servant Ban-hadad says, ‘Please let me live!’ The king of Yashar'AL responded, “Is he still alive? he is my brother!”

The men took this as a good sign and quickly picked up on his words. “Yes,” they said, “your brother Ban-hadad! “Go and get him,” the king of Yashar'AL told them. And when Ban-hadad arrived, Ahab invited him up into his chariot.

Ban-hadad told him, “I will give back the towns my father took from your father, and you may establish places of trade in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria.” Then Ahab said, “I will release you under these conditions.” So they made a new treaty, and Ban-hadad was set free.
Meanwhile, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH instructed one of the group of Nabym to say to another man, “Hit me!” But the man refused to hit the Nabym.
Then the Nabym told him, “Because you have not obeyed the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, a lion will kill you as soon as you leave me.” And when he had gone, a lion did attack and kill him.
Then the Nabym turned to another man and said, “Hit me!” So he struck the Nabym and wounded him.
The Nabym placed a bandage over his eyes to disguise himself and then waited beside the road for the king.

As the king passed by, the Nabym called out to him, “Sir, I was in the thick of battle, and suddenly a man brought me a prisoner. He said, ‘Guard this man; if for any reason he gets away, you will either die or pay a fine of seventy-five pounds of silver!’
But while I was busy doing something else, the prisoner disappeared! “Well, it’s your own fault,” the king replied. “You have brought the judgment on yourself.”
Then the Nabym quickly pulled the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Yashar'AL recognized him as one of the Nabym.
The Nabym said to him, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Because you have spared the man I said must be destroyed, now you must die in his place, and your people will die instead of his people.”
So the king of Yashar'AL went home to Samaria angry and sullen.
Now there was a man named Nabuth, from Yazraal, who owned a vineyard in Yazraal beside the palace of King Ahab of Samaria.

One day Ahab said to Nabuth, “Since your vineyard is so convenient to my palace, I would like to buy it to use as a vegetable garden. I will give you a better vineyard in exchange, or if you prefer, I will pay you for it.”
But Nabuth replied, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH forbid that I should give you the inheritance that was passed down by my ancestors.”
So Ahab went home angry and sullen because of Nabuth’s answer. The king went to bed with his face to the wall and refused to eat!
“What’s the matter?” his wife Yazabaal asked him. “What’s made you so upset that you are not eating?”
“Ahab told her; I asked Nabuth to sell me his vineyard or trade it, but he refused!”
“Yazabaal said to Ahab; Are you the king of Yashar'AL or not? “Get up and eat something, and do not worry about it. I will get you Nabuth’s vineyard!”
So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and other leaders of the town where Nabuth lived.
In her letters she commanded: “Call the citizens together for a time of fasting, and give Nabuth a place of honor.
And then seat two scoundrels across from him who will accuse him of cursing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the king. Then take him out and stone him to death.”
So the elders and other town leaders followed the instructions Yazabaal had written in the letters.
They called for a fast and put Nabuth at a prominent place before the people.

Then the two scoundrels came and sat down across from him. And they accused Naboth before all the people, saying, “he cursed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the king.” So he was dragged outside the town and stoned to death.
The town leaders then sent word to Yazabaal, “Nabuth has been stoned to death.”
When Yazabaal heard the news, she said to Ahab, “You know the vineyard Nabuth would not sell you? Well, you can have it now! he is dead!”
So Ahab immediately went down to the vineyard of Nabuth to claim it.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to AliYahu,
“Go down to meet King Ahab of Yashar'AL, who rules in Samaria, he will be at Nabuth’s vineyard in Yazraal, claiming it for himself.

Give him this message: ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Was it not enough that you killed Nabuth? Must you rob him, too? Because you have done this, dogs will lick your blood at the very place where they licked the blood of Nabuth!’”
“And Ahab said to AliYahu; So my enemy, you have found me!” AliYahu answered, Yes “I have come because you have sold yourself to what is evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
So now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, ‘I will bring disaster on you and consume you. I will destroy every one of your male descendants, slave and free alike, anywhere in Yashar'AL!
I am going to destroy your family as I did the family of Yarubuam son of Nabat and the family of Baasha son of Ahiyahu, for you have made me very angry and have led Yashar'AL into sin.’
“And regarding Yazabaal, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, ‘Dogs will eat Yazabaal’s body at the plot of land in Yazraal.’
“The members of Ahab’s family who die in the city will be eaten by dogs, and those who die in the field will be eaten by vultures.”
(No one else who completely sold himself to what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sight as Ahab did under the influence of his wife Yazabaal.
His worst outrage was worshiping idols just as the Amurites had done, the people whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had driven out from the land ahead of the Yasharalym.)
But when Ahab heard this message, he tore his clothing, dressed in burlap, and fasted, he even slept in burlap and went about in deep mourning.
Then another message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to AliYahu:
“Do you see how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has done this, I will not do what I promised during his lifetime. It will happen to his sons; I will destroy his dynasty.”
For three years there was no war between Aram and Yashar'AL.
Then during the third year, King Yahushaphat of Yahudah went to visit King Ahab of Yashar'AL.
During the visit, the king of Yashar'AL said to his officials, “Do you realize that the town of Ramuth-gilaad belongs to us? And yet we have done nothing to recapture it from the king of Aram!”

Then he turned to Yahushaphat and asked, “Will you join me in battle to recover Ramuth-gilaad? Yahushaphat replied to the king of Yashar'AL, “Yes, of course! you and I are as one, my troops are your troops, and my horses are your horses.”
Then Yahushaphat added, “But first let us find out what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar.”

So the king of Yashar'AL summoned the Nabym, about 400 of them, and asked them, “Should I go to war against Ramuth-gilaad, or should I hold back?” They all replied, “Yes, go right ahead! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give the king victory.”
But Yahushaphat asked, “Is there not also a Nabym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH here? We should ask him the same question.”

The king of Yashar'AL replied to Yahushaphat, “There is one man who could consult 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for us, but I hate him, he never prophesies anything but trouble for me! His name is Micayahu son of Imlah.” Yahushaphat replied, “That is not the way a king should talk! Let us hear what he has to say.”
So the king of Yashar'AL called one of his officials and said, “Quick! Bring Micayahu son of Imlah.”

King Ahab of Yashar'AL and King Yahushaphat of Yahudah, dressed in their royal robes, were sitting on thrones at the threshing floor near the gate of Samaria. All of Ahab’s prophets were prophesying there in front of them.
One of them, Zadakyahu son of Kanaanah, made some iron horns and proclaimed, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says: With these horns you will gore the Aramaans to death!”
All the other prophets agreed. “Yes,” they said, “go up to Ramuth-gilaad and be victorious, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give the king victory!”
Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micayahu said to him, “Look, all the prophets are promising victory for the king. Be sure that you agree with them and promise success.”
But Micayahu replied, “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, I will say only what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH tells me to say.”

When Micayahu arrived before the king, Ahab asked him, “Micayahu, should we go to war against Ramuth-gilaad, or should we hold back?” Micayahu replied sarcastically, “Yes, go up and be victorious, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give the king victory!”
But the king replied sharply, “How many times must I demand that you speak only the truth to me when you speak for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?”

Then Micayahu told him, “In a vision I saw all Yashar'AL scattered on the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to me, ‘Their master has been killed. Send them home in Shalum.’”
“Did not I tell you?” Ahab exclaimed to Yahushaphat. “he never prophesies anything but trouble for me.”
Then Micayahu continued, “Listen to what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar! I saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sitting on his throne with all the armies of Shamaym around him, on His right and on His left.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, ‘Who can entice Ahab to go into battle against Ramuth-gilaad so he can be killed?’ “There were many suggestions,
and finally a ruach approached 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and said, ‘I can do it!’
“‘How will you do this?’ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH asked. And the ruach replied, ‘I will go out and inspire all of Ahab’s prophets to speak lies. “You will succeed,’ said 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. ‘Go ahead and do it.’
“So you see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all your prophets. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has pronounced your doom.”
Then Zadakyahu son of Kenaanah walked up to Micayahu and slapped him across the face. “Since when did the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH leave me to speak to you?” he demanded.
And Micayahu replied, “You will find out soon enough when you are trying to hide in some secret room!”
“Arrest him!” the king of Yashar'AL ordered. “Take him back to Amun, the governor of the city, and to my son Yuash.
Give them this order from the king: ‘Put this man in prison, and feed him nothing but bread and water until I return safely from the battle!’”
But Micayahu replied, “If you return safely, it will mean that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has not spoken through me!” Then he added to those standing around, “Everyone mark my words!”
So King Ahab of Yashar'AL and King Yahushaphat of Yahudah led their armies against Ramuth-gilaad.

The king of Yashar'AL said to Yahushaphat, “As we go into battle, I will disguise myself so no one will recognize me, but you wear your royal robes.” So the king of Yashar'AL disguised himself, and they went into battle.
Meanwhile, the king of Aram had issued these orders to his thirty-two chariot commanders: “Attack only the king of Yashar'AL. Do not bother with anyone else!”
So when the Aramaan chariot commanders saw Yahushaphat in his royal robes, they went after him. “There is the king of Yashar'AL!” they shouted. But when Yahushaphat called out,
the chariot commanders realized he was not the king of Yashar'AL, and they stopped chasing him.

An Aramaan soldier, however, randomly shot an arrow at the Yasharalym troops and hit the king of Yashar'AL between the joints of his armor. “Turn the horses and get me out of here!” Ahab groaned to the driver of his chariot. “I am badly wounded!”
The battle raged all that day, and the king remained propped up in his chariot facing the Aramaans. The blood from his wound ran down to the floor of his chariot, and as evening arrived he died.
Just as the sun was setting, the cry ran through his troops: “We are done for! Run for your lives!”
So king Ahab died, and his body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
Then his chariot was washed beside the pool of Samaria, and dogs came and licked his blood at the place where the prostitutes bathed, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised.
The rest of the events in Ahab’s reign and everything he did, including the story of the Ibury palace and the towns he built, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
So Ahab died, and his son Ahazyahu became the next king.
Yahushaphat son of Asa began to rule over Yahudah in the fourth year of King Ahab’s reign in Yashar'AL.
Yahoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam twenty-five years. His mother was Azubah, the daughter of Shilhi.

Yahushaphat was a good king, following the example of his father Asa, he did what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, During his reign, however he failed to remove all the pagan shrines, and the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.
Yahushaphat also made Shalum with the king of Yashar'AL.
The rest of the events in Yahushaphat’s reign, the extent of his power, and the wars he waged are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
He banished from the land the rest of the male and female shrine prostitutes, who still continued their practices from the days of his father, Asa.
(There was no king in Adum at that time, only a deputy.)
Yahushaphat also built a fleet of trading ships to sail to Uphir for gold. But the ships never set sail, for they met with disaster in their home port of Aziun-gabar.
At one time Ahazyahu son of Ahab had proposed to Yahushaphat, “Let my men sail with your men in the ships.” But Yahushaphat refused the request.
When Yahushaphat died, he was buried with his ancestors in the City of Daud. Then his son Yahuram became the next king.
Ahazyahu son of Ahab began to rule over Yashar'AL in the seventeenth year of King Yahoshaphat’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria two years.
But he did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, following the example of his father and mother and the example of Yarubuam son of Nabat, who had led Yashar'AL to sin.
He served Baal and worshiped him, provoking the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, just as his father had done.

books.name: II Kings
chapters: After King Ahab’s death, the land of Muab rebelled against Yashar'AL.

One day Yashar'AL’s new king, Ahazyahu, fell through the latticework of an upper room at his palace in Samaria and was seriously injured. So he sent messengers to the temple of Baal-zabub, the idol of Akrun, to ask whether he would recover.

But the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to AliYahu, who was from Tishba, “Go and confront the messengers of the king of Samaria and ask them, ‘Is there no 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in Yashar'AL? Why are you going to Baal-zabub, the idol of Akrun, to ask whether the king will recover?
Now, therefore, this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says: You will never leave the bed you are lying on; you will surely die.’” So AliYahu went to deliver the message.
When the messengers returned to the king, he asked them, “Why have you returned so soon?”

They replied, “A man came up to us and told us to go back to the king and give him this message. ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Is there no 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in Yashar'AL? Why are you sending men to Baal-zabub, the idol of Akrun, to ask whether you will recover? Therefore, because you have done this, you will never leave the bed you are lying on; you will surely die.’”
“What sort of man was he?” the king demanded. “What did he look like?”
They replied, “he was a hairy man, and he wore a leather belt around his waist.” AliYahu from Tishba!” the king exclaimed.

Then he sent an army captain with fifty soldiers to arrest AliYahu, they found him sitting on top of a hill. The captain said to him, “Servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, the king has commanded you to come down with us.”
But AliYahu replied to the captain, “If I am a servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, let fire come down from Shamaym and destroy you and your fifty men!” Then fire fell from Shamaym and killed them all.
So the king sent another captain with fifty men. The captain said to him, “servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, the king demands that you come down at once.”
AliYahu replied, “If I am a servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, let fire come down from Shamaym and destroy you and your fifty men!” And again the fire of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH fell from Shamaym and killed them all.

Once more the king sent a third captain with fifty men. But this time the captain went up the hill and fell to his knees before AliYahu. he pleaded with him, “O servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, please spare my life and the lives of these, your fifty servants.
See how the fire from Shamaym came down and destroyed the first two groups. But now please spare my life!”
Then the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to AliYahu, “Go down with him, and do not be afraid of him.” So AliYahu got up and went with him to the king.

And AliYahu said to the king, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Why did you send messengers to Baal-zabub, the idol of Akrun, to ask whether you will recover? Is there no 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in Yashar'AL to answer your question? Therefore, because you have done this, you will never leave the bed you are lying on; you will surely die.”

So Ahazyahu died, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised through AliYahu. Since Ahazyahu did not have a son to succeed him, his brother Yuram became the next king. This took place in the second year of the reign of Yahuram son of Yahushaphat, king of Yahudah.
The rest of the events in Ahazyahu’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was about to take AliYahu up to Shamaym in a whirlwind, AliYahu and Alysha were traveling from Gilgal.
And AliYahu said to Alysha, “Stay here, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has told me to go to Bathal.”

The group of Nabym (prophets) from Bathal came to Alysha and asked him, “Did you know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is going to take your master away from you today? “Of course I know,” Alysha answered. “But be quiet about it.”

Then AliYahu said to Alysha, “Stay here, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has told me to go to Yarichu.” But Alysha replied again, “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives and you yourself live, I will never leave you.” So they went on together to Yarichu.

Then the group of Nabym from Yarichu came to Alysha and asked him, “Did you know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is going to take your master away from you today? “Of course I know,” Alysha answered. “But be quiet about it.”

Then AliYahu said to Alysha, “Stay here, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has told me to go to the Yurdan River.” But again Alysha replied, “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives and you yourself live, I will never leave you.” So they went on together.
Fifty men from the group of Nabym also went and watched from a distance as AliYahu and Alysha stopped beside the Yurdan River.
Then AliYahu folded his cloak together and struck the water with it. The river divided, and the two of them went across on dry ground!

When they came to the other side, AliYahu said to Alysha, “Tell me what I can do for you before I am taken away.” And Alysha replied, “Please let me inherit a double share of your Ruach and become your successor.”
“You have asked a difficult thing,” AliYahu replied. “If you see me when I am taken from you, then you will get your request. But if not, then you won’t.”

As they were walking along and talking, suddenly a chariot of fire appeared, drawn by horses of fire. It drove between the two men, separating them, and AliYahu was carried by a whirlwind into Shamaym.
Alysha saw it and cried out, “My father! My father! I see the chariots and charioteers of Yashar'AL!” And as they disappeared from sight, Alysha tore his clothes in distress.
Alysha picked up AliYahu’s cloak, which had fallen when AliYahu was taken up. Then Alysha returned to the bank of the Yurdan River.
He struck the water with AliYahu’s cloak and cried out, “Where is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of AliYahu?” Then the river divided, and Alysha went across.
When the group of Nabym from Yarichu saw from a distance what happened, they exclaimed, AliYahu’s ruach rests upon Alysha!” And they went to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

“Sir,” they said, “just say the word and fifty of our strongest men will search the wilderness for your master. Perhaps the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has left him on some mountain or in some valley.” No,” Alysha said, “don’t send them.”
But they kept urging him until they shamed him into agreeing, and he finally said, “All right, send them.” So fifty men searched for three days but did not find AliYahu.
Alysha was still at Yarichu when they returned. “Did I not tell you not to go?” he asked.

One day the leaders of the town of Yarichu visited Alysha. “We have a problem, my master,” they told him. “This town is located in pleasant surroundings, as you can see. But the water is bad, and the land is unproductive.”
And Alysha said, “Bring me a new bowl, and put salt in it.” So they brought bowl and salt to Alysha.
Then he went out to the source of the water, and cast in the salt there, and said, “Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘I have healed this water; from this water there shall be no more death or barrenness.’ ”
So the water remains healed to this day, according to the word of Alysha which he spoke.
Alysha left Yarichu and went up to Bathal. As he was walking along the road, a group of boys from the town began mocking and making fun of him. “Go away, baldy!” they chanted. “Go away, baldy!”
Alysha turned around and looked at them, and he cursed them in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then two bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of them.
From there Alysha went to Mount Carmel and finally returned to Samaria.
Ahab’s son Yuram began to rule over Yashar'AL in the eighteenth year of King Yahushaphat’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria twelve years.
He did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but not to the same extent as his father and mother, he at least tore down the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had set up.
Nevertheless, he continued in the sins that Yarubuam son of Nebat had committed and led the people of Yashar'AL to commit.
King Masha of Muab was a sheep breeder. He used to pay the king of Yashar'AL an annual tribute of 100,000 lambs and the wool of 100,000 rams.
But after Ahab’s death, the king of Muab rebelled against the king of Yashar'AL.
So King Yuram promptly mustered the army of Yashar'AL and marched from Samaria.

On the way, he sent this message to King Yahushaphat of Yahudah: “The king of Muab has rebelled against me. Will you join me in battle against him?” And Yahushaphat replied, “Why, of course! You and I are as one. My troops are your troops, and my horses are your horses.”
Then Yahushaphat asked, “What route will we take? “We will attack from the wilderness of Adum,” Yuram replied.
The king of Adum and his troops joined them, and all three armies traveled along a roundabout route through the wilderness for seven days. But there was no water for the men or their animals.
“What should we do?” the king of Yashar'AL cried out. “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought the three of us here to let the king of Muab defeat us.”

But King Yahushaphat of Yahudah asked, “Is there no prophet of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with us? If there is, we can ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what to do through him.” One of King Yuram’s officers replied, “Alysha son of Shaphat is here, he used to be AliYahu’s personal assistant.”
Yahushaphat said, “Yes, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH speaks through him.” So the king of Yashar'AL, King Yahushaphat of Yahudah, and the king of Adum went to consult with Alysha.

“Why are you coming to me?” Alysha asked the king of Yashar'AL. “Go to the pagan prophets of your father and mother!” But King Yuram of Yashar'AL said, “No! For it was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who called us three kings here, only to be defeated by the king of Muab!”
Alysha replied, “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Almighty lives, whom I serve, I would not even bother with you except for my respect for King Yahushaphat of Yahudah.
Now bring me someone who can play the harp.” While the harp was being played, the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came upon Alysha,
and he said, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: This dry valley will be filled with pools of water!
You will see neither wind nor rain, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but this valley will be filled with water. You will have plenty for yourselves and your cattle and other animals.
But this is only a simple thing for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make you victorious over the army of Muab!
You will conquer the best of their towns, even the fortified ones. You will cut down all their good trees, stop up all their springs, and ruin all their good land with stones.”
The next day at about the time when the morning sacrifice was offered, water suddenly appeared! It was flowing from the direction of Adum, and soon there was water everywhere.

Meanwhile, when the people of Muab heard about the three armies marching against them, they mobilized every man who was old enough to strap on a sword, and they stationed themselves along their border.
But when they got up the next morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it appear red to the Muabites—like blood.
“It is blood!” the Muabites exclaimed. “The three armies must have attacked and killed each other! Let us go, men of Muab, and collect the plunder!”

But when the Muabites arrived at the Yasharalym camp, the army of Yashar'AL rushed out and attacked them until they turned and ran. The army of Yashar'AL chased them into the land of Muab, destroying everything as they went.

They destroyed the towns, covered their good land with stones, stopped up all the springs, and cut down all the good trees. Finally, only Kir-harasath and its stone walls were left, but men with slings surrounded and attacked it.
When the king of Muab saw that he was losing the battle, he led 700 of his swordsmen in a desperate attempt to break through the enemy lines near the king of Adum, but they failed.

Then the king of Muab took his oldest son, who would have been the next king, and sacrificed him as a burnt offering on the wall. So there was great anger and wrath against Yashar'AL, and the Yasharalym withdrew and returned to their own land.

One day the widow of a member of the group of Nabym (prophets) came to Alysha and cried out, “My husband who served you is dead, and you know how he feared 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. But now a creditor has come, threatening to take my two sons as slaves.”
“What can I do to help you?” Alysha asked. “Tell me, what do you have in the house? “Nothing at all, except a flask of olive oil,” she replied.
And Alysha said, “Borrow as many empty jars as you can from your friends and neighbors.
Then go into your house with your sons and shut the door behind you. Pour olive oil from your flask into the jars, setting each one aside when it is filled.”
So she did as she was told, her sons kept bringing jars to her, and she filled one after another.
Soon every container was full to the brim! “Bring me another jar,” she said to one of her sons. There is no more jars!” he told her. And then the olive oil stopped flowing.
When she told the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH what had happened, he said to her, “Now sell the olive oil and pay your debts, and you and your sons can live on what is left over.”

One day Alysha went to the town of Shunam. A wealthy woman lived there, and she urged him to come to her home for a meal. After that, whenever he passed that way, he would stop there for something to eat.
She said to her husband, “I am sure this man who stops in from time to time is a qadash servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Let us build a small room for him on the roof and furnish it with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp. Then he will have a place to stay whenever he comes by.”
One day Alysha returned to Shunam, and he went up to this upper room to rest.
He said to his servant Gahazi, “Tell the woman from Shunam I want to speak to her.”,

Alysha said to Gahazi, “Tell her, ‘We appreciate the kind concern you have shown us. What can we do for you? Can we put in a good word for you to the king or to the commander of the army? “No,” she replied, “my family takes good care of me.”
