Later Alysha asked Gahazi, “What can we do for her?” Gahazi replied, “She does not have a son, and her husband is an old man.”
“Call her back again,” Alysha told him. When the woman returned, Alysha said to her as she stood in the doorway,
“Next year at this time you will be holding a son in your arms! “No, my master!” she cried. “O servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, do not deceive me and get my hopes up like that.”
But sure enough, the woman soon became pregnant. And at that time the following year she had a son, just as Alysha had said.
One day when her child was older, he went out to help his father, who was working with the harvesters.
Suddenly he cried out, “My head hurts! My head hurts!” his father said to one of the servants, “Carry him home to his mother.”
So the servant took him home, and his mother held him on her lap. But around noontime he died.
She carried him up and laid him on the bed of the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, then shut the door and left him there.
She sent a message to her husband: “Send one of the servants and a donkey so that I can hurry to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and come right back.”
“Why go today?” he asked. “It is neither a new moon festival nor a Shabbat.” But she said, “It will be all right.”
So she saddled the donkey and said to the servant, “Hurry! Do not slow down unless I tell you to.”
As she approached the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH at Mount Carmel, Alysha saw her in the distance, he said to Gahazi, “Look, the woman from Shunam is coming.
Run out to meet her and ask her, ‘Is everything all right with you, your husband, and your child?’” “Yes,” the woman told Gahazi, “everything is fine.”

But when she came to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH at the mountain, she fell to the ground before him and caught hold of his feet. Gahazi began to push her away, but the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said, “Leave her alone. She is deeply troubled, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has not told me what it is.”
Then she said, “Did I ask you for a son, my master? And did I not say, ‘Do not deceive me and get my hopes up’?”
Then Alysha said to Gahazi, “Get ready to travel; take my staff and go! Do not talk to anyone along the way. Go quickly and lay the staff on the child’s face.”
But the boy’s mother said, “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives and you yourself live, I will not go home unless you go with me.” So Alysha returned with her.
Gahazi hurried on ahead and laid the staff on the child’s face, but nothing happened. There was no sign of life, he returned to meet Alysha and told him, “The child is still dead.”
When Alysha arrived, the child was indeed dead, lying there on the Nabym bed.
He went in alone and shut the door behind him and prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then he lay down on the child’s body, placing his mouth on the child’s mouth, his eyes on the child’s eyes, and his hands on the child’s hands. And as he stretched out on him, the child’s body began to grow warm again!
Alysha got up, walked back and forth across the room once, and then stretched himself out again on the child. This time the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes!
Then Alysha summoned Gahazi. “Call the child’s mother!” And when she came in, Alysha said, “Here, take your son!”
She fell at his feet and bowed before him, overwhelmed with gratitude. Then she took her son in her arms and carried him downstairs.

Alysha now returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. One day as the group of Nabym was seated before him, he said to his servant, “Put a large pot on the fire, and make some stew for the rest of the group.”
One of the young men went out into the field to gather herbs and came back with a pocketful of wild gourds, he shredded them and put them into the pot without realizing they were poisonous.
Some of the stew was served to the men. But after they had eaten a bite or two they cried out, “Servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, there’s poison in this stew!” So they would not eat it.
Alysha said, “Bring me some flour.” Then he threw it into the pot and said, “Now it’s all right; go ahead and eat.” And the food did not harm them again.

One day a man from Baal-shalishah brought the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH a sack of fresh grain and twenty loaves of barley bread made from the first grain of his harvest. Alysha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”

“What?” his servant exclaimed. “Feed a hundred people with only this?” But Alysha repeated, “Give it to the people so they can eat, for this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Everyone will eat, and there will even be some left over!”
And when they gave it to the people, there was plenty for all and some left over, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had Dabar.

The king of Aram had great admiration for Naaman, the commander of his army, because through him 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given Aram great victories. But though Naaman was a mighty warrior, he suffered from leprosy.
At this time Aramaan raiders had invaded the land of Yashar'AL, and among their captives was a young girl who had been given to Naaman’s wife as a maid.
One day the girl said to her mistress, “I wish my master would go to see the Nabym in Samaria. He would heal him of his leprosy.”
So Naaman told the king what the young girl from Yashar'AL had said.

“Go and visit the Nabym,” the king of Aram told him. “I will send a letter of introduction for you to take to the king of Yashar'AL.” So Naaman started out, carrying as gifts 750 pounds of silver, 150 pounds of gold, and ten sets of clothing.
The letter to the king of Yashar'AL said: “With this letter I present my servant Naaman. I want you to heal him of his leprosy.”

When the king of Yashar'AL read the letter, he tore his clothes in dismay and said, “This man sends me a leper to heal! Am I 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, that I can give life and take it away? I can see that he’s just trying to pick a fight with me.”

But when Alysha, the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, heard that the king of Yashar'AL had torn his clothes in dismay, he sent this message to him: “Why are you so upset? Send Naaman to me, and he will learn that there is a true Nabym here in Yashar'AL.”
So Naaman went with his horses and chariots and waited at the door of Alysha’s house.
But Alysha sent a messenger out to him with this message: “Go and wash yourself seven times in the Yurdan River. Then your skin will be restored, and you will be healed of your leprosy.”

But Naaman became angry and stalked away. “I thought he would certainly come out to meet me!” he said. “I expected him to wave his hand over the leprosy and call on the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and heal me!
The rivers of Damascus, the Abana and the Pharpar, are better than any of the rivers of Yashar'AL? Why should I not wash in them and be healed?” So Naaman turned and went away in a rage.

But his officers tried to reason with him and said, “Sir, if the Nabym had told you to do something very difficult, would you not have done it? So you should certainly obey him when he says simply, ‘Go and wash and be cured!’

So Naaman went down to the Yurdan River and dipped himself seven times, as the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had instructed him. And his skin became as healthy as the skin of a young child, and he was healed!

Then Naaman and his entire party went back to find the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. They stood before him, and Naaman said, “Now I know that there is no 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in all the world except in Yashar'AL. So please accept a gift from your servant.”
But Alysha replied, “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, whom I serve, I will not accept any gifts.” And though Naaman urged him to take the gift, Alysha refused.

Then Naaman said, “All right, but please allow me to load two of my mules with earth from this place, and I will take it back home with me. From now on I will never again offer burnt offerings or sacrifices to idols, except 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
However, may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH pardon me in this one thing: When my master the king goes into the temple of the idol Rimmun to worship there and leans on my arm, may 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH pardon me when I bow, too.”
“Go in Shalum,” Alysha said. So Naaman started home again.

But Gehazi, the servant of Alysha, the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, said to himself, “My master should not have let this Aramaan get away without accepting any of his gifts. As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, I will chase after him and get something from him.”
So Gehazi set off after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gahazi running after him, he climbed down from his chariot and went to meet him. “Is everything all right?” Naaman asked.

“Yes,” Gahazi said, “but my master has sent me to tell you that two young Nabym from the hill country of Aphraim have just arrived. He would like 75 pounds of silver and two sets of clothing to give to them.”
“By all means, take twice as much silver,” Naaman insisted. He gave him two sets of clothing, tied up the money in two bags, and sent two of his servants to carry the gifts for Gahazi.
But when they arrived at the citadel, Gahazi took the gifts from the servants and sent the men back. Then he went and hid the gifts inside the house.
When he went in to his master, Alysha asked him, “Where have you been, Gahazi? “I have not been anywhere,” he replied.

But Alysha asked him, “Do you not realize that I was there in the ruach when Naaman stepped down from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to receive money and clothing, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, and male and female servants?
Because you have done this, you and your descendants will suffer from Naaman’s leprosy forever.” When Gehazi left the room, he was covered with leprosy; his skin was white as snow.
One day the group of Nabym came to Alysha and told him, “As you can see, this place where we meet with you is too small.
Let us go down to the Yurdan River, where there are plenty of logs. There we can build a new place for us to meet. “All right,” he told them, “go ahead.”
“Please come with us they said to him, and Alysha responded; “I will come with you.
So Alysha went with them. When they arrived at the Yurdan, they began cutting down trees.
But as one of them was cutting a tree, his ax head fell into the river. “Oh, sir!” he cried. “It was a borrowed ax!”
“Where did it fall?” the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH asked. When he showed him the place, Alysha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. Then the ax head floated to the surface.
“Grab it,” Alysha said. And the man reached out and grabbed it.
When the king of Aram was at war with Yashar'AL, he would confer with his officers and say, “We will mobilize our forces at such and such a place.”
But immediately Alysha, the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, would warn the king of Yashar'AL, “Do not go near that place, for the Aramaans are planning to mobilize their troops there.”
So the king of Yashar'AL would send word to the place indicated by the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Time and again Alysha warned the king, so that he would be on the alert there.
The king of Aram became very upset over this, he called his officers together and demanded, “Which of you is the traitor? Who has been informing the king of Yashar'AL of my plans?”
“It’s not us, my master the king,” one of the officers replied. “Alysha, the Nabym in Yashar'AL, tells the king of Yashar'AL even the words you speak in the privacy of your bedroom!”
“Go and find out where he is,” the king commanded, “so I can send troops to seize him.” And the report came back: Alysha is at Duthan.”
So one night the king of Aram sent a great army with many chariots and horses to surround the city.
When the servant of Alysha got up early the next morning and went outside, there were troops, horses, and chariots everywhere. “Oh, sir, what will we do now?” the young man cried to Alysha.
“Do not be afraid!” Alysha told him. “For there are more troops on our side than on their side!”

Then Alysha prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, open his eyes and let him see!” Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH opened the young man’s eyes, and when he looked up, he saw that the hillside around Alysha was filled with horses and chariots of fire.
As the Aramaan army advanced toward him, Alysha prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, please make them blind.” So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck them with blindness as Alysha had asked.
Then Alysha went out and told them, “You have come the wrong way! This is not the right city! Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are looking for.” And he led them to the city of Samaria.

As soon as they had entered Samaria, Alysha prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, now open their eyes and let them see.” So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH opened their eyes, and they discovered that they were in the middle of Samaria.
When the king of Yashar'AL saw them, he shouted to Alysha, “My father, should I kill them? Should I kill them?”
“Of course not!” Alysha replied. “Do we kill prisoners of war? Give them food and drink and send them home again to their master.”
So the king made a great feast for them and then sent them home to their master. After that, the Aramaan raiders stayed away from the land of Yashar'AL.
Some time later, however, King Ban-hadad of Aram mustered his entire army and besieged Samaria.
As a result, there was a great famine in the city. The siege lasted so long that a donkey’s head sold for eighty pieces of silver, and a cup of dove’s dung sold for five pieces of silver.
One day as the king of Yashar'AL was walking along the wall of the city, a woman called to him, “Please help me, my master the king!”
He answered, “If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH does not help you, what can I do? I have neither food from the threshing floor nor wine from the press to give you.”
But then the king asked, “What is the matter?” She replied, “This woman said to me: ‘Come on, let us eat your son today, then we will eat my son tomorrow.’
So we cooked my son and ate him. Then the next day I said to her, ‘Kill your son so we can eat him,’ but she has hidden her son.”
When the king heard this, he tore his clothes in despair. And as the king walked along the wall, the people could see that he was wearing burlap under his robe next to his skin.
“May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH strike me and even kill me if I do not separate Alysha’s head from his shoulders this very day,” the king vowed.

Alysha was sitting in his house with the elders of Yashar'AL when the king sent a messenger to summon him. But before the messenger arrived, Alysha said to the elders, “A murderer has sent a man to cut off my head. When he arrives, shut the door and keep him out. We will soon hear his master’s steps following him.”
While Alysha was still saying this, the messenger arrived. And the king said, “All this misery is from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! Why should I wait for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH any longer?”

Alysha replied, “Listen to this message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: By this time tomorrow in the markets of Samaria, six quarts of choice flour will cost only one piece of silver, and twelve quarts of barley grain will cost only one piece of silver.”

The officer assisting the king said to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, “That could not happen even if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH opened the windows of Shamaym!” But Alysha replied, “You will see it happen with your own eyes, but you will not be able to eat any of it!”
Now there were four men with leprosy sitting at the entrance of the city gates. “Why should we sit here waiting to die?” they asked each other.

“We will starve if we stay here, but with the famine in the city, we will starve if we go back there. So we might as well go out and surrender to the Aramaan army. If they let us live, it will be much better. But if they kill us, we would still have died if we stay here.”
So at twilight they set out for the camp of the Aramaans. But when they came to the edge of the camp, no one was there!

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had caused the Aramaan army to hear the clatter of speeding chariots and the galloping of horses and the sounds of a great army approaching. “The king of Yashar'AL has hired the Hittites and Mitzraym to attack us!” they cried to one another.
So they panicked and ran into the night, abandoning their tents, horses, donkeys, and everything else, as they fled for their lives.
When the lepers arrived at the edge of the camp, they went into one tent after another, eating and drinking wine; and they carried off silver and gold and clothing and hid it.

Finally, they said to each other, “This is not right. This is a day of good news, and we are not sharing it with anyone! If we wait until morning, some calamity will certainly fall upon us. Come on, let us go back and tell the people at the palace.”

So they went back to the city and told the gatekeepers what had happened. “We went out to the Aramaan camp,” they said, “and no one was there! The horses and donkeys were tethered and the tents were all in order, but there was not a single person around!”
Then the gatekeepers shouted the news to the people in the palace.

The king got out of bed in the middle of the night and told his officers, “I know what has happened. The Aramaans know we are starving, so they have left their camp and have hidden in the fields. They are expecting us to leave the city, and then they will take us alive and capture the city.”

One of his officers replied, “We had better send out scouts to check into this. Let them take five of the remaining horses. If something happens to them, it will be no worse than if they stay here and die with the rest of us.”
So two chariots with horses were prepared, and the king sent scouts to see what had happened to the Aramaan army.
They went all the way to the Yurdan River, following a trail of clothing and equipment that the Aramaans had thrown away in their mad rush to escape. The scouts returned and told the king about it.

Then the people of Samaria rushed out and plundered the Aramaan camp. So it was true that six quarts of choice flour were sold that day for one piece of silver, and twelve quarts of barley grain were sold for one piece of silver, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised.

The king appointed his officer to control the traffic at the gate, but he was knocked down and trampled to death as the people rushed out. So everything happened exactly as the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had predicted when the king came to his house.

The servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had said to the king, “By this time tomorrow in the markets of Samaria, six quarts of choice flour will cost one piece of silver, and twelve quarts of barley grain will cost one piece of silver.”

The king’s officer had replied, “That could not happen even if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH opened the windows of Shamaym!” And the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had said, “You will see it happen with your own eyes, but you will not be able to eat any of it!”
And so it was, for the people trampled him to death at the gate!
Alysha had told the woman whose son he had brought back to life, “Take your family and move to some other place, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has called for a famine on Yashar'AL that will last for seven years.”
So the woman did as the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH instructed. She took her family and settled in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
After the famine ended she returned from the land of the Philistines, and she went to see the king about getting back her house and land.
As she came in, the king was talking with Gahazi, the servant of Alysha. The king had just said, “Tell me some stories about the great things Alysha has done.”

And Gahazi was telling the king about the time Alysha had brought a boy back to life. At that very moment, the mother of the boy walked in to make her appeal to the king about her house and land. “Look, my master the king!” Gahazi exclaimed. “Here is the woman now, and this is her son the very one Alysha brought back to life!”

“Is this true?” the king asked her. And she told him the story. So he directed one of his officials to see that everything she had lost was restored to her, including the value of any crops that had been harvested during her absence.
Alysha went to Damascus, the capital of Aram, where King Ban-hadad lay sick. When someone told the king that the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had come,
the king said to Hazaal, “Take a gift to the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Then tell him to ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”

So Hazaal loaded down forty camels with the finest products of Damascus as a gift for Alysha, he went to Alysha and said, “Your servant Ban-hadad, the king of Aram, has sent me to ask, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”
And Alysha replied, “Go and tell him, ‘You will surely recover.’ But actually 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has shown me that he will surely die!”
Alysha stared at Hazaal with a fixed gaze until Hazaal became uneasy. Then the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH started weeping.

“What’s the matter, my master?” Hazaal asked him. Alysha replied, “I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Yashar'AL. You will burn their fortified cities, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little children to the ground, and rip open their pregnant women!”
Hazaal responded, “How could a nobody like me ever accomplish such great things?” Alysha answered, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has shown me that you are going to be the king of Aram.”
When Hazaal left Alysha and went back, the king asked him, “What did Alysha tell you?” And Hazaal replied, “He told me that you will surely recover.”
But the next day Hazaal took a blanket, soaked it in water, and held it over the king’s face until he died. Then Hazaal became the next king of Aram.
Yahuram son of King Yahushaphat of Yahudah began to rule over Yahudah in the fifth year of the reign of Yuram son of Ahab, king of Yashar'AL.
Yahuram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam eight years.
But Yahuram followed the example of the kings of Yashar'AL and was as wicked as King Ahab, for he had married one of Ahab’s daughters. So Yahuram did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did not want to destroy Yahudah, for he had promised his servant Daud that his descendants would continue to rule, shining like a lamp forever.
During Yahuram’s reign, the Adumites revolted against Yahudah and crowned their own king.

So Yahuram went with all his chariots to attack the town of Zair. The Adumites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, but he went out at night and attacked them under cover of darkness. But Yahuram’s army deserted him and fled to their homes.
So Adum has been independent from Yahudah to this day. The town of Libnah also revolted about that same time.
The rest of the events in Yahuram’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
When Yahuram died, he was buried with his ancestors in the City of Daud. Then his son Ahazyahu became the next king.
Ahazyahu son of Yahuram began to rule over Yahudah in the twelfth year of the reign of Yuram son of Ahab, king of Yashar'AL.
Ahazyahu was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam one year. His mother was Athalyahu, a granddaughter of King Umri of Yashar'AL.
Ahazyahu followed the evil example of King Ahab’s family, he did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, just as Ahab’s family had done, for he was related by marriage to the family of Ahab.
Ahazyahu joined Yuram son of Ahab in his war against King Hazaal of Aram at Ramuth-gilaad. When the Arameans wounded King Yuram in the battle,
he returned to Yazraal to recover from the wounds he had received at Ramuth. Because Yuram was wounded, King Ahazyahu of Yahudah went to Yazraal to visit him.
Meanwhile, Alysha the Nabym had summoned a member of the group of Nabym. “Get ready to travel,” he told him, “and take this flask of olive oil with you. Go to Ramuth-gilead,
and find Yahu son of Yahushaphat, son of Nimshi. Call him into a private room away from his friends,
and pour the oil over his head. Say to him, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: I anoint you to be the king over Yashar'AL.’ Then open the door and run for your life!”
So the young Nabym did as he was told and went to Ramuth-gilaad.
When he arrived there, he found Yahu sitting around with the other army officers. “I have a message for you, Commander,” he said. “For which one of us?” Yahu asked. “For you, Commander,” he replied.

So Yahu left the others and went into the house. Then the young Nabym poured the oil over Yahu’s head and said, “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, says: I anoint you king over 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s people, Yashar'AL.
You are to destroy the family of Ahab, your master. In this way, I will avenge the murder of my Nabyms and all the servants of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who were killed by Yazabaal.
The entire family of Ahab must be wiped out. I will destroy every one of his male descendants, slave and free alike, anywhere in Yashar'AL.
I will destroy the family of Ahab as I destroyed the families of Yarubuam son of Nebat and of Baasha son of Ahiyahu.
Dogs will eat Ahab’s wife Yazabaal at the plot of land in Yazraal, and no one will bury her.” Then the young Nabym opened the door and ran.
Yahu went back to his fellow officers, and one of them asked him, “What did that madman want? Is everything all right? “You know how a man like that babbles on,” Yahu replied.
“You are hiding something,” they said. “Tell us.” So Yahu told them, “He said to me, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: I have anointed you to be king over Yashar'AL.’”
Then they quickly spread out their cloaks on the bare steps and blew the ram’s horn, shouting, “Yahu is king!”
So Yahu son of Yahushaphat, son of Nimshi, led a conspiracy against King Yuram. (Now Yuram had been with the army at Ramuth-gilaad, defending Yashar'AL against the forces of King Hazaal of Aram.

But King Yuram was wounded in the fighting and returned to Yazraal to recover from his wounds.) So Yahu told the men with him, “If you want me to be king, do not let anyone leave town and go to Yazraal to report what we have done.”
Then Yahu got into a chariot and rode to Yazraal to find King Yuram, who was lying there wounded. King Ahazyahu of Yahudah was there too, for he had gone to visit him.

The watchman on the tower of Yazraal saw Yahu and his company approaching, so he shouted to Yuram, “I see a company of troops coming! “Send out a rider to ask if they are coming in Shalum,” King Yuram ordered.

So a horseman went out to meet Yahu and said, “The king wants to know if you are coming in Shalum.” Yahu replied, “What do you know about Shalum? Fall in behind me!” The watchman called out to the king, “The messenger has met them, but he is not returning.”
So the king sent out a second horseman. He rode up to them and said, “The king wants to know if you come in Shalum.” Again Yahu answered, “What do you know about Shalum? Fall in behind me!”
The watchman exclaimed, “The messenger has met them, but he is not returning either! It must be Yahu son of Nimshi, for he is driving like a madman.”

“Quick! Get my chariot ready!” King Yuram commanded. Then King Yuram of Yashar'AL and King Ahazyahu of Yahudah rode out in their chariots to meet Yahu. They met him at the plot of land that had belonged to Nabuth of Yazraal.
King Yuram demanded, “Do you come in Shalum, Yahu?” Yahu replied, “How can there be Shalum as long as the idolatry and witchcraft of your mother, Yazabaal, are all around us?”
Then King Yuram turned the horses around and fled, shouting to King Ahazyahu, “Treason, Ahazyahu!”
But Yahu drew his bow and shot Yuram between the shoulders. The arrow pierced his heart, and he sank down dead in his chariot.

Yahu said to Bidkar, his officer, “Throw him into the plot of land that belonged to Nabuth of Yazraal. Do you remember when you and I were riding along behind his father, Ahab? 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH pronounced this message against him:

‘I solemnly swear that I will repay him here on this plot of land, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for the murder of Nabuth and his sons that I saw yesterday.’ So throw him out on Nabuth’s property, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar.”

When King Ahazyahu of Yahudah saw what was happening, he fled along the road to Bath-haggan. Yahu rode after him, shouting, “Shoot him, too!” So they shot Ahazyahu in his chariot at the Ascent of Gur, near Iblaam, he was able to go on as far as Magiddu, but he died there.
His servants took him by chariot to Yahushalam, where they buried him with his ancestors in the City of Daud.
Ahazyahu had become king over Yahudah in the eleventh year of the reign of Yuram son of Ahab.
When Yazabaal, the queen mother, heard that Yahu had come to Yazraal, she painted her eyelids and fixed her hair and sat at a window.
When Yahu entered the gate of the palace, she shouted at him, “Have you come in Shalum, you murderer? You’re just like Zimri, who murdered his master!”
Yahu looked up and saw her at the window and shouted, “Who is on my side?” And two or three eunuchs looked out at him.
“Throw her down!” Yahu yelled. So they threw her out the window, and her blood spattered against the wall and on the horses. And Yahu trampled her body under his horses’ hooves.
Then Yahu went into the palace and ate and drank. Afterward he said, “Someone go and bury this cursed woman, for she is the daughter of a king.”
But when they went out to bury her, they found only her skull, her feet, and her hands.

When they returned and told Yahu, he stated, “This fulfills the message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, which he spoke through his servant AliYahu from Tishba: ‘At the plot of land in Yazraal, dogs will eat Yazabaal’s body.
Her remains will be scattered like dung on the plot of land in Yazraal, so that no one will be able to recognize her.’”
Ahab had seventy sons living in the city of Samaria. So Yahu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the elders and officials of the city, and to the guardians of King Ahab’s sons. He said,
“The king’s sons are with you, and you have at your disposal chariots, horses, a fortified city, and weapons. As soon as you receive this letter,
select the best qualified of your master’s sons to be your king, and prepare to fight for Ahab’s dynasty.”
But they were paralyzed with fear and said, “We’ve seen that two kings could not stand against this man! What can we do?”

So the palace and city administrators, together with the elders and the guardians of the king’s sons, sent this message to Yahu: “We are your servants and will do anything you tell us. We will not make anyone king; do whatever you think is best.”

Yahu responded with a second letter: “If you are on my side and are going to obey me, bring the heads of your master’s sons to me at Yazraal by this time tomorrow.” Now the seventy sons of the king were being cared for by the leaders of Samaria, where they had been raised since childhood.
When the letter arrived, the leaders killed all seventy of the king’s sons. They placed their heads in baskets and presented them to Yahu at Yazraal.
A messenger went to Yahu and said, “They have brought the heads of the king’s sons.” So Yahu ordered, “Pile them in two heaps at the entrance of the city gate, and leave them there until morning.”

In the morning Yahu went out and spoke to the crowd that had gathered around them. “You are not to blame,” he told them. “I am the one who conspired against my master and killed him. But who killed all these?
You can be sure that the message of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that was spoken concerning Ahab’s family will not fail. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH declared through his servant AliYahu that this would happen.”
Then Yahu killed all who were left of Ahab’s relatives living in Yazraal and all his important officials, his personal friends, and his priests. So Ahab was left without a single survivor.
Then Yahu set out for Samaria. Along the way, while he was at Bath-akad of the Shepherds,

he met some relatives of King Ahazyahu of Yahudah. “Who are you?” he asked them. And they replied, “We are relatives of King Ahazyahu. We are going to visit the sons of King Ahab and the sons of the queen mother.”
“Take them alive!” Yahu shouted to his men. And they captured all forty-two of them and killed them at the well of Bath-akad. None of them escaped.

When Yahu left there, he met Yahunadab son of Racab, who was coming to meet him. After they had greeted each other, Yahu said to him, “Are you as loyal to me as I am to you? “Yes, I am,” Yahunadab replied. If you are,” Yahu said, “then give me your hand.” So Yahunadab put out his hand, and Yahu helped him into the chariot.
Then Yahu said, “Now come with me, and see how devoted I am to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” So Yahunadab rode along with him.
When Yahu arrived in Samaria, he killed everyone who was left there from Ahab’s family, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised through AliYahu.
Then Yahu called a meeting of all the people of the city and said to them, “Ahab’s worship of Baal was nothing compared to the way I will worship him!

Therefore, summon all the prophets and worshipers of Baal, and call together all his priests. See to it that every one of them comes, for I am going to offer a great sacrifice to Baal. Anyone who fails to come will be put to death.” But Yahu’s cunning plan was to destroy all the worshipers of Baal.
Then Yahu ordered, “Prepare a solemn assembly to worship Baal!” So they did.
He sent messengers throughout all Yashar'AL summoning those who worshiped Baal. They all came, not a single one remained behind and they filled the temple of Baal from one end to the other.
And Yahu instructed the keeper of the wardrobe, “Be sure that every worshiper of Baal wears one of these robes.” So robes were given to them.
Then Yahu went into the temple of Baal with Yahunadab son of Racab. Yahu said to the worshipers of Baal, “Make sure no one who worships 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is here, only those who worship Baal.”

So they were all inside the temple to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Yahu had stationed eighty of his men outside the building and had warned them, “If you let anyone escape, you will pay for it with your own life.”

As soon as Yahu had finished sacrificing the burnt offering, he commanded his guards and officers, “Go in and kill all of them. Do not let a single one escape!” So they killed them all with their swords, and the guards and officers dragged their bodies outside. Then Yahu’s men went into the innermost fortress of the temple of Baal.
They dragged out the sacred pillar used in the worship of Baal and burned it.
They smashed the sacred pillar and wrecked the temple of Baal, converting it into a public toilet, as it remains to this day.
In this way, Yahu destroyed every trace of Baal worship from Yashar'AL.
He did not, however, destroy the gold calves at Bathal and Dan, with which Yarubuam son of Nabat had caused Yashar'AL to sin.

Nonetheless 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahu, “You have done well in following my instructions to destroy the family of Ahab. Therefore, your descendants will be kings of Yashar'AL down to the fourth generation.”
But Yahu did not obey the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, with all his heart, he refused to turn from the sins that Yarubuam had led Yashar'AL to commit.
At about that time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH began to cut down the size of Yashar'AL’s territory. King Hazaal conquered several sections of the country
east of the Yurdan River, including all of Gilaad, Gad, Rauban, and Manassah, he conquered the area from the town of Aruar by the Arnun Gurge to as far north as Gilaad and Bashan.
The rest of the events in Yahu’s reign, everything he did and all his achievements—are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When Yahu died, he was buried in Samaria. Then his son Yahuahaz became the next king.
In all, Yahu reigned over Yashar'AL from Samaria for twenty-eight years.
When Athalyahu, the mother of King Ahazyahu of Yahudah, learned that her son was dead, she began to destroy the rest of the royal family.

But Ahazyahu’s sister Yahushaba, the daughter of King Yahuram, took Ahazyahu’s infant son, Yuash, and stole him away from among the rest of the king’s children, who were about to be killed. She put Yuash and his nurse in a bedroom, and they hid him from Athalyahu, so the child was not murdered.
Yuash remained hidden in the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for six years while Athalyahu ruled over the land.

In the seventh year of Athalyahu’s reign, Yahuiada the Kuhan summoned the commanders, the Carite mercenaries, and the palace guards to come to the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he made a solemn pact with them and made them swear an oath of loyalty there in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple; then he showed them the king’s son.
Yahuiada told them, “This is what you must do. A third of you who are on duty on the Shabbat are to guard the royal palace itself.
Another third of you are to stand guard at the Sur Gate. And the final third must stand guard behind the palace guard. These three groups will all guard the palace.
The other two units who are off duty on the Sabbath must stand guard for the king at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple.
Form a bodyguard around the king and keep your weapons in hand. Kill anyone who tries to break through. Stay with the king wherever he goes.”

So the commanders did everything as Yahuiada the Kuhan ordered. The commanders took charge of the men reporting for duty that Shabbat, as well as those who were going off duty. They brought them all to Yahuiada the Kuhan,
and he supplied them with the spears and small shields that had once belonged to King Daud and were stored in the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The palace guards stationed themselves around the king, with their weapons ready. They formed a line from the south side of the Temple around to the north side and all around the altar.

Then Yahuiada brought out Yuash, the king’s son, placed the crown on his head, and presented him with a copy of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH’s laws. They anointed him and proclaimed him king, and everyone clapped their hands and shouted, “Long live the king!”
When Athalyahu heard the noise made by the palace guards and the people, she hurried to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple to see what was happening.

When she arrived, she saw the newly crowned king standing in his place of authority by the pillar, as was the custom at times of coronation. The commanders and trumpeters were surrounding him, and people from all over the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets. When Athalyahu saw all this, she tore her clothes in despair and shouted, “Treason! Treason!”

Then Yahuiada the Kuhan ordered the commanders who were in charge of the troops, “Take her to the soldiers in front of the Temple, and kill anyone who tries to rescue her.” For the Kuhan had said, “She must not be killed in the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So they seized her and led her out to the gate where horses enter the palace grounds, and she was killed there.
Then Yahuiada made a covenant between 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the king and the people that they would be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s people, he also made a covenant between the king and the people.

And all the people of the land went over to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They demolished the altars and smashed the idols to pieces, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars. Yahuiada the Kuhan stationed guards at the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then the commanders, the Carite mercenaries, the palace guards, and all the people of the land escorted the king from the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. They went through the gate of the guards and into the palace, and the king took his seat on the royal throne.
So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was in Shalum because Athalyahu had been killed at the king’s palace.
Yuash was seven years old when he became king.
Yuash began to rule over Yahudah in the seventh year of King Yahu’s reign in Yashar'AL. He reigned in Yahushalam forty years. His mother was Zibyahu from Baarshaba.
All his life Yuash did what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH because Yahuiada the Kuhan instructed him.
Yet even so, he did not destroy the pagan shrines, and the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.
One day King Yuash said to the Kuhanym, “Collect all the money brought as a sacred offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple, whether it is a regular assessment, a payment of vows, or a voluntary gift.
Let the Kuhanym take some of that money to pay for whatever repairs are needed at the Temple.”
But by the twenty-third year of Yuash’s reign, the Kuhanym still had not repaired the Temple.

So King Yuash called for Yahuiada and the other Kuhanym and asked them, “Why haven’t you repaired the Temple? Do not use any more money for your own needs. From now on, it must all be spent on Temple repairs.”
So the Kuhanym agreed not to accept any more money from the people, and they also agreed to let others take responsibility for repairing the Temple.

Then Yahuiada the Kuhan bored a hole in the lid of a large chest and set it on the right-hand side of the altar at the entrance of the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. The Kuhanym guarding the entrance put all of the people’s contributions into the chest.
Whenever the chest became full, the court secretary and the high Kuhan counted the money that had been brought to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple and put it into bags.
Then they gave the money to the construction supervisors, who used it to pay the people working on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple, the carpenters, the builders,

the masons, and the stonecutters. They also used the money to buy the timber and the finished stone needed for repairing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple, and they paid any other expenses related to the Temple’s restoration.
The money brought to the Temple was not used for making silver bowls, lamp snuffers, basins, trumpets, or other articles of gold or silver for the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
It was paid to the workmen, who used it for the Temple repairs.
No accounting of this money was required from the construction supervisors, because they were honest and trustworthy men.
However, the money that was contributed for guilt offerings and sin offerings was not brought into 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple. It was given to the Kuhanym for their own use.
About this time King Hazaal of Aram went to war against Gath and captured it. Then he turned to attack Yahushalam.

King Yuash collected all the sacred objects that Yahushaphat, Yahuram, and Ahazyahu, the previous kings of Yahudah, had dedicated, along with what he himself had dedicated, he sent them all to Hazaal, along with all the gold in the treasuries of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple and the royal palace. So Hazaal called off his attack on Yahushalam.
The rest of the events in Yuash’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
Yuash’s officers plotted against him and assassinated him at Bath-millu on the road to Silla.
The assassins were Yuzachar son of Shima'ath and Yahuzabad son of Shumer, both trusted advisers. Yuash was buried with his ancestors in the City of Daud. Then his son Amazyahu became the next king.
Yahuahaz son of Yahu began to rule over Yashar'AL in the twenty-third year of King Yuash’s reign in Yahudah. He reigned in Samaria seventeen years.
But he did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he followed the example of Yarubuam son of Nabat, continuing the sins that Yarubuam had led Yashar'AL to commit.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was very angry with Yashar'AL, and he allowed King Hazaal of Aram and his son Ban-hadad to defeat them repeatedly.
Then Yahuahaz prayed for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s help, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH heard his prayer, for he could see how severely the king of Aram was oppressing Yashar'AL.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH provided someone to rescue the Yasharalym from the tyranny of the Aramaans. Then Yashar'AL lived in safety again as they had in former days.
But they continued to sin, following the evil example of Yarubuam. They also allowed the Asharah pole in Samaria to remain standing.
Finally, Yahuahaz’s army was reduced to 50 charioteers, 10 chariots, and 10,000 foot soldiers. The king of Aram had killed the others, trampling them like dust under his feet.
The rest of the events in Yahuahaz’s reign—everything he did and the extent of his power are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When Yahuahaz died, he was buried in Samaria. Then his son Yahuash became the next king.
Yahuash son of Yahuahaz began to rule over Yashar'AL in the thirty-seventh year of King Yuash’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria sixteen years.
But he did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he refused to turn from the sins that Yarubuam son of Nebat had led Yashar'AL to commit.

The rest of the events in Yahuash’s reign and everything he did, including the extent of his power and his war with King Amazyahu of Yahudah, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When Yahuash died, he was buried in Samaria with the kings of Yashar'AL. Then his son Yarubuam II became the next king.
When Alysha was in his last illness, King Yahuash of Yashar'AL visited him and wept over him. “My father! My father! I see the chariots and charioteers of Yashar'AL!” he cried.
Alysha told him, “Get a bow and some arrows.” And the king did as he was told.
Alysha told him, “Put your hand on the bow,” and Alysha laid his own hands on the king’s hands.

Then he commanded, “Open that eastern window,” and he opened it. Then he said, “Shoot!” So he shot an arrow. Alysha proclaimed, “This is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s arrow, an arrow of victory over Aram, for you will completely conquer the Aramaans at Aphak.”
Then he said, “Now pick up the other arrows and strike them against the ground.” So the king picked them up and struck the ground three times.

But the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was angry with him. “You should have struck the ground five or six times!” he exclaimed. “Then you would have beaten Aram until it was entirely destroyed. Now you will be victorious only three times.”
Then Alysha died and was buried. Groups of Muabite raiders used to invade the land each spring.

Once when some Yasharalym were burying a man, they spied a band of these raiders. So they hastily threw the corpse into the tomb of Alysha and fled. But as soon as the body touched Alysha’s bones, the dead man revived and jumped to his feet!
King Hazaal of Aram had oppressed Yashar'AL during the entire reign of King Yahuahaz.

But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was kind and merciful to the people of Yashar'AL, and they were not totally destroyed. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH pitied them because of his covenant with Abraham, Yachaq, and Ya'aqub. And to this day he still has not completely destroyed them or banished them from his presence.
King Hazaal of Aram died, and his son Ban-hadad became the next king.

Then Yahuash son of Yahuahaz recaptured from Ban-hadad son of Hazaal the towns that had been taken from Yahuash’s father, Yahuahaz. Yahuash defeated Ban-hadad on three occasions, and he recovered the Yasharalym towns.
Amazyahu son of Yuash began to rule over Yahudah in the second year of the reign of King Yahuash of Yashar'AL.
Amazyahu was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam twenty-nine years, his mother was Yahuaddin from Yahushalam.
Amazyahu did what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but not like his ancestor Daud. Instead, he followed the example of his father, Yuash.
Amazyahu did not destroy the pagan shrines, and the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.
When Amazyahu was well established as king, he executed the officials who had assassinated his father.

However, he did not kill the children of the assassins, for he obeyed the commandment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as written by Musha in the Book of the Law: “Parents must not be put to death for the sins of their children, nor children for the sins of their parents. Those deserving to die must be put to death for their own crimes.”
Amazyahu also killed 10,000 Adumites in the Valley of Salt, he also conquered Sala and changed its name to Yukthaal, as it is called to this day.
One day Amazyahu sent messengers with this challenge to Yashar'AL’s king Yahuash, the son of Yahuahaz and grandson of Yahu: “Come and meet me in battle!”

But King Yahuash of Yashar'AL replied to King Amazyahu of Yahudah with this story: “Out in the Labanun mountains, a thistle sent a message to a mighty cedar tree: ‘Give your daughter in marriage to my son.’ But just then a wild animal of Labanun came by and stepped on the thistle, crushing it!
“You have indeed defeated Adum, and you are proud of it. But be content with your victory and stay at home! Why stir up trouble that will only bring disaster on you and the people of Yahudah?”
But Amazyahu refused to listen, so King Yahuash of Yashar'AL mobilized his army against King Amazyahu of Yahudah. The two armies drew up their battle lines at Bath-shamash in Yahudah.
Yahudah was routed by the army of Yashar'AL, and its army scattered and fled for home.

King Yahuash of Yashar'AL captured Yahudah’s king, Amazyahu son of Yuash and grandson of Ahazyahu, at Bath-shamash. Then he marched to Yahushalam, where he demolished 600 feet of Yahushalam’s wall, from the Aphraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
He carried off all the gold and silver and all the articles from the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he also seized the treasures from the royal palace, along with hostages, and then returned to Samaria.

The rest of the events in Yahuash’s reign and everything he did, including the extent of his power and his war with King Amazyahu of Yahudah, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When Yahuash died, he was buried in Samaria with the kings of Yashar'AL. And his son Yarubuam II became the next king.
King Amazyahu of Yahudah lived for fifteen years after the death of King Yahuash of Yashar'AL.
The rest of the events in Amaztahu’s reign are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
There was a conspiracy against Amazyahu’s life in Yahushalam, and he fled to Lachish. But his enemies sent assassins after him, and they killed him there.
They brought his body back to Yahushalam on a horse, and he was buried with his ancestors in the City of Daud.
All the people of Yahudah had crowned Amazyahu’s sixteen-year-old son, Uzzyahu, as king in place of his father, Amazyahu.
After his father’s death, Uzzyahu rebuilt the town of Alath and restored it to Yahudah.
Yarubuam II, the son of Yahuash, began to rule over Yashar'AL in the fifteenth year of King Amazyahu’s reign in Yahuudah, he reigned in Samaria forty-one years.
He did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he refused to turn from the sins that Yarubuam son of Nebat had led Yashar'AL to commit.

Yarubuam II recovered the territories of Yashar'AL between Labu-hamath and the Dead Sea, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, had promised through Yunah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hapher.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH saw the bitter suffering of everyone in Yashar'AL, and that there was no one in Yashar'AL, slave or free, to help them.
And because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had not said he would blot out the name of Yashar'AL completely, he used Yarubuam II, the son of Yahuash, to save them.

The rest of the events in the reign of Yarubuam II and everything he did—including the extent of his power, his wars, and how he recovered for Yashar'AL both Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Yahudah, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When Yarubuam II died, he was buried in Samaria with the kings of Yashar'AL. Then his son Zacharyahu became the next king.
Uzzyahu son of Amazyahu began to rule over Yahudah in the twenty-seventh year of the reign of King Yarubuam II of Yashar'AL.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam fifty-two years. His mother was Yaculyahu from Yahushalam.
He did what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, just as his father, Amazyahu, had done.
But he did not destroy the pagan shrines, and the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck the king with leprosy, which lasted until the day he died, he lived in isolation in a separate house. The king’s son Yutham was put in charge of the royal palace, and he governed the people of the land.
The rest of the events in Uzzyahu’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
When Uzzyahu died, he was buried with his ancestors in the City of Daud. And his son Yutham became the next king.
Zacharyahu son of Yarubuam II began to rule over Yashar'AL in the thirty-eighth year of King Uzzyahu’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria six months.
Zacharyahu did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as his ancestors had done, he refused to turn from the sins that Yarubuam son of Nabat had led Yashar'AL to commit.
Then Shallum son of Yabash conspired against Zacharyahu, assassinated him in public, and became the next king.
The rest of the events in Zacharyahu’s reign are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s message to Yahu came true: “Your descendants will be kings of Yashar'AL down to the fourth generation.”
Shallum son of Yabash began to rule over Yashar'AL in the thirty-ninth year of King Uzzyahu’s reign in Yahudah. Shallum reigned in Samaria only one month.
Then Manaham son of Gadi went to Samaria from Tirzah and assassinated him, and he became the next king.
The rest of the events in Shallum’s reign, including his conspiracy, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.

At that time Manaham destroyed the town of Tappuah and all the surrounding countryside as far as Tirzah, because its citizens refused to surrender the town, he killed the entire population and ripped open the pregnant women.
Manaham son of Gadi began to rule over Yashar'AL in the thirty-ninth year of King Uzzyahu’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria ten years.
But Manaham did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. During his entire reign, he refused to turn from the sins that Yarubuam son of Nabat had led Yashar'AL to commit.
Then King Tiglath-pilasar of Assyria invaded the land. But Manaham paid him thirty-seven tons of silver to gain his support in tightening his grip on royal power.

Manaham extorted the money from the rich of Yashar'AL, demanding that each of them pay fifty pieces of silver to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned from attacking Yashar'AL and did not stay in the land.
The rest of the events in Manaham’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
When Manaham died, his son Pakahyahu became the next king.
Pakahyahu son of Manaham began to rule over Yashar'AL in the fiftieth year of King Uzzyahu’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria two years.
But Pakahyahu did what was evil in the sight 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he refused to turn from the sins that Yarubuam son of Nabat had led Yashar'AL to commit.

Then Pakah son of Ramalyahu, the commander of Pakahyahu’s army, conspired against him. With fifty men from Gilaad, Pakah assassinated the king, along with Argub and Aryahu, in the citadel of the palace at Samaria. And Pakah reigned in his place.
The rest of the events in Pakahyahu’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
Pakah son of Ramalyahu began to rule over Yashar'AL in the fifty-second year of King Uzzyahu’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria twenty years.
But Pakah did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he refused to turn from the sins that Yarubuam son of Nabat had led Yashar'AL to commit.

During Pakah’s reign, King Tiglath-pilasar of Assyria attacked Yashar'AL again, and he captured the towns of Iyun, Abal-bath-maacah, Yanuah, Kadash, and Hazur, he also conquered the regions of Gilaad, Galily, and all of Naphtali, and he took the people to Assyria as captives.
Then Husha son of Alah conspired against Pakah and assassinated him, he began to rule over Yashar'AL in the twentieth year of Yutham son of Uzzyahu.
The rest of the events in Pakah’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yashar'AL.
Yutham son of Uzzyahu began to rule over Yahudah in the second year of King Pakah’s reign in Yashar'AL.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam sixteen years, his mother was Yarusha, the daughter of Zaduk.
Yutham did what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he did everything his father, Uzzyahu, had done.
But he did not destroy the pagan shrines, and the people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there, he rebuilt the upper gate of the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The rest of the events in Yutham’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
In those days 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH began to send King Razin of Aram and King Pakah of Yashar'AL to attack Yahudah.
When Yutham died, he was buried with his ancestors in the City of Daud. And his son Ahaz became the next king.
Ahaz son of Yutham began to rule over Yahudah in the seventeenth year of King Pakah’s reign in Yashar'AL.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam sixteen years, he did not do what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, as his ancestor Daud had done.

Instead, he followed the example of the kings of Yashar'AL, even sacrificing his own son in the fire. In this way, he followed the detestable practices of the pagan nations 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had driven from the land ahead of the Yasharalym.
He offered sacrifices and burned incense at the pagan shrines and on the hills and under every green tree.
Then King Razin of Aram and King Pakah of Yashar'AL came up to attack Yahushalam. They besieged Ahaz but could not conquer him.
At that time the king of Adum recovered the town of Alath for Adum, he drove out the people of Yahudah and sent Adumites to live there, as they do to this day.
King Ahaz sent messengers to King Tiglath-pilasar of Assyria with this message: “I am your servant and your vassal. Come up and rescue me from the attacking armies of Aram and Yashar'AL.”
Then Ahaz took the silver and gold from the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the palace treasury and sent it as a payment to the Assyrian king.
So the king of Assyria attacked the Aramaan capital of Damascus and led its population away as captives, resettling them in Kir, he also killed King Razin.

King Ahaz then went to Damascus to meet with King Tiglath-pilasar of Assyria. While he was there, he took special note of the altar. Then he sent a model of the altar to Uryahu the priest, along with its design in full detail.
Uryahu followed the king’s instructions and built an altar just like it, and it was ready before the king returned from Damascus.
When the king returned, he inspected the altar and made offerings on it.
He presented a burnt offering and a grain offering, he poured out a liquid offering, and he sprinkled the blood of Shalum offerings on the altar.
Then King Ahaz removed the old bronze altar from its place in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple, between the entrance and the new altar, and placed it on the north side of the new altar.

He told Uryahu the priest, “Use the new altar for the morning sacrifices of burnt offering, the evening grain offering, the king’s burnt offering and grain offering, and the burnt offerings of all the people, as well as their grain offerings and liquid offerings. Sprinkle the blood from all the burnt offerings and sacrifices on the new altar. The bronze altar will be for my personal use only.”
Uryahu the priest did just as King Ahaz commanded him.

Then the king removed the side panels and basins from the portable water carts, he also removed the great bronze basin called the Sea from the backs of the bronze oxen and placed it on the stone pavement.

In deference to the king of Assyria, he also removed the canopy that had been constructed inside the palace for use on the Shabbat day, as well as the king’s outer entrance to the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The rest of the events in Ahaz’s reign and everything he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
When Ahaz died, he was buried with his ancestors in the City of Daud. Then his son Hazakyahu became the next king.
Husha son of Alah began to rule over Yashar'AL in the twelfth year of King Ahaz’s reign in Yahudah, he reigned in Samaria nine years.
He did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but not to the same extent as the kings of Yashar'AL who ruled before him.
King Shalmanasar of Assyria attacked King Husha, so Husha was forced to pay heavy tribute to Assyria.

But Husha stopped paying the annual tribute and conspired against the king of Assyria by asking King So of Mitzraym to help him shake free of Assyria’s power. When the king of Assyria discovered this treachery, he seized Husha and put him in prison.
Then the king of Assyria invaded the entire land, and for three years he besieged the city of Samaria.

Finally, in the ninth year of King Husha’s reign, Samaria fell, and the people of Yashar'AL were exiled to Assyria. They were settled in colonies in Halah, along the banks of the Habur River in Guzan, and in the cities of the Madas.

This disaster came upon the people of Yashar'AL because they worshiped idols. They sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who had brought them safely out of Mitzraym and had rescued them from the power of Phar'uh, the king of Mitzraym.
They had followed the practices of the pagan nations 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had driven from the land ahead of them, as well as the practices the kings of Yashar'AL had introduced.

The people of Yashar'AL had also secretly done many things that were not pleasing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. They built pagan shrines for themselves in all their towns, from the smallest outpost to the largest walled city.
They set up sacred pillars and Asharah poles at the top of every hill and under every green tree.

They offered sacrifices on all the hilltops, just like the nations 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had driven from the land ahead of them. So the people of Yashar'AL had done many evil things, arousing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger.
Yes, they worshiped idols, despite 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s specific and repeated warnings.

Again and again 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had sent his Nabyms and seers to warn both Yashar'AL and Yahudah: “Turn from all your evil ways. Obey my commandments and decrees, the entire law that I commanded your ancestors to obey, and that I gave you through my servants the Nabyms (prophets).”
But the Yasharalym would not listen. They were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to believe in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

They rejected the decrees and the covenant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had made with their ancestors, and they despised all His warnings. They worshiped worthless idols, so they became worthless themselves. They followed the example of the nations around them, disobeying 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command not to imitate them.
They rejected all the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and made two calves from metal. They set up an Asharah pole and worshiped Baal and all the forces of Shamaym.
They even sacrificed their own sons and daughters in the fire. They consulted fortune-tellers and practiced sorcery and sold themselves to evil, arousing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger.
Because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was very angry with Yashar'AL, he swept them away from his presence. Only the tribe of Yahudah remained in the land.
But even the people of Yahudah refused to obey the commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, for they followed the evil practices that Yashar'AL had introduced.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rejected all the descendants of Yashar'AL. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH punished them by handing them over to their attackers until He had banished Yashar'AL from His presence.

For when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH tore Yashar'AL away from the kingdom of Daud, they chose Yarubuam son of Nabat as their king. But Yarubuam drew Yashar'AL away from following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and made them commit a great sin.
And the people of Yashar'AL persisted in all the evil ways of Yarubuam. They did not turn from these sins
until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH finally swept them away from His presence, just as all His Nabyms (prophets) had warned. So Yashar'AL was exiled from their land to Assyria, where they remain to this day.

The king of Assyria transported groups of people from Babylun, Cuthah, Abba, Hamath, and Sepharbaim and resettled them in the towns of Samaria, replacing the people of Yashar'AL. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns.
But since these foreign settlers did not worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH when they first arrived, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent lions among them, which killed some of them.

So a message was sent to the king of Assyria: “The people you have sent to live in the towns of Samaria do not know the religious customs of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the land. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent lions among them to destroy them because they have not worshiped Him correctly.”
The king of Assyria then commanded, “Send one of the exiled priests back to Samaria. Let him live there and teach the new residents the religious customs of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the land.”
So one of the priests who had been exiled from Samaria returned to Bathal and taught the new residents how to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

But these various groups of foreigners also continued to worship their own idols. In town after town where they lived, they placed their idols at the pagan shrines that the people of Samaria had built.
Those from Babylun worshiped idols of their deity Succuth-banuth. Those from Cuthah worshiped their idol Nargal. And those from Hamath worshiped Ashima.
The Abbites worshiped their idols Nibhaz and Tartak. And the people from Sapharbaim even burned their own children as sacrifices to their idols Adrammalach and Anammalach.
These new residents worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but they also appointed from among themselves all sorts of people as priests to offer sacrifices at their places of worship.
And though they worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they continued to follow their own idols according to the religious customs of the nations from which they came.

And this is still going on today. They continue to follow their former practices instead of truly worshiping 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and obeying the decrees, regulations, instructions, and commands 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave the descendants of Ya'aqub, whose name he changed to Yashar'AL.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had made a covenant with the descendants of Ya'aqub and commanded them: “Do not worship any images idols or bow before them or serve them or offer sacrifices to them.
But worship only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who brought you out of Mitzraym with great strength and a powerful arm. Bow down to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH alone, and offer sacrifices only to him.
Be careful at all times to obey the decrees, regulations, instructions, and commands that He wrote for you. You must not worship idols.
Do not forget the covenant I made with you, and do not worship idols.
You must worship only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. He is the one who will rescue you from all your enemies.”
But the people would not listen and continued to follow their former practices.
So while these new residents worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they also worshiped their idols. And to this day their descendants do the same.
Hazakyahu son of Ahaz began to rule over Yahudah in the third year of King Husha’s reign in Yashar'AL.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam twenty-nine years, his mother was Abiyahu, the daughter of Zacharyahu.
He did what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, just as his ancestor Daud had done.

He removed the pagan shrines, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asharah poles, he broke up the bronze serpent that Musha had made, because the people of Yashar'AL had been offering sacrifices to it. The bronze serpent was called Nahushtan.
Hazakyahu trusted in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL. There was no one like him among all the kings of Yahudah, either before or after his time.
He remained faithful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in everything, and he carefully obeyed all the commandments 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given Musha.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with him, and Hazakyahu was successful in everything he did, he revolted against the king of Assyria and refused to pay him tribute.
He also conquered the Philistines as far distant as Gaza and its territory, from their smallest outpost to their largest walled city.
During the fourth year of Hazakyahu’s reign, which was the seventh year of King Husha’s reign in Yashar'AL, King Shalmanasar of Assyria attacked the city of Samaria and began a siege against it.
Three years later, during the sixth year of King Hazakiahu’s reign and the ninth year of King Husha’s reign in Yashar'AL, Samaria fell.
At that time the king of Assyria exiled the Yasharalym to Assyria and placed them in colonies in Halah, along the banks of the Habur River in Guzan, and in the cities of the Madas.
For they refused to listen to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and obey Him. Instead, they violated His covenant, all the laws that Musha 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s servant had commanded them to obey.
In the fourteenth year of King Hazakyahu’s reign, King Sannacharib of Assyria came to attack the fortified towns of Yahudah and conquered them.

King Hazakyahu sent this message to the king of Assyria at Lachish: “I have done wrong. I will pay whatever tribute money you demand if you will only withdraw.” The king of Assyria then demanded a settlement of more than eleven tons of silver and one ton of gold.
To gather this amount, King Hazakyahu used all the silver stored in the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and in the palace treasury.
Hazakiah even stripped the gold from the doors of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple and from the doorposts he had overlaid with gold, and he gave it all to the Assyrian king.

Nevertheless, the king of Assyria sent his commander in chief, his field commander, and his chief of staff from Lachish with a huge army to confront King Hazakyahu in Yahushalam. The Assyrians took up a position beside the aqueduct that feeds water into the upper pool, near the road leading to the field where cloth is washed.

They summoned King Hazakyahu, but the king sent these officials to meet with them: Aliakim son of Hilkyahu, the palace administrator; Shabna the court secretary; and Yuah son of Asaph, the royal historian.
Then the Assyrian king’s chief of staff told them to give this message to Hazakyahu: “This is what the great king of Assyria says: What are you trusting in that makes you so confident?
Do you think that mere words can substitute for military skill and strength? Who are you counting on, that you have rebelled against me?
On Mitzraym? If you lean on Mitzraym, it will be like a reed that splinters beneath your weight and pierces your hand. Phar'uh, the king of Mitzraym, is completely unreliable!

“But perhaps you will say to me, We are trusting in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH! But is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH not the one who was insulted by Hazakyahu? Did Hazakyahu not tear down His altars and make everyone in Yahudah and Yahushalam worship only at the altar here in Yahushalam?
“I will tell you what! Strike a bargain with my master, the king of Assyria. I will give you 2,000 horses if you can find that many men to ride on them!
With your tiny army, how can you think of challenging even the weakest contingent of my master’s troops, even with the help of Mitzraym’s chariots and charioteers?
What’s more, do you think we have invaded your land without 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s direction? 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH himself told us, ‘Attack this land and destroy it!’”

Then Aliakim son of Hilkyahu, Shabna, and Yuah said to the Assyrian chief of staff, “Please speak to us in Aramaic, for we understand it well. Do not speak in Abarym (Hebrew), for the people on the wall will hear.”

But Sannacharib’s chief of staff replied, “Do you think my master sent this message only to you and your master? He wants all the people to hear it, for when we put this city under siege, they will suffer along with you. They will be so hungry and thirsty that they will eat their own dung and drink their own urine.”
Then the chief of staff stood and shouted in Hebrew to the people on the wall, “Listen to this message from the great king of Assyria!
This is what the king says: Do not let Hazakyahu deceive you, he will never be able to rescue you from my power.
Do not let him fool you into trusting in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by saying, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will surely rescue us. This city will never fall into the hands of the Assyrian king!’

“Do not listen to Hazakyahu! These are the terms the king of Assyria is offering: Make Shalum with me, open the gates and come out. Then each of you can continue eating from your own grapevine and fig tree and drinking from your own well.

Then I will arrange to take you to another land like this one, a land of grain and new wine, bread and vineyards, olive groves and honey. Choose life instead of death! “Do not listen to Hazakyahu when he tries to mislead you by saying, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will rescue us!’
Have the idols of any other nations ever saved their people from the king of Assyria?
What happened to the idols of Hamath and Arpad? And what about the idols of Sapharbaim, Hana, and Ibbah? Did any deities rescue Samaria from my power?
What idols of any nation has ever been able to save its people from my power? So what makes you think that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH can rescue Yahushalam from me?”
But the people were silent and did not utter a word because Hazakyahu had commanded them, “Do not answer him.”

Then Aliakim son of Hilkyahu, the palace administrator; Shabna the court secretary; and Yuah son of Asaph, the royal historian, went back to Hazakyahu. They tore their clothes in despair, and they went in to see the king and told him what the Assyrian chief of staff had said.
When King Hazakyahu heard their report, he tore his clothes and put on burlap and went into the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And he sent Aliakim the palace administrator, Shabna the court secretary, and the leading Kuhanym, all dressed in burlap, to the Nabym Yashayahu son of Amuz.
They told him, “This is what King Hazakyahu says: Today is a day of trouble, insults, and dishonored. It is like when a child is ready to be born, but the mother has no strength to deliver the baby.

But perhaps 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has heard the Assyrian chief of staff, sent by the king to defy the living 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and will punish him for his words. Oh, pray for those of us who are left!”
After King Hazakyahu’s officials delivered the king’s message to Yashayahu,
the Nabym replied, “Say to your master, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Do not be disturbed by this blasphemous speech against ME from the Assyrian king’s messengers.
Listen! I Myself will move against him, and the king will receive a message that he is needed at home. So he will return to his land, where I will have him killed with a sword.’”
Meanwhile, the Assyrian chief of staff left Yahushalam and went to consult the king of Assyria, who had left Lachish and was attacking Libnah.

Soon afterward King Sannacharib received word that King Tirhakah of Athiupia was leading an army to fight against him. Before leaving to meet the attack, he sent messengers back to Hazakyahu in Yahushalam with this message:
“This message is for King Hazakyahu of Yahudah. Do not let your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, in whom you trust, deceive you with promises that Yahushalam will not be captured by the king of Assyria.
You know perfectly well what the kings of Assyria have done wherever they have gone. They have completely destroyed everyone who stood in their way! Why should you be any different?
Have the idols of other nations rescued them, such nations as Guzan, Haran, Razaph, and the people of Adan who were in Tal-assar? My predecessors destroyed them all!
What happened to the king of Hamath and the king of Arpad? What happened to the kings of Sapharbaim, Hana, and Ibbah?”
After Hazakyahu received the letter from the messengers and read it, he went up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple and spread it out before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

And Hazakyahu prayed this prayer before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, you are enthroned between the mighty charubim! You alone are 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of all the kingdoms of the Arath. You alone created the Shamaym and the Arath.
Bend down, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and listen! Open your eyes, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and see! Listen to Sannacharib’s words of defiance against the living 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
“It is true, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that the kings of Assyria have destroyed all these nations.

And they have thrown the idols of these nations into the fire and burned them. But of course the Assyrians could destroy them! They were not AL'Mighty at all, only idols of wood and stone shaped by man's hands.
Now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, rescue us from his power; then all the kingdoms of the Arath will know that you alone, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, are 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.”
Then Yashayahu son of Amuz sent this message to Hazakyahu: “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, Dabar: I have heard your prayer about King Sannacharib of Assyria.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has Dabar this word against him: “The virgin daughter of Ziun despises you and laughs at you, the daughter of Yahushalam shakes her head in derision as you flee.
“Whom have you been defying and ridiculing? Against whom did you raise your voice? At whom did you look with such haughty eyes? It was the Qadash One of Yashar'AL!

By your messengers you have defied 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. You have said, ‘With my many chariots I have conquered the highest mountains yes, the remotest peaks of Labanun. I have cut down its tallest cedars and its finest cypress trees. I have reached its farthest corners and explored its deepest forests.
I have dug wells in many foreign lands and refreshed myself with their water. With the sole of my foot I stopped up all the rivers of Mitzraym!’
“But have you not heard? I decided this long ago. Long ago I planned it, and now I am making it happen. I planned for you to crush fortified cities into heaps of rubble.

That is why their people have so little power and are so frightened and confused. They are as weak as grass, as easily trampled as tender green shoots. They are like grass sprouting on a housetop, scorched before it can grow lush and tall.
“But I know you well, where you stay and when you come and go. I know the way you have raged against me.

And because of your raging against me and your arrogance, which I have heard for myself, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth. I will make you return by the same road on which you came.”

Then Yashayahu said to Hazakyahu, “Here is the proof that what I say is true: “This year you will eat only what grows up by itself, and next year you will eat what springs up from that. But in the third year you will plant crops and harvest them; you will tend vineyards and eat their fruit.
And you who are left in Yahudah, who have escaped the ravages of the siege, will put roots down in your own soil and will grow up and flourish.
For a remnant of my people will spread out from Yahushalam, a group of survivors from Mount Ziun. The passionate commitment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will make this happen!

“And this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar about the king of Assyria: “his armies will not enter Yahushalam. They will not even shoot an arrow at it. They will not march outside its gates with their shields nor build banks of earth against its walls.
The king will return to his own country by the same road on which he came, he will not enter this city, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
For my own honor and for the sake of my servant Daud, I will defend this city and protect it.”
That night the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH went out to the Assyrian camp and killed 185,000 Assyrian soldiers. When the surviving Assyrians woke up the next morning, they found corpses everywhere.
Then King Sannacharib of Assyria broke camp and returned to his own land, he went home to his capital of Ninabah and stayed there.
