One day while he was worshiping in the temple of his idol Nisruch, his sons Adrammalach and Sharazar killed him with their swords. They then escaped to the land of Ararat, and another son, Asarhaddun, became the next king of Assyria.

About that time Hazakyahu became deathly ill, and the Nabym Yashayahu son of Amuz went to visit him, he gave the king this message: “This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: Set your affairs in order, for you are going to die, you will not recover from this illness.”
When Hazakyahu heard this, he turned his face to the wall and prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
“Remember, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, how I have always been faithful to you and have served you single-mindedly, always doing what pleases you.” Then he broke down and wept bitterly.
But before Yashayahu had left the middle courtyard, this message came to him from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH:

“Go back to Hazakyahu, the leader of my people. Tell him, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your ancestor Daud, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. I will heal you, and three days from now you will get out of bed and go to the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
I will add fifteen years to your life, and I will rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria. I will defend this city for my own honor and for the sake of my servant Daud.’”
Then Yashayahu said, “Make an ointment from figs.” So Hazakyahu’s servants spread the ointment over the boil, and Hazakyahu recovered!
Meanwhile, Hazakyahu had said to Yashayahu, “What sign will 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH give to prove that he will heal me and that I will go to the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH three days from now?”
YashaYahu replied, “This is the sign from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to prove that he will do as He promised. Would you like the shadow on the sundial to go forward ten steps or backward ten steps?”
“The shadow always moves forward,” Hazakyahu replied, “so that would be easy. Make it go ten steps backward instead.”
So Yashayahu the Nabym asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to do this, and he caused the shadow to move ten steps backward on the sundial of Ahaz!
Soon after this, Marudach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylun, sent Hazakyahu his best wishes and a gift, for he had heard that Hazakyahu had been very sick.

Hazakyahu received the Babylunian envoys and showed them everything in his treasure-houses, the silver, the gold, the spices, and the aromatic oils, he also took them to see his armory and showed them everything in his royal treasuries! There was nothing in his palace or kingdom that Hazakyahu did not show them.
Then Yashayahu the Nabym went to King Hazakyahu and asked him, “What did those men want? Where were they from?” Hazakyahu replied, “They came from the distant land of Babylun.”
“What did they see in your palace?” Yashayahu asked. “They saw everything,” Hazakyahu replied. “I showed them everything I own, all my royal treasuries.”
Then Yashayahu said to Hazakyahu, Listen to this message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH:
The time is coming when everything in your palace, all the treasures stored up by your ancestors until now, will be carried off to Babylun. Nothing will be left, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Some of your very own sons will be taken away into exile. They will become eunuchs who will serve in the palace of Babylun’s king.”
Then Hazakyahu said to Yashayahu, “This message you have given me from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is good.” For the king was thinking, “At least there will be Shalum and security during my lifetime.”

The rest of the events in Hazakyahu’s reign, including the extent of his power and how he built a pool and dug a tunnel to bring water into the city, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
Hazakyahu died, and his son Manassah became the next king.
Manassah was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam fifty-five years. His mother was Haphzibah.
He did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, following the detestable practices of the pagan nations that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had driven from the land ahead of the Yasharalym.

He rebuilt the pagan shrines his father, Hazakyahu, had destroyed, he constructed altars for Baal and set up an Asharah pole, just as King Ahab of Yashar'AL had done, he also bowed before all the powers of the Shamaym and worshiped them.
He built pagan altars in the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said, “My Name will remain in Yahushalam forever.”
He built these altars for all the powers of the Shamaym in both courtyards of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple.

Manassah also sacrificed his own son in the fire, he practiced sorcery and divination, and he consulted with mediums and psychics, he did much that was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, arousing his anger.

Manassah even made a carved image of Asharah and set it up in the Temple, the very place where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had told Daud and his son Shalumah: “My name will be honored forever in this Temple and in Yahushalam, the city I have chosen from among all the tribes of Yashar'AL.
If the Yasharalym will be careful to obey my commands, all the laws my servant Musha gave them, I will not send them into exile from this land that I gave their ancestors.”
But the people refused to listen, and Manassah led them to do even more evil than the pagan nations that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had destroyed when the people of Yashar'AL entered the land.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar through his servants the Nabyms:

“King Manassah of Yahudah has done many detestable things, he is even more wicked than the Amurites, who lived in this land before Yashar'AL, he has caused the people of Yahudah to sin with his idols.
So this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, Dabar: I will bring such disaster on Yahushalam and Yahudah that the ears of those who hear about it will tingle with horror.

I will judge Yahushalam by the same standard I used for Samaria and the same measure I used for the family of Ahab. I will wipe away the people of Yahushalam as one wipes a dish and turns it upside down.
Then I will reject even the remnant of my own people who are left, and I will hand them over as plunder for their enemies.
For they have done great evil in my sight and have angered me ever since their ancestors came out of Mitzraym.”

Manassah also murdered many innocent people until Yahushalam was filled from one end to the other with innocent blood. This was in addition to the sin that he caused the people of Yahudah to commit, leading them to do evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The rest of the events in Manassah’s reign and everything he did, including the sins he committed, are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
When Manassah died, he was buried in the palace garden, the garden of Uzza. Then his son Amun became the next king.
Amun was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam two years. His mother was Mashullamath, the daughter of Haruz from Yutbah.
He did what was evil in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s sight, just as his father, Manassah, had done.
He followed the example of his father, worshiping the same idols his father had worshiped.
He abandoned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of his ancestors, and he refused to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s ways.
Then Amun’s own officials conspired against him and assassinated him in his palace.
But the people of the land killed all those who had conspired against King Amun, and they made his son Yusyahu the next king.
The rest of the events in Amun’s reign and what he did are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza. Then his son Yusiah became the next king.
Yusyahu was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam thirty-one years. His mother was Yadidah, the daughter of Adayahu from Buzkath.
He did what was pleasing in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and followed the example of his ancestor Daud, he did not turn away from doing what was right.
In the eighteenth year of his reign, King Yusyahu sent Shaphan son of Azalyahu and grandson of Mashullam, the court secretary, to the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he told him,
“Go to Hilkyahu the high Kuhan and have him count the money the gatekeepers have collected from the people at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple.
Entrust this money to the men assigned to supervise the restoration of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple. Then they can use it to pay workers to repair the Temple.
They will need to hire carpenters, builders, and masons. Also have them buy the timber and the finished stone needed to repair the Temple.
But do not require the construction supervisors to keep account of the money they receive, for they are honest and trustworthy men.”
Hilkyahu the high Kuhan said to Shaphan the court secretary, “I have found the Book of the Turah (Law) in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple!” Then Hilkyahu gave the scroll to Shaphan, and he read it.
Shaphan went to the king and reported, “Your officials have turned over the money collected at the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to the workers and supervisors at the Temple.”
Shaphan also told the king, “Hilkyahu the Kuhan has given me a scroll.” So Shaphan read it to the king.
When the king heard what was written in the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes in despair.
Then he gave these orders to Hilkyahu the Kuhan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Acbur son of Micayahu, Shaphan the court secretary, and Asayahu the king’s personal adviser:

“Go to the Temple and speak to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for me and for the people and for all Yahudah. Inquire about the words written in this scroll that has been found. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s great anger is burning against us because our ancestors have not obeyed the Dabar in this scroll. We have not been doing everything it says we must do.”

So Hilkyahu the Kuhan, Ahikam, Acbur, Shaphan, and Asayahu went to the New Quarter of Yahushalam to consult with the Nabym Huldah. She was the wife of Shallum son of Tikbah, son of Harhas, the keeper of the Temple wardrobe.
She said to them, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, has spoken! Go back and tell the man who sent you,
‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: I am going to bring disaster on this city and its people. All the words written in the scroll that the king of Yahudah has read will come true.

For my people have abandoned me and offered sacrifices to pagan idols, and I am very angry with them for everything they have done. My anger will burn against this place, and it will not be quenched.’
“But go to the king of Yahudah who sent you to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and tell him: ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL have Dabar concerning the message you have just heard:

You were sorry and humbled yourself before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH when you heard what I said against this city and its people, that this land would be cursed and become desolate. You tore your clothing in despair and wept before me in repentance. And I have indeed heard you, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

So I will not send the promised disaster until after you have died and been buried in Shalum. You will not see the disaster I am going to bring on this city.’ So they took her message back to the king.
Then the king summoned all the elders of Yahudah and Yahushalam.

And the king went up to the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all the people of Yahudah and Yahushalam, along with the Kuhanym and the Nabyms, all the people from the least to the greatest. There the king read to them the entire Book of the Covenant that had been found in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple.

The king took his place of authority beside the pillar and renewed the covenant in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he pledged to obey 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by keeping all his commands, laws, and decrees with all his heart and soul. In this way, he confirmed all the terms of the covenant that were written in the scroll, and all the people pledged themselves to the covenant.

Then the king instructed Hilkyahu the high Kuhan and the Kuhanym of the second rank and the Temple gatekeepers to remove from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple all the articles that were used to worship Baal, Asharah, and all the powers of the Shamaym. The king had all these things burned outside Yahushalam on the terraces of the Kidrun Valley, and he carried the ashes away to Bathal.

He did away with the idolatrous priests, who had been appointed by the previous kings of Yahudah, for they had offered sacrifices at the pagan shrines throughout Yahudah and even in the vicinity of Yahushalam. They had also offered sacrifices to Baal, and to the sun, the moon, the constellations, and to all the powers of the Shamaym.

The king removed the Asharah pole from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple and took it outside Yahushalam to the Kidrun Valley, where he burned it. Then he ground the ashes of the pole to dust and threw the dust over the graves of the people.
He also tore down the living quarters of the male and female shrine prostitutes that were inside the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, where the women wove coverings for the Asharah pole.

Yusyahu brought to Yahushalam all the Kuhanym who were living in other towns of Yahudah, he also defiled the pagan shrines, where they had offered sacrifices, all the way from Gaba to Baarshaba. He destroyed the shrines at the entrance to the gate of Husha, the governor of Yahushalam. This gate was located to the left of the city gate as one enters the city.
The priests who had served at the pagan shrines were not allowed to serve at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s altar in Yahushalam, but they were allowed to eat unleavened bread with the other Kuhanym.
Then the king defiled the altar of Tuphath in the valley of Ban-Hinnum, so no one could ever again use it to sacrifice a son or daughter in the fire as an offering to Mulach.

He removed from the entrance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple the horse statues that the former kings of Yahudah had dedicated to the sun. They were near the quarters of Nathan-malach the eunuch, an officer of the court. The king also burned the chariots dedicated to the sun.

King Yusyahu tore down the altars that the kings of Yahudah had built on the palace roof above the upper room of Ahaz. The king destroyed the altars that Manassah had built in the two courtyards of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple, he smashed them to bits and scattered the pieces in the Kidrun Valley.

The king also desecrated the pagan shrines east of Yahushalam, to the south of the Mount of Corruption, where King Shalumah of Yashar'AL had built shrines for Ashturath, the detestable female idol of the Sidunians; and for Chamush, the detestable idol of the Muabites; and for Mulach, the vile idol of the Ammunites.
He smashed the sacred pillars and cut down the Asharah poles. Then he desecrated these places by scattering the bones of men over them.

The king also tore down the altar at Bathal the pagan shrine that Yarubuam son of Nabat had made when he caused Yashar'AL to sin, he burned down the shrine and ground it to dust, and he burned the Asharah pole.

Then King Yusyahu turned around and noticed several tombs in the side of the hill. He ordered that the bones be brought out, and he burned them on the altar at Bathal to desecrate it. (This happened just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised through the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH when Yarubuam stood beside the altar at the festival.) Then Yusyahu turned and looked up at the tomb of the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who had predicted these things.

“What is that monument over there?” Yusyahu asked. And the people of the town told him, “It is the tomb of the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who came from Yahudah and predicted the very things that you have just done to the altar at Bathal!”
Yusyahu replied, “Leave it alone. Do not disturb his bones.” So they did not burn his bones or those of the old Nabym from Samaria.

Then Yusyahu demolished all the buildings at the pagan shrines in the towns of Samaria, just as he had done at Bathal. They had been built by the various kings of Yashar'AL and had made 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH very angry.
He executed the priests of the pagan shrines on their own altars, and he burned the bones of men on the altars to desecrate them. Finally, he returned to Yahushalam.
King Yusyahu then issued this order to all the people: “You must celebrate the Passover to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, as required in this Book of the Covenant.”
There had not been a Passover celebration like that since the time when the judges ruled in Yashar'AL, nor throughout all the years of the kings of Yashar'AL and Yahudah.
But in the eighteenth year of King Yusyahu’s reign, this Passover was celebrated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Yahushalam.

Yusyahu also got rid of the mediums and psychics, the household idols, and every other kind of detestable practice, both in Yahushalam and throughout the land of Yahudah. He did this in obedience to the laws written in the scroll that Hilkyahu the Kuhan had found in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple.
Never before had there been a king like Yusyahu, who turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all his heart and soul and strength, obeying all the laws of Musha. And there has never been a king like him since.
Even so, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was very angry with Yahudah because of all the wicked things Manassah had done to provoke Him.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “I will also banish Yahudah from my presence just as I have banished Yashar'AL. And I will reject my chosen city of Yahushalam and the Temple where my Name was to be honored.”
The rest of the events in Yusyahu’s reign and all his deeds are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.

While Yusyahu was king, Phar'uh Nacu, king of Mitzraym, went to the Euphrates River to help the king of Assyria. King Yusyahu and his army marched out to fight him, but King Nacu killed him when they met at Magiddu.
Yusyahu’s officers took his body back in a chariot from Magiddu to Yahushalam and buried him in his own tomb. Then the people of the land anointed Yusyahu’s son Yahuahaz and made him the next king.
Yahuahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam three months. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Yarayahu from Libnah.
He did what was evil in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s sight, just as his ancestors had done.

Phar'uh Nacu put Yahuahaz in prison at Riblah in the land of Hamath to prevent him from ruling in Yahushalam, he also demanded that Yahudah pay 7,500 pounds of silver and 75 pounds of gold as tribute.
Pharuh Nacu then installed Aliakim, another of Yusyahu’s son, to reign in place of his father, and he changed Aliakim’s name to Yahuiakim. Yahuahaz was taken to Mitzraym as a prisoner, where he died.
In order to get the silver and gold demanded as tribute by Phar'uh Nacu, Yahuiakim collected a tax from the people of Yahudah, requiring them to pay in proportion to their wealth.
Yahuiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam eleven years. His mother was Zabidah, the daughter of Padayahu from Rumah.
He did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, just as his ancestors had done.
During Yahuiakim’s reign, King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun invaded the land of Yahudah. Yahuiakim surrendered and paid him tribute for three years but then rebelled.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent bands of Babylunian, Aramaan, Muabite, and Ammunite raiders against Yahudah to destroy it, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised through his Nabyms.
These disasters happened to Yahudah because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had decided to banish Yahudah from his presence because of the many sins of Manassah,
who had filled Yahushalam with innocent blood. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH would not forgive this.
The rest of the events in Yahuiakim’s reign and all his deeds are recorded in The Book of the History of the Kings of Yahudah.
When Yahuiakim died, his son Yahuiachin became the next king.
The king of Mitzraym did not venture out of his country after that, for the king of Babylun captured the entire area formerly claimed by Mitzraym, from the Brook of Mitzraym to the Euphrates River.
Yahuiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam three months. His mother was Nahushta, the daughter of Alnathan from Yahushalam.
Yahuiachin did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, just as his father had done.
During Yahuiachin’s reign, the officers of King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun came up against Yahushalam and besieged it.
Nabuchadnazzar himself arrived at the city during the siege.

Then King Yahuiachin, along with the queen mother, his advisers, his commanders, and his officials, surrendered to the Babylunians. In the eighth year of Nabuchadnazzar’s reign, he took Yahuiachin prisoner.

As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said beforehand, Nabuchadnazzar carried away all the treasures from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple and the royal palace, he stripped away all the gold objects that King Shalumah of Yashar'AL had placed in the Temple.
King Nabuchadnazzar took all of Yahushalam captive, including all the commanders and the best of the soldiers, craftsmen, and artisans, 10,000 in all. Only the poorest people were left in the land.
Nabuchadnazzar led King Yahuiachin away as a captive to Babylun, along with the queen mother, his wives and officials, and all Yahushalam’s elite.
He also exiled 7,000 of the best troops and 1,000 craftsmen and artisans, all of whom were strong and fit for war.
Then the king of Babylun installed Mattanyahu, Yahuiachin’s uncle, as the next king, and he changed Mattanyahu’s name to Zadakyahu.
Zadakyahu was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam eleven years. His mother was Hamutal, the daughter of Yaramyahu from Libnah.
But Zadakyahu did what was evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, just as Yahuiakim had done.

These things happened because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger against the people of Yahushalam and Yahudah, until he finally banished them from his presence and sent them into exile. Zadakyahu rebelled against the king of Babylun.

Now it came to pass in the ninth year of Zadakyahu reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun and all his army came against Yahushalam and encamped against it; and they built a siege wall against it all around.
So the city was besieged until the eleventh year of King Zadakyahu.
By the ninth day of the fourth month the famine had become so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land.

Then the city wall was broken through, and all the men of war fled at night by way of the gate between two walls, which was by the king’s garden, even though the Chaldaans were still encamped all around against the city. And the king went by way of the plain.
But the army of the Chaldaans pursued the king, and they overtook him in the plains of Yarichu. All his army was scattered from him.
So they took the king Zadakyahu and brought him up to the king of Babylun at Riblah, and they pronounced judgment on him.
Then they killed the sons of Zadakyahu before his eyes, put out the eyes of Zadakyahu, bound him with bronze fetters, and took him to Babylun.

And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month (which was the nineteenth year of King Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun), Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylun, came to Yahushalam.
He burned the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the king’s house; all the houses of Yahushalam, that is, all the houses of the great, he burned with fire.
And all the army of the Chaldaans who were with the captain of the guard broke down the walls of Yahushalam all around.

Then Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive the rest of the people who remained in the city and the defectors who had deserted to the king of Babylun, with the rest of the multitude.
But the captain of the guard left some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and farmers.
The bronze pillars that were in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the carts and the bronze Sea that were in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the Chaldaans broke in pieces, and carried their bronze to Babylun.
They also took away the pots, the shovels, the trimmers, the spoons, and all the bronze utensils with which the Kuhanym ministered.
The firepans and the basins, the things of solid gold and solid silver, the captain of the guard took away.
The two pillars, one Sea, and the carts, which Shalumah had made for the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the bronze of all these articles was beyond measure.

The height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, and the capital on it was of bronze. The height of the capital was three cubits, and the network and pomegranates all around the capital were all of bronze. The second pillar was the same, with a network.
And the captain of the guard took Sarayahu the chief Kuhan, Zaphanyahu the second Kuhan, and the three doorkeepers.

He also took out of the city an officer who had charge of the men of war, five men of the king’s close associates who were found in the city, the chief recruiting officer of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
So Nabuzaradan, captain of the guard, took these and brought them to the king of Babylun at Riblah.
Then the king of Babylun struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Yahudah was carried away captive from its own land.
Then he made Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor over the people who remained in the land of Yahudah, whom Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun had left.

Now when all the captains of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylun had made Gadalyahu governor, they came to Gadalyahu at Mizpah, Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu, Yuhanan the son of Caraah, Sarayahu the son of Tanhumath the Natuphathite, and Yaazanyahu the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.

And Gadalyahu took an oath before them and their men, and said to them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldaans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylun, and it shall be well with you.”

But it happened in the seventh month that Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu, the son of Alishama, of the royal family, came with ten men and struck and killed Gadalyahu the Yahudym, as well as the Chaldaans who were with him at Mizpah.
And all the people, small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose and went to Mitzraym; for they were afraid of the Chaldaans.

Now it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Yahuiachin king of Yahudah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Avil-Marudach king of Babylun, in the year that he began to reign, released Yahuiachin king of Yahudah from prison.
He spoke kindly to him, and gave him a more prominent seat than those of the kings who were with him in Babylun.
So Yahuiachin changed from his prison garments, and he ate bread regularly before the king all the days of his life.
And as for his provisions, there was a regular ration given him by the king, a portion for each day, all the days of his life.

books.name: I Chronicles
chapters: Adam, Shath, Anush,
Cainan, Mahalalal, Yarad,
Chanuk, Mathusalah, Lamach,
Nuah, Sham, Ham, and Yaphath.
The sons of Yaphath were Gumar, Magug, Madai, Yaban, Tubal, Mashach, and Tiras.
The sons of Gumer were Ashkanaz, Diphath, and Tugarmah.
The sons of Yaban were Alishah, Tarshishah, Kittim, and Rudanim.
The sons of Ham were Cush, Mitzraym, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush were Saba, Habilah, Sabta, Raama, and Sabtacha. The sons of Raama were Shaba and Dadan.
Cush begot Nimrud; he began to be a heroic warrior on the Arath.
Mitzraym begot Ludim, Anamim, Lahabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusym, Casluhym (from whom came the Philistines and the Caphturym).
Canaan begot Sidun, his firstborn, and Hath;
the Yabusite, the Amurite, and the Girgashite;
the Hibite, the Arkite, and the Sinite;
the Arbadites, the Zamarite, and the Hamathite.
The sons of Sham were Alam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gathar, and Mashach.
Arphaxad begot Shalah, and Shalah begot Abar.
To Abar were born two sons: the name of one was Palag, for in his days the Arath was divided; and his brother’s name was Yuktan.
Yuktan begot Almudad, Shalaph, Hazarmabath, Yarah,
Haduram, Uzal, Diklah,
Abal, Abimaal, Shaba,
Uphir, Habilah, and Yubab. All these were the sons of Yuktan.
Sham, Arphaxad, Shalah,
Aber, Palag, Rau,
Sarug, Nahur, Tarah,
and Abram, who is Abraham.
The sons of Abraham were Yachaq and Ishmaal.
These are their genealogies: The firstborn of Ishmaal was Nabayuth; then Kadar, Adbaal, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tama,
Yatur, Naphish, and Kadamah. These were the sons of Ishmaal.
Now the sons born to Katurah, Abraham’s concubine, were Zimran, Yukshan, Madan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Yukshan were Sheba and Dadan.
The sons of Midian were Aphah, Aphar, Hanuch, Abida, and Aldaah. All these were the children of Katurah.
And Abraham begot Yachaq. The sons of Yachaq were Asau and Yashar'AL.
The sons of Asau were Aliphaz, Raual, Yaush, Yaalam, and Kurah.
And the sons of Aliphaz were Taman, Umar, Zaphi, Gatam, and Kanaz; and by Timna, Amalak.
The sons of Raual were Nahath, Zarah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Sair were Lutan, Shubal, Zibaun, Anah, Dishun, Azar, and Dishan.
And the sons of Lutan were Huri and Humam; Lutan’s sister was Timna.
The sons of Shubal were Alian, Manahath, Abal, Shaphi, and Unam. The sons of Zibaun were Ayah and Anah.
The son of Anah are Dishun. The sons of Dishun were Hamran, Ashban, Ithran, and Charan.
The sons of Azar were Bilhan, Zaaban, and Yaakan. The sons of Dishan were Uz and Aran.
Now these were the kings who reigned in the land of Adum before a king reigned over the children of Yashar'AL: Bala the son of Baur, and the name of his city was Dinhabah.
And when Bala died, Yubab the son of Zarah of Buzrah reigned in his place.
When Yubab died, Husham of the land of the Tamanites reigned in his place.
And when Husham died, Hadad the son of Badad, who attacked Midian in the field of Muab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Abith.
When Hadad died, Samlah of Masrakah reigned in his place.
And when Samlah died, Shaul of Rehubuth-by-the-Riber reigned in his place.
When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan the son of Achbur reigned in his place.
And when Baal-Hanan died, Hadad reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Pai. His wife’s name was Mahatabal the daughter of Matrad, the daughter of Mazahab.
Hadad died also. And the chiefs of Adum were Chief Timnah, Chief Aliah, Chief Yathath,
Chief Ahulibamah, Chief Alah, Chief Pinun,
Chief Kanaz, Chief Taman, Chief Mibzar,
Chief Magdial, and Chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Adum.
These were the sons of Yashar'AL: Rauban, Simaun, Lauy, Yahudah, Issachar, Zabulun,
Dan, Ya'asaf, Banyamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Ashar.

The sons of Yahudah were Ar, Unan, and Shalah. These three were born to him by the daughter of Shua, the Canaanitess. ar, the firstborn of Yahudah, was wicked in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH killed him.
And Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him Paraz and Zarah. All the sons of Yahudah were five.
The sons of Paraz were Hazrun and Hamul.
The sons of Zarah were Zimri, Athan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara—five of them in all.
The son of Carmi was Achar, the troubler of Yashar'AL, who transgressed in the accursed thing.
The son of Athan was Azaryahu.
Also the sons of Hazrun who were born to him were Yarahmaal, Ram, and Chaaubai.
Ram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Nahshun, leader of the children of Yahudah;
Nahshun begot Salma, and Salma begot Buaz;
Buaz begot Ubad, and Ubad begot Yassa;
Yassa begot Aliab his firstborn, Abinadab the second, Shima the third,
Nathanal the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Uzam the sixth, and Daud the seventh.
Now their sisters were Zaruyahu and Abigail. And the sons of Zaruyahu were Abishai, Yuab, and Asahal, three.
Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa was Yathar the Ishmaalite.
Calab the son of Hazrun had children by Azubah, his wife, and by Yariuth. Now these were her sons: Yashar, Shubab, and Ardun.
When Azubah died, Calab took Aphrath as his wife, who bore him Hur.
And Hur begot Uri, and Uri begot Bazalal.
Now afterward Hazrun went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilaad, whom he married when he was sixty years old; and she bore him Sagub.
Sagub begot Yair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilaad.
(Gashur and Syria took from them the towns of Yair, with Kanath and its towns—sixty towns.) All these belonged to the sons of Machir the father of Gilaad.
After Hazrun died in Calab Aphrathah, Hazrun’s wife Abiyahu bore him Ashhur the father of Takua.
The sons of Yarahmaal, the firstborn of Hazrun, were Ram, the firstborn, and Bunah, Uran, Uzam, and Ahiyahu.
Yarahmaal had another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Unam.
The sons of Ram, the firstborn of Yarahmaal, were Maaz, Yamin, and Akar.
The sons of Unam were Shammai and Yada. The sons of Shammai were Nadab and Abishur.
And the name of the wife of Abishur was Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Mulid.
The sons of Nadab were Salad and Appaim; Salad died without children.
The son of Appaim was Ishi, the son of Ishi was Sheshan, and Sheshan’s son was Ahlai.
The sons of Yada, the brother of Shammai, were Yathar and Yunathan; Yathar died without children.
The sons of Yunathan were Palath and Zaza. These were the sons of Yarahaal.
Now Shashan had no sons, only daughters. And Shsshan had a Mitzraym servant whose name was Yarha.
Shashan gave his daughter to Yarha his servant as wife, and she bore him Attai.
Attai begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabad;
Zabad begot Aphlal, and Aphlal begot Ubad;
Ubad begot Yahu, and Yahu begot Azaryahu;
Azaryahu begot Halaz, and Halaz begot Alasah;
Alaasah begot Sismai, and Sismai begot Shallum;
Shallum begot Yakamyahu, and Yakamyahu begot Alishama.
The descendants of Calab the brother of Yarahmaal were Masha, his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Marashah the father of Habrun.
The sons of Habrun were Kurah, Tappuah, Rakam, and Shama.
Shama begot Raham the father of Yurkuam, and Rakam begot Shammai.
And the son of Shammai was Maun, and Maun was the father of Bath Zur.
Aphah, Calab’s concubine, bore Haran, Muza, and Gazaz; and Haran begot Gazaz.
And the sons of Yahdai were Ragam, Yutham, Gashan, Palat, Aphah, and Shaaph.
Maachah, Calab’s concubine, bore Shabar and Tirhanah.
She also bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Shaba the father of Machbanah and the father of Gibaa. And the daughter of Calab was Achsah.
These were the descendants of Calab: The sons of Hur, the firstborn of Aphrathah, were Shubal the father of Kirjath Yaarym,
Salma the father of Bathlaham, and Haraph the father of Bath Gadar.
And Shubal the father of Kirjath Yaarim had descendants: Haruah, and half of the families of Manuhuth.
The families of Kiryath Yaarym were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. From these came the Zurathites and the Ashtaulites.
The sons of Salma were Bethlaham, the Natuphathites, Atruth Bath Yuab, half of the Manahathites, and the Zurites.
And the families of the scribes who dwelt at Yabaz were the Tirathites, the Shimaathites, and the Suchathites. These were the Kanites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rachab.
Now these were the sons of Daud who were born to him in Habrun: The firstborn was Amnun, by Ahinuam the Yazraalitess; the second, Danial, by Abigail the Carmalitess;
the third, Absalum the son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Gashur; the fourth, Aduniyahu the son of Haggith;
the fifth, Shephatyahu, by Abital; the sixth, Ithream, by his wife Aglah.
These six were born to him in Habrun. There he reigned seven years and six months, and in Yahushalam he reigned thirty-three years.
And these were born to him in Yahushalam: Shimaa, Shubab, Nathan, and Shalumah, four by Bathshua the daughter of Ammial.
Also there were Ibhar, Alishama, Aliphalat,
Nugah, Naphag, Yaphia,
Alishama, Aliada, and Aliphalat, nine in all.
These were all the sons of Daud, besides the sons of the concubines, and Tamar their sister.
Shalumah’s son was Rahubuam; Abiyahu was his son, Asa his son, Yahushaphat his son,
Yuram his son, Ahazyahu his son, Yuash his son,
Amazyahu his son, Azaryahu his son, Yutham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hazakyahu his son, Manassah his son,
Amun his son, and Yusyahu his son.
The sons of Yusyahu were Yuhanan the firstborn, the second Yuhuiakim, the third Zadakyahu, and the fourth Shallum.
The sons of Yuhuiakim were Yacunyahu his son and Zadakyahu his son.
And the sons of Yacunyahu were Assir, Shaaltial his son,
and Malchiram, Padayahu, Shanazzar, Yakamyahu, Hushama, and Nadabyahu.
The sons of Padayahu were Zarubbabal and Shimai. The sons of Zarubbabal were Mashullam, Hananyahu, Shalumith their sister,
and Hashubah, Uhal, Barachyahu, Hasadyahu, and Yushab-Hasad, five in all.
The sons of Hananyahu were Palatyahu and Yashayahu, the sons of Raphayahu, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Ubadyahu, and the sons of Shachanyahu.
The son of Shachanyahu was Shamayahu. The sons of Shemayahu were Hattush, Igal, Baryahu, Naaryahu, and Shaphat, six in all.
The sons of Naaryahu were Aliuanai, Hazakyahu, and Azrikam, three in all.
The sons of Aliuanai were Hudabyahu, Aliashib, Palayahu, Akkub, Yuhanan, Dalayahu, and Anani, seven in all.
The sons of Yahudah were Paraz, Hazrun, Carmi, Hur, and Shubal.
And Rayahu the son of Shubal begot Yahath, and Yahath begot Ahumai and Lahad. These were the families of the Zurathites.
These were the sons of the father of Atam: Yazraal, Ishma, and Idbash; and the name of their sister was Hazalalpuni;
and Panual was the father of Gadur, and Azar was the father of Hushah. These were the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Aphrathah the father of Bathlaham.
And Ashhur the father of Takua had two wives, Halah and Naarah.
Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Haphar, Tamani, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah.
The sons of Halah were Zarath, Zuhar, and Athnan;
and Kuz begot Anub, Zubabah, and the families of Aharhal the son of Harum.
Now Yabaz was more honorable than his brothers, and his mother called his name Yabaz, saying, “Because I bore him in pain.”

And Yabaz called on the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL saying, “Oh, that You would barak me indeed, and enlarge my territory, that Your hand would be with me, and that You would keep me from evil, that I may not cause pain!” So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH granted him what he requested.
Chalub the brother of Shuhah begot Mahir, who was the father of Ashtun.
And Ashtun begot Bath-Rapha, Pasah, and Tahinnah the father of Ir-Nahash. These were the men of Rechah.
The sons of Kanaz were Uthnial and Sarayahu. The sons of Uthnial were Hathath,
and Maunuthai who begot Uphrah. Sarayahu begot Yuab the father of Ga Harashim, for they were craftsmen.
The sons of Calab the son of Yaphunnah were Iru, Alah, and Naam. The son of Alah was Kanaz.
The sons of Yahallalal were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asaral.
The sons of Azrah were Yathar, Marad, Aphar, and Yalun. And Marad’s wife bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Ashtamua.
(His wife Yahudiyah bore Yarad the father of Gadur, Habar the father of Suchuh, and Yakuthial the father of Zanuah.) And these were the sons of Bithyahu the daughter of Phar'uh, whom Marad took.
The sons of Hudyahu’s wife, the sister of Naham, were the fathers of Kailah the Garmite and of Ashtamua the Maachathite.
And the sons of Shimun were Amnun, Rinnah, Ban-Hanan, and Tilun. And the sons of Ishi were Zuhath and Ban-Zuhath.
The sons of Shalah the son of Yahudah were Ar the father of Lacah, Laadah the father of Marashah, and the families of the house of the linan workers of the house of Ashbaa;
also Yukim, the men of Chuzaba, and Yuash; Saraph, who ruled in Muab, and Yashubi-Laham. Now the records are ancient.
These were the potters and those who dwell at Nataim and Gadarah; there they dwelt with the king for his work.
The sons of Simaun were Namual, Yamin, Yarib, Zarah, and Shaul,
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, and Mishma his son.
And the sons of Mishma were Hamual his son, Zacchur his son, and Shimai his son.
Shimai had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers did not have many children, nor did any of their families multiply as much as the children of Yahudah.
They dwelt at Baarshaba, Muladah, Hazar Shual,
Bilhah, Azam, Tulad,
Bathual, Hurmah, Ziklag,
Bath Marcabuth, Hazar Susim, Bath Biri, and at Shaaraim. These were their cities until the reign of Daud.
And their villages were Atam, Ain, Rimmun, Tuchan, and Ashan—five cities—
and all the villages that were around these cities as far as Baal. These were their dwelling places, and they maintained their genealogy:
Mashubab, Yamlach, and Yushah the son of Amazyahu;
Yual, and Yahu the son of Yushibyahu, the son of Sarayahu, the son of Asial;
Aliuanai, Yaakubah, Yashuhayahu, Asayahu, Adial, Yasimial, and Banayahu;
Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allun, the son of Yadayahu, the son of Shimri, the son of Shamaiah,
these mentioned by name were leaders in their families, and their father’s house increased greatly.
So they went to the entrance of Gadur, as far as the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
And they found rich, good pasture, and the land was broad, quiet, and in Shalum; for some Hamites formerly lived there.

These recorded by name came in the days of Hazakyahu king of Yahudah; and they attacked their tents and the Maunites who were found there, and utterly destroyed them, as it is to this day. So they dwelt in their place, because there was pasture for their flocks there.
Now some of them, five hundred men of the sons of Simaun, went to Mount Seir, having as their captains Palatyahu, Naaryahu, Raphayahu, and Uzzyahu, the sons of Ishi.
And they defeated the rest of the Amalakites who had escaped. They have dwelt there to this day.

Now the sons of Rauban the firstborn of Yashar'AL he was indeed the firstborn, but because he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Ya'asaf, the son of Yashar'AL, so that the genealogy is not listed according to the birthright;
Yet Yahudah prevailed over his brothers, and from him came a ruler, although the birthright was Ya'asaf’s
the sons of Rauban the firstborn of Yashar'AL were Hanuch, Pallu, Hazrun, and Carmi.
The sons of Yual were Shamayahu his son, Gug his son, Shimai his son,
Micah his son, Raayahu his son, Baal his son,
and Baarah his son, whom Tiglath-Pilasar king of Assyria carried into captivity. He was leader of the Raubanites.
And his brethren by their families, when the genealogy of their generations was registered: the chief, Yaial, and Zacharyahu,
and Bala the son of Azaz, the son of Shama, the son of Yual, who dwelt in Aruar, as far as Nabu and Baal Maun.
Eastward they settled as far as the entrance of the wilderness this side of the River Euphrates, because their cattle had multiplied in the land of Gilaad.
Now in the days of Shaul they made war with the Hagrites, who fell by their hand; and they dwelt in their tents throughout the entire area east of Gilaad.
And the children of Gad dwelt next to them in the land of Bashan as far as Salcah:
Yual was the chief, Shapham the next, then Yaanai and Shaphat in Bashan,
and their brethren of their father’s house: Michaal, Mashullam, Shaba, Yurai, Yachan, Zia, and Abar, seven in all.
These were the children of Abihail the son of Huri, the son of Yaruah, the son of Gilaad, the son of Michaal, the son of Yashishai, the son of Yahdu, the son of Buz;
Ahi the son of Abdial, the son of Guni, was chief of their father’s house.
And the Gadites dwelt in Gilaad, in Bashan and in its villages, and in all the common-lands of Sharun within their borders.
All these were registered by genealogies in the days of Yutham king of Yahudah, and in the days of Yarubuam king of Yashar'AL.

The sons of Rauban, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manassah had forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty valiant men, men able to bear shield and sword, to shoot with the bow, and skillful in war, who went to war.
They made war with the Hagrites, Yatur, Naphish, and Nudab.

And they were helped against them, and the Hagrites were delivered into their hand, and all who were with them, for they cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the battle. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH heeded their prayer, because they put their trust in Him.
Then they took away their livestock, fifty thousand of their camels, two hundred and fifty thousand of their sheep, and two thousand of their donkeys, also one hundred thousand of their men;
for many fell dead, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was fighting against them in the battle. And they dwelt in their place until the captivity.
So the children of the half-tribe of Manassah dwelt in the land. Their numbers increased from Bashan to Baal Harmun, that is, to Sanir, or Mount Harmun.
These were the heads of their fathers’ houses: Aphar, Ishi, Alial, Azrial, Yaramyahu, Hudabyahu, and Yahdial. They were mighty men of valor, famous men, and heads of their fathers’ houses.
And they were unfaithful to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers, and played the harlot after the idols of the peoples of the land, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had destroyed before them.

So the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, that is, Tiglath-pilasar king of Assyria, and he carried the Raubanites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manassah into captivity, he took them to Halah, Habur, Hara, and the river of Guzan to this day.
The sons of Lauy were Garshun, Kuhath, and Marari.
The sons of Kuhath were Amram, Izhar, Habrun, and Uzzyahu.
The children of Amram were Aarun, Musha, and Miriam. And the sons of Aarun were Nadab, Abihu, Alaazar, and Ithamar.
Alaazar begot Phinahas, and Phinahas begot Abishua;
Abishua begot Bukki, and Bukki begot Uzzi;
Uzzi begot Zarahyahu, and Zarahyahu begot Maraiuth;
Maraiuth begot Amaryahu, and Amaryahu begot Ahitub;
Ahitub begot Zaduk, and Zaduk begot Ahimaaz;
Ahimaaz begot Azaryahu, and Azaryahu begot Yuhanan;
Yuhanan begot Azaryahu (it was he who ministered as Kuhan in the temple that Shalumah built in Yahushalam);
Azaryahu begot Amaryahu, and Amaryahu begot Ahitub;
Ahitub begot Zaduk, and Zaduk begot Shallum;
Shallum begot Hilkyahu, and Hilkyahu begot Azaryahu;
Azaryahu begot Sarayahu, and Sarayahu begot Yahuzadak.
Yahuzadak went into captivity when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH carried Yahudah and Yahushalam into captivity by the hand of Nabuchadnazzar.
The sons of Lauy were Garshun, Kuhath, and Marari.
These are the names of the sons of Garshun: Libni and Shimai.
The sons of Kuhath were Amram, Izhar, Hebrun, and Uzzial.
The sons of Marari were Mahli and Mushi. Now these are the families of the Lauym according to their fathers:
Of Garshun were Libni his son, Yahath his son, Zimmah his son,
Yuah his son, Iddu his son, Zarah his son, and Yaatherai his son.
The sons of Kuhath were Amminadab his son, Kurah his son, Assir his son,
Alkanah his son, Abiasaph his son, Assir his son,
Tahath his son, Urial his son, Uzzyahu his son, and Shaul his son.
The sons of Alkanah were Amasai and Ahimuth.
As for Alkanah, the sons of Alkanah were Zuphai his son, Nahath his son,
Aliab his son, Yaruham his son, and Alkanah his son.
The sons of Samual were Yual the firstborn, and Abiyahu the second.
The sons of Merari were Mahli, Libni his son, Shimai his son, Uzzah his son,
Shimaa his son, Haggyahu his son, and Asayahu his son.
Now these are the men whom Daud appointed over the service of song in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, after the ark came to rest.

They were ministering with music before the dwelling place of the tabernacle of meeting, until Shalumah had built the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Yahushalam, and they served in their office according to their order.
And these are the ones who ministered with their sons: Of the sons of the Kuhathites were Haman the singer, the son of Yual, the son of Shamu'AL,
the son of Alkanah, the son of Yaruham, the son of Alial, the son of Tuah,
the son of Zuph, the son of Alkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,
the son of Alkanah, the son of Yual, the son of Azaryahu, the son of Zaphanyahu,
the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Abiasaph, the son of Kurah,
the son of Izhar, the son of Kuhath, the son of Lauy, the son of Yashar'AL.
And his brother Asaph, who stood at his right hand, was Asaph the son of Barachyahu, the son of Shimaa,
the son of Michaal, the son of Baasayahu, the son of Malchiyahu,
the son of Athni, the son of Zarah, the son of Adayahu,
the son of Athan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimai,
the son of Yahath, the son of Garshun, the son of Lauy.
Their brethren, the sons of Marari, on the left hand, were Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
the son of Hashabyahu, the son of Amazyahu, the son of Hilkyahu,
the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shamar,
the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Marari, the son of Lauy.
And their brethren, the Lauym, were appointed to every kind of service of the tabernacle of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

But Aarun and his sons offered sacrifices on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense, for all the work of the Most Qadash Place, and to make atonement for Yashar'AL, according to all that Musha the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded.
Now these are the sons of Aarun: Alaazar his son, Phinahas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zarahyahu his son,
Maraiuth his son, Amaryahu his son, Ahitub his son,
Zaduk his son, and Ahimaaz his son.
Now these are their dwelling places throughout their settlements in their territory, for they were given by lot to the sons of Aarun, of the family of the Kuhathites:
They gave them Habrun in the land of Yahudah, with its surrounding common-lands.
But the fields of the city and its villages they gave to Calab the son of Yaphunnah.
And to the sons of Aarun they gave one of the cities of refuge, Habrun; also Libnah with its common-lands, Yattir, Ashtemua with its common-lands,
Hilan with its common-lands, Dabir with its common-lands,
Ashan with its common-lands, and Bath Shamash with its common-lands.
And from the tribe of Banyamin: Gaba with its common-lands, Alamath with its common-lands, and Anathuth with its common-lands. All their cities among their families were thirteen.
To the rest of the family of the tribe of the Kuhathites they gave by lot ten cities from half the tribe of Manassah.

And to the sons of Garshun, throughout their families, they gave thirteen cities from the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Ashar, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the tribe of Manassah in Bashan.
To the sons of Marari, throughout their families, they gave twelve cities from the tribe of Rauban, from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zabulun.
So the children of Yashar'AL gave these cities with their common-lands to the Lauym.
And they gave by lot from the tribe of the children of Yahudah, from the tribe of the children of Simaun, and from the tribe of the children of Banyamin these cities which are called by their names.
Now some of the families of the sons of Kuhath were given cities as their territory from the tribe of Aphraim.
And they gave them one of the cities of refuge, Shacham with its common-lands, in the mountains of Aphraim, also Gazar with its common-lands,
Yukmaam with its common-lands, Bath Hurun with its common-lands,
Aiyalun with its common-lands, and Gath Rimmun with its common-lands.
And from the half-tribe of Manassah: Anar with its common-lands and Bilaam with its common-lands, for the rest of the family of the sons of Kuhath.
From the family of the half-tribe of Manassah the sons of Garshun were given Gulan in Bashan with its common-lands and Ashtaruth with its common-lands.
And from the tribe of Issachar: Kadash with its common-lands, Dabarath with its common-lands,
Ramuth with its common-lands, and Anam with its common-lands.
And from the tribe of Ashar: Mashal with its common-lands, Abdun with its common-lands,
Hukuk with its common-lands, and Rahub with its common-lands.
And from the tribe of Naphtali: Kadash in Galily with its common-lands, Hammun with its common-lands, and Kiryathaim with its common-lands.
From the tribe of Zabulun the rest of the children of Marari were given Rimmun with its common-lands and Tabur with its common-lands.

And on the other side of the Yurdan, across from Yarichu, on the east side of the Yurdan, they were given from the tribe of Rauban: Bazar in the wilderness with its common-lands, Yahzah with its common-lands,
Kadamuth with its common-lands, and Maphaath with its common-lands.
And from the tribe of Gad: Ramuth in Gilaad with its common-lands, Mahanaim with its common-lands,
Hashbun with its common-lands, and Yazar with its common-lands.
The sons of Issachar were Tula, Puah, Yashub, and Shimrun, four in all.

The sons of Tula were Uzzi, Raphayahu, Yarial, Yahmai, Yibsam, and Shamu'AL, heads of their father’s house. The sons of Tula were mighty men of valor in their generations; their number in the days of Daud was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
The son of Uzzi was Izrahyahu, and the sons of Izrahyahu were Michaal, Ubadyahu, Yual, and Ishyahu. All five of them were chief men.
And with them, by their generations, according to their fathers’ houses, were thirty-six thousand troops ready for war; for they had many wives and sons.
Now their brethren among all the families of Issachar were mighty men of valor, listed by their genealogies, eighty-seven thousand in all.
The sons of Banyamin were Bala, Bachar, and Yadiaal, three in all.

The sons of Bala were Azbun, Uzzi, Uzzial, Yarimuth, and Iri, five in all. They were heads of their fathers’ houses, and they were listed by their genealogies, twenty-two thousand and thirty-four mighty men of valor.
The sons of Bachar were Zamirah, Yuash, Aliazar, Aliuanai, Umri, Yarimuth, Abiyahu, Anathoth, and Alamath. All these are the sons of Bachar.
And they were recorded by genealogy according to their generations, heads of their fathers’ houses, twenty thousand two hundred mighty men of valor.
The son of Yadiaal was Bilhan, and the sons of Bilhan were Yaush, Banyamin, Ahud, Chanaanah, Zathan, Tharshish, and Ahishahar.
All these sons of Yadiaal were heads of their fathers’ houses; there were seventeen thousand two hundred mighty men of valor fit to go out for war and battle.
Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir, and Hushim was the son of Ahar.
The sons of Naphtali were Yahzial, Guni, Yazar, and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah.
The descendants of Manassah: his Syrian concubine bore him Machir the father of Gilaad, the father of Asrial.
Machir took as his wife the sister of Huppim and Shuppim, whose name was Maachah. The name of Gilaad’s grandson was Zaluphahad, but Zaluphahad begot only daughters.
(Maachah the wife of Machir bore a son, and she called his name Parash. The name of his brother was Sharash, and his sons were Ulam and Rakam.
The son of Ulam was Badan.) These were the descendants of Gilaad the son of Machir, the son of Manassah.
His sister Hammulakath bore Ishhud, Abiazelar, and Mahlah.
And the sons of Shamida were Ahian, Shacham, Likhi, and Aniam.
The sons of Aphraim were Shuthalah, Barad his son, Tahath his son, Aladah his son, Tahath his son,
Zabad his son, Shuthalah his son, and Azar and Alaad. The men of Gath who were born in that land killed them because they came down to take away their cattle.
Then Aphraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him.
And when he went in to his wife, she conceived and bore a son; and he called his name Baryahu, because tragedy had come upon his house.
Now his daughter was Shaarah, who built Lower and Upper Bath Hurun and Uzzan Shaarah;
and Raphah was his son, as well as Rashaph, and Talah his son, Tahan his son,
Laadan his son, Ammihud his son, Alishama his son,
Nun his son, and Yushua his son.
Now their possessions and dwelling places were Bathal and its towns: to the east Naaran, to the west Gazar and its towns, and Shacham and its towns, as far as Ayyah and its towns;

and by the borders of the children of Manassah were Bath Shaan and its towns, Taanach and its towns, Magiddu and its towns, Dur and its towns. In these dwelt the children of Ya'asaf, the son of Yashar'AL.
The sons of Ashar were Imnah, Ishbah, Ishbi, Baryahu, and their sister Sarah.
The sons of Baryahu were Habar and Malchial, who was the father of Birzaith.
And Habar begot Yaphlat, Shumar, Hutham, and their sister Shua.
The sons of Yaphlat were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashbath. These were the children of Yaphlat.
The sons of Shamar were Ahi, Ruhgah, Yahubbah, and Aram.
And the sons of his brother Halam were Zuphah, Imna, Shalash, and Amal.
The sons of Zuphah were Suah, Harnaphar, Shual, Bari, Imrah,
Bazar, Hud, Shamma, Shilshah, Yithran, and Baara.
The sons of Yathar were Yaphunnah, Pispah, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla were Arah, Hanial, and Rizia.

All these were the children of Ashar, heads of their fathers’ houses, choice men, mighty men of valor, chief leaders. And they were recorded by genealogies among the army fit for battle; their number was twenty-six thousand.
Now Banyamin begot Bala his firstborn, Ashbal the second, Aharah the third,
Nuhah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.
The sons of Bala were Addar, Gara, Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, Ahuah,
Gara, Shaphuphan, and Huram.
These are the sons of Ahud, who were the heads of the fathers’ houses of the inhabitants of Gaba, and who forced them to move to Manahath:
Naaman, Ahiyahu, and Gara who forced them to move. He begot Uzza and Ahihud.
Also Shaharaim had children in the country of Muab, after he had sent away Hushim and Baara his wives.
By Hudash his wife he begot Yubab, Zibia, Masha, Malcam,
Yauz, Sachyahu, and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of their fathers’ houses.
And by Hushim he begot Abitub and Alpaal.
The sons of Alpaal were Aber, Misham, and Shamad, who built Unu and Lud with its towns;
and Baryahu and Shama, who were heads of their fathers’ houses of the inhabitants of Aiyalun, who drove out the inhabitants of Gath.
Ahiu, Shashak, Yaramuth,
Zabadyahu, Arad, Adar,
Michaal, Ispah, and Yuha were the sons of Baryahu.
Zabadyahu, Meshullam, Hizki, Habar,
Ishmarai, Yizlyahu, and Yubab were the sons of Alpaal.
Yakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
Alianai, Zillethai, Alial,
Adayahu, Barayahu, and Shimrath were the sons of Shimai.
Ishpan, Abar, Alial,
Abdun, Zichri, Hanan,
Hananyahu, Alam, Antuthiyahu,
Iphdayahu, and Panual were the sons of Shashak.
Shamsharai, Shaharyahu, Athalyahu,
Yaareshyahu, Aliyahu, and Zichri were the sons of Yaruham.
These were heads of the fathers’ houses by their generations, chief men. These dwelt in Yahushalam.
Now the father of Gibaun, whose wife’s name was Maacah, dwelt at Gibaun.
And his firstborn son was Abdun, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
Gadur, Ahiu, Zachar,
and Mikluth, who begot Shimaah. They also dwelt alongside their relatives in Yahushalam, with their brethren.
Nar begot Kish, Kish begot Shaul, and Shaul begot Yunathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Ash-Baal.
The son of Yunathan was Marib-Baal, and Marib-Baal begot Micah.
The sons of Micah were Pithun, Malach, Taraa, and Ahaz.
And Ahaz begot Yahuaddah; Yahuaddah begot Alamath, Azmabath, and Zimri; and Zimri begot Muza.
Muza begot Binea, Raphah his son, Alaasah his son, and Azal his son.
Azal had six sons whose names were these: Azrikam, Bucharu, Ishmaal, Shaaryahu, Ubadyahu, and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azal.
And the sons of Ashak his brother were Ulam his firstborn, Yaush the second, and Aliphalat the third.
The sons of Ulam were mighty men of valor, archers. They had many sons and grandsons, one hundred and fifty in all. These were all sons of Banyamin.
So all Yashar'AL was recorded by genealogies, and indeed, they were inscribed in the book of the kings of Yashar'AL. But Yahudah was carried away captive to Babylun because of their unfaithfulness.
And the first inhabitants who dwelt in their possessions in their cities were Yashar'AL, Kuhanym, Lauym, and the Nathinym.
Now in Yahushalam the children of Yahudah dwelt, and some of the children of Banyamin, and of the children of Aphraim and Manassah
Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Umri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the descendants of Paraz, the son of Yahudah.
Of the Shilunites: Yashayahu the firstborn and his sons.
Of the sons of Zarah: Yaual, and their brethren, six hundred and ninety.
Of the sons of Banyamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hudabyahu, the son of Hassanuah;
Ibnayahu the son of Yaruham; Alah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri; Mashullam the son of Shaphatyahu, the son of Raual, the son of Ibniyahu;
and their brethren, according to their generations—nine hundred and fifty-six. All these men were heads of their father’s houses.
Of the Kuhanym: Yadayahu, Yahuiarib, and Yachin;
Azaryahu the son of Hilkyahu, the son of Mashullam, the son of Zaduk, the son of Maraiuth, the son of Ahitub, the officer over the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH;
Adayahu the son of Yaruham, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchiyahu; Maasai the son of Adial, the son of Yahzarah, the son of Mashullam, the son of Meshillamith, the son of Immar;
and their brethren, heads of their fathers’ houses, one thousand seven hundred and sixty. They were very able men for the work of the service of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Of the Lauym: Shamayahu the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabyahu, of the sons of Marari;
Bakbakkar, Harash, Galal, and Mattanyahu the son of Micah, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph;
Obadyahu the son of Shemayahu, the son of Galal, the son of Yaduthun; and Barachyahu the son of Asa, the son of Alkanah, who lived in the villages of the Natuphathites.
And the gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmun, Ahiman, and their brethren. Shallum was the chief.
Until then they had been gatekeepers for the camps of the children of Lauy at the King’s Gate on the east.

Shallum the son of Kuraa, the son of Abiasaph, the son of Kurah, and his brethren, from his father’s house, the Kurahites, were in charge of the work of the service, gatekeepers of the tabernacle. Their fathers had been keepers of the entrance to the camp of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And Phinahas the son of Alaazar had been the officer over them in time past; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with him.
Zacharyahu the son of Mashalamiah was keeper of the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
All those chosen as gatekeepers were two hundred and twelve. They were recorded by their genealogy, in their villages. Daud and Shamual the seer had appointed them to their trusted office.
So they and their children were in charge of the gates of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the house of the tabernacle, by assignment.
The gatekeepers were assigned to the four directions: the east, west, north, and south.
And their brethren in their villages had to come with them from time to time for seven days.
For in this trusted office were four chief gatekeepers; they were Lauym. And they had charge over the chambers and treasuries of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And they lodged all around the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH because they had the responsibility, and they were in charge of opening it every morning.
Now some of them were in charge of the serving vessels, for they brought them in and took them out by count.
Some of them were appointed over the furnishings and over all the implements of the sanctuary, and over the fine flour and the wine and the oil and the incense and the spices.
And some of the sons of the Kuhanym made the ointment of the spices.
Mattithyahu of the Lauym, the firstborn of Shallum the Kurahite, had the trusted office over the things that were baked in the pans.
And some of their brethren of the sons of the Kuhathites were in charge of preparing the showbread for every Shabbat.
These are the singers, heads of the fathers’ houses of the Lauym, who lodged in the chambers, and were free from other duties; for they were employed in that work day and night.
These heads of the fathers’ houses of the Lauym were heads throughout their generations. They dwelt at Yahushalam.
Yaial the father of Gibaun, whose wife’s name was Maacah, dwelt at Gibaun.
His firstborn son was Abdun, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nar, Nadab,
Gadur, Ahiu, Zacharyahu, and Mikluth.
And Mikluth begot Shimaam. They also dwelt alongside their relatives in Yahushalam, with their brethren.
Nar begut Kish, Kish begot Shaul, and Shaul begot Yunathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Ash-Baal.
The son of Yunathan was Marib-Baal, and Marib-Baal begot Micah.
The sons of Micah were Pithun, Malach, Tahraa, and Ahaz.
And Ahaz begot Yarah; Yarah begot Alamath, Azmabath, and Zimri; and Zimri begot Muza;
Muza begot Binaa, Raphayahu his son, Alaasah his son, and Azal his son.
And Azal had six sons whose names were these: Azrikam, Bucharu, Ishmaal, Shaaryahu, Obadyahu, and Hanan; these were the sons of Azal.
Now the Philistines fought against Yashar'AL; and the men of Yashar'AL fled from before the Philistines, and fell slain on Mount Gilbua.
Then the Philistines followed hard after Shaul and his sons. And the Philistines killed Yunathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, Shaul’s sons.
The battle became fierce against Shaul. The archers hit him, and he was wounded by the archers.

Then Shaul said to his armorbearer, “Draw your sword, and thrust me through with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and abuse me.” But his armorbearer would not, for he was greatly afraid. Therefore Shaul took a sword and fell on it.
And when his armorbearer saw that Shaul was dead, he also fell on his sword and died.
So Shaul and his three sons died, and all his house died together.
And when all the men of Yashar'AL who were in the valley saw that they had fled and that Shaul and his sons were dead, they forsook their cities and fled; then the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
So it happened the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Shaul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilbua.
And they stripped him and took his head and his armor, and sent word throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news in the temple of their idols and among the people.
Then they put his armor in the temple of their idols, and fastened his head in the temple of Dagun.
And when all Yabash Gilaad heard all that the Philistines had done to Shaul,
all the valiant men arose and took the body of Shaul and the bodies of his sons; and they brought them to Yabash, and buried their bones under the tamarisk tree at Yabash, and fasted seven days.
So Shaul died for his unfaithfulness which he had committed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, because he did not keep the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and also because he consulted a medium for guidance.
But he did not inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH killed Shaul, and turned the kingdom over to Daud the son of Yassa.
Then all Yashar'AL came together to Daud at Habrun, saying, “Indeed we are your bone and your flesh.

Also, in time past, even when Shaul was king, you were the one who led Yashar'AL out and brought them in; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH said to you, ‘You shall shepherd My people Yashar'AL, and be ruler over My people Yashar'AL.’ ”

Therefore all the elders of Yashar'AL came to the king at Habrun, and Daud made a covenant with them at Habrun before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And they anointed Daud king over Yashar'AL, according to the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by Shamu'AL.
And Daud and all Yashar'AL went to Yahushalam, which is Yabus, where the Yabusites were, the inhabitants of the land.
But the inhabitants of Yabus said to Daud, “You shall not come in here!” Nevertheless Daud took the stronghold of Ziun (that is, the City of Daud).
Now Daud said, “Whoever attacks the Yabusites first shall be chief and captain.” And Yuab the son of Zaruyahu went up first, and became chief.
Then Daud dwelt in the stronghold; therefore they called it the City of Daud.
And he built the city around it, from the Millo to the surrounding area. Yuab repaired the rest of the city.
So Daud went on and became great, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut was with him.

Now these were the heads of the mighty men whom Daud had, who strengthened themselves with him in his kingdom, with all Yashar'AL, to make him king, according to the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH concerning Yashar'AL.
And this is the number of the mighty men whom Daud had: Yashubaam the son of a Hachmunita, chief of the captains; he had lifted up his spear against three hundred, killed by him at one time.
After him was Aleaazar the son of Dudu, the Ahuhite, who was one of the three mighty men.
He was with Daud at Pasdammim. Now there the Philistines were gathered for battle, and there was a piece of ground full of barley. So the people fled from the Philistines.
But they stationed themselves in the middle of that field, defended it, and killed the Philistines. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought about a great victory.
Now three of the thirty chief's men went down to the rock to Daud, into the cave of Adullam; and the army of the Philistines encamped in the Valley of Raphaim.
Daud was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Bathlaham.
And Daud said with longing, “Oh, that someone would give me a drink of water from the well of Bathlaham, which is by the gate!”

So the three broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the well of Bathlaham that was by the gate, and took it and brought it to Daud. Nevertheless Daud would not drink it, but poured it out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

And he said, “Far be it from me, O my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, that I should do this! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy? For at the risk of their lives they brought it.” Therefore he would not drink it. These things were done by the three mighty men.
Abishai the brother of Yuab was chief of another three, he had lifted up his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name among these three.
Of the three he was more honored than the other two men. Therefore he became their captain. However he did not attain to the first three.

Banaiyah was the son of Yahuiada, the son of a valiant man from Kabzaal, who had done many deeds, he had killed two lion-like heroes of Muab, he also had gone down and killed a lion in the midst of a pit on a snowy day.

And he killed a Mitzraym, a man of great height, five cubits tall. In the Mitzraym’s hand there was a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he went down to him with a staff, wrested the spear out of the Mitzraym’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
These things Banayahu the son of Yahuiada did, and won a name among three mighty men.
Indeed he was more honored than the thirty, but he did not attain to the first three. And Daud appointed him over his guard.
Also the mighty warriors were Asahal the brother of Yuab, Alhanan the son of Dudu of Bathlaham,
Shammuth the Harurite, Halaz the Palunite,
Ira the son of Ikkash the Takuite, Abiazar the Anathuthite,
Sibbechai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netuphathite, Halad the son of Baanah the Natuphathite,
Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibaah, of the sons of Banyamin, Banaiyah the Pirathonite,
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abial the Arbathite,
Azmabath the Baharumite, Aliahba the Shaalbunite,
the sons of Hasham the Gizunite, Yunathan the son of Shagah the Hararite,
Ahiam the son of Sacar the Hararite, Aliphal the son of Ur,
Haphar the Macharathite, Ahiyah the Palunite,
Hazru the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Azbai,
Yual the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri,
Zalak the Ammunites, Naharai the Baruthite (the armorbearer of Yuab the son of Zaruyahu),
Ira the Ithrite, Garab the Ithrite,
Uryahu the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai,
Adina the son of Shiza the Raubanites (a chief of the Raubanites) and thirty with him,
Hanan the son of Maachah, Yushaphat the Mithnite,
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Yaial the sons of Hutham the Aruarite,
Yadiaal the son of Shimri, and Yuha his brother, the Tizite,
Alial the Mahabite, Yaribai and Yushabyahu the sons of Alnaam, Ithmah the Muabite,
Alial, Ubad, and Yaasial the Mazubaite.
Now these were the men who came to Daud at Ziklag while he was still a fugitive from Shaul the son of Kish; and they were among the mighty men, helpers in the war,
armed with bows, using both the right hand and the left in hurling stones and shooting arrows with the bow. They were of Banyamin, Shaul’s brethren.
The chief was Ahiazar, then Yuash, the sons of Shamaah the Gibaathite; Yazial and Palat the sons of Azmabath; Barachah, and Yahu the Anathuthite;
Ishmayahu the Gibaunites, a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty; Yaramyahu, Yahazial, Yuhanan, and Yuzabad the Gadarathite;
Aluzai, Yarimuth, Baalyahu, Shamaryahu, and Shaphatyahu the Haruphite;
Alkanah, Yisshyahu, Azaral, Yuazar, and Yashubaam, the Kurahites;
and Yualah and Zabadyahu the sons of Yaruham of Gadur.

Some Gadites joined Daud at the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for battle, who could handle shield and spear, whose faces were like the faces of lions, and were as swift as gazallas on the mountains:
Azar the first, Ubadyahu the second, Aliab the third,
Mishmannah the fourth, Yaramyahu the fifth,
Attai the sixth, Alial the seventh,
Yuhanan the eighth, Alzabad the ninth,
Yaramyahu the tenth, and Machbanai the eleventh.
These were from the sons of Gad, captains of the army; the least was over a hundred, and the greatest was over a thousand.
These are the ones who crossed the Yurdan in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks; and they put to flight all those in the valleys, to the east and to the west.
Then some of the sons of Banyamin and Yahudah came to Daud at the stronghold.

And Daud went out to meet them, and answered and said to them, “If you have come in Shalum to me to help me, my heart will be united with you; but if to betray me to my enemies, since there is no wrong in my hands, may the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of our fathers look and bring judgment.”

Then the Ruach came upon Amasai, chief of the captains, and he said: “We are yours, O Daud; We are on your side, O son of Yassa! Shalum, Shalum to you, And Shalum to your helpers! For your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH helps you.” So Daud received them, and made them captains of the troop.

And some from Manassah defected to Daud when he was going with the Philistines to battle against Shaul; but they did not help them, for the leaders of the Philistines sent him away by agreement, saying, “he may defect to his master Shaul and endanger our heads.”
When he went to Ziklag, those of Manassah who defected to him were Adnah, Yuzabad, Yadiaal, Michaal, Yuzabad, Alihu, and Zillathai, captains of the thousands who were from Manassah.
And they helped Daud against the bands of raiders, for they were all mighty men of valor, and they were captains in the army.
For at that time they came to Daud day by day to help him, until it was a great army, like the army of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Now these were the numbers of the divisions that were equipped for war, and came to Daud at Habrun to turn over the kingdom of Shaul to him, according to the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH:
of the sons of Yahudah bearing shield and spear, six thousand eight hundred armed for war;
of the sons of Simaun, mighty men of valor fit for war, seven thousand one hundred;
of the sons of Lauy four thousand six hundred;
Yahuiada, the leader of the Aarunites, and with him three thousand seven hundred;
Zaduk, a young man, a valiant warrior, and from his father’s house twenty-two captains;
of the sons of Banyamin, relatives of Shaul, three thousand (until then the greatest part of them had remained loyal to the house of Shaul);
of the sons of Aphraim twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men throughout their father’s house;
of the half-tribe of Manassah eighteen thousand, who were designated by name to come and make Daud king;
of the sons of Issachar who had understanding of the times, to know what Yashar'AL ought to do, their chiefs were two hundred; and all their brethren were at their command;
of Zabulun there were fifty thousand who went out to battle, expert in war with all weapons of war, stouthearted men who could keep ranks;
of Naphtali one thousand captains, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear;
of the Danites who could keep battle formation, twenty-eight thousand six hundred;
of Ashar, those who could go out to war, able to keep battle formation, forty thousand;
of the Raubanites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, from the other side of the Yurdan, one hundred and twenty thousand armed for battle with every kind of weapon of war.
All these men of war, who could keep ranks, came to Habrun with a loyal heart, to make Daud king over all Yashar'AL; and all the rest of Yashar'AL were of one mind to make Daud king.
And they were there with Daud three days, eating and drinking, for their brethren had prepared for them.

Moreover those who were near to them, from as far away as Issachar and Zabulun and Naphtali, were bringing food on donkeys and camels, on mules and oxen, provisions of flour and cakes of figs and cakes of raisins, wine and oil and oxen and sheep abundantly, for there was joy in Yashar'AL.
Then Daud consulted with the captains of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader.

And Daud said to all the assembly of Yashar'AL, “If it seems good to you, and if it is of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, let us send out to our brethren everywhere who are left in all the land of Yashar'AL, and with them to the Kuhanym and Lauym who are in their cities and their common-lands, that they may gather together to us;
and let us bring the ark of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH back to us, for we have not inquired at it since the days of Shaul.”
Then all the assembly said that they would do so, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.
So Daud gathered all Yashar'AL together, from Shihur in Mitzraym to as far as the entrance of Hamath, to bring the ark of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH from Kiryath Yaarym.

And Daud and all Yashar'AL went up to Baalah, to Kiryath Yaarym, which belonged to Yahudah, to bring up from there the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who dwells between the charubim, where His Name is proclaimed.
So they carried the ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzza and Ahiu drove the cart.
Then Daud and all Yashar'AL played music before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all their might, with singing, on harps, on stringed instruments, on tambourines, on cymbals, and with trumpets.
And when they came to Chidun’s threshing floor, Uzza put out his hand to hold the ark, for the oxen stumbled.
Then the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was aroused against Uzza, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck Uzza because he put his hand to the ark; and he died there before Ark of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL,
And Daud became angry because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s outbreak against Uzza; therefore that place is called Paraz Uzza to this day.
Daud was afraid of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that day, saying, “How can I bring the ark of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL to me?”
So Daud would not move the ark with him into the City of Daud, but took it aside into the house of Ubad-Adum the Gittite.
The ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH remained with the family of Ubad-Adum in his house three months. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Baraked the house of Ubad-Adum and all that he had.
Now Hiram king of Tyra sent messengers to Daud, and cedar trees, with masons and carpenters, to build him a house.
So Daud knew that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had established him as king over Yashar'AL, for his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH's people Yashar'AL.
Then Daud took more wives in Yahushalam, and Daud begot more sons and daughters.
And these are the names of his children whom he had in Yahushalam: Shammua, Shubab, Nathan, Shalumah,
Ibhar, Alishua, Alpalat,
Nugah, Naphag, Yaphia,
Alishama, Baaliada, and Aliphalat.
Now when the Philistines heard that Daud had been anointed king over all Yashar'AL, all the Philistines went up to search for Daud. And Daud heard of it and went out against them.
Then the Philistines went and made a raid on the Valley of Raphaim.
