At that time Shalumah kept the feast seven days, and all Yashar'AL with him, a very great assembly from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of Mitzraym.
And on the eighth day they held a sacred assembly, for they observed the dedication of the altar seven days, and the feast seven days.

On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the good that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done for Daud, for Shalumah, and for His people Yashar'AL.
Thus Shalumah finished the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the king’s house; and Shalumah successfully accomplished all that came into his heart to make in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and in his own house.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared to Shalumah by night, and said to him: “I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.
When I shut up Shamaym and there is no rain, or command the locusts to devour the land, or send pestilence among My people,

if My people who are called by My Name will humble themselves, and pray and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from Shamaym, and will forgive their sin and heal their land.
Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to prayer made in this place.
For now I have chosen and sanctified this house, that My Name may be there forever; and My eyes and My heart will be there perpetually.
As for you, if you walk before Me as your father Daud walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and if you keep My statutes and My judgments,
then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with Daud your father, saying, ‘You shall not fail to have a man as ruler in Yashar'AL.’
“But if you turn away and forsake My statutes and My commandments which I have set before you, and go and serve other nations idols, and worship them,
then I will uproot them from My land which I have given them; and this house which I have sanctified for My Name I will cast out of My sight, and will make it a proverb and a byword among all people.
“And as for this house, which is exalted, everyone who passes by it will be astonished and say, ‘Why has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH done thus to this land and this house?’

Then they will answer, ‘Because they forsook 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Mitzraym, and they embraced other nations pagan idols, as their mighty ones for worship; therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought all this calamity on them.’ ”
It came to pass at the end of twenty years, when Shalumah had built the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and his own house,
that the cities which Hiram had given to Shalumah, King Shalumah built them; and he settled the children of Yashar'AL there.
And Shalumah went to Hamath Zubah and seized it.
He also built Tadmur in the wilderness, and all the storage cities which he built in Hamath.
He built Upper Bath Hurun and Lower Bath Hurun, fortified cities with walls, gates, and bars,

also Baalath and all the storage cities that Shalumah had, and all the chariot cities and the cities of the cavalry, and all that Shalumah desired to build in Yahushalam, in Labanun, and in all the land of his dominion.
All the people who were left of the Hittites, Amurites, Parizzites, Hibites, and Yabusites, who were not of Yashar'AL
that is, their descendants who were left in the land after them, whom the children of Yashar'AL did not destroy from these Shalumah raised forced labor, as it is to this day.
But Shalumah did not make the children of Yashar'AL servants for his work. Some were men of war, captains of his officers, captains of his chariots, and his cavalry.
And others were chiefs of the officials of King Shalumah: two hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people.

Now Shalumah brought the daughter of Phar'uh up from the City of Daud to the house he had built for her, for he said, “My wife shall not dwell in the house of Daud king of Yashar'AL, because the place to which the Ark of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has come are Qadash.”
Then Shalumah offered burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which he had built before the vestibule,

according to the daily rate, offering according to the commandment of Musha, for the Shabbats, the New Moons, and the three appointed yearly feasts, the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles.

And, according to the order of Daud his father, he appointed the divisions of the Kuhanym for their service, the Lauym for their duties (to Yadah and serve before the Kuhanym) as the duty of each day required, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate; for so Daud the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded.
They did not depart from the command of the king to the Kuhanym and Lauym concerning any matter or concerning the treasuries.
Now all the work of Shalumah was well-ordered from the day of the foundation of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH until it was finished. So the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was completed.
Then Shalumah went to Aziun Gaabar and Alath on the seacoast, in the land of Adum.

And Hiram sent him on ships by the hand of his servants, and servants who knew the sea. They went with the servants of Shalumah to Uphir and acquired four hundred and fifty talents of gold from there, and brought it to King Shalumah.

Now when the queen of Shaba heard of the fame of Shalumah, she came to Yahushalam to test Shalumah with hard questions, having a very great retinue, camels that bore spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones; and when she came to Shalumah, she spoke with him about all that was in her heart.
So Shalumah answered all her questions; there was nothing so difficult for Shalumah that he could not explain it to her.
And when the queen of Shaba had seen the wisdom of Shalumah, the house that he had built,

the food on his table, the seating of his servants, the service of his waiters and their apparel, his cupbearers and their apparel, and his entryway by which he went up to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, there was no more spirit in her.
Then she said to the king: “It was a true report which I heard in my own land about your words and your wisdom.
However I did not believe their words until I came and saw with my own eyes; and indeed the half of the greatness of your wisdom was not told me. You exceed the fame of which I heard.
Happy are your men and happy are these your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!

Baraked be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who delighted in you, setting you on His throne to be king for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH! Because your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has loved Yashar'AL, to establish them forever, therefore He made you king over them, to do justice and righteousness.”
And she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, spices in great abundance, and precious stones; there never were any spices such as those the queen of Shaba gave to King Shalumah.
Also, the servants of Hiram and the servants of Shalumah, who brought gold from Uphir, brought algum wood and precious stones.

And the king made walkways of the algum wood for the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and for the king’s house, also harps and stringed instruments for singers; and there were none such as these seen before in the land of Yahudah.
Now King Shalumah gave to the queen of Shaba all she desired, whatever she asked, much more than she had brought to the king. So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.
The weight of gold that came to Shalumah yearly was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
besides what the traveling merchants and traders brought. And all the kings of Arabia and governors of the country brought gold and silver to Shalumah.
And King Shalumah made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of hammered gold went into each shield.
He also made three hundred shields of hammered gold; three hundred shekels of gold went into each shield. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps, with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne; there were armrests on either side of the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the armrests.
Twelve lions stood there, one on each side of the six steps; nothing like this had been made for any other kingdom.

All King Shalumah’s drinking vessels were gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Labanun were pure gold. Not one was silver, for gold was accounted as nothing in the days of Shalumah.
For the king’s ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Hiram. Once every three years the merchant ships came, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and monkeys.
So King Shalumah surpassed all the kings of the Arath in riches and wisdom.
And all the kings of the Arath sought the presence of Shalumah to hear his wisdom, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had put in his heart.
Each man brought his present: articles of silver and gold, garments, armor, spices, horses, and mules, at a set rate year by year.
Shalumah had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king at Yahushalam.
So he reigned over all the kings from the River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Mitzraym.
The king made silver as common in Yahushalam as stones, and he made cedar trees as abundant as the sycamores which are in the lowland.
And they brought horses to Shalumah from Mitzraym and from all lands.

Now the rest of the acts of Shalumah, first and last, are written in the book of Nathan the Nabym, in the prophecy of Ahiyahu the Shilunites, and in the visions of Iddu the seer concerning Yarubuam the son of Nabat?
Shalumah reigned in Yahushalam over all Yashar'AL forty years.
Then Shalumah rested with his fathers, and was buried in the City of Daud his father. And Rahubuam his son reigned in his place.
And Rahubuam went to Shacham, for all Yashar'AL had gone to Shacham to make him king.
So it happened, when Yarubuam the son of Nabat heard it (he was in Mitzraym, where he had fled from the presence of King Shalumah), that Yarubuam returned from Mitzraym.
Then they sent for him and called him. And Yarubuam and all Yashar'AL came and spoke to Rahubuam, saying,
“Your father made our yoke heavy; now therefore, lighten the burdensome service of your father and his heavy yoke which he put on us, and we will serve you.”
So he said to them, “Come back to me after three days.” And the people departed.
Then King Rahubuam consulted the elders who stood before his father Shalumah while he still lived, saying, “How do you advise me to answer these people?”
And they spoke to him, saying, “If you are kind to these people, and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
But he rejected the advice which the elders had given him, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
And he said to them, “What advice do you give? How should we answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke which your father put on us’?”

Then the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, “Thus you should speak to the people who have spoken to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you make it lighter on us’—thus you shall say to them: ‘My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s waist!
And now, whereas my father put a heavy yoke on you, I will add to your yoke; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scourges!’ ”
So Yarubuam and all the people came to Rahubuam on the third day, as the king had directed, saying, “Come back to me the third day.”
Then the king answered them roughly. King Rahubuam rejected the advice of the elders,

and he spoke to them according to the advice of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scourges!”

So the king did not listen to the people; for the turn of events was from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH might fulfill His Dabar, which He had spoken by the hand of Ahiyahu the Shilunites to Yarubuam the son of Nabat.

Now when all Yashar'AL saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king, saying: “What share have we in Daud? We have no inheritance in the son of Yassa. Every man to your tents, O Yashar'AL! Now see to your own house, O Daud!” So all Yashar'AL departed to their tents.
But Rahubuam reigned over the children of Yashar'AL who dwelt in the cities of Yahudah.

Then King Rahubuam sent Haduram, who was in charge of revenue; but the children of Yashar'AL stoned him with stones, and he died. Therefore King Rahubuam mounted his chariot in haste to flee to Yahushalam.
So Yashar'AL has been in rebellion against the house of Daud to this day.

Now when Rahubuam came to Yahushalam, he assembled from the house of Yahudah and Banyamin one hundred and eighty thousand chosen men who were warriors, to fight against Yashar'AL, that he might restore the whole kingdom to himself.
But the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to Shamayahu the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, saying,
“Speak to Rahubuam the son of Shalumah, king of Yahudah, and to all Yashar'AL in Yahudah and Banyamin, saying,

‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: “You must not go up or fight against your brethren! Let every man return to his house, for this thing is from Me.” Therefore they obeyed the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and turned back from attacking Yarubuam.
So Rahubuam dwelt in Yahushalam, and built cities for defense in Yahudah.
And he built Bathlaham, Atam, Takua,
Bath Zur, Suchuh, Adullam,
Gath, Marashah, Ziph,
Aduraim, Lachish, Azakah,
Zurah, Aiyalun, and Habrun, which are in Yahudah and Banyamin, fortified cities.
And he fortified the strongholds, and put captains in them, and stores of food, oil, and wine.
Also in every city Rahubuam put shields and spears, and made them very strong, having Yahudah and Banyamin on his side.
And from all their territories the Kuhanym and the Lauym who were in all Yashar'AL took their stand with him.
For the Lauym left their common-lands and their possessions and came to Yahudah and Yahushalam, for Yarubuam and his sons had rejected them from serving as Kuhanym to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then Yarubuam appointed for himself priests for the high places, for the demons, and the calf idols which he had made in Yashar'AL.

And after the Lauym left, those from all the tribes of Yashar'AL, such as set their heart to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the only 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, they all came to Yahushalam to sacrifice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers.
So they strengthened the kingdom of Yahudah, and made Rahubuam the son of Shalumah strong for three years, because they walked in the way of Daud and Shalumah for three years.
Then King Rahubuam took for himself as wife Mahalath the daughter of Yarimuth the son of Daud, and of Abihail the daughter of Alyahu the son of Yassa.
And she bore him children: Yaush, Shamaryahu, and Zaham.
After her he took Maachah the granddaughter of Absalum; and she bore him Abiyahu, Attai, Ziza, and Shalumith.
Now Rahubuam loved Maachah the granddaughter of Absalum more than all his wives and his concubines; for he took eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and begot twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
And Rahubuam appointed Abiyahu the son of Maachah as chief, to be leader among his brothers; for he intended to make him king.

He dealt wisely, and dispersed some of his sons throughout all the territories of Yahudah and Banyamin, to every fortified city; and he gave them provisions in abundance, he also sought many wives for them.
Now it came to pass, when Rahubuam had established the kingdom and had strengthened himself, that he forsook the law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and all Yashar'AL along with him.
And it happened in the fifth year of King Rahubuam that Shishak king of Mitzraym came up against Yahushalam, because they had transgressed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
with one thousand two hundred chariots, sixty thousand horsemen, and people without number who came with him out of Mitzraym, the Lubim and the Sukkiim and the Athiupians.
And he took the fortified cities of Yahudah and came to Yahushalam.

Then Shamayahu the Nabym came to Rahubuam and the leaders of Yahudah, who were gathered together in Yahushalam because of Shishak, and said to them, “Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘You have forsaken Me, and therefore I also have left you in the hand of Shishak.’ ”
So the leaders of Yashar'AL and the king humbled themselves; and they said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is righteous.”

Now when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH saw that they humbled themselves, the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to Shamayahu, saying, “They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance. My wrath shall not be poured out on Yahushalam by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless they will be his servants, that they may distinguish My service from the service of the kingdoms of the nations.”

So Shishak king of Mitzraym came up against Yahushalam, and took away the treasures of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the treasures of the king’s house; he took everything. He also carried away the gold shields which Shalumah had made.
Then King Rahubuam made bronze shields in their place, and committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard, who guarded the doorway of the king’s house.
And whenever the king entered the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the guard would go and bring them out; then they would take them back into the guardroom.
When he humbled himself, the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH turned from him, so as not to destroy him completely; and things also went well in Yahudah.

Thus King Rahubuam strengthened himself in Yahushalam and reigned. Now Rahubuam was forty-one years old when he became king; and he reigned seventeen years in Yahushalam, the city which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had chosen out of all the tribes of Yashar'AL, to put His Name there. His mother’s name was Naamah, an Ammunitess.
And he did evil, because he did not prepare his heart to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The acts of Rahubuam, first and last, are written in the book of Shamayahu the Nabym, and of Iddu the seer concerning genealogies? And there were wars between Rahubuam and Yarubuam all their days.
So Rahubuam rested with his fathers, and was buried in the City of Daud. Then Abiyahu his son reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Yarubuam, Abiyahu became king over Yahudah.
He reigned three years in Yahushalam, his mother’s name was Michayahu the daughter of Urial of Gibaah. And there was war between Abiyahu and Yarubuam.

Abiyahu set the battle in order with an army of valiant warriors, four hundred thousand choice men. Yarubuam also drew up in battle formation against him with eight hundred thousand choice men, mighty men of valor.
Then Abiyahu stood on Mount Zamaraim, which is in the mountains of Aphraim, and said, “Hear me, Yarubuam and all Yashar'AL:
Should you not know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL gave the dominion over Yashar'AL to Daud forever, to him and his sons, by a covenant of salt?
Yet Yarubuam the son of Nabat, the servant of Shalumah the son of Daud, rose up and rebelled against his master.
Then worthless rogues gathered to him, and strengthened themselves against Rahubuam the son of Shalumah, when Rahubuam was young and inexperienced and could not withstand them.

And now you think to withstand the kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, which is in the hand of the sons of Daud; and you are a great multitude, and with you are the gold calves which Yarubuam made for you to worship.

Have you not cast out the Kuhanym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the sons of Aarun, and the Lauym, and made for yourselves priests, like the peoples of other lands, so that whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams may be a priest to your worthless idols?
But as for us, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and we have not forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and the Kuhanym who minister to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH are the sons of Aarun, and the Lauym attend to their duties.

And they burn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense; they also set the showbread in order on the pure gold table, and the lampstand of gold with its lamps to burn every evening; for we keep the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, but you have forsaken Him.

Now look, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Himself is with us as our head, and His Kuhanym with sounding trumpets to sound the alarm against you. O children of Yashar'AL, do not fight against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your fathers, for you shall not prosper!”
But Yarubuam caused an ambush to go around behind them; so they were in front of Yahudah, and the ambush was behind them.
And when Yahudah looked around, to their surprise the battle line was at both front and rear; and they cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the Kuhanym sounded the trumpets.
Then the men of Yahudah gave a shout; and as the men of Yahudah shouted, it happened that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck Yarubuam and all Yashar'AL before Abiyahu and Yahudah.
And the children of Yashar'AL fled before Yahudah, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH delivered them into their hand.
Then Abiyahu and his people struck them with a great slaughter; so five hundred thousand choice men of Yashar'AL fell slain.
Thus the children of Yashar'AL were subdued at that time; and the children of Yahudah prevailed, because they relied on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers.
And Abiyahu pursued Yaruboam and took cities from him: Bathal with its villages, Yashanah with its villages, and Aphrain with its villages.
So Yarubuam did not recover strength again in the days of Abiyahu; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck Yarubuam, and he died.
But Abiyah grew mighty, married fourteen wives, and begot twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
Now the rest of the acts of Abiyahu, his ways, and his sayings are written in the annals of the Nabym Iddu.
So Abiyahu rested with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of Daud. Then Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years.
Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH,
for he removed the altars of the foreign idols and the high places, and broke down the sacred pillars and cut down the wooden images.
He commanded Yahudah to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers, and to observe the law and the commandments.
He also removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Yahudah, and the kingdom was quiet under him.
And he built fortified cities in Yahudah, for the land had rest; he had no war in those years, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given him rest.

Therefore he said to Yahudah, “Let us build these cities and make walls around them, and towers, gates, and bars, while the land is yet before us, because we have sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; and He has given us rest on every side.” So they built and prospered.

And Asa had an army of three hundred thousand from Yahudah who carried shields and spears, and from Banyamin two hundred and eighty thousand men who carried shields and drew bows; all these were mighty men of valor.
Then Zarah the Athiupian came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and he came to Marashah.
So Asa went out against him, and they set the troops in battle array in the Valley of Zaphathah at Marashah.

And Asa cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, it is nothing for You to help, whether with many or with those who have no power; help us, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, for we rest on You, and in Your Name we go against this multitude. O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, You are our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; do not let man prevail against You!”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck the Athiupians before Asa and Yahudah, and the Athiupians fled.

And Asa and the people who were with him pursued them to Garar. So the Athiupians were overthrown, and they could not recover, for they were broken before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and His army. And they carried away very many and much spoil.
Then they defeated all the cities around Garar, for the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came upon them; and they plundered all the cities, for there was exceedingly much spoil in them.
They also attacked the livestock enclosures, and carried off sheep and camels in abundance, and returned to Yahushalam.
Now the RUACH of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH came upon Azaryahu the son of Udad.

And he went out to meet Asa, and said to him: “Hear me, Asa, and all Yahudah and Banyamin. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with you while you are with Him. If you seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, He will be found by you; but if you forsake 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, He will forsake you.
For a long time Yashar'AL has been without the true 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, without a teaching Kuhanym, and without law;
but when in their trouble they turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, and sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and He was found by them.
And in those times there was no Shalum to the one who went out, nor to the one who came in, but great turmoil was on all the inhabitants of the lands.
So nation was destroyed by nation, and city by city, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH troubled them with every adversity.
But you, be strong and do not let your hands be weak, for your work shall be rewarded!”

And when Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Udad the Nabym, he took courage, and removed the abominable idols from all the land of Yahudah and Banyamin and from the cities which he had taken in the mountains of Aphraim; and he restored the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that was before the vestibule of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then King Asaba gathered all Yahudah and Banyamin, and those who dwelt with them from Aphraim, Manassah, and Simaun, for they came over to him in great numbers from Yashar'AL when they saw that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was with him.
So they gathered together at Yahushalam in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
And they offered to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, seven hundred bulls and seven thousand sheep from the spoil they had brought.
Then they entered into a covenant to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;
and whoever would not seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL was to be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
Then they took an oath before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with a loud voice, with shouting and trumpets and rams’ horns.
And all Yahudah rejoiced at the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all their soul; and He was found by them, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them rest all around.

King Asaba also removed Maachah, his own mother, from being queen mother, because she had made an obscene image of Asharah; and Asa cut down her obscene image, then crushed and burned it by the Brook Kidrun.
But the high places were not removed from Yashar'AL. Nevertheless the heart of Asa was loyal all his days.
He also brought into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the things that his father had dedicated and that he himself had dedicated: silver and gold and utensils.
And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of King Asa.
In the thirty-sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha king of Yashar'AL came up against Yahudah and built Ramah, that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Yahudah.
Then Asa brought silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and of the king’s house, and sent to Ban-Hadad king of Syria, who dwelt in Damascus, saying,

“Let there be a treaty between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. See, I have sent you silver and gold; come, break your treaty with Baasha king of Yashar'AL, so that he will withdraw from me.”
So Ban-Hadad heeded King Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Yashar'AL. They attacked Iyun, Dan, Abal Maim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali.
Now it happened, when Baasha heard it, that he stopped building Ramah and ceased his work.
Then King Asa took all Yahudah, and they carried away the stones and timber of Ramah, which Baasha had used for building; and with them he built Gaba and Mizpah.

And at that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Yahudah, and said to him: “Because you have relied on the king of Syria, and have not relied on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, therefore the army of the king of Syria has escaped from your hand.
Were the Athiupians and the Lubim not a huge army with very many chariots and horsemen? Yet, because you relied on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, He delivered them into your hand.

For the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH run to and fro throughout the whole Arath, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is loyal to Him. In this you have done foolishly; therefore from now on you shall have wars.”
Then King Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in prison, for he was enraged at him because of this. And Asa oppressed some of the people at that time.
Note that the acts of Asa, first and last, are indeed written in the book of the kings of Yahudah and Yashar'AL.
And in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his malady was severe; yet in his disease he did not seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but the physicians.
So Asa rested with his fathers; he died in the forty-first year of his reign.

They buried him in his own tomb, which he had made for himself in the City of Daud; and they laid him in the bed which was filled with spices and various ingredients prepared in a mixture of ointments. They made a very great burning for him.
Then Yahushaphat his son reigned in his place, and strengthened himself against Yashar'AL.
And he placed troops in all the fortified cities of Yahudah, and set garrisons in the land of Yahudah and in the cities of Aphraim which Asa his father had taken.
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with Yahushaphat, because he walked in the former ways of his father Daud; he did not seek the Baals,
but sought the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of his father, and walked in the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and not according to the acts of Yashar'AL.
Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH established the kingdom in his hand; and all Yahudah gave presents to Yahushaphat, and he had riches and honor in abundance.
And his heart took delight in the ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and king Yahushaphat also removed the high places and wooden images from Yahudah.
Also in the third year of his reign he sent his leaders, Ban-Hail, Ubadyahu, Zacharyahu, Nathanal, and Michayahu, to teach in the cities of Yahudah.
And with them he sent Lauym: Shamayahu, Nathanyahu, Zabadyahu, Asahal, Shamiramuth, Yahunathan, Aduniyahu, Tubiyahu, and Tubaduniyahu the Lauym; and with them Alishama and Yahuram, the Kuhanym.
So they taught in Yahudah, and had the Book of the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with them; they went throughout all the cities of Yahudah and taught the people.
And the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH fell on all the kingdoms of the lands that were around Yahudah, so that they did not make war against Yahushaphat.
Also some of the Philistines brought Yahushaphat presents and silver as tribute; and the Arabians brought him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
So Yahushaphat became increasingly powerful, and he built fortresses and storage cities in Yahudah.
He had much property in the cities of Yahudah; and the men of war, mighty men of valor, were in Yahushalam.
These are their numbers, according to their fathers’ houses. Of Yahudah, the captains of thousands: Adnah the captain, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valor;
and next to him was Yahuhanan the captain, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;
and next to him was Amasyahu the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor.
Of Banyamin: Aliada a mighty man of valor, and with him two hundred thousand men armed with bow and shield;
and next to him was Yahuzabad, and with him one hundred and eighty thousand prepared for war.
These served the king, besides those the king put in the fortified cities throughout all Yahudah.
Yahushaphat had riches and honor in abundance; and by marriage he allied himself with Ahab.
After some years he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria; and Ahab killed sheep and oxen in abundance for him and the people who were with him, and persuaded him to go up with him to Ramuth Gilaad.

So Ahab king of Yashar'AL said to Yahushaphat king of Yahudah, “Will you go with me against Ramuth Gilaad?” And he answered him, “I am as you are, and my people as your people; we will be with you in the war.”
Also Yahushaphat said to the king of Yashar'AL, “Please inquire for the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH today.”

Then the king of Yashar'AL gathered the prophets together, four hundred men, and said to them, “Shall we go to war against Ramuth-gilaad, or shall I refrain?” So they said, “Go up, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will deliver it into the king’s hand.”
But Yahushaphat said, “Is there not still a Nabym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH here, that we may inquire of Him?”

So the king Ahab of Yashar'AL said to Yahushaphat, “There is still one man by whom we may inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; but I hate him, because he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil, he is Micayahu the son of Imla.” And Yahushaphat said, “Let not the king say such things!”
Then the king of Yashar'AL called one of his officers and said, “Bring Micayahu the son of Imla quickly!”

The king of Yashar'AL and Yahushaphat king of Yahudah, clothed in their robes, sat each on his throne; and they sat at a threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets prophesied before them.
Now Zadakyahu the son of Chanaanah had made horns of iron for himself; and he said, “Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘With these you shall gore the Syrians until they are destroyed.’
And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, “Go up to Ramuth-gilaad and prosper, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will deliver it into the king’s hand.”

Then the messenger who had gone to call Micayahu spoke to him, saying, “Now listen, the words of the prophets are with one accord encourage the king. Therefore please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak encouragement.”
And Micayahu said, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, whatever my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH says, that is what I will always speak.”

Then he came to the king; and the king said to him, “Micayahu, shall we go to war against Ramuth-gilaad, or shall I refrain?” And he said, “Go and prosper, and they shall be delivered into your hand!”
So the king said to him, “How many times shall I make you swear that you must tell me nothing but the truth in the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?”
Then he said, “I saw all Yashar'AL scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, ‘These have no master. Let each return to his house in Shalum.’ ”
And the king of Yashar'AL said to king Yahushaphat, “Did I not tell you he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”
Then Micayahu said, “Therefore hear the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: I saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sitting on His throne, and all the host of Shamaym standing on His right hand and His left.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, ‘Who will persuade Ahab king of Yashar'AL to go up, that he may fall at Ramuth Gilaad?’ So one spoke in this manner, and another spoke in that manner.
Then a spirit came forward and stood before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and said, ‘I will persuade him.’ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to him, ‘In what way?’
So the spirit said, ‘I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, ‘You shall persuade him and also prevail; go out and do so.’
Therefore look! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has declared disaster against you.”
Then Zadakyahu the son of Chanaanah went near and struck Micayahu on the cheek, and said, “Which way did the spirit from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH go from me to speak to you?”
And Micayahu said, “Indeed you shall see on that day when you go into an inner chamber to hide!”
Then the king of Yashar'AL said, “Take Micayahu, and return him to Amun the governor of the city and to Yuash the king’s son;
and say, ‘Thus says the king: “Put this fellow in prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and water of affliction, until I return in Shalum.” ’ ”
But Micayahu said, “If you ever return in Shalum, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has not spoken by me.” And he said, “Take heed, all you people!”
So the king of Yashar'AL and Yahushaphat the king of Yahudah went up to Ramuth Gilaad.
And the king of Yashar'AL said to Yahushaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into battle; but you put on your robes.” So the king of Yashar'AL disguised himself, and they went into battle.
Now the king of Syria had commanded the captains of the chariots who were with him, saying, “Fight with no one small or great, but only with the king of Yashar'AL.”

So it was, when the captains of the chariots saw Yahushaphat, that they said, “It is the king of Yashar'AL!” Therefore they surrounded him to attack; but Yahushaphat cried out, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH helped him, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH diverted them from him.
For so it was, when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Yashar'AL, that they turned back from pursuing him.

Now a certain man drew a bow at random, and struck the king of Yashar'AL between the joints of his armor. So he said to the driver of his chariot, “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for I am wounded.”
The battle increased that day, and the king of Yashar'AL propped himself up in his chariot facing the Syrians until evening; and about the time of sunset he died.
Then Yahushaphat the king of Yahudah returned safely to his house in Yahushalam.

And Yahu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him, and said to King Yahushaphat, “Should you help the wicked and love those who hate 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? Therefore the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is upon you.
Nevertheless good things are found in you, in that you have removed the wooden images from the land, and have prepared your heart to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So Yahushaphat dwelt at Yahushalam; and he went out again among the people from Baarshaba to the mountains of Aphraim, and brought them back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers.
Then he set judges in the land throughout all the fortified cities of Yahudah, city by city,
and said to the judges, “Take heed to what you are doing, for you do not judge for man but for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who is with you in the judgment.
Now therefore, let the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH be upon you; take care and do it, for there is no iniquity with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, no partiality, nor taking of bribes.”

Moreover in Yahushalam, for the judgment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and for controversies, Yahushaphat appointed some of the Lauym and Kuhanym, and some of the chief fathers of Yashar'AL, when they returned to Yahushalam.
And he commanded them, saying, “Thus you shall act in the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, faithfully and with a loyal heart:

Whatever case comes to you from your brethren who dwell in their cities, whether of bloodshed or offenses against law or commandments, against statutes or ordinances, you shall warn them, lest they trespass against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and wrath come upon you and your brethren. Do this, and you will not be guilty.

And take notice: Amaryahu the chief Kuhan is over you in all matters of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and Zabadyahu the son of Ishmaal, the ruler of the house of Yahudah, for all the king’s matters; also the Lauym will be officials before you. Behave courageously, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be with the righteous.”
It happened after this that the people of Muab with the people of Ammun, and others with them besides the Ammunites, came to battle against Yahushaphat.
Then some came and told Yahushaphat, saying, “A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Syria; and they are in Hazazun Tamar” (which is An-Gadi).
And Yahushaphat feared, and set himself to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Yahudah.
So Yahudah gathered together to ask help from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and from all the cities of Yahudah they came to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then Yahushaphat stood in the assembly of Yahudah and Yahushalam, in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, before the new court,

and said: “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of our fathers, are You not 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in Shamaym, and do You not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations, and in Your hand is there not power and might, so that no one is able to withstand You?
Are You not our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who drove out the inhabitants of this land before Your people Yashar'AL, and gave it to the descendants of Abraham Your friend forever?
And they dwell in it, and have built You a sanctuary in it for Your Name, saying,

‘If disaster comes upon us, been it sword, judgment, pestilence, or famine, we will stand before this temple and in Your presence (for Your Name is in this temple), and cry out to You in our affliction, and You will hear and save us.’
And now, here are the people of Ammun, Muab, and Mount Sair, whom You would not let Yashar'AL invade when they came out of the land of Mitzraym, but they turned from them and did not destroy them
here they are, rewarding us by coming to throw us out of Your possession which You have given us to inherit.
O our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, will You not judge them? For we have no power against this great multitude that is coming against us; nor do we know what to do, but our eyes are upon You.”
Now all Yahudah, with their little ones, their wives, and their children, stood before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then the RUACH of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came upon Yahazial the son of Zacharyahu, the son of Banayahu, the son of Yaial, the son of Mattanyahu, a Lauym of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly.

And he said, “Listen, all you of Yahudah and you inhabitants of Yahushalam, and you, King Yahushaphat! Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to you: ‘Do not be afraid nor dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours, but 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH’s.
Tomorrow go down against them. They will surely come up by the Ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the brook before the Wilderness of Yarual.

You will not need to fight in this battle. Position yourselves, stand still and see the salvation of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who is with you, O Yahudah and Yahushalam!’ Do not fear or be dismayed; tomorrow go out against them, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with you.”
And Yahushaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Yahudah and the inhabitants of Yahushalam bowed and worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then the Lauym of the children of the Kuhathites and of the children of the Kurahites stood up to Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL with voices loud and high.

So they rose early in the morning and went out into the Wilderness of Takua; and as they went out, Yahushaphat stood and said, “Hear me, O Yahudah and you inhabitants of Yahushalam: Believe in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and you shall be established; believe His Nabym, and you shall prosper.”

And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed those who should sing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and who should Yadah (praise) the beauty of Qadash Name, as they went out before the army and were saying:
Now when they began to sing and to Yadah, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH set ambushes against the people of Ammun, Muab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Yahudah; and they were defeated.

For the people of Ammun and Muab stood up against the inhabitants of Mount Sair to utterly kill and destroy them. And when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Sair, they helped to destroy one another.
So when Yahudah came to a place overlooking the wilderness, they looked toward the multitude; and there were their dead bodies, fallen on the Arath. No one had escaped.

When Yahushaphat and his people came to take away their spoil, they found among them an abundance of valuables on the dead bodies, and precious jewelry, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away; and they were three days gathering the spoil because there was so much.
And on the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Barachah, for there they Baraked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; therefore the Name of that place was called The Valley of Barachah until this day.
Then they returned, every man of Yahudah and Yahushalam, with Yahushaphat in front of them, to go back to Yahushalam with joy, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had made them rejoice over their enemies.
So they came to Yahushalam, with stringed instruments and harps and trumpets, to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was on all the kingdoms of those countries when they heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had fought against the enemies of Yashar'AL.
Then the realm of Yahushaphat was quiet, for his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH gave him rest all around.
So Yahushaphat was king over Yahudah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Yahushalam. His mother’s name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.
And he walked in the way of his father Asa, and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Nevertheless the high places were not taken away, for as yet the people had not directed their hearts to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers.
Now the rest of the acts of Yahushaphat, first and last, indeed they are written in the book of Yahu the son of Hanani, which is mentioned in the book of the kings of Yashar'AL.
After this Yahushaphat king of Yahudah allied himself with Ahazyahu king of Yashar'AL, who acted very wickedly.
And he allied himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the ships in Aziun Gabar.

But Aliazer the son of Dudabah of Marashah prophesied against Yahushaphat, saying, “Because you have allied yourself with Ahazyahu, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has destroyed your works.” Then the ships were wrecked, so that they were not able to go to Tarshish.
And Yahushaphat rested with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the City of Daud. Then Yahuram his son reigned in his place.
Yahuram had brothers, the sons of Yahushaphat: Azaryahu, Yahial, Zacharyahu, Azaryahu, Michaal, and Shaphatyahu; all these were the sons of Yahushaphat king of Yashar'AL.
Their father gave them great gifts of silver and gold and precious things, with fortified cities in Yahudah; but he gave the kingdom to Yahuram, because he was the firstborn.
Now when Yahuram was established over the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself and killed all his brothers with the sword, and also others of the princes of Yashar'AL.
Yahuram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Yahushalam.
And he walked in the way of the kings of Yashar'AL, just as the house of Ahab had done, for he had the daughter of Ahab as a wife; and he did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Yet 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH would not destroy the house of Daud, because of the covenant that He had made with Daud, and since He had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.
In his days Adum revolted against Yahudah’s authority, and made a king over themselves.
So Yahuram went out with his officers, and all his chariots with him. And he rose by night and attacked the Adumites who had surrounded him and the captains of the chariots.
Thus Adum has been in revolt against Yahudah’s authority to this day. At that time Libnah revolted against his rule, because he had forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of his fathers.
Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Yahudah, and caused the inhabitants of Yahushalam to commit harlotry, and led Yahudah astray.

And a letter came to him from AliYahu the Nabym, saying, Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your father Daud: Because you have not walked in the ways of Yahushaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa king of Yahudah,

but have walked in the way of the kings of Yashar'AL, and have made Yahudah and the inhabitants of Yahushalam to play the harlot like the harlotry of the house of Ahab, and also have killed your brothers, those of your father’s household, who were better than yourself,
behold, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will strike your people with a serious affliction, your children, your wives, and all your possessions;
and you will become very sick with a disease of your intestines, until your intestines come out by reason of the sickness, day by day.
Moreover 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH stirred up against Yahuram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians who were near the Athiupians.

And they came up into Yahudah and invaded it, and carried away all the possessions that were found in the king’s house, and also his sons and his wives, so that there was not a son left to him except Yahuahaz, the youngest of his sons.
After all this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck him in his intestines with an incurable disease.

Then it happened in the course of time, after the end of two years, that his intestines came out because of his sickness; so he died in severe pain. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning for his fathers.

Yahuram was thirty-two years old when he became king, he reigned in Yahushalam eight years and, no one felt sorrowful about his death, however they buried him in the City of Daud, but not in the tombs of the kings.

Then the inhabitants of Yahushalam made Ahazyahu his youngest son king in his place, for the raiders who came with the Arabians into the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahazyahu the son of Yahuram, king of Yahudah, reigned.
Ahazyahu was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Yahushalam. His mother’s name was Athalyahu the granddaughter of Umri.
He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother advised him to do wickedly.
Therefore he did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, like the house of Ahab; for they were his counselors after the death of his father, to his destruction.
He also followed their advice, and went with Yahuram the son of Ahab king of Yashar'AL to war against Hazaal king of Syria at Ramuth Gilaad; and the Syrians wounded Yuram.

Then he returned to Yazraal to recover from the wounds which he had received at Ramah, when he fought against Hazaal king of Syria. And Azaryahu the son of Yahuram, king of Yahudah, went down to see Yahuram the son of Ahab in Yazraal, because he was sick.

His going to Yuram was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s occasion for Ahazyahu’s downfall; for when he arrived, he went out with Yahuram against Yahu the son of Nimshi, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And it happened, when Yahu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Yahudah and the sons of Ahazyahu’s brothers who served Ahazyahu, that he killed them.

Then he searched for Ahazyahu; and they caught him (he was hiding in Samaria), and brought him to Yahu. When they had killed him, they buried him, “because,” they said, “he is the son of Yahushaphat, who sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all his heart.” So the house of Ahazyahu had no one to assume power over the kingdom.
Now when Athalyahu the mother of Ahazyahu saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal heirs of the house of Yahudah.

But Yahushabaath, the daughter of the king, took Yuash the son of Ahazyahu, and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being murdered, and put him and his nurse in a bedroom. So Yahushabaath, the daughter of King Yahuram, the wife of Yahuiada the Kuhan (for she was the sister of Ahazyahu), hid him from Athalyahu so that she did not kill him.
And he was hidden with them in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for six years, while Athalyahu reigned over the land.

In the seventh year Yahuiada strengthened himself, and made a covenant with the captains of hundreds: Azaryahu the son of Yaruham, Ishmaal the son of Yahuhanan, Azaryahu the son of Ubad, Maasayahu the son of Adayahu, and Alishaphat the son of Zichri.
And they went throughout Yahudah and gathered the Lauym from all the cities of Yahudah, and the chief fathers of Yashar'AL, and they came to Yahushalam.
Then all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And he said to them, “Behold, the king’s son shall reign, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has Dabar of the sons of Daud.
This is what you shall do: One-third of you entering on the Shabbat, of the Kuhanym and the Lauym, shall be keeping watch over the doors;
one-third shall be at the king’s house; and one-third at the Gate of the Foundation. All the people shall be in the courts of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
But let no one come into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH except the Kuhanym and those of the Lauym who serve. They may go in, for they are Qadash; but all the people shall keep the watch of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

And the Lauym shall surround the king on all sides, every man with his weapons in his hand; and whoever comes into the house, let him be put to death. You are to be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.”

So the Lauym and all Yahudah did according to all that Yahuiada the Kuhan commanded. And each man took his men who were to be on duty on the Shabbat, with those who were going off duty on the Shabbat; for Yahuiada the Kuhan had not dismissed the divisions.
And Yahuiada the Kuhan gave to the captains of hundreds the spears and the large and small shields which had belonged to King Daud, that were in the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then he set all the people, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, along by the altar and by the temple, all around the king.
And they brought out the king’s son, put the crown on him, gave him the Testimony, and made him king. Then Yahuiada and his sons anointed him, and said, “Long live the king!”
Now when Athalyahu heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people in the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

When she looked, there was the king standing by his pillar at the entrance; and the leaders and the trumpeters were by the king. All the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, also the singers with musical instruments, and those who led in praise. So Athalyahu tore her clothes and said, “Treason! Treason!”

And Yahuiada the Kuhan brought out the captains of hundreds who were set over the army, and said to them, “Take her outside under guard, and slay with the sword whoever follows her.” For the Kuhan had said, “Do not kill her in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So they seized her; and she went by way of the entrance of the Horse Gate into the king’s house, and they killed her there.
Then Yahuiada made a covenant between himself, the people, and the king, that they should be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s people.
And all the people went to the temple of Baal, and tore it down. They broke in pieces its altars and images, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

Also Yahuiada appointed the oversight of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to the hand of the Kuhanym, the Lauym, whom Daud had assigned in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to offer the burnt offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as it is written in the Law of Musha, with rejoicing and with singing, as it was established by Daud.
And he set the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, so that no one who was in any way unclean should enter.

Then he took the captains of hundreds, the nobles, the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and they went through the Upper Gate to the king’s house, and set the king on the throne of the kingdom.
So all the people of the land rejoiced; and the city was quiet, for they had slain Athalyahu with the sword.
Yuash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Yahushalam. His mother’s name was Zibyahu of Baarshaba.
Yuash did what was right in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH all the days of Yahuiada the Kuhan.
And Yahuiada took two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.
Now it happened after this that Yuash set his heart on repairing the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then he gathered the Kuhanym and the Lauym, and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Yahudah, and gather from all Yashar'AL money to repair the house of your 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH from year to year, and see that you do it quickly.” However the Lauym did not do it quickly.

So the king called Yahuiada the chief Kuhan, and said to him, “Why have you not required the Lauym to bring in from Yahudah and from Yahushalam the collection, according to the commandment of Musha the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and of the assembly of Yashar'AL, for the tabernacle of witness?”
For the sons of Athalyahu, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and had also presented all the dedicated things of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to the Baals.
Then at the king’s command they made a chest, and set it outside at the gate of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And they made a proclamation throughout Yahudah and Yahushalam to bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the collection that Musha the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had imposed on Yashar'AL in the wilderness.
Then all the leaders and all the people rejoiced, brought their contributions, and put them into the chest until all had given.

So it was, at that time, when the chest was brought to the king’s official by the hand of the Lauym, and when they saw that there was much money, that the king’s scribe and the high priest’s officer came and emptied the chest, and took it and returned it to its place. Thus they did day by day, and gathered money in abundance.

The king and Yahuiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and they hired masons and carpenters to repair the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and also those who worked in iron and bronze to restore the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
So the workmen labored, and the work was completed by them; they restored the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to its original condition and reinforced it.

When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Yahuiada; they made from it articles for the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, articles for serving and offering, spoons and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH continually all the days of Yahuiada.
But Yahuiada grew old and was full of days, and he died; he was one hundred and thirty years old when he died.
And they buried him in the City of Daud among the kings, because he had done good in Yashar'AL, both toward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and His house.
Now after the death of Yahuiada the leaders of Yahudah came and bowed down to the king. And the king listened to them.
Therefore they left the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers, and served wooden images and idols; and wrath came upon Yahudah and Yahushalam because of their trespass.
Yet He sent Nabym to them, to bring them back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and they testified against them, but they would not listen.

Then the RUACH of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came upon Zacharyahu the son of Yahuiada the Kuhan, who stood above the people, and said to them, “Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘Why do you transgress the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, He has also forsaken you.’ ”
So they conspired against him, and at the command of the king they stoned Zacharyahu the Nabym to death in the court of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Thus Yuash the king did not remember the kindness which Yahuiada his father had done to him, but killed Zacharyahu his son; and as he died, he said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH look on it, and repay!”

So it happened in the spring of the year that the army of Syria came up against him; and they came to Yahudah and Yahushalam, and destroyed all the leaders of the people from among the people, and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.

For the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men; but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH delivered a very great army into their hand, because they had forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers. So they executed judgment against King Yuash.

And when they had withdrawn from him (for they left him severely wounded), his own servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Yahuiada the Kuhan, and killed him on his bed. So he died. And they buried him in the City of Daud, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
These are the ones who conspired against him: Zabad the son of Shima'ath the Ammunitess, and Yahuzabad the son of Shimrith the Muabitess.

Now concerning his sons, and the many oracles about him, and the repairing of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, indeed they are written in the annals of the book of the kings. Then Amazyahu his son reigned in his place.
Amazyah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yahushalam. His mother’s name was Yahuaddan of Yahushalam.
And he did what was right in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but not with a loyal heart.
Now it happened, as soon as the kingdom was established for him, that he executed his servants who had murdered his father the king.

However he did not execute their children, but did as it is written in the Law in the Book of Musha, where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded, saying, “The fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor shall the children be put to death for their fathers; but a person shall die for his own sin.”

Moreover Amazyahu gathered Yahudah together and set over them captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, according to their fathers’ houses, throughout all Yahudah and Banyamin; and he numbered them from twenty years old and above, and found them to be three hundred thousand choice men, able to go to war, who could handle spear and shield.
He also hired one hundred thousand mighty men of valor from Yashar'AL for one hundred talents of silver.
But a servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to him, saying, “O king, do not let the army of Yashar'AL go with you, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is not with Yashar'AL and not with any of the children of Aphraim.
But if you go, Be strong in battle! Even so, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH shall make you fall before the enemy; for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has power to help and to overthrow.”

Then Amazyahu said to the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “But what shall we do about the hundred talents which I have given to the troops of Yashar'AL? And the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH answered, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is able to give you much more than this.”
So Amazyahu discharged the troops that had come to him from Aphraim, to go back home. Therefore their anger was greatly aroused against Yahudah, and they returned home in great anger.
Then Amazyahu strengthened himself, and leading his people, he went to the Valley of Salt and killed ten thousand of the people of Sair.
Also the children of Yahudah took captive ten thousand alive, brought them to the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, so that they all were dashed in pieces.

But as for the soldiers of the army which Amazyahu had discharged, so that they would not go with him to battle, they raided the cities of Yahudah from Samaria to Bath Hurun, killed three thousand in them, and took much spoil.

Now it was so, after Amazyahu came from the slaughter of the Adumites, that he brought the idols of the people of Sair, set them up to be his aluahym (mighty ones), and bowed down before them and burned incense to them.

Therefore the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was aroused against Amazyahu, and He sent him a Nabym who said to him, “Why have you sought the idols of the people, which could not rescue their own people from your hand?”

So it was, as he talked with him, that the king said to him, “Have we made you the king’s counselor? Cease! Why should you be killed?” Then the Nabym ceased, and said, “I know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not heeded my advice.”
Now Amazyahu king of Yahudah asked advice and sent to Yuash the son of Yahuahaz, the son of Yahu, king of Yashar'AL, saying, “Come, let us face one another in battle.”

And Yahuash king of Yashar'AL sent to Amazyahu king of Yahudah, saying, “The thistle that was in Labanun sent to the cedar that was in Labanun, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife’; and a wild beast that was in Labanun passed by and trampled the thistle.
Indeed you say that you have defeated the Adumites, and your heart is lifted up to boast. Stay at home now; why should you meddle with trouble, that you should fall, you and Yahudah with you?”
But Amazyahu would not heed, for it came from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that He might give them into the hand of their enemies, because they sought the idols of Adum.
So Yahuash king of Yashar'AL went out; and Amazyahu king of Yahudah faced one another at Bath Shamash, which belongs to Yahudah.
And Yahudah was defeated by Yashar'AL, and every man fled to his tent.

Then Yahuash the king of Yashar'AL captured Amazyahu king of Yahudah, the son of Yuash, the son of Yahuahaz, at Bath Shamash; and he brought him to Yahushalam, and broke down the wall of Yahushalam from the Gate of Aphraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
And he took all the gold and silver, all the articles that were found in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with Ubad-Adum, the treasures of the king’s house, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.
Amazyahu the son of Yuash, king of Yahudah, lived fifteen years after the death of Yahuash the son of Yahuahaz, king of Yashar'AL.
Now the rest of the acts of Amazyahu, from first to last, indeed are they not written in the book of the kings of Yahudah and Yashar'AL?

After the time that Amazyahu turned away from following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they made a conspiracy against him in Yahushalam, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent people after him to Lachish and killed him there.
Then they brought him on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Yahudah.
Now all the people of Yahudah took Uzzyahu, who was sixteen years old, and made him king instead of his father Amazyahu.
He built Alath and restored it to Yahudah, after the king rested with his fathers.
Uzzyahu was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yahushalam. His mother’s name was Yachulyahu of Yahushalam.
And he did what was right in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, according to all that his father Amazyahu had done.
He sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the days of Zacharyahu, who had understanding in the visions of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and as long as he sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH made him prosper.
Now he went out and made war against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Yabnah, and the wall of Ashdud; and he built cities around Ashdud and among the Philistines.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabians who lived in Gur Baal, and against the Maunites.
Also the Ammunites brought tribute to Uzzyahu. His fame spread as far as the entrance of Mitzraym, for he became exceedingly strong.
And Uzzyahu built towers in Yahushalam at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the corner buttress of the wall; then he fortified them.

Also he built towers in the desert, he dug many wells, for he had much livestock, both in the lowlands and in the plains; he also had farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in Carmel, for he loved the soil.

Moreover Uzzyahu had an army of fighting men who went out to war by companies, according to the number on their roll as prepared by Yaial the scribe and Maasayahu the officer, under the hand of Hananyahu, one of the king’s captains.
The total number of chief officers of the mighty men of valor was two thousand six hundred.
And under their authority was an army of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, that made war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.
Then Uzzyahu prepared for them, for the entire army, shields, spears, helmets, body armor, bows, and slings to cast stones.

And he made devices in Yahushalam, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and large stones. So his fame spread far and wide, for he was marvelously helped by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH till he became strong.

But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction, for he transgressed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH by entering the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to burn incense on the altar of incense.
So Azaryahu the Kuhan went in after him, and with him were eighty Kuhanym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH valiant men.

And they withstood King Uzzyahu, and said to him, “It is not for you, Uzzyahu, to burn incense to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but for the Kuhanym, the sons of Aarun, who are consecrated to burn incense. Get out of the sanctuary, for you have trespassed! You shall have no honor from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.”

Then Uzzyahu became furious; and he had a censer in his hand to burn incense. And while he was angry with the Kuhanym, leprosy broke out on his forehead, before the Kuhanym in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, beside the incense altar.

And Azaryahu the chief Kuhan and all the Kuhanym looked at him, and there, on his forehead, he was leprous; so they thrust him out of that place. Indeed he also hurried to get out, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had struck him.

King Uzzyahu was a leper until the day of his death, he dwelt in an isolated house, because he was a leper; for he was cut off from the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then Yutham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Uzzyahu, from first to last, the Nabym Yashayahu the son of Amuz wrote.
So Uzzyahu rested with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of burial which belonged to the kings, for they said, “He is a leper.” Then Yutham his son reigned in his place.
Yutham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Yahushalam. His mother’s name was Yarushah the daughter of Zaduk.
And he did what was right in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, according to all that his father Uzzyahu had done (although he did not enter the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH). But still the people acted corruptly.
He built the Upper Gate of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and he built extensively on the wall of Uphal.
Moreover he built cities in the mountains of Yahudah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.

He also fought with the king of the Ammunites and defeated them. And the people of Ammun gave him in that year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand kurs of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. The people of Ammun paid this to him in the second and third years also.
So Yutham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Now the rest of the acts of Yutham, and all his wars and his ways, indeed they are written in the book of the kings of Yashar'AL and Yahudah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Yahushalam.
So Yutham rested with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of Daud. Then Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Yahushalam; and he did not do what was right in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as his father Daud had done.
For he walked in the ways of the kings of Yashar'AL, and made molded images for Baals.
He burned incense in the Valley of the Son of Hinnum, and burned his children in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had cast out before the children of Yashar'AL.
And he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH delivered him into the hand of the king of Syria. They defeated him, and carried away a great multitude of them as captives, and brought them to Damascus. Then he was also delivered into the hand of the king of Yashar'AL, who defeated him with a great slaughter.
For Pakah the son of Remalyahu killed one hundred and twenty thousand in Yahudah in one day, all valiant men, because they had forsaken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers.
Zichri, a mighty man of Aphraim, killed Maasayahu the king’s son, Azrikam the officer over the house, and Alkanah who was second to the king.
And the children of Yashar'AL carried away captive of their brethren two hundred thousand women, sons, and daughters; and they also took away much spoil from them, and brought the spoil to Samaria.

But a Nabym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was there, whose name was Udad; and he went out before the army that came to Samaria, and said to them: “Look, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your fathers was angry with Yahudah, He has delivered them into your hand; but you have killed them in a rage that reaches up to Shamaym.
And now you propose to force the children of Yahudah and Yahushalam to be your male and female slaves; but are you not also guilty before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH?
Now hear me therefore, and return the captives, whom you have taken captive from your brethren, for the fierce wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is upon you.”

Then some of the heads of the children of Aphraim, Azaryahu the son of Yuhanan, Barachyahu the son of Mashullamath, Yahizkiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, stood up against those who came from the war,

and said to them, “You shall not bring the captives here, for we already have offended 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. You intend to add to our sins and to our guilt; for our guilt is great, and there is fierce wrath against Yashar'AL.”
So the armed men left the captives and the spoil before the leaders and all the assembly.

Then the men who were designated by name rose up and took the captives, and from the spoil they clothed all who were naked among them, dressed them and gave them sandals, gave them food and drink, and anointed them; and they let all the feeble ones ride on donkeys. So they brought them to their brethren at Yarichu, the city of palm trees. Then they returned to Samaria.
At the same time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.
For again the Adumites had come, attacked Yahudah, and carried away captives.

The Philistines also had invaded the cities of the lowland and of the South of Yahudah, and had taken Bath Shamash, Aiyalun, Gadaruth, Suchuh with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzu with its villages; and they dwelt there.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought Yahudah low because of Ahaz, for he had encouraged moral decline in Yahudah and had been continually unfaithful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Also Tiglath-pilasar king of Assyria came to him and distressed him, and did not assist him.
For Ahaz took part of the treasures from the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, from the house of the king, and from the leaders, and he gave it to the king of Assyria; but he did not help him.
Now in the time of his distress King Ahaz became increasingly unfaithful to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. This is that King Ahaz.

For he sacrificed to the idols of Damascus which had defeated him, saying, “Because the idols of the kings of Syria help them, I will sacrifice to them that they may help me.” But they were the ruin of him and of all Yashar'AL.

So Ahaz gathered the articles of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, cut in pieces the articles of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, shut up the doors of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and made for himself altars in every corner of Yahushalam.
And in every single city of Yahudah he made high places to burn incense to idol, and provoked to anger 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of his fathers.
Now the rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, indeed they are written in the book of the kings of Yahudah and Yashar'AL.
So Ahaz rested with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Yahushalam; but they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Yashar'AL. Then Hazakyahu his son reigned in his place.
Hazakyahu became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yahushalam, his mother’s name was Abiyahu the daughter of Zacharyahu.
And he did what was right in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, according to all that his father Daud had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and repaired them.
Then he brought in the Kuhanym and the Lauym, and gathered them in the East Square,
and said to them: “Hear me, Lauym! Now sanctify yourselves, sanctify the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your fathers, and carry out the rubbish from the Qadash place.

For our fathers have trespassed and done evil in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; they have forsaken Him, and have turned their faces away from the dwelling place of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and turned their backs on Him.
They have also shut up the doors of the vestibule, put out the lamps, and have not burned incense or offered burnt offerings in the Qadash place to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
Therefore the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH fell upon Yahudah and Yahushalam, and He has given them up to trouble, to desolation, and to jeering, as you see with your eyes.
For indeed, because of this our fathers have fallen by the sword; and our sons, our daughters, and our wives are in captivity.
“Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, that His fierce wrath may turn away from us.
My sons, do not be negligent now, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has chosen you to stand before Him, to serve Him, and that you should minister to Him and burn incense.”

Then these Lauym arose: Mahath the son of Amasai and Yual the son of Azaryahu, of the sons of the Kuhathites; of the sons of Marari, Kish the son of Abdi and Azaryahu the son of Yahallalal; of the Garshunites, Yuah the son of Zimmah and Adan the son of Yuah;
of the sons of Alizaphan, Shimri and Yaial; of the sons of Asaph, Zacharyahu and Mattanyahu;
of the sons of Haman, Yahial and Shimai; and of the sons of Yaduthun, Shamayahu and Uzzial.
And they gathered their brethren, sanctified themselves, and went according to the command of the king, at the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to cleanse the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then the kuhanym went into the inner part of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to cleanse it, and brought out all the debris that they found in the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to the court of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And the Lauym took it out and carried it to the Bruuk Kidrun.

Now they began to sanctify on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the vestibule of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. So they sanctified the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
Then they went in to King Hazakyahu and said, “We have cleansed all the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the altar of burnt offerings with all its articles, and the table of the showbread with all its articles.
Moreover all the articles which King Ahaz in his reign had cast aside in his transgression we have prepared and sanctified; and there they are, before the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then King Hazakyahu rose early, gathered the rulers of the city, and went up to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

And they brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats for a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Yahudah. Then he commanded the Kuhanym, the sons of Aarun, to offer them on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

So they killed the bulls, and the Kuhanym received the blood and sprinkled it on the altar. Likewise they killed the rams and sprinkled the blood on the altar. They also killed the lambs and sprinkled the blood on the altar.
Then they brought out the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.

And the Kuhanym killed them; and they presented their blood on the altar as a sin offering to make an atonement for all Yashar'AL, for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering be made for all Yashar'AL.

And he stationed the Lauym in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with cymbals, with stringed instruments, and with harps, according to the command of Daud, and of Gad the king’s seer, and of Nathan the Nabym; for thus was the commandment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by His Nabyms.
