The Lauym stood with the instruments of Daud, and the Kuhanym with the trumpets.

Then Hazakyahu commanded them to offer the burnt offering on the altar. And when the burnt offering began, the song of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH also began, with the trumpets and with the instruments of Daud king of Yashar'AL.
So all the assembly worshiped, the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded; all this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
And when they had finished offering, the king and all who were present with him bowed and worshiped.

Moreover King Hazakyahu and the leaders commanded the Lauym to sing praise to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with the words of Daud and of Asaph the seer. So they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshiped.

Then Hazakyahu answered and said, “Now that you have consecrated yourselves to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, come near, and bring sacrifices and thanksgiving offerings into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” So the assembly brought in sacrifices and thanksgiving offerings, and as many as were of a willing heart brought burnt offerings.
And the number of the burnt offerings which the assembly brought was seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs; all these were for a burnt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The consecrated things were six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep.

But the Kuhanym were too few, so that they could not skin all the burnt offerings; therefore their brethren the Lauym helped them until the work was ended and until the other Kuhanym had sanctified themselves, for the Lauym were more diligent in sanctifying themselves than the Kuhanym.
Also the burnt offerings were in abundance, with the fat of the Shalum offerings and with the drink offerings for every burnt offering. So the service of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was set in order.
Then Hazakyahu and all the people rejoiced that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had prepared the people, since the events took place so suddenly.

And Hazakyahu sent to all Yashar'AL and Yahudah, and also wrote letters to Aphraim and Manassah, that they should come to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at Yahushalam, to keep the Passover to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
For the king and his leaders and all the assembly in Yahushalam had agreed to keep the Passover in the second month.
For they could not keep it at the regular time, because a sufficient number of Kuhanym had not consecrated themselves, nor had the people gathered together at Yahushalam.
And the matter pleased the king and all the assembly.

So they resolved to make a proclamation throughout all Yashar'AL, from Baarshaba to Dan, that they should come to keep the Passover to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL at Yahushalam, since they had not done it for a long time in the prescribed manner.

Then the runners went throughout all Yashar'AL and Yahudah with the letters from the king and his leaders, and spoke according to the command of the king: “Children of Yashar'AL, return to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, Yachaq, and Yashar'AL; then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will return to the remnant of you who have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
And do not be like your fathers and your brethren, who trespassed against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers, that is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them up to desolation, as you see.

Now do not be stiff-necked, as your fathers were, but yield yourselves to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and enter His sanctuary, which He has sanctified forever, and serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, that the fierceness of His wrath may turn away from you.

For if you return to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, your brethren and your children will be treated with compassion by those who lead them captive, so that they may come back to this land; for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is kind and merciful, and will not turn His face from you if you return to Him.”
So the runners passed from city to city through the country of Aphraim and Manassah, as far as Zabulun; but they laughed at them and mocked them.
Nevertheless some from Ashar, Manassah, and Zabulun humbled themselves and came to Yahushalam.
Also the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was on Yahudah to give them singleness of heart to obey the command of the king and the leaders, at the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Now many people, a very great assembly, gathered at Yahushalam to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month.
They arose and took away the altars that were in Yahushalam, and they took away all the incense altars and cast them into the Brook Kidrun.

Then they slaughtered the Passover lambs on the fourteenth day of the second month. The Kuhanym and the Lauym were ashamed, and sanctified themselves, and brought the burnt offerings to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
They stood in their place according to their custom, according to the Law of Musha the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; the Kuhanym sprinkled the blood received from the hand of the Lauym.

For there were many in the assembly who had not sanctified themselves; therefore the Lauym had charge of the slaughter of the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to sanctify them to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

For a multitude of the people, many from Aphraim, Manassah, Issachar, and Zabulun, had not cleansed themselves, yet they ate the Passover contrary to what was written. But Hazakyahu prayed for them, saying, “May the merciful 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH provide atonement for everyone
who prepares his heart to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers, though they are not cleanse according to the purification of the sanctuary.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH listened to Hazakyahu and healed the people.

So the children of Yashar'AL who were present at Yahushalam kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with great gladness; and the Lauym and the Kuhanym Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH day by day, singing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, accompanied by loud instruments.

And Hazakyahu gave encouragement to all the Lauym who taught the good knowledge of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and they ate throughout the feast seven days, offering Shalum offerings and making confession to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers.
Then the whole assembly agreed to keep the feast another seven days, and they kept it another seven days with gladness.

For Hazakyahu king of Yahudah gave to the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the leaders gave to the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and a great number of Kuhanym sanctified themselves.
The whole assembly of Yahudah rejoiced, also the Kuhanym and Lauym, all the assembly that came from Yashar'AL, the sojourners who came from the land of Yashar'AL, and those who dwelt in Yahudah.
So there was great joy in Yahushalam, for since the time of Shalumah the son of Daud, king of Yashar'AL, there had been nothing like this in Yahushalam.
Then the Kuhanym, the Lauym, arose and Baraked the people, and their voice was heard; and their prayer came up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH's Qadash dwelling place in Shamaym.

Now when the Passak was finished, all Yashar'AL who were present went out to the cities of Yahudah and broke the sacred pillars in pieces, cut down the wooden images, and threw down the high places and the altars from all Yahudah, Banyamin, Aphraim, and Manassah until they had utterly destroyed them all. Then all the children of Yashar'AL returned to their own cities, every man to his possession.

And Hazakyahu appointed the divisions of the Kuhanym and the Lauym according to their divisions, each man according to his service, the Kuhanym and Lauym for burnt offerings and Shalum offerings, to serve, to give Tudah, and to Yadah in the gates of the camp of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

The king also appointed a portion of his possessions for the burnt offerings: for the morning and evening burnt offerings, the burnt offerings for the Shabbats and the New Moons and the set feasts, as it is written in the Turah (Law) of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Moreover he commanded the people who dwelt in Yahushalam to contribute support for the Kuhanym and the Lauym, that they might devote themselves to the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

As soon as the commandment was circulated, the children of Yashar'AL brought in abundance the firstfruits of grain and wine, oil and honey, and of all the produce of the field; and they brought in abundantly the tithe of everything.

And the children of Yashar'AL and Yahudah, who dwelt in the cities of Yahudah, brought the tithe of oxen and sheep; also the tithe of Qadash things which were consecrated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH they laid in heaps.
In the third month they began laying them in heaps, and they finished in the seventh month.
And when Hazakyahu and the leaders came and saw the heaps, they Baraked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and His people Yashar'AL.
Then Hazakyahu questioned the Kuhanym and the Lauym concerning the heaps.

And Azaryahu the chief Kuhan, from the house of Zaduk, answered him and said, “Since the people began to bring the offerings into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, we have had enough to eat and have plenty left, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has Baraked His people; and what is left is this great abundance.”
Now Hazakyahu commanded them to prepare rooms in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and they prepared them.
Then they faithfully brought in the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things; Cununyahu the Lauy had charge of them, and Shimai his brother was the next.

Yahial, Azazyahu, Nahath, Asahal, Yarimuth, Yuzabad, Alial, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Banayahu were overseers under the hand of Cununyahu and Shimai his brother, at the command of Hazakyahu the king and Azaryahu the ruler of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Kura the son of Imnah the Lauy, the keeper of the East Gate, was over the freewill offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to distribute the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the most Qadash things.

And under him were Adan, Miniamin, Yashua, Shamayahu, Amaryahu, and Shacanyahu, his faithful assistants in the cities of the Kuhanym, to distribute allotments to their brethren by divisions, to the great as well as the small.

Besides those males from three years old and up who were written in the genealogy, they distributed to everyone who entered the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his daily portion for the work of his service, by his division,
and to the Kuhanym who were written in the genealogy according to their father’s house, and to the Lauym from twenty years old and up according to their work, by their divisions,

and to all who were written in the genealogy, their little ones and their wives, their sons and daughters, the whole company of them, for in their faithfulness they sanctified themselves in righteousness.

Also for the sons of Aarun the Kuhanym, who were in the fields of the common-lands of their cities, in every single city, there were men who were designated by name to distribute portions to all the males among the Kuhanym and to all who were listed by genealogies among the Lauym.
Thus Hazakyahu did throughout all Yahudah, and he did what was good and right and true before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
And in every work that he began in the service of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, in the law and in the commandments, to seek his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, he did it with all his heart. So he prospered.
After these deeds of faithfulness, Sannacharib king of Assyria came and entered Yahudah; he encamped against the fortified cities, thinking to win them over to himself.
And when Hazakyahu saw that Sannacharib had come, and that his purpose was to make war against Yahushalam,
he consulted with his leaders and commanders to stop the water from the springs which were outside the city; and they helped him.
Thus many people gathered together who stopped all the springs and the brook that ran through the land, saying, “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find much water?”

And he strengthened himself, built up all the wall that was broken, raised it up to the towers, and built another wall outside; also he repaired the Millo in the City of Daud, and made weapons and shields in abundance.
Then he set military captains over the people, gathered them together to him in the open square of the city gate, and gave them encouragement, saying,
“Be strong and courageous; do not be afraid nor dismayed before the king of Assyria, nor before all the multitude that is with him; for there are more with us than with him.
With him is an arm of flesh; but with us is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, to help us and to fight our battles.” And the people were strengthened by the words of Hazakyahu king of Yahudah.

After this Sannacharib king of Assyria sent his servants to Yahushalam (but he and all the forces with him laid siege against Lachish), to Hazakyahu king of Yahudah, and to all Yahudah who were in Yahushalam, saying,
“Thus says Sannacharib king of Assyria: ‘In what do you trust, that you remain under siege in Yahushalam?
Does Hazakyahu persuade you to give yourselves over to die by famine and by thirst, saying' 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will deliver us from the hand of the king of Assyria”?
Do you not realize that Hazakyahu is the one who destroyed your high places and altars, and commanded Yahudah and Yahushalam, saying, “You must worship before one altar and burn incense on it”?
Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the idols of the nations of those lands in any way able to deliver their lands out of my hand?
Who was there among all the idols of those nations that my fathers utterly destroyed that could deliver his people from my hand, that your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH should be able to deliver you from my hand?

Now therefore, do not let Hazakyahu deceive you or persuade you like this, and do not believe him; for no idol of any nation or kingdom was able to deliver his people from my hand or the hand of my fathers. How much less will your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH deliver you from my hand?’ ”
Furthermore, his servants spoke against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL and against His servant Hazakyahu.

He also wrote letters to revile 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, and to speak against Him, saying, “As the idols of the nations of other lands have not delivered their people from my hand, so the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Hazakiah will not deliver His people from my hand.”
Then they called out with a loud voice in Abarym (Hebrew) to the people of Yahushalam who were on the wall, to frighten them and trouble them, that they might take the city.
And they spoke against the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yahushalam, as against the idols of the people of the Arath, the work of men’s hands.
Now because of this King Hazakyahu and the Nabym Yashayahu, the son of Amuz, prayed and cried out to Shamaym.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent a Malak who cut down every mighty man of valor, leader, and captain in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned shamefaced to his own land. And when he had gone into the temple of his idols, some of his own offspring struck him down with the sword there.
Thus 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH saved Hazakyahu and the inhabitants of Yahushalam from the hand of Sannacharib the king of Assyria, and from the hand of all others, and guided them on every side.
And many brought gifts to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at Yahushalam, and presents to Hazakyahu king of Yahudah, so that he was exalted in the sight of all nations thereafter.
In those days Hazakyahu was sick and near death, and he prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH spoke to him and gave him a sign.
But Hazakyahu did not repay according to the favor shown him, for his heart was lifted up; therefore wrath was looming over him and over Yahudah and Yahushalam.
Then Hazakyahu humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Yahushalam, so that the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did not come upon them in the days of Hazakyahu.
Hazakyahu had very great riches and honor. And he made himself treasuries for silver, for gold, for precious stones, for spices, for shields, and for all kinds of desirable items;
storehouses for the harvest of grain, wine, and oil; and stalls for all kinds of livestock, and folds for flocks.
Moreover he provided cities for himself, and possessions of flocks and herds in abundance; for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given him very much property.
This same Hazakyahu also stopped the water outlet of Upper Gihun, and brought the water by tunnel to the west side of the City of Daud. Hazakyahu prospered in all his works.

However, regarding the ambassadors of the princes of Babylun, whom they sent to him to inquire about the wonder that was done in the land, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH withdrew from him, in order to test him, that He might know all that was in his heart.
Now the rest of the acts of Hazakyahu, and his goodness, indeed they are written in the vision of Yashayahu the Nabym, the son of Amuz, and in the book of the kings of Yahudah and Yashar'AL.

So Hazakyahu rested with his fathers, and they buried him in the upper tombs of the sons of Daud; and all Yahudah and the inhabitants of Yahushalam honored him at his death. Then Manassah his son reigned in his place.
Manassah was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Yahushalam.
But he did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, according to the abominations of the nations whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had cast out before the children of Yashar'AL.

For he rebuilt the high places which Hazakyahu his father had broken down; he raised up altars for the Baals, and made wooden images; and he worshiped all the host of sky (sun, moon and stars) and served them.
He also built altars in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said, “In Yahushalam shall My name be forever.”
And he built altars for all the host of sky in the two courts of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH

Also he caused his sons to pass through the fire in the Valley of the Son of Hinnum; he practiced soothsaying, used witchcraft and sorcery, and consulted mediums and spiritists, he did much evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to provoke 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to anger.

He even set a carved image, the idol which he had made, in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said to Daud and to Shalumah his son, “In this house and in Yahushalam, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Yashar'AL, I will put My Name forever;

and I will not again remove the foot of Yashar'AL from the land which I have appointed for your fathers, only if they are careful to do all that I have commanded them, according to the whole law and the statutes and the ordinances by the hand of Musha.”
So Manassah seduced Yahudah and the inhabitants of Yahushalam to do more evil than the nations whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had destroyed before the children of Yashar'AL.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH spoke to Manassah and his people, but they would not listen.
Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought upon them the captains of the army of the king of Assyria, who took Manassah with hooks, bound him with bronze fetters, and carried him off to Babylun.
Now when he was in affliction, he implored 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and humbled himself greatly before the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of his fathers,
and he prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and He received his entreaty, heard his supplication, and brought him back to Yahushalam into his kingdom. Then Manassah knew that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

After this he built a wall outside the City of Daud on the west side of Gihun, in the valley, as far as the entrance of the Fish Gate; and it enclosed Uphal, and he raised it to a very great height. Then he put military captains in all the fortified cities of Yahudah.

He took away the foreign idols and the idol from the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and all the altars that he had built in the mount of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and in Yahushalam; and he cast them out of the city.
He also repaired the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, sacrificed Shalum offerings and thank offerings on it, and commanded Yahudah to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
Nevertheless the people still sacrificed on the high places, but only to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

Now the rest of the acts of Manassah, his prayer to his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, indeed they are written in the book of the kings of Yashar'AL.

Also his prayer and how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH received his entreaty, and all his sin and trespass, and the sites where he built high places and set up wooden images and carved images, before he was humbled, indeed they are written among the sayings of Huzai.
So Manassah rested with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house. Then his son Amun reigned in his place.
Amun was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Yahushalam.
But he did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as his father Manassah had done; for Amun sacrificed to all the carved images which his father Manassah had made, and served them.
And he did not humble himself before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as his father Manassah had humbled himself; but Amun trespassed more and more.
Then his servants conspired against him, and killed him in his own house.
But the people of the land executed all those who had conspired against King Amun. Then the people of the land made his son Yusyahu king in his place.
Yusyahu was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Yahushalam.
And he did what was right in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and walked in the ways of his father Daud; he did not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.

For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of his father Daud; and in the twelfth year he began to purge Yahudah and Yahushalam of the high places, the wooden images, the carved images, and the molded images.

They broke down the altars of the Baals in his presence, and the incense altars which were above them he cut down; and the wooden images, the carved images, and the molded images he broke in pieces, and made dust of them and scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He also burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and cleansed Yahudah and Yahushalam.
And so he did in the cities of Manassah, Aphraim, and Simaun, as far as Naphtali and all around, with axes.

When he had broken down the altars and the wooden images, had beaten the carved images into powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Yashar'AL, he returned to Yahushalam.

In the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the land and the temple, he sent Shaphan the son of Azalyahu, Maasayahu the governor of the city, and Yuah the son of Yuahaz the recorder, to repair the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

When they came to Hilkyahu the high Kuhan, they delivered the money that was brought into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, which the Lauym who kept the doors had gathered from the hand of Manassah and Aphraim, from all the remnant of Yashar'AL, from all Yahudah and Banyamin, and which they had brought back to Yahushalam.
Then they put it in the hand of the foremen who had the oversight of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; and they gave it to the workmen who worked in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to repair and restore the house.
They gave it to the craftsmen and builders to buy hewn stone and timber for beams, and to floor the houses which the kings of Yahudah had destroyed.

And the men did the work faithfully. Their overseers were Yahath and Ubadyahu the Lauym, of the sons of Marari, and Zacharyahu and Mashullam, of the sons of the Kuhathites, to supervise. Others of the Lauy, all of whom were skillful with instruments of music,
were over the burden bearers and were overseers of all who did work in any kind of service. And some of the Lauym were scribes, officers, and gatekeepers.
Now when they brought out the money that was brought into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Hilkyahu the Kuhan found the Book of the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH given by Musha.
Then Hilkyahu answered and said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the Book of the Law in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” And Hilkyahu gave the book to Shaphan.
So Shaphan carried the book to the king, bringing the king word, saying, “All that was committed to your servants they are doing.
And they have gathered the money that was found in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and have delivered it into the hand of the overseers and the workmen.”
Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, “Hilkyahu the Kuhan has given me a book.” And Shaphan read it before the king.
Thus it happened, when the king heard the words of the Law, that he tore his clothes.
Then the king commanded Hilkyahu, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdun the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asayahu a servant of the king, saying,

“Go, inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for me, and for those who are left in Yashar'AL and Yahudah, concerning the words of the book that is found; for great is the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that is poured out on us, because our fathers have not kept the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to do according to all that is written in this book.”

So Hilkyahu and those the king had appointed went to Huldah the woman Nabym, the wife of Shallum the son of Tukhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. (She dwelt in Yahushalam in the Second Quarter.) And they spoke to her to that effect.
Then she answered them, “Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, ‘Tell the man who sent you to Me,
“Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘Behold, I will bring calamity on this place and on its inhabitants, all the curses that are written in the book which they have read before the king of Yahudah,

because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other nations idols, that they might provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands. Therefore My wrath will be poured out on this place, and not be quenched.’ ” ’

But as for the king of Yahudah, who sent you to inquire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, in this manner you shall speak to him, ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL: “Concerning the words which you have heard

because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH when you heard His words against this place and against its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before Me, and you tore your clothes and wept before Me, I also have heard you,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

“Surely I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your grave in Shalum; and your eyes shall not see all the calamity which I will bring on this place and its inhabitants.” So they brought back word to the king.
Then the king sent and gathered all the elders of Yahudah and Yahushalam.

The king went up to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, with all the men of Yahudah and the inhabitants of Yahushalam, the Kuhanym and the Lauym, and all the people, great and small. And he read in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant which had been found in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then the king stood in his place and made a covenant before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and to keep His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes with all his heart and all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant that were written in this book.
And he made all who were present in Yahushalam and Banyamin take a stand. So the inhabitants of Yahushalam did according to the covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers.

Thus King Yusyahu removed all the abominations from all the country that belonged to the children of Yashar'AL, and made all who were present in Yashar'AL diligently serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. All his days they did not depart from following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers.
Now King Yusyahu kept the Pasakh (Passover) to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Yahushalam, and they slaughtered the Pasakh lambs on the fourteenth day of the first month.
And he set the Kuhanym in their duties and encouraged them for the service of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then he said to the Lauym who taught all Yashar'AL, who were set apart to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: “Put the Qadash Ark in the house which Shalumah the son of Daud, king of Yashar'AL built. It shall no longer be a burden on your shoulders. Now serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and teach His people Yashar'AL.
Prepare yourselves according to your fathers’ houses, according to your divisions, following the written instruction of Daud king of Yashar'AL and the written instruction of Shalumah his son.
And stand in the Qadash place according to the divisions of the fathers’ houses of your brethren the lay people, and according to the division of the father’s house of the Lauym.
So slaughter the Pasakh offerings, consecrate yourselves, and prepare them for your brethren, that they may do according to the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by the hand of Musha.”

Then King Yusyahu gave the lay people lambs and young goats from the flock, all for Pasakh offerings for all who were present, to the number of thirty thousand, as well as three thousand cattle; these were from the king’s possessions.

And his leaders gave willingly to the people, to the Kuhanym, and to the Lauym. Hilkyahu, Zacharyahu, and Yahial, rulers of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, gave to the Kuhanym for the Pasakh offerings two thousand six hundred from the flock, and three hundred cattle.

Also Cunanyahu, his brothers Shamayahu and Nathanal, and Hashabyahu and Yaial and Yuzabad, chief of the Lauym, gave to the Lauym for Passover offerings five thousand from the flock and five hundred cattle.
So the service was prepared, and the Kuhanym stood in their places, and the Lauym in their divisions, according to the king’s command.
And they slaughtered the Pasakh offerings; and the priests sprinkled the blood with their hands, while the Lauym skinned the animals.

Then they removed the burnt offerings that they might give them to the divisions of the fathers’ houses of the lay people, to offer to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as it is written in the Book of Musha. And so they did with the cattle.

Also they roasted the Pasakh offerings with fire according to the ordinance; but the other Qadash offerings they boiled in pots, in caldrons, and in pans, and divided them quickly among all the lay people.

Then afterward they prepared portions for themselves and for the Kuhanym, because the Kuhanym, the sons of Aarun, were busy in offering burnt offerings and fat until night; therefore the Lauym prepared portions for themselves and for the Kuhanym, the sons of Aarun.

And the singers, the sons of Asaph, were in their places, according to the command of Daud, Asaph, Haman, and Yaduthun the king’s seer. Also the gatekeepers were at each gate; they did not have to leave their position, because their brethren the Lauym prepared portions for them.
So all the service of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was prepared the same day, to keep the Pasakh and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, according to the command of King Yusyahu.
And the children of Yashar'AL who were present kept the Pasakh at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

There had been no Pasakh (passover) kept in Yashar'AL like that since the days of Shamu'AL the Nabym; and none of the kings of Yashar'AL had kept such a Pasakh as king Yusyahu kept, with the Kuhanym and the Lauym, all Yahudah and Yashar'AL who were present, and the inhabitants of Yahushalam.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of king Yusyahu this Passover was kept.
After all this, when Yusyahu had prepared the temple, Nachu king of Mitzraym came up to fight against Carchamish by the Euphrates; and Yusyahu went out against him.

But he sent messengers to him, saying, “What have I to do with you, king of Yahudah? I have not come against you this day, but against the house with which I have war; for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded me to make haste. Refrain from meddling with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who is with me, lest He destroy you.”

Nevertheless Yusyahu would not turn his face from him, but disguised himself so that he might fight with him, and did not heed the words of Nachu from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. So he came to fight in the Valley of Magiddu.
And the archers shot King Yusyahu; and the king said to his servants, “Take me away, for I am severely wounded.”

His servants therefore took him out of that chariot and put him in the second chariot that he had, and they brought him to Yahushalam. So he died, and was buried in one of the tombs of his fathers. And all Yahudah and Yahushalam mourned for Yusyahu.

Yaramyahu also lamented for Yusyahu. And to this day all the singing men and the singing women speak of Yusyahu in their lamentations. They made it a custom in Yashar'AL; and indeed they are written in the Laments.
Now the rest of the acts of Yusyahu and his goodness, according to what was written in the Turah (Law) of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
and his deeds from first to last, indeed they are written in the book of the kings of Yashar'AL and Yahudah.
Then the people of the land took Yahuahaz the son of Yusyahu, and made him king in his father’s place in Yahushalam.
Yahuahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Yahushalam.
Now the king of Mitzraym deposed him at Yahushalam; and he imposed on the land a tribute of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
Then the king of Mitzraym made Yahuahaz’s brother Aliakim king over Yahudah and Yahushalam, and changed his name to Yahuiakim. And Nachu took Yahuahaz his brother and carried him off to Mitzraym.
Yahuiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Yahushalam. And he did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun came up against him, and bound him in bronze fetters to carry him off to Babylun.
Nabuchadnazzar also carried off some of the articles from the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to Babylun, and put them in his temple at Babylun.

Now the rest of the acts of Yahuiakim, the abominations which he did, and what was found against him, indeed they are written in the book of the kings of Yashar'AL and Yahudah. Then Yahuiachin his son reigned in his place.
Yahuiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yahushalam three months and ten days. And he did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH

At the turn of the year King Nabuchadnazzar summoned him and took him to Babylun, with the costly articles from the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and made Zadakyahu, Yahuiakim’s brother, king over Yahudah and Yahushalam.
Zadakyahu was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Yahushalam.
He did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and did not humble himself before Yaramyahu the Nabym, who spoke from the mouth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

And he also rebelled against King Nabuchadnazzar, who had made him swear an oath by 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; but he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.

Moreover all the leaders of the Kuhanym and the people transgressed more and more, according to all the abominations of the nations, and defiled the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which He had consecrated in Yahushalam.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of their fathers sent warnings to them by His messengers, rising up early and sending them, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had compassion on His people and on His dwelling place.
But they mocked the messengers of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, despised His words, and scoffed at His Nabym, until the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH arose against His people, till there was no remedy.

Therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought against them the king of the Chaldaans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man or virgin, on the aged or the weak; He gave them all into his hand.
And all the articles from the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, great and small, the treasures of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the treasures of the king and of his leaders, all these he took to Babylun.
Then they burned the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, broke down the wall of Yahushalam, burned all its palaces with fire, and destroyed all its precious possessions.
And those who escaped from the sword he carried away to Babylun, where they became servants to him and his sons until the rule of the kingdom of Persia,
to fulfill the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by the mouth of Yaramyahu, until the land had enjoyed her Shabbats. As long as she lay desolate she kept Shabbat, to fulfill seventy years.

Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by the mouth of Yaramyahu might be fulfilled, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH stirred up the ruach of Cyrus king of Parsia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also put it in writing, saying,

Thus says Cyrus king of Parsia: All the kingdoms of the Arath 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym has given me. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has commanded me to build Him a house at Yahushalam which is in Yahudah. Who is among you of all His people? May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be with him, and let him go up for this task!

books.name: Ezra
chapters: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Parsia, that the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by the mouth of Yaram'Yahu might be fulfilled, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Parsia, so that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also put it in writing, saying,

Thus says Cyrus king of Parsia: All the kingdoms of the Arath have been given to me by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym. And He has commanded me to build Him a house at Yahushalam which is in Yahudah.
Who amongst you of all the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? May his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be with him, and let him go up to Yahushalam which is in Yahudah, and build the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.

And whoever is left in any place where he dwells, let the men of his place help him with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, besides the freewill offerings for the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which is in Yahushalam.

Then the heads of the fathers’ houses of Yahudah and Banyamin, and the Kuhanym and the Lauym, with all whose ruach 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had moved, arose to go up and build the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which is in Yahushalam.
And all those who were around them encouraged them with articles of silver and gold, with goods and livestock, and with precious things, besides all that was willingly offered.
King Cyrus also brought out the articles of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, which Nabuchadnazzar had taken from Yahushalam and put in the temple of his idols;
And Cyrus king of Parsia brought them out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counted them out to Shashbazzar the prince of Yahudah.
This is the number of them: thirty gold platters, one thousand silver platters, twenty-nine knives,
thirty gold basins, four hundred and ten silver basins of a similar kind, and one thousand other articles.
All the articles of gold and silver were five thousand four hundred. All these Shashbazzar took with the captives who were brought from Babylun to Yahushalam.

Now these are the people of the province who came back from the captivity, of those who had been carried away, whom Nabuchadnazzar the king of Babylun had carried away to Babylun, and who returned to Yahushalam and Yahudah, everyone to his own city.
Those who came with Zarubbabal were Yashua, Nahamayahu, Sarayahu, Raalayahu, Murdacayahu, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigbai, Rahum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Yashar'AL:
the people of Parush, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
the people of Shaphatyahu, three hundred and seventy-two;
the people of Arah, seven hundred and seventy-five;
the people of Pahath-Muab, of the people of Yashua and Yuab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
the people of Alam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the people of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five;
the people of Zaccayah, seven hundred and sixty;
the people of Bani, six hundred and forty-two;
the people of Babai, six hundred and twenty-three;
the people of Azgad, one thousand two hundred and twenty-two;
the people of Adunikam, six hundred and sixty-six;
the people of Bigbai, two thousand and fifty-six;
the people of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four;
the people of Atar of Hazakyahu, ninety-eight;
the people of Bazai, three hundred and twenty-three;
the people of Yurah, one hundred and twelve;
the people of Hashum, two hundred and twenty-three;
the people of Gibbar, ninety-five;
the people of Bathlaham, one hundred and twenty-three;
the men of Natuphah, fifty-six;
the men of Anathuth, one hundred and twenty-eight;
the people of Azmabath, forty-two;
the people of Kiryath Arim, Chaphirah, and Baaruth, seven hundred and forty-three;
the people of Ramah and Gaba, six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas, one hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bathal and Ai, two hundred and twenty-three;
the people of Nabu, fifty-two;
the people of Magbish, one hundred and fifty-six;
the people of the other Alam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the people of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
the people of Lud, Hadid, and Unu, seven hundred and twenty-five;
the people of Yarichu, three hundred and forty-five;
the people of Sanaah, three thousand six hundred and thirty.
The Kuhanym: the sons of Yadayahu, of the house of Yashua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
the sons of Immar, one thousand and fifty-two;
the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
The Lauym: the sons of Yashua and Kadmial, of the sons of Hudabyahu, seventy-four.
The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and twenty-eight.
The sons of the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Atar, the sons of Talmun, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, and the sons of Shubai, one hundred and thirty-nine in all.
The Nathinim: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbauth,
the sons of Karus, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padun,
the sons of Labanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub,
the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shalmai, the sons of Hanan,
the sons of Giddal, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Raayahu,
the sons of Razin, the sons of Nakuda, the sons of Gazzam,
the sons of Uzza, the sons of Pasaah, the sons of Basai,
the sons of Asnah, the sons of Maunim, the sons of Naphusim,
the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mahida, the sons of Harsha,
the sons of Barkus, the sons of Sisara, the sons of Tamah,
the sons of Nazyahu, and the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of Shalumah’s servants: the sons of Sutai, the sons of Supharath, the sons of Paruda,
the sons of Yaala, the sons of Darkun, the sons of Giddal,
the sons of Shaphatyahu, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pucharath of Zabaim, and the sons of Ami.
All the Nathinim and the children of Shalumah’s servants were three hundred and ninety-two.
And these were the ones who came up from Tal Malah, Tal Harsha, Charub, Addan, and Immar; but they could not identify their father’s house or their genealogy, whether they were of Yashar'AL:
the sons of Dalayahu, the sons of Tubiyahu, and the sons of Nakuda, six hundred and fifty-two;
and of the sons of the Kuhanym: the sons of Habayah, the sons of Kuz, and the sons of Barzillyahu, who took a wife of the daughters of Barzillyahu the Gilaadite, and was called by their name.
These sought their listing among those who were registered by genealogy, but they were not found; therefore they were excluded from the Kuhanhood as defiled.
And the governor said to them that they should not eat of the most Qadash things till a Kuhan could consult with the Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly together was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
besides their male and female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred men and women singers.
Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six, their mules two hundred and forty-five,
their camels four hundred and thirty-five, and their donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
Some of the heads of the fathers’ houses, when they came to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which is in Yahushalam, offered freely for the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, to erect it in its place:
According to their ability, they gave to the treasury for the work sixty-one thousand gold drachmas, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred Kuhanym garments.
So the Kuhanym and the Lauym, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the Nathinim, dwelt in their cities, and all Yashar'AL in their cities.
And when the seventh month had come, and the children of Yashar'AL were in the cities, the people gathered together as one man to Yahushalam.

Then Yashua the son of Yuzadak and his brethren the Kuhanym, and Zarubbabal the son of Shaaltial and his brethren, arose and built the altar of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the Law of Musha the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

Though fear had come upon them because of the people of those countries, they set the altar on its bases; and they offered burnt offerings on it to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, both the morning and evening burnt offerings.
They also kept the Feast of Tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings in the number required by ordinance for each day.

Afterwards they offered the regular burnt offering, and those for New Moons and for all the appointed feasts of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that were consecrated, and those of everyone who willingly offered a freewill offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, although the foundation of the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had not been laid.

They also gave money to the masons and the carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidun and Tyra to bring cedar logs from Labanun to the sea, to Yuppa, according to the permission which they had from Cyrus king of Persia.

Now in the second month of the second year of their coming to the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH at Yahushalam, Zarubbabal the son of Shaaltial, Yashua the son of Yuzadak, and the rest of their brethren the Kuhanym and the Lauym, and all those who had come out of the captivity to Yahushalam, began work and appointed the Lauym from twenty years old and above to oversee the work of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Then Yashua with his sons and brothers, Kadmial with his sons, and the sons of Yahudah, arose as one to oversee those working on the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH: the sons of Hanadad with their sons and their brethren the Lauym.

When the builders laid the foundation of the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the Kuhanym stood in their apparel with trumpets, and the Lauym, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, according to the ordinance of Daud king of Yashar'AL.

And they sang responsively, Yadah and giving Tudah to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: “For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is good, For His mercy endures forever toward Yashar'AL.” Then all the people shouted with a great shout, when they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, because the foundation of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was laid.

But many of the Kuhanym and Lauym and heads of the fathers’ houses, old men who had seen the first temple, wept with a loud voice when the foundation of this temple was laid before their eyes. Yet many shouted aloud for joy,
so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people, for the people shouted with a loud shout, and the sound was heard afar off.
Now when the adversaries of Yahudah and Banyamin heard that the descendants of the captivity were building the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL,

they came to Zarubbabal and the heads of the fathers’ houses, and said to them, “Let us build with you, for we seek your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH as you do; and we have sacrificed to Him since the days of Asarhaddun king of Assyria, who brought us here.”

But Zarubbabal and Yashua and the rest of the heads of the fathers’ houses of Yashar'AL said to them, “You may do nothing with us to build a house for our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; but we alone will build to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, as King Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.”
Then the people of the land tried to discourage the people of Yahudah. They troubled them in building,
And hired counselors against them to frustrate their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
In the reign of Ahasuarus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Yahudah and Yahushalam.

In the days of Artaxarxas also, Bishlam, Mithradath, Tabal, and the rest of their companions wrote to Artaxarxas king of Persia; and the letter was written in Aramaic script, and translated into the Aramaic language.
Rahum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Yahushalam to King Artaxarxas in this fashion:

From Rahum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their companions, representatives of the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpalites, the people of Persia and Arach and Babylun and Shushan, the Dahavites, the Alamites,
and the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Usnappar took captive and settled in the cities of Samaria and the remainder beyond the River and so forth.
(This is a copy of the letter that they sent him.) To King Artaxarxas from your servants, the men of the region beyond the River, and so forth:

Let it be known to the king that the Yahudym who came up from you have come to us at Yahushalam, and are building the rebellious and evil city, and are finishing its walls and repairing the foundations.
Let it now be known to the king that, if this city is built and the walls completed, they will not pay tax, tribute, or custom, and the king’s treasury will be diminished.
Now because we receive support from the palace, it was not proper for us to see the king’s dishonor; therefore we have sent and informed the king,

That search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. And you will find in the book of the records and know that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that they have incited sedition within the city in former times, for which cause this city was destroyed.
We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are completed, the result will be that you will have no dominion beyond the River.
The king sent an answer: To Rahum the commander, to Shimshai the scribe, to the rest of their companions who dwell in Samaria, and to the remainder beyond the River: Shalum, and so forth.
The letter which you sent to us has been clearly read before me.
And I gave the command, and a search has been made, and it was found that this city in former times has revolted against kings, and rebellion and sedition have been fostered in it.
There have also been mighty kings over Yahushalam, who have ruled over all the region beyond the River; and tax, tribute, and custom were paid to them.
Now give the command to make these men cease, that this city may not be built until the command is given by me.
Take heed now that you do not fail to do this. Why should damage increase to the hurt of the kings?

Now when the copy of King Artaxarxas’ letter was read before Rahum, Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went up in haste to Yahushalam against the Yahudym, and by force of arms made them cease.
Thus the work of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which is at Yahushalam ceased, and it was discontinued until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
Then the Nabym Haggyahu and Zacharyahu the son of Iddu, prophesied to the Yahudym who were in Yahudah and Yahushalam, in the Name of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, who was over them.

So Zarubbabal the son of Shaaltial and Yashua the son of Yuzadak rose up and began to build the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which is in Yahushalam; and the Nabyms of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH were with them, helping them.

At the same time Tattanai the governor of the region beyond the River and Shathar-Buznai and their companions came to them and spoke thus to them: “Who has commanded you to build this temple and finish this wall?”
Then, accordingly, we told them the names of the men who were constructing this building.
But the eye of their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was upon the elders of the Yahudym, so that they could not make them cease till a report could go to Darius. Then a written answer was returned concerning this matter.

This is a copy of the letter that Tattanai sent: The governor of the region beyond the River, and Shathar-Buznai, and his companions, the Parsians who were in the region beyond the River, to Darius the king.
They sent a letter to him, in which was written thus. To Darius the king: All Shalum.

Let it be known to the king that we went into the province of Yahudah, to the temple of the great 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, which is being built with heavy stones, and timber is being laid in the walls; and this work goes on diligently and prospers in their hands.
Then we asked those elders, and spoke thus to them: “Who commanded you to build this temple and to finish these walls?”
We also asked them their names to inform you, that we might write the names of the men who were chief among them.

And thus they returned us an answer, saying: “We are the servants of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym and Arath, and we are rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago, which a great king of Yashar'AL built and completed.

But because our fathers provoked the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym to wrath, He gave them into the hand of Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun, the Chaldaans, who destroyed this temple and carried the people away to Babylun.
However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylun, King Cyrus issued a decree to build this house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Also, the gold and silver articles of the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, which Nabuchadnazzar had taken from the temple that was in Yahushalam and carried into the temple of Babylun, those King Cyrus took from the temple of Babylun, and they were given to one named Shashbazzar, whom he had made governor.
And he said to him, ‘Take these articles; go, carry them to the temple site that is in Yahushalam, and let the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH be rebuilt on its former site.’
Then the same Shashbazzar came and laid the foundation of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which is in Yahushalam; but from that time even until now it has been under construction, and it is not finished.”

Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king’s treasure house, which is there in Babylun, whether it is so that a decree was issued by King Cyrus to build this house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at Yahushalam, and let the king send us his pleasure concerning this matter.
Then King Darius issued a decree, and a search was made in the archives, where the treasures were stored in Babylun.
And at Achmatha, in the palace that is in the province of Madia, a scroll was found, and in it a record was written thus:

In the first year of King Cyrus, he issued a decree concerning the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at Yahushalam: “Let the house be rebuilt, the place where they offered sacrifices; and let the foundations of it be firmly laid, its height sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits,
with three rows of heavy stones and one row of new timber. Let the expenses be paid from the king’s treasury.

Also let the gold and silver articles of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, which Nabuchadnazzar took from the temple which is in Yahushalam and brought to Babylun, be restored and taken back to the temple which is in Yahushalam, each to its place; and deposit them in the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH”
Now therefore, Tattanai, governor of the region beyond the River, and Shathar-Buznai, and your companions the Persians who are beyond the River, keep yourselves far from there.
Let the work of this house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH alone; let the governor of the Yahudym and the elders of the Yahudym build this house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH on its site.

Moreover I issue a decree as to what you shall do for the elders of these Yahudym, for the building of this house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: Let the cost be paid at the king’s expense from taxes on the region beyond the River; this is to be given immediately to these men, so that they are not hindered.

And whatever they need, young bulls, rams, and lambs for the burnt offerings of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym, wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the request of the Kuhanym who are in Yahushalam let it be given them day by day without fail,
that they may offer sacrifices of sweet aroma to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym, and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
Also I issue a decree that whoever alters this edict, let a timber be pulled from his house and erected, and let him be hanged on it; and let his house be made a refuse heap because of this.

And may the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who causes His Name to dwell there, destroy any king or people who put their hand to alter it, or to destroy this house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which is in Yahushalam. I Darius issue a decree; let it be done diligently.
Then Tattanai, governor of the region beyond the River, Shathar-Buznai, and their companions diligently did according to what King Darius had sent.

So the elders of the Yahudym built, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the Nabym and Zacharayah the son of Iddu. And they built and finished it, according to the command of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, and according to the command of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxarxas king of Persia.
Now the temple was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
Then the children of Yashar'AL, the Kuhanym and the Lauym and the rest of the descendants of the captivity, celebrated the dedication of this house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with joy.

And they offered sacrifices at the dedication of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Yashar'AL twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Yashar'AL.
They assigned the Kuhanym to their divisions and the Lauym to their divisions, over the service of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Yahushalam, as it is written in the Book of Musha.
And the descendants of the captivity kept the Pasakh on the fourteenth day of the first month.

For the Kuhanym and the Lauym had purified themselves; all of them were ritually clean. And they slaughtered the Passover lambs for all the descendants of the captivity, for their brethren the Kuhanym, and for themselves.

Then the children of Yashar'AL who had returned from the captivity ate together with all who had separated themselves from the filth of the nations of the land in order to seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.

And they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with joy; for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made them joyful, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxarxas king of Persia, Azrah the son of Sarayahu, the son of Azaryahu, the son of Hilkyahu,
the son of Shallum, the son of Zaduk, the son of Ahitub,
the son of Amaryahu, the son of Azaryahu, the son of Maraiuth,
the son of Zarahyahu, the son of Uzzi, the son of Bukki,
the son of Abishua, the son of Phinahas, the son of Alaazar, the son of Aarun the chief Kuhan

this Azrah came up from Babylun; and he was a skilled scribe in the Law of Musha, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL had given. The king granted him all his request, according to the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH upon him.
Some of the children of Yashar'AL, the Kuhanym, the Lauym, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the Nathinim came up to Yahushalam in the seventh year of King Artaxarxas.
And Azrah came to Yahushalam in the fifth month, which was in the seventh year of the king.
On the first day of the first month he began his journey from Babylun, and on the first day of the fifth month he came to Yahushalam, according to the good hand of his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH upon him.
For Azrah had prepared his heart to seek the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Yashar'AL.
This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxarxas gave Azrah the chief Kuhan, the scribe, expert in the words of the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and of His statutes to Yashar'AL:
Artaxerxes, king of kings, To Azrah the Kuhan, a scribe of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym: Perfect Shalum, and so forth.
I issue a decree that all those of the people of Yashar'AL and the Kuhanym and Lauym in my realm, who volunteer to go up to Yahushalam, may go with you.
And where you are being sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire concerning Yahudah and Yahushalam, with regard to the Law of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH which is in your hand;
and where you are to carry the silver and gold which the king and his counselors have freely offered to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, whose dwelling is in Yahushalam;

and where all the silver and gold that you may find in all the province of Babylun, along with the freewill offering of the people and the Kuhanym, are to be freely offered for the house of their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in Yahushalam

now therefore, be careful to buy with this money bulls, rams, and lambs, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of the house of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in Yahushalam.
And whatever seems good to you and your brethren to do with the rest of the silver and the gold, do it according to the will of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Also the articles that are given to you for the service of the house of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, deliver in full before the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yahushalam.
And whatever more may be needed for the house of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, which you may have occasion to provide, pay for it from the king’s treasury.

And I, even I, Artaxarxas the king, issue a decree to all the treasurers who are in the region beyond the River, that whatever Azrah the chief Kuhan, the scribe of the Law of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym, may require of you, let it be done diligently,
up to one hundred talents of silver, one hundred kurs of wheat, one hundred baths of wine, one hundred baths of oil, and salt without prescribed limit.
Whatever is commanded by the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym, let it diligently be done for the house of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym. For why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons?
Also we inform you that it shall not be lawful to impose tax, tribute, or custom on any of the Kuhanym, Lauym, singers, gatekeepers, Nathinim, or servants of this house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

And you, Azrah, according to the wisdom your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given you, set magistrates and judges who may judge all the people who are in the region beyond the River, all such as know the laws of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; and teach those who do not know them.
Whoever will not observe the law of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and the law of the king, let judgment be executed speedily on him, whether it be death, or banishment, or confiscation of goods, or imprisonment.
Baraked be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which is in Yahushalam,

and has extended mercy to me before the king and his counselors, and before all the king’s mighty princes. So I was encouraged, as the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was upon me; and I gathered leading men of Yashar'AL to go up with me.
These are the heads of their fathers’ houses, and this is the genealogy of those who went up with me from Babylun, in the reign of King Artaxarxas:
of the sons of Phinahas, Garshum; of the sons of Ithamar, Dany'AL; of the sons of Daud, Hattush;
of the sons of Shacanyahu, of the sons of Parush, Zacharyahu; and registered with him were one hundred and fifty males;
of the sons of Pahath-Muab, Aliahuanai the son of Zarahyahu, and with him two hundred males;
of the sons of Shachanyahu, Ban-Yahazial, and with him three hundred males;
of the sons of Adin, Abad the son of Yunathan, and with him fifty males;
of the sons of Alam, Yashayahu the son of Athalyahu, and with him seventy males;
of the sons of Shaphatyahu, Zabadyahu the son of Michaal, and with him eighty males;
of the sons of Yuab, Ubadyahu the son of Yahial, and with him two hundred and eighteen males;
of the sons of Shalumith, Ban-Yusiphyahu, and with him one hundred and sixty males;
of the sons of Babai, Zacharyahu the son of Babai, and with him twenty-eight males;
of the sons of Azgad, Yuhanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred and ten males;
of the last sons of Adunikam, whose names are these, Aliphalat, Yaial, and Shamayahu and with them sixty males;
also of the sons of Bigbai, Uthai and Zabbud, and with them seventy males.
Now I gathered them by the river that flows to Ahaba, and we camped there three days. And I looked among the people and the Kuhanym, and found none of the sons of Lauy there.
Then I sent for Aliazar, Arial, Shamayahu, Alnathan, Yarib, Alnathan, Nathan, Zacharyahu, and Mashullam, leaders; also for Yuiarib and Alnathan, men of understanding.

And I gave them a command for Iddu the chief man at the place Casiphia, and I told them what they should say to Iddu and his brethren the Nathinim at the place Casiphia that they should bring us servants for the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

Then, by the good hand of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH upon us, they brought us a man of understanding, of the sons of Mahli the son of Lauy, the son of Yashar'AL, namely Sharabyahu, with his sons and brothers, eighteen men;
and Hashabyahu, and with him Yashayahu of the sons of Marari, his brothers and their sons, twenty men;
also of the Nathinim, whom Daud and the leaders had appointed for the service of the Lauym, two hundred and twenty Nathinim. All of them were designated by name.
Then I proclaimed a fast there at the river of Ahaba, that we might humble ourselves before our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, to seek from Him the right way for us and our little ones and all our possessions.

For I was ashamed to request of the king an escort of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the enemy on the road, because we had spoken to the king, saying, “The hand of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is upon all those for good who seek Him, but His power and His wrath are against all those who forsake Him.”
So we fasted and entreated our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for this, and He answered our prayer.
And I separated twelve of the leaders of the Kuhanym, Sharabyahu, Hashabyahu, and ten of their brethren with them,

and weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the articles, the offering for the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH which the king and his counselors and his princes, and all Yashar'AL who were present, had offered.
I weighed into their hand six hundred and fifty talents of silver, silver articles weighing one hundred talents, one hundred talents of gold,
twenty gold basins worth a thousand drachmas, and two vessels of fine polished bronze, precious as gold.
And I said to them, “You are qadash to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH; the articles are Qadash also; and the silver and the gold are a freewill offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your fathers.
Watch and keep them until you weigh them before the leaders of the Kuhanym and the Lauym and heads of the fathers’ houses of Yashar'AL in Yahushalam, in the chambers of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So the Kuhanym and the Lauym received the silver and the gold and the articles by weight, to bring them to Yahushalam to the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

Then we departed from the river of Ahaba on the twelfth day of the first month, to go to Yahushalam. And the hand of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH was upon us, and He delivered us from the hand of the enemy and from ambush along the road.
So we came to Yahushalam, and stayed there three days.

Now on the fourth day the silver and the gold and the articles were weighed in the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH by the hand of Maramuth the son of Uryahu the Kuhan, and with him was Alaazar the son of Phinahas; with them were the Lauym, Yuzabad the son of Yashua and Nuadyahu the son of Binnui,
with the number and weight of everything. All the weight was written down at that time.

The children of those who had been carried away captive, who had come from the captivity, offered burnt offerings to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL: twelve bulls for all Yashar'AL, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering. All this was a burnt offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And they delivered the king’s orders to the king’s satraps and the governors in the region beyond the River. So they gave support to the people and the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

When these things were done, the leaders came to me, saying, “The people of Yashar'AL and the Kuhanym and the Lauym have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands, with respect to the abominations of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Parizzites, the Yabusites, the Ammunites, the Muabites, the Mitzraym, and the Amurites.

For they have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and their sons, so that the Qadash seed is mixed with the peoples of those lands. Indeed, the hand of the leaders and rulers has been foremost in this trespass.”
So when I heard this thing, I tore my garment and my robe, and plucked out some of the hair of my head and beard, and sat down astonished.

Then everyone who trembled at the Dabar of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL assembled to me, because of the transgression of those who had been carried away captive, and I sat astonished until the evening sacrifice.
At the evening sacrifice I arose from my fasting; and having torn my garment and my robe, I fell on my knees and spread out my hands to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
And I said: “O my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, I am too ashamed and humiliated to lift up my face to You, my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; for our iniquities have risen higher than our heads, and our guilt has grown up to the Shamaym.

Since the days of our fathers to this day we have been very guilty, and for our iniquities we, our kings, and our Kuhanym have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to humiliation, as it is this day.

And now for a little while Mercy has been shown from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a security in His Qadash place, that our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH may enlighten our eyes and give us a measure of revival in our bondage.

For we were slaves. Yet our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH did not forsake us in our bondage; but He extended mercy to us in the sight of the kings of Parsia, to revive us, to repair the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, to rebuild its ruins, and to give us a wall in Yahudah and Yahushalam.
And now, O our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, what shall we say after this? For we have forsaken Your commandments,

which You commanded by Your servants the Nabyms, saying, ‘The land which you are entering to possess is an unclean land, with the uncleanness of the peoples of the lands, with their abominations which have filled it from one end to another with their impurity.

Now therefore, do not give your daughters as wives for their sons, nor take their daughters to your sons; and never seek their Shalum or prosperity, that you may be strong and eat the good of the land, and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.’
And after all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and for our great guilt, since You our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH have punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and have given us such deliverance as this,

should we again break Your commandments, and join in marriage with the people committing these abominations? Would You not be angry with us until You had consumed us, so that there would be no remnant or survivor?

O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, You are righteous, for we are left as a remnant, as it is this day. Here we are before You, in our guilt, though no one can stand before You because of this!”

Now while Azrah was praying, and while he was confessing, weeping, and bowing down before the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, a very large assembly of men, women, and children gathered to him from Yashar'AL; for the people wept very bitterly.

And Shachanyahu the son of Yahial, one of the sons of Alam, spoke up and said to Azrah, “We have trespassed against our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and have taken pagan wives from the peoples of the land; yet now there is hope in Yashar'AL in spite of this.

Now therefore, let us make a covenant with our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH to put away all these wives and those who have been born to them, according to the advice of my master and of those who tremble at the commandment of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; and let it be done according to the law.
Arise, for this matter is your responsibility. We also are with you. Be of good courage, and do it.”
Then Azrah arose, and made the leaders of the Kuhanym, the Lauym, and all Yashar'AL swear an oath that they would do according to this word. So they swore an oath.

Then Azrah rose up from before the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and went into the chamber of Yahuhanan the son of Aliashib; and when he came there, he ate no bread and drank no water, for he mourned because of the guilt of those from the captivity.
And they issued a proclamation throughout Yahudah and Yahushalam to all the descendants of the captivity, that they must gather at Yahushalam,

and that whoever would not come within three days, according to the instructions of the leaders and elders, all his property would be confiscated, and he himself would be separated from the assembly of those from the captivity.

So all the men of Yahudah and Banyamin gathered at Yahushalam within three days. It was the ninth month, on the twentieth of the month; and all the people sat in the open square of the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, trembling because of this matter and because of heavy rain.
Then Azrah the chief Kuhan stood up and said to them, “You have transgressed and have taken pagan wives, adding to the guilt of Yashar'AL.
Now therefore, make confession to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your fathers, and do His will; separate yourselves from the peoples of the land, and from the pagan wives.”
Then all the assembly answered and said with a loud voice, “Yes! As you have said, so we must do.

But there are many people; it is the season for heavy rain, and we are not able to stand outside. Nor is this the work of one or two days, for there are many of us who have transgressed in this matter.

Please, let the leaders of our entire assembly stand; and let all those in our cities who have taken pagan wives come at appointed times, together with the elders and judges of their cities, until the fierce wrath of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is turned away from us in this matter.”
Only Yunathan the son of Asahal and Yahazyahu the son of Tikbah opposed this, and Mashullam and Shabbathai the Lauy gave them support.

Then the descendants of the captivity did so. And Azrah the chief Kuhan, with certain heads of the fathers’ households, were set apart by the fathers’ households, each of them by name; and they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
By the first day of the first month they finished questioning all the men who had taken pagan wives.
And among the sons of the Kuhanym who had taken pagan wives the following were found of the sons of Yashua the son of Yuzadak, and his brothers: Maasayah, Aliazar, Yarib, and Gadalyahu.
And they gave their promise that they would put away their wives; and being guilty, they presented a ram of the flock as their trespass offering.
Also of the sons of Immar: Hanani and Zabadyahu;
of the sons of Harim: Maasayahu, Aliyahu, Shamayahu, Yahial, and Uzzyahu;
of the sons of Pashhur: Aliuanai, Maasayahu, Ishmaal, Nethanal, Yuzabad, and Alasah.
Also of the Lauym: Yuzabad, Shimai, Kalayahu (the same is Kalita), Pathahyahu, Yahudah, and Aliazar.
Also of the singers: Aliashib; and of the gatekeepers: Shallum, Talam, and Uri.
And others of Yashar'AL: of the sons of Parush: Ramyahu, Yazyahu, Malchyahu, Miyamin, Alaazar, Malchiyahu, and Banayahu;
of the sons of Alam: Mattanyahu, Zacharyahu, Yahial, Abdi, Yaramuth, and Alyah;
of the sons of Zattu: Aliuanai, Aliashib, Mattanyahu, Yaramuth, Zabad, and Aziza;
of the sons of Babai: Yahuhanan, Hananyah, Zabbai, and Athlai;
of the sons of Bani: Mashullam, Malluch, Adayahu, Yashub, Shaal, and Ramuth;
of the sons of Pahath-Muab: Adna, Chalal, Banayahu, Maasayahu, Mattanyahu, Bazalal, Binnui, and Manassah;
of the sons of Harim: Aliazar, Ishiyahu, Malchiyah, Shemayahu, Shimaun,
Banyamin, Malluch, and Shamaryahu;
of the sons of Hashum: Mattanai, Mattattah, Zabad, Aliphalat, Yaramai, Manassah, and Shimai;
of the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Ual,
Banayahu, Badayahu, Chaluh,
Vanyahu, Maramuth, Aliashib,
Mattanyahu, Mattanai, Yaasai,
Bani, Binnui, Shimai,
Shalamyahu, Nathan, Adayahu,
Machnadabai, Shashai, Sharai,
Azaral, Shalamyahu, Shamaryahu,
Shallum, Amariahu, and Ya'asaf;
of the sons of Nabu: Yayal, Mattithyahu, Zabad, Zabina, Yaddai, Yual, and Banayahu.
All these had taken pagan wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had children.

books.name: Nehemiah
chapters: The words of Nahamyahu the son of Hachalyahu. It came to pass in the month of Chislab, in the twentieth year, as I was in Shushan the citadel,
that Hanani one of my brethren came with men from Yahudah; and I asked them concerning the Yahudym who had escaped, who had survived the captivity, and concerning Yahushalam.

And they said to me, “The survivors who are left from the captivity in the province are there in great distress and reproach. The wall of Yahushalam is also broken down, and its gates are burned with fire.”
So it was, when I heard these words, that I sat down and wept, and mourned for many days; I was fasting and praying before the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym.
And I said: O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym, O great and awesome 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, You who keep Your covenant and mercy with those who love You and observe Your commandments,

please let Your ear be attentive and Your eyes open, that You may hear the prayer of Your servant which I pray before You now, day and night, for the children of Yashar'AL Your servants, and confess the sins of the children of Yashar'AL which we have sinned against You. Both my father’s house and I have sinned.
We have acted very corruptly against You, and have not kept the commandments, the statutes, nor the ordinances which You commanded Your servant Musha.
Remember, I pray, the word that You commanded Your servant Musha, saying, ‘If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations;

but if you return to Me, and keep My commandments and do them, though some of you were cast out to the farthest part of the Shamaym, yet I will gather them from there, and bring them to the place which I have chosen as a dwelling for My Name.’
Now these are Your servants and Your people, whom You have redeemed by Your great power, and by Your strong hand.

O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, I pray, please let Your ear be attentive to the prayer of Your servant, and to the prayer of Your servants who desire to fear Your Name; and let Your servant prosper this day, I pray, grant him mercy in the sight of this man. For I was the king’s cupbearer.

And it came to pass in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxarxas, when wine was before him, that I took the wine and gave it to the king. Now I had never been sad in his presence before.
Therefore the king said to me, “Why is your face sad, since you are not sick? This is nothing but sorrow of heart.” So I became dreadfully afraid,
and said to the king, “May the king live forever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ tombs, lies waste, and its gates are burned with fire?”
Then the king said to me, “What do you request?” So I prayed to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym.
And I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, I ask that you send me to Yahudah, to the city of my fathers’ tombs, that I may rebuild it.”
