Then the king said to me (the queen also sitting beside him), “How long will your journey be? And when will you return?” So it pleased the king to send me; and I set him a time.
Furthermore I said to the king, “If it pleases the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of the region beyond the River, that they must permit me to pass through till I come to Yahudah,

and a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king’s forest, that he must give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel which pertains to the temple, for the city wall, and for the house that I will occupy.” And the king granted them to me according to the good hand of my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH upon me.
Then I went to the governors in the region beyond the River, and gave them the king’s letters. Now the king had sent captains of the army and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat the Hurunite and Tubiah the Ammunites official heard of it, they were deeply disturbed that a man had come to seek the well-being of the children of Yashar'AL.
So I came to Yahushalam and was there three days.
Then I arose in the night, I and a few men with me; I told no one what my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had put in my heart to do at Yahushalam; nor was there any animal with me, except the one on which I rode.
And I went out by night through the Valley Gate to the Serpent Well and the Refuse Gate, and viewed the walls of Yahushalam which were broken down and its gates which were burned with fire.
Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and to the King’s Pool, but there was no room for the animal under me to pass.
So I went up in the night by the valley, and viewed the wall; then I turned back and entered by the Valley Gate, and so returned.
And the officials did not know where I had gone or what I had done; I had not yet told the Yahudym, the Kuhanym, the nobles, the officials, or the others who did the work.

Then I said to them, “You see the distress that we are in, how Yahushalam lies waste, and its gates are burned with fire. Come and let us build the wall of Yahushalam, that we may no longer be a reproach.”

And I told them of the hand of my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH which had been good upon me, and also of the king’s words that he had spoken to me. So they said, “Let us rise up and build.” Then they set their hands to this good work.

But when Sanballat the Hurunite, Tubiah the Ammunite official, and Gasham the Arab heard of it, they laughed at us and despised us, and said, “What is this thing that you are doing? Will you rebel against the king?”
So I answered them, and said to them, “The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym Himself will prosper us; therefore we His servants will arise and build, but you have no heritage or right or memorial in Yahushalam.”

Then Aliashib the high Kuhan rose up with his brethren the Kuhanym and built the Sheep Gate; they consecrated it and hung its doors. They built as far as the Tower of the Hundred, and consecrated it, then as far as the Tower of Hananal.
Next to Aliashib the men of Yarichu built. And next to them Zaccur the son of Imri built.
Also the sons of Hassanaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and hung its doors with its bolts and bars.

And next to them Maramuth the son of Uriyahu, the son of Kuz, made repairs. Next to them Mashullam the son of Barachyahu, the son of Mashazabal, made repairs. Next to them Zaduk the son of Baana made repairs.
Next to them the Takuites made repairs; but their nobles did not put their shoulders to the work of their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Moreover Yahuiada the son of Pasaah and Mashullam the son of Basudayahu repaired the Old Gate; they laid its beams and hung its doors, with its bolts and bars.
And next to them Malatyahu the Gibaunite, Yadun the Marunuthite, the men of Gibaun and Mizpah, repaired the residence of the governor of the region beyond the River.
Next to him Uzzial the son of Harhayahu, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs. Also next to him Hananyahu, one of the perfumers, made repairs; and they fortified Yahushalam as far as the Broad Wall.
And next to them Raphayah the son of Hur, leader of half the district of Yahushalam, made repairs.
Next to them Yadayahu the son of Harumaph made repairs in front of his house. And next to him Hattush the son of Hashabnyahu made repairs.
Malchiyahu the son of Harim and Hashub the son of Pahath-Muab repaired another section, as well as the Tower of the Ovens.
And next to him was Shallum the son of Halluhash, leader of half the district of Yahushalam; he and his daughters made repairs.
Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanuah repaired the Valley Gate. They built it, hung its doors with its bolts and bars, and repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Refuse Gate.
Malchiyahu the son of Rachab, leader of the district of Bath Haccaram, repaired the Refuse Gate; he built it and hung its doors with its bolts and bars.

Shallun the son of Cul-Huzah, leader of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate; he built it, covered it, hung its doors with its bolts and bars, and repaired the wall of the Pool of Shalah by the King’s Garden, as far as the stairs that go down from the City of Daud.

After him Nahamyahu the son of Azbuk, leader of half the district of Bath Zur, made repairs as far as the place in front of the tombs of Daud, to the man-made pool, and as far as the House of the Mighty.
After him the Lauym, under Rahum the son of Bani, made repairs. Next to him Hashabyahu, leader of half the district of Kailah, made repairs for his district.
After him their brethren, under Babai the son of Hanadad, leader of the other half of the district of Kailah, made repairs.
And next to him Azar the son of Yashua, the leader of Mizpah, repaired another section in front of the Ascent to the Armory at the buttress.
After him Baruch the son of Zabbai carefully repaired the other section, from the buttress to the door of the house of Aliashib the high Kuhan.
After him Maramuth the son of Uriyahu, the son of Kuz, repaired another section, from the door of the house of Aliashib to the end of the house of Aliashib.
And after him the Kuhanym, the men of the plain, made repairs.
After him Banyamin and Hasshub made repairs opposite their house. After them Azaryahu the son of Maasayahu, the son of Ananyahu, made repairs by his house.
After him Binnui the son of Hanadad repaired another section, from the house of Azaryahu to the buttress, even as far as the corner.

Palal, the son of Uzai made repairs opposite the buttress, and on the tower which projects from the king’s upper house that was by the court of the prison. After him Padayahu the son of Parush made repairs.
Moreover the Nathinim who dwelt in Uphal made repairs as far as the place in front of the Water Gate toward the east, and on the projecting tower.
After them the Takuites repaired another section, next to the great projecting tower, and as far as the wall of Uphal.
Beyond the Horse Gate the Kuhanym made repairs, each in front of his own house.
After them Zaduk the son of Immar made repairs in front of his own house. After him Shamayahu the son of Shachanyahu, the keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.
After him Hananyahu the son of Shalamyahu, and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After him Mashullam the son of Barachyahu made repairs in front of his dwelling.
After him Malchiyahu, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the Nathinim and of the merchants, in front of the Miphkad Gate, and as far as the upper room at the corner.
And between the upper room at the corner, as far as the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
But it so happened, when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, that he was furious and very indignant, and mocked the Yahudym.

And he spoke before his brethren and the army of Samaria, and said, “What are these feeble Yahudym doing? Will they fortify themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they complete it in a day? Will they revive the stones from the heaps of rubbish stones that are burned?”
Now Tubiah the Ammunite was beside him, and he said, “Whatever they build, if even a fox goes up on it, he will break down their stone wall.”
Then I prayed, Hear us, O our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, for we are mocked; turn their reproach on their own heads, and give them as plunder to a land of captivity!
Do not cover their iniquity, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before You; for they have provoked You to anger before the builders.
So we built the wall, and the entire wall was joined together up to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.

Now it happened, when Sanballat, Tubiah, the Arabs, the Ammunites, and the Ashdudites heard that the walls of Yahushalam were being restored and the gaps were beginning to be closed, that they became very angry,
and all of them conspired together to come and attack Yahushalam and create confusion.
Nevertheless we made our prayer to our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and because of them we set a watch against them day and night.
Then Yahudah said, “The strength of the laborers is failing, and there is so much rubbish that we are not able to build the wall.”
And our adversaries said, “they will neither know nor see anything, till we come into their midst and kill them and cause the work to cease.”
So it was, when the Yahudym who dwelt near them came, that they told us ten times, “From whatever place you turn, they will be upon us.”
Therefore I positioned men behind the lower parts of the wall, at the openings; and I set the people according to their families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows.

And I looked, and arose and said to the nobles, to the leaders, and to the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who is great and awesome, and fight for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses.”
And it happened, when our enemies heard that it was known to us, and that 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had brought their plot to nothing, that all of us returned to the wall, everyone to his work.

So it was, from that time on, that half of my servants worked at construction, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows, and wore armor; and the leaders were behind all the house of Yahudah.
Those who built on the wall, and those who carried burdens, loaded themselves so that with one hand they worked at construction, and with the other held a weapon.
Every one of the builders had his sword girded at his side as he built. And the one who sounded the trumpet was beside me.
Then I said to the nobles, the rulers, and the rest of the people, “The work is great and extensive, and we are separated far from one another on the wall.
Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally to us there. Our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will fight for us.”
So we labored in the work, and half of the men held the spears from daybreak until the stars appeared.
At the same time I also said to the people, “Let each man and his servant stay at night in Yahushalam, that they may be our guard by night and a working party by day.”
So neither I, my brethren, my servants, nor the men of the guard who followed me took off our clothes, except that everyone took them off for washing.
About this time some of the men and their wives raised a cry of protest against their fellow Yahudym.
They were saying, “We have such large families. We need more food to survive.”
Others said, “We have mortgaged our fields, vineyards, and homes to get food during the famine.”
And others said, “We have had to borrow money on our fields and vineyards to pay our taxes.

We belong to the same family as those who are wealthy, and our children are just like theirs. Yet we must sell our children into slavery just to get enough money to live. We have already sold some of our daughters, and we are helpless to do anything about it, for our fields and vineyards are already mortgaged to others.”
When I heard their complaints, I was very angry.

After thinking it over, I spoke out against these nobles and officials. I told them, “You are hurting your own relatives by charging interest when they borrow money!” Then I called a public meeting to deal with the problem.

At the meeting I said to them, “We are doing all we can to redeem our Yahudym relatives who have had to sell themselves to pagan foreigners, but you are selling them back into slavery again. How often must we redeem them?” And they had nothing to say in their defense.
Then I pressed further, “What you are doing is not right! Should you not walk in the fear of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH in order to avoid being mocked by enemy nations?
I myself, as well as my brothers and my workers, have been lending the people money and grain, but now let us stop this business of charging interest.
You must restore their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and homes to them this very day. And repay the interest you charged when you lent them money, grain, new wine, and olive oil.”

They replied, “We will give back everything and demand nothing more from the people. We will do as you say.” Then I called the Kuhanym and made the nobles and officials swear to do what they had promised.

I shook out the folds of my robe and said, “If you fail to keep your promise, may our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH shake you like this from your homes and from your property!” The whole assembly responded, “so be it,” and they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And the people did as they had promised.

For the entire twelve years that I was governor of Yahudah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of the reign of King Artaxarxas, neither I nor my officials drew on our official food allowance.

The former governors, in contrast, had laid heavy burdens on the people, demanding a daily ration of food and wine, besides forty pieces of silver. Even their assistants took advantage of the people. But because I feared my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, I did not act that way.
I also devoted myself to working on the wall and refused to acquire any land. And I required all my servants to spend time working on the wall.
I asked for nothing, even though I regularly fed one hundred and fifty Yahudym officials at my table, besides all the visitors from other lands!

The provisions I paid for each day included one ox, six choice sheep or goats, and a large number of poultry. And every ten days we needed a large supply of all kinds of wine. Yet I refused to claim the governor’s food allowance because the people already carried a heavy burden.
Remember, O my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, all that I have done for these people, and barak me for it.
Sanballat, Tubiah, Gasham the Arab, and the rest of our enemies found out that I had finished rebuilding the wall and that no gaps remained, though we had not yet set up the doors in the gates.
So Sanballat and Gasham sent a message asking me to meet them at one of the villages in the plain of Unu. But I realized they were plotting to harm me,
so I replied by sending this message to them: “I am engaged in a great work, so I can not come. Why should I stop working to come and meet with you?”
Four times they sent the same message, and each time I gave the same reply.
The fifth time, Sanballat’s servant came with an open letter in his hand,

and this is what it said: “There is a rumor among the surrounding nations, and Gasham tells me it is true, that you and the Yahudym are planning to rebel and that is why you are building the wall. According to his reports, you plan to be their king.

He also reports that you have appointed Nabyms in Yahushalam to proclaim about you, ‘Look! There is a king in Yahudah!’ “You can be very sure that this report will get back to the king, so I suggest that you come and talk it over with me.”
I replied, “There is no truth in any part of your story. You are making up the whole thing.”
They were just trying to intimidate us, imagining that they could discourage us and stop the work. So I continued the work with even greater determination.

Later I went to visit Shamayahu son of Delayahu and grandson of Mahatabal, who was confined to his home, he said, “Let us meet together inside the Temple of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and bolt the doors shut. Your enemies are coming to kill you tonight.”
But I replied, “Should someone in my position run from danger? Should someone in my position enter the Temple to save his life? No, I will not do it!”
I realized that my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH had not spoken to him, but that he had uttered this prophecy against me because Tubiah and Sanballat had hired him.
They were hoping to intimidate me and make me sin. Then they would be able to accuse and discredit me.
Remember, O my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, all the evil things that Tubiah and Sanballat have done. And remember Nuadyahu the Nabym and all the Nabyms like her who have tried to intimidate me.
So the wall was completed on the twenty fifth day of Alul in fifty two days.
When our enemies and the surrounding nations heard about it, they were frightened and humiliated. They realized this work had been done with the help of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
During those fifty-two days, many letters went back and forth between Tubiah and the nobles of Yahudah.
For many in Yahudah had sworn allegiance to him because his father-in-law was Shacanyahu son of Arah, and his son Yahuhanan was married to the daughter of Mashullam son of Barakyahu.
They kept telling me about Tubiah’s good deeds, and then they told him everything I said. And Tubiah kept sending threatening letters to intimidate me.
Then it was, when the wall was built and I had hung the doors, when the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Lauym had been appointed,
that I gave the charge of Yahushalam to my brother Hanani, and Hananyahu the leader of the citadel, for he was a faithful man and he feared our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH more than many.

And I said to them, “Do not let the gates of Yahushalam be opened until the sun is hot; and while they stand guard, let them shut and bar the doors; and appoint guards from among the inhabitants of Yahushalam, one at his watch station and another in front of his own house.”
Now the city was large and spacious, but the people in it were few, and the houses were not rebuilt.

Then my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH put it into my heart to gather the nobles, the rulers, and the people, that they might be registered by genealogy. And I found a register of the genealogy of those who had come up in the first return, and found written in it:

These are the people of the province who came back from the captivity, of those who had been carried away, whom Nabuchadnazzar the king of Babylun had carried away, and who returned to Yahushalam and Yahudah, everyone to his city.
Those who came with Zarubbabal were Yashua, Nahamyahu, Azaryahu, Raamyah, Nahamani, Murdacai, Bilshan, Misparathu, Bigbai, Nahum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Yashar'AL:
the sons of Parush, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Shaphatyahu, three hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Arah, six hundred and fifty-two;
the sons of Pahath-Muab, of the sons of Yashua and Yuab, two thousand eight hundred and eighteen;
the sons of Alam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Zattu, eight hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;
the sons of Binnui, six hundred and forty-eight;
the sons of Babai, six hundred and twenty-eight;
the sons of Azgad, two thousand three hundred and twenty-two;
the sons of Adunikam, six hundred and sixty-seven;
the sons of Bigbai, two thousand and sixty-seven;
the sons of Adin, six hundred and fifty-five;
the sons of Atar of Hazakyahu, ninety-eight;
the sons of Hashum, three hundred and twenty-eight;
the sons of Bazai, three hundred and twenty-four;
the sons of Hariph, one hundred and twelve;
the sons of Gibaun, ninety-five;
the men of Bathlaham and Natuphah, one hundred and eighty-eight;
the men of Anathuth, one hundred and twenty-eight;
the men of Bath Azmabath, forty-two;
the men of Kiryath Yearim, Chaphirah, and Baaruth, seven hundred and forty-three;
the men of Ramah and Gaba, six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas, one hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bathal and Ai, one hundred and twenty-three;
the men of the other Nabu, fifty-two;
the sons of the other Alam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
the sons of Yarichu, three hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Lud, Hadid, and Unu, seven hundred and twenty-one;
the sons of Sanaah, three thousand nine hundred and thirty.
The Kuhanym: the sons of Yadayahu, of the house of Yashua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
the sons of Immar, one thousand and fifty-two;
the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
The Lauym: the sons of Yashua, of Kadmial, and of the sons of Hudabah, seventy-four.
The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and forty-eight.
The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Atar, the sons of Talmun, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shubai, one hundred and thirty-eight.
The Nethinim: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbauth,
the sons of Karus, the sons of Sia, the sons of Padun,
the sons of Labana, the sons of Hagaba, the sons of Salmai,
the sons of Hanan, the sons of Giddal, the sons of Gahar,
the sons of Raayah, the sons of Razin, the sons of Nakuda,
the sons of Gazzam, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Pasaah,
the sons of Basai, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Naphishasim,
the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
the sons of Bazlith, the sons of Mahida, the sons of Harsha,
the sons of Barkus, the sons of Sisara, the sons of Tamah,
the sons of Nazyahu, and the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of Shalumah’s servants: the sons of Sutai, the sons of Supharath, the sons of Parida,
the sons of Yaala, the sons of Darkun, the sons of Giddal,
the sons of Shaphatyahu, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pucharath of Zebaim, and the sons of Amon.
All the Nathinim, and the sons of Shalumah’s servants, were three hundred and ninety-two.
And these were the ones who came up from Tal Malah, Tal Harsha, Charub, Addun, and Immar, but they could not identify their father’s house nor their lineage, whether they were of Yashar'AL:
the sons of Dalayahu, the sons of Tubyahu, the sons of Nakuda, six hundred and forty-two;
and of the Kuhanym: the sons of Habayahu, the sons of Kuz, the sons of Barzillai, who took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gilaadite, and was called by their name.
These sought their listing among those who were registered by genealogy, but it was not found; therefore they were excluded from the Kuhanym as defiled.
And the governor said to them that they should not eat of the most Qadash things till a Kuhan could consult with the Urim and Thummim.
Altogether the whole assembly was forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
besides their male and female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had two hundred and forty-five men and women singers.
Their horses were seven hundred and thirty-six, their mules two hundred and forty-five,
their camels four hundred and thirty-five, and donkeys six thousand seven hundred and twenty.
And some of the heads of the fathers’ houses gave to the work. The governor gave to the treasury one thousand gold drachmas, fifty basins, and five hundred and thirty priestly garments.
Some of the heads of the fathers’ houses gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand gold drachmas, and two thousand two hundred silver minas.
And that which the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand gold drachmas, two thousand silver minas, and sixty-seven Kuhanym garments.

So the Kuhanym, the Lauym, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the Nathinim, and all Yashar'AL dwelt in their cities. When the seventh month came, the children of Yashar'AL were in their cities.

Now all the people gathered together as one man in the open square that was in front of the Water Gate; and they told Azrah the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Musha, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded Yashar'AL.
So Azrah the high Kuhan brought the Law before the assembly of men and women and all who could hear with understanding on the first day of the seventh month.

Then he read from it in the open square that was in front of the Water Gate from morning until midday, before the men and women and those who could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive to the Book of the Law.

So Azrah the scribe stood on a platform of wood which they had made for the purpose; and beside him, at his right hand, stood Mattithyahu, Shama, Anayahu, Uriyahu, Hilkyahu, and Maasayahu; and at his left hand Padayahu, Mishaal, Malchiyahu, Hashum, Hashbadana, Zacharyahu, and Mashullam.
And Azrah opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he was standing above all the people; and when he opened it, all the people stood up.

And Azrah Baraked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the great 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Then all the people answered, “Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!” while lifting up their hands. And they bowed their heads and worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with their faces to the ground.

Also Yashua, Bani, Sharabyahu, Yamin, Akkub, Shabbathai, Hudiyahu, Maasaiyahu, Kalita, Azaryahu, Yuzabad, Hanan, Palayahu, and the Lauy, helped the people to understand the Law; and the people stood in their place.
So they read distinctly from the book, in the Law of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; and they gave the sense, and helped them to understand the reading.

And Nahamyahu, who was the governor, Azrah the chief Kuhan and scribe, and the Lauym who taught the people said to all the people, “This day is Qadash to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; do not mourn nor weep.” For all the people wept, when they heard the Dabar of the Law.

Then Ázrah said to them, “Go your way, eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to those for whom nothing is prepared; for this day is Qadash to our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. Do not be sorrowful, for the joy of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is your strength.”
So the Lauym quieted all the people, saying, “Be still, for the day is Qadash; do not be grieved.”
And all the people went their way to eat and drink, to send portions and rejoice greatly, because they understood the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that was declared to them.
Now on the second day the heads of the fathers’ houses of all the people, with the Kuhanym and Lauym, were gathered to meet Azrah the scribe, in order to understand the Dabar of the Law.
And they found written in the Law, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had commanded by Musha, that the children of Yashar'AL should dwell in booths during the feast of the seventh month,

and that they should announce and proclaim in all their cities and in Yahushalam, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and bring olive branches, branches of oil trees, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written.”

Then the people went out and brought them and made themselves booths, each one on the roof of his house, or in their courtyards or the courts of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and in the open square of the Water Gate and in the open square of the Gate of Aphraim.

So the whole assembly of those who had returned from the captivity made booths and sat under the booths; for since the days of Yahusha Ba'Nun (the son of Nun) until that day the children of Yashar'AL had not done so. And there was very great gladness.

Also day by day, from the first day until the last day, Ázrah read from the Book of the Law of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. And they kept the feast seven days; and on the eighth day there was a sacred assembly, according to the prescribed manner.
Now on the twenty-fourth day of same month the children of Yashar'AL were assembled with fasting, in sackcloth, and with dust on their heads.
Then those of Yasharalym lineage separated themselves from all foreigners; and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

And they stood up in their place and read from the Book of the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for one-fourth of the day; and for another fourth they confessed and worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Then Yashua, Bani, Kadmial, Shabanyahu, Bunni, Sharabyahu, Bani, and Chanani stood on the stairs of the Lauym and cried out with a loud voice to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

And the Lauym, Yashua, Kadmial, Bani, Hashabnyahu, Sharabyahu, Hudiyahu, Shabanyahu, and Pathahyahu, said: Stand up and barak 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH Forever and ever! Baraked be Your Esteemed Name, Which is exalted above all Barakah and Yadah!

You are our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH alone; You have made Shamaym, The Shamaym of Shamaym, with all their host, The Arath and everything in it, The Yam (seas) and all that is in them, And You preserve them all. The host of Shamaym worships You.
“You are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, Who chose Abram, And brought him out of Ur of the Chaldaans, And gave him the name Abraham;

You found his heart faithful before You, And made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanites, The Hittites, the Amurites,The Parizzites, the Yabusites, And the Girgashites, To give it to his descendants. You have performed Your words, For You are righteous.
“You saw the affliction of our fathers in Mitzraym, And heard their cry by the Red Sea.

You showed signs and wonders against Phar'uh, Against all his servants, And against all the people of his land. For You knew that they acted proudly against them. So You made a Name for Yourself, as it is this day.
And You divided the sea before them, So that they went through the midst of the sea on the dry land; And their persecutors You threw into the deep, As a stone into the mighty waters.
Moreover You led them by day with a cloudy pillar, And by night with a pillar of fire, To give them light on the road Which they should travel.
“You came down also on Mount Sinai, And spoke with them from Shamaym, And gave them just ordinances and true laws, Good statutes and commandments.
You made known to them Your Qadash Shabbat, And commanded them precepts, statutes and laws, By the hand of Musha Your servant.
You gave them bread from Shamaym for their hunger, And brought them water out of the rock for their thirst, and told them to go in to possess the land Which You had sworn to give them.
“But they and our fathers acted proudly, Hardened their necks, and did not heed Your commandments.

They refused to obey, and they were not mindful of Your wonders that You did among them. But they hardened their necks, and in their rebellion they appointed a leader to return to their bondage. But You are our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, Ready to pardon, kind and merciful, Slow to anger, abundant in kindness, And did not forsake them.
“Even when they made a molded calf for themselves, and said, ‘This is your idol That brought you up out of Mitzraym, ’and worked great provocations,

Yet in Your manifold mercies you did not forsake them in the wilderness. The pillar of the cloud did not depart from them by day, To lead them on the road; Nor the pillar of fire by night, To show them light, And the way they should go.
You also gave Your good RUACH to instruct them, And did not withhold Your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst.
Forty years You sustained them in the wilderness; They lacked nothing; Their clothes did not wear out And their feet did not swell.
“Moreover you gave them kingdoms and nations, and divided them into districts. So they took possession of the land of Sihun, the land of the king of Hashbun, and the land of Ug king of Bashan.
You also multiplied their children as the stars of Shamaym, and brought them into the land Which You had told their fathers to go in and possess.

So the people went in And possessed the land; You subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, The Canaanites, And gave them into their hands, With their Kings and the people of the land, That they might do with them as they wished.

And they took strong cities and a rich land, And possessed houses full of all goods, Cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. So they ate and were filled and grew fat, and delighted themselves in Your great goodness.

“Nevertheless they were disobedient and rebelled against You, Cast Your law behind their backs And killed Your Nabyms, who testified against them To turn them to Yourself and they worked great provocations.

Therefore You delivered them into the hand of their enemies, Who oppressed them; And in the time of their trouble, When they cried to You, »You heard from Shamaym; and according to Your abundant mercies You gave them deliverers who saved them From the hand of their enemies.

“But after they had rest, They again did evil before You. Therefore You left them in the hand of their enemies, So that they had dominion over them; Yet when they returned and cried out to You, You heard from Shamaym; And many times You delivered them according to Your mercies,

And testified against them, That You might bring them back to Your law. Yet they acted proudly, And did not heed Your commandments, But sinned against Your judgments, Which if a man does, he shall live by them. And they shrugged their shoulders, Stiffened their necks, And would not hear.
Yet for many years You had patience with them, And testified against them by Your RUACH in Your Nabyms. Yet they would not listen; Therefore You gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
Nevertheless in Your great mercy you did not utterly consume them nor forsake them; For You are their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, kind and merciful.

“Now therefore, our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, The great, the mighty, and awesome 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, Who keeps covenant and mercy: Do not let all the trouble seem small before You that has come upon us, Our kings and our princes, Our Kuhanym and our Nabyms, Our fathers and on all Your people, From the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.
However You are just in all that has befallen us; For You have dealt faithfully, But we have done wickedly.
Neither our kings nor our princes, our priests nor our fathers, Have kept Your law, Nor heeded Your commandments and Your testimonies, with which You testified against them.
For they have not served You in their kingdom, Or in the many good things that You gave them, Or in the large and rich land which You set before them; Nor did they turn from their wicked works.
“Here we are, servants today! and the land that You gave to our fathers, to eat its fruit and its bounty, Here we are, servants in it!
And it yields much increase to the kings you have set over us, because of our sins; also they have dominion over our bodies and our cattle at their pleasure; and we are in great distress.
“And because of all this, we make a sure covenant and write it; Our leaders, our Lauym, and our Kuhanym seal it.”
Now those who placed their seal on the document were: Nahamyahu the governor, the son of Hachalyahu, and Zadakyahu,
Sarayahu, Azaryahu, Yaramyahu,
Pashhur, Amaryahu, Malchiyahu,
Hattush, Shabanyahu, Malluch,
Harim, Maramuth, Ubadyahu,
DanyAL, Ginnathun, Baruch,
Mashullam, Abiyah, Miyamin,
Maazyah, Bilgai, and Shamayahu. These were the Kuhanym.
The Lauym: Yashua the son of Azanyahu, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, and Kadmial.
Their brethren: Shabanyahu, Hudiyahu, Kelita, Pelayahu, Hanan,
Micha, Rahub, Hashabyahu,
Zaccur, Sharabyahu, Shabanyahu,
Hudiyahu, Bani, and Beninu.
The leaders of the people: Parush, Pahath-Moab, Alam, Zattu, Bani,
Bunni, Azgad, Babai,
Aduniyahu, Bigbai, Adin,
Atar, Hazakyahu, Azzur,
Hudiyahu, Hashum, Bazai,
Hariph, Anathuth, Nabai,
Magpiash, Mashullam, Hazir,
Mashazabal, Zaduk, Yaddua,
Palatyahu, Hanan, Anayahu,
Husha, Hananyahu, Hasshub,
Halluhash, Pilha, Shubak,
Rahum, Hashabnah, Maasayahu,
Ahiyahu, Hanan, Anan,
Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

Now the rest of the people, the Kuhanym, the Lauym, the gatekeepers, the singers, the Nathinim, and all those who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, everyone who had knowledge and understanding

These joined with their brethren, their nobles, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, which was given by Musha the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and to observe and do all the commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and His ordinances and His statutes:
We would not give our daughters as wives to the peoples of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons;

if the peoples of the land brought wares or any grain to sell on the Shabbat day, we would not buy it from them on the Shabbat, or on a Qadash day; and we would forego the seventh year’s produce and the exacting of every debt.
Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to exact from ourselves yearly one-third of a shekel for the service of the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH:

for the showbread, for the regular grain offering, for the regular burnt offering of the Shabbats, the New Moons, and the set feasts; for the Qadash things, for the sin offerings to make atonement for Yashar'AL, and all the work of the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

We cast lots among the Kuhanym, the Lauym, and the people, for bringing the wood offering into the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, according to our fathers’ houses, at the appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH as it is written in the Law.
And we made ordinances to bring the firstfruits of our ground and the firstfruits of all fruit of all trees, year by year, to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH;

to bring the firstborn of our sons and our cattle, as it is written in the Law, and the firstborn of our herds and our flocks, to the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, to the Kuhanym who minister in the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH;

to bring the firstfruits of our dough, our offerings, the fruit from all kinds of trees, the new wine and oil, to the Kuhanym, to the storerooms of the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and to bring the tithes of our land to the Lauym, for the Lauym should receive the tithes in all our farming communities.

And the Kuhan, the descendant of Aarun, shall be with the Lauym when the Lauym receive tithes; and the Lauym shall bring up a tenth of the tithes to the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, to the rooms of the storehouse.

For the children of Yashar'AL and the children of Lauy shall bring the offering of the grain, of the new wine and the oil, to the storerooms where the articles of the sanctuary are, where the Kuhanym who minister and the gatekeepers and the singers are; and we will not neglect the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Now the leaders of the people dwelt at Yahushalam; the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to dwell in Yahushalam, the qadash city, and nine-tenths were to dwell in other cities.
And the people Baraked all the men who willingly offered themselves to dwell at Yahushalam.

These are the heads of the province who dwelt in Yahushalam. (But in the cities of Yahudah everyone dwelt in his own possession in their cities, Yasharalym, Kuhanym, Lauym, Nathinim, and descendants of Shalumah’s servants.)

Also in Yahushalam dwelt some of the children of Yahudah and of the children of Banyamin. The children of Yahudah: Athayahu the son of Uzzyahu, the son of Zacharyahu, the son of Amaryahu, the son of Shaphatyahu, the son of Mahalalal, of the children of Paraz;
and Maasayahu the son of Baruch, the son of Cul-Huzah, the son of Hazayahu, the son of Adayahu, the son of Yuiarib, the son of Zacharyahu, the son of Shiluni.
All the sons of Paraz who dwelt at Yahushalam were four hundred and sixty-eight valiant men.
And these are the sons of Banyamin: Sallu the son of Mashullam, the son of Yuad, the son of Padayahu, the son of Kulayahu, the son of Maasayahu, the son of Ithial, the son of Yashayahu;
and after him Gabbai and Sallai, nine hundred and twenty-eight.
Yual the son of Zichri was their overseer, and Yahudah the son of Sanuah was second over the city.
Of the Kuhanym: Yadayahu the son of Yuiarib, and Yachin;
Sarayahu the son of Hilkyahu, the son of Mashullam, the son of Zaduk, the son of Maraiuth, the son of Ahitub, was the leader of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Their brethren who did the work of the house were eight hundred and twenty-two; and Adayahu the son of Yaruham, the son of Palayahu, the son of Amzi, the son of Zacharyahu, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchiyahu,
and his brethren, heads of the fathers’ houses, were two hundred and forty-two; and Amashai the son of Azaral, the son of Ahzai, the son of Mashillamuth, the son of Immar,
and their brethren, mighty men of valor, were one hundred and twenty-eight. Their overseer was Zabdial the son of one of the great men.
Also of the Lauym: Shamayahu the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabyahu, the son of Bunni;
Shabbathai and Yuzabad, of the heads of the Lauym, had the oversight of the business outside of the house of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH;

Mattanyahu the son of Micha, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, the leader who began the thanksgiving with prayer; Bakbukyahu, the second among his brethren; and Abda the son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Yaduthun.
All the Lauym in the qadash city were two hundred and eighty-four.
Moreover the gatekeepers, Akkub, Talmun, and their brethren who kept the gates, were one hundred and seventy-two.
And the rest of Yashar'AL, of the Kuhanym and Lauym, were in all the cities of Yahudah, everyone in his inheritance.
But the Naahinim dwelt in Uphal. And Ziha and Gishpa were over the Nathinim.

Also the overseer of the Lauym at Yahushalam was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabyahu, the son of Mattanyahu, the son of Micha, of the sons of Asaph, the singers in charge of the service of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
For it was the king’s command concerning them that a certain portion should be for the singers, a quota day by day.
Pathahyahu the son of Mashazabal, of the children of Zarah the son of Yahudah, was the king’s deputy in all matters concerning the people.
And as for the villages with their fields, some of the children of Yahudah dwelt in Kiryath Arba and its villages, Dibun and its villages, Yakabzaal and its villages;
in Yashua, Muladah, Bath Palat,
Hazar Shual, and Baarshaba and its villages;
in Ziklag and Macunah and its villages;
in An Rimmun, Zurah, Yarmuth,
Zanuah, Adullam, and their villages; in Lachish and its fields; in Azakah and its villages. They dwelt from Baarshaba to the Valley of Hinnum.
Also the children of Banyamin from Gaba dwelt in Michmash, Aiya, and Bathal, and their villages;
in Anathuth, Nub, Ananyahu;
in Hazur, Ramah, Gittaim;
in Hadid, Zabum, Naballat;
in Lud, Unu, and the Valley of Craftsmen.
Some of the Yahudah divisions of Lauym were in Banyamin.
Now these are the Kuhanym and the Lauym who came up with Zarubbabal the son of Shaaltyal, and Yashua: Sarayahu, Yaramyahu, Azrah,
Amaryahu, Malluch, Hattush,
Shachanyahu, Rahum, Maramuth,
Iddu, Ginnathui, Abiyahu,
Miyamin, Maadyahu, Bilgah,
Shamayahu, Yuiarib, Yadayahu,
Sallu, Amuk, Hilkyahu, and Yadayahu. These were the heads of the Kuhanym and their brethren in the days of Yashua.
Moreover the Lauym were Yashua, Binnui, Kadmial, Sharabyah, Yahudah, and Mattanyahu who led the thanksgiving Tahalym (psalms), he and his brethren.
Also Bakbukyahu and Unni, their brethren, stood across from them in their duties.
Yashua begot Yuiakim, Yuiakim begot Aliashib, Aliashib begot Yuiada,
Yuiada begot Yunathan, and Yunathan begot Yaddua.
Now in the days of Yuiakim, the Kuhanym, the heads of the fathers’ houses were: of Sarayahu, Marayahu; of Yaramyahu, Hananyahu;
of Azrah, Mashullam; of Amaryahu, Yahuhanan;
of Malichu, Yunathan; of Shabanyahu, Ya'asaf;
of Harim, Adna; of Maraiuth, Halkai;
of Iddu, Zacharyahu; of Ginnathun, Mashullam;
of Abiyahu, Zichri; the son of Minyamin; of Muadyahu, Piltai;
of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shamayahu, Yahunathan;
of Yuiarib, Mattanai; of Yadayahu, Uzzi;
of Sallai, Kallai; of Amuk, Abar;
of Hilkyahu, Hashabyahu; and of Yadayahu, Nethanel.
During the reign of Darius the Parsian, a record was also kept of the Lauym and Kuhanym who had been heads of their fathers’ houses in the days of Aliashib, Yuiada, Yuhanan, and Yaddua.
The sons of Lauy, the heads of the fathers’ houses until the days of Yuhanan the son of Aliashib, were written in the book of the chronicles.

And the heads of the Lauym were Hashabyahu, Sharabyahu, and Yashua the son of Kadmial, with their brothers across from them, to praise and give thanks, group alternating with group, according to the command of Daud the servant of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Mattanyahu, Bakbukyahu, Ubadyahu, Meshullam, Talmun, and Akkub were gatekeepers keeping the watch at the storerooms of the gates.
These lived in the days of Yuiakim the son of Yashua, the son of Yuzadak, and in the days of Nahamyahu the governor, and of Azrah the Kuhan, the scribe.

Now at the dedication of the wall of Yahushalam they sought out the Lauym in all their places, to bring them to Yahushalam to celebrate the dedication with gladness, both with thanksgivings and singing, with cymbals and stringed instruments and harps.
And the sons of the singers gathered together from the countryside around Yahushalam, from the villages of the Natuphathites,
from the house of Gilgal, and from the fields of Gaba and Azmabath; for the singers had built themselves villages all around Yahushalam.
Then the Kuhanym and Lauym purified themselves, and purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
So I brought the leaders of Yahudah up on the wall, and appointed two large thanksgiving choirs. One went to the right hand on the wall toward the Refuse Gate.
After them went Hushayahu and half of the leaders of Yahudah,
and Azaryahu, Azrah, Mashullam,
Yahudah, Banyamin, Shamayahu, Yaramyahu,
and some of the Kuhanym’ sons with trumpets, Zacharyahu the son of Yunathan, the son of Shamayahu, the son of Mattanyahu, the son of Michayahu, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,
and his brethren, Shamayahu, Azaral, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nathanal, Yahudah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of Daud the servant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And Azrah the scribe went before them.
By the Fountain Gate, in front of them, they went up the stairs of the City of Daud, on the stairway of the wall, beyond the house of Daud, as far as the Water Gate eastward.
The other thanksgiving choir went the opposite way, and I was behind them with half of the people on the wall, going past the Tower of the Ovens as far as the Broad Wall,
and above the Gate of Aphraim, above the Old Gate, above the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananal, the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate; and they stopped by the Gate of the Prison.
So the two thanksgiving choirs stood in the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, likewise I and the half of the rulers with me;
and the Kuhanym, Aliakim, Maasayahu, Minyamin, Michayahu, Aliuanai, Zacharyahu, and Hananyahu, with trumpets;
also Maasayahu, Shemayahu, Alaazar, Uzzi, Yahuhanan, Malchiyah, Alam, and Azar. The singers sang loudly with Yazrahyah the director.

Also that day they offered great sacrifices, and rejoiced, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had made them rejoice with great joy; the women and the children also rejoiced, so that the joy of Yahushalam was heard afar off.

And at the same time some were appointed over the rooms of the storehouse for the offerings, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the cities the portions specified by the Law for the Kuhanym and Lauym; for Yahudah rejoiced over the Kuhanym and Lauym who ministered.
Both the singers and the gatekeepers kept the charge of their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and the charge of the purification, according to the command of Daud and Shalumah his son.
For in the days of Daud and Asaph of old there were chiefs of the singers, and songs of Yadah (praise) and Tudah (thanksgiving) to our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

In the days of Zarubbabal and in the days of Nahamyahu all Yashar'AL gave the portions for the singers and the gatekeepers, a portion for each day. They also consecrated qadash things for the Lauym, and the Lauym consecrated them for the children of Aarun.
On that day they read from the Book of Musha in the hearing of the people, and in it was found written that no Ammunite or Muabite should ever come into the assembly of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH,
because they had not greet the children of Yashar'AL with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them. However, our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH turned the curse into a Barakah.
So it was, when they had heard the Law, that they separated all the mixed multitude from Yashar'AL.
Now before this, Aliashib the Kuhan, having authority over the storerooms of the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, was allied with Tubiah.

And he had prepared for him a large room, where previously they had stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the articles, the tithes of grain, the new wine and oil, which were commanded to be given to the Lauym and singers and gatekeepers, and the offerings for the Kuhanym.
But during all this I was not in Yahushalam, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxarxas king of Babylun I had returned to the king. Then after certain days I obtained leave from the king,
and I came to Yahushalam and discovered the evil that Aliashib had done for Tubiah, in preparing a room for him in the courts of the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
And it grieved me bitterly; therefore I threw all the household goods of Tubiah out of the room.
Then I commanded them to cleanse the rooms; and I brought back into them the articles of the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
I also realized that the portions for the Lauym had not been given them; for each of the Lauym and the singers who did the work had gone back to his field.
So I contended with the rulers, and said, “Why is the house of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH forsaken?” And I gathered them together and set them in their place.
Then all Yahudah brought the tithe of the grain and the new wine and the oil to the storehouse.

And I appointed as treasurers over the storehouse Shalamyahu the Kuhan and Zaduk the scribe, and of the Lauym, Padayahu; and next to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattanyahu; for they were considered faithful, and their task was to distribute to their brethren.
Remember me, O my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, concerning this, and do not wipe out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and for its services!

In those days I saw people in Yahudah treading winepresses on the Shabbat, and bringing in sheaves, and loading donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of burdens, which they brought into Yahushalam on the Shabbat day. And I warned them about the day on which they were selling provisions.
Men of Tyra dwelt there also, who brought in fish and all kinds of goods, and sold them on the Shabbat to the children of Yahudah, and in Yahushalam.
Then I contended with the nobles of Yahudah, and said to them, “What evil thing is this that you do, by which you profane the Shabbat day?
Did not your fathers do thus, and did not our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Yet you bring added wrath on Yashar'AL by profaning the Shabbat.”

So it was, at the gates of Yahushalam, as it began to be dark before the Shabbat, that I commanded the gates to be shut, and charged that they must not be opened till after the Shabbat. Then I posted some of my servants at the gates, so that no burdens would be brought in on the Shabbat day.
Now the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares lodged outside Yahushalam once or twice.
Then I warned them, and said to them, “Why do you spend the night around the wall? If you do so again, I will lay hands on you!” From that time on they came no more on the Shabbat.

And I commanded the Lauym that they should cleanse themselves, and that they should go and guard the gates, to sanctify the Shabbat day. Remember me, O my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, concerning this also, and spare me according to the greatness of Your mercy!
In those days I also saw Yahudym who had married women of Ashdud, Ammun, and Muab.
And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdud, and could not speak the language of Yahudah, but spoke according to the language of one or the other people.

So I contended with them and cursed them, struck some of them and pulled out their hair, and made them swear by our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, saying, “You shall not give your daughters as wives to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons or yourselves.

Did Shalumah king of Yashar'AL not sin by these things? Yet among many nations there was no king like him, who was beloved of his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made him king over all Yashar'AL. Nevertheless pagan women caused even him to sin.
Should we then hear of your doing all this great evil, transgressing against our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH by marrying pagan women?”
And one of the sons of Yuiada, the son of Aliashib the high Kuhan, was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Hurunite; therefore I drove him from me.
Remember them, O my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, because they have defiled the Kuhanym and the covenant of the Kuhanym and the Lauym.
Thus I cleansed them of everything pagan. I also assigned duties to the Kuhanym and the Lauym, each to his service,
and to bringing the wood offering and the firstfruits at appointed times. Remember me, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH remember me for good!

books.name: Esther
chapters: This is a record of what happened during the reign of Ahasuarus, the Ahasuarus who ruled over one hundred and twenty seven provinces from India to Cush.
At that time King Ahasuarus was ruling from Susa the capital.
In the third year of his reign, he gave a banquet for all his officials and ministers, and the military leaders of Parsia and Madia, the nobles, and the provincial officials were present.
He displayed the enormous wealth of his kingdom, along with its splendid beauty and greatness for many days, for 180 days in all.

When those days were over, the king held a seven-day banquet in the courtyard of the garden of his palace for all the people who were present in Susa the capital, from the greatest to the least important.

There were curtains of white and blue linen tied with cords of fine linen and purple material to silver rings on marble columns. There were couches of gold and silver on a mosaic pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl and other precious stones.
Drinks were served in gold vessels of various kinds, and there was plenty of royal wine because the king was generous.
According to the king’s decree the drinking was not compulsory because the king instructed every steward in his house to serve each individual what he desired.
Queen Vashti also held a banquet in the royal palace of King Ahasuarus for the women.
A week later, when the king was under the influence of all that wine, he ordered Mahuman, Biztha, Harbuna, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zathar, and Carcas, the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuarus,
to bring Queen Vashti to the king, wearing the royal crown to display her beauty to the people and the officials, since she was lovely to look at.
Queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s order that was brought by the eunuchs. Then the king flew into a rage.
The king spoke to the wise men who understood the times, for it was the king’s custom to consult all those who understood law and justice.

His closest advisors were: Carshana, Shathar, Admatha, Tarshish, Maras, Marsana, and Mamucan, the seven officials of Parsia and Madia who had direct access to the king and who held the highest rank in the kingdom.
The king inquired, “According to law, what should be done to Queen Vashti because she did not obey the order of King Ahasuarus that was delivered by the eunuchs?”

Then Mamucan replied in the presence of the king and his officials, “It is not the king alone whom Vashti has wronged, but rather all of the officials and all of the people who are in the provinces of King Ahasuarus.

When the report about the queen goes out to all the women, it will cause them to despise their husbands. They will say, ‘King Ahasuerus ordered Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she wouldn’t come.’

This very day the wives of the officials of Parsia and Madia who hear the report about the queen will speak in the same way to all the officials of the king, and there will be more than enough contempt and anger.

If it seems good to the king, let a royal decree go out from him and let it be written in the laws of Parsia and Madia, which cannot be repealed, that Vashti is never again to enter the presence of King Ahasuarus. Let the king give her royal position to another woman who is better than she.
When the edict that the king issues is heard throughout his kingdom, for it is vast then all the women will give honor to their husbands, from the greatest to the least important.”
This seemed like a good idea to the king and his officials, so the king did what Mamucan suggested.

He sent letters to all the provinces of the king, written in the script of that province, and to each people in their own language, ordering that every man should be the master in his house and speak the language of his own people.
After these things, when the wrath of King Ahasuarus subsided, he remembered Vashti, what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
Then the king’s servants who attended him said: “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king;

and let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather all the beautiful young virgins to Shushan the citadel, into the women’s quarters, under the custody of Hagai the king’s eunuch, custodian of the women. And let beauty preparations be given them.
Then let the young woman who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti.” This thing pleased the king, and he did so.
In Shushan the citadel there was a certain Yahudym whose name was Murdacayahu the son of Yair, the son of Shimai, the son of Kish, a Banyamin.
Kish had been carried away from Yahushalam with the captives who had been captured with Yacunyahu king of Yahudah, whom Nabuchadnazzar the king of Babylun had carried away.

And Murdacayahu had brought up Hadassah, that is, Austah, his uncle’s daughter, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was lovely and beautiful. When her father and mother died, Murdacayahu took her as his own daughter.

So it was, when the king’s command and decree were heard, and when many young women were gathered at Shushan the citadel, under the custody of Hagai, that Austah also was taken to the king’s palace, into the care of Hagai the custodian of the women.

Now the young woman pleased him, and she obtained his favor; so he readily gave beauty preparations to her, besides her allowance. Then seven choice maidservants were provided for her from the king’s palace, and he moved her and her maidservants to the best place in the house of the women.
Austah had not revealed her people or family, for Murdacayahu had charged her not to reveal it.
And every day Murdacayahu paced in front of the court of the women’s quarters, to learn of Austah’s welfare and what was happening to her.

Each young woman’s turn came to go in to King Ahasuarus after she had completed twelve months’ preparation, according to the regulations for the women, for thus were the days of their preparation apportioned: six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with perfumes and preparations for beautifying women.
Thus prepared, each young woman went to the king, and she was given whatever she desired to take with her from the women’s quarters to the king’s palace.

In the evening she went, and in the morning she returned to the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch who kept the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and called for her by name.

Now when the turn came for Austah the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Murdacayahu, who had taken her as his daughter, to go in to the king, she requested nothing but what Hagai the king’s eunuch, the custodian of the women, advised. And Austah obtained favor in the sight of all who saw her.
So Austah was taken to King Ahasuarus, into his royal palace, in the tenth month, which is the month of Tabath, in the seventh year of his reign.
The king loved Austah more than all the other women, and she obtained favor in his sight more than all the virgins; so he set the royal crown upon her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Then the king made a great feast, the Feast of Austah, for all his officials and servants; and he proclaimed a freeday in the provinces and gave gifts according to the generosity of a king.
When virgins were gathered together a second time, Murdacayahu sat within the king’s gate.
Now Austah had not revealed her family and her people, just as Murdacayahu had charged her, for Austah obeyed the command of Murdacayahu as when she was brought up by him.
In those days, while Murdacayahu sat within the king’s gate, two of the king’s eunuchs, Bigthan and Tarash, doorkeepers, became furious and sought to lay hands on King Ahasuarus.
So the matter became known to Murdacayahu, who told Queen Austah, and Austah informed the king in Murdacayahu’s name.
And when an inquiry was made into the matter, it was confirmed, and both were hanged on a gallows; and it was written in the book of the chronicles in the presence of the king.
After these things King Ahasuarus promoted Haman, the son of Hammadatha the Agagite, and advanced him and set his seat above all the princes who were with him.
And all the king’s servants who were within the king’s gate bowed and paid homage to Haman, for so the king had commanded concerning him. But Murdacayahu would not bow or pay homage.
Then the king’s servants who were within the king’s gate said to Murdacayahu, “Why do you transgress the king’s command?”

Now it happened, when they spoke to him daily and he would not listen to them, that they told it to Haman, to see whether Murdacaiyahu’s words would stand; for Murdacayahu had told them that he is Yahudym.
When Haman saw that Murdacayahu did not bow or pay him homage, Haman was filled with wrath.

But he disdained to lay hands on Murdacayahu alone, for they had told him of the people of Murdacayahu. Instead, Haman sought to destroy all the Yahudym who were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuarus, the people of Murdacayahu.
In the first month, of the twelfth year of King Ahasuarus, they cast Pur (that is, the lot), before Haman to determine the day and the month, until it fell on the twelfth month.

Then Haman said to King Ahasuarus, “There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of your kingdom; their laws are different from all other people’s, and they do not keep the king’s laws. Therefore it is not fitting for the king to let them remain.
If it pleases the king, let a decree be written that they be destroyed, and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who do the work, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.”
So the king took his signet ring from his hand and gave it to Haman, the son of Hammadatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Yahudym.
And the king said to Haman, “The money and the people are given to you, to do with them as seems good to you.”

Then the king’s scribes were called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and a decree was written according to all that Haman commanded to the king’s satraps, to the governors who were over each province, to the officials of all people, to every province according to its script, and to every people in their language. In the name of King Ahasuerus it was written, and sealed with the king’s signet ring.

And the letters were sent by couriers into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate all the Yahudym, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, and to plunder their possessions.
A copy of the document was to be issued as law in every province, being published for all people, that they should be ready for that day.
The couriers went out, hastened by the king’s command; and the decree was proclaimed in Shushan the citadel. So the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Shushan was perplexed.
When Murdacayahu learned all that had happened, he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, he cried out with a loud and bitter cry.
He went as far as the front of the king’s gate, for no one might enter the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.
And in every province where the king’s command and decree arrived, there was great mourning among the Yahudym, with fasting, weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
So Austah’s maids and eunuchs came and told her, and the queen was deeply distressed. Then she sent garments to clothe Murdacayahu and take his sackcloth away from him, but he would not accept them.
Then Austah called Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend her, and she gave him a command concerning Murdacayahu, to learn what and why this was.
So Hathach went out to Murdacayahu in the city square that was in front of the king’s gate.
And Murdacayahu told him all that had happened to him, and the sum of money that Haman had promised to pay into the king’s treasuries to destroy the Yahudym.

He also gave him a copy of the written decree for their destruction, which was given at Shushan, that he might show it to Austah and explain it to her, and that he might command her to go in to the king to make supplication to him and plead before him for her people.
So Hathach returned and told Austah the words of Murdacayahu.
Then Austar spoke to Hathach, and gave him a command for Murdacayahu:

“All the king’s servants and the people of the king’s provinces know that any man or woman who goes into the inner court to the king, who has not been called, he has but one law: put all to death, except the one to whom the king holds out the golden scepter, that he may live. Yet I myself have not been called to go in to the king these thirty days.”
So they told Murdacayahu Austah’s words.
And Murdacayahu told them to answer Austah: “Do not think in your heart that you will escape in the king’s palace any more than all the other Yahudym.

For if you remain completely silent at this time, relief and deliverance will arise for the Yahudym from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Yet who knows whether you have come to this kingdom for such a time as this?”
Then Austah told them to reply to Murdacayahu:

“Go, gather all the Yahudym who are present in Shushan, and fast for me; neither eat nor drink for three days, night or day. My maids and I will fast likewise. And so I will go to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish!”
So Murdacayahu went his way and did according to all that Austah commanded him.

Now it happened on the third day that Austah put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the king’s palace, across from the king’s house, while the king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, facing the entrance of the house.

So it was, when the king saw Queen Austah standing in the court, that she found favor in his sight, and the king held out to Austah the golden scepter that was in his hand. Then Austah went near and touched the top of the scepter.
And the king said to her, “What do you wish, Queen Austah? What is your request? It shall be given to you, up to half the kingdom!”
So Austah answered, “If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him.”
Then the king said, “Bring Haman quickly, that he may do as Austah has said.” So the king and Haman went to the banquet that Austah had prepared.
At the banquet of wine the king said to Austah, “What is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your request, up to half the kingdom? It shall be done!”
Then Austah answered and said, “My petition and request is this:

If I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request, then let the king and Haman come to the banquet which I will prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do as the king has said.”

So Haman went out that day joyful and with a glad heart; but when Haman saw Murdacayahu in the king’s gate, and that he did not stand or tremble before him, he was filled with indignation against Murdacayahu.
Nevertheless Haman restrained himself and went home, and he sent and called for his friends and his wife Zarash.
Then Haman told them of his great riches, the multitude of his children, everything in which the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the officials and servants of the king.
Moreover Haman said, “Besides, Queen Austah invited no one but me to come in with the king to the banquet that she prepared; and tomorrow I am again invited by her, along with the king.
Yet all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Murdacayahu the Yahudym sitting at the king’s gate.”

Then his wife Zarash and all his friends said to him, “Let a gallows be made, fifty cubits high, and in the morning suggest to the king that Murdacayahu be hanged on it; then go merrily with the king to the banquet.” And the thing pleased Haman; so he had the gallows made.
That night the king could not sleep. So one was commanded to bring the book of the records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.
And it was found written that Murdacayahu had told of Bigthana and Tarash, two of the king’s eunuchs, the doorkeepers who had sought to lay hands on King Ahasuarus.
Then the king said, “What honor or dignity has been bestowed on Murdacayahu for this?”
So the king said, “Who is in the court?” Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the king’s palace to suggest that the king hang Murdacayahu on the gallows that he had prepared for him.
The king’s servants said to him, “Haman is there, standing in the court. And the king said, “Let him come in.”
So Haman came in, and the king asked him, “What shall be done for the man whom the king delights to honor? Now Haman thought in his heart, “Whom would the king delight to honor more than me?”
And Haman answered the king, “For the man whom the king delights to honor,
let a royal robe be brought which the king has worn, and a horse on which the king has ridden, which has a royal crest placed on its head.

Then let this robe and horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that he may array the man whom the king delights to honor. Then parade him on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him: ‘Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!’ ”

Then the king said to Haman, “Hurry, take the robe and the horse, as you have suggested, and do so for Murdacayahu the Yahudym who sits within the king’s gate! Leave nothing undone of all that you have spoken.”

So Haman took the robe and the horse, and arrayed Murdacayah and led him on horseback through the city square, and proclaimed before him, “Thus shall it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!”
Afterward Murdacayahu went back to the king’s gate. But Haman hurried to his house, mourning and with his head covered.

When Haman told his wife Zarash and all his friends everything that had happened to him, his wise men and his wife Zarash said to him, “If Murdacayahu, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Yahudym descent, you will not prevail against him but will surely fall before him.”
While they were still talking with him, the king’s eunuchs came, and hastened to bring Haman to the banquet which queen Austah had prepared.
So the king and Haman went to dine with Queen Austah.

And on the second day, at the banquet of wine, the king again said to Austah, “What is your petition, Queen Austar? It shall be granted you. And what is your request, up to half the kingdom? It shall be done!”
Then Queen Austah answered and said, “If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.

For we have been sold, my people and I, to be destroyed, to be killed, and to be annihilated. Had we been sold as male and female slaves, I would have held my tongue, although the enemy could never compensate for the king’s loss.”
So King Ahasuarus answered and said to Queen Austah, “Who is he, and where is he, who would dare presume in his heart to do such a thing?”
And Austah said, “The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman!” So Haman was terrified before the king and queen.

Then the king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden; but Haman stood before Queen Austah, pleading for his life, for he saw that evil was determined against him by the king.

When the king returned from the palace garden to the place of the banquet of wine, Haman had fallen across the couch where Austah was. Then the king said, “Will he also assault the queen while I am in the house?” As the word left the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

Now Harbunah, one of the eunuchs, said to the king, “Look! The gallows, fifty cubits high, which Haman made for Murdacayahu, who spoke good on the king’s behalf, is standing at the house of Haman.” Then the king said, “Hang him on it!”
So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Murdacayah. Then the king’s wrath subsided.
On that day King Ahasuarus gave Queen Austah the house of Haman, the enemy of the Yahudym. And Murdacayahu came before the king, for Austah had told how he was related to her.
So the king took off his signet ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Murdacayahu; and Austah appointed Murdacayahu over the house of Haman.
Now Austah spoke again to the king, fell down at his feet, and implored him with tears to counteract the evil of Haman the Agagite, and the scheme which he had devised against the Yahudym.
And the king held out the golden scepter toward Austah. So queen Austah arose and stood before the king,

and said, “If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his sight and the thing seems right to the king and I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to revoke the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammadatha the Agagite, which he wrote to annihilate the Yahudym who are in all the king’s provinces.
For how can I endure to see the evil that will come to my people? Or how can I endure to see the destruction of my countrymen?”

Then King Ahasuarus said to Queen Austah and Murdacayahu the Yahudym, “Indeed, I have given Austah the house of Haman, and they have hanged him on the gallows because he tried to lay his hand on the Yahudym.

You yourselves write a decree concerning the Yahudym, as you please, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s signet ring; for whatever is written in the king’s name and sealed with the king’s signet ring no one can revoke.”

So the king’s scribes were called at that time, in the third month, on the twenty-third day; and it was written, according to all that Murdacayahu commanded, to the Yahudym, the satraps, the governors, and the princes of the provinces from India to Athiupia, one hundred and twenty-seven provinces in all, to every province in its own script, to every people in their own language, and to the Yahudym in their own script and language.
And he wrote in the name of King Ahasuarus, sealed it with the king’s signet ring, and sent letters by couriers on horseback, riding on royal horses bred from swift steeds.

By these letters the king permitted the Yahudym who were in every city to gather together and protect their lives, to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the forces of any people or province that would assault them, both little children and women, and to plunder their possessions,
on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuarus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month,
A copy of the document was to be issued as a decree in every province and published for all people, so that the Yahudym would be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
The couriers who rode on royal horses went out, hastened and pressed on by the king’s command. And the decree was issued in Shushan the citadel.

So Murdacayahu went out from the presence of the king in royal apparel of blue and white, with a great crown of gold and a garment of fine linen and purple; and the city of Shushan rejoiced and was glad.
The Yahudym had light and gladness, joy and honor.

And in every province and city, wherever the king’s command and decree came, the Yahudym had joy and gladness, a feast and a joyful day. Then many of the people of the land became Yahudym, because fear of the Yahudym fell upon them.

Now in the twelfth month, that is, on the thirteenth day, the time came for the king’s command and his decree to be executed. On the day that the enemies of the Yahudym had hoped to overpower them, the opposite occurred, in that the Yahudym themselves overpowered those who hated them.

The Yahudym gathered together in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuarus to lay hands on those who sought their harm. And no one could withstand them, because fear of them fell upon all people.
And all the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and all those doing the king’s work, helped the Yahudym, because the fear of Murdacayahu fell upon them.
For Murdacayahu was great in the king’s palace, and his fame spread throughout all the provinces; for this man Murdacayahu became increasingly prominent.
Thus the Yahudym defeated all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, with slaughter and destruction, and did what they pleased with those who hated them.
And in Shushan the citadel the Yahudym killed and destroyed five hundred men.
Also Parshandatha, Dalphun, Aspatha,
Puratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Bayazatha,
the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammadatha, the enemy of the Yahudym, they killed; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
On that day the number of those who were killed in Shushan the citadel was brought to the king.

And the king said to Queen Austah, “The Yahudym have killed and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the citadel, and the ten sons of Haman. What have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? Now what is your petition? It shall be granted to you. Or what is your further request? It shall be done.”

Then queen Austah said, “If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Yahudym who are in Shushan to do again tomorrow according to today’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.”
So the king commanded this to be done; the decree was issued in Shushan, and they hanged Haman’s ten sons.
And the Yahudym who were in Shushan gathered together again on the fourteenth day and killed three hundred men at Shushan; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.

The remainder of the Yahudym in the king’s provinces gathered together and protected their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of their enemies; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
This was on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth of the month they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
But the Yahudym who were at Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth day, as well as on the fourteenth; and on the fifteenth of the month they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
Therefore the Yahudym of the villages who dwelt in the unwalled towns celebrated the fourteenth day of the month with gladness and feasting, as a freeday, and for sending presents to one another.
And Murdacayahu wrote these things and sent letters to all the Yahudym, near and far, who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuarus,
