What sorrow for those who get up early in the morning looking for a drink of alcohol, and spend long evenings drinking wine to make themselves flaming drunk.
They furnish wine and lovely music at their grand parties, lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, but they never think about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or notice what He is doing.
So my people will go into exile far away because they do not know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Those who are great and honored will starve, and the common people will die of thirst.
The grave is licking its lips in anticipation, opening its mouth wide, the great and the lowly and all the drunken mob will be swallowed up.
Mankind will be destroyed, and people brought down; even the arrogant will lower their eyes in humiliation.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will be exalted by His justice. The qadashym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be displayed by His righteousness.
In that day lambs will find good pastures, and fattened sheep and young goats will feed among the ruins.
What sorrow for those who drag their sins behind them with ropes made of lies, who drag wickedness behind them like a cart!
They even mock 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and say, “Hurry up and do something! We want to see what you can do. Let the Qadash One of Yashar'AL carry out his plan, for we want to know what it is.”
What sorrow for those who say that evil is good and good is evil, that dark is light and light is dark, that bitter is sweet and sweet is bitter.
What sorrow for those who are wise in their own eyes and think themselves so clever.
What sorrow for those who are heroes at drinking wine and boast about all the alcohol they can hold.
They take bribes to let the wicked go free, and they punish the innocent.

Therefore, just as fire licks up stubble and dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will rot and their flowers wither, For they have rejected the law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut; they have despised the Dabar of the Qadash One of Yashar'AL.

That is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger burns against His people, and why He has raised His fist to crush them, the mountains tremble, and the corpses of his people litter the streets like garbage, But even then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger is not satisfied, His fist is still poised to strike!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will send a signal to distant nations far away and whistle to those at the ends of the Arath, they will come racing toward Yahushalam.
They will not get tired or stumble, They will not stop for rest or sleep, not a belt will be loose, not a sandal strap broken.
Their arrows will be sharp and their bows ready for battle, sparks will fly from their horses’ hooves, and the wheels of their chariots will spin like a whirlwind.
They will roar like lions, like the strongest of lions, growling, they will pounce on their victims and carry them off, and no one will be there to rescue them.

They will roar over their victims on that day of destruction like the roaring of the sea. If someone looks across the land, only darkness and distress will be seen; even the light will be darkened by clouds.
It was in the year King Uzzyahu died that I saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. He was sitting on a lofty throne, and the train of his robe filled the Temple.
Attending Him were mighty saraphim, each having six wings. With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
They were calling out to each other, “Qadash, Qadash, Qadash is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut! The whole Arath is filled with the kabad of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
Their voices shook the Temple to its foundations, and the entire building was filled with smoke.
Then I said, “It’s all over! I am doomed, for I am a sinful man. I have filthy lips, and I live among a people with filthy lips. Yet I have seen the RULER of all things, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
Then one of the saraphim flew to me with a burning coal he had taken from the altar with a pair of tongs.
He touched my lips with it and said, “See, this coal has touched your lips. Now your guilt is removed, and your sins are forgiven.”
Then I heard 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH asking, “Whom should I send as a messenger to this people? Who will go for us?” I said, “Here I am. Send me.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “Yes, go, and say to this people, ‘Listen carefully, but you will not understand. Watch closely, but you will learn nothing.’

Harden the hearts of these people, Plug their ears and shut their eyes, That way, they will not see with their eyes, nor hear with their ears, nor understand with their hearts and turn to me for healing.”
Then I said, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, how long will this go on?” And He replied, “Until their towns are empty, their houses are deserted, and the whole country is a wasteland;
until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent everyone away, and the entire land of Yashar'AL lies deserted.
If even a tenth, a remnant survive, it will be invaded again and burned, But as a terebinth or oak tree leaves a stump when it is cut down, so Yashar'AL’s stump will be a Qadash seed.”

When Ahaz, son of Yutham and grandson of Uzzyahu, was king of Yahudah, King Razin of Syria and Pakah son of Ramalyahu, the king of Yashar'AL, set out to attack Yahushalam. However, they were unable to carry out their plan.
The news had come to the royal court of Yahudah: “Syria is allied with Yashar'AL against us!” So the hearts of the king and his people trembled with fear, like trees shaking in a storm.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yashayahu, “Take your son Shaar-yashub and go out to meet King Ahaz. You will find him at the end of the aqueduct that feeds water into the upper pool, near the road leading to the field where cloth is washed.
Tell him to stop worrying. Tell him he does not need to fear the fierce anger of those two burned-out embers, King Razin of Syria and Pakah son of Remalyahu.
Yes, the kings of Syria and Yashar'AL are plotting against him, saying,
‘We will attack Yahudah and capture it for ourselves. Then we will install the son of Tabaal as Yahudah’s king.’
But this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “This invasion will never happen; it will never take place;
for Syria is no stronger than its capital, Damascus, and Damascus is no stronger than its king Razin, As for Yashar'AL, within sixty-five years it will be crushed and completely destroyed.
Yashar'AL is no stronger than its capital, Samaria, and Samaria is no stronger than its king, Pakah son of Remalyahu, Unless your Amunah (faith) is firm, I cannot make you stand firm.”
Later, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent this message to King Ahaz:
“Ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for a sign of confirmation, Ahaz. Make it as difficult as you want, as high as Shamaym or as deep as the place of the dead.”
But the king refused. “No,” he said, “I will not test 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH like that.”
Then Yashayahu said, “Listen well, you royal family of Daud! Is it not enough to exhaust man's patience? Must you exhaust the patience of my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH as well?
All right then, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Himself will give you the sign. Look! The virgin will conceive a child! She will give birth to a son and will call him Immanu'AL (which means ‘𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is with us’).
By the time this child is old enough to choose what is right and reject what is wrong, he will be eating yogurt and honey.
For before the child is that old, the lands of the two kings you fear so much will both be deserted.
“Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will bring things on you, your nation, and your family unlike anything since Yashar'AL broke away from Yahudah. He will bring the king of Assyria upon you!”
In that day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will whistle for the army of southern Mitzraym and for the army of Assyria. They will swarm around you like flies and bees.
They will come in vast hordes and settle in the fertile areas and also in the desolate valleys, caves, and thorny places.
In that day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will hire a “razor” from beyond the Euphrates River and the king of Assyria will use it to shave off everything: your land, your crops, and your people.
In that day a farmer will be fortunate to have a cow and two sheep or goats left.
Nevertheless, there will be enough milk for everyone because so few people will be left in the land. They will eat their fill of yogurt and honey.
In that day the lush vineyards, now worth 1,000 pieces of silver, will become patches of briers and thorns.
The entire land will become a vast expanse of briers and thorns, a hunting ground overrun by wildlife.
No one will go to the fertile hillsides where the gardens once grew, for briers and thorns will cover them. Cattle, sheep, and goats will graze there.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to me, “Make a large signboard and clearly write this name on it: Mahar-shalal-hash-baz.”
I asked Uriyahu the Kuhan and Zacharyahu son of Yabarakyahu, both known as honest men, to witness me doing this.
Then I slept with my wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said, “Call him Mahar-shalal-hash-baz.
For before this child is old enough to say ‘Papa’ or ‘Mama,’ the king of Assyria will carry away both the abundance of Damascus and the riches of Samaria.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH spoke to me again and said,
“My care for the people of Yahudah is like the gently flowing waters of Shiluah, but they have rejected it. They are rejoicing over what will happen to King Razin and King Pakah.
Therefore, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will overwhelm them with a mighty flood from the Euphrates River the king of Assyria and all his kabad. This flood will overflow all its channels
and sweep into Yahudah until it is chin deep. It will spread its wings, submerging your land from one end to the other, O Immanu'AL.
“Huddle together, you nations, and be terrified. Listen, all you distant lands. Prepare for battle, but you will be crushed! Yes, prepare for battle, but you will be crushed!
Call your councils of war, but they will be worthless, Develop your strategies, but they will not succeed, For 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is with us!”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given me a strong warning not to think like everyone else does. He said,
“Do not call everything a conspiracy, like they do, and do not live in dread of what frightens them.
Make 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Qadash in your life, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the one you should fear, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the one who should make you tremble.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will keep you safe. But to Yashar'AL and Yahudah, He will be a stone that makes people stumble, a rock that makes them fall, and for the people of Yahushalam, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be a trap and a snare.
Many will stumble and fall, never to rise again, They will be snared and captured.”
Preserve the teaching of your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH; entrust His instructions to those who follow me.
I will wait for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who has turned away from the descendants of Ya'aqub. I will put my hope in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
I and the children 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had given me serve as signs and warnings to Yashar'AL, from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut who dwells in His Temple on Mount Ziun.

Someone may say to you, “Let us ask the mediums and those who consult the spirits of the dead. With their whisperings and mutterings, they will tell us what to do.” But should people not ask their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for guidance? Should the living seek guidance from the dead?
Look to the instructions and teachings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! People who contradict 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar (word) are completely in the dark.
They will go from one place to another, weary and hungry. And because they are hungry, they will rage and curse their king and their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. They will look up to Shamaym
and down at the Arath, but wherever they look, there will be trouble and anguish and dark despair. They will be thrown out into the darkness.

Nevertheless, that time of darkness and despair will not go on forever, the land of Zabulun and Naphtali will be humbled, but there will be a time in the future when Galily of the other nations, which lies along the road that runs between the Yurdan and the sea, will be filled with Kabad.
The people who walk in darkness will see a great light, For those who live in a land of deep darkness, a light will shine.
You will enlarge the nation of Yashar'AL, and its people will rejoice, they will rejoice before you as people rejoice at the harvest and like warriors dividing the plunder.
For you will break the yoke of their slavery and lift the heavy burden from their shoulders, you will break the oppressor’s rod, just as you did when you destroyed the army of Midian.
The boots of the warrior and the uniforms bloodstained by warwill all be burned. They will be fuel for the fire.

For a child is born to us, a son is given to us, the government will rest on His shoulders. And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty one, from Everlasting ABBA (Father), He is the Prince of Shalum.

His government and its Shalum will never end, He will rule with fairness and justice from the throne of his father Daud for all eternity, The passionate commitment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will make this happen!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has spoken out against Ya'aqub; the judgement of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has fallen upon Yashar'AL.
And the people of Yashar'AL and Samaria, who spoke with such pride and arrogance, will soon know it.
They said, “We will replace the broken bricks of our ruins with finished stone, and replant the felled sycamore-fig trees with cedars.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will bring Razin’s enemies against Yashar'AL and stir up all their foes.
The Syrians from the east and the Philistines from the west will bare their fangs and devour Yashar'AL, But even then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger will not be satisfied. His fist is still poised to strike.
For after all this punishment, the people will still not repent. They will not seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
Therefore, in a single day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will destroy both the head and the tail, the noble palm branch and the lowly reed.
The leaders of Yashar'AL are the head, and the lying prophets are the tail.
For the leaders of the people have misled them. They have led them down the path of destruction.

That is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH takes no pleasure in the young men and shows no mercy even to the widows and orphans, For they are all wicked hypocrites, and they all speak foolishness, But even then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger will not be satisfied. His fist is still poised to strike.
This wickedness is like a brushfire. It burns not only briers and thorns but also sets the forests ablaze. Its burning sends up clouds of smoke.
The land will be blackened by the fury of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, the people will be fuel for the fire, and no one will spare even his own brother.
They will attack their neighbor on the right but will still be hungry, they will devour their neighbor on the left but will not be satisfied, In the end they will even eat their own children.
Manassah will feed on Aphraim, Aphraim will feed on Manassah, and both will devour Yahudah, but even then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger will not be satisfied, His fist is still poised to strike.
What sorrow awaits the unjust judges and those who issue unfair laws.
They deprive the poor of justice and deny the rights of the needy among my people, they prey on widows and take advantage of orphans.
What will you do when I punish you, when I send disaster upon you from a distant land? To whom will you turn for help? Where will your treasures be safe?
You will stumble along as prisoners or lie among the dead, but even then the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will not be satisfied. His fist is still poised to strike.
“What sorrow awaits Assyria, the rod of my anger. I use it as a club to express my anger.
I am sending Assyria against an unrighteous nation, against a people with whom I am angry, Assyria will plunder them, trampling them like dirt beneath its feet.
But the king of Assyria will not understand that he is my tool; his mind does not work that way, his plan is simply to destroy, to cut down nation after nation.
He will say, ‘Each of my princes will soon be a king.
We destroyed Calno just as we did Carchamish. Hamath fell before us as Arpad did, and we destroyed Samaria just as we did Damascus.
Yes, we have finished off many kingdoms whose idols were greater than those in Yahushalam and Samaria.
So we will defeat Yahushalam and her idols, just as we destroyed Samaria with hers.’”
After 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has used the king of Assyria to accomplish his purposes on Mount Ziun and in Yahushalam, he will turn against the king of Assyria and punish him, for he is proud and arrogant.

He boasts, “By my own powerful arm I have done this, With my own shrewd wisdom I planned it. I have broken down the defenses of nations and carried off their treasures. I have knocked down their kings like a bull.
I have robbed their nests of riches and gathered up kingdoms as a farmer gathers eggs, No one can even flap a wing against me or utter a peep of protest.”
But can the ax boast greater power than the person who uses it? Is the saw greater than the person who saws? Can a rod strike unless a hand moves it? Can a wooden cane walk by itself?
Therefore, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will send a plague among Assyria’s proud troops, and a flaming fire will consume its Kabad.
And the light of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, will be a fire; the Qadash One will be a flame, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will devour the thorns and briers with fire, burning up the enemy in a single night.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will consume Assyria’s kabad like a fire consumes a forest in a fruitful land; it will waste away like sick people in a plague.
Of all that awesome forest, only a few trees will survive, so few that a child could count them!

In that day the remnant left in Yashar'AL, the survivors in the house of Ya'aqub, will no longer depend on allies who seek to destroy them, But they will faithfully trust 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the Qadash One of Yashar'AL.
A remnant will return; yes, the remnant of Ya'aqub will return to the Mighty 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
But though the people of Yashar'AL are as numerous as the sand of the seashore, only a remnant of them will return, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has rightly decided to destroy his people.
Yes, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, has already decided to destroy the entire land.
So this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Dabar: “O my people in Ziun, do not be afraid of the Assyrians when they oppress you with rod and club as the Mitzraym did long ago.
In a little while my anger against you will end, and then my anger will rise up to destroy them.”

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will lash them with His whip, as he did when Gidaun triumphed over the Midianites at the rock of Urab, or when the staff of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was raised to drown the Mitzraym army in the sea.
In that day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will end the bondage of His people. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will break the yoke of slavery and lift it from their shoulders.
Look, the Assyrians are now at Aiath, They are passing through Migrun and are storing their equipment at Micmash.
They are crossing the pass and are camping at Gaba, fear strikes the town of Ramah. All the people of Gibaah, the hometown of King Shaul, are running for their lives.
Scream in terror, you people of Gallim! Shout out a warning to Laishah. Oh, poor Anathuth!
There go the people of Madmanah, all fleeing. The citizens of Gabim are trying to hide.
The enemy stops at Nub for the rest of that day. He shakes his fist at beautiful Mount Ziun, the mountain of Yahushalam.
But look! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, will chop down the mighty tree of Assyria with great power! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will cut down the proud. That lofty tree will be brought down.
He will cut down the forest trees with an ax, Labanun will fall to the Mighty One.
Out of the stump of Daud’s family will grow a shoot, yes a new Branch bearing fruit from the old root.
And the Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will rest on him, the Ruach of wisdom and understanding, the Ruach of counsel and might, the Ruach of knowledge and the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
He will delight in obeying 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. He will not judge by appearance nor make a decision based on hearsay.
He will give justice to the poor and make fair decisions for the exploited, the Arath will shake at the force of his word, and one breath from his mouth will destroy the wicked.
He will wear righteousness like a belt and truth like an undergarment.
In that day the wolf and the lamb will live together; the leopard will lie down with the baby goat, the calf and the yearling will be safe with the lion, and a little child will lead them all.
The cow will graze near the bear. The cub and the calf will lie down together, the lion will eat hay like a cow.
The baby will play safely near the hole of a cobra, Yes a little child will put its hand in a nest of deadly snakes without harm.
Nothing will hurt or destroy in all my Qadash mountain, for as the waters fill the sea, so the Arath will be filled with people who know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
In that day the heir to Daud’s throne will be a banner of salvation to all the world, the nations will rally to him, and the land where he lives will be a marvelous place.

In that day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will reach out his hand a second time to bring back the remnant of his people, those who remain in Assyria and northern Mitzraym, in southern Mitzraym, Athiupia, and Alam; in Babylunia, Hamath, and all the distant coastlands.
He will raise a flag among the nations and assemble the exiles of Yashar'AL. He will gather the scattered people of Yahudah from the ends of the Arath.
Then at last the jealousy between Yashar'AL and Yahudah will end, They will not be rivals anymore.
They will join forces to swoop down on Philistia to the west. Together they will attack and plunder the nations to the east. They will occupy the lands of Adum and Muab, and Ammun will obey them.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make a dry path through the gulf of the Red Sea. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will wave His hand over the Euphrates River, sending a mighty wind to divide it into seven streams so it can easily be crossed on foot.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make a highway for the remnant of His people, the remnant coming from Assyria, just as he did for Yashar'AL long ago when they returned from Mitzraym.
In that day you will sing: “I will Yadah you, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! You were angry with me, but not any more, Now you comfort me.
See, my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has come to save me, I will trust in Him and not be afraid. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is my strength and my song; He has given me victory.”
With joy you will drink deeply from the fountain of salvation!
In that wonderful day you will sing: “Tudah Raba 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! and Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! Tell the nations what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done, Let them know how mighty He is!
Sing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for He has done wonderful things. Make known His Yadah around the world.
Let all the people of Yahushalam shout His Yadah with joy! For great is the Qadash One of Yashar'AL who lives among you.”
Yashayahu son of Amuz received this message concerning the destruction of Babylun:
“Raise a signal flag on a bare hilltop, Call up an army against Babylun, Wave your hand to encourage them as they march into the palaces of the high and mighty.
I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have dedicated these soldiers for this task, Yes, I have called mighty warriors to express my anger, and they will rejoice when I am exalted.”
Hear the noise on the mountains! Listen, as the vast armies march! It is the noise and shouting of many nations, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has called this army together.
They come from distant countries, from beyond the farthest horizons, They are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s weapons to carry out His anger, With them He will destroy the whole land.
Scream in terror, for the day of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has arrived, the time for the AL'Mighty to destroy.
Every arm is paralyzed with fear, Every heart melts,
and people are terrified, pangs of anguish grip them, like those of a woman in labor, They look helplessly at one another, their faces aflame with fear.
See, the day of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is coming, the terrible day of his fury and fierce anger, The land will be made desolate, and all the sinners destroyed with it.
The Shamaym will be black above them; the stars will give no light, the sun will be dark when it rises, and the moon will provide no light.
“I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their sin, I will crush the arrogance of the proud and humble the pride of the mighty.
I will make people scarcer than gold, more rare than the fine gold of Ophir.
For I will shake the Shamaym, The Arath will move from its place when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut displays His wrath in the day of His fierce anger.
Everyone in Babylun will run about like a hunted gazelle, like sheep without a shepherd, they will try to find their own people and flee to their own land.
Anyone who is captured will be cut down, run through with a sword.
Their little children will be dashed to death before their eyes, Their homes will be sacked, and their wives will be raped.
“Look, I will stir up the Madas against Babylun. They cannot be tempted by silver or bribed with gold.
The attacking armies will shoot down the young men with arrows, they will have no mercy on helpless babies and will show no compassion for children.”
Babylun, the most awesome of kingdoms, the flower of Chaldaans pride, will be devastated like Sudum and Gumurrah when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH destroyed them.
Babylun will never be inhabited again. It will remain empty for generation after generation, Nomads will refuse to camp there, and shepherds will not bed down their sheep.
Desert animals will move into the ruined city, and the houses will be haunted by howling creatures, Owls will live among the ruins, and wild goats will go there to dance.
Hyenas will howl in its fortresses, and jackals will make dens in its luxurious palaces, Babylun’s days are numbered; its time of destruction will soon arrive.

But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will have mercy on the descendants of Ya'aqub, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will choose Yashar'AL as his special people once again. He will bring them back to settle once again in their own land, and people from many different nations will come and join them there and unite with the people of Yashar'AL.

The nations of the world will help the people of Yashar'AL to return, and those who come to live in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s land will serve them. Those who captured Yashar'AL will themselves be captured, and Yashar'AL will rule over its enemies.
In that wonderful day when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives His people rest from sorrow and fear, from slavery and chains,
you will taunt the king of Babylun. You will say, “The mighty man has been destroyed. Yes, your insolence is ended.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has crushed your wicked power and broken your evil rule.
You struck the people with endless blows of rage and held the nations in your angry grip with unrelenting tyranny.
But finally the Arath is at rest and quiet. Now it can sing again!
Even the trees of the forest, the cypress trees and the cedars of Labanun, sing out this joyous song: ‘Since you have been cut down, no one will come now to cut us down!’
“In the place of the dead there is excitement over your arrival, the spirits of world leaders and mighty kings long dead stand up to see you.
With one voice they all cry out, ‘Now you are as weak as we are!
Your might and power were buried with you. The sound of the harp in your palace has ceased, Now maggots are your sheet, and worms your blanket.’
“How you are fallen from Shamaym, O Lucifer, son of the morning! You have been thrown down to the Arath, you who destroyed the nations of the world.
For you said to yourself, ‘I will ascend to Shamaym and set my throne above 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s stars. I will preside on the mountain of the deities far away in the north.
I will climb to the highest Shamaym and be like the MOST HIGH.’
Instead, you will be brought down to the place of the dead, down to its lowest depths.
Everyone there will stare at you and ask, ‘Can this be the one who shook the Arath and made the kingdoms of the world tremble?
Is this the one who destroyed the world and made it into a wasteland? Is this the king who demolished the world’s greatest cities and had no mercy on his prisoners?’
“The kings of the nations lie in stately Kabad, each in his own tomb,
but you will be thrown out of your grave like a worthless branch, like a corpse trampled underfoot, you will be dumped into a mass grave with those killed in battle, you will descend to the pit.
You will not be given a proper burial, for you have destroyed your nation and slaughtered your people, the descendants of such an evil person will never again receive honor.
Kill this man’s children! Let them die because of their father’s sins! They must not rise and conquer the Arath, filling the world with their cities.”
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Dabar: “I, myself, have risen against Babylun! I will destroy its children and its children’s children,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“I will make Babylun a desolate place of owls, filled with swamps and marshes, I will sweep the land with the broom of destruction, I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, have spoken!”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has sworn this oath: “It will all happen as I have planned. It will be as I have decided.
I will break the Assyrians when they are in Yashar'AL; I will trample them on my mountains, My people will no longer be their slaves nor bow down under their heavy loads.
I have a plan for the whole Arath, a hand of judgment upon all the nations.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has spoken, who can change the plans of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? When His hand is raised, who can stop Him?”
This message came to me the year King Ahaz died:

Do not rejoice, you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken, that the king who attacked you is dead, For from that snake a more poisonous snake will be born, a fiery serpent to destroy you!
I will feed the poor in my pasture; the needy will lie down in Shalum, but as for you, I will wipe you out with famine and destroy the few who remain.
Wail at the gates! Weep in the cities! Melt with fear, you Philistines! A powerful army comes like smoke from the north, Each soldier rushes forward eager to fight.
What should we tell the Philistine messengers? Tell them, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has built Yahushalam; its walls will give refuge to His oppressed people.”
This message came to me concerning Muab: In one night the town of Ar will be leveled, and the city of Kir will be destroyed.

Your people will go to their temple in Dibun to mourn, They will go to their sacred shrines to weep, they will wail for the fate of Nabu and Madaba, shaving their heads in sorrow and cutting off their beards.
They will wear burlap as they wander the streets, From every home and public square will come the sound of wailing.
The people of Hashbun and Alaalah will cry out; their voices will be heard as far away as Yahaz! The bravest warriors of Muab will cry out in utter terror, they will be helpless with fear.
My heart weeps for Muab. Its people flee to Zuar and Aglath-shalishiyah weeping, they climb the road to Luhith, Their cries of distress can be heard all along the road to Hurunaim.
Even the waters of Nimrim are dried up! The grassy banks are scorched, the tender plants are gone; nothing green remains.
The people grab their possessions and carry them across the Ravine of Willows.
A cry of distress echoes through the land of Muab from one end to the other, from Aglaim to Baar-alim.
The stream near Dibun runs red with blood, but I am still not finished with Dibun! Lions will hunt down the survivors, both those who try to escape and those who remain behind.
Send lambs from Sala as tribute to the ruler of the land, send them through the desert to the mountain of beautiful Ziun.
The women of Muab are left like homeless birds at the shallow crossings of the Arnun River.
“Help us,” they cry, “Defend us against our enemies, Protect us from their relentless attack, Do not betray us now that we have escaped.
Let our refugees stay among you, hide them from our enemies until the terror is past.” When oppression and destruction have ended and enemy raiders have disappeared,
then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will establish one of Daud’s descendants as king, he will rule with mercy and truth, he will always do what is just and be eager to do what is right.
We have heard about proud Muab, about its pride and arrogance and rage, but all that boasting has disappeared.
The entire land of Muab weeps, Yes, everyone in Muab mourns for the cakes of raisins from Kir-harasath, They are all gone now.

The farms of Hashbun are abandoned; the vineyards at Sibmah are deserted, the rulers of the nations have broken down Muab, that beautiful grapevine, its tendrils spread north as far as the town of Yazar and trailed eastward into the wilderness, Its shoots reached so far west that they crossed over the Dead Sea.
So now I weep for Yazar and the vineyards of Sibmah; my tears will flow for Hashbun and Alaalah, there are no more shouts of joy over your summer fruits and harvest.
Gone now is the gladness, gone the joy of harvest there will be no singing in the vineyards, no more happy shouts, no treading of grapes in the winepresses, I have ended all their harvest joys.
My heart’s cry for Muab is like a lament on a harp, I am filled with anguish for Kir-harasath.
The people of Muab will worship at their pagan shrines, but it will do them no good, They will cry to the idols in their temples, but no one will be able to save them.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has already Dabar of these things about Muab in the past.
But now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says, “Within three years, counting each day, the kabad of Muab will be ended, from its great population, only a feeble few will be left alive.”
This message came to me concerning Damascus: “Look, the city of Damascus will disappear! It will become a heap of ruins.
The towns of Aruar will be deserted. Flocks will graze in the streets and lie down undisturbed, with no one to chase them away.

The fortified towns of Yashar'AL will also be destroyed, and the royal power of Damascus will end, All that remains of Syria will share the fate of Yashar'AL’s departed kabad,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
“In that day Yashar'AL’s kabad will grow dim; its robust body will waste away.
The whole land will look like a grainfield after the harvesters have gathered the grain. It will be desolate, like the fields in the valley of Raphaim after the harvest.

Only a few of its people will be left, like stray olives left on a tree after the harvest, Only two or three remain in the highest branches, four or five scattered here and there on the limbs,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
Then at last the people will look to their Creator and turn their eyes to the Qadash One of Yashar'AL.
They will no longer look to their idols for help or worship what their own hands have made, they will never again bow down to their Asharah poles or worship at the pagan shrines they have built.
Their largest cities will be like a deserted forest, like the land the Hibites and Amurites abandoned when the Yasharalym came here so long ago, It will be utterly desolate.
Why? Because you have turned from the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who can save you, and You have forgotten the Rock who can hide you, So you may plant the finest grapevines and import the most expensive seedlings.

They may sprout on the day you set them out; yes, they may blossom on the very morning you plant them, but you will never pick any grapes from them. Your only harvest will be a load of grief and unrelieved pain.
Listen! The armies of many nations roar like the roaring of the sea, hear the thunder of the mighty forces as they rush forward like thundering waves.
But though they thunder like breakers on a beach, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will silence them, and they will run away, they will flee like chaff scattered by the wind, like a tumbleweed whirling before a storm.
In the evening Yashar'AL waits in terror, but by dawn its enemies are dead, This is the just reward of those who plunder us, a fitting end for those who destroy us.
Listen, Athiupia land of fluttering sails that lies at the headwaters of the Nile,

that sends ambassadors in swift boats down the river. Go, swift messengers! Take a message to a tall, smooth-skinned people, who are feared far and wide for their conquests and destruction, and whose land is divided by rivers.
All you people of the world, everyone who lives on the Arath, when I raise my battle flag on the mountain, look! When I blow the ram’s horn, listen!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has told me this: “I will watch quietly from my dwelling place, as quietly as the heat rises on a summer day, or as the morning dew forms during the harvest.”
Even before you begin your attack, while your plans are ripening like grapes, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will cut off your new growth with pruning shears. He will snip off and discard your spreading branches.
Your mighty army will be left dead in the fields for the mountain vultures and wild animals, the vultures will tear the corpses all summer. The wild animals will gnaw at the bones all winter.

At that time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will receive gifts from this land divided by rivers, from this tall, smooth-skinned people, who are feared far and wide for their conquests and destruction, They will bring the gifts to Yahushalam, where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut dwells.
This message came to me concerning Mitzraym: Look! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is advancing against Mitzraym, riding on a swift cloud, the idols of Mitzraym tremble, The hearts of the Mitzraym melt with fear.
“I will make Mitzraym fight against Mitzraym brother against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, province against province.
The Mitzraym will lose heart, and I will confuse their plans, They will plead with their idols for wisdom and call on spirits, mediums, and those who consult the spirits of the dead.
I will hand Mitzraym over to a hard, cruel master, A fierce king will rule them,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
The waters of the Nile will fail to rise and flood the fields, The riverbed will be parched and dry.
The canals of the Nile will dry up, and the streams of Mitzraym will stink with rotting reeds and rushes.
All the greenery along the riverbank and all the crops along the river will dry up and blow away.
The fishermen will lament for lack of work. Those who cast hooks into the Nile will groan, and those who use nets will lose heart.
There will be no flax for the harvesters, no thread for the weavers.
They will be in despair, and all the workers will be sick at heart.

What fools are the officials of Zuan! Their best counsel to the king of Mitzraym is stupid and wrong. Will they still boast to Phar'uh of their wisdom? Will they dare brag about all their wise ancestors?
Where are your wise counselors, Phar'uh? Let them tell you what 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH plans, what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut is going to do to Mitzraym.
The officials of Zuan are fools, and the officials of Mamphis are deluded, the leaders of the people have led Mitzraym astray.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent a spirit of foolishness on them, so all their suggestions are wrong, they cause Mitzraym to stagger like a drunk in his vomit.
There is nothing Mitzraym can do. All are helpless, the head and the tail, the noble palm branch and the lowly reed.
In that day the Mitzraym will be as weak as women. They will cower in fear beneath the upraised fist of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
Just to speak the name of Yashar'AL will terrorize them, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has laid out his plans against them.

In that day five of Mitzraym’s cities will follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, they will even begin to speak Abarym (Hebrew), the language of Canaan. One of these cities will be Haliupulis, the City of the Sun.
In that day there will be an altar to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the heart of Mitzraym, and there will be a monument to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at its border.

It will be a sign and a witness that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut is worshiped in the land of Mitzraym. When the people cry to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for help against those who oppress them, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will send them a savior who will rescue them.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make himself known to the Mitzraym. Yes, they will know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and will give their sacrifices and offerings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. They will make a vow to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and will keep it.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will strike Mitzraym, and then He will bring healing. For the Mitzraym will turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and He will listen to their pleas and heal them.
In that day Mitzraym and Assyria will be connected by a highway. The Mitzraym and Assyrians will move freely between their lands, and they will both worship 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of all life.
In that day Yashar'AL will be the third, along with Mitzraym and Assyria, a Barakah in the midst of the Arath.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will Dabar, “baraked be Mitzraym, my people. Baraked be Assyria, the land I have made. Baraked be Yashar'AL, my special possession!”
In the year when King Sargun of Assyria sent his commander in chief to capture the Philistine city of Ashdud,
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told Yashayahu son of Amuz, “Take off the burlap you have been wearing, and remove your sandals.” Yashayahu did as he was told and walked around naked and barefoot.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “My servant Yashayahu has been walking around naked and barefoot for the last three years. This is a sign, a symbol of the terrible troubles I will bring upon Mitzraym and Athiupia.
For the king of Assyria will take away the Mitzraym and Athiupians as prisoners. He will make them walk naked and barefoot, both young and old, their buttocks bared, to the shame of Mitzraym.
Then the Philistines will be thrown into panic, for they counted on the power of Athiupia and boasted of their allies in Mitzraym!
They will say, ‘If this can happen to Mitzraym, what chance do we have? We were counting on Mitzraym to protect us from the king of Assyria.’”
This message came to me concerning Babylun, the desert by the sea: Disaster is roaring down on you from the desert, like a whirlwind sweeping in from the Nagab.
I see a terrifying vision: I see the betrayer betraying, the destroyer destroying, Go ahead, you Elamites and Medes, attack and lay siege, I will make an end to all the groaning Babylun caused.
My stomach aches and burns with pain. Sharp pangs of anguish are upon me, like those of a woman in labor, I grow faint when I hear what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is planning; I am too afraid to look.
My mind reels and my heart races. I longed for evening to come, but now I am terrified of the dark.
Look! They are preparing a great feast. They are spreading rugs for people to sit on. Everyone is eating and drinking, But quick! Grab your shields and prepare for battle. You are being attacked!
Meanwhile, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to me, “Put a watchman on the city wall, Let him shout out what he sees.
He should look for chariots drawn by pairs of horses, and for riders on donkeys and camels. Let the watchman be fully alert.”
Then the watchman called out, “Day after day I have stood on the watchtower, my master. Night after night I have remained at my post.
Now at last look! Here comes a man in a chariot with a pair of horses! ”Then the watchman said, Babylun is fallen, is fallen! All the idols of Babylun lie broken on the ground!
O my people, threshed and winnowed, I have told you everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has Dabar, everything the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL has told me.
This message came to me concerning Adum: Someone from Adum keeps calling to me, “Watchman, how much longer until morning? When will the night be over?”
The watchman replies,“Morning is coming, but night will soon return. If you wish to ask again, then come back and ask.”
This message came to me concerning Arabia: O caravans from Dadan, hide in the deserts of Arabia.
O people of Tama, bring water to these thirsty people, food to these weary refugees.
They have fled from the sword, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow and the terrors of battle.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to me, “Within a year, counting each day, all the happiness of Kadar will come to an end.
Only a few of its courageous archers will survive. I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL have spoken!”
This message came to me concerning Yahushalam, the Valley of Vision: What is happening? Why is everyone running to the rooftops?
The whole city is in a terrible uproar, what do I see in this reveling city? Bodies are lying everywhere, killed not in battle but by famine and disease.
All your leaders have fled, they surrendered without resistance, the people tried to slip away, but they were captured, too.
That’s why I said, “Leave me alone to weep; do not try to comfort me, Let me cry for my people as I watch them being destroyed.”

Oh, what a day of crushing defeat! What a day of confusion and terror brought by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, upon the Valley of Vision! The walls of Yahushalam have been broken, and cries of death echo from the mountainsides.
Alamites are the archers, with their chariots and charioteers, The men of Kir hold up the shields.
Chariots fill your beautiful valleys, and charioteers storm your gates.
Yahudah’s defenses have been stripped away. You run to the armory for your weapons.
You inspect the breaks in the walls of Yahushalam, you store up water in the lower pool.
You survey the houses and tear some down for stone to strengthen the walls.
Between the city walls, you build a reservoir for water from the old pool, But you never ask for help from the One who did all this. You never considered the One who planned this long ago.
At that time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, called you to weep and mourn, He told you to shave your heads in sorrow for your sins and to wear clothes of burlap to show your remorse.
But instead, you dance and play; you slaughter cattle and kill sheep. You feast on meat and drink wine, You say, “Let’s feast and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has revealed this to me: “Till the day you die, you will never be forgiven for this sin.” That is the judgment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Dabar to me: “Confront Shabna, the palace administrator, and give him this message:
“Who do you think you are, and what are you doing here, building a beautiful tomb for yourself a monument high up in the rock?
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is about to hurl you away, mighty man, He is going to grab you,
crumple you into a ball, and toss you away into a distant, barren land, There you will die, and your beautiful chariots will be broken and useless, You have brought shame to your master!
“Yes, I will drive you out of office,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “I will pull you down from your high position.
And then I will call my servant Aliakim son of Hilkyahu to replace you.
I will dress him in your royal robes and will give him your title and your authority. And he will be a father to the people of Yahushalam and Yahudah.
I will give him the key to the house of Daud, the highest position in the royal court. When he opens doors, no one will be able to close them; when he closes doors, no one will be able to open them.
He will bring honor to his family name, for I will drive him firmly in place like a nail in the wall.
They will give him great responsibility, and he will bring honor to even the lowliest members of his family.”

But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut also says: “The time will come when I will pull out the nail that seemed so firm. It will come out and fall to the ground. Everything it supports will fall with it, I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have spoken!”
This message came to me concerning Tyra:
Mourn in silence, you people of the coast and you merchants of Sidun, your traders crossed the sea,
sailing over deep waters, they brought you grain from Mitzraym and harvests from along the Nile, You were the marketplace of the world.
But now you are put to shame, city of Sidun, for Tyra, the fortress of the sea, says, “Now I am childless; I have no sons or daughters.”
When Mitzraym hears the news about Tyra, there will be great sorrow.
Send word now to Tarshish! Wail, you people who live in distant lands!
Is this silent ruin all that is left of your once joyous city? What a long history was yours! Think of all the colonists you sent to distant places.
Who has brought this disaster on Tyra, that great creator of kingdoms? Her traders were all princes, her merchants were nobles.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has done it to destroy your pride and bring low all the Arath’s nobility.
Come, people of Tarshish, sweep over the land like the flooding Nile, for Tyra is defenseless.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH held out his hand over the sea and shook the kingdoms of the Arath, He has spoken out against Phuanicia, ordering that her fortresses be destroyed.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says, “Never again will you rejoice, O daughter of Sidun, for you have been crushed, Even if you flee to Cyprus, you will find no rest.”

Look at the land of Babylunia, the people of that land are gone! The Assyrians have handed Babylun over to the wild animals of the desert, They have built siege ramps against its walls, torn down its palaces, and turned it to a heap of rubble.
Wail, you ships of Tarshish, for your harbor is destroyed!
For seventy years, the length of a king’s life, Tyra will be forgotten. But then the city will come back to life as in the song about the prostitute:
Take a harp and walk the streets, you forgotten harlot. Make sweet melody and sing your songs so you will be remembered again.
Yes, after seventy years 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will revive Tyra. But she will be no different than she was before, She will again be a prostitute to all kingdoms around the world.
But in the end her profits will be given to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Her wealth will not be hoarded but will provide good food and fine clothing for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Kuhanym.
Look! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is about to destroy the Arath and make it a vast wasteland, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH devastates the surface of the Arath and scatters the people.
Kuhanym and lay people, servants and masters, maids and mistresses, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, bankers and debtors, none will be spared.
The Arath will be completely emptied and looted, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has spoken!
The Arath mourns and dries up, and the land wastes away and withers, Even the greatest people on Arath waste away.
The Arath suffers for the sins of its people, for they have twisted the instructions of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, violated the law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and broken His everlasting covenant.
Therefore, a curse consumes the Arath, Its people must pay the price for their sin, They are destroyed by fire, and only a few are left alive.
The grapevines waste away, and there is no new wine, All the merrymakers sigh and mourn.
The cheerful sound of tambourines is stilled; the happy cries of celebration are heard no more, The melodious chords of the harp are silent.
Gone are the joys of wine and song; alcoholic drink turns bitter in the mouth.
The city writhes in chaos; every home is locked to keep out intruders.
Mobs gather in the streets, crying out for wine, Joy has turned to gloom, Gladness has been banished from the land.
The city is left in ruins, its gates battered down.
Throughout the Arath the story is the same, only a remnant is left, like the stray olives left on the tree or the few grapes left on the vine after harvest.
But all who are left shout and sing for joy. Those in the west sing Yadah to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s majesty.
In eastern lands, give Kabad to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. In the lands beyond the sea, Yadah the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.

We hear songs of Yadah from the ends of the Arath, songs that give Kabad to the Righteous One! But my heart is heavy with grief, Weep for me, for I wither away, Deceit still prevails, and treachery is everywhere.
Terror and traps and snares will be your lot, you people of the Arath.
Those who flee in terror will fall into a trap, and those who escape the trap will be caught in a snare. Destruction falls like rain from the Shamaym; the foundations of the Arath shake.
The Arath has broken up. It has utterly collapsed; it is violently shaken.
The Arath staggers like a drunk, It trembles like a tent in a storm, It falls and will not rise again, for the guilt of its rebellion is very heavy.
In that day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will punish the deities in the Shamaym and the proud rulers of the nations on Arath.
They will be rounded up and put in prison. They will be shut up in prison and will finally be punished.

Then the Kabad of the moon will wane, and the brightness of the sun will fade, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will rule on Mount Ziun, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will rule in great Kabad in Yahushalam, in the sight of all the leaders of His people.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, I will honor and Yadah your Name, for you are my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, You do such wonderful things! You planned them long ago, and now you have accomplished them.
You turn mighty cities into heaps of ruins. Cities with strong walls are turned to rubble, Beautiful palaces in distant lands disappear and will never be rebuilt.
Therefore, strong nations will declare your Kabad; ruthless nations will fear you.

But you are a tower of refuge to the poor, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, a tower of refuge to the needy in distress, You are a refuge from the storm and a shelter from the heat, For the oppressive acts of ruthless people are like a storm beating against a wall,
or like the relentless heat of the desert, But you silence the roar of foreign nations, As the shade of a cloud cools relentless heat, so the boastful songs of ruthless people are stilled.
In Yahushalam, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will spread a wonderful feast for all the people of the world, It will be a delicious banquet with clear, well-aged wine and choice meat.
There he will remove the cloud of gloom, the shadow of death that hangs over the Arath.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will swallow up death forever! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will wipe away all tears, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will remove forever all insults and mockery against His land and people, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has spoken!
In that day the people will proclaim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH! We trusted in Him, and He saved us! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, in whom we trusted, Let us rejoice in the salvation He brings!”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s hand of Barakah will rest on Yahushalam, But Muab will be crushed, It will be like straw trampled down and left to rot.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will push down Muab’s people as a swimmer pushes down water with his hands, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will end their pride and all their evil works.
The high walls of Muab will be demolished. They will be brought down to the ground, down into the dust.
In that day, everyone in the land of Yahudah will sing this song: Our city is strong! We are surrounded by the walls of our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH’s salvation.
Open the gates to all who are righteous; allow the faithful to enter.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will keep in perfect Shalum all who trust in Him, all whose thoughts are fixed in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
Trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH always, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH is the eternal Rock.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH humbles the proud and brings down the arrogant city, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brings it down to the dust.
The poor and oppressed trample it underfoot, and the needy walk all over it.
But for those who are righteous, the way is not steep and rough, You are our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who does what is right, and you smooth out the path ahead of them.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, we show our trust in You by obeying your laws; our heart’s desire is to Esteemed your Name.
In the night I search for you; in the morning I earnestly seek you. For only when You come to judge the Arath will people learn what is right.
Your kindness to the wicked does not make them do good, Although others do right, the wicked keep doing wrong and take no notice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s majesty.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they pay no attention to your upraised fist, Show them your eagerness to defend your people, then they will be ashamed, Let your fire consume your enemies.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you will grant us Shalum; all we have accomplished is really from you.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, others have ruled us, but you alone are the one we worship.
Those we served before are dead and gone, their departed spirits will never return! You attacked them and destroyed them, and they are long forgotten.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you have made our nation great; yes, you have made us great, You have extended our borders, and we give you the Kabad!
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, in distress we searched for you, We prayed beneath the burden of your discipline.
Just as a pregnant woman writhes and cries out in pain as she gives birth, so were we in your presence, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
We, too, writhe in agony, but nothing comes of our suffering, We have not given salvation to the Arath, nor brought life into the world.

But those who die in the righteousness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will live; their bodies will rise again! Those who sleep in the Arath will rise up and sing for joy! For your life-giving light will fall like dew on your people in the place of the dead!
Go home, my people, and lock your doors! Hide yourselves for a little while until 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger has passed.
Look! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is coming from Shamaym to punish the people of the Arath for their sins, The Arath will no longer hide those who have been killed, they will be brought out for all to see.
In that day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will take His terrible, swift sword and punish Laviathan, the swiftly moving serpent, the coiling, writhing serpent. He will kill the dragon of the sea.
“In that day, sing about the fruitful vineyard.
I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will watch over it, watering it carefully, Day and night I will watch so no one can harm it.
My anger will be gone, If I find briers and thorns growing, I will attack them; I will burn them up,
unless they turn to me for help, let them make Shalum with me; yes, let them make Shalum with me.”
The time is coming when Ya'aqub’s descendants will take root, Yashar'AL will bud and blossom and fill the whole Arath with fruit!
Has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck Yashar'AL as He struck her enemies? Has He punished her as He punished them?
No, but He exiled Yashar'AL to call her to account, She was exiled from her land as though blown away in a storm from the east.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did this to purge Yashar'AL’s wickedness, to take away all her sin, As a result all the pagan altars will be crushed to dust, No Asharah pole or pagan shrine will be left standing.
The fortified towns will be silent and empty, the houses abandoned, the streets overgrown with weeds, Calves will graze there, chewing on twigs and branches.

The people are like the dead branches of a tree, broken off and used for kindling beneath the cooking pots, Yashar'AL is a foolish and stupid nation, for its people have turned away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Therefore, the one who made them will show them no pity or mercy.
Yet the time will come when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will gather them together like handpicked grain, One by one he will gather them, from the Auphrates River in the east to the Brook of Mitzraym in the west.
In that day the great trumpet will sound. Many who were dying in exile in Assyria and Mitzraym will return to Yahushalam to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH on his Qadash mountain.

What sorrow awaits the proud city of Samaria, the Esteemed crown of the drunks of Yashar'AL, It sits at the head of a fertile valley, but its awesome beauty will fade like a flower, It is the pride of a people brought down by wine.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will send a mighty army against it, Like a mighty hailstorm and a torrential rain, they will burst upon it like a surging flood and smash it to the ground.
The proud city of Samaria, the Esteemed crown of the drunks of Yashar'AL will be trampled beneath its enemies’ feet.
It sits at the head of a fertile valley, but its awesome beauty will fade like a flower, Whoever sees it will snatch it up, as an early fig is quickly picked and eaten.
Then at last 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will Himself be Yashar'AL’s Esteemed crown, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be the pride and joy of the remnant of His people.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give a longing for justice to their judges, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give great courage to their warriors who stand at the gates.

But now presently, Yashar'AL is led by drunks who reel with wine and stagger with alcohol. The Kuhanym and Nabyms stagger with alcohol and lose themselves in wine, They reel when they see visions and stagger as they render decisions.
Their tables are covered with vomit; filth is everywhere.
“Who does 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH think we are?” they ask, “Why does He speak to us like this? Are we little children, just recently weaned?
He tells us everything over and over, one line at a time, one line at a time, a little here, and a little there!”
So now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will have to speak to His people through foreign oppressors who speak a strange language!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has told His people, “Here is a place of rest; let the weary rest here, This is a place of quiet rest.” But they would not listen.

So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will spell out His message for them again, one line at a time, one line at a time, a little here, and a little there, so that they will stumble and fall. They will be injured, trapped, and captured.
Therefore, listen to this message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you scoffing rulers in Yahushalam.
You boast, “We have struck a bargain to cheat death and have made a deal to dodge the grave, The coming destruction can never touch us, for we have built a strong refuge made of lies and deception.”

Therefore, this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Dabar: “Look! I am placing a foundation stone in Yahushalam, a firm and tested stone, It is a precious cornerstone that is safe to build on, Whoever believes will not be in haste.

I will test you with the measuring line of justice and the plumb line of righteousness, Since your refuge is made of lies, a hailstorm will knock it down, Since it is made of deception, a flood will sweep it away.
I will cancel the bargain you made to cheat death, and I will overturn your deal to dodge the grave, When the terrible enemy sweeps through, you will be trampled into the ground.
Again and again that flood will come, morning after morning, day and night, until you are carried away.” This message will bring terror to your people.
The bed you have made is too short to lie on, The blankets are too narrow to cover you.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will come as he did against the Philistines at Mount Perazim and against the Amurites at Gibaun, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will come to do a strange thing; He will come to do an unusual deed:
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Tsaba'ut has plainly said that He is determined to crush the whole land, So scoff no more, or your punishment will be even greater.
Listen to me; listen, and pay close attention.
Does a farmer always plow and never sow? Is he forever cultivating the soil and never planting?
Does he not finally plant his seeds, black cumin, cumin wheat, barley, and emmer wheat, each in its proper way, and each in its proper place?
The farmer knows just what to do, for his 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has given him understanding.
A heavy sledge is never used to thresh black cumin; rather, it is beaten with a light stick, a threshing wheel is never rolled on cumin; instead, it is beaten lightly with a flail.
Grain for bread is easily crushed, so he does not keep on pounding it, He threshes it under the wheels of a cart, but he does not pulverize it.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut is a wonderful teacher, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives the farmer great wisdom.
“What sorrow awaits Arial, the City of Daud. Year after year you celebrate your feasts.
Yet I will bring disaster upon you, and there will be much weeping and sorrow, For Yahushalam will become what her name Arial means, an altar covered with blood.
I will be your enemy, surrounding Yahushalam and attacking its walls, I will build siege towers and destroy it.
Then deep from the Arath you will speak; from low in the dust your words will come, Your voice will whisper from the ground like a ghost conjured up from the grave.
“But suddenly, your ruthless enemies will be crushed like the finest of dust, Your many attackers will be driven away like chaff before the wind, Suddenly, in an instant,
I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, will act for you with thunder and earthquake and great noise, with whirlwind and storm and consuming fire.
All the nations fighting against Yahushalam will vanish like a dream! Those who are attacking her walls will vanish like a vision in the night.

A hungry person dreams of eating but wakes up still hungry, A thirsty person dreams of drinking but is still faint from thirst when morning comes, So it will be with your enemies, with those who attack Mount Ziun.”
Are you amazed and incredulous? Do you not believe it? Then go ahead and be blind, you are stupid, but not from wine! You stagger, but not from liquor!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has closed the eyes of your Nabym and visionaries.
All the future events in this vision are like a sealed book to them, When you give it to those who can read, they will say, “We cannot read it because it is sealed.”
When you give it to those who cannot read, they will say, “We do not know how to read.”

And so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar, “These people say they are mine, They honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is false (fake worship) but they are focused on man-made rules, and their fear towards Me is taught by the commandment of men,
Because of this, I will once again astound these hypocrites with amazing wonders, the wisdom of the wise will pass away, and the intelligence of the intelligent will disappear.”
What sorrow awaits those who try to hide their plans from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who do their evil deeds in the dark!“ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH cannot see us,” they say, “He does not know what’s going on!”

How foolish can you be? 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the Potter, and He is certainly greater than you the clay! Should the created thing say of the one who made it, “He didn’t make me”? Does a jar ever say, “The potter who made me is stupid”?
Soon and it will not be very long the forests of Labanun will become a fertile field, and the fertile field will yield bountiful crops.
In that day the deaf will hear words read from a book, and the blind will see through the gloom and darkness.
The humble will be filled with fresh joy from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, The poor will rejoice in the Qadash One of Yashar'AL.
The scoffer will be gone, the arrogant will disappear, and those who plot evil will be killed.
Those who convict the innocent by their false testimony will disappear, A similar fate awaits those who use trickery to pervert justice and who tell lies to destroy the innocent.
That is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who redeemed Abraham, says to the people of Yashar'AL, “My people will no longer be ashamed or turn pale with fear.
For when they see their many children and all the Barakah I have given them, they will recognize the Qadash One of Ya'aqub, They will stand in awe of the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.
Then the wayward will gain understanding, and complainers will accept instruction.
“What sorrow awaits my rebellious children, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, You make plans that are contrary to mine, You make alliances not directed by my RUACH, thus piling up your sins.
For without consulting me, you have gone down to Mitzraym for help, you have put your trust in Pharuh’s protection, You have tried to hide in his shade.
But by trusting Phar'uh, you will be humiliated, and by depending on him, you will be put to shame.
For though his power extends to Zuan and his officials have arrived in Hanes,
all who trust in him will be ashamed, he will not help you. Instead, he will give you to shame.”

This message came to me concerning the animals in the Nagab: The caravan moves slowly across the terrible desert to Mitzraym donkeys weighed down with riches and camels loaded with treasure, all to pay for Mitzraym’s protection, they travel through the wilderness, a place of lionesses and lions, a place where vipers and poisonous snakes live, all this, and Mitzraym will give you nothing in return.
Mitzraym’s promises are worthless Therefore, I call her Rahab the Harmless Dragon.
Now go and write down these words. Write them in a book, they will stand until the end of time as a witness
that these people are stubborn rebels who refuse to pay attention to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s instructions.
They tell the seers, “Stop seeing visions! ”They tell the Nabym, “Do not tell us what is right, Tell us nice things, Tell us lies.
Forget all this gloom, Get off your narrow path, Stop telling us about your Qadash One of Yashar'AL.’”
This is the reply of the Qadash One of Yashar'AL: “Because you despise what I tell you and trust instead in oppression and lies,
calamity will come upon you suddenly like a bulging wall that bursts and falls, In an instant it will collapse and come crashing down.
You will be smashed like a piece of pottery shattered so completely that there will not be a piece big enough to carry coals from a fireplace or a little water from the well.”

This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, the Qadash One of Yashar'AL, says: “Only in returning to me and resting in me will you be saved, In quietness and confidence is your strength, But you would have none of it.
You said, ‘No, we will get our help from Mitzraym, They will give us swift horses for riding into battle. ’But the only swiftness you are going to see is the swiftness of your enemies chasing you!
One of them will chase a thousand of you. Five of them will make all of you flee, You will be left like a lonely flagpole on a hill or a tattered banner on a distant mountaintop.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH must wait for you to come to Him so he can show you His love and compassion, For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is a faithful 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, Baraked are those who wait for the help of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
O people of Ziun, who live in Yahushalam, you will weep no more, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be merciful if you ask for help, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will surely respond to the sound of your cries.
Though 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave you adversity for food and suffering for drink, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will still be with you to teach you, You will see your teacher with your own eyes.
Your own ears will hear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Right behind you a voice will say, “This is the way you should go,” whether to the right or to the left.
Then you will destroy all your silver idols and your precious gold images, You will throw them out like filthy rags, saying to them, “Good riddance!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will barak you with rain at planting time. There will be wonderful harvests and plenty of pastureland for your livestock.
The oxen and donkeys that till the ground will eat good grain, its chaff blown away by the wind.
In that day, when your enemies are slaughtered and the towers fall, there will be streams of water flowing down every mountain and hill.

The moon will be as bright as the sun, and the sun will be seven times brighter like the light of seven days in one! So it will be when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH begins to heal his people and cure the wounds he gave them.
Look! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is coming from far away, burning with anger, surrounded by thick, rising smoke, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH's lips are filled with fury; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH's Dabar consume like fire.
His hot breath pours out like a flood up to the neck of his enemies, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will sift out the proud nations for destruction, He will bridle them and lead them away to ruin.

But the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will sing a song of joy, like the songs at the qadash festivals, You will be filled with joy, as when a flutist leads a group of pilgrimsto Yahushalam, the mountain of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to the Rock of Yashar'AL.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make His majestic voice heard, He will display the strength of his mighty arm, It will descend with devouring flames, with cloudbursts, thunderstorms, and huge hailstones.
At 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command, the Assyrians will be shattered, He will strike them down with His royal scepter.

And as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH strikes them with his rod of punishment, the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will celebrate with tambourines and harps. Lifting the mighty arm of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will fight the Assyrians.
Tuphath the place of burning, has long been ready for the Assyrian king; the pyre is piled high with wood, The breath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, like fire from a volcano, will set it ablaze.

What sorrow awaits those who look to Mitzraym for help, trusting their horses, chariots, and charioteers and depending on the strength of the armies of men instead of looking to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the Qadash One of Yashar'AL.
In his wisdom, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will send great disaster; he will not change his mind, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will rise against the wicked and against their helpers.

For these Mitzraym are mere men, not 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH! Their horses are puny flesh, not Mighty ruach! When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raises His fist against them, those who help will stumble, and those being helped will fall. They will all fall down and die together.

But this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has told me: “When a strong young lion stands growling over a sheep it has killed, it is not frightened by the shouts and noise of a whole crowd of shepherds, In the same way, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will come down and fight on Mount Ziun.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will hover over Yahushalam and protect it like a bird protecting its nest, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will defend and save the city; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will pass over it and rescue it.”
Though you are such wicked rebels, my people, come and return to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
I know the beautiful day will come when each of you will throw away the gold idols and silver images your sinful hands have made.
“The Assyrians will be destroyed, but not by the swords of men, the sword of 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will strike them, and they will panic and flee, The strong young Assyrians will be taken away as captives.
Even the strongest will quake with terror, and princes will flee when they see your battle flags, ”says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, whose fire burns in Ziun, whose flame blazes from Yahushalam.
Look, a righteous king is coming! And honest princes will rule under him.
Each one will be like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in the desert and the shadow of a great rock in a parched land.
Then everyone who has eyes will be able to see the truth, and everyone who has ears will be able to hear it.
Even the hotheads will be full of sense and understanding, Those who stammer will speak out plainly.
In that day unrighteous fools will not be heroes, Scoundrels will not be respected.
For fools speak foolishness and make evil plans, they practice Unrighteousness and spread false teachings about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they deprive the hungry of food and give no water to the thirsty.
The smooth tricks of scoundrels are evil, they plot crooked schemes, they lie to convict the poor, even when the cause of the poor is just.
But generous people plan to do what is generous, and they stand firm in their generosity.
Listen, you women who lie around in ease. Listen to me, you who are so smug.
In a short time just a little more than a year, you careless ones will suddenly begin to care, For your fruit crops will fail, and the harvest will never take place.
Tremble, you women of ease; throw off your complacency, Strip off your pretty clothes, and put on burlap to show your grief.
Beat your breasts in sorrow for your bountiful farms and your fruitful grapevines.
For your land will be overgrown with thorns and briers, Your joyful homes and happy towns will be gone.
The palace and the city will be deserted, and busy towns will be empty, Wild donkeys will frolic and flocks will graze in the empty forts and watchtowers
until at last the RUACH is poured out on us from Shamaym, then the wilderness will become a fertile field, and the fertile field will yield bountiful crops.
Justice will rule in the wilderness and righteousness in the fertile field.
And this righteousness will bring Shalum, Yes it will bring quietness and confidence forever.
My people will live in safety, quietly at home, They will be at rest.
Even if the forest should be destroyed and the city torn down,
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut will greatly barak His people, Wherever they plant seed, bountiful crops will spring up, Their cattle and donkeys will graze freely.

What sorrow awaits you Assyrians, who have destroyed others but have never been destroyed yourselves, You betray others, but you have never been betrayed, When you are done with destroying, you will be destroyed, When you are done betraying, you will be betrayed.
But O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, be merciful to us, for we have waited for you, Be our strong arm each day and our salvation in times of trouble.
The enemy runs at the sound of your Voice, when you stand up, the nations flee!
Just as caterpillars and locusts strip the fields and vines, so the fallen army of Assyria will be stripped!
Though 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is very great and lives in Shamaym, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make Yahushalam His home of justice and righteousness.
In that day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be your sure foundation, providing a rich store of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge, The fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be your treasure.
But now your brave warriors weep in public. Your ambassadors of Shalum cry in bitter disappointment.
Your roads are deserted; no one travels them anymore, The Assyrians have broken their Shalum treaty and care nothing for the promises they made before witnesses, They have no respect for anyone.
The land of Yashar'AL wilts in mourning. Labanun withers with shame, The plain of Sharun is now a wilderness, Bashan and Carmel have been plundered.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “Now I will stand up, Now I will show my power and might.
You Assyrians produce nothing but dry grass and stubble, Your own breath will turn to fire and consume you.
Your people will be burned up completely, like thornbushes cut down and tossed in a fire.
Listen to what I have done, you nations far away! And you that are near, acknowledge my might!”
The sinners in Yahushalam shake with fear. Terror seizes the unrighteous. “Who can live with this devouring fire?” they cry, Who can survive this all-consuming fire?”
Those who are honest and fair, who refuse to profit by fraud, who stay far away from bribes, who refuse to listen to those who plot murder, who shut their eyes to all enticement to do wrong
these are the ones who will dwell on high. The rocks of the mountains will be their fortress. Food will be supplied to them, and they will have water in abundance.
Your eyes will see the king in all his splendor, and you will see a land that stretches into the distance.
You will think back to this time of terror, asking, “Where are the Assyrian officers who counted our towers? Where are the book keepers who recorded the plunder taken from our fallen city?”
You will no longer see these fierce, violent people with their strange, unknown language.
Instead, you will see Ziun as a place of Qadash festivals, You will see Yahushalam, a city quiet and secure, It will be like a tent whose ropes are taut and whose stakes are firmly fixed.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be our Mighty One. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be like a wide river of protection that no enemy can cross, that no enemy ship can sail upon.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is our judge, our law giver, and our Ruler, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will care for us and save us.
The enemies’ sails hang loose on broken masts with useless tackle, Their treasure will be divided by the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Even the lame will take their share!
The people of Yashar'AL will no longer say, “We are sick and helpless,” for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will forgive their sins.
Come here and listen, O nations of the Arath, Let the world and everything in it hear my words.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is enraged against the nations, His fury is against all their armies, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will completely destroy them, dooming them to slaughter.
Their dead will be left unburied, and the stench of rotting bodies will fill the land, The mountains will flow with their blood.
The Shamaym above will melt away and disappear like a rolled-up scroll, the stars will fall from the sky like withered leaves from a grapevine, or shriveled figs from a fig tree.
And when my sword has finished its work in the Shamaym, it will fall upon Adum, the nation I have marked for destruction.
