It may be that the house of Yahudah will hear all the adversities which I purpose to bring upon them, that everyone may turn from his evil way, that I may forgive their iniquity and their sin.”
Then Yaramyahu called Baruch the son of Naryahu; and Baruch wrote on a scroll of a book, at the instruction of Yaramyahu, all the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which He had spoken to him.
And Yaramyahu commanded Baruch, saying, “I am confined, I cannot go into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

You go, therefore, and read from the scroll which you have written at my instruction, the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, in the hearing of the people in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s house on the day of fasting, and you shall also read them in the hearing of all Yahudah who come from their cities.

It may be that they will present their supplication before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and everyone will turn from his evil way, For great is the anger and the fury that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has pronounced against this people.”
And Baruch the son of Naryahu did according to all that Yaramyahu the Nabym commanded him, reading from the book of the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Now it came to pass in the fifth year of Yahuiakim the son of Yusyahu, king of Yahudah, in the ninth month, that they proclaimed a fast before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to all the people in Yahushalam, and to all the people who came from the cities of Yahudah to Yahushalam.

Then Baruch read from the book the words of Yaramyahu in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, in the chamber of Gamaryahu the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entry of the New Gate of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s house, in the hearing of all the people.
When Michayahu the son of Gamaryahu, the son of Shaphan, heard all the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH from the book,

He then went down to the king’s house, into the scribe’s chamber; and there all the princes were sitting, Alishama the scribe, Dalayahu the son of Shamayahu, Alnathan the son of Achbur, Gamaryahu the son of Shaphan, Zadakyahu the son of Hananyahu, and all the princes.
Then Michayahu declared to them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read the book in the hearing of the people.

Therefore all the princes sent Yahudi the son of Nathanyahu, the son of Shalamyahu, the son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, “Take in your hand the scroll from which you have read in the hearing of the people, and come.” So Baruch the son of Naryahu took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
And they said to him, “Sit down now, and read it in our hearing.” So Baruch read it in their hearing.
Now it happened, when they had heard all the words, that they looked in fear from one to another, and said to Baruch, “We will surely tell the king of all these words.”
And they asked Baruch, saying, “Tell us now, how did you write all these words, at Yaramyahu's instruction?”
So Baruch answered them, “he proclaimed with his mouth all these words to me, and I wrote them with ink in the book.”
Then the princes said to Baruch, “Go and hide, you and Yaramyahu; and let no one know where you are.”
And they went to the king, into the court; but they stored the scroll in the chamber of Alishama the scribe, and told all the words in the hearing of the king.

So the king sent Yahudi to bring the scroll, and he took it from Alishama the scribe’s chamber, and Yahudi read it in the hearing of the king and in the hearing of all the princes who stood beside the king.
Now the king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, with a fire burning on the hearth before him.

And it happened, when Yahudi had read three or four columns, that the king cut it with the scribe’s knife and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the scroll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth.
Yet they were not afraid, nor did they tear their garments, the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words.
Nevertheless Alnathan, Dalayahu, and Gamaryahu implored the king not to burn the scroll; but he would not listen to them.
And the king commanded Yarahmaal the king’s son, Sarayahu the son of Azrial, and Shalamyahu the son of Abdaal, to seize Baruch the scribe and Yaramyahu the Nabym, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH hid them.
Now after the king had burned the scroll with the words which Baruch had written at the instruction of Yaramyahu, the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to Yaramyahu, saying:
“Take yet another scroll, and write on it all the former words that were in the first scroll which Yahuiakim the king of Yahudah has burned.

And you shall say to Yahuiakim king of Yahudah, ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: “You have burned this scroll, saying, ‘Why have you written in it that the king of Babylun will certainly come and destroy this land, and cause man and beast to cease from here?’ ”

Therefore thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH concerning Yahuiakim king of Yahudah: “He shall have no one to sit on the throne of Daud, and his dead body shall be cast out to the heat of the day and the frost of the night.

I will punish him, his family, and his servants for their iniquity; and I will bring on them, on the inhabitants of Yahushalam, and on the men of Yahudah all the doom that I have pronounced against them; but they did not heed.” ’ ”

Then Yaramyahu took another scroll and gave it to Baruch the scribe, the son of Naryahu, who wrote on it at the instruction of Yaramyahu all the words of the book which Yahuiakim king of Yahudah had burned in the fire, and besides, there were added to them many similar words.
Now King Zadakyahu the son of Yusyahu reigned instead of Conyahu the son of Yahuiakim, whom Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun made king in the land of Yahudah.
But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land gave heed to the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which He spoke by the Nabym Yaramyahu.
And Zadakyahu the king sent Yahucal the son of Shalamyahu, and Zaphanyahu the son of Maasayahu the Kuhan, to the Nabym Yaramyahu saying, Pray now to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH for us.
Now Yaramyahu was coming and going among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
Then Phar'uh’s army came up from Mitzraym; and when the Chaldaans who were besieging Yahushalam heard news of them, they departed from Yahushalam.
Then the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to the Nabym Yaramyahu saying,

Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, ‘Thus you shall say to the king of Yahudah, who sent you to Me to inquire of Me: “Behold, Phar'uh’s army which has come up to help you will return to Mitzraym, to their own land.
And the Chaldaans shall come back and fight against this city, and take it and burn it with fire.”
Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘do not deceive yourselves, saying, “The Chaldaans will surely depart from us,” for they will not depart.

For though you had defeated the whole army of the Chaldaans who fight against you, and there remained only wounded men among them, they would rise up, every man in his tent, and burn the city with fire.’
And it happened, when the army of the Chaldaans left the siege of Yahushalam for fear of Phar'uh’s army,
that Yaramyahu went out of Yahushalam to go into the land of Banyamin to claim his property there among the people.

And when he was in the Gate of Banyamin, a captain of the guard was there whose name was Iriyahu the son of Shalamyahu, the son of Hananyahu; and he seized Yaramyahu the Nabym, saying, “You are defecting to the Chaldaans!”
Then Yaramyahu said, “False! I am not defecting to the Chaldaans.” But he did not listen to him.
Therefore the princes were angry with Yaramyahu, and they struck him and put him in prison in the house of Yunathan the scribe. For they had made that the prison.
When Yaramyahu entered the dungeon and the cells, and Yaramyahu had remained there many days,

then Zadakyahu the king sent and took him out. The king asked him secretly in his house, and said, “Is there any Dabar from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?” and Yaramyahu said, “There is.” Then he said, “You shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylun!”
Moreover Yaramyahu said to King Zadakyahu, “What offense have I committed against you, against your servants, or against this people, that you have put me in prison?
Where now are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, ‘The king of Babylun will not come against you or against this land’?
Therefore please hear now, O my master the king, Please, let my petition be accepted before you, and do not make me return to the house of Yunathan the scribe, lest I die there.”

Then Zadakyahu the king commanded that they should commit Yaramyahu to the court of the prison, and that they should give him daily a piece of bread from the bakers’ street, until all the bread in the city was gone. Thus Yaramyahu remained in the court of the prison.
Now Shamayahu the son of Mattan, Gadalyahu the son of Pashhur, Yucal the son of Shalamyahu, and Pashhur the son of Malchyahu heard the words that Yaramyahu had spoken to all the people, saying,

“Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘he who remains in this city shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence; but he who goes over to the Chaldaans shall live; his life shall be as a prize to him, and he shall live.’
Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘this city shall surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylun’s army, which shall take it.’ ”

Therefore the princes said to the king, “Please, let this man be put to death, for thus he weakens the hands of the men of war who remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, by speaking such words to them. For this man does not seek the welfare of this people, but their harm.”
Then Zadakyahu the king said, “Look, he is in your hand. For the king can do nothing against you.”

So they took Yaramyahu and cast him into the dungeon of Malchyahu the king’s son, which was in the court of the prison, and they let Yaramyahu down with ropes, And in the dungeon there was no water, but mire. So Yaramyahu sank in the mire.
Now Abad-Malach the Athiupian, one of the eunuchs, who was in the king’s house, heard that they had put Yaramyahu in the dungeon. When the king was sitting at the Gate of Banyamin,
Abad-Malach went out of the king’s house and spoke to the king, saying:

“My master the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Yaramyahu the Nabym, whom they have cast into the dungeon, and he is likely to die from hunger in the place where he is. For there is no more bread in the city.”
Then the king commanded Abad-Malach the Athiupian, saying, “Take from here thirty men with you, and lift Yaramyahu the Nabym out of the dungeon before he dies.”
So Abad-Malach took the men with him and went into the house of the king under the treasury, and took from there old clothes and old rags, and let them down by ropes into the dungeon to Yaramyahu.
Then Abad-Malach said to Yaramyahu, “Please put these old clothes and rags under your armpits, under the ropes.” and Yaramyahu did so.
So they pulled Yaramyahu up with ropes and lifted him out of the dungeon. And Yaramyahu remained in the court of the prison.

Then Zedekiahu the king sent and had Yaramyahu the Nabym brought to him at the third entrance of the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH And the king said to Yaramyahu, “I will ask you something. Hide nothing from me.”
Yaramyahu said to Zadakyahu, “If I declare it to you, will you not surely put me to death? and if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.”

So Zadakyahu the king swore secretly to Yaramyahu, saying, “As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives, who made our very souls, I will not put you to death, nor will I give you into the hand of these men who seek your life.”

Then Yaramyahu said to Zadakyah, “Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL: ‘If you surely surrender to the king of Babylun’s princes, then your soul shall live; this city shall not be burned with fire, and you and your house shall live.
But if you do not surrender to the king of Babylun’s princes, then this city shall be given into the hand of the Chaldaans; they shall burn it with fire, and you shall not escape from their hand.’ ”
And Zadakyahu the king said to Yaramyahu, “I am afraid of the Yahudym who have defected to the Chaldaans, lest they deliver me into their hand, and they abuse me.”
But Yaramyahu said, “they shall not deliver you. Please, obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH which I speak to you, So it shall be well with you, and your soul shall live.
But if you refuse to surrender, this is the Dabar that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has shown me:

‘Now behold, all the women who are left in the king of Yahudah’s house shall be surrendered to the king of Babylun’s princes, and those women shall say: “Your close friends have set upon you and prevailed against you; Your feet have sunk in the mire, and they have turned away again.”

‘So they shall surrender all your wives and children to the Chaldaans, you shall not escape from their hand, but shall be taken by the hand of the king of Babylun, and you shall cause this city to be burned with fire.’ ”
Then Zadakyahu said to Yaramyahu, “Let no one know of these words, and you shall not die.

But if the princes hear that I have talked with you, and they come to you and say to you, ‘Declare to us now what you have said to the king, and also what the king said to you; do not hide it from us, and we will not put you to death,’
then you shall say to them, ‘I presented my request before the king, that he would not make me return to Yunathan’s house to die there.’ ”

Then all the princes came to Yaramyahu and asked him, and he told them according to all these words that the king had commanded, So they stopped speaking with him, for the conversation had not been heard.
Now Yaramyahu remained in the court of the prison until the day that Yahushalam was taken, and he was there when Yahushalam was taken.
In the ninth year of Zadakyahu king of Yahudah, in the tenth month, Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun and all his army came against Yahushalam, and besieged it.
In the eleventh year of Zadakyahu, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was penetrated.

Then all the princes of the king of Babylun came in and sat in the Middle Gate: Nargal-Sharazar, Samgar-Nabu, Sarsachim, Rabsaris, Nargal-Sarazar, Rabmag, with the rest of the princes of the king of Babylun.

So it was, when Zadakyahu the king of Yahudah and all the men of war saw them, that they fled and went out of the city by night, by way of the king’s garden, by the gate between the two walls, and he went out by way of the plain.

But the Chaldaans army pursued them and overtook Zadakyahu in the plains of Yarichu and when they had captured him, they brought him up to Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun, to Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
Then the king of Babylun killed the sons of Zadakyahu before his eyes in Riblah; the king of Babylun also killed all the nobles of Yahudah.
Moreover he put out Zadakyahu’s eyes, and bound him with bronze fetters to carry him off to Babylun.
And the Chaldaans burned the king’s house and the houses of the people with fire, and broke down the walls of Yahushalam.
Then Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive to Babylun the remnant of the people who remained in the city and those who defected to him, with the rest of the people who remained.
But Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard left in the land of Yahudah the poor people, who had nothing, and gave them vineyards and fields at the same time.
Now Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun gave charge concerning Yaramyahu to Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard, saying,
“Take him and look after him, and do him no harm; but do to him just as he says to you.”
So Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard sent Nabushasban, Rabsaris, Nergal-Sharezer, Rabmag, and all the king of Babylun’s chief officers;

then they sent someone to take Yaramyahu from the court of the prison, and committed him to Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, that he should take him home. So he dwelt among the people.
Meanwhile the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had come to Yaramyahu while he was shut up in the court of the prison, saying,

“Go and speak to Abad-Malach the Athiupian, saying, ‘Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH of hosts, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL: “Behold, I will bring My Dabar upon this city for adversity and not for good, and they shall be performed in that day before you.
But I will deliver you in that day,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “and you shall not be given into the hand of the men of whom you are afraid.
For I will surely deliver you, and you shall not fall by the sword; but your life shall be as a prize to you, because you have put your trust in Me,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’ ”

The Dabar that came to Yaramyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH after Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he had taken him bound in chains among all who were carried away captive from Yahushalam and Yahudah, who were carried away captive to Babylun.
And the captain of the guard took Yaramyahu and said to him: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has pronounced this doom on this place.
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought it, and has done just as He said. Because you people have sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and not obeyed His Dabar, therefore this thing has come upon you.

And now look, I free you this day from the chains that were on your hand. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylun, come, and I will look after you. But if it seems wrong for you to come with me to Babylun, remain here. See, all the land is before you; wherever it seems good and convenient for you to go, go there.”

Now while Yaramyahu had not yet gone back, Nabuzaradan said, “Go back to Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylun has made governor over the cities of Yahudah, and dwell with him among the people, Or go wherever it seems convenient for you to go.” So the captain of the guard gave him rations and a gift and let him go.
Then Yaramyahu went to Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, to Mizpah, and dwelt with him among the people who were left in the land.

And when all the captains of the armies who were in the fields, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylun had made Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam governor in the land, and had committed to him men, women, children, and the poorest of the land who had not been carried away captive to Babylun,

then they came to Gadalyahu at Mizpah, Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu, Yuhanan and Yunathan the sons of Karaah, Sarayahu the son of Tanhumath, the sons of Aphai the Natuphathite, and Yazanyahu the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.

And Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, took an oath before them and their men, saying, “Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldaans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylun, and it shall be well with you.

As for me, I will indeed dwell at Mizpah and serve the Chaldaans who come to us. But you, gather wine and summer fruit and oil, put them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken.”

Likewise, when all the Yahudym who were in Muab, among the Ammunites, in Adum, and who were in all the countries, heard that the king of Babylun had left a remnant of Yahudah, and that he had set over them Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan,
then all the Yahudym returned out of all places where they had been driven, and came to the land of Yahudah, to Gadalyahu at Mizpah, and gathered wine and summer fruit in abundance.
Moreover Yuhanan the son of Karaah and all the captains of the forces that were in the fields came to Gadalyahu at Mizpah,
and said to him, “Do you certainly know that Baalis the king of the Ammunites has sent Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu to murder you?” But Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Yuhanan the son of Karaah spoke secretly to Gadalyahu in Mizpah, saying, “Let me go, please, and I will kill Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu, and no one will know it. Why should he murder you, so that all the Yahudym who are gathered to you would be scattered, and the remnant in Yahudah perish?”
But Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam said to Yuhanan the son of Karaah, “You shall not do this thing, for you speak falsely concerning Ishmaal.”

Now it came to pass in the seventh month that Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu, the son of Alishama, of the royal family and of the officers of the king, came with ten men to Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, at Mizpah, and there they ate bread together in Mizpah.

Then Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu, and the ten men who were with him, arose and struck Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, with the sword, and killed him whom the king of Babylun had made governor over the land.
Ishmaal also struck down all the Yahudym who were with him, that is, with Gadalyahu at Mizpah, and the Chaldaans who were found there, the men of war.
And it happened, on the second day after he had killed Gadalyahu, when as yet no one knew it,

that certain men came from Shacham, from Shiluh, and from Samaria, eighty men with their beards shaved and their clothes torn, having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Now Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went along; and it happened as he met them that he said to them, “Come to Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam!”
So it was, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmaal killed them and cast them into the midst of a pit, he and the men who were with him.

But ten men were found among them who said to Ishmaal, “Do not kill us, for we have treasures of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the field.” So he desisted and did not kill them among their brethren.

Now the pit into which Ishmaal had cast all the dead bodies of the men whom he had slain, because of Gadalyahu, was the same one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Yashar'AL. Ishmaal filled it with the slain.

Then Ishmaal carried away captive all the rest of the people who were in Mizpah, the king’s daughters and all the people who remained in Mizpah, whom Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam. And Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu carried them away captive and departed to go over to the Ammunites.
But when Yuhanan the son of Karaah and all the captains of the forces that were with him heard of all the evil that Ishmaal had done,
they took all the men and went to fight with Ishmaal; and they found him by the great pool that is in Gibaun.
So it was, when all the people who were with Ishmaal saw Yuhanan the son of Karaah, and all the captains of the forces who were with him, that they were glad.
Then all the people whom Ishmaal had carried away captive from Mizpah turned around and came back, and went to Yuhanan the son of Karaah.
But Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu escaped from Yuhanan with eight men and went to the Ammunites.

Then Yuhanan, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, took from Mizpah all the rest of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmaal after he had murdered Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, the mighty men of war and the women and the children and the eunuchs, whom he had brought back from Gibaun.
And they departed and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is near Bathlaham, as they went on their way to Mitzraym,
because of the Chaldaans; for they were afraid of them, because Ishmaal the son of Nathanyahu had murdered Gadalyahu the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylun had made governor in the land.
Now all the captains of the forces, Yuhanan the son of Karaah, Yazanyahu the son of Hushayahu, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, came near

and said to Yaramyahu the Nabym, “Please, let our petition be acceptable to you, and pray for us to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, for all this remnant (since we are left but a few of many, as you can see),
that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH may show us the way in which we should walk and the thing we should do.”

Then Yaramyahu the Nabym said to them, “I have heard, Indeed I will pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH according to your words, and it shall be, that whatever 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH answers you, I will declare it to you, I will keep nothing back from you.”
So they said to Yaramyahu, Let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH be a true and faithful witness between us, if we do not do according to everything which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH sends us by you.
Whether it is pleasing or displeasing, we will obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH to whom we send you, that it may be well with us when we obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.”
And it happened after ten days that the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to Yaramyahu.
Then he called Yuhanan the son of Karaah, all the captains of the forces which were with him, and all the people from the least even to the greatest,
and said to them, Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, to whom you sent me to present your petition before Him:
‘If you will still remain in this land, then I will build you and not pull you down, and I will plant you and not pluck you up, For I relent concerning the disaster that I have brought upon you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylun, of whom you are afraid; do not be afraid of him,’ says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, ‘for I am with you, to save you and deliver you from his hand.
And I will show you mercy, that he may have mercy on you and cause you to return to your own land.’
“But if you say, ‘We will not dwell in this land,’ disobeying the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH,
saying, ‘No, but we will go to the land of Mitzraym where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor be hungry for bread, and there we will dwell’
Then hear now the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, O remnant of Yahudah! Thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL: ‘If you wholly set your faces to enter Mitzraym, and go to dwell there,

then it shall be that the sword which you feared shall overtake you there in the land of Mitzraym; the famine of which you were afraid shall follow close after you there in Mitzraym; and there you shall die.

So shall it be with all the men who set their faces to go to Mitzraym to dwell there. They shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence, and none of them shall remain or escape from the disaster that I will bring upon them.’

“For thus says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL: ‘As My anger and My fury have been poured out on the inhabitants of Yahushalam, so will My fury be poured out on you when you enter Mitzraym. And you shall be an oath, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach; and you shall see this place no more.’
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has Dabar concerning you, O remnant of Yahudah, do not go to Mitzraym! Know certainly that I have admonished you this day.

For you were hypocrites in your hearts when you sent me to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, saying, ‘Pray for us to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, and according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH says, so declare to us and we will do it.’
And I have this day declared it to you, but you have not obeyed the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, or anything which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent you by me.
Now therefore, know certainly that you shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence in the place where you desire to go dwell.”
When Yaramyahu had stopped giving the people of Yashar'AL the message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH,
Azaryahu son of Hushayahu and Yuhanan son of Karaah and all the other proud men said to Yaramyahu, “You lie! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has not forbidden us to go to Mitzraym!
Baruch son of Naryahu has convinced you to say this, because he wants us to stay here and be killed by the Babylunians or be carried off into exile.”
So Yuhanan and the other guerrilla leaders and all the people refused to obey 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s command to stay in Yahudah.
Yuhanan and the other leaders took with them all the people who had returned from the nearby countries to which they had fled.
In the crowd were men, women, and children, the king’s daughters, and all those whom Nabuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had left with Gadalyahu, the Nabym Yaramyahu and Baruch were also included.
The people refused to obey the voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and went to Mitzraym, going as far as the city of Tahpanhas.
Then at Tahpanhas, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave another message to Yaramyahu. He said,
“While the people of Yahudah are watching, take some large rocks and bury them under the pavement stones at the entrance of Phar'uh’s palace here in Tahpanhas.

Then say to the people of Yahudah, ‘This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar: I will certainly bring my servant Nabuchadnazzar, king of Babylun, here to Mitzraym, I will set his throne over these stones that I have hidden. He will spread his royal canopy over them.
And when he comes, he will destroy the land of Mitzraym, he will bring death to those destined for death, captivity to those destined for captivity, and war to those destined for war.

He will set fire to the temples of Mitzraym’s idols; he will burn the temples and carry the idols away as plunder. He will pick clean the land of Mitzraym as a shepherd picks fleas from his cloak, and he himself will leave unharmed.
He will break down the sacred pillars standing in the temple of the sun in Mitzraym, and he will burn down the temples of Mitzraym’s idols.
This is the message Yaramyahu received concerning the Yahudym living in northern Mitzraym in the cities of Migdul, Tahpanhas, and Mamphis, and in southern Mitzraym as well:
“This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar: You saw the calamity I brought on Yahushalam and all the towns of Yahudah. They now lie deserted and in ruins.
They provoked my anger with all their wickedness. They burned incense and worshiped other idols, the idols that neither they nor you nor any of your ancestors had ever even known.
“Again and again I sent my servants, the Nabym, to plead with them, ‘Do not do these horrible things that I hate so much.’
But my people would not listen or turn back from their wicked ways. They kept on burning incense to these idols.
And so My fury boiled over and fell like fire on the towns of Yahudah and into the streets of Yahushalam, and they are still a desolate ruin today.

“And now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL asks you: Why are you destroying yourselves? For not one of you will survive, not a man, woman, or child among you who has come here from Yahudah, not even the babies in your arms.

Why provoke my anger by burning incense to the idols you have made here in Mitzraym? You will only destroy yourselves and make yourselves an object of cursing and mockery for all the nations of the Arath.
Have you forgotten the sins of your ancestors, the sins of the kings and queens of Yahudah, and the sins you and your wives committed in Yahudah and Yahushalam?
To this very hour you have shown no remorse or reverence. No one has chosen to follow my Dabar and the decrees I gave to you and your ancestors before you.
“Therefore, this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar: I am determined to destroy every one of you!

I will take this remnant of Yahudah, those who were determined to come here and live in Mitzraym, and I will consume them. They will fall here in Mitzraym, killed by war and famine, all will die from the least to the greatest, they will be an object of damnation, horror, cursing, and mockery.
I will punish them in Mitzraym just as I punished them in Yahushalam, by war, famine, and disease.
Of that remnant who fled to Mitzraym, hoping someday to return to Yahudah, there will be no survivors, even though they long to return home, only a handful will do so.”

Then all the women present and all the men who knew that their wives had burned incense to idols, a great crowd of all the Yahudym living in northern Mitzraym and southern Mitzraym answered Yaramyahu,
“We will not listen to your messages from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!

We will do whatever we want, we will burn incense and pour out liquid offerings to the Queen of sky just as much as we like, just as we, and our ancestors, and our kings and officials have always done in the towns of Yahudah and in the streets of Yahushalam, for in those days we had plenty to eat, and we were well off and had no troubles!
But ever since we quit burning incense to the Queen of sky and stopped worshiping her with liquid offerings, we have been in great trouble and have been dying from war and famine.”

“Besides,” the women added, “do you suppose that we were burning incense and pouring out liquid offerings to the Queen of sky, and making cakes marked with her image, without our husbands knowing it and helping us? Of course not!”
Then Yaramyahu said to all of them, men and women alike, who had given him that answer,

“Do you think 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did not know that you and your ancestors, your kings and officials, and all the people were burning incense to idols in the towns of Yahudah and in the streets of Yahushalam?
It was because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH could no longer bear all the disgusting things you were doing that he made your land an object of cursing, a desolate ruin without inhabitants as it is today.

All these terrible things happened to you because you have burned incense to idols and sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. You have refused to obey 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and have not followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH's instructions, His decrees, and laws.”
Then Yaramyahu said to them all, including the women, “Listen to this message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, all you citizens of Yahudah who live in Mitzraym.

This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar: ‘You and your wives have said, “We will keep our promises to burn incense and pour out liquid offerings to the Queen of sky,” and you have proved by your actions that you meant it. So go ahead and carry out your promises and vows to her!’

“But listen to this message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH all you Yahudym now living in Mitzraym: ‘I have sworn by my great Name,’ says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, ‘that my Name will no longer be spoken by any of the Yahudym in the land of Mitzraym. None of you may invoke my Name or use this oath: “As surely as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH lives.”
For I will watch over you to bring you disaster and not good, everyone from Yahudah who is now living in Mitzraym will suffer war and famine until all of you are dead.
Only a small number will escape death and return to Yahudah from Mitzraym. Then all those who came to Mitzraym will find out whose words are true, mine or theirs!
‘And this is the proof I give you,’ says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, ‘that all I have pronounced will happen to you and that I will punish you here.’

This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: ‘I will turn Phar'uh Huphra, king of Mitzraym, over to his enemies who want to kill him, just as I turned King Zadakyahu of Yahudah over to King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun.’”

The Nabym Yaramyahu gave a message to Baruch son of Naryahu in the fourth year of the reign of Yahuiakim son of Yusyahu, after Baruch had written down everything Yaramyahu had dictated to him, he said,
“This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar to you, Baruch:
You have said, ‘I am overwhelmed with trouble! Have I not had enough pain already? And now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has added more! I am worn out from sighing and can find no rest.’
Baruch, this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: ‘I will destroy this nation that I built, I will uproot what I planted.
Are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not do it! I will bring great disaster upon all these people; but I will give you your life as a reward wherever you go. I, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have spoken!’”
The following messages were given to Yaramyahu the Nabym from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH concerning foreign nations.

This message concerning Mitzraym was given in the fourth year of the reign of Yahuiakim son of Yusyahu, the king of Yahudah, on the occasion of the battle of Carchamish when Phar'uh Naco, king of Mitzraym, and his army were defeated beside the Euphrates River by King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun.
“Prepare your shields, and advance into battle!
Harness the horses, and mount the stallions, take your positions, Put on your helmets, sharpen your spears, and prepare your armor.
But what do I see? The Mitzraym army flees in terror, the bravest of its fighting men run without a backward glance, they are terrorized at every turn, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“The swiftest runners cannot flee; the mightiest warriors cannot escape, by the Euphrates River to the north, they stumble and fall.
“Who is this, rising like the Nile at floodtime, overflowing all the land?
It is the Mitzraym army, overflowing all the land, boasting that it will cover the Arath like a flood, destroying cities and their people.
Charge, you horses and chariots; attack, you mighty warriors of Mitzraym! Come, all you allies from Athiupia, Libyah, and Lydia who are skilled with the shield and bow!

For this is the day of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, a day of vengeance on His enemies, the sword will devour until it is satisfied, yes, until it is drunk with your blood! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, will receive a sacrifice today in the north country beside the Euphrates River.
“Go up to Gilaad to get medicine, O virgin daughter of Mitzraym! But your many treatments will bring you no healing.
The nations have heard of your shame. The Arath is filled with your cries of despair, your mightiest warriors will run into each other and fall down together.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave the Nabym Yaramyahu this message about King Nabuchadnazzar’s plans to attack Mitzraym.
“Shout it out in Mitzraym! Publish it in the cities of Migdul, Mamphis, and Tahpanhas! Mobilize for battle, for the sword will devour everyone around you.
Why have your warriors fallen? They cannot stand, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has knocked them down.
They stumble and fall over each other and say among themselves,‘Come, let us go back to our people, to the land of our birth. Let us get away from the sword of the enemy!’
There they will say, ‘Phar'uh, the king of Mitzraym is a loud mouth who missed his opportunity!’
“As surely as I live,” says the Ruler of all, whose Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, “one is coming against Mitzraym who is as tall as Mount Tabur, or as Mount Carmel by the sea!
Pack up! Get ready to leave for exile, you citizens of Mitzraym! The city of Mamphis will be destroyed, without a single inhabitant.
Mitzraym is as sleek as a beautiful heifer, but a horsefly from the north is on its way!
Mitzraym’s mercenaries have become like fattened calves, they too will turn and run, for it is a day of great disaster for Mitzraym a time of great punishment.
Mitzraym flees, silent as a serpent gliding away, The invading army marches in; they come against her with axes like woodsmen.
They will cut down her people like trees,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “for they are more numerous than locusts.
Mitzraym will be humiliated; she will be handed over to people from the north.”

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar: “I will punish Amun, the idol of Thabas, and all the other idols of Mitzraym. I will punish its rulers and Phar'uh too, and all who trust in him.
I will hand them over to those who want them killed, to King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun and his army. But afterward the land will recover from the ravages of war, I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have spoken!

“But do not be afraid, Ya'aqub my servant; do not be dismayed, Yashar'AL, For I will bring you home again from distant lands, and your children will return from their exile, Yashar'AL will return to a life of Shalum and quiet, and no one will terrorize them.

Do not be afraid Ya'aqub my servant, for I am with you says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “I will completely destroy the nations to which I have exiled you, but I will not completely destroy you, I will discipline you, but with justice; I cannot let you go unpunished.”
This is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s message to the Nabym Yaramyahu concerning the Philistines of Gaza, before it was captured by the Mitzraym army.

This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “A flood is coming from the north to overflow the land, It will destroy the land and everything in it cities and people alike, people will scream in terror, and everyone in the land will wail.
Hear the clatter of stallions’ hooves and the rumble of wheels as the chariots rush by, terrified fathers run madly, without a backward glance at their helpless children.

“The time has come for the Philistines to be destroyed, along with their allies from Tyra and Sidun, yes 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is destroying the remnant of the Philistines, those colonists from the island of Crata.
Gaza will be humiliated, its head shaved bald; Ashkalun will lie silent, you remnant from the Maditerranaan coast, how long will you cut yourselves in mourning?
“Now, O sword of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, when will you be at rest again? Go back into your sheath; rest and be still.
“But how can it be still when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent it on a mission? For the city of Ashkalun and the people living along the sea must be destroyed.”

This message was given concerning Muab. This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar: “What sorrow awaits the city of Nabu; it will soon lie in ruins, the city of Kiriathaim will be humiliated and captured; the fortress will be humiliated and broken down.

No one will ever brag about Muab again, for in Hashbun there is a plot to destroy her.‘ Come,’ they say, ‘we will cut her off from being a nation.’ The town of Mad men too, it will be silenced; the sword will follow you there.
Listen to the cries from Hurunaim, cries of devastation and great destruction.
All Muab is destroyed, Her little ones will cry out.
Her refugees weep bitterly, climbing the slope to Luhith, they cry out in terror, descending the slope to Hurunaim.
Flee for your lives! Hide in the wilderness!
Because you have trusted in your wealth and skill, you will be taken captive, your idol Chamush, with his priests and officials, will be hauled off to distant lands!
“All the towns will be destroyed, and no one will escape, either on the plateaus or in the valleys, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has spoken.
Oh, that Muab had wings so she could fly away, for her towns will be left empty, with no one living in them.
Cursed are those who refuse to do 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s work, who hold back their swords from shedding blood!

“From his earliest history, Muab has lived in Shalum, never going into exile, he is like wine that has been allowed to settle, he has not been poured from flask to flask, and he is now fragrant and smooth.
But the time is coming soon,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH “when I will send men to pour him from his jar, they will pour him out, then shatter the jar!
At last Muab will be ashamed of his idol Chamush, as the people of Yashar'AL were ashamed of their gold calf at Bathal.
“You used to boast, ‘We are heroes, mighty men of war.’
But now Muab and his towns will be destroyed, his most promising youth are doomed to slaughter,” says the Ruler of all, whose Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
“Destruction is coming fast for Muab; calamity threatens ominously.
You friends of Muab, weep for him and cry! See how the strong scepter is broken, how the beautiful staff is shattered!
“Come down from your Kabad and sit in the dust, you people of Dibun, for those who destroy Muab will shatter Dibun too, they will tear down all your towers.
You people of Aruar, stand beside the road and watch, shout to those who flee from Muab, ‘What has happened there?’
“And the reply comes back, Muab lies in ruins and shame; weep and wail! Tell it by the banks of the Arnun River: Muab has been destroyed!’
Judgment has been poured out on the towns of the plataau, on Hulun and Yahaz and Maphaath,
on Dibun and Nabu and Bath-diblathaim,
on Kiriathaim and Bath-gamul and Bath-maun,
on Kariuth and Buzrah, all the towns of Muab, far and near.
“The strength of Muab has ended, his arm has been broken,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Let him stagger and fall like a drunkard, for he has rebelled against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Muab will wallow in his own vomit, ridiculed by all.
Did you not ridicule the people of Yashar'AL? Were they caught in the company of thieves that you should despise them as you do?
“You people of Muab, flee from your towns and live in the caves, Hide like doves that nest in the clefts of the rocks.
We have all heard of the pride of Muab, for his pride is very great, we know of his lofty pride, his arrogance, and his haughty heart.
I know about his insolence,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “but his boasts are empty, as empty as his deeds.
So now I wail for Muab; yes, I will mourn for Muab, My heart is broken for the men of Kir-harasath.

“You people of Sibmah, rich in vineyards, I will weep for you even more than I did for Yazar, your spreading vines once reached as far as the Dead Sea, but the destroyer has stripped you bare! He has harvested your grapes and summer fruits.
Joy and gladness are gone from fruitful Muab, The presses yield no wine, no one treads the grapes with shouts of joy, There is shouting, yes, but not of joy.

“Instead, their awful cries of terror can be heard from Hashbun clear across to Alaalah and Yahaz; from Zuar all the way to Hurunaim and Aglath-shalishiyah, Even the waters of Nimrim are dried up now.
“I will put an end to Muab,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “for the people offer sacrifices at the pagan shrines and burn incense to their false idols.
My heart moans like a flute for Muab and Kir-harasath, for all their wealth has disappeared.
The people shave their heads and beards in mourning. They slash their hands and put on clothes made of burlap.
There is crying and sorrow in every Muabite home and on every street. For I have smashed Muab like an old, unwanted jar.
How it is shattered! Hear the wailing! See the shame of Muab! It has become an object of ridicule, an example of ruin to all its neighbors.”
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “Look! The enemy swoops down like an eagle, spreading his wings over Muab.
Its cities will fall, and its strongholds will be seized, even the mightiest warriors will be in anguish like a woman in labor.
Muab will no longer be a nation, for it has boasted against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Terror and traps and snares will be your lot, O Muab,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

“Those who flee in terror will fall into a trap, and those who escape the trap will step into a snare, I will see to it that you do not get away, for the time of your judgment has come,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“The people flee as far as Hashbun but are unable to go on, for a fire comes from Hashbun, King Sihun’s ancient home, to devour the entire land with all its rebellious people.
“What sorrow awaits you, O people of Muab! The people of the idol Chamush are destroyed! Your sons and your daughters have been taken away as captives.
But I will restore the fortunes of Muab in days to come, I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have spoken!”

This message was given concerning the Ammunites. This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “Are there no descendants of Yashar'AL to inherit the land of Gad? Why are you, who worship Mulach, living in its towns?

In the days to come,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “I will sound the battle cry against your city of Rabbah, It will become a desolate heap of ruins, and the neighboring towns will be burned, then Yashar'AL will take back the land you took from her,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

“Cry out, O Hashbun, for the town of Ai is destroyed, Weep O people of Rabbah! Put on your clothes of mourning, Weep and wail, hiding in the hedges, for your idol Mulach, with his priests and officials, will be hauled off to distant lands.
You are proud of your fertile valleys, but they will soon be ruined, you trusted in your wealth, you rebellious daughter, and thought no one could ever harm you.
But look! I will bring terror upon you,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut. “Your neighbors will chase you from your land, and no one will help your exiles as they flee.
But I will restore the fortunes of the Ammunites in days to come, I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have spoken.”
This message was given concerning Adum. This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Dabar: “Is there no wisdom in Taman? Is no one left to give wise counsel?
Turn and flee! Hide in deep caves, you people of Dadan! For when I bring disaster on Adum, I will punish you, too!
Those who harvest grapes always leave a few for the poor, If thieves came at night, they would not take everything.
But I will strip bare the land of Adum, and there will be no place left to hide, Its children, its brothers, and its neighbors will all be destroyed, and Adum itself will be no more.
But I will protect the orphans who remain among you, Your widows too, can depend on me for help.”
And this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “If the innocent must suffer, how much more must you! You will not go unpunished! You must drink this cup of judgment!

For I have sworn by my own Name,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “that Buzrah will become an object of horror and a heap of ruins; it will be mocked and cursed, all its towns and villages will be desolate forever.”
I have heard a message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that an ambassador was sent to the nations to say, “Form a coalition against Adum, and prepare for battle!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Adum,“I will cut you down to size among the nations. You will be despised by all.

You have been deceived by the fear you inspire in others and by your own pride, you live in a rock fortress and control the mountain heights, but even if you make your nest among the peaks with the eagles, I will bring you crashing down,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Adum will be an object of horror, all who pass by will be appalled and will gasp at the destruction they see there.
It will be like the destruction of Sudum and Gumurrah and their neighboring towns,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. “No one will live there; no one will inhabit it.

I will come like a lion from the thickets of the Yurdan, leaping on the sheep in the pasture, I will chase Adum from its land, and I will appoint the leader of my choice, For who is like me, and who can challenge me? What ruler can oppose my will?”
Listen to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s plans against Adum and the people of Taman, even the little children will be dragged off like sheep, and their homes will be destroyed.
The Arath will shake with the noise of Adum’s fall, and its cry of despair will be heard all the way to the Red Sea.
Look! The enemy swoops down like an eagle, spreading his wings over Buzrah, Even the mightiest warriors will be in anguish like a woman in labor.

This message was given concerning Damascus, This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar “The towns of Hamath and Arpad are struck with fear, for they have heard the news of their destruction, their hearts are troubled like a wild sea in a raging storm.
Damascus has become feeble, and all her people turn to flee, fear, anguish, and pain have gripped her as they grip a woman in labor.
That famous city, a city of joy, will be forsaken!
Her young men will fall in the streets and die, Her soldiers will all be killed,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
“And I will set fire to the walls of Damascus that will burn up the palaces of Ban-hadad.”

This message was given concerning Kadar and the kingdoms of Hazur, which were attacked by King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun. This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “Advance against Kadar! Destroy the warriors from the East!
Their flocks and tents will be captured, and their household goods and camels will be taken away, Everywhere shouts of panic will be heard: ‘We are terrorized at every turn!’
Run for your lives,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Hide yourselves in deep caves, you people of Hazur, for King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun has plotted against you and is preparing to destroy you.
“Go up and attack that complacent nation,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Its people live alone in the desert without walls or gates.
Their camels and other livestock will all be yours, I will scatter to the winds these people who live in remote places, I will bring calamity upon them from every direction,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Hazur will be inhabited by jackals, and it will be desolate forever, no one will live there; no one will inhabit it.”
This message concerning Alam came to the Nabym Yaramyahu from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at the beginning of the reign of King Zadakyahu of Yahudah.
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Dabar: “I will destroy the archers of Alam, the best of their forces.
I will bring enemies from all directions, and I will scatter the people of Alam to the four winds, they will be exiled to countries around the world.

I myself will go with Alam’s enemies to shatter it, In my fierce anger, I will bring great disaster upon the people of Alam,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “Their enemies will chase them with the sword until I have destroyed them completely.
I will set my throne in Alam,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “and I will destroy its king and officials.
But I will restore the fortunes of Alam in days to come, I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have spoken!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave Yaramyahu the Nabym this message concerning Babylun and the land of the Babylunians.

This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “Tell the whole world, and keep nothing back, raise a signal flag to tell everyone that Babylun will fall! her images and idols will be shattered, her deity Bal and Marduk will be utterly put to shame.
For a nation will attack her from the north and bring such destruction that no one will live there again, Everything will be gone; both people and animals will flee.
In those coming days, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “the people of Yashar'AL will return home together with the people of Yahudah, they will come weeping and seeking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
They will ask the way to Yahushalam and will start back home again, they will bind themselves to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with an eternal covenant that will never be forgotten.
“My people have been lost sheep, their shepherds have led them astray and turned them loose in the mountains, they have lost their way and cannot remember how to get back to the sheepfold.
All who found them devoured them, Their enemies said, ‘We did nothing wrong in attacking them, for they sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their true place of rest, and the hope of their ancestors.’
“But now, flee from Babylun! Leave the land of the Babylunians, Like male goats at the head of the flock, lead my people home again.
For I am raising up an army of great nations from the north, they will join forces to attack Babylun, and she will be captured the enemies’ arrows will go straight to the mark; they will not miss!
Babylunia will be looted until the attackers are glutted with loot, I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have spoken!
“You rejoice and are glad, you who plundered my chosen people, you frisk about like a calf in a meadow and neigh like a stallion.
But your homeland will be overwhelmed with shame and dishonor, You will become the least of nations, a wilderness, a dry and desolate land.
Because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s anger, Babylun will become a deserted wasteland, all who pass by will be horrified and will gasp at the destruction they see there.
“Yes, prepare to attack Babylun, all you surrounding nations, let your archers shoot at her; spare no arrows, for she has sinned against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Shout war cries against her from every side, Look! She surrenders! Her walls have fallen, It is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s vengeance, so take vengeance on her, do to her as she has done to others!
Take from Babylun all those who plant crops; send all the harvesters away, because of the sword of the enemy, everyone will run away and rush back to their own lands.
“The Yashar'AL are like sheep that have been scattered by lions, first the king of Assyria ate them up, then King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun cracked their bones.”
Therefore, this is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, Dabar: “Now I will punish the king of Babylun and his land, just as I punished the king of Assyria.
And I will bring Yashar'AL home again to its own land, to feed in the fields of Carmel and Bashan, and to be satisfied once more in the hill country of Aphraim and Gilaad.
In those days,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “no sin will be found in Yashar'AL or in Yahudah for I will forgive the remnant I preserve.
“Go up, my warriors, against the land of Marathaim and against the people of Pakud, pursue, kill, and completely destroy them, as I have commanded you,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Let the battle cry be heard in the land, a shout of great destruction.
Babylun, the mightiest hammer in all the Arath, lies broken and shattered, Babylun is desolate among the nations!
Listen, Babylun, for I have set a trap for you, and you are caught in it, for you have fought against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has opened His armory and brought out weapons to vent His fury, the terror that falls upon the Babylunians will be the work of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.
Yes, come against her from distant lands. Break open her granaries, crush her walls and houses into heaps of rubble, Destroy her completely, and leave nothing!
Destroy even her young bulls, it will be terrible for them too! Slaughter them all! For Babylun’s day of reckoning has come.
Listen to the people who have escaped from Babylun, as they tell in Yahushalam how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has taken vengeance against those who destroyed his Temple.
“Send out a call for archers to come to Babylun, Surround the city so none can escape, do to her as she has done to others, for she has defied 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the Qadash One of Yashar'AL.
Her young men will fall in the streets and die, Her soldiers will all be killed,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“See, I am your enemy, you arrogant people,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Tsaba'ut. “Your day of reckoning has arrived, the day when I will punish you.
O land of arrogance, you will stumble and fall, and no one will raise you up, for I will light a fire in the cities of Babylun that will burn up everything around them.”
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Dabar: “The people of Yashar'AL and Yahudah have been wronged, Their captors hold them and refuse to let them go.
But the one who redeems them is strong. His Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will defend them and give them rest again in Yashar'AL, but for the people of Babylun there will be no rest!
“The sword of destruction will strike the Babylunians,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “It will strike the people of Babylun, her officials and wise men, too.
The sword will strike her wise counselors, and they will become fools, the sword will strike her mightiest warriors, and panic will seize them.
The sword will strike her horses and chariots and her allies from other lands, and they will all become like women, the sword will strike her treasures, and they all will be plundered.
A drought will strike her water supply, causing it to dry up, and why? Because the whole land is filled with idols, and the people are madly in love with the idols.
“Soon Babylun will be inhabited by desert animals and hyenas, It will be a home for owls, never again will people live there; it will lie desolate forever.
I will destroy it as I destroyed Sudum and Gumurrah and their neighboring towns,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “No one will live there; no one will inhabit it.
“Look! A great army is coming from the north, a great nation and many kings are rising against you from far-off lands.

They are armed with bows and spears. They are cruel and show no mercy, as they ride forward on horses, they sound like a roaring sea, they are coming in battle formation, planning to destroy you Babylun.
The king of Babylun has heard reports about the enemy, and he is weak with fright, Pangs of anguish have gripped him, like those of a woman in labor.

“I will come like a lion from the thickets of the Yurdan, leaping on the sheep in the pasture, I will chase Babylun from its land, and I will appoint the leader of my choice, For who is like me? and who can challenge me? What ruler can oppose my will?”
Listen to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s plans against Babylun and the land of the Babylunians, even the little children will be dragged off like sheep, and their homes will be destroyed.
The Arath will shake with the shout, “Babylun has been taken!” and its cry of despair will be heard around the world.
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar: “I will stir up a destroyer against Babylun and the people of Babylunia.
Foreigners will come and winnow her, blowing her away as chaff, they will come from every side to rise against her in her day of trouble.
Do not let the archers put on their armor or draw their bows, do not spare even her best soldiers! Let her army be completely destroyed.
They will fall dead in the land of the Babylunians, slashed to death in her streets.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has not abandoned Yashar'AL and Yahudah, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is still their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, even though their land was filled with sin against the Qadash One of Yashar'AL.”
Flee from Babylun! Save yourselves! Do not get trapped in her punishment! It is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s time for vengeance; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will repay her in full.
Babylun has been a gold cup in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s hands, a cup that made the whole Arath drunk, the nations drank Babylun’s wine, and it drove them all mad.
But suddenly Babylun too, has fallen. Weep for her, Give her medicine, Perhaps she can yet be healed.

We would have helped her if we could, but nothing can save her now, Let her go; abandon her, Return now to your own land, For her punishment reaches to the Shamaym; it is so great it cannot be measured.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has vindicated us. Come, let us announce in Yahushalam everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH has done.

Sharpen the arrows! Lift up the shields! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has inspired the kings of the Madas to march against Babylun and destroy her, this is his vengeance against those who desecrated the temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Raise the battle flag against Babylun! Reinforce the guard and station the watchmen, Prepare an ambush, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will fulfill all his plans against Babylun.
You are a city by a great river, a great center of commerce, but your end has come. The thread of your life is cut.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut has taken this vow and has sworn to it by his own Name: “Your cities will be filled with enemies, like fields swarming with locusts, and they will shout in triumph over you.”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made the Arath by His power, and He preserves it by His wisdom, With His own understanding 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH stretched out the Shamaym.

When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH speaks in the thunder, the Shamaym roar with rain, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH causes the clouds to rise over the Arath, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sends the lightning with the rain and releases the wind from his storehouses.
The whole race of men is foolish and has no knowledge! The craftsmen are put to shame by the idols they make, for their carefully shaped works are a fraud, these idols have no breath or power.
Idols are worthless; they are ridiculous lies! On the day of reckoning they will all be destroyed.
But the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL is no idol! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the Creator of everything that exists, including His people, His own special possession, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut is His Name!
“You are my battle-ax and sword,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. “With you I will shatter nations and destroy many kingdoms.
With you I will shatter armies, destroying the horse and rider, the chariot and charioteer.
With you I will shatter men and women, old people and children, young men and young women.
With you I will shatter shepherds and flocks farmers and oxen, captains and officers.
“I will repay Babylun and the people of Babylunia for all the wrong they have done to my people in Yahushalam,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

“Look, O mighty mountain, destroyer of the Arath! I am your enemy,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “I will raise my fist against you, to knock you down from the heights, When I am finished, you will be nothing but a heap of burnt rubble.
You will be desolate forever, Even your stones will never again be used for building, You will be completely wiped out,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Raise a signal flag to the nations, Sound the battle cry! Mobilize them all against Babylun, Prepare them to fight against her! Bring out the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkanaz. Appoint a commander, and bring a multitude of horses like swarming locusts!
Bring against her the armies of the nations led by the kings of the Madas and all their captains and officers.
The Arath trembles and writhes in pain, for everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has planned against Babylun stands unchanged, Babylun will be left desolate without a single inhabitant.
Her mightiest warriors no longer fight, they stay in their barracks, their courage gone. They have become like women, the invaders have burned the houses and broken down the city gates.
The news is passed from one runner to the next as the messengers hurry to tell the king that his city has been captured.
All the escape routes are blocked, The marshes have been set aflame, and the army is in a panic.
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL Dabar: “Babylun is like wheat on a threshing floor, about to be trampled, In just a little while her harvest will begin.”

“King Nabuchadnazzar of Babylun has eaten and crushed us and drained us of strength, he has swallowed us like a great monster and filled his belly with our riches, he has thrown us out of our own country.
Make Babylun suffer as she made us suffer,” say the people of Ziun, “Make the people of Babylunia pay for spilling our blood,” says Yahushalam.
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Yahushalam: “I will be your lawyer to plead your case, and I will avenge you, I will dry up her river, as well as her springs,
and Babylun will become a heap of ruins, haunted by jackals, She will be an object of horror and contempt, a place where no one lives.
Her people will roar together like strong lions, they will growl like lion cubs.

And while they lie inflamed with all their wine, I will prepare a different kind of feast for them, I will make them drink until they fall asleep, and they will never wake up again,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams and goats to be sacrificed.
“How Babylun is fallen, great Babylun, praised throughout the Arath! Now she has become an object of horror among the nations.
The sea has risen over Babylun; she is covered by its crashing waves.
Her cities now lie in ruins; she is a dry wasteland where no one lives or even passes by.
And I will punish Bal, the idol deity of Babylun, and make him vomit up all he has eaten, the nations will no longer come and worship Bal, the wall of Babylun has fallen!
“Come out, my people, flee from Babylun. Save yourselves! Run from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s fierce anger.

But do not panic; do not be afraid when you hear the first rumor of approaching forces. For rumors will keep coming year by year, violence will erupt in the land as the leaders fight against each other.
For the time is surely coming when I will punish this great city and all her idols, her whole land will be put to shame and her dead will lie in the streets.
Then the Shamaym and Arath will rejoice, for out of the north will come destroying armies against Babylun, says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Just as Babylun killed the people of Yashar'AL and others throughout the world, so must her people be killed.
Get out, all you who have escaped the sword! Do not stand and watch, flee while you can! remember 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, though you are in a far-off land, and think about your home in Yahushalam.”
“We are ashamed,” the people say, “We are insulted and dishonored because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple has been defiled by foreigners.”
“Yes,” says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “but the time is coming when I will destroy Babylun’s idols, the groans of her wounded people will be heard throughout the land.
Though Babylun reaches as high as the Shamaym and makes her fortifications incredibly strong, I will still send enemies to plunder her, I 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH have spoken!
“Listen! Hear the cry of Babylun, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Babylunians.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is destroying Babylun. He will silence her loud voice, Waves of enemies pound against her; the noise of battle rings through the city.

Destroying armies come against Babylun. Her mighty men are captured, and their weapons break in their hands, For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is an 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who gives just punishment; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH always repays in full.

I will make her officials and wise men drunk, along with her captains, officers, and warriors, They will fall asleep and never wake up again! ”says the Ruler of all, whose name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut.

This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut Dabar: “The thick walls of Babylun will be leveled to the ground, and her massive gates will be burned, The builders from many lands have worked in vain, for their work will be destroyed by fire!”

The Nabym Yaramyahu gave this message to Sarayahu son of Naryahu and grandson of Maasayahu, a staff officer, when Sarayahu went to Babylun with King Zadakyahu of Yahudah. This was during the fourth year of Zadakyahu’s reign.
Yaramyahu had recorded on a scroll all the terrible disasters that would soon come upon Babylun, all the words written here.
Yaramyahu said to Sarayahu, “When you get to Babylun, read aloud everything on this scroll.
Then say, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you have said that you will destroy Babylun so that neither people nor animals will remain here, She will lie empty and abandoned forever.’
When you have finished reading the scroll, tie it to a stone and throw it into the Euphrates River.
Then say, ‘In this same way Babylun and her people will sink, never again to rise, because of the disasters I will bring upon her.’ This is the end of Yaramyahu’s messages.
Zadakyahu was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Yahushalam. His mother’s name was Hamutal the daughter of Yaramyahu of Libnah.
Zadakyahu also did evil in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, according to all that Yahuiakim had done.
For because of the anger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH this happened in Yahushalam and Yahudah, till 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH finally cast them out from His presence, then Zadakyahu rebelled against the king of Babylun.

Now it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun and all his army came against Yahushalam and encamped against it; and they built a siege wall against it all around.
So the city was besieged until the eleventh year of King Zadakyahu.
By the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine had become so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land.

Then the city wall was broken through, and all the men of war fled and went out of the city at night by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden, even though the Chaldaans were near the city all around, and they went by way of the plain.
But the army of the Chaldaans pursued the king, and they overtook Zadakyahu in the plains of Yarichu, all his army was scattered from him.
So they took the king and brought him up to the king of Babylun at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgment on him.
Then the king of Babylun killed the sons of Zadakyahu before his eyes, and he killed all the princes of Yahudah in Riblah.
He also put out the eyes of Zadakyahu; and the king of Babylun bound him in bronze fetters, took him to Babylun, and put him in prison till the day of his death.

Now in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month (which was the nineteenth year of King Nabuchadnazzar king of Babylun), Nabuzaradan, the captain of the guard, who served the king of Babylun, came to Yahushalam.
He burned the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the king’s house; all the houses of Yahushalam, that is, all the houses of the great, he burned with fire.
And all the army of the Chaldaans who were with the captain of the guard broke down all the walls of Yahushalam all around.

Then Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive some of the poor people, the rest of the people who remained in the city, the defectors who had deserted to the king of Babylun, and the rest of the craftsmen.
But Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard left some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and farmers.

The bronze pillars that were in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the carts and the bronze Sea that were in the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the Chaldaans broke in pieces, and carried all their bronze to Babylun.
They also took away the pots, the shovels, the trimmers, the bowls, the spoons, and all the bronze utensils with which the Kuhanym ministered.
The basins, the firepans, the bowls, the pots, the lampstands, the spoons, and the cups, whatever was solid gold and whatever was solid silver, the captain of the guard took away.
The two pillars, one Sea, the twelve bronze bulls which were under it, and the carts, which King Shalumah had made for the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the bronze of all these articles was beyond measure.
Now concerning the pillars: the height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, a measuring line of twelve cubits could measure its circumference, and its thickness was four fingers; it was hollow.
A capital of bronze was on it; and the height of one capital was five cubits, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar, with pomegranates was the same.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; all the pomegranates, all around on the network, were one hundred.
The captain of the guard took Serayahu the chief Kuhan, Zaphanyahu the second Kuhan, and the three doorkeepers.

He also took out of the city an officer who had charge of the men of war, seven men of the king’s close associates who were found in the city, the principal scribe of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
And Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard took these and brought them to the king of Babylun at Riblah.
Then the king of Babylun struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath, Thus Yahudah was carried away captive from its own land.
These are the people whom Nabuchadnazzar carried away captive: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Yahudym;
in the eighteenth year of Nabuchadnazzar he carried away captive from Yahushalam eight hundred and thirty-two persons;

in the twenty-third year of Nabuchadnazzar, Nabuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive of the Yahudym seven hundred and forty-five persons, all the persons were four thousand six hundred.

Now it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Yahuiachin king of Yahudah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, that Ávil-Merudach king of Babylun, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Yahuiachin king of Yahudah and brought him out of prison.
And he spoke kindly to him and gave him a more prominent seat than those of the kings who were with him in Babylun.
So Yahuiachin changed from his prison garments, and he ate bread regularly before the king all the days of his life.
And as for his provisions, there was a regular ration given him by the king of Babylun, a portion for each day until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

books.name: Lamentations
chapters: Yahushalam, once so full of people, is now deserted, She who was once great among the nations now sits alone like a widow, Once the queen of all the Arath, she is now a slave.
She sobs through the night; tears stream down her cheeks, among all her lovers, there is no one left to comfort her, all her friends have betrayed her and become her enemies.
Yahudah has been led away into captivity, oppressed with cruel slavery, She lives among foreign nations and has no place of rest, her enemies have chased her down, and she has nowhere to turn.
The roads to Yahushalam are in mourning, for crowds no longer come to celebrate the festivals, the city gates are silent, her Kuhanym groan, her young women are crying, how bitter is her fate!
Her oppressors have become her masters, and her enemies prosper, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has punished Yahushalam for her many sins, her children have been captured and taken away to distant lands.
All the majesty of beautiful Yahushalam has been stripped away, her princes are like starving deer searching for pasture, they are too weak to run from the pursuing enemy.

In the midst of her sadness and wandering, Yahushalam remembers her ancient splendor, but now she has fallen to her enemy, and there is no one to help her, for her enemy struck her down and laughed as she fell.

Yahushalam has sinned greatly, so she has been tossed away like a filthy rag, all who once honored her now despise her, for they have seen her stripped naked and humiliated, all she can do is groan and hide her face.
She defiled herself with immorality and gave no thought to her future, now she lies in the gutter with no one to lift her out, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, see my misery,” she cries, the enemy has triumphed.”
The enemy has plundered her completely, taking every precious thing she owns, she has seen foreigners violate her sacred Temple, the place 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had forbidden them to enter.
Her people groan as they search for bread, they have sold their treasures for food to stay alive, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, look,” she mourns, “and see how I am despised.
“Does it mean nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look around and see if there is any suffering like mine, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought on me when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH erupted in fierce anger.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent fire from Shamaym that burns in my bones, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has placed a trap in my path and turned me back, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has left me devastated, racked with sickness all day long.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH wove my sins into ropes to hitch me to a yoke of captivity. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sapped my strength and turned me over to my enemies; I am helpless in their hands.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has treated my mighty men with contempt, at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH command a great army has come to crush my young warriors, He has trampled His beloved city like grapes are trampled in a winepress.
“For all these things I weep; tears flow down my cheeks, no one is here to comfort me; anyone who might encourage me are far away, my children have no future, for the enemy has conquered us.”
Yahushalam reaches out for help, but no one comforts her, regarding His people Yashar'AL, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has Dabar, “Let their neighbors be their enemies! Let them be thrown away like a filthy rag!”

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is right,” Yahushalam says, “for I rebelled against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Listen people everywhere; look upon my anguish and despair, for my sons and daughters have been taken captive to distant lands.
“I begged my allies for help, but they betrayed me, My Kuhanym and leaders starved to death in the city, even as they searched for food to save their lives.
“O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, see my anguish! My heart is broken and my soul despairs, for I have rebelled against you, In the streets the sword kills, and at home there is only death.

“Others heard my groans, but no one turned to comfort me, when my enemies heard about my troubles, they were happy to see what you had done, Oh, bring the day you promised, when they will suffer as I have suffered.
Look at all their evil deeds, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Punish them, as you have punished me for all my sins, my groans are many, and I am sick at heart.”

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in his anger has cast a dark shadow over beautiful Yahushalam, The fairest of Yashar'AL’s cities lies in the dust, thrown down from the heights of Shamaym, in his day of great anger, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has shown no mercy even to his Temple.

Without mercy 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has destroyed every home in Yashar'AL, in His anger 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has broken down the fortress walls of beautiful Yahushalam, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought them to the ground, dishonoring the kingdom and its rulers.

All the strength of Yashar'AL vanishes beneath His fierce anger, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has withdrawn His protection as the enemy attacks, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH consumes the whole land of Yashar'AL like a raging fire.
