“The kingdom of Shamaym is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again, and then in his joy went and sold all he had and bought that field.
“Again, the kingdom of Shamaym is like a merchant looking for fine pearls.
When he found one of great value, he went away and sold everything he had and bought it.
“Once again, the kingdom of Shamaym is like a net that was let down into the lake and caught all kinds of fish.
When it was full, the fishermen pulled it up on the shore. Then they sat down and collected the good fish in baskets, but threw the bad away.
This is how it will be at the end of the age. The Malakym will come and separate the wicked from the righteous
and throw them into the blazing furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
“Have you understood all these things?” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “Yes,” they replied.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Therefore every teacher of the law who has become a disciple in the kingdom of Shamaym is like the owner of a house who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old.”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had finished these parables, he moved on from there.
Coming to His hometown, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began teaching the people in their congregation, and they were amazed. “Where did this man get this wisdom and these miraculous powers?” they asked.
“Is this not the carpenter’s son? Is His mother’s name not Maryam, and are his brothers not Ya'aqub, Ya'asaf, Simun and Yudas?
Are all his sisters not with us? Where then did this man get all these things?”
And they took offense at Him, But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “A Nabym is honored everywhere, except in his own town and in his own home.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA did not do many miracles there because of their lack of Amunah (faith).
When Harud Antipas, the ruler of Galily, heard about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA,
he said to his advisers, “This must be Yahukanun the Baptist raised from the dead! That is why he can do such miracles.”
For Harud had arrested and imprisoned Yahukanun as a favor to his wife Harudias (the former wife of Harud’s brother Philip).
Yahukanun had been telling Harud, “It is against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s law for you to marry her.”
Harud wanted to kill Yahukanun, but he was afraid of a riot, because all the people believed Yahukanun was a Nabym.
But at a birthday party for Harud, Harudias’s daughter performed a dance that greatly pleased Harud,
So he promised with a vow to give her anything she wanted.
At her mother’s demand, the girl said, “I want the head of Yahukanun the Baptist on a tray!”
Then the king regretted what he had said; but because of the vow he had made in front of his guests, he issued the necessary orders.
So Yahukanun was beheaded in the prison,
And his head was brought on a tray and given to the girl, who took it to her mother.
Later, Yahukanun’s followers came for his body and buried him. Then they went and told 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA what had happened.
As soon as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard the news, He left in a boat to a remote area to be alone. But the crowds heard where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was headed and followed Him on foot from many towns.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw the huge crowd as He stepped from the boat, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had compassion on them and healed their sick.
That evening the Talmidym came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and said, “This is a remote place, and it is already getting late. Send the crowds away so they can go to the villages and buy food for themselves.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “That is not necessary, you can feed them here.”
“But we have only five loaves of bread and two fish!” they answered.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. “Bring the fish and bread here,”

Then he told the people to sit down on the grass, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the five loaves and two fish, looking up toward Shamaym, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA baraked them, Then He broke the loaves into pieces, he gave the bread to the Talmidym, who distributed it to the people.
They all ate as much as they wanted, and afterward, the Talmidym picked up twelve baskets of leftovers.
Five thousand men were fed that day, besides women and children!
Immediately after feeding the people, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA insisted that His Talmidym gets back into the boat and cross to the other side of the lake, and He sent the people home.
After sending them home, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went up into the hills by Himself to pray. Night fell while He was there alone.
Meanwhile, the Talmidym were in trouble far away from land, for a strong wind had risen, and they were fighting heavy waves.
Shortly before dawn in the morning 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came toward them, walking on the water.
When the Talmidym saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA walking on the water, they were terrified, In their fear, they cried out, “It is a ghost!”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spoke to them at once. “Do not be afraid, “Take courage. I Am here!”
Then Kafa called to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Master, if it is really you, tell me to come to you, walking on the water.”
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to Kafa. come,”
But when Kafa saw the strong wind and the waves, Kafa was terrified and began to sink. “Save me, Master!” he shouted.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA immediately reached out and grabbed Kafa and said to him. “You have so little Amunah (faith), “Why did you doubt me?”
When they climbed back into the boat, the wind stopped.
Then the Talmidym worshiped Him. “You really are the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!” they exclaimed.
After they had crossed the lake, they landed at Gannasarat.
When the people recognized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the news of His arrival spread quickly throughout the whole area, and soon people were bringing all their sick to be healed.
They begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to let the sick touch at least the edge of His robe, and all who touched Him were healed.
Some Pharisees and teachers of religious law arrived from Yahushalam to see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they asked him,
“Why do your Talmidym disobey our age old tradition? For they ignore our tradition of ceremonial hand washing before they eat.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “And why do you, by your traditions, violate the direct commandments of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?
For instance, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to you, ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and ‘Anyone who speaks disrespectfully of father or mother must be put to death.’
But you say it is all right for people to say to their parents, ‘Sorry, I cannot help you. For I have vowed to give to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what I would have given to you.’
In this way, you say they do not need to honor their parents. And so you cancel the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for the sake of your own tradition.
You hypocrites! Yashayahu was right when he prophesied about you, for he wrote,
‘These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
Their worship is a farce, for they teach man-made ideas as Commandments from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called to the crowd to come and He said. “Listen,“and try to understand.
It’s not what goes into your mouth that defiles you; you are defiled by the words that come out of your mouth.”
Then the Talmidym came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and asked, “Do you realize you offended the Pharisees by what you just said?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Every plant not planted by my ABBA in Shamaym will be uprooted,
so ignore them. They are blind guides leading the blind, and if one blind person guides another, they will both fall into a ditch.”
Then Kafa said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Explain to us the parable that says people are not defiled by what they eat.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Are you also still without understanding?
“Anything you eat passes through the stomach and then goes into the sewer.
But the words you speak come from the heart, that is what defiles you.
From the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, all sexual immorality, theft, lying, and slander.
These are what defile you. Eating with unwashed hands will never defile you.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left Galily and went north to the region of Tyra and Sidun.
A woman who lived there came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, pleading, “Have mercy on me, O Master, Son of Daud! For my daughter is possessed by a demon that torments her severely.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave her no reply, not even a word, Then his Talmidym urged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to send her away. “Tell her to go away,” they said. “She is bothering us with all her begging.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the woman, “I was sent only to help 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s lost sheep, the people of Yashar'AL.”
But she came and worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, pleading again, Master, help me!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA responded, “It is not right to take food from the children and throw it to the dogs.”
She replied, “That’s true, Master, but even dogs are allowed to eat the scraps that fall beneath their masters’ table.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to her, “Dear woman,” your Amunah (faith) is great. Your request is granted.” And her daughter was instantly healed.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned to the Sea of Galily and climbed a hill and sat down.
A vast crowd brought to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA people who were lame, blind, crippled, those who could not speak, and many others. They laid them before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and He healed them all.

The crowd was amazed! Those who have not been able to speak were talking, the crippled were made well, the lame were walking, and the blind could see again! And they sing Yadah to the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called his Talmidym and told them, “I feel sorry for these people. They have been here with me for three days, and they have nothing left to eat. I don’t want to send them away hungry, or they will faint along the way.”
The Talmidym replied, “Where would we get enough food here in the wilderness for such a huge crowd?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked, “How much bread do you have?” They replied, “Seven loaves, and a few small fish.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told all the people to sit down on the ground.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the seven loaves and the fish and Tudah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for them, and broke them into pieces and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave them to the Talmidym, who distributed the food to the crowd.
They all ate as much as they wanted. Afterward, the Talmidym picked up seven large baskets of leftover food.
There were four thousand men who were fed that day, besides women and children.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent the people home, and He got into a boat and crossed over to the region of Magadan.
One day the Pharisees and Sadducees came to test 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, demanding that he show them a miraculous sign from Shamaym to prove His authority.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “You know the saying, ‘Red sky at night means fair weather tomorrow;
red sky in the morning means foul weather all day.’ You know how to interpret the weather signs in the sky, but you do not know how to interpret the signs of the times!
Only an evil, adulterous generation would demand a miraculous sign, but the only sign I will give them is the sign of the Nabym Yunah. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left them and went away.
Later, after they crossed to the other side of the lake, the Talmidym discovered they had forgotten to bring any bread.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA warned them. “Watch out! “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
At this they began to argue with each other because they had not brought any bread.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew what they were saying, so He said, “You have so little Amunah! Why are you arguing with each other about having no bread?
Do you not understand even yet? Do you not remember the five thousand I fed with five loaves, and the baskets of leftovers you picked up?
Or the four thousand I fed with seven loaves, and the large baskets of leftovers you picked up?
Why can you not understand that I Am not talking about bread? So again I say, ‘Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.’”
Then at last they understood that He was not speaking about the yeast in bread, but about the deceptive teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, He asked his Talmidym, “Who do people say that the Son of Adam is?”
“Well,” they replied, “some say Yahukanun the Baptist, some say AliYahu, and others say Yaramyahu or one of the other Nabym.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “But who do you say I Am?”
Simun Kafa answered, “You are Ha'Mashyach, the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “You are baraked Simun Ba-Yunah, because my ABBA in Shamaym has revealed this to you. You did not learn this from any man.
Now I say to you that you are Kafa (which means ‘rock’), and upon this rock I will build my Qadash Assembly, and all the powers of evil can not conquer it.
And I will give you the keys of the Kingdom of Shamaym. Whatever you forbid on the Arath will be forbidden in Shamaym, and whatever you permit on Arath will be permitted in Shamaym.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sternly warned the Talmidym not to tell anyone that He is Ha'Mashyach.

From then on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began to tell his Talmidym plainly that it was necessary for him to go to Yahushalam, and that he would suffer many terrible things at the hands of the elders, the leading Kuhanym, and the teachers of religious law. He would be killed, but on the third day He would be raised from the dead.
But Kafa took him aside and began to reprimand him for saying such things. “Shamaym forbid, Master,” Kafa said. “This will never happen to you!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to Kafa and said, “Get away from me, Ha'shatan! You are a dangerous trap to me. You are seeing things merely from a man's point of view, not from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to his Talmidym, “If any of you wants to be my follower, you must turn from your selfish ways, take up your death stake, and follow me.
If you try to hang on to your life, you will lose it. But if you give up your life for my sake, you will save it.
And what do you benefit if you gain the whole world but lose your own soul? Is anything worth more than your soul?
For the Son of Adam will come with his Malakym in the Kabad of his ABBA and will judge all people according to their deeds.
Assuredly, I say to you, there are some standing here who will not taste death till they see the Son of Adam coming in His kingdom.”
Six days later 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took Kafa and the two brothers, Ya'aqub and Yahukanun, and led them up a high mountain to be alone.
As they watched 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they noticed His appearance was transformed, and the face of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was shining like the sun, and His clothes became as white as light.
Suddenly, Musha and AliYahu appeared and began talking with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Kafa exclaimed, “Master, it is wonderful for us to be here! If you want, I will make three shelters as memorials one for you, one for Musha, and one for AliYahu.”
But even as Kafa spoke, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is my dearly loved Son, who brings me great joy. Listen to him.”
The Talmidym were terrified and fell face down on the ground.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came over and touched them and said. “Get up, Do not be afraid.”
And when they looked up, Musha and AliYahu were gone, and they saw only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
As they went back down the mountain, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA commanded them, “Do not tell anyone what you have seen until the Son of Adam has been raised from the dead.”
Then They asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Why do the teachers of religious law insist that AliYahu must return before Ha'Mashyach comes?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “AliYahu is indeed coming first to get everything ready.
But I tell you, AliYahu has already come, but he was not recognized, and they chose to abuse him. Likewise they will also make the Son of Adam suffer.”
Then the Talmidym realized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was talking about Yahukanun the Baptist.
At the foot of the mountain, a large crowd was waiting for them. A man came and knelt before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and said,
“Master, have mercy on my son, he has seizures and suffers terribly, he often falls into the fire or into the water.
So I brought him to your Talmidym, but they could not heal him.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “You faithless and corrupt people! How long must I be with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to me.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rebuked the demon in the boy, and it left him. From that moment the boy was well.
Afterward the Talmidym asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA privately, “Why could we not cast out that demon?”

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them. “You do not have enough Amunah (faith),” I tell you the truth, if you had Amunah even as small as a mustard seed, you could say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it would move. Nothing would be impossible.”
However, this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting.”
After they gathered again in Galily, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “The Son of Adam is going to be betrayed into the hands of his enemies.
He will be killed, but on the third day he will be raised from the dead.” And the Talmidym were filled with grief.
On their arrival in Capernaum, the collectors of the Temple tax came to Kafa and asked him, “Does your teacher not pay the Temple tax?”

“Yes, he does,” Kafa replied. Then Kafa went into the house. But before Kafa had a chance to speak, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked him, “What do you think Kafa? Do kings tax their own people or the people they have conquered?”
Kafa said, They tax the people they have conquered, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said “Well, then, “the citizens are free!

Nevertheless, lest we offend them, go to the sea, cast in a hook, and take the fish that comes up first. And when you have opened its mouth, you will find a piece of money; take that and give it to them for Me and you.”
About that time the Talmidym came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and asked, “Who is greatest in the Kingdom of Shamaym?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called a little child to him and put the child among them.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “I tell you the truth, unless you turn from your sins and become like little children, you will never get into the Kingdom of Shamaym.
So anyone who becomes as humble as this little child is the greatest in the Kingdom of Shamaym.
“And anyone who welcomes a little child like this on my behalf is welcoming me.
But if you cause one of these little ones who trusts in me to fall into sin, it would be better for you to have a large millstone tied around your neck and be drowned in the depths of the sea.
“What sorrow awaits the world, because it tempts people to sin. Temptations are inevitable, but what sorrow awaits the person who does the tempting.

So if your hand or foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It’s better to enter eternal life with only one hand or one foot than to be thrown into eternal fire with both of your hands and feet.
And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It’s better to enter eternal life with only one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
“Beware that you don’t look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that in Shamaym their Malakym are always in the presence of my ABBA in Shamaym.
For the Son of Adam has come to save that which was lost.
“If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them wanders away, what will he do? Won’t he leave the ninety-nine others on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?
And if he finds it, I tell you the truth, he will rejoice over it more than over the ninety-nine that didn’t wander away!
In the same way, it is not my ABBA in Shamaym's WILL that even one of these little ones should perish.
“If another believer sins against you, go privately and point out the offense. If the other person listens and confesses it, you have won that person back.
But if you are unsuccessful, take one or two others with you and go back again, so that everything you say may be confirmed by two or three witnesses.
If the person still refuses to listen, take your case to the Qadash assembly. Then if he or she won’t accept the Qadash Assemblies decision, treat that person as a pagan or a corrupt tax collector.
“I tell you the truth, whatever you forbid on the Arath will be forbidden in Shamaym, and whatever you permit on the Arath will be permitted in Shamaym.
“I also tell you this: If two of you agree here on the Arath concerning anything you ask, My ABBA in Shamaym will do it for you.
For where two or three are gathered together in my Name, I will be there among them.”
Then Kafa came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and asked, “Master, how often should I forgive someone who sins against me? Seven times?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, No, not seven times,” but seventy times seven!
“Therefore, the Kingdom of Shamaym can be compared to a king who decided to bring his accounts up to date with servants who had borrowed money from him.
In the process, one of the King's debtors was brought in who owed him ten thousand talents.
He could not pay, so his master ordered that he be sold along with his wife, his children, and everything he owned, to pay the debt.
“But the man fell down before his master and begged him, ‘Please, be patient with me, and I will pay it all.’
Then his master was filled with pity for him, and he released him and forgave his debt.
“But when the man left the king, he went to a fellow servant who owed him a few thousand talents. He grabbed him by the throat and demanded instant payment.
“His fellow servant fell down before him and begged for a little more time. ‘Be patient with me, and I will pay it,’ he pleaded.
But his creditor wouldn’t wait, he had the man arrested and put in prison until the debt could be paid in full.
“When some of the other servants saw this, they were very upset. They went to the king and told him everything that had happened.
Then the king called in the man he had forgiven and said, ‘You evil servant! I forgave you that tremendous debt because you pleaded with me.
Shouldn’t you have mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?’
Then the angry king sent the man to prison to be tortured until he had paid his entire debt.
“That’s what my ABBA in Shamaym will do to you if you refuse to forgive your brothers and sisters from your heart.”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had finished saying these things, He left Galily and went down to the region of Yahudah east of the Yurdan River.
Large crowds followed Him there, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA healed their sick.
Some Pharisees came and tried to trap 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with this question: “Should a man be allowed to divorce his wife for just any reason?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied. “Have you not read the Scriptures? They record that from the beginning 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made them male and female.’”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “‘This explains why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife, and the two are united into one.’
Since they are no longer two but one, let no one split apart what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has joined together.”
“Then why did Musha say in the law that a man could give his wife a written notice of divorce and send her away?” they asked.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Musha permitted divorce only as a concession to your hard hearts, but it was not what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had originally intended.
And I tell you this, whoever divorces his wife and marries someone else commits adultery, unless his wife has been unfaithful.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s Talmidym then said to Him, “If this is the case, it is better not to marry!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. Not everyone can accept this statement, only those whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH helps.
Some are born as eunuchs, some have been made eunuchs by others, and some choose not to marry for the sake of the Kingdom of Shamaym. Let anyone who can accept this.”
One day some parents brought their children to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA so he could lay his hands on them and pray for them. But the Talmidym scolded the parents for bothering 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Let the children come to me, do not stop them! For the Kingdom of Shamaym belongs to those who are like these children.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA placed his hands on their heads and baraked them before he left.
Someone came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with this question: “Teacher, what good deed must I do to have eternal life?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied. “Why ask me about what is good?” There is only One who is good. But to answer your question, if you want to receive eternal life, you must keep and obey the commandments.”
“Which ones?” the man asked. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied: “‘You must not murder. You must not commit adultery. You must not steal. You must not testify falsely.
Honor your father and mother, Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
I have obeyed all these commandments, the young man replied. “What else must I do?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told him, “If you want to be perfect, go and sell all your possessions and give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in Shamaym, then come, follow me.”
But when the young man heard this, he went away sad, for he had many possessions.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to his Talmidym, “I tell you the truth, it is very hard for a rich person to enter the Kingdom of Shamaym.
I will say it again, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
The Talmidym were astounded. “Then who in the world can be saved?” they asked.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked at them intently and said, “with men, it is impossible, But with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH all things are possible.”
Then Kafa said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “We have given up everything to follow you. What will we get?”

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “I assure you that when the world is made new and the Son of Adam sits upon his Esteemed throne, you who have been my followers will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'AL.
And everyone who has given up houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or children or property, for my sake, will receive a hundred times as much in return and will inherit eternal life.
But many who are the greatest now will be least important then, and those who seem least important now will be the greatest then.
“For the Kingdom of Shamaym is like the landowner who went out early one morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed to pay the normal daily wage and sent them out to work.
“At the third hour of the day he was passing through the marketplace and saw some people standing around doing nothing.
So he hired them, telling them he would pay them whatever was right at the end of the day.
So they went to work in the vineyard. At sixth hour and again at ninth hour he did the same thing.
“At the eleventh hour he was in town again and saw some more people standing around. He asked them, ‘Why have you not been working today?’
“They replied, ‘Because no one hired us.’
“That evening he told the foreman to call the workers in and pay them, beginning with the last workers first.
When those hired at eleventh hour were paid, each received a full day wage.
When those hired first at the third hour came to get their pay, they assumed they would receive more, But they too were paid a day wage.
When they received their pay, they protested to the owner,
‘Those people worked only one hour, and yet you have paid them just as much as you paid us who worked all day in the scorching heat.’
“He answered one of them, ‘Friend, I have not been unfair! Did you not agree to work all day for the usual wage?
Take your money and go, I will pay this last worker the same as you.
Is it against the law for me to do what I want with my money? Should you be jealous because I am kind to others?’
“So those who are the last now will be first, and those who are the first will be last, for many are called but few are chosen.”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was going up to Yahushalam, he took the twelve Talmidym aside privately and told them what was going to happen to him.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, Listen, we are going up to Yahushalam, where the Son of Adam will be betrayed to the leading Kuhanym and the teachers of religious law. They will sentence Him to death.
Then they will hand Him over to the Romans to be mocked, flogged with a whip, and impaled. But on the third day He will rise again from death.”
Then the mother of Ya'aqub and Yahukanun, the sons of Zabadyahu, came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with her sons. She knelt respectfully to ask a favor.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked her, What is your request? She replied, “In your Kingdom, please let my two sons sit in places of honor next to you, one on your right and the other on your left.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered by saying to them, “You don’t know what you are asking! Are you able to drink from the bitter cup of suffering I am about to drink?” “Oh yes,” they replied, “we are able!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “You will indeed drink from my bitter cup. But I have no right to say who will sit on my right or my left, My ABBA has prepared those places for the ones He has chosen.”
When the ten other Talmidym heard what Ya'aqub and Yahukanun had asked, they were greatly displeased.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called them together and said, “You know that the rulers in this world display control over their people, and officials flaunt their authority over those under them.
But among you it will be different. Whoever wants to be a leader among you, must be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you must become your slave.
For even the Son of Adam came not to be served but to serve others and to give His life as a ransom for many.”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and the Talmidym left the town of Yarichu, a large crowd followed behind.
Two blind men were sitting beside the road. When they heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was coming that way, they began shouting, “Master, Son of Daud, have mercy on us!”
“Be quiet!” the crowd yelled at them.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard them, he stopped and called, “What do you want me to do for you?”
“Master,” they said, “we want to see!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had compassion for them and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA touched their eyes, immediately their eyes could see! Then they followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and His Talmidym approached Yahushalam, they came to the town of Bathphage on the Mount of Olives and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent two of his Talmidym ahead.
“Go into the village over there, “As soon as you enter the village you will see a donkey tied there, with its colt beside it. Untie them and bring them to me.
If anyone asks what you are doing, just say, ‘The Master has need of them,’ and he will immediately let you take them.”
This took place to fulfill the prophecy that said,
“Tell the people of Yahushalam, ‘Look, your King is coming to you, He is humble, riding on a donkey riding on a donkey’s colt.’”
The two Talmidym did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA commanded.
They brought the donkey and the colt to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and threw their garments over the colt, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat on it.
A great multitude spread their garments on the road ahead of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was in the center of the procession, and the people all around Him were shouting, “Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for the Son of Daud! Barakah to the one who comes in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut!”
The entire city of Yahushalam was in an uproar as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA entered. “Who is this?” they asked.
And the crowds replied, “It is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the Nabym from Nazarath in Galily.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA entered the Temple and began to drive out all the people buying and selling animals for sacrifice, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knocked over the tables of the money changers and the chairs of those selling doves.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “The Scriptures declare, ‘My Temple will be called a house of prayer,’ but you have turned it into a den of thieves!”
The blind and the lame came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in the Temple, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA healed them.

The leading Kuhanym and the teachers of religious law saw these wonderful miracles and heard even the children in the Temple shouting, “Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for the Son of Daud.” But the leaders were indignant.
They asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Do you hear what these children are saying?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned to Bathany, where He stayed overnight.
In the morning, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was returning to Yahushalam, He was hungry,

and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA noticed a fig tree beside the road, Then He went over to see if there were any figs, but there were only leaves. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the fig tree, “May you never bear fruit again!” And immediately the fig tree withered up.
The Talmidym were amazed when they saw this and asked, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “I tell you the truth, if you have Amunah (Faith and believe) and do not doubt, you can do things like this and much more. You can even say to this mountain, ‘May you be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and it will happen.
You can pray for anything, and if you have Amunah, you will receive it.”

When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned to the Temple and began teaching, the leading Kuhanym and elders came up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. They demanded, “By what authority are you doing all these things? Who gave you the right?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied them, “I’ll tell you by what authority I do these things if you answer one question,”

“Did Yahukanun’s authority to baptize come from Shamaym, or was it merely from man?” And they talked it over among themselves. “If we say it was from Shamaym, he will ask us why we did not believe Yahukanun.
But if we say it was merely from man, we will be mobbed because the people believe Yahukanun was a Nabym.”
So they answered and said to Him, “We do not know.”
“But what do you think about this? A man with two sons told the older boy, ‘Son, go out and work in the vineyard today.’
The son answered, ‘No, I won’t go,’ but later he changed his mind and went anyway.
Then the father told the other son, ‘You go,’ and he said, ‘Yes, sir, I will.’ But he did not go.
“Which of the two obeyed his father?”

For Yahukanun the Baptist came and showed you the right way to live, but you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes believed in Yahukanun‘s repentance message. And even when you saw this happening, you refused to believe the message and repent of your sins.

“Now listen to another story. A certain landowner planted a vineyard, built a wall around it, dug a pit for pressing out the grape juice, and built a lookout tower. Then he leased the vineyard to tenant farmers and moved to another country.
At the time of the grape harvest, the landowner sent his servants to collect his share of the crop.
But the vinedresser he rented the land to, grabbed the landowner's servants, they beat one, they killed one, and stoned another.
So the landowner sent a larger group of his servants to collect for him, but the results were the same.
“Finally, the landowner owner sent his son, thinking, ‘Surely they will respect my son.’
“But when the tenant vinedresser saw the landowner's son coming, they said to one another, ‘Here comes the heir to this estate. Come on, let us kill him and get the estate for ourselves!’
So they grabbed the Landowner's Son, dragged him out of the vineyard, and murdered him.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, When the landowner of the vineyard returns,” what do you think he will do to those farmers?”
The religious leaders replied, “He will put the wicked men to a horrible death and lease the vineyard to others who will give him his share of the crop after each harvest.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “Did you not ever read this in the Scriptures? ‘The stone that the builders rejected has now become the chief cornerstone, This is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes.’
I tell you, the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be taken away from you and given to a nation that will produce the proper fruit.
And whoever falls on this stone will be broken; but on whomever the stone falls upon, the stone will grind him to powder.”
When the leading Kuhanym and Pharisees heard this parable, they realized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was telling the story against them, they were the wicked farmers.
They wanted to arrest 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, but they were afraid of the crowds, who considered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to be a Nabym.
And again 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spoke to them in parables, saying,
“The kingdom of Shamaym may be compared to a king who gave a wedding feast for his son,
and sent his servants to call those who were invited to the wedding feast, but they would not come.

Again he sent other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who are invited, “See, I have prepared my dinner, my oxen and my fat calves have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.”’
But they paid no attention and went off, one to his farm, another to his business,
while the rest seized his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them.
The king was angry, and he sent his troops and destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but those invited were not worthy.
Go therefore to the main roads and invite to the wedding feast as many as you find.’
And those servants went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both bad and good. So the wedding hall was filled with guests.
“But when the king came in to look at the guests, he saw there a man who had no wedding garment.
And he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you get in here without a wedding garment?’ And he was speechless.
Then the king said to the attendants, ‘Bind him hand and foot and cast him into the outer darkness. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
For many are called, but few are chosen.”
Then the Pharisees went and plotted how to entangle 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in his words.

And they sent their followers to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, along with the Harudians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are true and teach the way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH truthfully, and you do not care about anyone's opinion, for you are not swayed by appearances.
Tell us, then, what you think. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew their evil motives, “Why put me to the test, you hypocrites?
Show me the coin for the tax.” And they brought him a Roman Coin.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Whose picture and title are stamped on it?”
They said, “Caesar's.” Then. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Therefore give to Caesar the things that belong to Caesar's, and give to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the things that belong to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
When they heard it, they marveled. And they left him and went away.
The same day the Sadducees came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, who say that there is no resurrection, and they asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA a question,
saying, “Teacher, Musha said, ‘If a man dies having no children, his brother must marry the widow and raise up offspring for his brother.’
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.
So too the second and third, down to the seventh.
After them all, the woman died.
In the resurrection, therefore, of the seven, whose wife will she be? For they all had her.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered them, “You are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like Malakym in Shamaym.
And as for the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was said to you by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH:
‘I am the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yachaq, and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Ya'aqub. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Living, not of the dead.”
And when the crowd heard it, they were astonished at the teaching of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
But when the Pharisees heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
And one of them, a lawyer, asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA a question to test him.
“Teacher, which is the great commandment in the Law?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him, “You must love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.
This is the great and first commandment.
And a second is like it: You must love your neighbor as yourself.
The entire law and all the demands of the Nabyms are based on these two commandments.”
Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them a question,
saying, “What do you think about Ha'Mashyach? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “The son of Daud.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “How is it then that Daud, in the Ruach, calls Ha'Mashyach his Master, saying,
“‘For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to my Master, “Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies under your feet”’?
If then Daud calls Ha'Mashyach his Master, how is Ha'Mashyach Daud's son?”
And no one was able to answer 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA a word, nor from that day did anyone dare to ask Him any more questions.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the crowds and to his Talmidym,
“The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Musha' seat,
Practice and obey whatever they tell you, but do not follow their examples. For they preach, but do not practice.
They tie up heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger.
“Everything they do is for show. On their arms they wear extra wide prayer boxes with Scripture verses inside, and they wear robes with extra long tassels.
And they love to sit at the head table at banquets and in the seats of honor in the synagogues.
They love to receive respectful greetings as they walk in the marketplaces, and to be called ‘Rabbi (teacher).’
“Do not let anyone call you ‘Rabbi,’ for you have only one Master and teacher, all of you are equal as brothers and sisters.
And do not address anyone here on Arath as ‘ABBA,’ for only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Shamaym is your spiritual ABBA.
And do not let anyone call you ‘MASTER,’ for you have only one Master, Ha'Mashyach.
The greatest among you must be a servant.
But those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.

“What sorrow awaits you teachers of religious law and you Pharisees. Hypocrites! For you shut the door of the Kingdom of Shamaym in people’s faces. You will not go in yourselves, and you do not let others enter either.
What sorrow awaits you scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour the houses of widows, and for a pretense make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.

“What sorrow awaits you teachers of religious law and you Pharisees. Hypocrites! For you cross land and sea to make one convert, and then you turn that person into twice the child of destruction you yourselves are!
“You blind guides! What sorrow awaits you! For you say that it means nothing to swear ‘by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Temple,’ but that it is binding to swear ‘by the gold in the Temple.’
You blind fools! Which is more important, the gold or the Temple that makes the gold sacred?
And you say that to swear ‘by the altar’ is not binding, but to swear ‘by the gifts on the altar’ is binding.
Fools and blind! For which is more important, the gift on the altar or the altar that makes the gift sacred?
When you swear ‘by the altar,’ you are swearing by it and by everything on it.
And when you swear ‘by the Temple,’ you are swearing by it and by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who lives in it.
And when you swear ‘by Shamaym,’ you are swearing by the throne of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who sits on the throne.

What sorrow awaits you teachers of religious law and you Pharisees. Hypocrites! For you are careful to tithe even the tiniest income from your herb gardens, but you ignore the more important aspects of the law, justice, mercy, and Amunah. You should tithe, yes, but do not neglect the more important things.
You blind guides, you filter out a gnat, and swallow a camel!
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and the plate, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.
You blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the plate, that the outside also may be clean.
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead people's bones and all uncleanness.
So you also outwardly appear righteous to others, but within you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
“Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the Nabyms and decorate the monuments of the righteous,
saying, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have taken part with them in shedding the blood of the Nabyms.’
Thus you witness against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the Nabyms.
Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers.
You serpents, you brood of vipers, how are you to escape being sentenced to everlasting destruction?
Therefore I send you Nabyms and wise men and scribes, some of whom you will kill and hang in dead stake, and some you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town,

so that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on Arath, from the blood of righteous Ábál to the blood of Zacharyahu the son of Barachyahu, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
Truly, I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.

“O Yahushalam, Yahushalam the city that kills the Nabyms and stones those who are sent to it! How often would I have gathered your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
See, your house is left to you desolate.
For I tell you, you will not see me again, until you say, ‘Baraked is he who comes in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was leaving the Temple grounds, his Talmidym pointed out to him the various Temple buildings.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Do you see all these buildings? I tell you the truth, they will be completely demolished. Not one stone will be left on top of another!”
Later, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat on the Mount of Olives. His Talmidym came to him privately and said, “Tell us, when will all this happen? What sign will signal your return and the end of the world?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “Do not let anyone mislead you,
for many will come in my name, claiming, ‘I am Ha'Mashyach.’ They will deceive many.
And you will hear of wars and threats of wars, but do not panic. Yes, these things must take place, but the end will not follow immediately.
Nation will go to war against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in many parts of the world.
But all this is only the first of the birth pains, with more to come.
“Then you will be arrested, persecuted, and killed. You will be hated all over the world because you are my followers.
And many will turn away from me and betray and hate each other.
And many false prophets will appear and will deceive many people.
Sin will be rampant everywhere, and the love of many will grow cold.
But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
And the Good News about the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be preached throughout the whole world, so that all nations will hear it; and then the end will come.
“The day is coming when you will see what Danyal the Nabym spoke about, the sacrilegious object that causes desecration standing in the Qadash Place.”
“Then those in Yahudah must flee to the hills.
Anybody on the rooftop must not go down into the house to pack.
Anybody that is out in the field must not return even to get a coat.
How terrible it will be for pregnant women and for nursing mothers in those days.
And pray that your flight will not be on the winter or on the Shabbat day.
For there will be greater anguish than at any time since the world began. And it will never be so great again.
In fact, unless that time of calamity is shortened, not a single person will survive, but it will be shortened for the sake of the chosen ones of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Then if anyone tells you, ‘Look, here is Ha'Mashyach,’ or ‘There He is,’ do not believe it.
For false Mashyach and false Nabym (prophets) will rise up and perform great signs and wonders so as to deceive, if possible, even the chosen ones of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
See, I have warned you about this ahead of time.
“So if someone tells you, ‘Look, Ha'Mashyach is out in the desert,’ do not bother to go and look. Or they say to you, ‘Look, Ha'Mashyach is hiding here,’ do not believe it!
For as the lightning flashes in the east and shines to the west, so it will be when the Son of Adam comes.
Just as the gathering of vultures shows there is a carcass nearby, so these signs indicate that the end is near.
“Immediately after the anguish of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will give no light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers in the Shamaym will be shaken.

And then at last, the sign that the Son of Adam is coming and will appear in the Shamaym, there will be deep mourning among all the peoples of the Arath, And they will see the Son of Adam coming on the clouds of Shamaym with power and great Kabad.
And he will send out his Malakym with the mighty blast of a trumpet, and they will gather his chosen ones from all over the world, from the farthest ends of the Arath and Shamaym.
“Now learn a lesson from the fig tree. When its branches bud and its leaves begin to sprout, you know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see all these things, you can know Ha'Mashyach return is very near, right at the door.
I tell you the truth, this generation will not pass from the scene until all these things take place.
Shamaym and Arath will disappear, but my Dabar will never disappear.
“However, no one knows the day or hour when these things will happen, not even the Malakym in Shamaym or the Son himself. Only ABBA knows.
“When the Son of Adam returns, it will be like it was in Nuah’s day.
In those days before the flood, the people were enjoying banquets and parties and weddings right up to the time Nuah entered his boat.
People did not realize what was going to happen until the flood came and swept them all away. That is the way it will be when the Son of Adam comes.
“Two men will be working together in the field; one will be taken, the other left.
Two women will be grinding flour at the mill; one will be taken, the other left.
“So you, too, must keep watch! For you do not know what day your Master is coming.
But know this, that if the master of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into.
You also must be ready all the time, for the Son of Adam will come unexpected.
“A faithful, sensible servant is one to whom the master can give the responsibility of managing his other household servants and feeding them.
If the master returns and finds that the servant has done a good job, there will be a reward.
I tell you the truth, the master will put that servant in charge of all he owns.
But what if the servant is evil and thinks, ‘My master will not be back for a while,’
and he begins beating the other servants, partying, and getting drunk?
The master will return unannounced and unexpected,
and the master will cut the servant to pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
“For the Kingdom of Shamaym will be like ten bridesmaids who took their lamps and went to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
The five who were foolish did not take enough olive oil for their lamps,
but the other five were wise enough to take along extra oil.
When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
“At midnight they were roused by the shout, ‘Look, the bridegroom is coming! Come out and meet him!’
“All the bridesmaids got up and prepared their lamps.
Then the five foolish ones asked the others, ‘Please give us some of your oil because our lamps are going out.’
“But the others replied, ‘We don’t have enough for all of us. Go to a shop and buy some for yourselves.’
“But while they were gone to buy oil, the bridegroom came. Then those who were ready went in with him to the marriage feast, and the door was locked.
Later, when the other five bridesmaids returned, they stood outside, calling, ‘Master! Master! Open the door for us!’
“The Master said to them, ‘go from here, I do not know you!’
“You must always keep watch! For you do not know the day or hour of My return.
“Again, the Kingdom of Shamaym can be illustrated by the story of a man going on a long trip. He called together his servants and entrusted his money to them while he was gone.
He gave five bags of silver to one, two bags of silver to another, and one bag of silver to the last, dividing it in proportion to their abilities. He then left on his trip.
“The servant who received the five bags of silver began to invest the money and earned five more.
The servant with two bags of silver also went to work and earned two more.
But the servant who received the one bag of silver dug a hole in the ground and hid the master’s money.
“After a long time their master returned from his trip and called them to give an account of how they had used his money.
The servant to whom he had entrusted the five bags of silver came forward with five more and said, ‘Master, you gave me five bags of silver to invest, and I have earned five more.’

“The master was full of praise. ‘Well done, my good and faithful servant. You have been faithful in handling this small amount, so now I will give you many more responsibilities. Let us celebrate together!’
“The servant who had received the two bags of silver came forward and said, ‘Master, you gave me two bags of silver to invest, and I have earned two more.’
“The master said, ‘Well done, my good and faithful servant. You have been faithful in handling this small amount, so now I will give you many more responsibilities. Let us celebrate together!’
“Then the servant with the one bag of silver came and said, ‘Master, I knew you were a harsh man, harvesting crops you did not plant and gathering crops you did not cultivate.
I was afraid I would lose your money, so I hid it in the under ground. Look, here is your money back.’
“But the master replied, ‘You wicked and lazy servant! If you knew I harvested crops I did not plant and gathered crops I did not cultivate,
why did you not deposit my money in the bank? At least I could have gotten some interest on it.’
“Then he ordered, ‘Take the money from this servant, and give it to the one with the ten bags of silver.
To those who use well what they are given, even more will be given, and they will have an abundance. But from those who do nothing, even what little they have will be taken away.
Now throw this useless servant into outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
“But when the Son of Adam comes in his Kabad, and all the Malakym with him, then he will sit upon his esteemed throne.
All the nations will be gathered in his presence, and he will separate the people as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will place the sheep at his right hand and the goats at his left.
“Then the King will say to those on his right, ‘Come, you who are baraked by my ABBA, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the creation of the world.
For I was hungry, and you fed me. I was thirsty, and you gave me a drink. I was a stranger, and you invited me into your home.
I was naked, and you gave me clothing. I was sick, and you cared for me. I was in prison, and you visited me.’
“Then these righteous ones will reply, ‘Master, when did we ever see you hungry and feed you? Or thirsty and give you something to drink?
Or a stranger and show you hospitality? Or naked and give you clothing?
When did we ever see you sick or in prison and visit you?’
“And the King will say, ‘I tell you the truth, when you did it to one of the least of these my brothers and sisters, you were doing it to me!’
“Then the King will turn to those on the left and say, ‘Away with you, you cursed ones, into the eternal fire prepared for ha'shatan and his demons.
For I was hungry, and you did not feed me. I was thirsty, and you did not give me a drink.
I was a stranger, and you did not invite me into your home. I was naked, and you did not give me clothing. I was sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.’
“Then they will reply, ‘Master, when did we ever see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and not help you?’
“And he will answer, ‘I tell you the truth, when you refused to help the least of these my brothers and sisters, you were refusing to help me.’
“And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous will go into eternal life.”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had finished saying all these things, He said to his Talmidym,
“As you know, Passakh (Passover) begins in two days, and the Son of Adam will be handed over to be impaled.”
At that same time the leading Kuhanym and elders were meeting at the residence of Caiaphas, the high Kuhan,
plotting how to capture 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA secretly and kill him.
“But not during the Passakh celebration,” they agreed, “or the people may riot.”
Meanwhile, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was in Bethany at the home of Simun, a man who had previously had leprosy.
While he was eating, a woman came in with a beautiful alabaster jar of expensive perfume and poured it over the head of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
The Talmidym were indignant when they saw this. “What a waste!” they said.
“It could have been sold for a high price and the money given to the poor.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA aware of this, said to them, “Why criticize this woman for doing such a good thing to me?
You will always have the poor among you, but you will not always have me.
She has poured this perfume on me to prepare my body for burial.
Assuredly I say to you, wherever the Basurah (Good News) is preached throughout the world, this woman’s deed will be remembered and discussed.”
Then Yudas Iscariut, one of the twelve Talmidym, went to the leading Kuhanym
and asked, “How much will you pay me to betray 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to you?” And they gave him thirty pieces of silver.
From that time on, Yudas began looking for an opportunity to betray 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Talmidym came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and asked, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passakh meal for you?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “As you go into the city,” “you will see a certain man. Tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My time has come, and I will eat the Passakh meal with my Talmidym at your house.’”
So the Talmidym did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them and prepared the Passakh meal there.
When it was evening, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat down at the table with the Twelve.
While they were eating, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, Assuredly I say to you, one of you will betray me.”
Greatly distressed, each one asked in turn, “Am I the one, Master?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “One of you who has just eaten from this bowl with me will betray me.
For the Son of Adam must die, as the Scriptures declared long ago. But how terrible it will be for the one who betrays Him. It would be far better for that man if he had never been born!”
Yudas Iscariut, the one who would betray 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, also asked, “Rabbi (Master), am I the one?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told him, “You have said it.”
As they were eating, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took some bread and Baraked it. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA broke it in pieces and gave it to the Talmidym, saying, “Take this and eat it, for this is my body.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took a cup of wine and He Tudah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for it, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave it to the Talmidym and said, “Each of you drink from it,
for this is my blood, which confirms the Renewed covenant between 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and His people. It is poured out as a sacrifice to forgive the sins of many.
Mark my words, I will not drink wine again until the day I drink it new with you in my ABBA’s Kingdom.”
Then they sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives.
On the way, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told His Talmidym, “Tonight all of you will desert me. For the Scriptures say, I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
But after I have been raised from the dead, I will go ahead of you to Galily and meet you there.”
Kafa declared, “Even if everyone else deserts you, I will never desert you.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied Kafa, “Assuredly, I say to you that this night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
“No!” Kafa insisted. “Even if I have to die with you, I will never deny you!” And all the other Talmidym vowed the same.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went with them to the olive grove called Gathsamana, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Sit here while I go over there to pray.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took Kafa and Zabadyahu’s two sons, Ya'aqub and Yahukanun, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA became anguished and distressed.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “My soul is crushed with grief to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with me.”

So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went on a little farther and bowed with His face to the ground, praying, “My ABBA! If it is possible, let this cup of suffering be taken away from me. Yet I want your Will to be done, not mine.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned to the Talmidym and found them asleep, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to Kafa, “Could you not watch with me even one hour?
Keep watch and pray, so that you will not give in to temptation, For the ruach is willing, but the body is weak!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left them a second time and prayed, “O My ABBA! If this cup cannot be taken away unless I drink it, let your WILL be done.”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned to the Talmidym again, he found them sleeping, for they could not keep their eyes open.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went to pray a third time, saying the same words again.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came to the Talmidym and said, “Go ahead and sleep. Have your rest. But look, the time has come. The Son of Adam is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us be going. Look, my betrayer is here!”

And even as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said this, Yudas Iscariut, one of the twelve Talmidym, arrived with a crowd of men armed with swords and clubs, They had been sent by the leading Kuhanym and elders of the people.
The traitor, Yudas Iscariut, had given them a prearranged signal: “You will know which one to arrest when I greet him with a kiss.”
So Yudas Iscariut came straight to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Greetings, Rabbi!” he exclaimed and he kissed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “My friend, go ahead and do what you have come for.” Then the others grabbed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and arrested him.
But one of the men with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA pulled out his sword and struck the high Kuhan’s slave, slashing off his ear.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told him. “Put away your sword, “Those who use the sword will die by the sword.
Do you not realize that I could ask my ABBA for thousands of Malakym to protect us, and my ABBA would send them instantly?
But if I did, how would the Scriptures be fulfilled that describe what must happen now?”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the crowd, “Am I some dangerous criminal (revolutionary), that you come with swords and clubs to arrest me? Why did you not arrest me in the Temple? I was there teaching every day.
But this is all happening to fulfill the words of the Nabyms as recorded in the Scriptures.” At that point, all the Talmidym deserted 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and fled.
Then the people who had arrested 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA led him to the home of Caiaphas, the high Kuhan, where the teachers of religious law and the elders had gathered.
Meanwhile, Kafa followed him at a distance and came to the high Kuhan’s courtyard, he went in and sat with the guards and waited to see how it would all end.
Inside, the leading Kuhanym and the entire high council were trying to find witnesses who would lie about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, so they could put him to death.
But even though they found many who agreed to give false witness, they could not use anyone’s testimony. Finally, two men came forward
who declared, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the Temple of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and rebuild it in three days.’”
Then the high Kuhan stood up and said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Well, are you not going to answer these charges? What do you have to say for yourself?”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA remained silent. Then the high Kuhan said to him, “I demand in the name of the living 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, tell us if you are the Mashyach, the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “You have said it. And in the future you will see the Son of Adam seated in the place of power at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s right hand and coming on the clouds of Shamaym.”
Then the high Kuhan tore his clothes in anger and said, “Blasphemy! Why do we need other witnesses? You have all heard 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA's blasphemy.
What is your verdict? “Guilty!” they shouted. “He deserves to die!”
Then they began to spit in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s face and beat Him with their fists. And some slapped Him,
They started Mocking and they said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Prophesy to us, you Ha'Mashyach! Who is the one who struck you?”
Meanwhile, Kafa was sitting outside in the courtyard, a servant girl came over and said to Kafa, “You were one of those with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA the Galilyan.”
But Kafa denied it in front of everyone. “I do not know what you are talking about,” he said.
Later, out by the gate, another servant girl noticed Kafa and said to those standing around, “This man was with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of Nazarym.”
Again Kafa denied it, this time with an oath. “I do not even know the man,” he said.
A little later some of the other bystanders came over to Kafa and said, “You must be one of them; we can tell by your Galilyan accent.”
Kafa swore, “A curse on me if I am lying, I do not know the man!” And immediately the rooster Cock crowed.
Suddenly, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s words flashed through Kafa’s mind: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times that you do not know me.” And he went away, weeping bitterly.
Very early in the morning the leading Kuhanym and the elders of the people met again to lay plans for putting 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to death.
Then they bound 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and led him away, they took Him to Pilate, the Roman governor.

When Yudas Iscariut, who had betrayed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, realized that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had been condemned to die, Yudas was filled with remorse. So he took the thirty pieces of silver back to the leading Kuhanym and the elders.
“I have sinned,” he declared, “for I have betrayed an innocent man. “What do we care? they retorted. That’s your problem.”
Then Yudas Iscarius threw the silver coins down in the Temple and went out and hanged himself.
The leading Kuhanym picked up the coins. “It would not be right to put this money in the Temple treasury,” they said, “since it was payment for murder.”
After some discussion they finally decided to buy the potter’s field, and they made it into a cemetery for foreigners.
That is why the field is still called the Field of Blood.
This fulfilled the prophecy of Yaramyahu that says, “They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price at which he was valued by the people of Yashar'AL,
and purchased the potter’s field, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH directed.”
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was standing before Pilate, the Roman governor. “Are you the king of the Yahudym?” the governor asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA,
But when the leading Kuhanym and the elders made their accusations against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, He remained silent.
“Do you not hear all these charges they are bringing against you?” Pilate demanded.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA made no response to any of the charges, much to the governor’s surprise.
Now it was the governor’s custom each year during the Passakh celebration to release one prisoner to the crowd, anyone they wanted.
This year there was a notorious prisoner, a man named Barabbas.
As the crowds gathered before Pilate’s house that morning, he asked them, “Which one do you want me to release to you, Barabbas or 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA who is called Ha'Mashyach?”
(He knew very well that the religious leaders had arrested 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA out of envy.)
Just then, as Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him this message: “Leave that innocent man alone. I suffered through a terrible nightmare about Him last night.”
Meanwhile, the leading Kuhanym and the elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas to be released and for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to be put to death.
So the governor asked again, “Which of these two do you want me to release to you?” The crowd shouted back, “Barabbas!”
Pilate responded, “Then what should I do with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA who is called Ha'Mashyach?” They shouted back, “impale him!”
“Why?” Pilate demanded. “What crime has he committed?” but the mob roared even louder, impale him!”

Pilate saw that he was not getting anywhere and that a riot was developing. So he sent for a bowl of water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this man’s blood. The responsibility is yours!”
And all the people yelled back, “We will take responsibility for His death, we and our children!”
So Pilate released Barabbas to them. He ordered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA flogged with a lead-tipped whip, then turned him over to the Roman soldiers to be impaled.
Some of the governor’s soldiers took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to their headquarters and called out the entire regiment.
They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.

They wove thorn branches into a crown and put it on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA's head, and they placed a reed stick in his right hand as a scepter. Then they knelt before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in mockery and taunted, “Hail! King of the Yahudym!”
And they spit on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and grabbed the stick and struck 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA on the head with it.
When they were finally tired of mocking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they took off the robe and put his own clothes on him again. Then they led 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA away to be impaled.
Along the way, they came across a man named Simun, who was from Cyrana, and the soldiers forced him to carry the execution stake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And they went out to a place called Gulgutha (which means “Place of the Skull”).
The soldiers gave 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA wine mixed with bitter gall, but when He had tasted it, he refused to drink it.
After they had nailed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to the execution Stake, the soldiers gambled for His clothes by throwing dice.
Then they sat around and kept guard as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was impaled on the death stake.
They put a sign above the head of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, with the charge against Him. It read:"
Two criminals were impaled with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, one on his right and one on his left.
The people passing by shouted abuse, shaking their heads in mockery.

“Look at you now!” they yelled at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. “You said you were going to destroy the Temple and rebuild it in three days. Well then, if you are the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, save yourself and come down from the death stake!”
The leading Kuhanym, the teachers of religious law, and the elders also mocked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
“He saved others,” they scoffed, “but he cannot save himself! So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is the King of Yashar'AL, is He? Let him come down from the death stake right now, and we will believe in Him!
He trusted 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, so let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rescue Him now if He wants Him! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, ‘I am the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’”
Even the revolutionaries who were impaled with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA ridiculed him in the same way.
At noon, darkness fell across the whole land until ninth hour.
At about ninth hour, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called out with a loud voice, “Aly, Aly, lamah zabachthany?” which means “My 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, my 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, why have you abandoned me?”
Some of the bystanders misunderstood and thought he was calling for the Nabym AliYahu.
One of them ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, holding it up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA on a reed stick so He could drink.
But the rest said, “Wait! Let us see whether AliYahu will come to save him.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA shouted out with a loud voice, and He gave up his Ruach.
At that moment the Veil in the sanctuary of the Temple was torn in two, from top to bottom. The Arath shook, rocks split apart,
and tombs opened. The bodies of many righteous men and women who had died were raised from the dead.
They left the grave after 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s resurrection, went into the Qadash city of Yahushalam, and appeared to many people.

So when the centurion and those with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, who were guarding 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, saw the earthquake and the things that had happened, they feared greatly, saying, Truly this was the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
And many women who followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from Galily, ministering to Him, were there looking on from afar,
among whom were Maryam Magdalyn, Maryam the mother of Ya'aqub and Ya'asaf, and the mother of Zabadyahu’s sons.
As evening approached, Ya'asaf, a rich man from Arimathaa who had become a follower of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA,
went to Pilate and asked for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s body, And Pilate issued an order to release it to him.
Ya'asaf took the body and wrapped it in a long sheet of clean linen cloth.
And Ya'asaf placed the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in his own new tomb, which had been carved out of the rock. Then he rolled a great stone across the entrance and left.
Both Maryam Magdalyn and the other Maryam were sitting across from the tomb and watching.
The next day, on the Shabbat, the leading Kuhanym and Pharisees went to see Pilate.
They told him, “Sir, we remember what that deceiver once said while he was still alive: ‘After three days I will rise from the dead.’

So we request that you seal the tomb until the third day. This will prevent his Talmidym from coming and stealing his body and then telling everyone 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was raised from the dead! If that happens, we will be worse off than we were at first.”
Pilate replied, “Take guards and secure it the best you can.”
So they sealed the tomb and posted guards to protect it.
Now after the Shabbat, as the first day of the week began to dawn, Maryam Magdalyn and the other Maryam came to see the tomb.
And behold, there was a great earthquake and a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH descended from Shamaym, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat on it.
The Malak face shone like lightning, and his clothing was as white as snow.
The guards shook with fear when they saw the Malak, and they fell into a dead faint.
Then the Malak spoke to the women. “Do not be afraid!” he said. “I know you are looking for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, who was impaled.
He is not here! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA has risen from the dead, just as He said would happen. Come, see where His body was lay.
And now, go quickly and tell his Talmidym that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA has risen from the dead, and He is going ahead of you to Galily. You will see Him there. Remember what I have told you.”
The women ran quickly from the tomb. They were very frightened but also filled with great joy, and they rushed to give the Talmidym the Malak’s message.
And as they went to tell the Talmidym, behold, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA met them, saying, “Rejoice!” So they came and held 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA by the feet and worshiped Him..
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Do not be afraid! Go tell my brothers to leave for Galily, and they will see me there.”
As the women were on their way, some of the guards went into the city and told the leading Kuhanym what had happened.
A meeting with the elders was called, and they decided to give the soldiers a large bribe.
They told the soldiers, “You must say, the Talmidym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
If the governor hears about it, we will stand up for you so you will not get into trouble.”
So the guards accepted the bribe and said what they were told to say. Their story spread widely among the Yahudym, and they still tell it today.
Then the eleven Talmidym left for Galily, going to the mountain where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had told them to go.
When they saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they worshiped Him, but some of them doubted!
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came and told His Talmidym, “I have been given all authority in Shamaym and on Arath.
Therefore, go and make Talmidym of all the nations, baptizing them in the Name of ABBA YAHUAH and the Name of the Son and of the RUACH Ha'Qadash.
Teach these new Talmidym to obey all the commandments I have given you. And be sure of this: I Am with you always, even to the end of the age.”

books.name: Mark
chapters: This is the Basurah about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach, the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, It began
just as the Nabym Yashayahu had written: “Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, and he will prepare your way.
He is a voice shouting in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Master’s coming! Clear the road for him!’”
This messenger was Yahukanun the Baptist, he was in the wilderness and preached that people should be baptized to show that they had repented of their sins and turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to be forgiven.
All of Yahudah, including all the people of Yahushalam, went out to see and hear Yahukanun, and when they confessed their sins, he baptized them in the Yurdan River.
Yahukanun's clothes were woven from coarse camel hair, and he wore a leather belt around his waist. For food he ate locusts and wild honey.
Yahukanun announced: “Someone is coming soon who is greater than I am, so much greater that I am not even worthy to stoop down like a slave and untie the straps of his sandals.
I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the RUACH Ha'Qadash!”
One day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came from Nazarath in Galily, and Yahukanun baptized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in the Yurdan River.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came up out of the water, He saw the Shamaym splitting apart and the RUACH Ha'Qadash descending on Him like a dove.
And a voice from Shamaym said, “You are my dearly loved Son, and you bring me great joy.”
The RUACH then compelled 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to go into the wilderness,
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was there in the wilderness forty days, and tempted by Ha'shatan, and was with the wild beasts; and the Malakym ministered to Him.
Later on, after Yahukanun the Baptist was arrested, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went into Galily, where he preached 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Good News.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA announced. “The time promised by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has come at last! “The Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is near! Repent of your sins and believe the Good News!”
One day as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was walking along the shore of the Sea of Galily, he saw Simun and his brother Andraw throwing a net into the water, for they fished for a living.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called out to them, “Come, follow me, and I will show you how to fish for people!”
And they left their nets at once and followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
A little farther up the shore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw Zabadyahu’s sons, Ya'aqub and Yahukanun, in a boat repairing their nets.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called them at once, and they also followed him, leaving their father, Zabadyahu in the boat with the hired men.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and his Talmidym went to the town of Capernaum. When the Shabbat day came, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went into the congregation and began to teach.
The people were amazed at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s teaching, for He taught with real authority, quite unlike the teachers of religious law.
Suddenly, a man in the synagogue who was possessed by an evil spirit began shouting,
“Why are you interfering with us, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of Nazarym? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are the Qadash One of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rebuked him. “Be quiet! And Come out of the man,” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA ordered the demons.
At that, the evil spirit screamed, threw the man into a convulsion, and then came out of him.
Amazement gripped the audience, and they began to discuss what had happened. “What sort of new teaching is this?” they asked excitedly. “It has such authority! Even evil spirits obey his orders!”
The news about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spread quickly throughout the entire region of Galily.
After 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left the synagogue with Ya'aqub and Yahukanun, they went to Simun and Andraw’s home.
Now Simun’s mother-in-law was sick in bed with a high fever. They told 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA about her right away.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went to her bedside, took her by the hand, and helped her sit up. Then the fever left her, and she prepared a meal for them.
That evening after sunset, many sick and demon possessed people were brought to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
The whole town gathered at the door to watch.
