So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA healed many people who were sick with various diseases, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA cast out many demons. But because the demons knew who 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was, He did not allow the demons to speak.
Before daybreak the next morning, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA got up and went out to an isolated place to pray.
Later Simun and the others went out to find 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
When they found 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they said, “Everyone is looking for you.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “We must go on to other towns as well, and I will preach to them, too. That is why I came.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA traveled throughout the region of Galily, preaching in the congregations and casting out demons.
A man with leprosy came and knelt in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, begging to be healed. “If you are willing, you can heal me and make me clean,” he said.
Moved with compassion, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA reached out and touched him and said. “I am willing, “Be healed!”
Instantly the leprosy disappeared, and the man was healed.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent him on his way with a stern warning:

“Do not tell anyone about this. Instead, go to the Kuhan and let him examine you. Take along the offering required in the instructions Musha commanded for those who have been healed of leprosy. This will be a public testimony that you have been cleansed.”

But the man went and spread the word, proclaiming to everyone what had happened. As a result, large crowds soon surrounded 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and He could not publicly enter a town anywhere. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had to stay out in the secluded places, but people from everywhere kept coming to Him.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned to Capernaum several days later, the news spread quickly that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was back home.
Soon the house where he was staying was so packed with visitors that there was no more room, even outside the door. While he was preaching 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Dabar to them,
four men arrived carrying a paralyzed man on a mat.

They could not bring him to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA because of the crowd, so they dug a hole through the roof above 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA's head. Then they lowered the man on his mat, right down in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Seeing their Amunah, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the paralyzed man, “My child, your sins are forgiven.”
But some of the teachers of religious law who were sitting there thought to themselves,
“What is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saying? This is blasphemy! Only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH can forgive sins!”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew immediately what they were thinking, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “Why do you question this in your hearts?
Is it easier to say to the paralyzed man ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or ‘Stand up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
So I will prove to you that the Son of Adam has the authority on Arath to forgive sins.” Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to the paralyzed man and said,
“Stand up, pick up your mat, and go home!”
And the man jumped up, grabbed his mat, and walked out in the presence of them all, they were all amazed and they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, exclaiming, We have never seen anything like this before!
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went out to the lakeshore again and taught the crowds that were coming to Him.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA walked along, He saw Lauy son of Alphaus sitting at his tax collector’s booth. “Follow Me and be My Talmid,” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him. So Lauy got up and followed him.

Later, Lauy invited 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and His Talmidym to his home as dinner guests, along with many tax collectors and other disreputable sinners. (There were many people of this kind among 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s followers.)
But when the teachers of religious law who were Pharisees saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA eating with tax collectors and other sinners, they asked His Talmidym, “Why does He eat with such scum?”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard this, He told them, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, sick people do. I have come to call not those who think they are righteous, but those who know they are sinners.”
Once when Yahukanun’s followers and the Pharisees were fasting, some people came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and asked, “Why do your Talmidym not fast like Yahukanun’s followers and the Pharisees do?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Do wedding guests fast while celebrating with the groom? Of course not. They cannot fast while the groom is with them.
But someday the groom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.
“Besides, who would patch old clothing with new cloth? For the new patch would shrink and rip away from the old cloth, leaving an even bigger tear than before.
“And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. For the wine would burst the wineskins, and the wine and the skins would both be lost. New wine calls for new wineskins.”
One Shabbat day as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was walking through some grainfields, and His Talmidym began breaking off heads of grain to eat.
And the Pharisees said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Look, why are they breaking the law by harvesting grain on the Shabbat?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, Have you not ever read in the Scriptures what Daud did when he and his companions were hungry?

He went into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH (during the days when Abiathar was high Kuhan) and broke the law by eating the sacred loaves of bread that only the Kuhanym are allowed to eat. He also gave some to his companions.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Shabbat.
Therefore the Son of Adam is also High Kuhan of the Shabbat.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went into the congregation again and noticed a man with a deformed hand.
Since it was the Shabbat, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s enemies watched Him closely. If he healed the man’s hand, they planned to accuse Him of working on the Shabbat.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the man with the deformed hand, “Come and stand in front of everyone.”
Then he turned to his critics and asked, “Does the law permit good deeds on the Shabbat, or is it a day for doing evil? Is this a day to save life or to destroy it?” But they would not answer Him.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked around at them angrily and was deeply saddened by their hard hearts, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So the man stretches out his hand, and the hand was restored!
At once the Pharisees went away and met with the supporters of Harud to plot how to kill 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went out to the lake with his Talmidym, and a large crowd followed Him. They came from all over Galily, Yahudah,

Yahushalam, Idumaa, from east of the Yurdan River, and even from as far north as Tyra and Sidun. The news about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s miracles had spread far and wide, and vast numbers of people came to see Him.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA instructed His Talmidym to have a boat ready so the crowd would not crush him.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had healed many people that day, so all the sick people eagerly pushed forward to touch 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And whenever those possessed by evil spirits saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the spirits would throw them to the ground in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and cried out, “You are the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sternly commanded the spirits not to reveal who He was.
Afterward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went up on a mountain and called out the ones he wanted to go with him. And they came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA appointed twelve of them and called them his Shaliach (apostles). They were to accompany 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and he would send them out to preach,
giving them authority to cast out demons.
These are the twelve he chose:
Ya'aqub and Yahukanun (the sons of Zabadyahu, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA nicknamed them “Sons of Thunder”),
Andraw, Philip, Barthulumaw, Mattatyahu, Thomas, Ya'aqub (son of Alphaus), Thaddaus, Simon (the zalut),
Yudas Iscariot (who later betrayed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA).
One time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA entered a house, and the crowds began to gather again. Soon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and His Talmidym could not even find time to eat.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s family heard what was happening, They went to get him because people said he was crazy.
But the teachers of religious law who had arrived from Yahushalam said, “He’s possessed by Ha'shatan, the prince of demons. That is where he gets the power to cast out demons.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called them over and responded with an illustration. “How can ha'shatan cast out ha'shatan?”.
“A kingdom divided by civil war will collapse.
Similarly, a family splintered by feuding will fall apart.
And if ha'shatan is divided and fights against himself, how can he stand? He would never survive.

Let me illustrate this further. Who is powerful enough to enter the house of a strong man like ha'shatan and plunder his goods? Only someone even stronger, someone who could tie him up and then plunder his house.
“I tell you the truth, all sin and blasphemy can be forgiven,
but anyone who blasphemes against the RUACH Ha'Qadash will never be forgiven. This is a sin with eternal consequences.”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them this because they were saying, “He is possessed by an evil spirit.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s mother and brothers came to see Him. They stood outside and sent word for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to come out and talk with them.
There was a crowd sitting around 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and someone said, “Your mother and your brothers are outside asking for you.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked at those around him and said, “Look, these are my mother and brothers.
Anyone who does 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s will is my brother and sister and mother.”
Once again 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began teaching by the lakeshore. A very large crowd soon gathered around him, so He got into a boat. Then He sat in the boat while all the people remained on the shore.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA taught them by telling many stories in the form of parables, such as this one:
“Listen! A farmer went out to plant some seed.
As he scattered it across his field, some of the seed fell on a footpath, and the birds came and ate it.
Some fell on stony ground, where it did not have much soil; and immediately it sprang up because it had no depth of soil.
But the plant soon wilted under the hot sun, and since it did not have deep roots, it died.
Other seed fell among thorns that grew up and choked out the tender plants so they produced no grain.
Still other seeds fell on fertile soil, and they sprouted, grew, and produced a crop that was thirty, sixty, and even a hundred times as much as had been planted!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Anyone with ears to hear should listen and understand.”
Later, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was alone with the twelve Talmidym and with the others who were gathered around, they asked Him what the parables meant.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “You are permitted to understand the secret of the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. But I use parables for everything I say to outsiders,
So that ‘Seeing they may see and not perceive, And hearing they may hear and not understand; Lest they should turn, And their sins be forgiven them.’
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “If you cannot understand the meaning of this parable, how will you understand all the other parables?
The sower sows the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And these are the ones by the wayside where the Dabar is sown. When they hear the Dabar, ha'shatan comes immediately and takes away the Dabar that was sown in their hearts.
These likewise are the ones sown on stony ground who, when they hear the Dabar, immediately receive it with gladness;
and they have no root in themselves, and so endure only for a time. Afterward, when tribulation or persecution arises for the Dabar’s sake, immediately they stumble.
Now these are the ones sown among thorns; they are the ones who hear the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
and the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things entering in choke the Dabar, and it becomes unfruitful.
But these are the ones sown on good ground, those who hear the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and accept it, and the Dabar bear fruit: some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some a hundred.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “Would anyone light a lamp and then put it under a basket or under a bed? Of course not! A lamp is placed on a stand, where its light will shine.
For everything that is hidden will eventually be brought into the open, and every secret will be brought to light.
Anyone with ears to hear should listen and understand.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA added, “Pay close attention to what you hear. The more attention you pay listen, the more understanding you will be given and you will receive even more.
To those who listen to my teaching, more understanding will be given. But for those who are not listening, even what little understanding they have will be taken away from them.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA also said, “The Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is like a farmer who scatters seed on the ground.
Night and day, while he is asleep or awake, the seed sprouts and grows, but he does not understand how it happens.
The Arath produces the crops on its own. First a leaf blade pushes through, then the heads of wheat are formed, and finally the grain ripens.
And as soon as the grain is ready, the farmer comes and harvests it with a sickle, for the harvest time has come.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “How can I describe the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? What story should I use to illustrate it?
It is like a mustard seed planted in the ground. It is the smallest of all seeds,
but it becomes the largest of all garden plants; it grows long branches, and birds can make nests in its shade.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA used many similar stories and illustrations to teach the people as much as they could understand.
In fact, in His public ministry 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA never taught without using parables; but afterward, when He was alone with his Talmidym, He explained everything to them.
As evening came, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to his Talmidym, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.”
So they took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in the boat and started out, leaving the crowds behind (although other boats followed).
But soon a fierce storm came up. High waves were breaking into the boat, and it began to fill with water.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was sleeping at the back of the boat with his head on a cushion, and the Talmidym woke him up, shouting, “Master, do you not care that we are going to drown?”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA woke up, He rebuked the wind and said to the waves, “Silence! Be still!” Suddenly the wind stopped, and there was a great calm.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “Why are you afraid? Do you still have no Amunah?”
The Talmidym were absolutely terrified. “Who is this man?” they asked each other. “Even the wind and waves obey Him!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and His Talmidym arrived at the other side of the lake, in the region of the Garasanas.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA climbed out of the boat, a man possessed by an evil spirit came out from a cemetery to meet 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
This man lived among the burial caves and could no longer be restrained, even with a chain.
Whenever he was put into chains and shackles, as he often was, he snapped the chains from his wrists and smashed the shackles. No one was strong enough to subdue him.
Day and night he wandered among the burial caves and in the hills, howling and cutting himself with sharp stones.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was still some distance away, the man saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and ran to meet him, and bowed low before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
With a shriek, he screamed, “Why are you interfering with me, Oh 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? I beg you In the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, do not torture me!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the evil spirit, “Come out of the man, you evil spirit.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked the evil spirit, “What is your name?” And he replied, “My name is Legion, because there are many of us inside this man.”
Then the evil spirits begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA again and again not to send them to some distant place.
There happened to be a large herd of pigs feeding on the hillside nearby.
“Send us into those pigs,” the spirits begged. “Let us enter them.”

So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave them permission. The evil spirits came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the entire herd of about two thousand pigs plunged down the steep hillside into the lake and drowned in the water.
The herdsmen fled to the nearby town and the surrounding countryside, spreading the news as they ran. People rushed out to see what had happened.
A crowd soon gathered around 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons, he was sitting there fully clothed and perfectly sane, and they were all afraid.
Then those who had seen what happened told the others about the demon possessed man and the pigs.
And the crowd began pleading with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to go away and leave them alone.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon possessed begged to go with him.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “No, go home to your family, and tell them everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done for you and how merciful 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has been.”
So the man started off to visit the Ten Towns of that region and began to proclaim the great things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had done for him; and everyone was amazed at what he told them.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA got into the boat again and went back to the other side of the lake, where a large crowd gathered around Him on the shore.
Then a leader of the local congregation, whose name was Yairus, arrived. When he saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, he fell at his feet,
pleading fervently with him. “My little daughter is dying,” he said. “Please come and lay your hands on her; heal her so she can live.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went with him, and all the people followed, crowding around 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
A woman in the crowd had suffered for twelve years with constant bleeding.
She had suffered a great deal from many doctors, and over the years she had spent everything she had to pay them, but she had gotten no better. In fact, she had gotten worse.
She had heard about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, so she came up behind 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA through the crowd and touched His robe.
For she thought to herself, “If I can just touch His robe, I will be healed.”
Immediately the bleeding stopped, and she could feel in her body that she had been healed of her terrible condition.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA realized at once that healing power had gone out from Him, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched my robe?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s Talmidym said to Him, “Look at this crowd pressing around you. How can you ask, ‘Who touched me?’”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA kept on looking around to see who had done it.
Then the frightened woman, trembling at the realization of what had happened to her, came and fell to her knees in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and told Him what she had done.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to her, “Daughter, your Amunah has made you well. Go in Shalum. Your suffering is over.”

While 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was still speaking to her, messengers arrived from the home of Yairus, the leader of the congregation. They told him, “Your daughter is dead. There is no use troubling the TEACHER now.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA overheard them and said to Yairus, “Do not be afraid. Just have Amunah.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA stopped the crowd and would not let anyone go with Him except Kafa, Ya'aqub, and Yahukanun (the brother of Ya'aqub).
When they came to the home of the congregation leader, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw much commotion and weeping and wailing.
And He went inside and asked, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead; she is only asleep.”
The crowd laughed at Him. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA made them all leave, and He took the girl’s father and mother and His three Talmidym into the room where the girl was lying.
Holding the girls hand, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to her, “Talitha kumi,” which means “Little girl, I say to you rise up!”
And the girl, who was twelve years old, immediately stood up and walked around! They were overwhelmed and totally amazed.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave them strict orders not to tell anyone what had happened, and then he told them to give her something to eat.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left that part of the country and returned with His Talmidym to Nazarath, His hometown.
The next Shabbat He began teaching in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were amazed. They asked, “Where did He get all this wisdom and the power to perform such miracles?”

Then they scoffed, “He is just a carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of Ya'aqub, Ya'asaf, Yahudas, and Simun. And his sisters live right here among us.” They were deeply offended and refused to believe in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “A Nabym is honored everywhere except in his own hometown and among his relatives and his own family.”
And because of their unbelief, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA could not do any miracles among them except to place His hands on a few sick people and heal them.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was amazed at their unbelief. Then He went from village to village, teaching the people.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called His twelve Talmidym together and began sending them out two by two, giving them authority to cast out evil spirits.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them to take nothing for their journey except a walking stick no food, no traveler’s bag, no money.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA allowed them to wear sandals but not to take a change of clothes.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Wherever you go,” “stay in the same house until you leave town.

And whoever will not receive you nor hear you, when you depart from there, shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony against them. Assuredly, I say to you, it will be more tolerable for Sudum and Gumurrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
So the Talmidym went out, telling everyone they met to repent of their sins and turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And they cast out many demons and healed many sick people, anointing them with olive oil.

Harud Antipas, the king, soon heard about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, because everyone was talking about Him. Some were saying, “This must be Yahukanun the Baptist raised from the dead. That is why he can do such miracles.”
Others said, “He is the Nabym AliYahu.” Still others said, “He is a Nabym like the other great Nabyms of the past.”
When Harud heard about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, he said, “Yahukanun, the man I beheaded, has come back from the dead.”
For Harud had sent soldiers to arrest and imprison Yahukanun as a favor to Harudias. She had been his brother Philip’s wife, but Harud had married her.
Yahukanun had been telling Harud, “It is against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s law for you to marry your brother’s wife.”
So Harudias bore a grudge against Yahukanun and wanted to kill him. But without Harud’s approval she was powerless,
for Harud respected Yahukanun; and knowing that he was a good and Qadash man, he protected him. Harud was greatly disturbed whenever he talked with Yahukanun, but even so, he liked to listen to him.
Harudias’s chance finally came on Harud’s birthday. He gave a party for his high government officials, army officers, and the leading citizens of Galily.

Then his daughter, also named Harudias, came in and performed a dance that greatly pleased Harud and his guests. “Ask me for anything you like,” the king said to the girl, “and I will give it to you.”
He even vowed, “I will give you whatever you ask, up to half my kingdom!”
She went out and asked her mother, “What should I ask for?” Her mother told her, “Ask for the head of Yahukanun the Baptist!”
So the girl hurried back to the king and told him, “I want the head of Yahukanun the Baptist, right now, on a tray!”
Then the king deeply regretted what he had said; but because of the vows he had made in front of his guests, he could not refuse her.
So he immediately sent an executioner to the prison to cut off Yahukanun’s head and bring it to him. The soldier beheaded Yahukanun in the prison,
brought his head on a tray, and gave it to the girl, who took it to her mother.
When Yahukanun’s followers heard what had happened, they came to get his body and buried it in a tomb.
The Shaliachs (Apostles) returned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from their ministry tour and told Him all they had done and taught.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Let us go off by ourselves to a quiet place and rest awhile.” for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said this because there were so many people coming and going that Him and his Talmidym did not even have time to eat.
So they left by boat for a quiet place, where they could be alone.
But many people recognized them and saw them leaving, and people from many towns ran ahead along the shore and got there ahead of them.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw the huge crowd as he stepped from the boat, and he had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he began teaching them many things.
Late in the day His Talmidym came to him and said, “This is a remote place, and it is already getting late.
Send the crowds away so they can go to the nearby farms and villages and buy something to eat.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “You feed them.” “With what?” they asked. “We have to work for months to earn enough money to buy food for all these people!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “How much bread do you have? “Go and find out.” They came back and reported, “We have five loaves of bread and two fish.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told the Talmidym to have the people sit down in groups on the green grass.
So they sat down in groups of fifty or a hundred.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the five loaves and two fish, looked up toward Shamaym, and baraked them. Then, breaking the loaves into pieces, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA kept giving the bread to the Talmidym so they could distribute it to the people. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA also divided the fish for everyone to share.
They all ate as much as they wanted,
and afterward, the Talmidym picked up twelve baskets of leftover bread and fish.
A total of five thousand men, women and children where not counted.
Immediately after feeding the people, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA insisted that His Talmidym get back into the boat and head across the lake to Bathsaida, while he sent the people home.
After telling everyone good bye, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went up into the hills by himself to pray.
Late that night, the Talmidym were in their boat in the middle of the lake, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was alone on land.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw that they were in serious trouble, rowing hard and struggling against the wind and waves. At Night time, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came toward them, walking on the water. He intended to go past them,
but when they saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA walking on the water, they cried out in terror, thinking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was a ghost.
They were all terrified when they saw Him. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spoke to them at once. “Do not be afraid, “Take courage! I Am here!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA climbed into the boat, and the wind stopped. They were totally amazed,
for they still did not understand the significance of the miracle of the loaves. Their hearts were too hard to take it in.
After they had crossed the lake, they landed at Gannasarat. They brought the boat to shore
And climbed out. The people recognized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA at once,
And they ran throughout the whole area, carrying sick people on mats to wherever they heard He was.

Wherever 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went in the villages, cities, or the countryside, they brought the sick out to the marketplaces. They begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to let the sick touch at least the fringe of his robe, and all who touched him were healed.
One day some Pharisees and teachers of religious law arrived from Yahushalam to see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
They noticed that some of His Talmidym failed to follow the Yahudym ritual of hand washing before eating.
For the Pharisees and all the Yahudym do not eat unless they wash their hands in a special way, holding the tradition of the elders.

Similarly, they do not eat anything from the market until they immerse their hands in water. This is just one of many traditions they have hold, such as their ceremonial washing of cups, pitchers, and kettles.
So the Pharisees and teachers of religious law asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Why do your Talmidym not follow our age old tradition? They eat without first performing the hand washing ceremony.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “You hypocrites! Yashayahu was right when he prophesied about you, for he wrote, ‘These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.
Their worship is a farce, for they teach man made ideas as commandments from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’
For you ignore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s law and substitute your own tradition.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “All too well you reject the commandment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that you may keep your tradition.
For instance, Musha gave you this law from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and ‘Anyone who speaks disrespectfully of father or mother must be put to death.’
But you say it is all right for people to say to their parents, ‘Sorry, I cannot help you. For I have vowed to give to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what I would have given to you.’
In this way, you let the people disregard their needy parents.
And so you cancel the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in order to hand down your own tradition. And this is only one example among many others.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called to the crowd to come and hear. “All of you listen, “and understand.
It is not what goes into your body that defiles you; You are defiled by what comes from your heart.”
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went into a house to get away from the crowd, and his Talmidym asked him what he meant by the parable He had just used.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked Do you not understand either? “Can you not see that the food you put into your body cannot defile you?
Food does not go into your heart, but only passes through the stomach and then goes into the sewer.”
And then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA added, “It is what comes from inside that defiles you.
From within, out of a person’s heart, come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder,
adultery, greed, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, envy, slander, pride, and foolishness.
All these vile things come from within; they are what defile you.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left Galily and went north to the region of Tyra. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA did not want anyone to know which house He was staying in, but He could not keep it a secret.
Right away a woman who had heard about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came and fell at His feet, her little girl was possessed by an evil spirit,
and she begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to cast out the demon from her daughter. Since she was a foreigner, from Syrian Phuanicia,
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told her, First let the children eat all they want, “for it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
She replied, “That’s true, Master, but even the dogs under the table are allowed to eat the scraps from the children’s plates.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to her. “Good answer!” Now go home, for the demon has left your daughter.”
And when she arrived home, she found her little girl lying quietly in bed, and the demon was gone.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left Tyra and went up to Sidun before going back to the Sea of Galily and the region of the Ten Towns.
A deaf man with a speech impediment was brought to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and the people begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to lay his hands on the man to heal him.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA led the deaf man away from the crowd so they could be alone, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then, spitting on his own fingers, he touched the man’s tongue.
Looking up to Shamaym, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sighed and said, “Aphphatha,” which means, “Be opened!”
Instantly the man could hear perfectly, and his tongue was freed so he could speak plainly!
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told the crowd not to tell anyone, but the more 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them not to tell others, the more they spread the news.
They were completely amazed and said again and again, “Everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA does is wonderful. He even makes the deaf to hear and gives speech to those who cannot speak.”
On a different gathering, another large crowd had gathered, and the people ran out of food again, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called His Talmidym and told them,
“I feel sorry for these people. They have been here with me for three days, and they have nothing left to eat.
If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a long distance.”
And the Talmidym replied, “How are we supposed to find enough food to feed them out here in the wilderness?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked, “How much bread do you have?” Seven loaves,” they replied.

So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told all the people to sit down on the ground. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the seven loaves, and Tudah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for them, and broke them into pieces. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave them to His Talmidym, who distributed the bread to the crowd.
A few small fish were found, too, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA also baraked these and told the Talmidym to distribute them.
They ate as much as they wanted. Afterward, the Talmidym picked up seven large baskets of leftover food.
There were about four thousand men in the crowd that day, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent them home after they had eaten.
Immediately after this, He got into a boat with His Talmidym and crossed over to the region of Dalmanutha.
When the Pharisees heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had arrived, they came and started to argue with Him. Testing Him, they demanded that He show them a miraculous sign from Shamaym to prove His authority.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard this, he sighed deeply in his Ruach and said, “Why do these people keep demanding a miraculous sign? I tell you the truth, I will not give this generation any such sign.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA got back into the boat and left them, and He crossed to the other side of the lake.
But the Talmidym had forgotten to bring any food. They had only one loaf of bread with them in the boat.
As they were crossing the lake, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA warned them, “Watch out! Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and of Harud.”
At this they began to argue with each other because they had not brought any bread.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew what they were saying, so He said, “Why are you arguing about having no bread? Do you not know or understand even yet? Are your hearts too hard to take it in?
‘You have eyes, can you not see? You have ears, can you not hear?’ Do you not remember anything at all?
When I fed the five thousand men with five loaves of bread, how many baskets of leftovers did you pick up afterward?”
“And when I fed the four thousand with seven loaves, how many large baskets of leftovers did you pick up?” They said “Seven, baskets.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them. “Don’t you understand yet?”
When they arrived at Bathsaida, some people brought a blind man to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and they begged him to touch the man and heal him.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. Then, spitting on the man’s eyes, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA laid his hands on the blind man and asked, “Can you see anything now?”
The man looked around. “Yes,” he said, “I see people, but I cannot see them very clearly. They look like trees walking around.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA placed his hands on the man’s eyes again, and his eyes were opened. His sight was completely restored, and he could see everything clearly.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent him away, saying, “Do not go back into the village on your way home.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and his Talmidym left Galily and went up to the villages near Caasaraa Philippi. As they were walking along, He asked His Talmidym, “Who do people say I Am?”
“Well,” they replied, “some say Yahukanun the Baptist, some say AliYahu, and others say you are one of the other Nabyms.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “But who do you say I Am?” Kafa replied, “You are Ha'Mashyach.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA warned them not to tell anyone about Him.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began to tell them that the Son of Man must suffer many terrible things and be rejected by the elders, the leading Kuhanym, and the teachers of religious law. That He would be killed, but three days later He would rise from the dead.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA talked about this openly with his Talmidym, Kafa took Him aside and began to reprimand him for saying such things.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned around and looked at Kafa, then reprimanded him. “Get away from me, Shatan! “You are seeing things merely from a man's point of view, not from the Will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then, calling the crowd to join his Talmidym, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “If any of you wants to be my follower, you must turn from your selfish ways, take up your execution stake, and follow me.
If you try to hang on to your life, you will lose it. But if you give up your life for my sake and for the sake of the Basurah (Good News), you will save it.
And what do you benefit if you gain the whole world but lose your own soul?
Is anything worth more than your soul?
If anyone is ashamed of me and my message in these adulterous and sinful days, the Son of Adam will be ashamed of that person when he returns in the Kabad of His ABBA with the Qadash Malakym.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went on to say, I tell you the truth, some standing here right now will not die before they see the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH arrive in great power!
Six days later 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took Kafa, Ya'aqub, and Yahukanun, and led them up a high mountain to be alone. As the men watched, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’ appearance was transformed,
and His clothes became dazzling white, far whiter than any earthly bleach could ever make them.
Then AliYahu and Musha appeared and began talking with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Kafa exclaimed, “Rabbi, it is wonderful for us to be here! Let us make three shelters as memorials, one for you, one for Musha, and one for AliYahu.”
Kafa said this because he did not really know what else to say, for they were all terrified.
Then a cloud overshadowed them, and a voice from the cloud said, “This is my dearly loved Son. Listen to him.”
Suddenly, when they looked around, Musha and AliYahu were gone, and they saw only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with them.
As they went back down the mountain, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Adam had risen from the dead.
So they kept it to themselves, but they often asked each other what He meant by “rising from the dead.”
Then they asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Why do the teachers of religious law insist that AliYahu must return before Ha'Mashyach comes?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA responded, “AliYahu is indeed coming first to get everything ready. Yet why do the Scriptures say that the Son of Adam must suffer greatly and be treated with utter contempt?
But I tell you, AliYahu has already come, and they chose to abuse him, just as the Scriptures predicted.”
When they returned to the other Talmidym, they saw a large crowd surrounding them, and some teachers of religious law were arguing with them.
When the crowd saw Him, they were overwhelmed with awe, and they ran to greet 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And He asked. “What is all this arguing about?”
One of the men in the crowd spoke up and said, “Teacher, I brought my son so you could heal him, he is possessed by an evil spirit that won’t let him talk.

And whenever this spirit seizes him, it throws him violently to the ground. Then he foams at the mouth and grinds his teeth and becomes rigid. So I asked your Talmidym to cast out the evil spirit, but they could not do it.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “You faithless people! How long must I be with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to me.”
So they brought the boy. But when the evil spirit saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, it threw the child into a violent convulsion, and he fell to the ground, writhing and foaming at the mouth.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked the boy’s father. “How long has this been happening?” He replied, “Since he was a little boy.
The spirit often throws him into the fire or into water, trying to kill him. Have mercy on us and help us, if you can.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “What do you mean, ‘If I can’? “Anything is possible if you believe.”
The father instantly cried out, “I do believe, but help me overcome my unbelief!”

When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw that the crowd of onlookers was growing, he rebuked the evil spirit. “Listen, you spirit that makes this boy unable to hear and speak, “I command you to come out of this child and never enter him again!”
Then the spirit screamed and threw the boy into another violent convulsion and left him. The boy appeared to be dead. A murmur ran through the crowd as people said, “He is dead.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up.
Afterward, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was alone in the house with his Talmidym, they asked him, “Why could we not cast out that evil spirit?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “This kind can be cast out only by prayer and fasting.”
Leaving that region, they traveled through Galily, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA did not want anyone to know He was there,

for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA wanted to spend more time with His Talmidym and teach them, and He said to them, “The Son of Adam is going to be betrayed into the hands of His enemies. He will be killed, but three days later He will rise from the dead.”
They did not understand what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was saying, however, and they were afraid to ask Him what He meant.
After they arrived at Capernaum and settled in a house, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked His Talmidym, “What were you discussing out on the road?”
But they did not answer, because they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat down, called the twelve Talmidym over to him, and said, “Whoever wants to be first must take last place and be the servant of everyone else.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA put a little child among them. Taking the child in his arms, He said to them,
“Anyone who welcomes a little child like this on my behalf welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me welcomes not only me but also my ABBA who sent me.
Then Yahukanun said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Teacher, we saw someone using your Name to cast out demons, but we told Him to stop because he was not in our group.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. “Do not stop him! “No one who performs a miracle in my Name, will be able to speak evil of Me.
Anyone who is not against us, is with us.
If anyone gives you even a cup of water because you belong to Ha'Mashyach, I tell you the truth, that person will surely be rewarded.
“But if you cause one of these little ones who trusts in me to fall into sin, it would be better for you to be thrown into the sea with a large millstone hung around your neck.
If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better to enter eternal life with only one hand than to go into the unquenchable fires of punishment with two hands.
Where ‘Their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.’
If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better to enter eternal life with only one foot than to be thrown into eternal punishment with two feet.
Where ‘Their worms never die and the fire never quenched.’
And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out. It is better to enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with only one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into eternal punishment,
‘where the maggots never die and the fire never goes out.’
“For everyone will be tested with fire.
Salt is good for seasoning. But if it loses its flavor, how do you make it salty again? You must have the qualities of salt among yourselves and live in Shalum with each other.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left Capernaum and went down to the region of Yahudah, the area east of the Yurdan River. Once again crowds gathered around Him, and as usual 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was teaching them.
Some Pharisees came and tried to trap 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with this question: “Should a man be allowed to divorce his wife?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered them with a question: “What did Musha say in the law about divorce?”
“And they said Well, Musha permitted it, “Musha said a man can give his wife a written notice of divorce and send her away.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA responded, “Musha wrote this command only as a concession to your hard hearts.
But ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made them male and female from the beginning of creation.
‘This explains why a man leaves his father and mother and is joined to his wife,
and the two are united into one.’ Since they are no longer two but one,
let no one split apart what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has joined together.”
Later, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was alone with his Talmidym in the house, they brought up the subject again.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries someone else commits adultery against her.
And if a woman divorces her husband and marries someone else, she commits adultery.”
One day some parents brought their children to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA so He could touch and barak them. But the Talmidym scolded the parents for bothering 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.

When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw what was happening, He was angry with His Talmidym, and He said to them, “Let the children come to me. Do not stop them! For the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH belongs to those who are like these children.
I tell you the truth, anyone who does not receive the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH like a child, will never enter the kingdom.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the children in His arms and placed His hands on their heads and baraked them.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was starting out on his way to Yahushalam, a man came running up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, knelt down, and asked, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “Why do you call me good?” Only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is truly good.

But to answer your question, you know the commandments: ‘You must not murder. You must not commit adultery. You must not steal. You must not testify falsely. You must not cheat anyone. Honor your father and mother.’”
“Teacher,” the man replied, “I’ve obeyed all these commandments since I was young.”

Looking at the man, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA felt genuine love for him, and He told him. “There is still one thing you have not done,” Go and sell all your possessions and give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in Shamaym, then come, follow me.”
At this the man’s face fell, and he went away sad, for he had many possessions.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked around and said to his Talmidym, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
This amazed them, But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said again, “Dear children, it is very hard to enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
In fact, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
The Talmidym were astounded. “Then who in the world can be saved?” they asked.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked at them intently and said, “with man, it is impossible. But not with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. For all things are possible with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then Kafa began to speak up. “We have given up everything to follow you,” Kafa said.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Yes,” and I assure you that everyone who has given up house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or property, for my sake and for the Basurah (Good News),
will receive now in return a hundred times as many houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and property, along with persecution. And in the world to come that person will have eternal life.
But many who are the greatest now will be least important then, and those who seem least important now will be the greatest then.”

They were now on the way up to Yahushalam, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was walking ahead of them. The Talmidym were filled with awe, and the people following behind were overwhelmed with fear. Taking the twelve Talmidym aside, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA once more began to describe everything that was about to happen to him.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Listen,” “we are going up to Yahushalam, where the Son of Adam will be betrayed to the leading Kuhanym and the teachers of religious law. They will sentence him to die and hand him over to the Romans.
They will mock him, spit on him, flog him with a whip, and kill him, but after three days he will rise again.”
Then Ya'aqub and Yahukanun, the sons of Zabadyahu, came over and spoke to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. “Teacher,” they said, “we want you to do us a favor.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “What is your request?”
They replied, “When you sit on your Esteemed throne, we want to sit in places of honor next to you, one on your right and the other on your left.”

But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “You do not know what you are asking! Are you able to drink from the bitter cup of suffering I am about to drink? Are you able to be baptized with the baptism of suffering I must be baptized with?”
“Oh yes,” they replied, “we are able!”
But I have no right to say who will sit on my right or My left. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has prepared those places for the ones He has chosen.”
When the ten other Talmidym heard what Ya'aqub and Yahukanun had asked, they were indignant.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called them together and said, “You know that the rulers in this world want control over their people, and officials flaunt their authority over those under them.
But among you it will be different. Whoever wants to be a leader among you must be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you must be the slave of everyone else.
For even the Son of Adam came not to be served but to serve others and to give His life as a ransom for many.”
Then they reached Yarichu, and as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and his Talmidym left town, a large crowd followed Him. A blind beggar named Bartimaus (son of Timaus) was sitting beside the road.
When Bartimaus heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of Nazarath was nearby, he began to shout, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, Son of Daud, have mercy on me!”
“Be quiet!” many of the people yelled at him. But he only shouted louder, “Son of Daud, have mercy on me!”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard him, he stopped and said, “Tell him to come here.”
Bartimaus threw aside his coat, jumped up, and came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “What do you want me to do for you?” “My Rabbi,” the blind man said, “I want to see!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the blind man, “Go, for your Amunah has healed you.” Instantly the man could see, and he followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA down the road.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and his Talmidym approached Yahushalam, they came to the towns of Bathphage and Bathany on the Mount of Olives. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent two of the Talmidym on ahead.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them. “Go into that village over there,” “As soon as you enter it, you will see a young donkey tied there that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks, ‘What are you doing?’ just say, ‘The Master needs it and will return it soon.’”
The two Talmidym left and found the colt standing in the street, tied outside the front door.
As they were untying it, some bystanders demanded, “What are you doing, untying that colt?”
They said what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had told them to say, and they were permitted to take it.
Then they brought the colt to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and threw their garments over it, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat on it.
Many in the crowd spread their garments on the road ahead of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and others spread leafy branches they had cut in the fields.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was in the center of the procession, and the people all around Him were shouting, “Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! Barakah on the one who comes in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
Barakah on the coming Kingdom of our ancestor Daud! Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in highest Shamaym!”

So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came to Yahushalam and went into the Temple. After looking around carefully at everything, He left because it was late in the afternoon. Then He returned to Bathany with the twelve Talmidym.
The next morning as they were leaving Bathany, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was hungry.
And He noticed a fig tree in full leaf, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went over to see if He could find any figs. But there were only leaves because it was too early in the season for fruit.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the tree, “May no one ever eat your fruit again!” And the Talmidym heard what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said.

When they arrived back in Yahushalam, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA entered the Temple and began to drive out the people buying and selling animals for sacrifices. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knocked over the tables of the money changers and the chairs of those selling doves,
and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA stopped everyone from using the Temple as a marketplace.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “The Scriptures declare, ‘My Temple will be called a house of prayer for all nations,’ but you have turned it into a den of thieves.”

When the leading Kuhanym and teachers of religious law heard what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had done, they began planning how to kill Him. But they were afraid of Him because the people were so amazed at His teaching.
That evening 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and the Talmidym left the city.
The next morning as they passed by the fig tree He had cursed, the Talmidym noticed it had withered from the roots up.
Then Kafa remembered what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said to the tree on the previous day and exclaimed, “Look, Rabbi! The fig tree you cursed has withered and died!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the Talmidym, Have Amunah in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
I tell you the truth, you can say to this mountain, ‘May you be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and it will happen. But you must really believe it will happen and have no doubt in your heart.
I tell you, You can pray for anything, and if you believe that you have received it, it will be yours.
But when you are praying, first forgive anyone you are holding a grudge against, so that your ABBA in Shamaym will forgive your sins, too.”
But if you do not forgive, neither will your ABBA in Shamaym forgive your trespasses.”
Again they entered Yahushalam. As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was walking through the Temple area, the leading Kuhanym, the teachers of religious law, and the elders came up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
They demanded, “By what authority are you doing all these things? Who gave you the right to do them?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied. “I will tell you by what authority I do these things if you answer one question,”
“Did Yahukanun’s authority to baptize come from Shamaym, or was it merely man's idea? Answer me!”
They talked it over among themselves. “If we say it was from Shamaym, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA will ask why we did not believe Yahukanun.
But do we dare say it was merely man's idea?” For they were afraid of what the people would do, because everyone believed that Yahukanun was a Nabym.
So they finally replied, “We do not know.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA responded, “Then I will not tell you by what authority I do these things.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began to speak to the people in parables: “A man planted a vineyard and set a hedge around it, he dug a place for the wine vat and built a tower. And he leased it to vinedressers and went into a far country.
Now at vintage-time he sent a servant to the vinedressers, that he might receive some of the fruit of the vineyard from the vinedressers.
And they took the servant and beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
Again he sent them another servant, and at him they threw stones, wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully treated.
And again the owner sent another servant, and they killed him; and many others, beating some and killing some.
Therefore still having one son, his beloved, the owner also sent his dear son to them last, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
But those vinedressers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
So they took the owner‘s son and killed him and cast him out of the vineyard.
“Therefore what will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the vinedressers, and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not even read this Scripture:
This was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
And they sought to lay hands on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, but feared the multitude, for they knew He had spoken the parable against them. So they left 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and went away.
Then they sent to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA some of the Pharisees and the Harudians, to catch Him in His words.

When they had come, they said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Teacher, we know that You are true, and care about no one; for You do not regard the person of men, but teach the way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in truth. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?
Shall we pay, or shall we not pay?”
So they brought it. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Whose image and inscription is this?” They said, “it is Caesar’s image.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered and said to them, “render to Caesar the things that belong to Caesar’s, and render to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH the things that belong's 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” And they marveled at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Then some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA; and they asked Him, saying:
“Teacher, Musha wrote to us that if a man’s brother dies, and leaves his wife behind, and leaves no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife; and dying, he left no offspring.
And the second took her, and he died; nor did he leave any offspring. And the third likewise.
So the seven had her and left no offspring. Last of all the woman died also.
Therefore, in the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as wife.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered and said to them, “you are in error, because you do not know the Scriptures nor the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?
For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like Malakym in Shamaym.

But concerning the dead, that they rise, have you not read in the book 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave Musha, in the burning bush passage, how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH spoke to Musha, saying, ‘I am the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yachaq, and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Ya'aqub’?
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is not the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the dead, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of only the living. You are therefore greatly mistaken.”
Then one of the scribes came, and having heard them reasoning together, perceiving that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had answered them well, he asked Him, “Which is the first commandment of all?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered him, “The first of all the commandments is: ‘Hear, O Yashar'AL, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, is one.
And you must love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment.
And the second is equally important: ‘You must love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
The teacher of religious law replied to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Well said Teacher. You have spoken the truth by saying that there is only one 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and no other.

And I know it is important to love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with all my heart and all my understanding and all my strength, and to love my neighbor as myself. This is more important than to offer all of the burnt offerings and sacrifices required in the law.”
Realizing how much the man understood, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him, “You are not far from the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.” And after that, no one dared to ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA any more questions.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered and said, while He taught in the temple, “How is it that the scribes say that Ha'Mashyach is the Son of Daud?
For Daud himself said by the RUACH Ha'Qadash, he said: ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to my MASTER, “Sit at My right hand, Till I make Your enemies Your footstool.” ’
Therefore Daud himself calls Ha'Mashyach his ‘MASTER’; how is Ha'Mashyach, who is Daud MASTER, now become Daud Son?” the crowd listened to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with great delight.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA also taught them saying: “Beware of these teachers of religious law! For they like to parade around in flowing robes and receive respectful greetings as they walk in the marketplaces.
And how they love the seats of honor in the congregation and the head table at banquets.
Yet they shamelessly cheat widows out of their property and then pretend to be pious by making long prayers in public. Because of this, they will be more severely punished.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat down near the collection box in the Temple and watched as the crowds dropped in their money. Many rich people put in large amounts.
Then a poor widow came and dropped in two small coins.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called His Talmidym to himself and said, “I tell you the truth, this poor widow has given more than all the others who are making contributions.
For they gave a tiny part of their surplus, but this widow, poor as she is, has given everything she had to live on.”
Then as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went out of the temple, one of His Talmidym said to Him, “Teacher, see what manner of stones and what buildings are here!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered and said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone shall be left upon another, that shall not be thrown down.”
Now as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Kafa, Ya'aqub, Yahukanun, and Andraw, asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA privately,
“Tell us, when will these things be? And what will be the sign when all these things will be fulfilled?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, answering them Saying: “Take heed that no one deceives you.
For many will come in My name, saying, I am Ha'Mashyach, and will deceive many.
But when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be troubled; for such things must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and troubles. These are the beginnings of sorrows.
“But watch out for yourselves, for they will deliver you up to councils, and you will be beaten in the congregation. You will be brought before rulers and kings for My sake, for a testimony to them.
And the Basurah (good news) must first be preached to all the nations.

But when they arrest you and deliver you up, do not worry beforehand, or premeditate what you will speak. But whatever is given you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who will speak, but the RUACH Ha'Qadash.
Now brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.
And you will be hated by all for My Name’s sake. But he who endures to the end shall be saved.
“So when you see the ‘abomination of desolation,’ spoken of by Danyal the Nabym, standing where it ought not” “then let those who are in Yahudah flee to the mountains.
Let him who is on the housetop not go down into the house, nor enter to take anything out of his house.
And let him who is in the field not go back to get his clothes.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing babies in those days!
And pray that your flight may not be in winter.
For in those days there will be tribulation, such as has not been since the beginning of the creation which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH created until this time, nor ever shall be.
In fact, unless 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH shortened those days, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen ones, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH chose, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH shortened the days.
“Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is Ha'Mashyach!’ or, ‘Look, He is there!’ do not believe it.
For false Mashyach and false Nabyms will rise and show signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the chosen ones.
But take heed; see, I have told you all things beforehand.
“But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light;
the stars of Shamaym will fall, and the powers in the Shamaym will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds with great power and Kabad.
And then He will send His Malakym, and gather together His chosen ones from the four winds, from the farthest part of Arath to the farthest part of Shamaym.
“Now learn this parable from the fig tree: When its branch has already become tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is near.
So you also, when you see these things happening, know that it is near at the doors!
Assuredly, I say to you, this generation will by no means pass away till all these things take place.
Shamaym and Arath will pass away, but My words will never pass away.
“But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the Malakym in Shamaym, not even the Son, but only ABBA knows the day and hours.
Take heed, watch and pray; for you do not know when the time is.
It is like a man going to a far country, who left his house and gave authority to his servants, and to each his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to watch.
Watch therefore, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, in the evening, at midnight, at the crowing of the rooster, or in the morning
lest, the master coming suddenly, he find you sleeping.
And what I say to you, I say to all: Watch!”
After two days it was the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. And the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA by trickery and put Him to death.
But they said, “Not during the feast, lest there be an uproar of the people.”

And being in Bathany at the house of Simun the leper, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat at the table, a woman came having an alabaster flask of very costly oil of spikenard. Then she broke the flask and poured it on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s head.
But there were some who were indignant among themselves, and said, “Why was this fragrant oil wasted?
For it might have been sold for more than three hundred denarius and given to the poor.” And they criticized her sharply.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Let her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for Me.
For you have the poor with you always, and whenever you wish you may do them good; but Me you do not have always.
She has done what she could. She has come beforehand to anoint My body for burial.
Assuredly, I say to you, wherever this Basurah is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be told as a memorial to her.”
Then Yudas Iscariot, one of the twelve Talmidym, went to the chief Kuhanym to betray 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to them.
And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him money. So Yudas Iscarius sought how he might conveniently betray 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Now on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they killed the Passakh lamb, the Talmidym said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Where do You want us to go and prepare, that You may eat the Passakh?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent out two of His Talmidym and said to them, “Go into the city, and a man will meet you carrying a pitcher of water; follow him.
Wherever he goes in, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room in which I may eat the Passakh with My Talmidym?” ’
Then he will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared; there make ready for us.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s Talmidym went out, and came into the city, and found it just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said to them; and they prepared the Passakh.
In the evening 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came with the twelve Talmidym.
Now as they sat and ate, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Assuredly, I say to you, one of you who eats with Me will betray Me.”
And they began to be sorrowful, and to say to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA one by one, “Is it I?” And another said, “Is it I?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered and said to them, “It is one of the twelve, who dips with Me in the dish.
The Son of Adam must die just as it is written of Him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Adam is betrayed! It would have been good for that man if he had never been born.”
And as they were eating, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took bread and Baraked the bread and broke it, then He gave it to His Talmidym and said, “Take, eat; this is My body.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the cup, and when He had given TUDAH to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH He gave it to his Talmidym, and they all drank from it.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “This is My blood of the renewed covenant, which is shed for many.
Assuredly, I say to you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to his Talmidym, “All of you will be made to stumble because of Me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, And the sheep will be scattered.’
“But after I have been raised, I will go before you to Galily.”
Kafa said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Even if all are made to stumble, yet I will not be.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to Kafa, “Assuredly, I say to you that today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”
But Kafa spoke more vehemently, “If I have to die with You, I will not deny You!”
Then they came to a place which was named Gethsemane; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to His Talmidym, “Sit here while I pray.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took Kafa, Ya'aqub, and Yahukanun with Him, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began to be troubled and deeply distressed.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went a little farther, and fell on the ground, and prayed that if it were possible, the hour might pass from Him.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “ABBA, all things are possible for You. Take this cup away from Me; nevertheless, not what I Will, but what You Will.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came and found his Talmidym sleeping, and said to Kafa, “Simun, are you sleeping? Could you not watch for one hour?
Watch and pray, else you will enter into temptation. The Ruach indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went away and prayed, and spoke the same words.
And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned, He found them still asleep again, for their eyes were heavy; and they did not know what to answer Him.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came the third time and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough! The hour has come; behold, the Son of Adam is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us be going. See, My betrayer is at hand.”
And immediately, while 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was still speaking, Yudas, one of the twelve Talmidym, with a great multitude with swords and clubs, came from the chief Kuhanym and the scribes and the elders.
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA's betrayer had given them a signal, saying, “Whomever I kiss, He is the One; seize Him and lead Him away safely.”
As soon as Yudas had come, immediately he went up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and said to Him, “Rabbi, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
Then they laid their hands on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and took Him.
And one of those who stood by drew his sword and struck the servant of the high Kuhan, and cut off his ear.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered and said to them, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs to take Me?
Why did you not arrest me in the Temple? I was there among you teaching every day. But these things are happening to fulfill what the Scriptures say about me.”
Then the Talmidym all forsook 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and fled.
Now a certain young man followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, having a linen cloth thrown around his naked body. And the young men laid hold of him,
and he left the linen cloth and fled from them naked.
And they led 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA away to the high Kuhan; and with him were assembled all the chief Kuhanym, the elders, and the scribes.
But Kafa followed at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high Kuhan. And Kafa sat with the servants and warmed himself at the fire.
Now the chief Kuhanym and all the council sought testimony against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to put Him to death, but found none.
For many bore false witness against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, but their testimonies did not agree.
Then some rose up and bore false witness against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, saying,
“We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this temple made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.’ ”
But not even then did their testimony agree.
And the high Kuhan stood up in the midst and asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, saying, “Do You answer nothing? What is it these men testify against You?”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA kept silent and answered nothing. Again the high Kuhan asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, saying to Him, “Are You Ha'Mashyach, the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “I Am, and you will see the Son of Adam sitting at the right hand of the Power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and coming on the clouds of Shamaym.”
Then the high Kuhan tore his garment and said, “What further need do we have of witnesses?
You have heard the blasphemy! What do you think? And they all condemned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to be deserving of death.
Then some began to spit on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and they blindfold Him, and they beat Him, and they said to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers struck 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with the palms of their hands.
Now as Kafa was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high Kuhan came.
And when she saw Kafa warming himself, she looked at him and said, “You also were with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of Nazarath.”
But Kafa denied it, saying, “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” And Kafa went out on the porch, and a rooster crowed.
And the servant girl saw Kafa again, and began to say to those who stood by, “This is one of them.”
But Kafa denied it again, and a little later those who stood by said to Kafa again, “Surely you are one of them; for you are a Galilyan, and your speech shows it.”
Then Kafa began to curse and swear, “I do not know this Man of whom you speak!”

A second time the rooster crowed. Then Kafa called to mind the word that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said to him, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.” And when he thought about it, Kafa wept.
Immediately, in the morning, the chief Kuhanym held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council; and they bound 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and led Him away, then they delivered Him to Pilate.
Then Pilate asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Are You the King of the Yahudym?”
And the chief Kuhanym accused 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of many things, but He answered nothing.
Then Pilate asked Him again, saying, “Do You answer nothing? See how many things they testify against You!”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA still answered nothing, so that Pilate marveled.
Now at the feast Pilate was accustomed to releasing one prisoner to them, whomever they requested.
And there was one named Barabbas, who was chained with his fellow rebels; they had committed murder in the rebellion.
Then the multitude, crying aloud, began to ask him to do just as he had always done for them.
But Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Yahudym?”
For Pilate knew that the chief Kuhanym had handed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA over because of envy.
But the chief Kuhanym stirred up the crowd, so that Pilate should rather release Barabbas to them.
Pilate answered and said to them again, “What then do you want me to do with Him whom you call the King of the Yahudym?”
So they cried out again, “Impale 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA!”
Then Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA done?”
So Pilate, wanting to gratify the crowd, released Barabbas to them; and he delivered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, after he had scourged Him, to be impaled.
Then the soldiers led 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA away into the hall called Praaturium, and they called together the whole garrison.
And they clothed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with purple; and they twisted a crown of thorns, put it on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s head,
And began to salute 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Hail, King of the Yahudym!”
Then they struck Him on the head with a reed and spat on Him; and bowing the knee, they worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And when they had mocked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they took the purple off Him, and they put His own clothes on Him, and led Him out to be impaled.
Then they compelled a certain man, Simun a Cyranian, the father of Alaxandar and Rufus, as he was coming out of the country and passing by, to bear the execution stake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And they brought Him to the place Gulgutha, which is translated, Place of a Skull.
Then they gave Him wine mingled with myrrh to drink, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA did not take it.
And when they impaled 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they divided His garment by casting lots for them to determine what every man should take.
Now it was the third hour, and they impaled 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And the inscription of His accusation was written above:
With 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA they also impaled two robbers, one on His right and the other on His left.
So the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was numbered with the transgressors.”
And those who passed by blasphemed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, wagging their heads and saying, “Aha! You who destroy the temple and build it in three days,
Save Yourself, and come down from the execution Stake!”
Likewise the chief Kuhanym also, mocking among themselves with the scribes, said, “He saved others; but He cannot save Himself.
Let Ha'Mashyach, the King of Yashar'AL, descend now from the execution Stake, that we may see and believe. Even those who were impaled with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA taunted Him.
Now when the sixth hour had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA cried out with a loud voice, saying, “ALy, ALy, Lamah Zabachthani?” which is translated, “My 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, My 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, why have You forsaken Me?”
Some of those who stood by, when they heard that, said, “Look, He is calling for AliYahu!”
Then someone ran and filled a sponge full of sour wine, put it on a reed, and offered it to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to drink, saying, “Let Him alone; let us see if AliYahu will come to take Him down.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA cried out with a loud voice, and breathed His last breath.
Then the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
So when the centurion, who stood opposite 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, saw that He cried out like this and breathed His last, he said, “Truly this Man was the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
There were also women looking on from afar, among whom were Maryam Magdalyn, Maryam the mother of Ya'aqub the younger and of Ya'asaf, and Saluma.
They had been followers of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and had cared for Him while He was in Galily. Many other women who had come with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to Yahushalam were also there.
Now when evening had come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Shabbat,
Ya'asaf of Arimathaa took a risk and went to Pilate and asked for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s body. (Ya'asaf was an honored member of the high council, and he was waiting for the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to come.)
Pilate could not believe that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was already dead, so he called for the Roman officer and asked if he had died yet.
The officer confirmed that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was dead, so Pilate told Ya'asaf he could have the body.

Ya'asaf bought a long sheet of linen cloth. Then Ya'asaf took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s body down from the impaled Stake, and Ya'asaf wrapped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s body in the cloth, and laid it in a tomb that had been carved out of the rock. Then Ya'asaf rolled a stone in front of the entrance.
Maryam Magdalana and Maryam the mother of Ya'asaf saw where the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was laid.
Now when the Shabbat was past, Maryam Magdalyn, Maryam the mother of Ya'aqub, and Saluma bought spices, that they might come and anoint 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Very early in the morning, on the first day of the week, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
And they said among themselves, “Who will roll away the stone from the door of the tomb for us?”
But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was very large.
And entering the tomb, they saw a young man clothed in a long white robe sitting on the right side; and they were alarmed.
But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of Nazarath, who was impaled. He is risen! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is not here. See the place where they laid Him.
But go, tell His Talmidym and Kafa that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is going before you into Galily; there you will see Him, as He said to you.”
So they went out quickly and fled from the tomb, for they trembled and were amazed. And they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
Now when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rose early on the first day of the week, He appeared first to Maryam Magdalyn, of whom He had cast out seven demons.
She went and told those who had been with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, as they mourned and wept.
