And when they heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe.
After that, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA appeared in another form to two of them as they walked and went into the country.
And they went and told it to the rest, but they did not believe them either.

Later 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA appeared to the eleven Talmidym as they sat at the table; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the Basurah (Good News) to everyone, everywhere
He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who does not believe will be condemned.
And these signs will follow those who believe: In My Name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new tongues;
They will take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will by no means hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
So then, after 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had spoken to them, He was received up into Shamaym, and sat down at the right hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And they went out and preached everywhere, The RUACH HA'QADASH working through them, confirming what they said by many miraculous signs.

books.name: Luke
chapters: Many people have set out to write accounts about the events that have been fulfilled among us.
They used the eyewitness reports circulating among us from the early Talmidym.
Having carefully investigated everything from the beginning, I also have decided to write a careful account for you, most honorable Thauphilus,
so you can be certain of the truth of everything you were taught.
When Harud was king of Yahudah, there was a Yahudym Kuhan named Zacharyahu. He was a member of the Kuhanym order of Abiyahu, and his wife, Alizabath, was also from the Kuhanym line of Aarun.
Zacharyahu and Alizabath were righteous in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s eyes, careful to obey all of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s commandments and regulations.
They had no children because Alizabath was unable to conceive, and they were both very old.
One day Zacharyahu was serving 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the Temple, for his order was on duty that week.
As was the custom of the Kuhanym, he was chosen by lot to enter the sanctuary of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and burn incense.
While the incense was being burned, a great crowd stood outside, praying.
While Zacharyahu was in the sanctuary, a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared to Zacharyahu, standing to the right of the incense altar.
Zacharyahu was shaken and overwhelmed with fear when he saw the Malak.
And the Malak said, “Do not be afraid, Zacharyahu! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has heard your prayer. Your wife, Alizabath, will give you a son, and you are to name him Yahukanun.
You will have great joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth,
for he will be great in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he must never touch wine or other alcoholic drinks, he will be filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash, even before his birth.
And he will turn many Yasharalym to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.

He will be a man with the Ruach and power of AliYahu, he will prepare the people for the coming of Ha'Mashyach. He will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children, and he will cause those who are rebellious to accept the wisdom of the righteous.”
Zacharyahu said to the Malak, “How can I be sure this will happen? I am an old man now, and my wife is also well along in years.”
Then the Malak said, “I am Gabri'AL! I stand in the very presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. It was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who sent me to bring you this good news!
But now, since you did not believe what I said, you will be silent and unable to speak until the child is born. For my words will certainly be fulfilled at the proper time.”

Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zacharyahu to come out of the sanctuary, wondering why he was taking so long. 22 When Zacharyahu finally did come out, he could not speak to them. Then they realized from his gestures and his silence that he must have seen a vision in the sanctuary.
When Zacharyahu’s week of service in the Temple was over, he returned home.
Soon afterward Zacharyahu‘s wife Alizabath, became pregnant and went into seclusion for five months.
“How kind 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is!” she exclaimed. “He has taken away my shame of having no children.”
In the sixth month of Alizabath’s pregnancy, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent the Malak Gabri'AL to Nazarath, a village in Galily,
to a virgin named Maryam. She was engaged to be married to a man named Ya'asaf, a descendant of King Daud.
The Malak Gabri'AL appeared to Maryam and said, “Greetings, favored woman! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with you!”
Confused and disturbed, Maryam tried to think what the Malak could mean. 30 “Do not be afraid, Maryam,” the Malak Gabri'AL told her, “for you have found favor with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will name him 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
He will be very great and will be called the Son of AL'ALYUN (the Most High), 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give him the throne of his ancestor Daud.
And he will reign over Yashar'AL forever; his Kingdom will never end!”
Maryam asked the Malak Gabri'AL, “But how can this happen? I am a virgin.”

The Malak Gabri'AL replied, “The RUACH Ha'Qadash will come upon you, and the power of AL'ALYUN (the most high) will overshadow you. So the baby to be born will be Qadash, and he will be called the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
What’s more, your relative Alizabath has become pregnant in her old age! People used to say she was barren, but she has conceived a son and is now in her sixth month.
For the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will never fail.”
Maryam responded, “I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s servant. May everything you have said about me come true.” And then the Malak Gabri'AL left her.
A few days later Maryam hurried to the hill country of Yahudah, to the town
where Zacharyahu lived. She entered the house and greeted Alizabath.
At the sound of Maryam’s greeting, Alizabath’s child leaped within her, and Alizabath was filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash.
Alizabath gave a glad cry and exclaimed to Maryam, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has baraked you above all women, and your child is baraked.
Why am I so honored, that the mother of my Master should visit me?
When I heard your greeting, the baby in my womb jumped for joy.
You are baraked because you believed that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH would do what He Dabar.”
Maryam responded,
How my ruach rejoices in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH my Savior!
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH took notice of His lowly servant girl, and from now on all generations will call me baraked.
For the Mighty One is Qadash, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done great things for me.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH shows mercy from generation to generation to all who fear HIM.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH's mighty arm has done tremendous things! He has scattered the proud and haughty ones.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has brought down princes from their thrones and exalted the humble.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away with empty hands.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has helped HIS servant Yashar'AL and remembered to be merciful.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made this promise to our ancestors, to Abraham and his children forever.”
Maryam stayed with Alizabath about three months and then went back to her own home.
When it was time for Alizabath’s baby to be born, she gave birth to a son.
And when her neighbors and relatives heard that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had been very merciful to her, everyone rejoiced with her.
When the baby was eight days old, they all came for the circumcision ceremony. They wanted to name him Zacharyahu, after his father.
But Alizabath said, “No! His name is Yahukanun!”
“What?” they exclaimed. “There is no one in all your family by that name.”
So they used gestures to ask the baby’s father what he wanted to name him.
He motioned for a writing tablet, and to everyone’s surprise he wrote, “His name is Yahukanun.”
Instantly Zacharyahu could speak again, and he began to Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Awe fell upon the whole neighborhood, and the news of what had happened spread throughout the Yahudym. 66 Everyone who heard about it reflected on these events and asked, “What will this child turn out to be?” For the hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was surely upon him in a special way.
Then Yahukanun father, Zacharyahu, was filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash and gave this prophecy:
“Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yashar'AL, because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has visited and redeemed his people.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent us a mighty Savior from the royal line of his servant King Daud,
just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH promised through his Qadash Nabyms long ago.
Now we will be saved from our enemies and from all who hate us.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has been merciful to our ancestors by remembering His sacred covenant
the covenant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH swore with an oath to our ancestor Abraham.
We have been rescued from our enemies so we can serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH without fear,
In Qadash and righteousness for as long as we live.
“And you, my little son, will be called the Nabym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, because you will prepare the way for Ha'Mashyach.
You will tell 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s people how to find salvation through forgiveness of their sins.
Because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s tender mercy, the morning light from Shamaym is about to break upon us,
To give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, and to guide us to the path of Shalum.”
Yahukanun grew up and became strong in Ruach. And he lived in the wilderness until he began his public ministry to Yashar'AL.
At that time the Roman emperor, Augustus, decreed that a census should be taken throughout the Roman Empire. 2 (This was the first census taken when Quirinius was governor of Syria.)
All returned to their own ancestral towns to register for this census.
And because Ya'asaf was a descendant of King Daud, he had to go to Bathlaham in Yahudah, Daud’s ancient home. He traveled there from the village of Nazarath in Galily.
Ya'asaf took with him Maryam, his fiancée, who was now obviously pregnant.
And while they were there, the time came for her baby to be born.
She gave birth to her first child, a son. She wrapped him snugly in strips of cloth and laid him in a manger, because there was no lodging available for them.
That night there were shepherds staying in the fields nearby, guarding their flocks of sheep.
Suddenly, a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared among them, and the radiance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Kabad surrounded them. They were terrified,
But the Malak reassured them. “Do not be afraid!” he said. “I bring you good news that will bring great joy to all people.
The Savior yes, Ha'Mashyach has been born today in Bathlaham, the city of Daud!
And you will recognize him by this sign: You will find a baby wrapped snugly in strips of cloth, lying in a manger.”
Suddenly, the Malak was joined by a vast host of other Malakym the armies of Shamaym Yadahym 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and saying,
“Kabad to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in highest Shamaym, and Shalum on Arath to those with whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is pleased.”
When the Malakym had returned to Shamaym, the shepherds said to each other, “Let us go to Bathlaham! Let us see this thing that has happened, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has told us about.”
They hurried to the village and found Maryam and Ya'asaf. And there was the baby, lying in the manger.
After seeing him, the shepherds told everyone what had happened and what the Malak had said to them about this child.
All who heard the shepherd's story were astonished,
but Maryam kept all these things in her heart and thought about them often.
The shepherds went back to their flocks, joyfully and they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for all they had heard and seen. It was just as the Malak had told them.
Eight days later, when the baby was circumcised, he was named 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the name given him by the Malak Gabri'AL who appeared to Maryam even before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was conceived.

Then it was time for their purification offering, as required by the law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH through Musha after the birth of a child; so his parents took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to Yahushalam to present 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH says, “If a woman’s first child is a boy, he must be dedicated to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So they offered the sacrifice required in the law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, “either a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
At that time there was a man in Yahushalam named Simaun, he was righteous and devout and was eagerly waiting for Ha'Mashyach to come and rescue Yashar'AL, the RUACH Ha'Qadash was upon him
And had revealed to him that he would not die until he had seen Ha'Mashyach.
That day the RUACH led him to the Temple. So when Maryam and Ya'asaf came to present the baby 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as the law required,
Simaun was there. He took the child in his arms and Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, saying,
“O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, now let your servant die in Shalum, as you have promised.
I have seen your salvation,
Which you have prepared for all men.
He is a light to reveal 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to the nations, and he is the Kabad of your people Yashar'AL!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s parents were amazed at what was being said about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.

Then Simaun baraked them, and he said to Maryam, the baby’s mother, “This child is destined to cause many in Yashar'AL to fall, but he will be a joy to many others. He has been sent as a sign from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but many will oppose him.
As a result, the deepest thoughts of many hearts will be revealed. And a sword will pierce your very soul.”
Anna, a Nabym, was also there in the Temple. She was the daughter of Phanual from the tribe of Ashar, and she was very old. Her husband died when they had been married only seven years.
Then she lived as a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the Temple but stayed there day and night, worshiping 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with fasting and prayer.

She came along just as Simaun was talking with Maryam and Ya'asaf, and she began to Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. She talked about the child to everyone who had been waiting expectantly for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to rescue Yahushalam.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s parents had fulfilled all the requirements of the law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, they returned home to Nazarath in Galily.
There the child grew up healthy and strong. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was filled with wisdom, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s favor was on him.
Every year 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s parents went to Yahushalam for the Passakh festival.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was twelve years old, they attended the festival as usual.
After the celebration was over, they started going home to Nazarath, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA stayed behind in Yahushalam. His parents did not miss him at first,
because they assumed he was among the other travelers. But when he did not show up that evening, they started looking for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA among their relatives and friends.
When they could not find him, they went back to Yahushalam to search for him there.
Three days later they finally discovered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in the Temple, sitting among the religious teachers, listening to them and asking questions.
All who heard 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
For his parents did not know what to think. “Son,” his mother said to him, “why have you done this to us? Your father and I have been frantic, searching for you everywhere.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “But why did you need to search? “Did you not know that I must be in my ABBA’s house?”
But they did not understand what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA meant.
Then he returned to Nazarath with them and was obedient to them. And his mother stored all these things in her heart.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA grew in wisdom and in stature and in favor with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and all the people.

It was now the fifteenth year of the reign of Tibarius, the Roman emperor. Puntius Pilate was governor over Yahudah; Harud Antipas was ruler over Galily; his brother Philip was ruler over Iturea and Tracunitis; Lysanias was ruler over Abilana.
Annas and Caiaphas were the high Kuhanym. At this time a message from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came to Yahukanun son of Zacharyahu, who was living in the wilderness.

Then Yahukanun went from place to place on both sides of the Yurdan River, preaching that people should be baptized to show that they had repented of their sins and turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to be forgiven.
Yashayahu had spoken of Yahukanun when he said, “He is a voice shouting in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for Ha'Mashyach’s coming! Clear the road for Ha'Mashyach!
The valleys will be filled, and the mountains and hills made level. The curves will be straightened, and the rough places made smooth.
And then all people will see the salvation sent from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’”
Then Yahukanun said to the multitudes that came out to be baptized by him, “Brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

Prove by the way you live that you have repented of your sins and turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Do not just say to each other, ‘We are safe, for we are descendants of Abraham. being a descendants to Abraham means nothing, for I tell you, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH can create children of Abraham from these very stones.
Even now the ax of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s judgment is poised, ready to sever the roots of the trees. Yes, every tree that does not produce good fruit will be chopped down and thrown into the fire.”
The crowds asked, “What should we do?”
Yahukanun replied, “If you have two shirts, give one to the poor. If you have food, share it with those who are hungry.”
Even corrupt tax collectors came to be baptized and asked, “Teacher, what should we do?”
Yahukanun replied, “Collect no more taxes than the government requires.”
“What should we do?” asked some soldiers. And Yahukanun replied, “Do not extort money or make false accusations. And be content with your pay.”
Everyone was expecting Ha'Mashyach to come soon, and they were eager to know whether Yahukanun might be Ha'Mashyach.

And Yahukanun answered their questions by saying, “I baptize you with water; but someone is coming soon who is greater than I am, so much greater that I am not even worthy to be his slave and untie the straps of his sandals. He will baptize you with the RUACH Ha'Qadash and with fire.
He is ready to separate the chaff from the wheat with his winnowing fork. Then he will clean up the threshing area, gathering the wheat into his barn but burning the chaff with never ending fire.”
Yahukanun used many such warnings as he announced the Good News to the people.
Yahukanun also publicly criticized Harud Antipas, the ruler of Galily, for marrying Harudias, his brother’s wife, and for many other wrongs he had done.
So Harud put Yahukanun in prison, adding this sin to his many others.
One day when the crowds were being baptized, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA himself was baptized. As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was praying, the Shamaym opened,
and the RUACH Ha'Qadash, in bodily form, descended on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA like a dove. And a voice from Shamaym said, “You are my dearly loved Son, and you bring me great joy.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was about thirty years old when he began His public ministry. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was known as the son of Ya'asaf. And Ya'asaf was the son of Hali.
Hali was the son of Mattatyahu and Mattatyahu was the son of Lauy and Lauy was the son of Malki and Malki was the son of Yannai and Yannai was the son of Ya'asaf.
Ya'asaf was the son of Mattathias, and Mattathias was the son of Amus and Amus was the son of Nahum and Nahum was the son of Asli and Asli was the son of Naggai.
Naggai was the son of Maath and Maath was the son of Mattathias and Mattathias was the son of Samain and Samain was the son of Yusach and Yusach was the son of Yuda.
Yuda was the son of Yuanan and Yuanan was the son of Rhasa and Rhasa was the son of Zarubbabal and Zerubbabel was the son of Shaaltial and Shaaltial was the son of Nari.
Nari was the son of Malki and Malki was the son of Addi and Addi was the son of Cusam and Cusam was the son of Almadam and Almadam was the son of Ar.
Ar was the son of Yushua and Yushua was the son of Aliazar and Aliazar was the son of Yurim and Yurim was the son of Mattatyahu and Mattatyahu was the son of Lauy.
Lauy was the son of Simaun and Simaun was the son of Yahudah and Yahudah was the son of Ya'asaf and Ya'asaf was the son of Yunam and Yunam was the son of Aliakim.
Aliakim was the son of Malaa and Malaa was the son of Manna and Manna was the son of Mattatha and Mattatha was the son of Nathan and Nathan was the son of Daud.
Daud was the son of Yassa and Yassa was the son of Ubad and Ubad was the son of Buaz and Buaz was the son of Salmun and Salmun was the son of Nahshun.
Nahshun was the son of Amminadab and Amminadab was the son of Admin and Admin was the son of Arni and Arni was the son of Hazrun and Hazrun was the son of Paraz and Perez was the son of Yahudah.
Yahudah was the son of Ya'aqub and Ya'aqub was the son of Yachaq and Yachaq was the son of Abraham and Abraham was the son of Tarah and Tarah was the son of Nahur.
Nahor was the son of Sarug and Sarug was the son of Rau and Rau was the son of Palag and Palag was the son of Abar and Abar was the son of Shalah.
Shalah was the son of Cainan and Cainan was the son of Arphaxad and Arphaxad was the son of Sham and Sham was the son of Nuah and Nuah was the son of Lamach.
Lamach was the son of Mathusalah and Mathusalah was the son of Chanuk and Chanuk was the son of Yarad and Yarad was the son of Mahalalal and Mahalalal was the son of Kanan.
Kanan was the son of Anush and Anush was the son of Sath and Sath was the son of Adam and Adam was the son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, full of the RUACH Ha'Qadash, returned from the Yurdan River and He was led by the RUACH into the wilderness,
where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was tempted by ha'shatan for forty days. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA ate nothing all that time and became very hungry.
Then ha'shatan said to Him, “If you are the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, tell this stone to become a loaf of bread.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told ha'shatan, “No! The Scriptures says, ‘man shall not live by bread alone.’” {Dabarym 8:3}
Then ha'shatan took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA up and revealed to Him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
“I will give you all the power of these kingdoms and authority over them,” ha'shatan said, “because they are mine to give to anyone I please.
I will give it all to you if you will worship me.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “The Scriptures say, ‘You must worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and serve only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’” {Dabarym 6:13 & 10:20}
Then ha'shatan took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to Yahushalam, to the highest point of the Temple, and said, “If you are the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, jump off!
For the Scriptures say, ‘He will order his Malakym to protect and guard you. {Tahalym 91:11}
And they will hold you up with their hands so you will not even hurt your foot on a stone.’” {Tahalym 91:12}
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA responded, “The Scriptures also say, ‘You must not test 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.’” {Dabarym 6:16}
When ha'shatan had finished tempting 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, he left him until the next opportunity came.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned to Galily, filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash's power. Reports about Him spread quickly through the whole region.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA taught regularly in their congregation and was praised by everyone.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came to the village of Nazarath, his boyhood home, he went as usual to the congregation on the Shabbat and stood up to read the Scriptures.
The scroll of Yashayahu the Nabym was handed to Him. He unrolled the scroll and found the place where this was written:

“The Ruach of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is upon me, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has anointed me to bring Good News to the poor, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent me to proclaim that captives will be released, that the blind will see, that the oppressed will be set free,
And the time of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s favor has come.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rolled up the scroll, handed it back to the attendant, and sat down. All eyes in the congregation looked at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA intently.
Then He began to speak to them. “The Scripture you have just heard has been fulfilled this very day!”
Everyone spoke well of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and was amazed by the courageous words that came from His lips. “How can this be?” they asked. “Is this not Ya'asaf’s son?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “You will undoubtedly quote me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself’, meaning, ‘Do miracles here in your hometown like those you did in Capernaum.’
But I tell you the truth, no Nabym is accepted in his own hometown.
“Certainly there were many needy widows in Yashar'AL in AliYahu’s time, when the Shamaym were closed for three and a half years, and a severe famine devastated the land.
Yet AliYahu was not sent to any of them. AliYahu was sent instead to a foreigner, a widow of Zaraphath in the land of Sidun.
And there were many lepers in Yashar'AL in the time of the Nabym Alishah, but the only one healed was Naaman, a Syrian.”
When they heard this, the people in the congregation were furious.
Jumping up, they mobbed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and forced him to the edge of the hill on which the town was built. They intended to push Him over the cliff,
but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA passed right through the crowd and went on his way.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went to Caparnaum, a town in Galily, and taught there in the congregation every Shabbat day.
There, too, the people were amazed at His teaching, for He spoke with authority.
Then when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was in the congregation, a man possessed by a demon an evil spirit began shouting at Him,
“Go away! Why are you interfering with us, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of Nazarath? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are, the Qadash One of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA cut the possessed man short. “Be quiet! And Come out of the man,” He ordered. At that, the demon threw the man to the floor as the crowd watched; then it came out of him without hurting him further.
Amazed, the people exclaimed, “What authority and power this man’s words possess! Even evil spirits obey Him, and they flee at His command!”
The news about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spread through every village in the entire region.
After leaving the congregation that day, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went to Simun’s home, where he found Simun’s mother-in-law very sick with a high fever. “Please heal her,” everyone begged.
Standing at her bedside, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rebuked the fever, and it left her. And she got up at once and prepared a meal for them.
As the sun went down that evening, people throughout the village brought sick family members to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. No matter what their diseases were, the touch of His hand healed every one.

Many were possessed by demons; and the demons came out at His command, shouting, “You are the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!” But because they knew 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was Ha'Mashyach, He rebuked them and refused to let them speak.
Early the next morning 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went out to an isolated place. The crowds searched everywhere for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and when they finally found Him, they begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA not to leave them.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “I must preach the Good News of the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in other towns, too, because that is why I was sent.”
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA continued to travel around, preaching in congregations throughout Yahudah.
One day as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was preaching on the shore of the Sea of Galily, great crowds pressed in on him to listen to the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA noticed two empty boats at the water’s edge, for the fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
Stepping into one of the boats, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked Simun, its owner, to push it out into the water. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat in the boat and taught the crowds from there.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had finished speaking, He said to Simun, “Now go out where it is deeper, and let down your nets to catch some fish.”
“Simun replied, Master “we worked hard all last night and did not catch a thing. But if you say so, at your words, I will let the nets down again.”
And this time their nets were so full of fish they began to tear!
A shout for help brought their partners in the other boat, and soon both boats were filled with fish and on the verge of sinking.
When Simun Kafa realized what had happened, he fell to his knees before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and said, “Oh, Master, please leave me, I am too much of a sinner to be around you.”
For he was awestruck by the number of fish they had caught, as were the others with him.
His partners, Ya'aqub and Yahukanun, the sons of Zabadyahu, were also amazed.
And as soon as they landed, they left everything and they followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.

In one of the villages, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA met a man with an advanced case of leprosy. When the man saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, he bowed with his face to the ground, begging to be healed. “Master,” he said, “if you are willing, you can heal me and make me clean.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA reached out and touched him. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. “I am willing, “Be healed!” And instantly the leprosy disappeared.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA instructed him not to tell anyone what had happened. He said, “Go to the Kuhan and let him examine you. Take along the offering required in the law for those who have been healed of leprosy. This will be a public testimony that you have been cleansed.”
But despite 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s instructions, the report of his power spread even faster, and vast crowds came to hear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA preach and to be healed of their diseases.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA often withdrew to the wilderness for prayer.

One day while 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was teaching, some Pharisees and teachers of religious law were sitting nearby. (It seemed that these men showed up from every village in all Galily and Yahudah, as well as from Yahushalam.) And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s healing power was strongly with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a sleeping mat. They tried to take him inside to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA,

but they could not reach 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA because of the crowd. So they went up to the roof and took off some tiles. Then they lowered the sick man on his mat down into the crowd, right in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And seeing their Amunah, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the man, “Young man, your sins are forgiven.”
But the Pharisees and teachers of religious law said to themselves, “Who does he think he is? That is blasphemy! Only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH can forgive sins!”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew what they were thinking, so He asked them, “Why do you question this in your hearts?
Is it easier to say ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or ‘Stand up and walk’?
So I will prove to you that the Son of Adam has the authority on Arath to forgive sins.” Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to the paralyzed man and said, “Stand up, pick up your mat, and go home!”
And immediately, as everyone watched, the man jumped up, picked up his mat, and went home and they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Everyone was gripped with great wonder and awe, and they also Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, exclaiming, “We have seen amazing things today!”
Later, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left the town, he saw a tax collector named Lauy sitting at his tax collector’s booth. “Follow me and be one of my Talmid,” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him.
So Lauy got up, left everything, and followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Later, Lauy held a banquet in his home with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA as the guest of honor. Many of Lauy’s fellow tax collectors and other guests also ate with them.
But the Pharisees and their teachers of religious law complained bitterly to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s Talmidym, “Why do you eat and drink with such scum?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered them, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, sick people do.
I have come to call not those who think they are righteous, but those who know they are sinners and need to repent.”
One day some people said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Yahukanun the Baptist’s followers fast and pray regularly, and so do the followers of the Pharisees. Why are your Talmidym always eating and drinking?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA responded, “Do wedding guests fast while celebrating with the groom? Of course not.
But someday the groom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave them this illustration: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old garment. If he does, the new cloth will tear, and the piece from the new cloth will not match the old cloth.
“And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. For the new wine would burst the wineskins, spilling the wine and ruining the skins.
New wine must be stored in new wineskins.
But no one who drinks the old wine seems to want the new wine. ‘The old is just fine,’ they say.”
One Shabbat day as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was walking through some grainfields, His Talmidym broke off heads of grain, rubbed off the husks in their hands, and ate the grain.
But some Pharisees said, “Why are you breaking the law by harvesting grain on the Shabbat?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Have you not read in the Scriptures what Daud did when he and his companions were hungry?
He went into the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and broke the law by eating the sacred loaves of bread that only the Kuhanym can eat. He also gave some to his companions.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA added, “The Son of Adam is High Kuhan, even over the Shabbat.”
On another Shabbat day, a man with a deformed right hand was in the congregation while 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was teaching.
The teachers of religious law and the Pharisees watched 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA closely. If He would heal the man’s hand, they planned to accuse 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of working on the Shabbat.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew their thoughts, and He said to the man with the deformed hand, “Come and stand in front of everyone.” So the man came forward.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to His critics, “I have a question for you. Does the law permit good deeds on the Shabbat, or is it a day for doing evil? Is this a day to save life or to destroy it?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked around at them one by one and then said to the man, “Hold out your hand.” So the man held out his hand, and it was restored!
At this, the enemies of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA were wild with rage and began to discuss what to do with Him.
One day soon afterward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went up on a mountain to pray, and He prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH all night.
At daybreak 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called together all of His Talmidym and chose twelve of them to be Shaliach (apostles). Here are their names:
Simun (whom he named Kafa), Andraw (Kafa’s brother), Ya'aqub, Yahukanun, Philip, Barthulumaw,
Mattatyahu, Thumas, Ya'aqub (son of Alphaus), Simun (who was called the zaalut),
Yahudah's (son of Ya'aqub), Yudas Iscariot (who later betrayed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA).

When they came down from the mountain, the Talmidym stood with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA on a large, level area, surrounded by many of his followers and by the crowds. There were people from all over Yahudah and from Yahushalam and from as far north as the seacoasts of Tyra and Sidun.
They had come to hear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and to be healed of their diseases; and those troubled by evil spirits were healed.
Everyone tried to touch 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, because healing power went out from him, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA healed everyone.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to his Talmidym and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Barak you who are poor, for the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is yours.
Baraked are you who hunger now, For you shall be filled. Baraked are you who weep now, For you shall laugh.
Baraked are you when men hate you, And when they exclude you, And revile you, and cast out your name as evil, For the Son of Man’s sake.
Rejoice in that day and leap for joy! For indeed your reward is great in Shamaym, For in like manner their fathers did to the Nabym.
“What sorrow awaits you who are rich, for you have your only happiness now.
What sorrow awaits you who are fat and prosperous now, for a time of awful hunger awaits you. What sorrow awaits you who laugh now, for your laughing will turn to mourning and sorrow.
What sorrow awaits you who are praised by the crowds, for their ancestors also praised false Nabyms.
“But to you who are willing to listen, I say, love your enemies! Do good to those who hate you.
Barak those who curse you. Pray for those who hurt you.
If someone slaps you on one cheek, offer the other cheek also. If someone demands your coat, offer your shirt also.
Give to anyone who asks; and when things are taken away from you, do not try to get them back.
Do to others as you would like them to do to you.
“If you love only those who love you, why should you get credit for that? Even sinners love those who love them!
And if you do good only to those who do good to you, why should you get credit? Even sinners do that much!
And if you lend money only to those who can repay you, why should you get credit? Even sinners will lend to other sinners for a full return.

“Love your enemies! Do good to them. Lend to them without expecting to be repaid. Then your reward from Shamaym will be very great, and you will truly be acting as children of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is kind to those who are unthankful and wicked.
You must be compassionate, just as your ABBA is compassionate.
“Do not judge others, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn others, or it will all come back against you. Forgive others, and you will be forgiven.

Give, and you will receive. Your gift will return to you in full pressed down, shaken together to make room for more, running over, and poured into your lap. The amount you give will determine the amount you get back.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave the following illustration: “Can one blind person lead another? Will they not both fall into a ditch?
Students are not greater than their teacher. But the student who is fully trained will become like the teacher.
“And why worry about a speck in your friend’s eye when you have a log in your own?

How can you think of saying, ‘Friend, let me help you get rid of that speck in your eye,’ when you cannot see past the log in your own eye? Hypocrite! First get rid of the log in your own eye; then you will see well enough to deal with the speck in your friend’s eye.

“A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot produce good fruit. 44 A tree is identified by its fruit. Figs are never gathered from thornbushes, and grapes are not picked from bramble bushes.
A good person produces good things from the treasury of a good heart, and an evil person produces evil things from the treasury of an evil heart. What you say flows from what is in your heart.
“So why do you keep calling me ‘Master, Master!’ when you do not do what I say?
I will show you what it is like when someone comes to me, listens to my teaching, and then follows it.
It is like a person building a house who digs deep and lays the foundation on solid rock. When the floodwaters rise and break against that house, it stands firm because it is well built.
But anyone who hears and does not obey is like a person who builds a house without a foundation. When the floods sweep down against that house, it will collapse into a heap of ruins.”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had finished saying all this to the people, He returned to Caparnaum.
At that time the highly valued slave of a Roman officer was sick and near death.
When the officer heard about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, he sent some respected Yahudym elders to ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to come and heal his slave.
So they earnestly begged .𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to help the man. “If anyone deserves your help, he does,” they said,
“for he loves the Yahudym people and even built a synagogue for us.”

So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went with them. But just before they arrived at the house, the officer sent some friends to say, “Master, do not trouble yourself by coming to my home, for I am not worthy of such an honor.
I am not even worthy to come and meet you. Just say the word from where you are, and my servant will be healed.

I know this because I am under the authority of my superior officers, and I have authority over my soldiers. I only need to say, ‘Go,’ and they go, or ‘Come,’ and they come. And if I say to my slaves, ‘Do this,’ they do it.”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard this, He was amazed. Turning to the crowd that was following him, He said, “I tell you, I have not seen Amunah (faith) like this in all Yashar'AL!
And when the officer’s friends returned to his house, they found the slave completely healed.
Soon afterward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went with His Talmidym to the village of Nain, and a large crowd followed Him.
A funeral procession was coming out as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA approached the village gate. The young man who had died was a widow’s only son, and a large crowd from the village was with her.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw her, His heart overflowed with compassion, and He said “Do not cry!”.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA walked over to the coffin and touched it, and the bearers stopped, and He said “Young man, “I say to you, rise up.”
Then the dead boy sat up and began to talk! And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave him back to his mother.
Great fear swept the crowd, and they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, saying, “A mighty Nabym has risen among us,” and “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has visited his people today.”
And the news about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spread throughout Yahudah and the surrounding countryside.
The followers of Yahukanun the Baptist told Yahukanun about everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was doing. So Yahukanun called for two of his followers,
and Yahukanun sent them to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to ask Him, “Are you Ha'Mashyach we have been expecting, or should we keep looking for someone else?”
Yahukanun’s two followers found 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and said to him, “Yahukanun the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are you Ha'Mashyach we have been expecting, or should we keep looking for someone else?’”
At that very time, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA cured many people of their diseases, illnesses, and evil spirits, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA restored sight to many who were blind.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told Yahukanun’s followers, “Go back to Yahukanun and tell him what you have seen and heard, the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cured, the deaf hear, the dead are raised to life, and the Good News is being preached to the poor.
And tell him, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Baraked those who do not turn away because of me.’”
After Yahukanun’s followers left, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began talking about Yahukanun to the crowds. What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
Or were you expecting to see a man dressed in expensive clothes? No, people who wear beautiful clothes and live in luxury are found in palaces.
Were you looking for a Nabym? Yes, and he is more than a Nabym.
Yahukanun is the man to whom the Scriptures refer when they say, ‘Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, and he will prepare your way before you.’
I tell you, of all who have ever lived, none is greater than Yahukanun. Yet even the least person in the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is greater than he is!”
When they heard this, all the people even the tax collectors, agreed that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s way was right, for they had been baptized by Yahukanun.
But the Pharisees and experts in religious law rejected 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s plan for them, for they had refused Yahukanun’s baptism.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “To what can I compare the people of this generation?” “How can I describe them?
They are like children playing a game in the public square. They complain to their friends, ‘We played wedding songs, and you did not dance, so we played funeral songs, and you did not weep.’
For Yahukanun the Baptist did not spend his time eating bread or drinking wine, and you say, ‘He is possessed by a demon.’
The Son of Adam, on the other hand, feasts and drinks, and you say, ‘He is a glutton and a drunkard, and a friend of tax collectors and other sinners!’
But wisdom is shown to be right by the lives of those who follow it.”
One of the Pharisees asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to have dinner with him, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went to his home and sat down to eat.
When a certain immoral woman from that city heard 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was eating there, she brought a beautiful alabaster jar filled with expensive perfume.
Then she knelt behind 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA at his feet, weeping. Her tears fell on His feet, and she wiped them off with her hair. Then she kept kissing His feet and putting perfume on them.
When the Pharisee who had invited 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a Nabym, he would know what kind of woman is touching him. She is a sinner!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered his thoughts. And said to the Pharisee, “Simun,” “I have something to say to you.” “Go ahead, Teacher,” Simun replied.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told him this story: “A man loaned money to two people, five hundred pieces of silver to one and fifty pieces to the other.
But neither of them could repay him, so he kindly forgave them both, canceling their debts. Who do you suppose loved the man more after that?”
Simun answered, “I suppose the one for whom he canceled the larger debt.” and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him

Then he turned to the woman and said to Simun, “Look at this woman kneeling here. When I entered your home, you did not offer me water to wash the dust from my feet, but she has washed them with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You did not greet me with a kiss, but from the time I first came in, she has not stopped kissing my feet.
You neglected the courtesy of olive oil to anoint my head, but she has anointed my feet with rare perfume.
“I tell you, her sins are many, they have been forgiven, so she has shown me much love. But a person who is forgiven little shows only little love.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the woman, “Your sins are forgiven.”
The men at the table said among themselves, “Who is this man, that he goes around forgiving sins?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the woman, “Your Amunah has saved you; go in Shalum.”
Soon afterward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began a tour of the nearby towns and villages, preaching and announcing the Good News about the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. and He took His twelve Talmidym with Him,
Along with some women who had been cured of evil spirits and diseases. Among them were Mary Magdalyn, from whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had cast out seven demons;
Yuanna, the wife of Chuza, Harud’s business manager; Susanna; and many others who were contributing from their own resources to support 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and his Talmidym.
One day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told a story in the form of a parable to a large crowd that had gathered from many towns to hear him:
“A farmer went out to plant his seed. As he scattered it across his field, some seed fell on a footpath, where it was stepped on, and the birds ate it.
Other seed fell among rocks. It began to grow, but the plant soon wilted and died for lack of moisture.
Other seed fell among thorns that grew up with it and choked out the tender plants.

Still other seed fell on fertile soil. This seed grew and produced a crop that was a hundred times as much as had been planted!” When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said this, He called out, “Anyone with ears to hear should listen and understand.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s Talmidym asked him what this parable meant.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “You are permitted to understand the secrets of the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. But I use parables to teach the others so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled: ‘When they look, they will not really see. When they hear, they will not understand.’
“This is the meaning of the parable: The seed is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Dabar.
The seeds that fell on the footpath represent those who hear the message, only to have ha'shatan come and take it away from their hearts and prevent them from believing and being saved.

The seeds on the rocky soil represent those who hear the message and receive it with joy. But since they do not have deep roots, they believe for a while, then they fall away when they face temptation.

The seeds that fell among the thorns represent those who hear the message, but all too quickly the message is crowded out by the cares and riches and pleasures of this life. And so they never grow into maturity.
And the seeds that fell on the good soil represent honest, good-hearted people who hear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Dabar and they cling to the Dabar, and with the Dabar they patiently produce a huge harvest.
“No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a bowl or hides it under a bed. A lamp is placed on a stand, where its light can be seen by all who enter the house.
For all that is secret will eventually be brought into the open, and everything that is concealed will be brought to light and made known to all.

“So pay attention to how you hear. To those who listen to my teaching, more understanding will be given. But for those who are not listening, even what they think they understand will be taken away from them.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s mother and brothers came to see Him, but they could not get to Him because of the crowd.
Someone told 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, and they want to see you.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “My mother and my brothers are all those who hear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Dabar and obey it.”
One day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to his Talmidym, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So they got into a boat and started out.
As they sailed across, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA settled down for a nap. But soon a fierce storm came down on the lake. The boat was filling with water, and they were in real danger.
The Talmidym went and woke 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA up, shouting, “Master, Master, we are going to drown!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “Where is your Amunah?” The Talmidym were terrified and amazed. “Who is this man?” they asked each other. “When He gives a command, even the wind and waves obey Him!”
So they arrived in the region of the Garasanas, across the lake from Galily.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was climbing out of the boat, a man who was possessed by demons came out to meet Him. For a long time he had been homeless and naked, living in a cemetery outside the town.

As soon as the demon possessed man saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, he shrieked and fell down in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. Then he screamed, “Why are you interfering with me, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH? Please, I beg you, do not torture me!”

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had already commanded the evil spirit to come out of him. This spirit had often taken control of the man. Even when he was placed under guard and put in chains and shackles, he simply broke them and rushed out into the wilderness, completely under the demon’s power.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA demanded,
The demons kept begging 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA not to send them into the bottomless pit.
There happened to be a large herd of pigs feeding on the hillside nearby, and the demons begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to let them enter into the pigs. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave them permission.
Then the demons came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the entire herd plunged down the steep hillside into the lake and drowned.
When the herdsmen saw it, they fled to the nearby town and the surrounding countryside, spreading the news as they ran.

People rushed out to see what had happened. A crowd soon gathered around 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and they saw the man who had been freed from the demons. He was sitting at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s feet, fully clothed and perfectly sane, and they were all afraid.
Then those who had seen what happened told the others how the demon possessed man had been healed.

And all the people in the region of the Garasanas begged 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to go away and leave them alone, for a great wave of fear swept over them. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA returned to the boat and left, crossing back to the other side of the lake.
The man who had been freed from the demons begged to go with Him. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent him home, saying,
“No, go back to your family, and tell them everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done for you.” So he went all through the town proclaiming the great things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had done for him.
On the other side of the lake the crowds welcomed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, because they had been waiting for Him.
Then a man named Yairus, a leader of the local congregation, came and fell at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s feet, pleading with Him to come home with him.
His only daughter, who was about twelve years old, was dying. As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went with him, He was surrounded by the crowds.
A woman in the crowd had suffered for twelve years with constant bleeding, and she could find no cure.
Coming up behind 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, she touched the fringe of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s robe. Immediately, the bleeding stopped.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked, “Who touched me?” Everyone denied it, and Kafa said, “Master, this whole crowd is pressing up against You.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, Someone deliberately touched me, for I felt healing power go out from me.”

When the woman realized that she could not stay hidden, she began to tremble and fell to her knees in front of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. The whole crowd heard her explain why she had touched 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and that she had been immediately healed.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to her, “Daughter, “your Amunah has made you well. Go in Shalum.”

While 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was still speaking to her, a messenger arrived from the home of Yairus, the leader of the congregation, he told him, “Your daughter is dead. There is no use troubling the Teacher now.”
But when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard what had happened, He said to Yairus, “Do not be afraid. Just have Amunah, and she will be healed.”
When they arrived at the house, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA would not let anyone go in with him except Kafa, Yahukanun, Ya'aqub, and the little girl’s father and mother.
The house was filled with people weeping and wailing, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Stop the weeping! She is not dead; she is only asleep.”
But the crowd laughed at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA because they all knew she had died.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took her by the hand and said in a loud voice, “Little girl, arise.”
And at that moment her life returned, and she immediately stood up! Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were overwhelmed, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA insisted that they should not tell anyone what had happened.
One day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called together his twelve Talmidym and gave them power and authority to cast out all demons and to heal all diseases.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent them out to tell everyone about the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and to heal the sick.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA instructed His Talmidym Saying. “Take nothing for your journey,” Do not take a walking stick, a traveler’s bag, food, money, or even a change of clothes.
Wherever you go, stay in the same house until you leave town.
And if a town refuses to welcome you, shake its dust from your feet as you leave to show that you have abandoned those people to their fate.”
So they began their circuit of the villages, preaching the Good News and healing the sick.
When Harud Antipas, the ruler of Galily, heard about everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was doing, he was puzzled. Some were saying that Yahukanun the Baptist had been raised from the dead.
Others thought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was AliYahu or one of the other Nabyms risen from the dead.
“I beheaded Yahukanun,” Harud said, “so who is this man about whom I hear such stories?” And Harud sought to see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
When the Shaliach (Apostles) returned, they told 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA everything they had done. Then He slipped quietly away with them toward the town of Bathsaida.
But the crowds found out where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was going, and they followed Him, and He welcomed them and taught them about the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA healed those who were sick.

Late in the afternoon the twelve Talmidym came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and said, “Send the crowds away to the nearby villages and farms, so they can find food and lodging for the night. There is nothing to eat here in this remote place.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “You feed them.” But we have only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered. “Or are you expecting us to go and buy enough food for this whole crowd?”
For there were about five thousand men there. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Tell them to sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
So the people all sat down.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the five loaves and two fish, looked up toward Shamaym, and Baraked them. Then, breaking the loaves into pieces, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA kept giving the bread and fish to the Talmidym so they could distribute it to the people.
They all ate as much as they wanted, and afterward, the Talmidym picked up twelve baskets of leftovers!
One day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left the crowds to pray alone. Only his Talmidym were with him, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “Who do people say I Am?”
“Well,” they replied, “some say Yahukanun the Baptist, some say AliYahu, and others say you are one of the other ancient Nabyms risen from the dead.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “But who do you say I Am?” Kafa replied, “You are Ha'Mashyach sent from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA warned His Talmidym not to tell anyone who He was.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. “The Son of Adam must suffer many terrible things, “He will be rejected by the elders, the leading Kuhanym, and the teachers of religious law. He will be killed, but on the third day He will be raised from the dead.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the crowd, “If any of you wants to be my follower, you must turn from your selfish ways, and take up your execution stake daily, then follow me.
If you try to hang on to your life, you will lose it. But if you give up your life for my sake, you will save it.
It is worth nothing for you to have the whole world and destroy yourself or lose yourself in the world.
If anyone is ashamed of Me and My message, the Son of Adam will be ashamed of that person when He returns in His Kabad and in the Kabad of ABBA and the Qadash Malakym.
I tell you the truth, some standing here right now will not die before they see the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
About eight days later 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took Kafa, Yahukanun, and Ya'aqub up on a mountain to pray.
And as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was praying, the appearance of his face was transformed, and His clothes became dazzling white.
Suddenly, two men, Musha and AliYahu, appeared and began talking with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
They were esteemed to see. And they were speaking about His exit from this world, which was about to be fulfilled in Yahushalam.
Kafa and the others had fallen asleep. When they woke up, they saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s Kabad and the two men standing with him.

Just as Musha and AliYahu were leaving, Kafa, not even knowing what he was saying, blurted out, “Master, it will be wonderful for us to be here! Let us make three shelters as memorials, one for you, one for Musha, and one for AliYahu.”
But even as Kafa was saying this, a cloud overshadowed them, and terror gripped them as the cloud covered them.
Then a voice from the cloud said, “This is My Son, My Chosen One. Listen to Him.”
When the voice finished, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was there alone. They did not tell anyone at that time what they had seen.
The next day, after they had come down the mountain, a large crowd met 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
A man in the crowd called out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, my only child.
An evil spirit keeps seizing him, making him scream. It throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It batters him and hardly ever leaves him alone.
I begged your Talmidym to cast out the spirit, but they could not do it.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “You faithless and corrupt people! How long must I be with you and put up with you?” Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the man, “Bring your son here.”

As the boy came forward, the demon knocked him to the ground and threw him into a violent convulsion. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rebuked the evil spirit and healed the boy. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA gave him back to his father.
Awe gripped the people as they saw this majestic display of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAHs power.
“Listen to me and remember what I say. The Son of Adam is going to be betrayed into the hands of his enemies.”
But they did not know what He meant. Its significance was hidden from them, so they could not understand it, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA's Talmidym began arguing about which of them was the greatest.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew their thoughts, so He brought a little child to His side.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Anyone who welcomes a little child like this on my behalf welcomes me, and anyone who welcomes me also welcomes My ABBA who sent me. Whoever is the least among you is the greatest.”
Yahukanun said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Master, we saw someone using your name to cast out demons, but we told him to stop because he is not in our group.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Do not stop him! Anyone who is not against you is for you.”
As the time drew near for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to ascend to Shamaym, He was determined to set out for Yahushalam.
And He sent messengers ahead to a Samaritan village to prepare for His arrival.
But the people of the village did not welcome 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA because He was on his way to Yahushalam.
When Ya'aqub and Yahukanun saw this, they said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Master, should we call down fire from Shamaym to burn them up?”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned and rebuked them.
So they went on to another village.
As they were walking along, someone said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “I will follow you wherever you go.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Foxes have dens to live in, and birds have nests, but the Son of Adam has no place even to lay his head.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to another person, “Come, follow me.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told him, “Let the spiritually dead bury their own dead! Your duty is to go and preach about the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Another said, “Yes, Master, I will follow you, but first let me say good-bye to my family.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told him, “Anyone who puts a hand to the plow and then looks back is not fit for the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA chose seventy other Talmidym and sent them ahead in pairs to all the towns and places He planned to visit.

These were 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s instructions to them: “The harvest is great, but the workers are few. So pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who is in charge of the harvest; ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to send more workers into His fields.
Now go, and remember that I am sending you out as lambs among wolves.
Do not take any money with you, nor a traveler’s bag, nor an extra pair of sandals. And do not stop to greet anyone on the road.
“Whenever you enter someone’s home, first say, ‘May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Shalum be on this house.’
If those who live there are in Shalum, the Barakah will stand; if they are not, the Barakah will return to you.
Do not move around from home to home. Stay in one place, eat and drink what they provide. Do not hesitate to accept hospitality, because those who work deserve their pay.
“If you enter a town and it welcomes you, eat whatever is set before you.
Heal the sick, and tell them, ‘The Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is near you now.’
But if a town refuses to welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
‘We wipe even the dust of your town from our feet to show that we have abandoned you to your fate. But Nevertheless know this today, the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is near!’
I assure you, even wicked Sudum will be better off than such a town on judgment day.

“What sorrow awaits you, Kurazin and Bathsaida! For if the miracles I did in you had been done in wicked Tyra and Sidun, their people would have repented of their sins long ago, clothing themselves in burlap and throwing ashes on their heads to show their remorse.
Yes, Tyra and Sidun will be better off on judgment day than you.
And you people of Capernaum, will you be honored in Shamaym? No, you will go down to the place of the dead.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the Talmidym, “Anyone who accepts your message, has also accepted me. And anyone who rejects you, has rejected me. And anyone who rejects me is rejecting 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who sent me.”
When the seventy-two Talmidym returned, they joyfully reported to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Master, even the demons obey us when we use your Name!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “Yes, “I saw ha'shatan fall from Shamaym like lightning!
Look, I have given you authority over all the power of the enemy, and you can walk among snakes and scorpions and crush them. Nothing will injure you.
But do not rejoice because evil spirits obey you; rejoice because your names are registered in Shamaym.”

At that same time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was filled with the joy of the RUACH Ha'Qadash, and He said, “O ABBA, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym and Arath, Tudah Rabah (thank you) for hiding these things from those who think themselves wise and clever, and for revealing them to the childlike. Yes, ABBA, it pleased you to do it this way.
“My ABBA has entrusted everything to Me, no one truly knows the Son except ABBA, and no one truly knows ABBA except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal ABBA to.”
Then when they were alone, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to the Talmidym and said, “Baraked are the eyes that see what you have seen.
I tell you, many Nabyms and kings longed to see what you see, but they did not see it. And they longed to hear what you hear, but they did not hear it.”
One day an expert in religious law stood up to test 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA by asking Him this question: “Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “What does the law say? How do you read it?”
The man answered, “‘You must love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH with all your heart, all your soul, all your strength, and all your mind.’ And, ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told him. “You have answered rightly; do this and you will live.”
The man wanted to justify his actions, so he asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “And who is my neighbor?”

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied with a story: “A Yahudym man was traveling from Yahushalam down to Yarichu, and he was attacked by bandits. They stripped him of his clothes, beat him up, and left him half dead beside the road.
“By chance a Kuhan came along. But when he saw the man lying there, the Kuhan crossed to the other side of the road and left the half dead Yahudym man without helping him.
A Temple assistant walked over and looked at him lying there, but he also passed by on the other side.
“Then a despised Samaritan came along, and when he saw the man, he felt compassion for him.
Going over to him, the Samaritan soothed his wounds with olive oil and wine and bandaged them. Then he put the man on his own donkey and took him to an inn, where he took care of him.
The next day the Samaritan man handed the innkeeper two silver coins, telling him, ‘Take care of this man. If his bill runs higher than this, I will pay you the next time I am here.’
“Now which of these three would you say was a neighbor to the man who was attacked by bandits?”
The man replied, “The one who showed him mercy.” Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Yes, now go and do the same.”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and the Talmidym continued on their way to Yahushalam, they came to a certain village where a woman named Martha welcomed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA into her home.
Her sister, Maryam, sat at the Master’s feet, listening to what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA taught.

But Martha was distracted by the big dinner she was preparing. She came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and said, “Master, does it not seem unfair to you that my sister just sits here while I do all the work? Tell her to come and help me.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to her, “Martha Martha, you are worried and upset over all these details!
There is only one thing worth being concerned about. Maryam has discovered it, and it will not be taken away from her.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was in a certain place praying. As He finished, one of His Talmidym came to Him and said, “Master, teach us to pray, just as Yahukanun taught his followers.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “This is how you should pray: “ABBA, may your Name be kept Qadash, May your Kingdom come soon.
Give us each day the food we need,
And forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us. And do not let us yield to temptation.”
Then, teaching the Talmidym more about prayer, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA used this story: “Suppose you went to a friend’s house at midnight, wanting to borrow three loaves of bread, you say to him,
‘A friend of mine has just arrived for a visit, and I have nothing for him to eat.’
And he answered out from his bedroom, ‘Do not bother me. The door is locked for the night, and my family and I are all in bed. I cannot help you.’
But I tell you this, though he will not do it for friendship’s sake, if you keep knocking long enough, he will get up and give you whatever you need because of your shameless persistence.
“And so I tell you, keep on asking, and you will receive what you ask for. Keep on seeking, and you will find. Keep on knocking, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks, receives. Everyone who seeks, finds. And to everyone who knocks, the door will be opened.
“You fathers if your children ask for a fish, do you give them a snake instead?
Or if they ask for an egg, do you give them a scorpion? Of course not!
So if you sinful people know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your ABBA in Shamaym give the RUACH Ha'Qadash to those who ask him.”
One day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA cast out a demon from a man who could not speak, and when the demon was gone, the man began to speak. The crowds were amazed,
But some of them said, “No wonder He can cast out demons. He gets his power from ha'shatan, the prince of demons.”
Others, trying to test 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, demanded that He show them a miraculous sign from Shamaym to prove His authority.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew their thoughts, so He said, “Any kingdom divided by civil war is doomed. A family splintered by feuding will fall apart.
You say I am empowered by ha'shatan. But if ha'shatan is divided and fighting against himself, how can his kingdom survive?
And if I am empowered by ha'shatan, what about your own exorcists? They cast out demons, too, so they will condemn you for what you have said.
But if I am casting out demons by the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, then the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has arrived among you.
For when a strong man like ha'shatan is fully armed and guards his palace, his possessions are safe
Until someone even stronger attacks and overpowers him, strips him of his weapons, and carries off his belongings.
“Anyone who is not with me opposes me, and anyone who is not working with me is actually working against me.
“When an evil spirit leaves a person, it goes into the desert, searching for rest. But when it finds none, it says, ‘I will return to the person I came from.’
So it returns and finds that its former home is all swept and in order.
Then the spirit finds seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they all enter the person and live there. And so that person is worse off than before.”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was speaking, a woman in the crowd called out, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Barak your mother, the womb from which you came, and the breasts that nursed you!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “But even more baraked are all who hear the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and put it into practice.”
As the crowd pressed in on, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “This evil generation keeps asking me to show them a miraculous sign. But the only sign I will give them is the sign of Yunah.
What happened to him was a sign to the people of Ninabah that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had sent him. What happens to the Son of Adam will be a sign to these people that He was sent by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

“The queen of Shyba will stand up against this generation on judgment day and condemn it, for she came from a distant land to hear the wisdom of Shalumah. Now someone greater than Shalumah is here, but you refuse to listen.

The people of Ninabah will also stand up against this generation on judgment day and condemn it, for they repented of their sins at the preaching of Yunah. Now someone greater than Yunah is here teaching you, but you refuse to repent.
“No one lights a lamp and then hides it or puts it under a basket. Instead, a lamp is placed on a stand, where its light can be seen by all who enter the house.
“Your eye is a lamp that provides light for your body. When your eye is good, your whole body is filled with light. But when it is bad, your body is filled with darkness.
Make sure that the light you think you have is not actually darkness.
If you are filled with light, with no dark corners, then your whole life will be radiant, as though a floodlight were filling you with light.”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was speaking, one of the Pharisees invited Him home for a meal. So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went in and took His place at the table.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s host was amazed to see that He sat down to eat without first performing the hand washing ceremony required by Yahudym custom.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him, “You Pharisees are so careful to clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside you are filthy full of greed and wickedness!
Fools! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made the inside as well as the outside?
So clean the inside by giving gifts to the poor, and you will be clean all over.

“What sorrow awaits you Pharisees! For you are careful to tithe even the tiniest income from your herb gardens, but you ignore justice and the Ahaba (love) of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. You should tithe, yes, but do not neglect the more important things.
“What sorrow awaits you Pharisees! For you love to sit in the seats of honor in the congregation and receive respectful greetings as you walk in the marketplaces.
Yes, what sorrow awaits you! For you are like hidden graves in a field. People walk over them without knowing the trap they are stepping on.”
“An expert in religious law said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, teacher “you have insulted us, in what you just said.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Yes what sorrow also awaits you experts in religious law! For you crush people with unbearable religious demands, and you never lift a finger to ease the burden.
What sorrow awaits you! For you build monuments for the Nabyms your own ancestors killed long ago.
But in fact, you stand as witnesses who agree with what your ancestors did. They killed the Nabyms, and you join in their crime by building the monuments!
This is what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in his wisdom said about you: ‘I will send Nabyms and Shaliach to them, but they will kill some and persecute the others.’
“As a result, this generation will be held responsible for the murder of all 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Nabyms from the creation of the world
from the murder of Abal to the murder of Zacharyahu, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, it will certainly be charged against this generation.
“What sorrow awaits you experts in religious law! For you remove the key to knowledge from the people. You do not enter the Kingdom yourselves, and you prevent others from entering.”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was leaving, the teachers of religious law and the Pharisees became hostile and tried to provoke Him with many questions.
They wanted to trap 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA into saying something they could use against Him.

Meanwhile, the crowds grew until thousands were milling about and stepping on each other. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned first to his Talmidym and warned them, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees their hypocrisy.
The time is coming when everything that is covered up will be revealed, and all that is secret will be made known to all.
Whatever you have said in the dark night will be heard in the day light, and what you have whispered behind closed doors will be shouted from the housetops for all to hear!
“Dear friends, do not be afraid of those who want to kill your body; they cannot do any more to you after that.
But I will tell you whom to fear. Fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, who has the power to kill you and then throw you into hell. Yes, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the one to fear.
“What is the price of five sparrows, two copper coins? Yet 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH does not forget a single one of them.
And the very hairs on your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are more valuable to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH than a whole flock of sparrows.
“I tell you the truth, everyone who acknowledges me publicly here on Arath, the Son of Adam will also acknowledge in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Malakym.
But anyone who denies me here on Arath will be denied before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Malakym.
Anyone who speaks against the Son of Adam can be forgiven, but anyone who blasphemes the RUACH Ha'Qadash will not be forgiven.
“And when you are brought to trial in the congregation and before rulers and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourself or what to say,
for the RUACH Ha'Qadash will teach you at that time what needs to be said.”
Then someone called from the crowd, “Teacher, please tell my brother to divide our father’s estate with me.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Man, who made Me a judge over you to decide such things as that?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Beware! Guard against every kind of greed. Life is not measured by how much you own.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them a story: “A rich man had a fertile farm that produced fine crops.
He said to himself, ‘What should I do? I do not have room for all my crops.’
Then he said, ‘I know! I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones. Then I will have room enough to store all my wheat and other goods.
And I will sit back and say to myself, “My friend, you have enough stored away for years to come. Now take it easy! Eat, drink, and be merry!”’
“But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to him, ‘You fool! You will die this very night, then who will get everything you worked for?’
“Yes, a man is a fool to store up wealth and not have a rich relationship with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then, turning to His Talmidym, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “That is why I tell you not to worry about everyday life, whether you have enough food to eat or enough clothes to wear.
For life is more than food, and your body more than clothing.
Look at the ravens. They do not plant or harvest or store food in barns, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH feeds them. And you are far more valuable to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH than any birds!
Can all your worries add a single moment to your life?
And if worry cannot accomplish a little thing like that, what is the use of worrying over bigger things?
“Look at the lilies and how they grow. They do not work or make their clothing, yet Shalumah in all his Kabad was not dressed as beautifully as they are.
And if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH cares so wonderfully for flowers that are here today and thrown into the fire tomorrow, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will certainly care for you. Why do you have so little Amunah?
“And do not be concerned about what to eat and what to drink. Do not worry about such things.
These things dominate the thoughts of unbelievers all over the world, but your Father already knows your needs.
But seek the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and HE will give you everything you need.
“So do not be afraid, little flock. For it gives your ABBA great happiness to give you the Kingdom.

“Sell your possessions and give to those in need. This will store up treasure for you in Shamaym! And the purses of Shamaym never get old or develop holes. Your treasure will be safe; no thief can steal it and no moth can destroy it.
Wherever your treasure is, there the desires of your heart will also be.
“Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning,
As though you were waiting for your master to return from the wedding feast. Then you will be ready to open the door and let your Master in the moment he arrives and knocks.
The servants who are ready and waiting for his master's return will be rewarded. I tell you the truth, the master himself will seat them, put on an apron, and serve them as they sit and eat!
The master may come in the middle of the night or just before dawn. But whenever the master comes, he will reward the servants who are ready.
“Understand this: If a homeowner knew exactly when a burglar was coming, he would not permit his house to be broken into.
You also must be ready all the time, for the Son of Adam will come when least expected.”
Kafa asked, “Master, is that illustration just for us or for everyone?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “A faithful, sensible servant is one to whom the master can give the responsibility of managing his other household servants and feeding them.
If the master returns and finds that the servant has done a good job, there will be a reward.
I tell you the truth, the master will put that servant in charge of all he owns.
