But what if the servant thinks, ‘My master will not be back for a while,’ and he begins beating the other servants, partying, and getting drunk?
The master will return unannounced and unexpected, and the master will cut the servant in pieces and banish him with the unbelievers.
“And a servant who knows what the master wants, but is not prepared and does not carry out those instructions, will be severely punished.

But someone who does not know, and then does something wrong, will be punished only lightly. When someone has been given much, much will be required in return; and when someone has been entrusted with much, even more will be required.
“I have come to set the world on fire, and I wish it were already burning!
I have a terrible baptism of suffering ahead of me, and I am under a heavy burden until it is accomplished.
Do you think I have come to bring Shalum to the Arath? No, I have come to divide people against each other!
From now on families will be split apart, three in favor of me, and two against me, or two in favor me and three against me.
‘Father will be divided against son and son against father; mother against daughter and daughter against mother; and mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.’”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to the crowd and said, “When you see clouds beginning to form in the west, you say, ‘Here comes a shower.’ And you are right.
When the south wind blows, you say, ‘Today will be a scorcher.’ And it is.
You fools! You know how to interpret the weather signs of the Arath and sky, but you do not know how to interpret the present times.
“Why can you not decide for yourselves what is right?

When you are on the way to court with your accuser, try to settle the matter before you get there. Otherwise, your accuser may drag you before the judge, who will hand you over to an officer, who will throw you into prison.
And if that happens, you will not be free again until you have paid the very last penny.
About this time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was informed that Pilate had murdered some people from Galily as they were offering sacrifices at the Temple.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. Do you think those Galilyans were worse sinners than all the other people from Galily?” “Is that why they suffered?
Not at all! And you will perish, too, unless you repent of your sins and turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And what about the eighteen people who died when the tower in Siluam fell on them? Were they the worst sinners in Yahushalam?
No, and I tell you again that unless you repent, you will perish, too.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told this story: “A man planted a fig tree in his garden and came again and again to see if there was any fruit on it, but he was always disappointed.
Finally, he said to his gardener, ‘I have waited three years, and there has not been a single fig! Cut it down. It is just taking up space in the garden.’
“The gardener answered, ‘Sir, give it one more chance. Leave it another year, and I will give it special attention and plenty of fertilizer.
If we get figs next year, fine. If not, then you can cut it down.’”
One Shabbat day as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was teaching in a congregation,
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw a woman who had been crippled by an evil spirit. She had been bent double for eighteen years and was unable to stand up straight.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw her, he called her over and said, “Dear woman, you are healed of your sickness!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA touched her, and instantly she could stand straight. How she Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!

But the leader in charge of the congregation was very angry that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had healed her on the Shabbat day. “There are six days of the week for working,” he said to the crowd. “Come on those days to be healed, not on the Shabbat.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “You hypocrites! Each of you works on the Shabbat day! Do you not untie your ox or your donkey from its stall on the Shabbat and lead it out for water?
This dear woman, a daughter of Abraham, has been held in bondage by ha'shatan for eighteen years. Is it not right that she be released, even on the Shabbat?”
This shamed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA's enemies, but all the people rejoiced at the wonderful things He did.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “What is the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH like? How can I illustrate it?
It is like a tiny mustard seed that a man planted in a garden; it grows and becomes a tree, and the birds make nests in its branches.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA also asked, “What else is the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH like?
It is like the yeast a woman used in making bread. Even though she put only a little yeast in three measures of flour, it permeated every part of the dough.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went through the towns and villages, teaching as he went, always pressing on toward Yahushalam.
Someone asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Master, will only a few be saved?” and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied,
“Work hard to enter the narrow door to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Kingdom, for many will try to enter but will fail.

When the master of the house has locked the door, it will be too late. You will stand outside knocking and pleading, ‘Master, open the door for us!’ But he will reply, ‘I do not know you or where you come from.’
Then you will say, ‘But we ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
And he will reply, ‘I tell you, I do not know you or where you come from. Get away from me, all you who do evil.’
“There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, for you will see Abraham, Yachaq, Ya'aqub, and all the Nabyms in the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but you will be thrown out.
And people will come from all over the world, from east and west, north and south to take their places in the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And note this: Some who seem least important now will be the greatest then, and some who are the greatest now will be least important then.”
At that time some Pharisees said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Get away from here if you want to live! Harud Antipas wants to kill you!”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Go tell that fox that I will keep on casting out demons and healing people today and tomorrow; and the third day I will accomplish my purpose.
Yes, today, tomorrow, and the next day I must proceed on my way. For it would not do for a Nabym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to be killed except in Yahushalam!

“O Yahushalam, Yahushalam, the city that kills the Nabyms and stones 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s messengers! How often I have wanted to gather your children together as a hen protects her chicks beneath her wings, but you would not let me.
And now, look, your house is abandoned. And you will never see me again until you say, ‘Baraked is the one who comes in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!’”
Now it happened, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees to eat bread on the Shabbat, that they watched 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA closely.
And behold, there was a certain man before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA who had dropsy.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked the Pharisees and experts in religious law, “Is it permitted in the law to heal people on the Shabbat day, or not?”
When they refused to answer, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA touched the sick man and healed him and sent him away.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to them and said, “If one of you has a child or an ox that falls into a well on the Shabbat day, will you not immediately pull it out?”
Again they could not answer.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA noticed that all who had come to the dinner were trying to sit in the seats of honor near the head of the table, He gave them this advice:
“When you are invited to a wedding feast, do not sit in the seat of honor. What if someone who is more distinguished than you has also been invited?
The host will come and say, ‘Give this person your seat.’ Then you will be embarrassed, and you will have to take whatever seat is left at the foot of the table!

“Instead, take the lowest place at the foot of the table. Then when your host sees you, he will come and say, ‘Friend, we have a better place for you!’ Then you will be honored in front of all the other guests.
For those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to his host. “When you put on a luncheon or a banquet, “do not invite your friends, brothers, relatives, and rich neighbors. For they will invite you back, and that will be your only reward.
Instead, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind.
Then at the resurrection of the righteous, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will reward you for inviting those who could not repay you.”
Hearing this, a man sitting at the table with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA exclaimed, “What a Barakah it will be to attend a banquet in the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied with this story: “A man prepared a great feast and sent out many invitations.
When the banquet was ready, he sent his servant to tell the guests, ‘Come, the banquet is ready.’
But they all began making excuses. One said, ‘I have just bought a field and must inspect it. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I have just bought five pairs of oxen, and I want to try them out. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I now have a wife, so I cannot come.’

“The servant returned and told his master what they had said. His master was furious and said, ‘Go quickly into the streets and alleys of the town and invite the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’
After the servant had done this, he reported, ‘There is still room for more.’
So his master said, ‘Go out into the country lanes and behind the hedges and urge anyone you find to come, so that the house will be full.
For none of those I first invited will get even the smallest taste of my banquet.’”
A large crowd was following 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. He turned around and said to them,

“If you want to be my Talmidym, you must hate everyone else by comparison, your father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes even your own life. Otherwise, you cannot be my Talmidym.
And if you do not carry your own execution stake and follow me, you cannot be my Talmidym.
“But do not begin until you count the cost. For who would begin construction of a building without first calculating the cost to see if there is enough money to finish it?
Otherwise, you might complete only the foundation before running out of money, and then everyone would laugh at you.
They would say, ‘There is the person who started that building and could not afford to finish it!’

“Or what king would go to war against another king without first sitting down with his counselors to discuss whether his army of ten thousand could defeat the twenty thousand soldiers marching against him?
And if he cannot, he will send a delegation to discuss terms of Shalum while the enemy is still far away.
So you cannot become my Talmidym without giving up everything you own.
“Salt is good for seasoning. But if it loses its flavor, how do you make it salty again?
Tasteless salt is not good for the soil nor for the manure pile. Tasteless salt is thrown away. Anyone with ears to hear should listen and understand!”
Tax collectors and other notorious sinners often came to listen to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA teach.
This made the Pharisees and teachers of religious law complain that He was associating with such sinful people, even eating with them!
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them this story:
“If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them gets lost, what will he do? Will he not leave the ninety nine others in the wilderness and go to search for the one that is lost until he finds it?
And when he has found it, he will joyfully carry it home on his shoulders.
When he arrives, he will call together his friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me because I have found my lost sheep.’
In the same way, there is more joy in Shamaym over one lost sinner who repents and returns to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH than over ninety nine others who are righteous and need no repentance!
“Or suppose a woman has ten silver coins and loses one. Will she not light a lamp and sweep the entire house and search carefully until she finds it?
And when she finds it, she will call in her friends and neighbors and say, ‘Rejoice with me because I have found my lost coin.’
In the same way, there is joy in the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Malakym when even one sinner repents.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said: “A man had two sons.
The younger son told his father, ‘I want my share of your estate now before you die.’ So his father agreed to divide his wealth between his sons.
“A few days later this younger son packed all his belongings and moved to a distant land, and there he wasted all his money in prodigal living.
About the time his money ran out, a great famine swept over the land, and he began to starve.
He persuaded a local farmer to hire him, and the man sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.
The young man became so hungry that even the pods he was feeding the pigs looked good to him. And no one gave him anything.
“When he finally came to his senses, he said to himself, ‘At home even the hired servants have food enough to spare, and here I am dying of hunger!
I will go home to my father and say, “Father, I have sinned against both Shamaym and you,
and I am no longer worthy of being called your son. Please take me on as a hired servant.”’
“So he returned home to his father. And while he was still a long way off, his father saw him coming. Filled with love and compassion, the father ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.
His son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against both Shamaym and you, and I am no longer worthy of being called your son.’
“But his father said to the servants, ‘Quick! Bring the finest robe in the house and put it on him. Get a ring for his finger and sandals for his feet.
And kill the calf we have been fattening. We must celebrate with a feast,
for this son of mine was dead and has now returned to life. He was lost, but now he is found.’ So the party began.
“Meanwhile, the older son was in the fields working. When he returned home, he heard music and dancing in the house,
And he asked one of the servants what was going on.
‘Your brother is back,’ he was told, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf. We are celebrating because of his safe return.’
“The older brother was angry and would not go in. His father came out and begged him,

But he replied, ‘All these years I have slaved for you and never once refused to do a single thing you told me to. And in all that time you never gave me even one young goat for a feast with my friends.
Yet when this son of yours comes back after squandering your money on prostitutes, you celebrate by killing the fattened calf!’
“His father said to him, ‘Look, dear son, you have always stayed by me, and everything I have is yours.
We had to celebrate this happy day. For your brother was dead and has come back to life! He was lost, but now he is found!’”

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told this story to his Talmidym: “There was a certain rich man who had a manager handling his affairs. One day a report came to the rich man that the manager was wasting his employer’s money.
So the employer called the manager in and said, ‘What is this I hear about you? Get your report in order, because you are going to be fired.’
“The manager thought to himself, what should I do? My boss has fired me. I do not have the strength to dig ditches, and I am too proud to beg.
I know how to ensure that I will have plenty of friends who will give me a home when I am fired.’
“So he invited each person who owed money to his employer to come and discuss the situation, he asked the first one, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
And he said, ‘A hundred measures of oil.’ So he said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
Then he said to another, ‘And how much do you owe?’ So he said, ‘A hundred measures of wheat.’ And he said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’
So the master commended the unjust steward because he had dealt shrewdly. For the sons of this world are more shrewd in their generation than the sons of light.
Here’s the lesson: Use your worldly resources to benefit others and make friends. Then, when your earthly possessions are gone, they will welcome you to an eternal home.
“If you are faithful in little things, you will be faithful in large ones. But if you are dishonest in little things, you will not be honest with greater responsibilities.
And if you are untrustworthy about worldly wealth, who will trust you with the true riches of Shamaym?
And if you are not faithful with other people’s things, why should you be trusted with things of your own?
“No one can serve two masters. For you will hate one and love the other; you will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve both 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and money.”
The Pharisees, who dearly loved their money, heard all this and they criticized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “You like to appear righteous in public, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH knows your hearts. What this world honors is detestable in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“Until Yahukanun, the law and the messages of the Nabym were your guides. But now the Good News of the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is preached, and everyone is eager to get in.
But that does not mean that the law has lost its force. It is easier for Shamaym and Arath to disappear than for the smallest point of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s law to be overturned.
“For example, a man who divorces his wife and marries someone else commits adultery. And anyone who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “There was a certain rich man who was splendidly clothed in purple and fine linen and who lived each day in luxury.
At his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus who was covered with sores.
As Lazarus lay there longing for scraps from the rich man’s table, the dogs would come and lick Lazarus open sores.
“Finally, the poor man died and was carried by the Malakym to be with Abraham. The rich man also died and was buried,
And the rich man's soul went to the place of the dead. There, in torment, he saw Abraham in the far distance with Lazarus at his side.
“The rich man shouted, ‘Father Abraham, have some pity on me! Please send Lazarus over here to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. I am in anguish in these flames.’
“But Abraham said to him, ‘Son, remember that during your lifetime you had everything you wanted, and Lazarus had nothing. So now he is here being comforted, and you are in anguish.
And besides, there is a great fissture separating us. No one can cross over to you from here, and no one can cross over to us from there.’
“Then the rich man said, ‘Please, Father Abraham, at least send Lazarus to my father’s home.
For I have five brothers, and I want him to warn them so they do not end up in this place of torment.’
“But Abraham said, they have the law that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave to ‘Musha and the writings of the Nabyms, Your brothers can read what they wrote.’
“The rich man replied, ‘No, Father Abraham! But if someone is sent to them from the dead, then they will repent of their sins and turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’
“But Abraham said, ‘If they will not listen to Musha and the Nabyms, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises back from the dead.’”
One day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to his Talmidym, “There will always be temptations to sin, but how terrible it will be for the person through whom they come!!
It would be better to be thrown into the sea with a millstone hung around your neck than to cause one of these little ones to fall into sin.
So watch yourselves! If another believer sins, rebuke that person; then if there is repentance, forgive.
Even if that person wrongs you seven times a day and each time turns again and asks forgiveness, you must forgive.”
The Talmidym said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Show us how to increase our Amunah.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered, “If you had Amunah even as small as a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, ‘May you be uprooted and thrown into the sea,’ and it would obey you!
“When a servant comes in from plowing or taking care of sheep, does his master say, ‘Come in and eat with me’?
No, he says, ‘Prepare my meal, put on your apron, and serve me while I eat. Then you can eat later.’
And does the master thank the servant for doing what he was told to do? Of course not.
In the same way, when you obey me you should say, ‘We are unworthy servants who have simply done our duty.’”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA continued on toward Yahushalam, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA reached the border between Galily and Samaria.
As He entered a village there where ten lepers that stood at a distance,
crying out, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, our Master, have mercy on us!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked at them and said, “Go show yourselves to the Kuhanym.” And as they went, they were cleansed of their leprosy.
One of them, when he saw that he was healed, came back to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, shouting, “Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
He fell to the ground at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s feet, thanking Him for what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had done. This man was a Samaritan.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked, “Did I not heal ten men? Where are the other nine?
Has no one returned to give TUDAH to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH except this foreigner?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the man, “Stand up and go. Your Amunah has made you well.”
One day the Pharisees asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “When will the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH come?”
You will not be able to say, ‘Here it is!’ or ‘It is over there!’ For the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is already among you.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to his Talmidym, “The time is coming when you will long to see the day when the Son of Adam returns, but you will not see it.
People will tell you, ‘Look, there is the Son of Adam,’ or ‘here He is,’ but do not go out and follow them.
For as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so it will be on the day when the Son of Adam comes.
But first the Son of Adam must suffer terribly and be rejected by this generation.
“When the Son of Adam returns, it will be like it was in Nuah’s day.
In those days, the people enjoyed banquets and parties and weddings right up to the time Nuah entered his boat and the flood came and destroyed them all.
“And the world will be as it was in the days of Lut. People went about their daily business, eating and drinking, buying and selling, farming and building
Until the morning Lut left Sudum. Then fire and burning sulfur rained down from Shamaym and destroyed them all.
Yes, it will be ‘business as usual’ right up to the day when the Son of Adam is revealed.
On that day a person out on the deck of a roof must not go down into the house to pack. A person out in the field must not return home.
Remember what happened to Lut’s wife!
If you cling to your life, you will lose it, and if you let your life go, you will save it.
That night two people will be asleep in one bed; one will be taken, the other left.
Two women will be grinding flour together at the mill; one will be taken, the other left.”
Two men will be in the field: the one will be taken and the other left.”
The Talmidym asked, Where will this happen, Master?”
One day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told his Talmidym a story to show that they should always pray and never give up.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “There was a judge in a certain city,” “who neither feared 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH nor cared about people.
A widow of that city came to him repeatedly, saying, ‘Give me justice in this dispute with my enemy.’
The judge ignored her for a while, but finally he said to himself, ‘I do not fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or care about people,
but this woman is driving me crazy. I am going to see that she gets justice, because she is wearing me out with her constant requests!’”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Learn a lesson from this unjust judge.

Even the judge rendered a just decision in the end. So do you not think 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will surely give justice to His chosen ones who cry out to Him day and night? Will 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH keep putting them off?
I tell you, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will grant justice to them quickly! But when the Son of Adam returns, how many will he find on the Arath who have Amunah?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told this story to some who had great confidence in their own righteousness and scorned everyone else:
“Two men went to the Temple to pray. One was a Pharisee, and the other was a despised tax collector.

The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed this prayer: ‘I thank you 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, that I am not a sinner like everyone else. For I do not cheat, I do not sin, and I do not commit adultery. I am certainly not like that tax collector!
I fast twice a week, and I give you a tenth of my income.’

“But the tax collector stood at a distance and dared not even lift his eyes to Shamaym as he prayed. Instead, he beat his chest in sorrow, saying, ‘O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, be merciful to me, for I am a sinner.’

I tell you, this sinner tax collector returned home justified before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and not the Pharisee, For those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.”
One day some parents brought their little children to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA so he could touch and barak them. But when the Talmidym saw this, they scolded the parents for bothering Him.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called for the children and said to the Talmidym, “Let the children come to Me. Do not stop them! For the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH belongs to those who are like these children.
I tell you the truth, anyone who does not receive the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH like a child will never enter it.”
Once a religious leader asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA this question: “Good Teacher, what should I do to inherit eternal life?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him. “Why do you call me good?” Only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is truly good.
But to answer your question, you know the commandments: ‘You must not commit adultery. You must not murder. You must not steal. You must not testify falsely. Honor your father and mother.’”
The man replied, “I’ve obeyed all these commandments since I was young.”

When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard his answer, he said, “There is still one thing you have not done. Sell all your possessions and give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in Shamaym. Then come, follow me.”
But when the man heard this he became very sad, for he was very rich.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw this, He said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!
In fact, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
Those who heard this said, “Then who in the world can be saved?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “What is impossible for men, is possible with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Kafa said, “We have left our homes to follow you.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, Yes “and I assure you that everyone who has given up house or wife or brothers or parents or children, for the sake of the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,
will be repaid many times over in this life, and will have eternal life in the world to come.”
Taking the twelve disciples aside, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Listen, we are going up to Yahushalam, where all the predictions of the Nabyms concerning the Son of Adam will come true.
He will be handed over to the Romans, and he will be mocked, treated shamefully, and spit upon.
They will flog him with a whip and kill him, but on the third day he will rise again.”
But they did not understand any of this. The significance of his words was hidden from them, and they failed to grasp what he was talking about.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA approached
When he heard the noise of a crowd going past, he asked what was happening.
They told him that
So he began shouting,
“Be quiet!” the people in front yelled at him. But he only shouted louder, “Son of Daud, have mercy on me!”
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA heard him, he stopped and ordered that the man be brought to him. As the man came near, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “All right, receive your sight! Your Amunah has healed you.”
Instantly the man could see, and he followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, then he Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And they who saw the miracle all Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA entered Yarichu and made his way through the town.
There was a man there named Zacchaus. He was the chief tax collector in the region, and he had become very rich.
He tried to get a look at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, but he was too short to see over the crowd.
So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore fig tree beside the road, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was going to pass that way.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came by, He looked up at Zacchaeus and called him by name. “Zacchaus! "hurry and come down! I must be a guest in your home today.”
Zacchaus quickly climbed down and took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to his house in great excitement and joy.
But the people were displeased. “He has gone to be the guest of a notorious sinner,” they grumbled.
Meanwhile, Zacchaeus stood before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and said, “I will give half my wealth to the poor, Master, and if I have cheated people on their taxes, I will give them back four times as much!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA responded, “Salvation has come to this home today, for this man has shown himself to be a true son of Abraham.
For the Son of Adam came to seek and save those who are lost.”
The crowd was listening to everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. And because he was nearing Yahushalam, he told them a story to correct the impression that the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH would begin right away.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “A nobleman was called away to a distant empire to be crowned king and then return.
Before he left, he called together ten of his servants and divided among them ten pounds of silver, saying, ‘Invest this for me while I am gone.’
But his people hated him and sent a delegation after him to say, ‘We do not want him to be our king.’
“After he was crowned king, he returned and called in the servants to whom he had given the money, he wanted to find out what their profits were.
The first servant reported, ‘Master, I invested your money and made ten times the original amount!’
“‘Well done!’ the king exclaimed. ‘You are a good servant. You have been faithful with the little I entrusted to you, so you will be governor of ten cities as your reward.’
“The next servant reported, ‘Master, I invested your money and made five times the original amount.’
“‘Well done!’ the king said. ‘You will be governor over five cities.’
“But the third servant brought back only the original amount of money and said, ‘Master, I hid your money and kept it safe.
I was afraid because you are a hard man to deal with, taking what is not yours and harvesting crops you did not plant.’
“‘You wicked servant!’ the king roared. ‘Your own words condemn you. If you knew that I am a hard man who takes what is not mine and harvests crops I did not plant,
why did you not deposit my money in the bank? At least I could have gotten some interest on it.’
“Then, turning to the others standing nearby, the king ordered, ‘Take the money from this servant, and give it to the one who has ten pounds.’
“‘But, master,’ they said, ‘he already has ten pounds!’
“‘Yes,’ the king replied, to those who use well what they are given, more will be added to them. But from those who do nothing, even what little they have will be taken away.
And as for these enemies of mine who did not want me to be their king, bring them in and execute them right here in front of me.’”
After telling this story, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went on toward Yahushalam, walking ahead of His Talmidym.
As He came to the towns of Bathphage and Bathany on the Mount of Olives, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent two Talmidym ahead.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them. “Go into that village over there, “As you enter it, you will see a young donkey tied there that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying that colt?’ just say, ‘The Master needs it.’”
So they went and found the colt, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said.
And sure enough, as they were untying it, the owners asked them, “Why are you untying that colt?”
And the Talmidym simply replied, “The Master needs it.”
So they brought the colt to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and threw their garments over it for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to ride on.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rode along, the crowds spread out their garments on the road ahead of Him.

When He had reached the place where the road started down the Mount of Olives, all of his followers began to shout and sing as they walked along, Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for all the wonderful miracles they had seen.
“Barakah on the King who comes in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! SHALUM in Shamaym, and Kabad in highest Shamaym!”
But some of the Pharisees among the crowd said, “Teacher, rebuke your followers for saying things like that!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “If they kept quiet, the stones along the road would burst into cheers!”
But as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came closer to Yahushalam and saw the city ahead, he began to weep.
“How I wish today that you of all people would understand the way to Shalum. But now it is too late, and Shalum is hidden from your eyes.
Before long your enemies will build ramparts against your walls and encircle you and close in on you from every side.
They will crush you into the ground, and your children with you. Your enemies will not leave a single stone in place, because you did not recognize it when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH visited you.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA entered the Temple and began to drive out the people selling animals for sacrifices.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “The Scriptures declare, ‘My Temple will be a house of prayer,’ but you have turned it into a den of thieves.”
After that, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA taught daily in the Temple, but the leading Kuhanym, the teachers of religious law, and the other leaders of the people began planning how to kill 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
But they could think of nothing, because all the people where hanging on every word 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said.
One day as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was teaching the people and preaching the Good News in the Temple, the leading Kuhanym, the teachers of religious law, and the elders came up to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
They demanded, “By what authority are you doing all these things? Who gave you the right?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied. “Let me ask you a question first,”
“Did Yahukanun’s authority to baptize come from Shamaym, or was it merely from man?”
They talked it over among themselves. “If we say it was from Shamaym, he will ask why we did not believe Yahukanun.
But if we say it was merely man's, the people will stone us because they are convinced Yahukanun was a Nabym.”
So they finally replied that they did not know.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA responded, “Then I will not tell you by what authority I do these things.”
Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to the people again and told them this story: “A man planted a vineyard, leased it to tenant farmers, and moved to another country to live for several years.
At the time of the grape harvest, he sent one of his servants to collect his share of the crop. But the farmers attacked the servant, beat him up, and sent him back empty handed.
So the owner sent another servant, but they also insulted him, beat him up, and sent him away empty handed.
A third man was sent, and they wounded him and chased him away.
“‘What will I do?’ the owner asked himself. ‘I know! I will send my cherished son. Surely they will respect him.’
“But when the tenant farmers saw his son, they said to each other, ‘Here comes the heir to this estate. Let us kill him and get the estate for ourselves!’
So they dragged the son out of the vineyard and murdered him. “What do you suppose the owner of the vineyard will do to them?”
“I will tell you, the owner of the vineyard will come and kill those farmers and lease the vineyard to others.” “How terrible that such a thing should ever happen,” they protested.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked at them and said, “Then what does this Scripture mean? ‘The stone that the builders rejected has now become the cornerstone.’
Whoever falls on that stone will be broken; but on whomever the stone falls on, the stone will grind the person to powder.”

The teachers of religious law and the leading Kuhanym wanted to arrest 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA immediately, for they realized He was telling the story against them, they were the wicked farmers. But they were afraid of the people’s reaction.

Watching for their opportunity, the leaders sent spies pretending to be honest men. They tried to get 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to say something that could be reported to the Roman governor so he would arrest 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
“Teacher,” they said, “we know that you speak and teach what is right and you are not influenced by what others think. You teach the way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH truthfully.
Now tell us, is it right for us to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw through their trickery and said,
“Show me a Roman coin. Whose picture and title are stamped on it?” “Caesar’s,” they replied.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Well then, “give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH what belongs to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
So they failed to trap 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA by what He said in front of the people. Instead, they were amazed by his answer, and they became silent.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was approached by some Sadducees, religious leaders who say there is no resurrection from the dead.
They posed this question: “Teacher, Musha gave us a law that if a man dies, leaving a wife but no children, his brother should marry the widow and have a child who will carry on the brother’s name.
Well, suppose there were seven brothers. The oldest one married and then died without children.
So the second brother married the widow, but he also died.
Then the third brother married her. This continued with all seven of them, who died without children.
Finally, the woman also died.
So tell us, whose wife will she be in the resurrection? For all seven were married to her!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Marriage is for people here on Arath.
But in the age to come, those worthy of being raised from the dead will neither marry nor be given in marriage.
And they will never die again. In this respect they will be like Malakym. They are children of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and children of the resurrection.

“But now, as to whether the dead will be raised, even Musha proved this when he wrote about the burning bush. Long after Abraham, Yachaq, and Ya'aqub had died, Musha referred to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as ‘the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Yachaq, and the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Ya'aqub.’
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the living, not the dead, for they are all alive to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
“Well said, Teacher!” remarked some of the teachers of religious law who were standing there.
And then no one dared to ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA any more questions.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA presented them with a question. “Why is it that Ha'Mashyach is said to be the son of Daud?
For Daud himself wrote in the book of Tahalym: that ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to My MASTER, Sit in the place of honor at My right hand
Till I make Your enemies Your footstool.
Since Daud called Ha'Mashyach ‘MASTER,’ how can Ha'Mashyach be daud‘s son?”
Then with the crowds listening, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned to his Talmidym and said,

“Beware of these teachers of religious law! For they like to parade around in long robes and love to receive respectful greetings as they walk in the marketplaces. And how they love the seats of honor in the congregation and the head table at banquets.
Yet they shamelessly cheat widows out of their property and then pretend to be pious by making long prayers in public. Because of this, they will be severely punished.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury,
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw also a certain poor widow putting in two mites.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Truly I say to you that this poor widow has put in more than all;
for they all offered out of their abundance in offerings for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but the widow out of her poverty put in all the livelihood that she had.”
Some of the Talmidym began talking about the temple, how it was adorned with beautiful stones and donations, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said,
“These things which you see, the days will come in which not one stone shall be left upon another that shall not be thrown down.”
So they asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, saying, “Teacher, but when will these things be? And what sign will there be when these things are about to take place?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said: “Take heed that you not be deceived. For many will come in My Name, saying, ‘I am Ha'Mashyach,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Therefore do not go after them.
But when you hear of wars and commotions, do not be terrified; for these things must come to pass first, but the end will not come immediately.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
And there will be great earthquakes in various places, and famines and pestilences; and there will be fearful sights and great signs from Shamaym.
But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, delivering you up to the congregation and prisons. You will be brought before kings and rulers for My Name’s sake.
But this will be your opportunity to tell them about Me.
Therefore settle it in your hearts not to meditate beforehand on what you will answer;
for I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all your adversaries will not be able to contradict or resist.
You will be betrayed even by parents and brothers, relatives and friends; and they will put some of you to death.
And you will be hated by all for My Name’s sake.
But not a hair of your head shall be lost.
By your patience possess your souls.
“But when you see Yahushalam surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is near.
Then let those who are in Yahudah flee to the mountains, let those who are in the midst of her depart, and let not those who are in the country enter her.
For these are the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing babies in those days! For there will be great distress in the land and wrath upon this people.
And they will fall by the edge of the sword, and be led away captive into all nations. And Yahushalam will be trampled by the other nations until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
“And there will be signs in the sun, in the moon, and in the stars; and on the Arath distress of nations, with perplexity, the sea and the waves roaring;
Men’s hearts failing them from fear and the expectation of those things which are coming on the Arath, for the powers of the Shamaym will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Adam coming in a cloud with power and great Kabad.
Now when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption draws near.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spoke to them a parable: “Look at the fig tree, and all the trees.
When they are already budding, you see and know for yourselves that summer is now near.
So you also, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is near.
Assuredly, I say to you, this generation will by no means pass away till all things take place.
Shamaym and Arath will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away.
“But take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life, and that Day come on you unexpectedly.
For it will come as a snare on all those who dwell on the face of the whole Arath.
Watch therefore, and pray always that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things that will come to pass, and to stand before the Son of Adam.”
And in the daytime 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was teaching in the temple, but at night He went out and stayed on the mountain called Ulivat.
Then early in the morning all the people came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in the temple to hear Him.
Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread drew near, which is called Passakh.
And the chief Kuhanym and the scribes sought how they might kill 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, for they feared the people.
Then ha'shatan entered Yudas, surnamed Iscariut, who was numbered among the twelve.
So he went his way and conferred with the chief Kuhanym and captains, how he might betray 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to them.
And they were glad, and agreed to give Yudas money.
So he promised and sought opportunity to betray 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to them in the absence of the multitude.
Then came the Day of Unleavened Bread, when the Passakh (Passover) Lamb must be killed.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sent Kafa and Yahukanun, saying, “Go and prepare the Passakh for us, that we may eat.”
So they said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Where do You want us to prepare?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Behold, when you have entered the city, a man will meet you carrying a pitcher of water; follow him into the house which he enters.
Then you shall say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says to you, “Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passakh with My Talmidym?” ’
Then he will show you a large, furnished upper room; make there ready.”
So they went and found it just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said to them, and they prepared the Passakh.
When the hour had come, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sat down, and the twelve Talmidym with Him.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “With fervent desire I have desired to eat this Passakh with you before I suffer;
for I say to you, I will no longer eat of it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the cup, and gave thanks, and said, “Take this and divide it among yourselves;
for I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH comes.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
Likewise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the Renewed Covenant in My blood, which is shed for you.
But behold, the hand of My betrayer is with Me on the table.
And truly the Son of Adam goes as it has been determined, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed!”
Then they began to question among themselves, which of them it was who would do this thing.
Now there was also a dispute among them, as to which of them should be considered the greatest.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “The kings of the other nations exercise dominion over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’
But among you it will be different. Those who are the greatest among you should take the lowest rank, and the leader should be like a servant.
Who is more important, the one who sits at the table or the one who serves? The one who sits at the table, of course. But not here! For I am among you as one who serves.
“But you are those who have continued with Me in My trials.
And I bestow upon you a kingdom, just as My ABBA bestowed one upon Me,
That you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'AL.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Simun, Simun! Indeed, 'ha'shatan has asked for you, that he may sift you as wheat.
But I have prayed for you, that your Amunah (faith) should not fail; and when you have returned to Me, strengthen your brethren.”
But Kafa said to Him, “Master, I am ready to go with You, both to prison and to death.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Kafa, let me tell you something. Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “When I sent you out to preach the Good News and you did not have money, a traveler’s bag, or an extra pair of sandals, did you lack anything?” So they said, “we lacked Nothing.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “But now, he who has a money bag, let him take it, and likewise a knapsack; and he who has no sword, let him sell his garment and buy one.
For I say to you that all which is written must still be accomplished in Me: ‘And He was numbered with the transgressors.’ For the things concerning Me have an end.”
So they said, “Master, look, here are two swords.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “It is enough.”
Coming out, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went to the Mount of Olives, as He was accustomed, and His Talmidym also followed Him.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came to the place, He said to them, “Pray that you may not enter into temptation.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA withdrawn from them a little distance, and He knelt down and prayed,
Saying, “ABBA, if you are willing, take this cup away from Me; nevertheless not My will, but Your Will be done.”
Then a Malak appeared to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from Shamaym, strengthening Him.
And being in agony, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA prayed more earnestly. Then His sweat became like great drops of blood falling down to the ground.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rose up from prayer, and had come to His Talmidym, He found them sleeping from sorrow.
Then He said to them, “Why do you sleep? Rise and pray, else you enter into temptation.”
And while 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was still speaking, behold, a multitude; and he who was called Yudas, one of the twelve Talmidym, went before them and drew near to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to kiss Him.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him, “Yudas, are you betraying the Son of Adam with a kiss?”
When those around 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw what was going to happen, they said to Him, “MASTER, shall we strike with the sword?”
And one of them struck the servant of the high Kuhan and cut off his right ear.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA answered and said, “No more of this.” And He touched his ear and healed him.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to the chief Kuhanym, captains of the temple, and the elders who had come to Him, “Have you come out, as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
When I was with you daily in the temple, you did not try to seize Me. But this is your hour, and the moment for the power of darkness.”
Having arrested 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they led Him and brought Him into the high Kuhan’s house. But Kafa followed at a distance.
Now when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard and sat down together, Kafa sat among them.
And a certain servant girl, seeing Kafa as he sat by the fire, looked intently at him and said, “This man was also with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.”
But Kafa denied 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, saying, “Woman, I do not know Him.”
And after a little while another saw Kafa and said, “You also are of them.” But Kafa said, “Man, I am not!”
Then after about an hour had passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, “Surely this fellow also was with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, for he is a Galilyan.”
But Kafa said, “Man, I do not know what you are saying!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned and looked at Kafa. Then Kafa remembered the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, how He had said to him, “Before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.”
So Kafa went out and wept bitterly.
Now the men who held 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA mocked Him and beat Him.
And having blindfolded 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they struck Him on the face and asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, saying, “Prophesy! Who is the one who struck You?”
And many other things they blasphemously spoke against Him.
As soon as it was day, the elders of the people, both chief Kuhanym and scribes, came together and led 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA into their council, saying,
“If You are Ha'Mashyach, tell us.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “If I tell you, you will by no means believe.
And if I also ask you, you will by no means answer Me or let Me go.
Hereafter the Son of Adam will sit on the right hand of the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then they all said, “Are You then the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?” then He said to them, “You rightly say that I Am.”
And they said “Why do we need other witnesses? “We ourselves heard it from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA himself.”
Then the entire council took 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to Pilate, the Roman governor.
They began to state their case: “This man has been leading our people astray by telling them not to pay their taxes to the Roman government and by claiming he is Ha'Mashyach, a king.”
So Pilate asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Are you the king of the Yahudym?” and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “You have said it.”
Pilate turned to the leading Kuhanym and to the crowd and said, “I find nothing wrong with this man!”
Then they became insistent. “But he is causing riots by his teaching wherever he goes, all over Yahudah, from Galily to Yahushalam!”
“Oh, is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA a Galilyan?” Pilate asked.
When they said that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was, Pilate sent him to Harud Antipas, because Galily was under Harud’s jurisdiction, and Harud happened to be in Yahushalam at the time.
Harud was delighted at the opportunity to see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, because he had heard about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and had been hoping for a long time to see him perform a miracle.
Harud asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA question after question, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA refused to answer.
Meanwhile, the leading Kuhanym and the teachers of religious law stood there shouting their accusations.
Then Harud and his soldiers began mocking and ridiculing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA ,Finally they put a royal robe on him and sent him back to Pilate.
(Harud and Pilate, who had been enemies before, became friends that day.)
Then Pilate called together the leading Kuhanym and other religious leaders, along with the people,
And pilate announced his verdict. “You brought this man to me, accusing him of leading a revolt. I have examined him thoroughly on this point in your presence and find him innocent.
Even Harud came to the same conclusion and sent him back to us. Nothing this man has done calls for the death penalty.
So I will have him flogged, and then I will release him.”
For it was necessary for him to release one to them at the feast.
Then a mighty roar rose from the crowd, and with one voice they shouted, “Kill him, and release Barabbas to us!”
(Barabbas was in prison for taking part in an insurrection in Yahushalam against the government, and for murder.)
Pilate argued with them, because he wanted to release 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
But they kept shouting, “impale him! Impale him!”
For the third time Pilate demanded, “Why? What crime has he committed? I have found no reason to sentence him to death. So I will have him flogged, and then I will release him.”
But the mob shouted louder and louder, demanding that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA be impaled, and their voices prevailed.
So Pilate sentenced 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to die as they demanded.
And as they had requested, he released Barabbas, the man in prison for insurrection and murder. But he turned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA over to them to do as they wished.

As they led 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA away, a man named Simun, who was from Cyrana, happened to be coming in from the countryside. The soldiers seized him and put the execution stake on him and made him carry it behind 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
A large crowd trailed behind, including many grief-stricken women.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA turned and said to them, “Daughters of Yahushalam, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
For the days are coming when they will say, ‘Fortunate indeed are the women who are childless, the wombs that have not borne a child and the breasts that have never nursed.’
People will beg the mountains, ‘Fall on us,’ and plead with the hills, ‘Bury us.’
For if these things are done when the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”
Two others, both criminals, were led out to be executed with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
When they came to a place called The Skull, they nailed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to the execution stake. And the criminals were also impaled, one on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA's right and one on His left.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “ABBA, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And the soldiers gambled for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s clothes by throwing dice.
The crowd watched and the leaders scoffed. “He saved others,” they said, “let Him save Himself if he is really Ha'Mashyach, the chosen One of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
Then the soldiers mocked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA too, by offering Him a drink of sour wine.
They called out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “If you are the King of the Yahudym, save yourself!”
A sign was fastened above 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with these words: “This is the King of the Yahudym.”
One of the criminals hanging beside 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA scoffed, “So you are Ha'Mashyach, are you? Prove it by saving yourself and us, too, while you are at it!”
But the other criminal protested, “Do you not fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH even when you have been sentenced to die?
We deserve to die for our crimes, but this man has not done anything wrong.”
Then he said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, my MASTER remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “I assure you, today you will be with me in paradise.”
By this time it was about noon, and darkness fell across the whole land until ninth hour.
The light from the sun was gone. And suddenly, the curtain in the sanctuary of the Temple was torn down the middle.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA shouted, “ABBA, I entrust my Ruach into your hands!” And with those words He breathed His last.
When the Roman officer overseeing the execution saw what had happened, he worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and said, “Surely this man was innocent.”
And when all the crowd that came to see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA impaled, saw what had happened, they went home in deep sorrow.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s friends, including the women who had followed Him from Galily, stood at a distance watching.
Now there was a good and righteous man named Ya'asaf, he was a member of the Yahudym high council,
But he had not agreed with the decision and actions of the other religious leaders. He was from the town of Arimathaa in Yahudah, and he was waiting for the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to come.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Then he took His body down from the execution stake and wrapped it in a long sheet of linen cloth and laid it in a new tomb that had been carved out of rock.
That day was the Preparation, and the Shabbat drew near.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s body was taken away, the women from Galily followed and saw the tomb where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s body was placed.
Then they went home and prepared spices and ointments to anoint 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s body. But by the time they were finished the Shabbat had begun, so they rested according to the Commandments.
Now on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women came to the tomb bringing the spices which they had prepared.
They found that the stone had been rolled away from the entrance.
So they went in, but they did not find the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
As they stood there puzzled, two men suddenly appeared to them, clothed in dazzling robes.
The women were terrified and bowed with their faces to the ground. Then the men asked, “Why are you looking among the dead for someone who is alive?
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is not here! He is risen from the dead! Remember what he told you back in Galily,
that the Son of Adam must be betrayed into the hands of sinful men and be impaled, and that he would rise again on the third day.”
Then they remembered that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said this.
So they rushed back from the tomb to tell His eleven Talmidym and everyone else what had happened.
It was Maryam Magdalyn, Yuanna, Maryam the mother of Ya'aqub, and several other women who told the Talmidym what had happened.
But the story sounded like nonsense to the men, so they did not believe it.
However, Kafa jumped up and ran to the tomb to look. Stooping, he peered in and saw the empty linen wrappings; then he went home again, wondering what had happened.
That same day two of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s followers were walking to the village of Ammaus, seven miles from Yahushalam.
As they walked along they were talking about everything that had happened.
As they talked and discussed these things, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Himself suddenly came and began walking with them.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH kept them from recognizing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?” They stood still and sadness written across their faces.
Then one of them, Claupas, replied, “You must be the only person in Yahushalam who has not heard about all the things that have happened there the last few days.”

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “What things? “The things that happened to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the man from Nazarath,” they said. “He was a Nabym who did powerful miracles, and he was a mighty teacher in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and all the people.
But our leading Kuhanym and other religious leaders handed him over to be condemned to death, and they impaled Him.
We had hoped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was Ha'Mashyach who had come to rescue Yashar'AL. This all happened three days ago.
“Then some women from our group of his followers were at his tomb early this morning, and they came back with an amazing report.
They said His body was missing, and they had seen Malakym who told them 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is alive!
Some of our men ran out to see, and sure enough, the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was gone, just as the women had said.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “You foolish people! You find it so hard to believe all that the Nabyms wrote in the Scriptures.
Was it not clearly predicted that Ha'Mashyach would have to suffer all these things before entering His Kabad?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took them through the writings of Musha and all the Nabyms, explaining from all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself.
By this time they were nearing Ammaus the end of their journey. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA acted as if He were going on,
but they begged Him, “Stay the night with us, since it is getting late.” So he went home with them.
As they sat down to eat, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA took the bread and Baraked it. Then He broke it and gave it to them.
Suddenly, their eyes were opened, and they recognized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. And at that moment He disappeared!
They said to each other, “Did our hearts not burn within us as He talked with us on the road and explained the Scriptures to us?”
And within the hour they were on their way back to Yahushalam. There they found the eleven Talmidym and the others who had gathered with them,
who said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA has really risen! He appeared to Kafa.”
Then the two from Ammaus told their story of how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had appeared to them as they were walking along the road, and how they had recognized 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA as He was breaking the bread.
And just as they were telling about it, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Himself was suddenly standing there among them. And He said to them; “Shalum be with you,”
But the whole group was startled and frightened, thinking they were seeing a ghost!
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked. “Why are you frightened? “Why are your hearts filled with doubt?
Look at my hands. Look at my feet. You can see that it is really Me. Touch Me and make sure that I Am alive, because ghosts do not have bodies, as you see that I do.”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spoke, He showed them his hands and his feet.
Still they stood there in disbelief, filled with joy and wonder. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”
They gave 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA a piece of broiled fish,
and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA ate it as they watched.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “When I was with you before, I told you that everything written about me in the law of Musha and the writing of the Nabyms and in the Tahalym concerning me.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Yes, it was written long ago that Ha'Mashyach would suffer and die and rise from the dead on the third day.
It was also written that this message would be proclaimed in the authority of His Name to all the nations, beginning in Yahushalam: ‘There is forgiveness of sins for all who repent.’
You are witnesses of all these things.
“And now I will send the RUACH Ha'Qadash, just as my ABBA promised. But stay here in the city until the RUACH Ha'Qadash comes and fills you with power from Shamaym.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA led them to Bathany, and lifting His hands to Shamaym He Baraked them.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Baraked them, He left them and was taken up to Shamaym.
So they all worshiped
And they spent all of their time in the Haykal (Temple), and they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

books.name: John
chapters: In the beginning the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar already existed, The 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar was with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar was 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
The 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar existed in the beginning with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH created everything through the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar, and nothing was created except through the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar.
In the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar was life, and the life was the light of men.
The light of the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar shines in the darkness, and the darkness can never extinguish the Light.
There was a man sent from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, whose name was Yahukanun.
to tell about the light so that everyone might believe because of his testimony.
Yahukanun himself was not the light; he was simply a witness to tell about the light.
The one who is the true light, who will give light to everyone, is on his way coming into the world.
The 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar came into the very world He created, but the world did not recognize Him.
The 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar came to His own people, and they rejected him.
But as many who received the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar, to them the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar gave the right to become children of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to those who believe in His Name:
who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
So the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar became a man and made his home among us. The 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar was full of unfailing love and faithfulness. And we have seen the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar‘s Kabad, the Kabad of ABBA’s one and only Son.

Yahukanun testified about the 𐤃𐤁𐤓𐤉_Dabar when he shouted to the crowds, “This is the one I was talking about when I said, ‘Someone is coming after me who is far greater than I am, for He existed long before me.’”
From His abundance we have all received one precious Barakah after another.
For the law was given through Musha, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s unfailing love and faithfulness came through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach.
No one has ever seen 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. But the unique One, who is himself 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, is near to ABBA’s heart, He has revealed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to us.
This was Yahukanun’s testimony when the Yahudym leaders sent Kuhanym and Temple assistants from Yahushalam to ask Yahukanun, “Who are you?”
He came right out and said, “I am not Ha'Mashyach.”
“Well then, who are you?” they asked. “Are you AliYahu? “No,” he replied.
“Then who are you? We need an answer for those who sent us. What do you have to say about yourself?”
Yahukanun replied in the words of the Nabym Yashayahu:
Then the Pharisees who had been sent 25 asked him, “If you are not Ha'Mashyach or AliYahu or the Nabym, what right do you have to baptize?”
Yahukanun told them, “I baptize with water, but right here in the crowd is someone you do not recognize.
Though His ministry follows mine, I am not even worthy to be His slave and untie the straps of his sandal.”
This encounter took place in Bathany, an area east of the Yurdan River, where Yahukanun was baptizing.
The next day Yahukanun saw YAHUSHA coming toward him and said, “Look! The Lamb of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who takes away the sin of the world!
He is the one I was talking about when I said, ‘A man is coming after me who is far greater than I am, for He existed long before me.’
I did not know who Ha'Mashyach was. But I came baptizing people with water so that Yashar'AL could know that He is Ha'Mashyach.”
Then Yahukanun testified, “I saw the RUACH Ha'Qadash descending like a dove from Shamaym and resting upon Ha'Mashyach.

I did not know Ha'Mashyach was the one, but when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent me to baptize with water, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to me, ‘The one on whom you see the RUACH descend and rest is the one who will baptize with the RUACH Ha'Qadash.’
I saw this happen to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, so I Yahukanun testify that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is the Chosen One of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
The following day Yahukanun was again standing with two of his followers.
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA walked by, Yahukanun looked at Him and declared, “Look! There is the Lamb of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
When Yahukanun’s two Talmidym heard this, they followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA looked around and saw them following. “What do you want?” 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked them. They replied, “Rabbi” (which means “Teacher”), “where are you staying?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was staying, and they remained with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA that day (now it was about the tenth hour).
Andraw, Simun Kafa’s brother, was one of these men who heard what Yahukanun said and then followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Andraw went to find his brother, Simun, and told him, “We have found Ha'Mashyach” (which means “Messiah”).
Then Andraw brought Simun to meet 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. Looking intently at Simun, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Your name is Simun Ba-Yunah, but you will be called Kafa”. (which means “A Rock”).
The next day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA decided to go to Galily. He found Philip and said to him, “Come, follow me.”
Philip was from Bathsaida, Andraw and Kafa’s hometown.
Philip went to look for Nathanaal and told him, “We have found the very person Musha and the Nabyms wrote about! His Name is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the son of Ya'asaf from Nazarath.”
“Nazarath!” exclaimed Nathanaal. “Can anything good come from Nazarath?”
As they approached, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Now here is a genuine son of Yashar'AL, a man of complete integrity.”
“How do you know about me?” Nathanaal asked. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “I could see you under the fig tree before Philip found you.”
Then Nathanaal exclaimed, “Rabbi, you are the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, the King of Yashar'AL!”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked him, “Do you believe this just because I told you I had seen you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than this.”

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Truly I tell all of you. You will all see Shamaym open and the Malakym of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH going up and down on the Son of Adam, the one who is the stairway between Shamaym and Arath.”
The next day there was a wedding celebration in the village of Cana in Galily. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s mother was there,
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and His Talmidym were also invited to the celebration.
The wine supply ran out during the festivities, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s mother told Him, “They have no more wine.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied. “Dear woman, that is not our problem, “My time has not yet come.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s mother told the servants, “Do whatever 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA tells you.”
Standing nearby were six stone water jars, used for Yahudym ceremonial washing. Each could hold twenty to thirty gallons.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” When the jars had been filled,
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Now dip some out, and take it to the master of ceremonies.” So the servants followed His instructions.
When the master of ceremonies tasted the water that was now wine, not knowing where it had come from (though, of course, the servants knew), the master of ceremonies called the bridegroom over.
“A host always serves the best wine first,” he said. “Then, when everyone has had a lot to drink, he brings out the less expensive wine. But you have kept the best until now!”
This miraculous sign at Cana in Galily was the first time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA revealed his Kabad. And His Talmidym believed in him.
After the wedding He went to Capernaum for a few days with his mother, his brothers, and His Talmidym.
It was nearly time for the Yahudym Passover celebration, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went to Yahushalam.
In the Temple area 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saw merchants selling cattle, sheep, and doves for sacrifices; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA also saw dealers at tables exchanging foreign money.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA made a whip from some ropes and chased them all out of the Temple. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA drove out the sheep and cattle, scattered the money changers coins over the floor, and turned over their tables.
Then, going over to the people who sold doves, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told them, “Get these things out of here. Stop turning my ABBA’s house into a marketplace!”
Then his Talmidym remembered this prophecy from the Scriptures: that said, “My Passion for the house of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has consumed me.”
But the Yahudym leaders demanded, “What are you doing? If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave you authority to do this, show us a miraculous sign to prove it.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied. “All right, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
“What!” they exclaimed. “It has taken forty-six years to build this Temple, and you can rebuild it in three days?”
But when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said “this temple,” he meant his own body.
After 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was raised from the dead, His Talmidym remembered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said this, and they believed both the Scriptures and what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had said.
Because of the miraculous signs 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA did in Yahushalam at the Passakh celebration, many began to trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA did not trust them, because He knew all about people.
For no one needs to tell Him about man's nature, for He knew what was in the heart of each man.
There was a man named Nicudamus, a Yahudym religious leader who was a Pharisee.

After dark one evening, Nicudamus came to speak with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. “Rabbi,” he said, “we all know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent you to teach us. Your miraculous signs are evidence that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with you.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “I tell you the truth, unless you are born again, you cannot see the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
“What do you mean?” exclaimed Nicudamus. “How can an old man go back into his mother’s womb and be born again?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “I assure you, no one can enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH without being born of water and the RUACH.
What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the RUACH is Ruach.
So do not be surprised when I say, ‘You must be born again.’
The wind blows wherever it wants. Just as you can hear the wind but cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going, so is everyone who is born of the Ruach.”
“How are these things possible?” Nicudamus asked.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “You are a respected Yahudym teacher, and yet you do not understand these things?
Most assuredly, I say to you, We speak what We know and testify what We have seen, and you do not receive Our testimony.
But if you do not believe me when I tell you things about this Arath, how can you possibly believe me if I tell you things about Shamaym?
No one has ever gone to Shamaym and returned. But the Son of Adam has come down from Shamaym.
And as Musha lifted up the bronze snake on a pole in the wilderness, so the Son of Adam must be lifted up,
so that everyone who believes in him will have eternal life.
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH loved the world that He created: and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave His one and only dear Son, so that everyone who believes in the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will not perish but have Everlasting life.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent His Son into the world not to judge the world, but to save the world through His Son.

“There is no judgment against anyone who believes in the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. But anyone who does not believe in the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has already been judged for not believing in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s One and only Son.
And the judgment is based on this fact: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s light came into the world, but people loved the darkness more than the light, for their actions were evil.
All who do evil hate the light and refuse to go near the light, for they fear their sins will be exposed if they come near the light.
But those who do what is right come to the light so others can see that they are doing what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH wants.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and his Talmidym left Yahushalam and went into the Yahudah countryside. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spent some time with them there, baptizing people.
At this time Yahukanun the Baptist was baptizing at Aanun, near Salim, because there was plenty of water there; and people kept coming to him for baptism.
(This was before Yahukanun was thrown into prison.)
A debate broke out between Yahukanun’s followers and a certain Yahudym over ceremonial cleansing.

So Yahukanun’s followers came to him and said, “Rabbi, the man you met on the other side of the Yurdan River, the one you identified as Ha'Mashyach, is also baptizing people. And everybody is going to him instead of coming to us.”
Yahukanun replied, “No one can receive anything unless 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives it from Shamaym.
You yourselves know how plainly I told you, ‘I am not Ha'Mashyach. I am only here to prepare the way for Ha'Mashyach.’
It is the bridegroom who marries the bride, and the best man is simply glad to stand with him and hear His vows. Therefore, I am filled with joy at His success.
Ha'Mashyach must become greater and greater, and I must become less and less.
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA has come from above and is greater than anyone else. We are of the Arath, and we speak things of the Arath, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA has come from Shamaym and is greater than anyone else.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA testifies about what He has seen and heard, but how few believe what He tells them!
Anyone who accepts the testimony of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA can affirm that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is true.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is sent by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And He speaks the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gives Him the RUACH without limit.
For ABBA loves his Son and has put everything into His hands.
And anyone who believes in the son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has eternal life. Anyone who does not obey the Son will never experience eternal life but remains under 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s angry judgment.”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA knew the Pharisees had heard that He was baptizing and making more followers than Yahukanun.
(though 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA himself did not baptize them, His Talmidym did).
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA left Yahudah and returned to Galily.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had to go through Samaria on the way.
Eventually 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came to the Samaritan village of Sychar, near the field that Ya'aqub gave to his son Ya'asaf.
Ya'aqub’s well was there; and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, tired from the long walk, sat wearily beside the well, it was about the sixth hour.
Soon a Samaritan woman came to draw water, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to her, “Please give me a drink.”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was alone at the time because His Talmidym had gone into the village to buy some food.
The woman was surprised, for Yahudym refuse to have anything to do with Samaritans. She said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “You are a Yahudym, and I am a Samaritan woman. Why are you asking me for a drink?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “If you only knew the gift 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has for you and who you are speaking to, you would ask me, and I would give you living water.”
“But sir, you do not have a rope or a bucket,” she said, “and this well is very deep. Where would you get this living water?
And besides, do you think you are greater than our ancestor Ya'aqub, who gave us this well? How can you offer better water than this water that Ya'aqub and his sons and his animals enjoyed?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Anyone who drinks this water will soon become thirsty again.
But those who drink the water I give, will never be thirsty again. It becomes a fresh, bubbling spring within them, giving them eternal life.”
“Please, sir,” the woman said, “give me this water! Then I will never be thirsty again, and I will not have to come here to get water.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told her. “Go and get your husband,”
“I do not have a husband,” the woman replied. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “You are right! You do not have a husband
for you have had five husbands, and you are not even married to the man you are living with now. You certainly spoke the truth!”
“Sir,” the woman said, “you must be a Nabym.
So tell me, why is it that you Yahudym insist that Yahushalam is the only place of worship, while we Samaritans claim it is here at Mount Garizim, where our ancestors worshiped?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “Believe me, dear woman, the time is coming when it will no longer matter whether you worship ABBA on this mountain or in Yahushalam.
You Samaritans know very little about the one you worship, while we Yahudym know all about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for salvation comes through the Yahudym.
But the time is coming, indeed it is here now, when the true worshipers will worship ABBA in Ruach and in 𐤀𐤌𐤕_Amat (Truth). For ABBA is looking for those who will worship Him that way.
