She saw two white-robed Malakym, one sitting at the head and the other at the foot of the place where the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had been lying.
“Dear woman, why are you crying?” the Malakym asked her. “Because they have taken away my Master,” she replied, “and I do not know where they have put Him.”
She turned to leave and saw someone standing there. It was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, but she did not recognize Him.

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked her. “Dear woman, why are you crying?” Who are you looking for?” She thought He was the gardener. “Sir,” she said, “if you have taken 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA away, tell me where you have put him, and I will go and get Him.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. Maryam” She turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and cried out, “Rabbuni!” (which is Abarym for “Teacher”).

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Do not cling to me,” for I have not yet ascended to ABBA 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. But go find My brothers and tell them, ‘I Am ascending to My ABBA and your ABBA, to My 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.’”
Maryam Magdalyn found the Talmidym and told them, “I have seen the Master!” Then she gave them His message.

On the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, the Talmidym assembled and the doors were shut, for fear of the Yahudym, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came and stood in their midst, and said to them, “Shalum be with you.”
As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spoke, He showed them the wounds in his hands and his side. They were filled with joy when they saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA!
Again 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Shalum be with you. As ABBA 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent Me, so I Am sending you.”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA breathed on them and said, “Receive the RUACH Ha'Qadash.
If you forgive anyone’s sins, they are forgiven. If you do not forgive them, they are not forgiven.”
One of the twelve Talmidym, Thumas (nicknamed the Twin), was not with the others when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came.
They told him, “We have seen the Master!” But he replied, “I will not believe it unless I see the nail wounds in his hands, put my fingers into them, and place my hand into the wound in his side.”

Eight days later the Talmidym were together again, and this time Thumas was with them. The doors were locked; but suddenly, as before, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was standing among them. And He said. “Shalum be with you,”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to Thumas, “Put your finger here, and look at My hands. Put your hand into the wound in My side, Stop doubting and Believe!”
“My Mashyach and my Master!” Thumas exclaimed.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told Thumas, “You believe because you have seen me. Baraked are those who believe without seeing me.”
The Talmidym saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA do many other miraculous signs in addition to the ones recorded in this book.

But these are written so that you may continue to believe that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is Ha'Mashyach, the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and that by believing in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA you will have life by the power of His Name.
Later, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA appeared again to the Talmidym beside the Sea of Galily. This is how it happened.
Several of the Talmidym were there, Simun Kafa, Thumas (nicknamed the Twin), Nathanaal from Cana in Galily, the sons of Zabadyahu, and two other Talmidym.
Simun Kafa said, “I am going fishing. “We will come, too,” they all said. So they went out in the boat, but they caught nothing all night.
At dawn 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was standing on the beach, but the Talmidym could not see who He was.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA called out, “Fellows, have you caught any fish?” “No,” they replied.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Throw out your net on the right-hand side of the boat, and you will get some!” So they did, and they could not haul in the net because there were so many fish in it.

Then the Talmidym that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA loved said to Kafa, “It’s the Master!” When Simun Kafa heard that it was the Master, he put on his tunic (for he had stripped for work), jumped into the water, and headed to shore.
The others stayed with the boat and pulled the loaded net to the shore, for they were only about a hundred yards from shore.
When they got there, they found breakfast waiting for them, fish cooking over a charcoal fire, and some bread.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. Bring some of the fish you have just caught,”
So Simun Kafa went aboard and dragged the net to the shore. There were one hundred and fifty three large fish, and yet the net had not torn.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. “Now come and have some breakfast!”. None of the Talmidym dared to ask 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “Who are you?” They knew it was the Master Himself.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA served them the bread and the fish.
This was the third time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had appeared to His Talmidym since He had been raised from the dead.
After breakfast 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked Kafa, “Simun son of Yunah, do you love me more than these?” “Yes, Master,” Kafa replied, “you know I love you.”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA repeated the question, “Simun son of Yunah, do you love me?” “Yes, Master,” Kafa said, “you know I love you.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said. “Then take care of my sheep,”

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked Kafa the third time, “Simun son of Yunah, do you love me?” Kafa was hurt that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA asked the question a third time, he said, “Master, you know everything. You know that I love you.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Then feed my sheep.

“I tell you the truth, when you were young, you were able to do as you liked; you dressed yourself and went wherever you wanted to go. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and others will dress you and take you where you do not want to go.”
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said this to let Kafa know by what kind of death he would esteem 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA told Kafa, “Follow me.”
Kafa turned around and saw behind them the Talmidym 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA loved, the one who had leaned over to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA during supper and asked, “Master, who will betray you?”
Kafa asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, “What about him, Master?”
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “If I want him to remain alive until I return, what is that to you? As for you, follow me.”

So the rumor spread among the set apart believers that this Talmidym would not die. But that is not what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said at all. He only said, “If I want him to remain alive until I return, what is that to you?”
This Talmidym is the one who testifies to these events and has recorded them here. And we know that his account of these things is accurate.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA also did many other things. If they were all written down, I suppose the whole world could not contain the books that would be written.

books.name: Acts
chapters: In my first book I told you, Thauphilus, I wrote about everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA began to do and teach
Until the day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was taken up to Shamaym after giving his chosen Shaliach (apostles) further instructions through the RUACH Ha'Qadash.

After 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had risen from death, during forty days He appeared to the Talmidym from time to time, and He proved to them in many ways that He was actually alive. And He talked to them about the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
On one occasion, while 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was eating with His Talmidym, He gave them this command: “Do not leave Yahushalam until ABBA 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sends you the gift HE promised, as I told you before.
Yahukanun baptized with water, but in just a few days you will be baptized with the RUACH Ha'Qadash.”
So when the Shaliach (apostles) were with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they kept asking Him, “Master, has the time come for you to free Yashar'AL and restore our kingdom?”
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA replied, “ABBA 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH alone has the authority to set those dates and times, and they are not for you to know.

But you will receive power when the RUACH Ha'Qadash comes upon you. And you will be my witnesses, telling people about Me everywhere in Yahushalam, throughout Yahudah, in Samaria, and to the ends of the Arath.”
After saying this, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was taken up into a cloud while they were watching, and they could no longer see Him.
As they strained to see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA rising into Shamaym, two white robed men suddenly stood among them.

“Men of Galily,” they said, “why are you standing here staring into Shamaym? 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA has been taken from you into Shamaym, but someday 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA will return from Shamaym in the same way you saw Him go!”
Then the Shaliach (apostles) returned to Yahushalam from the Mount of Olives, a distance of half a mile.
When they arrived, they went to the upstairs room of the house where they were staying.
They all met together and were constantly united in prayer, along with Maryam the mother of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, several other women, and the brothers of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
During this time, when about one hundred and twenty believers were together in one place, Kafa stood up and addressed them.

“Brothers,” he said, “the Scriptures had to be fulfilled concerning Yudas Iscariut, who guided those who arrested 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. This was predicted long ago by the RUACH Ha'Qadash, speaking through King Daud.
Yudas was numbered with us and shared in the twelve fold with us.”
(Yudas Iscariut had bought a field with the money he received for his treachery. Falling headfirst there, his body split open, spilling out all his intestines.
Everyone in Yahushalam heard about this, so they called that field in their language Akaldama, that is, Field of Blood.)

Kafa continued, “This was written in the book of Tahalym (Psalms), where it says, ‘Let his home become desolate, with no one living in it.’ It also says, ‘Let someone else take his position.’ (Tahalym 109:8)
“So now we must choose a replacement for Yudas Iscariut from among the men who were with us the entire time we were traveling with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach
from the time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was baptized by Yahukanun until the day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was taken from us. Whoever is chosen will join us as a witness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s resurrection.
So they nominated two men: Ya'asaf called Barsabbas (also known as Yustus) and Matthias.
Then they all prayed, “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you know every heart. Show us which of these men you have chosen
as a Shaliach (apostle) to replace Yudas in this twelve fold, for Yudas Iscariut has deserted us and gone where he belongs.”
Then they cast lots, and Matthias was selected to become a Talmidym with the other eleven.
On the day of Shabuut (Pentecost) all the believers were meeting together in one place.
Suddenly, there was a sound from Shamaym like the roaring of a mighty windstorm, and it filled the house where they were sitting.
Then they saw what looked like flames or tongues of fire appeared and settled on each of them.
And everyone present was filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash and they began speaking in other tongues (languages), as the RUACH Ha'Qadash gave them this ability.
At that time there were devout Yahudym from every nation living in Yahushalam.
When they heard the loud noise, everyone came running, and they were bewildered to hear their own languages being spoken by the believers.
They were completely amazed. “How can this be?” they exclaimed. “These people are all from Galily,
and yet we hear them speaking in our own native languages!
Here we are Parthians, Madas, Alamites, people from Masuputamia, Yahudah, Cappaducia, Puntus, the province of Asia,
Phrygia, Pamphylia, Mitzraym, and the areas of Libya around Cyrana, visitors from Rome
(both Yahudym and converts to Yahudym), Cratans, and Arabs. And we all hear these people speaking in our own languages about the wonderful things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has done!”
They stood there amazed and perplexed. “What can this mean?” they asked each other.
But others in the crowd ridiculed them, saying, “They are just drunk, that is all!”
Then Kafa stepped forward with the eleven other Talmidym and shouted to the crowd, “Listen carefully, all of you, fellow Yahudym and residents of Yahushalam! Make no mistake about this.
These people are not drunk, as some of you are assuming. since it is only the third hour of the day.
No, what you see was predicted long ago by the Nabym Yual:

‘In the last days,’ says 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, ‘I will pour out my RUACH upon all souls alive (people). Your sons and daughters will Naba (prophesy). Your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
In those days I will pour out my RUACH even on my servants men and women alike and they will Naba (prophesy).
And I will cause wonders in the Shamaym above and signs on the Arath below, blood and fire and clouds of smoke.
The sun will become dark and the moon will turn blood red before that great and esteemed day that Ha'Mashyach will arrive.
But everyone who calls on the Name of Ha'Mashyach will be saved.’
“People of Yashar'AL, listen! 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH publicly endorsed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA the Nazarym by doing powerful miracles, wonders, and signs through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, as you well know.

But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH knew what would happen, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH prearranged plan was carried out when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was betrayed. With the help of lawless foreigners, you nailed Him to an execution stake and killed Him.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH released 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from the horrors of death and raised Him back to life, for death could not keep 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in its grip.
King Daud said this about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA: ‘I see that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is always with me. I will not be shaken, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is right beside me.
No wonder my heart is glad, and my tongue shouts Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH! My body rests in hope.
For you will not leave my soul among the dead or allow your Qadash One to rot in the grave.
You have shown me the way of life, and you will fill me with the joy of your presence.’
“Dear brothers, think about this! You can be sure that the patriarch Daud was not referring to himself, for he died and was buried, and his tomb is still here among us.
But Daud was a Nabym, and Daud knew 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised with an oath that one of Daud’s own descendants would sit on his throne.
Daud was looking into the future and speaking of Ha'Mashyach’s resurrection. Daud was saying that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH would not leave Ha'Mashyach among the dead or allow His body to rot in the grave.
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from the dead, and we are all witnesses of this.

Now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is exalted to the place of highest honor in Shamaym, at the right hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And as ABBA 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised, HE gave 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA the RUACH Ha'Qadash to pour out upon us, just as you see and hear today.
For King Daud himself never ascended into Shamaym, yet Daud said, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to my MASTER, “Sit in the place of honor at my right hand
Until I humble your enemies, making them a footstool under your feet.”’
“So let everyone in Yashar'AL know for certain that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has made this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, whom you impaled, to be both MASTER and Ha'Mashyach!”
Kafa’s words pierced their hearts, and they said to him and to the other Talmidym, “Brothers, what should we do?”

Kafa replied, “Each of you must repent of your sins and turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and be baptized in the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach for the forgiveness of your sins. Then you will receive the gift of the RUACH Ha'Qadash.
This promise is to you, to your children, and to those far away, all who have been called by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH.
Then Kafa continued preaching for a long time, strongly urging all his listeners, “Save yourselves from this crooked generation!”
Then those who gladly received Kafa‘s word were baptized; and that day about three thousand souls were added to them.
And they continued steadfastly in the Shaliach's (apostle's) ways and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers.
Then fear came upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were done through the Shaliachs.
Now all who believed were together, and had all things in common,
They sold their property and possessions and shared the money with those in need.
So they continue daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, they ate their food with gladness and simplicity of heart,
All the while they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and enjoying the goodwill of all the people. And each day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH added to their fellowship those who were being saved.
Kafa and Yahukanun went to the Haykal (Temple) at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

As they approached the Haykal, a man lame from birth was being carried in. Each day he was put beside the Haykal (temple) gate, the one called the Beautiful Gate, so he could beg from the people going into the Haykal.
When the beggar saw Kafa and Yahukanun about to enter, he asked them for some money.
Kafa and Yahukanun looked at him intently, and Kafa said, “Look at us!”
The lame man looked at them eagerly, expecting some money.
But Kafa said, “I do not have any silver or gold for you. But I will give you what I have. In the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach the Nazarym, get up and walk!”
Then Kafa took the lame man by the right hand and helped him up. And as Kafa did, the man’s feet and ankles were instantly healed and strengthened.
He jumped up, stood on his feet, and began to walk! Then, walking, and leaping, he Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, he went into the Haykal (Temple) with them.
All the people saw him walking and heard him Yadahym 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
When they realized he was the lame beggar they had seen so often at the Beautiful Gate, they were absolutely astounded!
They all rushed out in amazement to Shalumah’s Colonnade, where the man was holding tightly to Kafa and Yahukanun.

Kafa saw his opportunity and addressed the crowd. “People of Yashar'AL,” he said, “what is so surprising about this? And why stare at us as though we had made this man walk by our own power or righteousness?

For it is the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, Yachaq, and Ya'aqub, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of all our ancestors, who has brought honor to HIS servant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA by doing this. This is the same 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA whom you handed over and rejected before Pilate, despite Pilate’s decision to release him.
You rejected this Qadash and righteous One and instead demanded the release of a murderer.
You killed the author of life, but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from the dead. And we are witnesses of this fact!
“Through Amunah in the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, this man was healed and you know how crippled he was before. Amunah in the Name 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA has healed him before your very eyes.
“Friends, I realize that what you and your leaders did to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was done in ignorance.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was fulfilling what all the Nabyms had foretold about Ha'Mashyach that He must suffer these things.
Now repent of your sins and turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, so that your sins may be wiped away.
Then times of refreshment will come from the presence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and HE will again send you 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the One 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH chose to be Ha'Mashyach.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA must remain in Shamaym until the time for the final restoration of all things, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH promised long ago through HIS Qadash Nabyms.
Musha said, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH your 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH will raise up for you a Nabym like me from among your own people. Listen carefully to everything He tells you.’
Then Musha said, ‘Anyone who will not listen to that Nabym will be completely cut off from the congregation of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.’
“Starting with Shamual, every Nabym spoke about what is happening today.

You are the children of those Nabym, and you are included in the covenant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH promised to your ancestors. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to Abraham, ‘Through your descendants all the families on Arath will be Baraked.’
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised up His servant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and then also 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA first to you people of Yashar'AL, to Barak you by turning each of you back from your sinful ways.”
While Kafa and Yahukanun were speaking to the people, they were confronted by the Kuhanym, the captain of the Temple's guard, and some of the Sadducees.
These leaders were very disturbed that Kafa and Yahukanun were teaching the people that in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA there is a resurrection of the dead.
They arrested them and, since it was already evening, they put them in jail until morning.
But many of the people who heard their message believed it, so the number of believers was five thousand men, not counting women and children.
The next day the council of all the rulers and elders and teachers of religious law met in Yahushalam.
Annas the high Kuhan was there, along with Caiaphas, Yahukanun, Alaxander, and other relatives of the high Kuhan.
They brought in the two Talmidym and demanded, “By what power, or in whose Name, have you done this?”
Then Kafa, filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash, said to them, “Rulers and elders of our people,
Are we being questioned today because we have done a good deed for a crippled man? Do you want to know how he was healed?

Let me clearly state to all of you and to all the people of Yashar'AL that he was healed by the powerful Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach the Nazarym, the man you impaled, whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised from the dead.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is the one referred to in the Scriptures, where it says, ‘The stone that you builders rejected has now become the chief cornerstone.’
There is no salvation in any other name! For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did not give any other name to save mankind under Shamaym.”

The members of the council were amazed when they saw the boldness of Kafa and Yahukanun, for they could see that they were ordinary men with no special training in the Scriptures. They also recognized them as men who had been with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
But since they could see the man who had been healed standing right there among them, there was nothing the council could say.
So they ordered Kafa and Yahukanun out of the council chamber and consult among themselves.
“What should we do with these men?” they asked each other. “We cannot deny that they have performed a miraculous sign, and everybody in Yahushalam knows about it.
But to keep the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from spreading further among the people, let us severely threaten them, that from now on they should no longer speak to anybody in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
So they called the Shaliachs (apostles) back in and commanded them never again to speak or teach in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
But Kafa and Yahukanun replied, “Do you think 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH wants us to obey you rather than HIM?
We cannot stop telling about everything we have seen and heard.”
The council then threatened them further, but they finally let them go because they did not know how to punish them without starting a riot. For everyone was giving Yadah to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH
For this miraculous sign, the healing of a man who had been lame for more than forty years.
As soon as they were freed, Kafa and Yahukanun returned to the other believers and told them what the leading Kuhanym and elders had said.

When they heard the report, all the believers lifted their voices together in prayer to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH: they prayed. “O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, Creator of Shamaym and Arath and the Yam (sea), and everything in them
YOU said long ago by the RUACH Ha'Qadash through our ancestor Daud, your servant, saying, ‘Why were the nations so angry? Why did they waste their time with futile plans?
The kings of the Arath prepared for battle; the rulers gathered together against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and against His Mashyach.’

“In fact, this has happened here in this very city! For Harud Antipas, Pontius Pilate the governor, the foreigner, and the people of Yashar'AL were all united against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, your Qadash Servant, whom you anointed.
But everything they did was determined beforehand according to your will.
And now, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, hear their threats, and give us, your servants, great boldness in preaching your Dabar.
Stretch out your hand with healing power; may miraculous signs and wonders be done through the Name of your Qadash Servant 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.”
After this prayer, the meeting place shook, and they were all filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash. Then they preached the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with boldness.
All the believers were united in heart and mind. And they felt that what they owned was not their own, so they shared everything they had.
The Shaliachs (apostles) testified powerfully to the resurrection of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach, and the great Barakah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was upon them all.
There were no needy people among them, because those who owned land or houses would sell them
And bring the money to the Shaliachs to give to those in need.
For instance, there was Ya'asaf, the one the Talmidym nicknamed Barnabas (which means “Son of Encouragement”). He was from the tribe of Lauy and came from the island of Cyprus.
He sold a field he owned and brought the money to the Shaliachs.
But there was a certain man named Ananias, who with his wife Sapphira, they sold some property.
He brought part of the money to the Shaliachs (apostles), claiming it was the full amount. With his wife’s consent, he kept the rest.
Then Kafa said, “Ananias, why have you let Satan fill your heart? You lied to the RUACH Ha'Qadash, and you kept some of the money for yourself.

The property was yours to sell or not sell, as you wished. And after selling it, the money was also yours to give away. How could you do a thing like this? You were not lying to us but to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
As soon as Ananias heard these words, he fell to the floor and died. Everyone who heard about it was terrified.
Then some young men got up, wrapped him in a sheet, and took him out and buried him.
About three hours later his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Kafa asked her, “Was this the price you and your husband received for your land?”

And Kafa said, “How could the two of you even think of conspiring to test the RUACH of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH like this? The young men who buried your husband are just outside the door, and they will carry you out, too.”
Instantly, she fell to the floor and died. When the young men came in and saw that she was dead, they carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear gripped the entire called out Assembly and everyone else who heard what had happened.
The Shaliachs were performing many miraculous signs and wonders among the people. And all the believers were meeting regularly at the Haykal (Temple) in the area known as Shalumah’s Colonnade.
But no one else dared to join them, even though all the people had high regard for them.
Yet more and more people believed and were brought to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s gathering of both men and women.
As a result of the Shaliachs work, sick people were brought out into the streets on beds and mats so that Kafa’s shadow might fall across some of them as Kafa went by.
Crowds came from the villages around Yahushalam, bringing their sick and those possessed by evil spirits, and they were all healed.
The high Kuhan and his officials, who were Sadducees, were filled with jealousy.
They arrested the Shaliachs and put them in the public jail.
But a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH came at night and opened the gates of the jail, and brought them out. Then the Malak told them,
“Go to the Temple and give the people this message of life!”

So at daybreak the Shaliachs entered the Temple, as they were told, and immediately began teaching. When the high Kuhan and his officials arrived, they convened the high council the full assembly of the elders of Yashar'AL. Then they sent for the Shaliachs to be brought from the jail for trial.
But when the Temple guards went to the jail, the men were gone. So they returned to the council and reported,
“The jail was securely locked, with the guards standing outside, but when we opened the gates, no one was there!”
When the captain of the Temple's guard and the leading Kuhanym heard this, they were perplexed, wondering where it would all end.
Then someone arrived with startling news: “The men you put in jail are standing in the Temple, teaching the people!”
The captain went with his Temple's guards and arrested the Shaliachs, but without violence, for they were afraid the people would stone them.
Then they brought the Shaliachs before the high council, where the high Kuhan confronted them.

“We gave you strict orders never again to teach in this Man’s Name!” the high Kuhan said. “Instead, you have filled all Yahushalam with your teaching about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and you want to make us responsible for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s death!”
But Kafa and the Shaliachs replied, “We must obey 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH rather than any man's authority.
The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of our ancestors raised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from the dead after you killed him by hanging Him on an execution stake.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has put 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in the place of honor at his right hand as Sar (Prince) and Savior. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did this so the people of Yashar'AL would repent of their sins and be forgiven.
We are witnesses of these things and so is the RUACH Ha'Qadash that was given by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to those who obey HIM.”
When they heard this, the high council was furious and decided to kill them.
But one member, a Pharisee named Gamalial, who was an expert in religious law and respected by all the people, stood up and ordered that the men be sent outside the council chamber for a while.
Then he said to his colleagues, “Men of Yashar'AL, take care what you are planning to do to these men!
For some time ago Thaudas rose up, claiming to be somebody. A number of men, about four hundred, joined him. He was slain, and all who obeyed him were scattered and came to nothing.
After him, at the time of the census, there was Yudas of Galily. He got people to follow him, but he was killed, too, and all his followers were scattered.
“So my advice is, leave these men alone. Let them go. If they are planning and doing these things merely on their own, it will soon be overthrown.
But if it is from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you will not be able to overthrow them. You may even find yourselves fighting against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”
The others accepted his advice. They called in the Shaliachs and had them flogged. Then they ordered them never again to speak in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and they let them go.
The Shaliachs left the high council rejoicing that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had counted them worthy to suffer dishonor for the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And every day, in the Temple and from house to house, they continued to teach and preach this message: “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is Ha'Mashyach.”

Now as the believers rapidly multiplied, there were rumblings of discontent. The Greek-speaking believers complained about the Hebrew-speaking believers, saying that their widows were being discriminated against in the daily distribution of food.
So the Twelve Shaliachs called a meeting of all the believers. They said, “We Shaliachs should spend our time teaching the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, not running a food program.
And so, brothers, select seven men who are well respected and are full of the RUACH and wisdom. We will give them this responsibility.
Then we Shaliachs can spend our time in prayer and teaching the Dabar.”

Everyone liked this idea, and they chose the following: Staphan (a man full of Amunah and the RUACH Ha'Qadash), Philip, Procorus, Nicanur, Timun, Parmanas, and Niculas of Antiuch (an earlier convert to the Yahudym faith).
These seven were presented to the Shaliachs, who prayed for them as they laid their hands on them.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s message continued to spread. The number of believers greatly increased in Yahushalam, and many of the Yahudym Kuhanym were converted, too.
Staphan, a man full of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Kabad and power, performed amazing miracles and signs among the people.
But one day some men from the congregation of Freed Slaves, as it was called, started to debate with him. They were Yahudym from Cyrana, Alexandria, Cilicia, and the province of Asia.
None of them could stand against the wisdom and the RUACH with which Staphan spoke.
So they persuaded some men to lie about Staphan, saying, “We heard him blaspheme Musha, and even 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
This roused the people, the elders, and the teachers of religious law. So they arrested Staphan and brought him before the high council.
The lying witnesses said, “This man is always speaking against the Qadash Temple and against the law of Musha.
We have heard him say that this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of Nazarym will destroy the Temple and change the customs Musha handed down to us.”
At this point everyone in the high council stared at Staphan, because his face became as bright as a Malak.
Then the high Kuhan asked Staphan, “Are these accusations true?”
This was Staphan’s reply: “Brothers and fathers, listen to me. Our marvelous 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH appeared to our ancestor Abraham in Masuputamia before he settled in Haran.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told Abraham, ‘Leave your native land and your relatives, and come into the land that I will show you.’
So Abraham left the land of the Chaldaans and lived in Haran until his father died. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH brought him here to the land where you now live.

“But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave Abraham no inheritance here, not even one square foot of land. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did promise, however, that eventually the whole land would belong to Abraham and his descendants, even though Abraham had no children yet.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH also told Abraham that his descendants would live in a foreign land, where they would be oppressed as slaves for four hundred years.
‘But I will punish the nation that enslaves them,’ then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said, ‘and in the end they will come out and worship ME here in this place.’

“And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH also gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision at that time. So when Abraham became the father of Yachaq, he circumcised him on the eighth day. And the practice was continued when Yachaq became the father of Ya'aqub, and when Ya'aqub became the father of the twelve patriarchs of the Yasharalym nation.
“These patriarchs were jealous of their brother Ya'asaf, and they sold him to be a slave in Mitzraym. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with Ya'asaf

And rescued Ya'asaf from all his troubles. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave Ya'asaf favor before Pharuh, king of Mitzraym. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH also gave Ya'asaf unusual wisdom, so that Pharuh appointed Ya'asaf governor over all of Mitzraym and put him in charge of the palace.
“But a famine came upon Mitzraym and Canaan. There was great misery, and our ancestors ran out of food.
Ya'aqub heard that there was still grain in Mitzraym, so he sent his sons, our ancestors to buy some.
The second time they went, Ya'asaf revealed his identity to his brothers, and they were introduced to Pharuh.
Then Ya'asaf sent for his father, Ya'aqub, and all his relatives to come to Mitzraym, seventy-five persons in all.
So Ya'aqub went to Mitzraym. He died there, as did our ancestors.
Their bodies were taken to Shacham and buried in the tomb Abraham had bought for a certain price from Hamur’s sons in Shacham.
“As the time drew near when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH would fulfill his promise to Abraham, the number of our people in Mitzraym greatly increased.
But then a new king came to the throne of Mitzraym who knew nothing about Ya'asaf.
This king exploited our people and oppressed them, forcing parents to abandon their newborn babies so they would die.
“At that time Musha was born, a beautiful child in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s eyes. His parents cared for him at home for three months.
Then they had to abandon him, Pharuh’s daughter adopted Musha and raised him as her own son.
Musha was taught all the wisdom of the Mitzraym, and Musha was powerful in both speech and action.
“One day when Musha was forty years old, he decided to visit his relatives, the people of Mitzraym.
He saw a Mitzraym mistreating a Yasharalym. So Musha came to the man’s defense and avenged him, killing the Mitzraym.
Musha assumed his fellow Yasharalym would realize that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had sent him to rescue them, but they did not.
“The next day Musha visited them again and saw two men of Yashar'AL fighting. Musha tried to bring Shalum to them. Musha said 'Men, ‘you are brothers. Why are you fighting each other?’
“But the man in the wrong pushed Musha aside. ‘Who made you a ruler and judge over us?’ he asked.
‘Are you going to kill me as you killed that Mitzraym yesterday?’
When Musha heard that, he fled the country and lived as a foreigner in the land of Midian. There his two sons were born.
“Forty years later, in the desert near Mount Sinai, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH appeared to Musha in the flame of a burning bush.
When Musha saw it, he was amazed at the sight. As he went to take a closer look, the Voice of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH called out to Musha,
‘I am the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of your fathers, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Abraham, Yachaq, and Ya'aqub.’ Musha shook with terror and did not dare to look.
“Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Dabar to Musha, ‘Take off your sandals, for you are standing on Qadash ground.
I have certainly seen the oppression of my people in Mitzraym. I have heard their groans and have come down to rescue them. Now go, for I am sending you back to Mitzraym.’

“So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent back the same Musha his people had previously rejected when they demanded, ‘Who made you a ruler and judge over us?’ Through the Malak who guided Musha to the burning bush, Where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH spoke to Musha, Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH sent Musha to be their ruler and savior.
And by means of many wonders and miraculous signs, Musha led them out of Mitzraym, through the Red Sea, and through the wilderness for forty years.
“Musha himself told the people of Yashar'AL, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will raise up for you a Nabym like me from among your own people.’
Musha was with our fathers, the Assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s people in the wilderness, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH spoke to Musha at Mount Sinai. And there Musha received life-giving Dabar to pass on to us.
“But our ancestors refused to listen to Musha. They rejected him and wanted to return to Mitzraym.
They told Aarun, ‘Make us an idol who can lead us, for we do not know what has become of this Musha, who brought us out of Mitzraym.’
So they made an idol shaped like a calf, and they sacrificed to it and celebrated over this thing they had made.

Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH turned away from them and abandoned them to serve the stars of Shamaym as their mighty ones! In the book of the Nabyms it is written, ‘Was it to me you were bringing sacrifices and offerings during those forty years in the wilderness, O Yashar'AL?
No, you carried your pagan idols, the shrine of Mulach, the star of your idol Raphan, and the images you made to worship them, so I will send you into exile as far away as Babylun.’
“Our ancestors carried the Tabernacle with them through the wilderness. It was constructed according to the plan 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had shown to Musha.

Years later, when Yahusha Ba'Nun led our fathers in battle against the nations that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH drove out of this land, the Tabernacle was taken with them into their new territory. And it stayed there until the time of King Daud.
“Daud found favor with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and asked for the privilege of building a permanent Temple for the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Ya'aqub.
But it was Shalumah who actually built the Temple.
However, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH does not live in a Temple made by man's hands. As the Nabyms said,
‘Shamaym is my throne, and the Arath is my footstool, Could you build me a Temple as good as that?’ asks 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. ‘Could you build me such a resting place?
Did my hands not make both Shamaym and the Arath?’
“You stubborn people! You are idol Worshipers at heart and deaf to the Truth. Must you forever resist the RUACH Ha'Qadash? That is what your fathers did, and so do you!
Name one Nabym your fathers did not persecute! They even killed the ones who predicted the coming of the Righteous One, Ha'Mashyach whom you betrayed and murdered.
You deliberately disobeyed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Turah, even though you received it from the hands of Musha and the guidance of the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH .”
The Yahudym leaders were infuriated by Staphan’s accusation, and they shook their fists at him in rage.
But Staphan, full of the RUACH Ha'Qadash, gazed steadily into Shamaym and saw the Kabad of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and he saw 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA standing in the place of honor at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s right hand.
And Staphan told them, “Look, I see the Shamaym opened and the Son of Adam standing in the place of honor at 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s right hand!”
Then they put their hands over their ears and began shouting. And they rushed at Staphan
And dragged Staphan out of the city and began to stone him, and his accusers took off their clothes and laid them at the feet of a young man named Shaul.
As they stoned Staphan, he prayed, my MASTER 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, receive my ruach.”
He fell to his knees, shouting, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, do not charge them with this sin!” And with that, Staphan died.
Shaul was one of the witnesses, and he agreed completely with the killing of Staphan.
(Some devout men came and buried Staphan with great mourning.)
But Shaul was going everywhere to destroy the Assemblies. Shaul went from house to house, dragging out both men and women to throw them into prison.
But the believers who were scattered preached the Basurah (Good News) about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA wherever they went.
Philip, for example, went to the city of Samaria and told the people there about Ha'Mashyach.
Crowds listened intently to Philip because they were eager to hear his message and see the miraculous signs he did.
Many evil spirits were cast out, screaming as they left their victims. And many who had been paralyzed or lame were healed.
So there was great joy in that city.
A man named Simun had been a sorcerer there for many years, amazing the people of Samaria and claiming to be someone great.
Everyone, from the least to the greatest, often spoke of him as “the Great one, the Power of the mighty one.”
They listened closely to him because for a long time he had astounded them with his magic.
But now the people believed Philip’s message of Good News concerning the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach. As a result, many men and women were baptized.
Then Simun himself believed and was baptized. He began following Philip wherever he went, and he was amazed by the signs and great miracles Philip performed.
When the Shaliachs in Yahushalam heard that the people of Samaria had accepted 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s message, they sent Kafa and Yahukanun there.
As soon as they arrived, they prayed for these new believers to receive the RUACH Ha'Qadash.
The RUACH Ha'Qadash had not yet come upon any of them, for they had only been baptized in the name of the 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach.
Then Kafa and Yahukanun laid their hands upon these believers, and they received the RUACH Ha'Qadash.
When Simun saw that the RUACH was given when the Shaliachs laid their hands on people, he offered them money to buy this power.
“Let me have this power, too,” he exclaimed, “so that when I lay my hands on people, they will receive the RUACH Ha'Qadash!”
But Kafa replied, “May your money perish with you, for thinking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s gift can be bought!
You cannot share with us in this work. Your heart is not right before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Change your heart! Turn away from these evil thoughts and pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Maybe He will forgive you.
I see that you are full of bitter jealousy and cannot stop yourself from doing wrong.”
“Pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for me,” Simun exclaimed, “that these terrible things you have said will not happen to me!”
After testifying and preaching the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Samaria, Kafa and Yahukanun returned to Yahushalam. And they stopped in many Samaritan villages along the way to preach the Good News.
As for Philip, a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said to him, “Go south down the desert road that runs from Yahushalam to Gaza.”
So he started out, and he met the treasurer of Athiupia, a eunuch of great authority under the Kandake, the queen of Athiupia. The eunuch had gone to Yahushalam to worship,
and he was now returning. Seated in his carriage, he was reading aloud from the book of the Nabym Yashayahu.
The RUACH Ha'Qadash said to Philip, “Go over and walk along beside the carriage.”
Philip ran over and heard the man reading from the Nabym Yashayahu. Philip asked, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
The man replied, “How can I, unless someone instructs me?” And he urged Philip to come up into the carriage and sit with him.
The passage of Scripture he had been reading was this: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter. And as a lamb is silent before the shearers, he did not open his mouth.
He was humiliated and received no justice. Who can speak of His descendants? For His life was taken from the Arath.”
The eunuch asked Philip, “Tell me, was the Nabym talking about himself or someone else?”
So beginning with this same Scripture, Philip told him the Good News about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
As they rode along, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, “Look! here is some water! What hinders me from being baptized?”
Then Philip said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may.” And he answered and said, “I believe that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach is the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.”
He ordered the carriage to stop, and they went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the RUACH of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH snatched Philip away. The eunuch never saw him again but went on his way rejoicing.
Meanwhile, Philip found himself farther north at the town of Azutus. He preached the Good News there and in every town along the way until he came to Caasaraa.
Meanwhile, Shaul was uttering threats with every breath and was eager to kill 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s followers. So Shaul went to the high Kuhan.

And Shaul requested letters addressed to the congregation in Damascus, asking for their cooperation in the arrest of any followers of Ha'Mashyach he found in Damascus. He wanted to bring them both men and women back to Yahushalam in chains.
As Shaul was approaching Damascus on this mission, a light from Shamaym suddenly shone down on him.
And Shaul fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, “Shaul! Shaul! Why are you persecuting Me?”
“Who are you?” Shaul asked.
Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”
The men with Shaul stood speechless, for they heard the sound of someone’s voice but saw no one!
Shaul picked himself up off the ground, but when he opened his eyes he was blind. So his companions led him by the hand to Damascus.
He remained there blind for three days and did not eat or drink.
Now there was a follower of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in Damascus named Ananyas. Who 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spoke to in a vision, calling, “Ananyas! “Yes, MASTER!” he replied.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to him, “Go over to the Street called Straight, to the house of a man named Yudas. When you get there, ask for a man from Tarsus named Shaul, he is praying to me right now.
I have shown him a vision of a man named Ananyas coming in and laying hands on him so he can see again.”
“But MASTER,” Ananyas exclaimed, “I have heard many people talk about the terrible things this man has done to the believers in Yahushalam!
And he is authorized by the leading Kuhanym to arrest everyone who calls upon your Name.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said, “Go, for Shaul is my chosen instrument to take my message to the other nations and to kings, as well as to the people of Yashar'AL.
And I will show Shaul how much he must suffer for my Name’s sake.”

So Ananyas went and found Shaul. And Ananyas laid his hands on Shaul and said, “brother Shaul, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, who appeared to you on the road, has sent me so that you might regain your sight and be filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash.”
Instantly something like scales fell from Shaul’s eyes, and he regained his sight. Then Shaul got up and was baptized.
So when Shaul had received food, he was strengthened. Then Shaul spent some days with Ananyas at Damascus.
And immediately Shaul began preaching about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in the congregation, saying, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is indeed the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH!”

All who heard him were amazed. “Is this not the same man who caused such devastation among 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s followers in Yahushalam?” they asked. “And did he not come here to arrest them and take them in chains to the leading Kuhanym?”
Shaul’s preaching became more and more powerful, and the Yahudym in Damascus could not refute his proofs that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was indeed Ha'Mashyach.
After a while some of the Yahudym plotted together to kill him.
They were watching for him day and night at the city gate so they could murder him, but Shaul was told about their plot.
So during the night, some of the other believers lowered Shaul in a large basket through an opening in the city wall.
When Shaul arrived in Yahushalam, he tried to meet with the believers, but they were all afraid of him. They did not believe he had truly become a believer!

Then Barnabas brought him to the Shaliachs and told them how Shaul had seen 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA on the way to Damascus and how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA had spoken to Shaul, Barnabas also told them that Shaul had preached boldly in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in Damascus.
So Shaul stayed with the Shaliachs and went all around Yahushalam with them, preaching boldly in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
Shaul debated with some Greek-speaking Yahudym, but they tried to murder him.
When the believers heard about this, they took him down to Caasaraa and sent him away to Tarsus, his hometown.

Then the Qadash ones had Shalum throughout Yahudah, Galily, and Samaria, and it became stronger as the believers lived in the fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And with the encouragement of the RUACH Ha'Qadash, they also grew in numbers.
Meanwhile, Kafa traveled from place to place, and he came down to visit the believers in the town of Lydda.
There Kafa met a man named Aanaas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
Kafa said to him, “Aanaas, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach heals you! Get up, and roll up your sleeping mat!” And Aanaas was healed instantly.
Then the whole population of Lydda and Sharun saw Aanaas walking around, and they turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
There was a believer in Yuppa named Tabitha (which in Greek is Durcas). She was always doing kind things for others and helping the poor.
About this time she became ill and died. Her body was washed for burial and laid in an upstairs room.
But the believers had heard that Kafa was nearby at Lydda, so they sent two men to beg Kafa, “Please come as soon as possible!”

So Kafa returned with them; and as soon as he arrived, they took him to the upstairs room. The room was filled with widows who were weeping and showing Kafa the coats and other clothes Dorcas had made for them.
But Kafa asked them all to leave the room; then he knelt and prayed. Turning to the body Kafa said, “Get up, Tabitha.” And she opened her eyes! When she saw Kafa, she sat up!
Kafa gave her his hand and helped her up. Then Kafa called in the widows and all the believers, and he presented her to them alive.
The news spread through the whole town, and many believed in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
And Kafa stayed a long time in Yuppa, living with Simun, a tanner of hides.
In Caasaraa there lived a Roman army officer named Curnalius, who was a captain of the Italian Regiment.
He was a devout man, one who fears 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, as was everyone in his household. He gave generously to the poor and prayed regularly to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
About the ninth hour of the day he saw clearly in a vision a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH coming in and saying to him, “Curnalius!”
Curnalius stared at him in terror. “What is it, sir?” he asked the Malak. And the Malak replied, “Your prayers and gifts to the poor have been received by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as an offering!
Now send some men to Yuppa, and summon a man named Simun Kafa.
He is staying with Simun, a tannar who lives near the seashore.”
As soon as the Malak was gone, Curnalius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier, one of his personal attendants.
He told them what had happened and sent them off to Yuppa.
The next day as Curnalius’s messengers were nearing the town, Kafa went up on the flat roof to pray. It was the sixth hour of the day,
And he was hungry. But while a meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
He saw the sky open, and something like a large sheet was let down by its four corners.
In the sheet were all sorts of animals, reptiles, and birds.
And a voice came to Kafa, “Rise, Kafa; kill and eat.”
“But Kafa said, “Not so, MASTER! For I have never eaten anything common or unclean.”
And a voice spoke to Kafa again the second time, “What 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has cleansed you must not call common.”
This was done three times. And the object was taken up into Shamaym again.
Kafa was very perplexed. What could the vision mean? Just then the men sent by Curnalius found Simun’s house. Standing outside the gate,
They asked if a man named Kafa was staying there.
Meanwhile, as Kafa was puzzling over the vision, the RUACH Ha'Qadash said to him, “Three men have come looking for you.
Get up, go downstairs, and go with them without hesitation. Do not worry, for I have sent them.”
So Kafa went down and said, “I am the man you are looking for. Why have you come?”

They said, “We were sent by Curnalius, a Roman officer. He is a devout man that fears 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, well respected by all the Yahudym. A Qadash Malak instructed him to summon you to his house so that he can hear your message.”
So Kafa invited the men to stay for the night. The next day he went with them, accompanied by some of the qadash ones from Yuppa.
They arrived in Caasaraa the following day. Curnalius was waiting for them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
Immediately Kafa entered his home, Curnalius fell at his feet and worshiped him.
But Kafa pulled him up and said, “Stand up! I am a man just like you!”
So they talked together and went inside, where many others were assembled.

Kafa told them, “You know it is against our laws for a Yahudym man to enter the home of a foreigner, or to associate with you. But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has shown me that I should no longer think of anyone as impure or unclean.
So I came without objection as soon as I was sent for. Now tell me why you sent for me.”
So Curnalius said, “Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
And said, ‘Curnalius, your prayer has been heard, and your giving of alms are remembered in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Send therefore to Yuppa and call Simun here, whose surname is Kafa. He is lodging in the house of Simun, a tanner, by the sea. When he comes, he will speak to you.’
So I sent to you immediately, and you have done well to come. Now therefore, we are all present before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to hear all the things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commanded you for us.”
Then Kafa replied, “I see very clearly that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH shows no favoritism.
In every nation 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH accepts those who fear HIM and does what is right.
This is the message of Good News for the people of Yashar'AL, that there is Shalum with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA who is Ha'Mashyach of all.
You know what happened throughout Yahudah, beginning in Galily, after Yahukanun began preaching his message of baptism.

And you know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH anointed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA of Nazarym with the RUACH Ha'Qadash and with power. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by ha'shatan, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
“And we Shaliachs are witnesses of all 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA did throughout Yahudah and in Yahushalam. They put 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to death by hanging Him on an execution stake,
but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to life on the third day. Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH allowed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to appear,
Not to the general public, but to us whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had chosen in advance to be his witnesses. We were those who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA ordered us to preach everywhere and to testify that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is the one appointed by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to be the judge of all the living and the dead.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is the one all the Nabyms testified about, saying that everyone who believes in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA will have their sins forgiven through His Name.”
Even as Kafa was saying these things, the RUACH Ha'Qadash fell upon all who were listening to the message.
The Yahudym believers who came with Kafa were amazed that the gift of the RUACH Ha'Qadash had been poured out on the other nations too.
For they heard them speaking in other tongues and they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then Kafa asked,
“Can anyone object to them being baptized, now that they have received the RUACH Ha'Qadash just as we did?”
So Kafa gave orders for them to be baptized in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach. Afterward Curnalius asked Kafa to stay with them for several days.
Soon the news reached the Shaliachs and other believers in Yahudah that the people of other nations (not Yahudym) had received the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
But when Kafa arrived back in Yahushalam, the Yahudym believers criticized him.
“You entered the home of someone that is not a Yahudym and even ate with them!” they said.
Then Kafa told them exactly what had happened.

“I was in the town of Yuppa,” he said, “and while I was praying, I went into a trance and saw a vision. Something like a large sheet was let down by its four corners from the sky. And it came right down to me.
When I looked inside the sheet, I saw all sorts of tame and wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
And I heard a voice say, ‘Get up, Kafa; kill and eat them.’
“‘No, MASTER,’ I replied. ‘I have never eaten anything that our Yahudym laws have declared impure or unclean.’
“But the voice from Shamaym spoke again: ‘Do not call something unclean if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has made it clean.’
This happened three times before the sheet and all it contained was pulled back up to Shamaym.
“Just then three men who had been sent from Caasaraa arrived at the house we were staying.

The RUACH Ha'Qadash told me to go with them and not to worry that they were from other nations (not Yahudym). These six brothers here accompanied me, and we soon entered the home of the man who had sent for us.
He told us how a Malak had appeared to him in his home and had told him, ‘Send messengers to Yuppa, and summon a man named Kafa.
He will tell you how you and everyone in your household can be saved!’
“As I began to speak,” Kafa continued, “the RUACH Ha'Qadash fell on them, just as He fell on us at the beginning.
Then I thought of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA’s words when He said, ‘Yahukanun baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the RUACH Ha'Qadash.’
And since 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave these other nations the same gift He gave us when we believed in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach, who was I to stand in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s way?”

When the others heard this, they stopped objecting and they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. They said, “We can see that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has also given the other nations the privilege of repenting of their sins and receiving eternal life.”

Meanwhile, the believers who had been scattered during the persecution after Staphan’s death traveled as far as Phuanicia, Cyprus, and Antiuch of Syria. They preached the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but only to Yahudym.
However, some of the believers who went to Antiuch from Cyprus and Cyrana began preaching to the other nations about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach.
The power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was with them, and a large number of these other nations believed and turned to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
When the Qadash ones at Yahushalam heard what had happened, they sent Barnabas to Antiuch.
When he arrived and saw this evidence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Barakah, he was filled with joy, and he encouraged the believers to stay true to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the RUACH Ha'Qadash and strong in Amunah. And many people were brought to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Then Barnabas went on to Tarsus to look for Shaul.

When he found Shaul, he brought him back to Antiuch. Both of them stayed there with the Qadash ones for a full year, teaching large crowds of people. (It was at Antiuch that the believers were first called followers of Ha'Mashyach.)
During this time some Nabym traveled from Yahushalam to Antiuch.
One of them named Agabus stood up in one of the meetings and predicted by the RUACH that a great famine was coming upon the entire Roman world. (This was fulfilled during the reign of Claudius.)
So the believers in Antiuch decided to send relief to the brothers and sisters in Yahudym, everyone giving as much as they could.
This they did, entrusting their gifts to Barnabas and Shaul to take to the elders of the followers of Ha'Mashyach (qadash ones) in Yahushalam.
After some time King Harud Agrippa began to persecute some believers in their congregation.
He killed Ya'aqub the brother of Yahukanun with a sword.
When Harud saw how much this pleased the Yahudym people, he also arrested Kafa. (This took place during the Passakh celebration.)
Then Harud imprisoned Kafa, placing him under the guard of four squads of four soldiers each. Harud intended to bring Kafa out for public trial after the Passakh.
But while Kafa was in prison, the Qadash ones prayed very earnestly for Kafa.
The night before Kafa was to be placed on trial, Kafa was asleep, fastened with two chains between two soldiers. Others stood guard at the prison gate.

Suddenly, there was a bright light in the cell, and the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH stood before Kafa. The Malak struck Kafa on the side to awaken him and said, “Quick! Get up!” And the chains fell off his wrists.
Then the Malak told Kafa, “Get dressed and put on your sandals.” And he did. “Now put on your coat and follow me,”
So Kafa left the cell, following the Malak. But all the time Kafa thought it was a vision. Kafa did not realize it was actually happening.

They passed the first and second guard posts and came to the iron gate leading to the city, and this opened for them all by itself. So they passed through and started walking down the street, and then the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH suddenly left Kafa.
When Kafa finally came to his senses. “It is really true!” Kafa said. “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has sent His Malak and saved me from Harud and from what the Yahudym leaders had planned to do to me!”
When he realized this, he went to the home of Maryam, the mother of Yunah Mark, where many Qadash ones were gathered for prayer.
And Kafa knocked at the door in the gate, and a servant girl named Rhuda came to open it.
When she recognized Kafa’s voice, she was so overjoyed that, instead of opening the door, she ran back inside and told everyone, “Kafa is standing at the door!”
“You are out of your mind!” they said. When she insisted, they decided, “It must be his Malak.”
Meanwhile, Kafa continued knocking. When they finally opened the door and saw Kafa, they were amazed.
Kafa motioned for them to quiet down and told them how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had led him out of prison. “Tell Ya'aqub and the other brothers what happened,” he said. And then he went to another place.
At dawn there was a great commotion among the soldiers about what had happened to Kafa.
Harud Agrippa ordered a thorough search for Kafa. When he could not be found, Harud interrogated the guards and sentenced them to death. Afterward Harud left Yahudah to stay in Caasaraa for a while.

Now Harud was very angry with the people of Tyra and Sidun. So they sent a delegation to make Shalum with him because their cities were dependent upon Harud’s country for food. The delegates won the support of Blastus, Harud’s personal assistant,
and an appointment with Harud was granted. When the day arrived, Harud put on his royal robes, sat on his throne, and made a speech to them.
The people gave him a great ovation, shouting, “It is the voice of a deity, not of a man!”
Instantly, the Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH struck Harud with a sickness, because he accepted the people’s worship instead of giving the Kabad to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. So he was consumed with worms and died.
Meanwhile, the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH continued to spread, and there were many new believers.
When Barnabas and Shaul had finished their mission to Yahushalam, they returned, taking Yunah Mark with them.

Among the Nabyms and teachers of the Qadash ones at Antiuch of Syria were Barnabas, Simaun (also called “the black man”), Lucius (from Cyrana), Manaan (the childhood companion of King Harud Antipas), and Shaul.
One day as these men were worshiping 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and fasting, the RUACH Ha'Qadash said, “Dedicate Barnabas and Shaul for the special work to which I have called them.”
So after more fasting and prayer, the men laid their hands on them and sent them on their way.
So Barnabas and Shaul were sent out by the RUACH Ha'Qadash. They went down to the seaport of Salaucia and then sailed for the island of Cyprus.
There, in the town of Salamis, they went to the Yahudym congregation and preached the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Yunah Mark went with them as their assistant.
Afterward they traveled from town to town across the entire island until finally they reached Paphus, where they met a Yahudym sorcerer, a false Nabym named Bar-Yasu.
He had attached himself to the governor, Sergius Palus, who was an intelligent man. The governor invited Barnabas and Shaul to visit him, for he wanted to hear the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
But Alymas, the sorcerer (as his name means in Greek), interfered and urged the governor to pay no attention to what Barnabas and Shaul said, he was trying to keep the governor from believing.
Shaul was filled with the RUACH Ha'Qadash, and Shaul looked the sorcerer in the eye.
Then Shaul said, “You son of ha'shatan, full of every sort of deceit and fraud, and enemy of all that is good! Will you never stop perverting the true ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?

Watch now, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has laid his hand of punishment upon you, and you will be struck blind. You will not see the sunlight for some time.” Instantly mist and darkness came over the evil man’s eyes, and he began groping around begging for someone to take his hand and lead him.
When the governor saw what had happened, he became a believer, for he was astonished at the teaching about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Shaul and his companions then left Paphus by ship for Pamphylia, landing at the port town of Perga. There Yunah Mark left them and returned to Yahushalam.
But Shaul and Barnabas traveled inland to Antiuch of Pisidia. On the Shabbat they went to the congregation for the services.

After the usual readings from the books of Musha and the Nabyms, those in charge of the service sent them this message: “ Achk (Brothers), if you have any word of encouragement for the people, come and give it.”
So Shaul stood, lifted his hand to quiet them, and started speaking. “Men of Yashar'AL,” he said, “and you who fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH from other nations, listen to me.
“The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the nation of Yashar'AL chose our fathers and made them multiply and grow strong during their stay in Mitzraym. Then with a powerful arm 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH led them out of their slavery.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH put up with them through forty years of wandering in the wilderness.
Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH destroyed seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to Yashar'AL as an inheritance.
“After that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them judges for about four hundred and fifty years, until Shamual the Nabym.
And afterward they asked for a king; so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them Shaul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Banyamin, for forty years.

But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH removed Shaul from being king and replaced him with Daud, a man about whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said, ‘I have found Daud son of Yassa, a man after my own heart. Daud will do everything I want him to do.’
“And it is one of King Daud’s descendants, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA who is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s promised Savior for Yashar'AL!
Before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came, Yahukanun the Baptist preached that all the people of Yashar'AL needed to repent of their sins and turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and be baptized.
As Yahukanun was finishing his ministry he asked, ‘Do you think I am Ha'Mashyach? No, I am not! But He is coming soon and I am not even worthy to be His slave and untie the sandals on his feet.’
“Achks (Brothers) you sons of Abraham, and also you who fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH from other nations, this message of salvation has been sent to us!

The people in Yahushalam and their leaders did not recognize 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA as the one the Nabyms had spoken about. Instead, they condemned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and in doing this they fulfilled the Nabyms’ words that are read every Shabbat.
They found no legal reason to execute 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, but they asked Pilate to have him killed anyway.
“When they had done all that the prophecies said about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, they took Him down from the execution stake and placed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in a tomb.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from the dead!
And over a period of many days 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA appeared to those who had gone with Him from Galily to Yahushalam. They are now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s witnesses to the people of Yashar'AL.
“And now we are here to bring you this Good News. The promise was made to our fathers,

And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has now fulfilled it for us, their descendants, by raising 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. This is what the second tahalym (psalm) says about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA: ‘You are my Son. Today I have become your ABBA.’
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had promised to raise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from the dead, not leaving 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA to rot in the grave. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH said, ‘I will give you the Qadash Barakah I promised to Daud.’
Another tahalym (psalm) explains it more fully: ‘You will not allow your Qadash One to rot in the grave.’
This is not a reference to Daud, for after Daud had done the will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in his own generation, he died and was buried with his ancestors, and his body decayed.
No, it was a reference to someone else, someone whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH raised and whose body did not decay.
“Brothers, listen! We are here to proclaim that through this man 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA there is forgiveness for your sins.
Everyone who believes in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is declared right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, something the law of Musha could never do.
Be careful! Do not let the Nabyms’ words apply to you. For they said,
‘Look, you mockers, be amazed and die! For I am doing something in your own day, something you would not believe even if someone told you about it.’”
As Shaul and Barnabas left the congregation that Shabbat day, the people begged them to speak about these things again the next week Shabbat.
Many devoted Yahudym followed Shaul and Barnabas, and they urged the new believers to continue to rely on the favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The following week Shabbat almost the entire city turned out to hear them preach the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
But when some of the Yahudym saw the crowds, they were jealous; so they slandered Shaul and argued against whatever he said.

Then Shaul and Barnabas spoke out boldly and declared, “It was necessary that we first preach the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to you Yahudym. But since you have rejected it and judged yourselves unworthy of eternal life, we will offer it to the other nations.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave us this command when he said, ‘I have made you a light to the other nations, to bring salvation to the farthest corners of the Arath.’”
When the other nations heard this, they were very glad and gave Tudah to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for His message; and all who were chosen for eternal life became believers.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s message spread throughout that region.
Then the Yahudym stirred up the influential religious women and the leaders of the city, and they incited a mob against Shaul and Barnabas and expelled them out of the region.
So they shook the dust from their feet as a sign of rejection and went to the town of Icunium.
And the believers were filled with joy and with the RUACH Ha'Qadash.
The same thing happened in Icunium. Shaul and Barnabas went to the congregation and preached with such power that a great number of both Yahudym and Greeks became believers.
Some of the Yahudym, however, dispute 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s message and poisoned the minds of the nations against Shaul and Barnabas.
But the Shaliachs stayed there a long time, preaching boldly about the favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH proved their message was true by giving them power to do miraculous signs and wonders.
But the people of the town were divided in their opinion about them. Some sided with the Yahudym, and some with the Shaliachs.
Then a mob from the people of the other nations and Yahudym, along with their leaders, decided to attack and stone the Shaliachs.
When the Shaliachs learned of it, they fled to the region of Lycaunia, to the towns of Lystra and Darba and the surrounding area.
And there they preached the Good News.
While they were at Lystra, Shaul and Barnabas came upon a man with crippled feet, he had been that way from birth, so he had never walked, the crippled man was sitting
And listening as Shaul preached. Looking straight at him, Shaul realized he had Amunah to be healed.
So Shaul called to him in a loud voice, “Stand up!” And the man jumped to his feet and started walking.
When the crowd saw what Shaul had done, they shouted in their local dialect, “These men are mighty ones in man's form!”
They decided that Barnabas was the Greek diety Zeus and that Shaul was Hermes, since he was the chief speaker.

Now the temple of Zeus was located just outside the town. So the priest of the temple and the crowd brought bulls and wreaths of flowers to the town gates, and they prepared to offer sacrifices to the Shaliachs.
But when the Shaliachs Barnabas and Shaul heard what was happening, they tore their clothing in dismay and ran out among the people, shouting,

“Friends, why are you doing this? We are merely men just like you! We have come to bring you the Good News that you should turn from these worthless things and turn to the living 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, who made Shamaym and Arath, the Yam (sea), and everything in them.
In the past 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH permitted all the nations to go their own ways,
but 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH never left them without evidence of Himself and His goodness. For instance, he sends you rain and good crops and gives you food and joyful hearts.”
But even with these words, Shaul and Barnabas could scarcely restrain the people from sacrificing to them.
Then some Yahudym arrived from Antiuch and Icunium, they won the crowds to their side, and they stoned Shaul and dragged him out of the town, thinking he was dead.
But as the believers gathered around him, he got up and went back into the town. The next day he left with Barnabas for Dayba.
After preaching the Good News in Dayba and making many Talmidym, Shaul and Barnabas returned to Lystra, Icunium, and Antiuch of Pisidia,
Where they strengthened the believers. They encouraged them to continue in the Amunah, reminding them that we must suffer many hardships to enter the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Shaul and Barnabas also appointed elders in every Qadash Assemblies. With prayer and fasting, they turned the elders over to the care of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, in whom they had put their trust.
Then they traveled back through Pisidia to Pamphylia.
They preached the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Perga, then went down to Attalia.
Finally, they returned by ship to Antiuch of Syria, where their journey had begun. The believers there had entrusted them to the divine favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to do the work they had now completed.

Upon arriving in Antiuch, they called the Qadash assembly together and reported everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done through them and how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had opened the door of Amunah to the other nations too.
And they stayed there with the believers for a long time.
While Shaul and Barnabas were at Antiuch of Syria, some men from Yahudah arrived and began to teach the believers: “Unless you are circumcised as required by the law of Musha, you cannot be saved.”

Shaul and Barnabas disagreed with them, arguing vehemently. Finally, the Qadash assembly decided to send Shaul and Barnabas to Yahushalam, accompanied by some local believers, to talk to the Shaliachs and elders about this question.
So being sent on their way by the Qadash assembly, they passed through Phuanicia and Samaria, describing the conversion of the other nations; and they caused great joy to all the Qadash ones.
And when they had come to Yahushalam, they were received by the Qadash assembly and the Shaliachs and the elders; and they reported all things that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done with them.
But some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed rose up, saying, “It is necessary to circumcise them, and to command them to keep the law of Musha.”
So the Shaliachs and elders met together to resolve this issue.

At the meeting, after a long discussion, Kafa stood and addressed them as follows: “Brothers, you all know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH chose me from among you some time ago to preach to the other nations so that they could hear the Good News and believe.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH knows the hearts, of everyone man and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH confirmed that He accepts the other nations by giving them the RUACH Ha'Qadash, just as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave to us.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made no distinction between us and them, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH cleansed their hearts through Amunah.
So why are you now challenging 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by burdening the other nations believers with a yoke that neither we nor our ancestors were able to bear?
We believe that we are all saved the same way, by the undeserved favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach.”
Everyone listened quietly as Barnabas and Shaul told them about the miraculous signs and wonders 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had done through them among the other nations (Non Yahudym).
When they had finished, Ya'aqub stood and said, “Brothers, listen to me.
Kafa has told you about the time 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH first visited the other nations to take from them a people for himself.
And this conversion of other nations is exactly what the Nabyms predicted. As it is written:
‘Afterward I will return and restore the fallen house of Daud, I will rebuild its ruins and restore it,
So that the rest of mankind might seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, including the other nations, all those I have called to be mine, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has spoken
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who made these things known so long ago.’
“And so my judgment is that we should not make it difficult for the other nations who are turning to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from eating food offered to idols, from sexual immorality, from eating the meat of strangled animals, and from consuming blood.
For these laws of Musha have been preached in Yahudym congregation in every city on every Shabbat for many generations.”

Then the Shaliachs and elders together with the whole Qadash assembly in Yahushalam chose delegates, and they sent them to Antiuch of Syria with Shaul and Barnabas to report on this decision. The men chosen were two of the Qadash assembly leaders, Yudas (also called Barsabas) and Silas.

This is the letter they took with them: “This letter is from the Shaliachs and elders, your brothers in Yahushalam. It is written to the other nations believers in Antiuch, Syria, and Cilicia. Greetings!
“We understand that some men from here have troubled you and upset you with their teaching, but we did not send them!
So we decided, having come to complete agreement, to send you official representatives, along with our beloved Barnabas and Shaul,
Who have risked their lives for the Name of our Master 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
We are sending Yudas and Silas to confirm what we have decided concerning your question.
“For it seemed good to the Ruach Ha'Qadash and to us to lay no greater burden on you than these few requirements:
You must abstain from eating food offered to idols, from consuming blood or the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. If you do this, you will do well. Farewell.”
The messengers went at once to Antiuch, where they called a general meeting of the believers and delivered the letter.
And there was great joy throughout the Qadash assembly that day as they read this encouraging message.
Then Yudas and Silas, both being Nabyms, spoke at length to the believers, encouraging and strengthening their Amunah.
They stayed for a while, and then the believers sent them back to the Qadash assembly in Yahushalam with a Barakah of Shalum.
