However, it seemed good to Silas to remain there.
Shaul and Barnabas stayed in Antiuch. They and many others taught and preached the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH there.
After some time Shaul said to Barnabas, “Let’s go back and visit each city where we previously preached the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, to see how the new believers are doing.”
Barnabas agreed and wanted to take along Yunah Mark.
But Shaul disagreed strongly, since Yunah Mark had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not continued with them in their work.
Their disagreement was so sharp that they separated. Barnabas took Yunah Mark with him and sailed for Cyprus.
Shaul chose Silas, and as he left, the believers entrusted him to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s delightful care.
Then Shaul traveled throughout Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the Qadash assembly there.
Shaul went first to Darba and then to Lystra, where there was a young follower named Timothy. His mother was a Yahudym believer, but his father was a Greek.
Timothy was well thought of by the believers in Lystra and Icunium,

Shaul wanted him to join them on their journey. Shaul arranged for Timothy to be circumcised before they left, because of the Yahudym who were in that region for everyone knew that his father was a Greek.
Then they went from town to town, instructing the believers to follow the decisions made by the Shaliachs and elders in Yahushalam.
So the Qadash assembly were strengthened in their Amunah and grew larger every day.
Next Shaul and Silas traveled through the area of Phrygia and Galatia, because the RUACH Ha'Qadash had prevented them from preaching the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the province of Asia at that time.
Then coming to the borders of Mysia, they headed north for the province of Bithynia, but again the RUACH did not allow them to go there.
So instead, they went on through Mysia to the seaport of Troas.
That night Shaul had a vision: A man from Macedonia in northern Greece was standing there, pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
So we decided to leave for Macedonia at once, having concluded that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was calling us to preach the Good News there.
We boarded a boat at Troas and sailed straight course to the island of Samothrace, and the next day we landed at Neapolis.
From there we reached Philippi, a major city of that district of Macedonia and a Roman colony. And we stayed there several days.
On the Shabbat we went a little way outside the city to a riverbank, where we thought people would be meeting for prayer, and we sat down to speak with some women who had gathered there.
One of them was Lydia from Thyatira, a merchant of expensive purple cloth, who worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. As she listened to us, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH opened her heart, and she accepted what Shaul was saying.

She and her household were baptized, and she asked us to be her guests. “If you agree that I am a true believer in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH,” she said, “come and stay at my home.” And she urged us until we agreed.
One day as we were going down to the place of prayer, we met a slave girl who had a spirit that enabled her to tell the future. She earned a lot of money for her masters by telling fortunes.
She followed Shaul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Tsaba'ut, and they have come to tell you how to be saved.”

This went on day after day until Shaul got greatly annoyed that he turned and said to the demon within her, “I command you in the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach to come out of her.” And instantly the evil spirit left her.
Her masters’ hopes of wealth were now shattered, so they grabbed Shaul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities at the marketplace.
“The whole city is in an uproar because of these Yahudym!” they shouted to the city officials.
“They are teaching customs that are illegal for us Romans to practice.”
A mob quickly formed against Shaul and Silas, and the city officials ordered them stripped and beaten with wooden rods.
They were severely beaten, and then they were thrown into prison. The jailer was ordered to make sure they did not escape.
So the jailer put them into the inner dungeon and clamped their feet in the stocks.
Around midnight Shaul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and the other prisoners were listening.
Suddenly, there was a massive earthquake, and the prison was shaken to its foundations. All the doors immediately flew open, and the chains of every prisoner fell off!
The jailer woke up to see the prison doors wide open, he assumed the prisoners had escaped, so he drew his sword and wanted to kill himself.
But Shaul shouted to him, “Stop! Do not kill yourself! We are all here!”
The jailer called for lights and ran to the dungeon and fell down trembling before Shaul and Silas.
Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
They replied, “Believe in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach and you will be saved, you and everyone in your household.”
And they shared the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with him and with all who lived in his household.
Even at that hour of the night, the jailer cared for them and washed their wounds. Then he and everyone in his household were immediately baptized.
He brought them into his house and set a meal before them, and he and his entire household rejoiced because they all believed in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
The next morning the city officials sent the officers to tell the jailer, “Let those men go!”
So the jailer told Shaul, “The city officials have said you and Silas are free to leave. Go in Shalum.”

But Shaul replied, “They have publicly beaten us without a trial and put us in prison and we are Roman citizens. So now they want us to leave secretly? Certainly not! Let them come themselves to release us!”
When the officers reported this, the city officials were alarmed to learn that Shaul and Silas were Roman citizens.
So they came to the jail and apologized to them. Then they brought them out and begged them to leave the city.
When Shaul and Silas left the prison, they returned to the home of Lydia. There they met with the believers and encouraged them once more. Then they left town.
Shaul and Silas then traveled through the towns of Amphipolis and Apollonia and came to Thessalonica, where there was a Yahudym congregation.
And according to Shaul's custom on the Shabbat Yum (day), Shaul went in among the Yahudym congregation, and on three sabbaths reasoned with them from the scriptures,
Shaul explained the scriptures and proved that Ha'Mashyach must suffer and rise from the dead. He said, “This 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA I am telling you about is Ha'Mashyach.”
Some of the Yahudym who listened were persuaded and joined Shaul and Silas, along with many Greek men and quite a few prominent women who fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

But some of the Yahudym were jealous, so they gathered some troublemakers from the marketplace to form a mob and start a riot. They attacked the home of Yason, searching for Shaul and Silas so they could drag them out to the crowd.

Not finding them there, they dragged out Yason and some of the other believers instead and took them before the city council. “Shaul and Silas has caused trouble all over the world,” they shouted, “and now they are here disturbing our city, too.
And Yason has welcomed them into his home. They are all guilty of treason against Caesar, for they profess allegiance to another king, named 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.”
The people of the city, as well as the city council, were thrown into turmoil by these reports.
So the officials forced Yason and the other believers to post bond, and then they released them.
That very night the believers of Truth sent Shaul and Silas to Baraa. When they arrived there, they went to the congregation.

And the people of Baraa were more open minded than those in Thessalonica, and they listened eagerly to Shaul’s message. They searched the Scriptures day after day to see if Shaul and Silas were teaching the Truth.
As a result, many Yahudym believed the Truth, and the prominent Greek women and men believed also.
But when some Yahudym in Thessalonica learned that Shaul was preaching the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in Baraa, they went there and stirred up trouble.
The believers of Truth acted at once, sending Shaul on to the coast, while Silas and Timothy remained behind.
Those escorting Shaul went with him all the way to Athens; then they returned to Baraa with instructions for Silas and Timothy to hurry and join him.
While Shaul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply troubled by all the idols he saw everywhere in the city.
Shaul went to the congregation to reason with the Yahudym and the people who fear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in the other nations and Shaul spoke daily in the public square to all who happened to be there.

Shaul also had a debate with some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers. When he told them about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA and his resurrection, they said, “What’s this babbler trying to say with these strange ideas he is picked up?” Others said, “He seems to be preaching about some foreign deity.”
Then they took him to the high council of the city. “Come and tell us about this new teaching,” they said.
“You are saying some rather strange things, and we want to know what it is all about.”
(It should be explained that all the Athenians as well as the foreigners in Athens seemed to spend all their time discussing the latest ideas.)
So Shaul, standing before the council, addressed them as follows: “Men of Athens, I notice that you are very religious in every way,

for as I was walking along I saw your many shrines. And one of your altars had this inscription on it: ‘To an Unknown 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH (AL'Mighty One).’ This 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, whom you worship without knowing, is the one I am telling you about.
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who made the world and everything in it. Since 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of Shamaym and Arath, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH does not live in man made temples,
and man's hands cannot serve the need of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has no needs. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH Himself gives life and breath to everything, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH satisfies every need.
From one man 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH created all the nations throughout the whole Arath. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH decided beforehand when they should rise and fall, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH determined their boundaries.
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s purpose was for the nations to seek after HIM as their 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH and perhaps feel their way toward Him and find Him, though 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is not far from any one of us.
For in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH we live and move and exist. As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are his offspring.’
And since this is true, we should not think of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH as an idol designed by craftsmen from gold or silver or stone.
“For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH overlooked the ignorance of men about these things in earlier times, but now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH commands everyone everywhere to repent of their sins and turn to HIM.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has set a day for judging the world with justice by the man He has appointed, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH proved to everyone who this man is by raising Him from the dead.”
When they heard Shaul speak about the resurrection of the dead, some laughed in contempt, but others said, “We want to hear more about this later.”
That ended Shaul’s discussion with them,
But some joined Shaul and became believers of the Truth. Among them were Dionysius, a member of the council, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
Then Shaul left Athens and went to Corinth.

There he became acquainted with a Yahudym named Aquila, born in Pontus, who had recently arrived from Italy with his wife, Priscilla. They had left Italy when Claudius Caesar deported all Yahudym from Rome.
Shaul lived and worked with them, for they were tentmakers just as he was.
And every Shabbat Shaul was found at the Yahudym congregation, trying to convince the Yahudym and Greeks alike.
And after Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Shaul spent all his time preaching the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. He testified to the Yahudym that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is Ha'Mashyach.
But when they opposed and insulted him, Shaul shook the dust from his clothes and said, “Your blood is upon your own heads, I am innocent. From now on I will go preach to the other nations.”
Then Shaul left and went to the home of Titius Justus, a non Yahudym who worshiped 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and lived next door to the Yahudym congregation.
Crispus, the leader of the Yahudym congregation, and everyone in his household believed in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Many others in Corinth also heard Shaul, became believers, and were baptized.
One night 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spoke to Shaul in a vision and told him, “Do not be afraid! Speak out! Do not be silent!
For I am with you, and no one will attack and harm you, for many people in this city belong to me.”
So Shaul stayed there for the next year and a half, teaching the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
But when Gallio became governor of Achaia, some Yahudym rose up together against Shaul and brought him before the governor for judgment.
They accused Shaul of “persuading people to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in ways that are contrary to their law.”

But just as Shaul started to make his defense, Gallio turned to Shaul’s accusers and said, “Listen, you Yahudym, if this were a case involving some wrongdoing or a serious crime, I would have a reason to accept your case.
But since it is merely a question of words and names and your Yahudym law, take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
And he threw them out of the courtroom.
The crowd then grabbed Sosthenes, the leader of the Yahudym congregation, and beat Shaul right there in the courtroom. But Gallio paid no attention.

Shaul stayed in Corinth for some time after that, then said goodbye to the Achk (brothers) and Achuty (sisters) and went to nearby Cenchrea. There he shaved his head according to Yahudym custom, marking the end of a vow. Then he set sail for Syria, taking Priscilla and Aquila with him.
They stopped first at the port of Ephesus, where Shaul left the others behind. While he was there, Shaul went to the Yahudym congregation to reason with the Yahudym.
They asked him to stay longer, but he declined.
As Shaul left, however, he said, “I will come back later, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH willing.” Then he set sail from Ephesus.
The next stop was at the port of Caesarea. From there he went up and visited the Qadash assembly at Yahushalam and then went back to Antiuch.
After spending some time in Antiuch, Shaul went back through Galatia and Phrygia, visiting and strengthening all the believers of Truth.
Meanwhile, a Yahudym named Apollos, an eloquent speaker who knew the Scriptures well, had arrived in Ephesus from Alexandria in Mitzraym.
Apollos had been taught the way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and he taught others about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA with an enthusiastic Ruach and with accuracy. However, he knew only about Yahukanun’s baptism.
When Priscilla and Aquila heard him preaching boldly in the Yahudym congregation, they took him aside and explained the way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH even more accurately.

Apollos had been thinking about going to Achaia, and the brothers and sisters in Ephesus encouraged him to go. They wrote to the believers in Achaia, asking them to welcome him. When he arrived there, he proved to be of great benefit to those who, by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s favor, had believed in the Dabar.
He refuted the Yahudym with powerful arguments in public debate. Using the Scriptures, Apollos explained to them that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA is Ha'Mashyach.
While Apollos was in Corinth, Shaul traveled through the interior regions until he reached Ephesus, on the coast, where he found several believers of the Dabar.
“Did you receive the RUACH Ha'Qadash when you believed in the Truth?” Shaul asked them. “No,” they replied, “we have not even heard that there is a RUACH Ha'Qadash.”
“Then what baptism did you experience?” Shaul asked them. And they replied, “The baptism of Yahukanun.”
Shaul said, “Yahukanun’s baptism called for repentance from sin. But Yahukanun himself told the people to believe in the one who would come later, He means 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach.”
As soon as they heard this, they were baptized in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach.
Then when Shaul laid his hands on them, the RUACH Ha'Qadash came on them, and they spoke in other tongues and prophesied.
There were about twelve men in all.
Then Shaul went to the Yahudym congregation and preached boldly for the next three months, arguing persuasively about the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

But some became stubborn, rejecting Shaul‘s message and publicly speaking against the Way of Truth. So Shaul left the Yahudym congregation and took the Qadash assembly with him. Then he held daily discussions at the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
This went on for the next two years, so that people throughout the province of Asia both Yahudym and Greeks heard the Dabar of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave Shaul the power to perform unusual miracles.
When handkerchiefs or aprons that had merely touched Shaul‘s skin were placed on sick people, they were healed of their diseases, and evil spirits were expelled.

A group of Yahudym was traveling from town to town casting out evil spirits. They tried to use the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA in their incantation, saying, “I command you in the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, whom Shaul preaches, to come out!”
Seven sons of Sceva, a leading Kuhanym, were doing this.
But one time when they tried it, the evil spirit replied, “I know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, and I know Shaul, but who are you?”
Then the man with the evil spirit leaped on them, overpowered them, and attacked them with such violence that they fled from the house, naked and battered.
The story of what happened spread quickly all through Ephesus, to Yahudym and Greeks alike. A solemn fear descended on the city, and the name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach was greatly honored.
Many who became believers confessed their sinful practices.

A number of them who had been practicing sorcery brought their incantation books and burned them at a public bonfire. And they counted up the value of them, and it totaled fifty thousand pieces of silver.
So the message about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA spread widely and had a powerful effect.
Afterward Shaul felt compelled by the RUACH to go over to Macedonia and Achaia before going to Yahushalam. “And after that,” he said, “I must go on to Rome!”
Shaul sent his two assistants, Timothy and Erastus, ahead to Macedonia while he stayed awhile longer in the province of Asia.
After some time, serious trouble developed in Ephesus concerning the Way of TRUTH.
It began with Demetrius, a silversmith who had a large business manufacturing silver shrines of the Greek female deity Artemis. He kept many craftsmen busy.
Demetrius called them together, along with others employed in similar trades, and addressed them as follows: “Gentlemen, you know that our wealth comes from this business.

But as you have seen and heard, this man Shaul has persuaded many people that handmade idols are not really mighty ones at all. And he as done this not only here in Ephesus but throughout the entire province!

Of course, I am not just talking about the loss of public respect for our business. I am also concerned that People will begin to think that the temple of the great female deity Artemis is not important, and the deity herself, whom everyone in the province of Asia and the whole world worships, will ·lose and will be stripped of her majesty.
At this their anger boiled, and they began shouting, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
Soon the whole city was filled with confusion. Everyone rushed to the amphitheater, dragging along Gaius and Aristarchus, who were Shaul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.
Shaul wanted to go in, too, but the believers of way of Truth, would not let Shaul go there.
Some of the officials of the province, friends of Shaul, also sent a message to him, begging him not to risk his life by entering the amphitheater.
Inside, the people were all shouting, some one thing and some another. Everything was in confusion. In fact, most of them did not even know why they were there.
The Yahudym in the crowd pushed Alexander forward and told him to explain the situation, he motioned for silence and tried to speak.
But when the crowd realized he was a Yahudym, they started shouting again and kept it up for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians! Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

At last the mayor was able to quiet them down enough to speak. “Citizens of Ephesus,” he said. “Everyone knows that Ephesus is the official guardian of the temple of Artemis, whose image fell down to us from the sky.
Since this is an undeniable fact, you should stay calm and not do anything rash.
You have brought these men here, but they have stolen nothing from the temple and have not spoken against our female idol.
“If Demetrius and the craftsmen have a case against them, the courts are in session and the officials can hear the case at once. Let them make formal charges.
And if there are complaints about other matters, they can be settled in a legal assembly.
I am afraid we are in danger of being charged with rioting by the Roman government, since there is no cause for all this commotion. And if Rome demands an explanation, we will not know what to say.”
Then he dismissed them, and they dispersed.
When the uproar was over, Shaul sent for the believers of Truth and encouraged them. Then Shaul said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.
While there, Shaul encouraged the believers of Truth in all the towns he passed through. Then Shaul traveled down to Greece,
Where he stayed for three months. He was preparing to sail back to Syria when he discovered a plot by some Yahudym against his life, so he decided to return through Macedonia.

Several men were traveling with him. They were Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea; Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica; Gaius from Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
They went on ahead and waited for us at Troas.
After the Passakh ended, we boarded a ship at Philippi in Macedonia and five days later joined them in Troas, where we stayed a week.

On the first day of the week (first day evening, after Shabbat sun set), we gathered with the local believers of Truth to share in Ha'Mashyach’s Supper. So Shaul was preaching to them, and since Shaul was leaving the next day, Shaul kept talking until midnight.
The upstairs room where we met was lighted with many flickering lamps.

And a young man sat in the window side, his name was Eutychus, who was sinking into a deep sleep, he was overcome by sleep; and as Shaul continued speaking, he fell down from the third story and was taken up dead.
Shaul went down, bent over him, and took him into his arms. “Do not worry,” he said, “he is alive!”
Then they all went back upstairs, shared in Ha'Mashyach’s Supper, and ate together. Shaul continued talking to them until dawn, and then Shaul left.
Meanwhile, the young man was taken home alive and well, and everyone was greatly relieved.
Shaul went by land to Assos, where he had arranged for us to join him, while we traveled by ship.
Shaul joined us there, and we sailed together to Mitylene.
The next day we sailed past the island of Kios. The following day we crossed to the island of Samos, and a day later we arrived at Miletus.

Shaul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, for he did not want to spend any more time in the province of Asia, he was hurrying to get to Yahushalam, if possible, in time for the Festival of shabut (weeks).
But when we landed at Miletus, Shaul sent a message to the elders of the Qadash assembly at Ephesus, asking them to come and meet him.
When they arrived Shaul declared, “You know that from the day I set foot in the province of Asia until now,
I have done 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s work humbly and with many tears. I have endured the trials that came to me from the plots of the Yahudym.
I never shrank back from telling you what you needed to hear, either publicly or in your homes.
I have had one message for Yahudym and Greeks alike, the necessity of repenting from sin and turning to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and of having Amunah in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA our salvation.
“And now I am bound by the RUACH to go to Yahushalam. I do not know what awaits me,
Except that the RUACH Ha'Qadash tells me in city after city that jail and suffering lie ahead.

But none of these things move me; for my life is worth nothing to me unless I use it for finishing the work assigned me by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the work of telling others the Good News about the wonderful favor of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
“And now I know that none of you to whom I have preached the Kingdom will ever see me again.
I declare today that I have been faithful. If anyone suffers eternal death, it is not my fault,
for I did not hold back from telling you everything that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH wants you to know.

“Keep watch over yourselves and all the Qadash ones of which the RUACH Ha'Qadash has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the Qadash assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA our Mashyach bought with His own blood.
I know that false teachers, like vicious wolves, will come in among you after I leave, not sparing the Qadash ones.
Even some men from your own group will rise up speaking perverse things against the way of Truth in order to draw the Qadash ones after themselves.
Watch out! Remember the three years I was with you, my constant watch and care over you night and day, and my many tears for you.
“And now I entrust you to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and the message of HIS favor that is able to build you up and give you an inheritance with all those 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has Qadash (Set Apart) for HIMSELF.
“I have never coveted anyone’s silver or gold or fine clothes.
Every one of you know that these my hands have worked to supply my own needs and even the needs of those who were with me.

And I have been a constant example of how you can help those in need by working hard. You should remember the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA our Mashyach: it said ‘It is more baraked to give than to receive.’”
When Shaul had finished speaking, he knelt and prayed with them.
They all cried as they embraced and kissed Shaul good bye.
They were sad most of all because Shaul had said that they would never see him again. Then they escorted Shaul down to the ship.
After saying farewell to the Ephesian elders, we sailed straight to the island of Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and then went to Patara.
There we boarded a ship sailing for Phoenicia.
We sighted the island of Cyprus, passed it on our left, and landed at the harbor of Tyra in Syria, where the ship was to unload its cargo.

We went ashore and found the local believers of Truth, and we stayed with them for seven days. These believers of Truth prophesied through the RUACH Ha'Qadash that Shaul the Shaliach should not go on to Yahushalam.

When we returned to the ship at the end of our stay, the entire congregation of the Qadash ones, including women and children, left the city and came down to the shore with us. There we knelt down on the shore and prayed.
And said our farewells. Then we went aboard, and they returned home.
The next stop after leaving Tyra was Ptolemais, where we greeted the Qadash Ones and stayed for one day.
The next day we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the basar, one of the seven men who had been chosen to distribute food.
He had four unmarried daughters who had the gift of prophecy.
Several days later a man named Agabus, who also had the gift of prophecy, arrived from Yahudah.

He came over, took Shaul’s belt, and bound his own feet and hands with it. Then he said, “The RUACH Ha'Qadash declares, ‘So shall the owner of this belt be bound by the Yahudym leaders in Yahushalam and turned over to the other nations (non Yahudym).’”
When we heard this, we and the local believers of Truth all begged Shaul not to go on to Yahushalam.
But he said, “Why all this weeping? You are breaking my heart! I am ready not only to be jailed at Yahushalam but even to die for the sake of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA my Mashyach.”
When it was clear that we could not persuade Shaul, we gave up and said, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s WILL be done.”
After this we packed our things and left for Yahushalam.
Some believers from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to the home of Mnason, a man originally from Cyprus and one of the early believers of Truth.
When we arrived, the Qadash assembly in Yahushalam welcomed us warmly.
The next day Shaul went with us to meet with Ya'aqub, and all the elders of the Yahushalam Qadash assembly were present.
After greeting them, Shaul gave a detailed account of the things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had accomplished among the other nations through his service.

After hearing this, they Yadah 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And then they said, “You know, dear Achk (brother) Shaul, how many thousands of Yahudym have also believed the Truth, and they all still follow the law of Musha very seriously.

But the Yahudym believers here in Yahushalam have been told that you are teaching all the Yahudym who live among the other nations to turn their backs on the laws of Musha. They have heard that you teach them not to circumcise their children or follow other Yahudym customs.
What should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.
“Here is what we want you to do. We have four men here who have completed their vow.

Go with them to the Haykal (Temple) and join them in the purification ceremony and pay for them to have their heads ritually shaved. Then everyone will know that the rumors are all false and that you yourself observe the Yahudym laws.

“As for the other nations believers of Truth, they should do what we already told them in a letter: They should abstain from eating food offered to idols, from consuming blood or the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”

So Shaul went to the Temple the next day with the other men. They had already started the purification ritual, so he publicly announced the date when their vows would end and sacrifices would be offered for each of them.
The seven days were almost ended when some Yahudym from the province of Asia saw Shaul in the Temple and roused a mob against him. They grabbed Shaul,

Yelling, “Men of Yashar'AL, help us! This is the man who preaches against our people everywhere and tells everybody to disobey the Yahudym laws. He speaks against the Temple and even defiles this qadash place by bringing in the people of other nations.”
(For earlier that day they had seen him in the city with Trophimus, a foreigner from Ephesus, and they assumed Shaul had taken him into the Temple)
The whole city was rocked by these accusations, and a great riot followed. Shaul was grabbed and dragged out of the Temple, and immediately the gates were closed behind him.
As they were trying to kill him, word reached the commander of the Roman regiment that all Yahushalam was in an uproar.
He immediately called out his soldiers and officers and ran down among the crowd. When the mob saw the commander and the troops coming, they stopped beating Shaul.
Then the commander arrested Shaul and ordered him bound with two chains. He asked the crowd who he was and what he had done.
Some shouted one thing and some another. Since he could not find out the truth in all the uproar and confusion, he ordered that Shaul be taken to the fortress.
As Shaul reached the stairs, the mob grew so violent the soldiers had to lift him to their shoulders to protect him.
And the crowd followed behind, shouting, “Kill him, kill him!”
As Shaul was about to be taken inside, he said to the commander, “May I have a word with you? “the Commander was surprised and he replied, can you speak Greek?”.
“Are you not the Mitzraym who led a rebellion some time ago and took four thousand members of the Assassins out into the desert?”
“No,” Shaul replied, “I am a Yahudym and a citizen of Tarsus in Cilicia, which is an important city. Please, let me talk to these people.”

The commander agreed, so Shaul stood on the stairs and motioned to the people to be quiet. Soon a deep silence enveloped the crowd, And when there was a great silence, Shaul spoke to them in the Abarym (Hebrew) language, saying,
“Brothers and esteemed fathers,” Shaul said, “listen to me as I offer my defense.”
When they heard him speaking in their own language, the silence was even greater.

Then Shaul said, “I am a Yahudym, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, and I was brought up and educated here in Yahushalam under Gamalial. As his student, I was carefully trained in our Yahudym laws and customs. I became very zealous to honor 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in everything I did, just like all of you today.
And I persecuted the followers of the Way of Truth, hounding some to death, arresting both men and women and throwing them in prison.

The high Kuhan and the whole council of elders can testify that this is so. For I received letters from them to our Yahudym brothers in Damascus, authorizing me to bring the followers of the Way of Truth from there to Yahushalam, in chains to be punished.
“As I was on the road, approaching Damascus about noon, a very bright light from Shamaym suddenly shone down around me.
I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Shaul, Shaul, why are you persecuting me?’
“‘Who are you?’ I asked.
The people with me saw the light but they did not understand the voice speaking to me.
“I asked, ‘What should I do, MASTER?’
“I was blinded by the intense light and had to be led by the hand to Damascus by my companions.
A man named Ananyas lived there, he was a righteous man, deeply devoted to the law, and well regarded by all the Yahudym of Damascus.
Ananyas came and stood beside me and said, ‘brother Shaul, regain your sight.’ And that very moment I could see him!
“Then he told me, ‘The 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of our ancestors has chosen you, that you should know HIS Will and that you should see the Righteous One and hear 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA speak.
For you are to be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s witness, telling everyone what you have seen and heard.
And Ananyas said, What are you waiting for? Get up and be baptized. And have your sins washed away by calling on the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.’
“After I returned to Yahushalam, I was praying in the Temple and fell into a trance.
I saw a vision of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Yahushalam, for the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’
“‘But Master,’ I argued, ‘they certainly know that in every Yahudym congregation I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.
And I was in complete agreement when your witness Staphan was killed. I stood by and kept the coats they took off when they stoned Staphan.’
“But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA said to me, ‘Go, for I will send you far away to the other nations!’
The crowd listened until Shaul said that word. Then they all began to shout, “Away with such a fellow! He is not fit to live!”
They yelled, and threw off their coats, and tossed handfuls of dust into the air.
The commander brought Shaul inside and ordered him lashed with whips to make him confess his crime. The commander wanted to find out why the crowd had become so furious.
When they tied Shaul down to lash him, Shaul said to the officer standing there, “Is it legal for you to whip a Roman citizen who has not even been tried?”
When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and asked, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
So the commander went over and asked Shaul, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen? “Yes, I certainly am,” Shaul replied.
“I am, too,” the commander muttered, “and it cost me plenty!” Shaul answered, “But I am a citizen by birth!”
The soldiers who were about to interrogate Shaul quickly withdrew when they heard he was a Roman citizen, and the commander was frightened because he had ordered him bound and whipped.

The next day the commander ordered the leading Kuhanym into session with the Yahudym high council. He wanted to find out what the trouble was all about, so he released Shaul to have him stand before them.
Gazing intently at the high council, Shaul began: “Brothers, I have always lived before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH with a clear conscience!”
Instantly Ananyas the high Kuhan commanded those close to Shaul to slap him on the mouth.
But Shaul said to him, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will slap you, because you are a corrupt hypocrite! What kind of judge are you to break the law yourself by ordering me struck like that?”
Those standing near Shaul said to him, “Do you dare to insult 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s high Kuhan?”
“I am sorry, brothers. I did not realize he was the high Kuhan,” Shaul replied, “for the Scriptures say, ‘You must not speak evil of any of your rulers.’”

Shaul realized that some members of the high council were Sadducees and some were Pharisees, so he shouted, Achks “(Brothers), I am a Pharisee, as were my ancestors! And I am on trial because my hope is in the resurrection of the dead!”
This divided the council, the Pharisees against the Sadducees
for the Sadducees say there is no resurrection or Malakym or ruach, but the Pharisees believe in all of these.

So there was a great uproar. Some of the teachers of religious law who were Pharisees jumped up and began to argue forcefully. “We see nothing wrong with him,” they shouted. “Perhaps a Ruach or a Malak spoke to him.”
As the conflict grew more violent, the commander was afraid they would tear Shaul apart. So he ordered his soldiers to go and rescue him by force and take him back to the fortress.
That night 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA appeared to Shaul and said, “Be encouraged, Shaul. Just as you have been a witness to me here in Yahushalam, you must preach the Good News in Rome as well.”
The next morning a group of Yahudym got together and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Shaul.
There were more than forty of them in the conspiracy.
They went to the leading Kuhanym and elders and told them, “We have bound ourselves with an oath to eat nothing until we have killed Shaul.
So you and the high council should ask the commander to bring Shaul back to the council again. Pretend you want to examine his case more fully. We will kill him on the way.”
But Shaul’s nephew, his sister’s son heard of their plan and went to the fortress and told Shaul.
Shaul called for one of the Roman officers and said, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something important to tell him.”
So the officer took him to the Commander, and he said, “Shaul, the prisoner, called me over and asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you.”
The commander took his hand, led him aside, and asked, “What is it you want to tell me?”
Shaul’s nephew told him, “Some Yahudym are going to ask you to bring Shaul before the high council tomorrow, pretending they want to get some more information.

But do not do it! There are more than forty men hiding along the way ready to ambush Shaul. They have vowed not to eat or drink anything until they have killed Shaul. They are ready now, just waiting for your consent.”
“Do not let anyone know you told me this,” the commander warned the young man.
Then the commander called two of his officers and ordered, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea at the third hour of the night;
And provide horses for Shaul to ride, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.”
He wrote a letter in the following manner:
“From Claudius Lysias, to his Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings!
“This man was seized by some Yahudym, and they were about to kill him, then I arrived with the troops. When I learned that he was a Roman citizen, I removed him to safety.
Then I took him to their high council to try to learn the basis of the accusations against him.
I soon discovered the charge was something regarding their religious law, certainly nothing worthy of imprisonment or death.
But when I was informed of a plot to kill him, I immediately sent him on to you. I have told his accusers to bring their charges before you.”
So that night, as ordered, the soldiers took Shaul as far as Antipatris.
They returned to the fortress the next morning, while the mounted troops took Shaul on to Caesarea.
When they arrived in Caesarea, they presented Shaul and the letter to Governor Felix.
He read it and then asked Shaul what province he was from. And Shaul said. “Cilicia,”
“I will hear your case myself when your accusers arrive,” the governor told him. Then the governor ordered him kept in the prison at Harud’s headquarters.
Now after five days Ananyas the high Kuhan came down with the elders and a certain lawyer named Tertullus. These gave evidence to the governor against Shaul.

When Shaul was called in, Tertullus presented the charges against Shaul in the following address to the governor: “You have provided a long period of Shalum for us Yahudym and with foresight have enacted reforms for us.
For all of this, Your Excellency, we are very grateful to you.
But I do not want to bore you, so please give me your attention for only a moment.
We have found this man to be a troublemaker who is constantly stirring up riots among the Yahudym all over the world. He is a ringleader of the cult known as the Nazarym.
Furthermore, this Shaul was trying to desecrate the Temple when we arrested him.
But the commander Lysias came by and with great violence took him out of our hands,
You can find out the truth of our accusations by examining him yourself.”
Then the other Yahudym commented in declaring that everything Tertullus said was true.
The governor then motioned for Shaul to speak. Shaul said, “I know, sir, that you have been a judge of Yahudym affairs for many years, so I gladly present my defense before you.
You can quickly discover that I arrived in Yahushalam no more than twelve days ago to worship at the Temple.
My accusers never found me arguing with anyone in the Temple, nor stirring up a riot in any Yahudym congregation or on the streets of the city.
These men cannot prove the things they accuse me of doing.
“But I admit that I follow the Way of Truth, which they call a cult. I worship the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of our fathers, and I firmly believe the Yahudym law and everything written by the Nabyms.
I have the same hope in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that these men have, that he will raise both the righteous and the unrighteous.
Because of this, I always try to maintain a clear conscience before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and all people.
“After several years away, I returned to Yahushalam with money to aid my people and to offer sacrifices to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
My accusers saw me in the Temple as I was completing a purification ceremony. There was no crowd around me and no rioting.
But some Yahudym from the province of Asia were there and they ought to be here before you to object if they had anything against me
Ask these men here what crime the Yahudym high council found me guilty of,
Except for the one time I shouted out, ‘I am on trial before you today because I believe in the resurrection of the dead!’”
At that point Felix, who was quite familiar with the Way of Truth, adjourned the hearing and said, “Wait until Lysias, the garrison commander arrives. Then I will decide the case.”
He ordered an officer to keep Shaul in custody but to give him some freedom and allow his friends to visit him and take care of his needs.
A few days later Felix came back with his wife, Drusilla, who was a Yahudym. Sending for Shaul, they listened as Shaul told them about Amunah in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach.

As Shaul reasoned with them about righteousness and self control and the coming day of judgment, Felix became frightened. “Go away for now,” Felix replied. “When it is more convenient I will call for you again.”
Felix also hoped that Shaul would bribe him, so Felix sent for Shaul quite often and talked with him.
After two years went by in this way, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And because Felix wanted to gain favor with the Yahudym people, he left Shaul in prison.
Three days after Festus arrived in Caesarea to take over his new responsibilities, he left for Yahushalam,
Where the leading Kuhanym and other Yahudym leaders met with him and made their accusations against Shaul.
They asked Festus as a favor to transfer Shaul to Yahushalam (planning to ambush and kill him on the way).
But Festus replied that Shaul was at Caesarea and he himself would be returning there soon.
So Festus said, “Those of you in authority can return with me. If Shaul has done anything wrong, you can make your accusations.”
About eight or ten days later Festus returned to Caesarea, and on the following day he took his seat in court and ordered that Shaul be brought in.
When Shaul arrived, the Yahudym leaders from Yahushalam gathered around and made many serious accusations they could not prove.
Shaul denied the charges. “I am not guilty of any crime against the Yahudym laws or the Temple or the Roman government,” Shaul said.
Then Festus, wanting to please the Yahudym, asked him, “Are you willing to go to Yahushalam and stand trial before me there?”
But Shaul replied, “No! This is the official Roman court, so I ought to be tried right here. You know very well I am not guilty of harming the Yahudym.
If I have done something worthy of death, I do not object of dying. But if I am innocent, no one has a right to turn me over to these men to kill me. I appeal to Caesar!”
Festus conferred with his advisers and then replied, “Very well! You have appealed to Caesar, and to Caesar you will go!”
A few days later King Agrippa arrived with his sister, Bernice, to pay their respects to Festus.
During their stay of several days, Festus discussed Shaul’s case with the king. “There is a prisoner here,” he told him, “whose case was left for me by Felix.
When I was in Yahushalam, the leading Kuhanym and Yahudym elders pressed charges against the prisoner and asked me to condemn him.
I pointed out to them that Roman law does not convict people without a trial. They must be given an opportunity to confront their accusers and defend themselves.
“When Shaul‘s accusers came here for the trial, I did not delay. I called the case the very next day and ordered Shaul to be brought in.
But the accusations made against him were not any of the crimes I expected.
Instead, it was something about their religion and a dead man named 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, who Shaul insists is alive.
I was at a loss to know how to investigate these things, so I asked Shaul whether he would be willing to stand trial on these charges in Yahushalam.
But Shaul appealed to have his case decided by the emperor. So I ordered that he be held in custody until I could arrange to send him to Caesar.”
“Then Agrippa said to Festus; I would like to hear from the man myself,” And Festus replied, “You will hear him tomorrow!”
So the next day Agrippa and Bernice arrived at the auditorium with great pomp, accompanied by military officers and prominent men of the city. Festus ordered that Shaul be brought in.
Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are here, this is the man whose death is demanded by all the Yahudym, both here and in Yahushalam.
But in my opinion he has done nothing deserving death. However, since he appealed his case to the emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.

“But what shall I write the emperor? For there is no clear charge against him. So I have brought him before all of you, and especially you, King Agrippa, so that after we examine him, I might have something to write.
For it makes no sense to send a prisoner to the emperor without specifying the charges against him!”
Then Agrippa said to Shaul, “You may speak in your defense.” So Shaul, gesturing with his hand, started his defense:
“I am fortunate, King Agrippa, that you are the one hearing my defense today against all these accusations made by the Yahudym leaders,
for I know you are an expert on all Yahudym customs and controversies. Now please listen to me patiently!
“As the Yahudym leaders are well aware, I was given a thorough Yahudym training from my earliest childhood among my own people and in Yahushalam.
If they would admit it, they know that I have been a member of the Pharisees, the strictest sect of our religion.
Now I am on trial because of my hope in the fulfillment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s promise made to our fathers.
In fact, that is why the twelve tribes of Yashar'AL zealously worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH night and day, and they share the same hope I have. Yet, Your Majesty, they accuse me for having this hope!
Why does it seem incredible to any of you that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH can raise the dead?
“I used to believe that I ought to do everything I could to oppose the very Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA the Nazarym.

Indeed, I did just that in Yahushalam. Authorized by the leading Kuhanym, I caused many believers of Truth in Yahushalam to be sent to prison. And I cast my vote against them when they were condemned to death.
Many times I had them punished in the Yahudym congregation to get them to curse 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA. I was so violently opposed to them that I even chased them down in foreign cities.
“One day I was on such a mission to Damascus, armed with the authority and commission of the leading Kuhanym.
About midday, Your Majesty, as I was on the road, a light from Shamaym brighter than the sun shone down on me and my companions.
We all fell down, and I heard a voice speaking to me in Abarym (Hebrew), ‘Shaul, Shaul, why are you persecuting me? It is useless for you to fight against my Will.’
“‘Who are you, Master?’ I asked. “And the Master replied, ‘I Am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA, the One you are persecuting.
Now get to your feet! For I have appeared to you to appoint you as my servant and witness. Tell people that you have seen Me, and tell them what I will show you in the future.
And I will rescue you from both your own people and the other nations. Yes, I am sending you to the other nations,

to open their eyes, so they may turn from darkness to light and from the traps of ha'shatan to the Power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. Then they will receive forgiveness for their sins and be given a place among 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s people, who are set apart by Amunah in Me.’
“And so, King Agrippa, I obeyed that vision from Shamaym.

I preached first to those in Damascus, then in Yahushalam and throughout all Yahudah, and also to the other nations, that all must repent of their sins and turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and prove they have changed by the good things they do.
Some Yahudym arrested me in the Temple for preaching this, and they tried to kill me.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has protected me right up to this present time so I can testify to everyone, from the least to the greatest. I teach nothing except what the Nabyms and Musha said would happen
That Ha'Mashyach would suffer and be the first to rise from the dead, and in this way announce 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s light to the Yahudym and the other nations alike.”
Suddenly, Festus shouted, “Shaul, you are insane. Too much study has made you crazy!”
But Shaul replied, “I am not insane, Most Excellent Festus. What I am saying is the sober Truth.
And King Agrippa knows about these things. I speak boldly, for I am sure these events are all familiar to him, for they were not done in a corner!
King Agrippa, do you believe the Nabyms? I know you do”
Agrippa interrupted him. “Do you think you can persuade me to become a believer so quickly?”
Shaul replied, “Whether quickly or not, I pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that both you and everyone here in this audience might become the same as I am, except for these chains.”
Then the king, the governor, Bernice, and all the others stood and left.
As they went out, they talked it over and agreed, “This man has not done anything to deserve death or imprisonment.”
And Agrippa said to Festus, “He could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
When the time came, we set sail for Italy. Shaul and several other prisoners were placed in the custody of a Roman officer named Julius, a captain of the Imperial Regiment.

Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was also with us. We left on a ship whose home port was Adramyttium on the northwest coast of the province of Asia; it was scheduled to make several stops at ports along the coast of the province.
The next day when we docked at Sidun, Julius was very kind to Shaul and let him go ashore to visit with friends so they could provide for his needs.
Putting out to sea from there, we encountered strong headwinds that made it difficult to keep the ship on course, so we sailed north of Cyprus between the island and the mainland.
Keeping to the open sea, we passed along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, landing at Myra, in the province of Lycia.
There the commanding officer found a Mitzraym ship from Alexandria that was bound for Italy, and he put us on board.

We had several days of slow sailing, and after great difficulty we finally neared Cnidus. But the wind was against us, so we sailed across to Crete and along the sheltered coast of the island, past the cape of Salmone.
We struggled along the coast with great difficulty and finally arrived at a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
We had lost a lot of time. The weather was becoming dangerous for sea travel because it was so late in the fall, and Shaul spoke to the ship’s officers about it.
“Men,” Shaul said, “I perceived there is trouble ahead if we go on the ship will wreck, loss of cargo, and danger to our lives as well.”
But the officer in charge of the prisoners listened more to the ship’s captain and the owner than to Shaul.

And since Fair Havens was an exposed harbor, a poor place to spend the winter, most of the crew wanted to go on to Phoenix, farther up the coast of Crete, and spend the winter there. Phoenix was a good harbor with only a southwest and northwest exposure.
When a light wind began blowing from the south, the sailors thought they could make it. So they pulled up anchor and sailed close to the shore of Crete.
But the weather changed abruptly, and a wind of typhoon strength (called a “northeaster”) burst across the island and blew us out to sea.
The sailors could not turn the ship into the wind, so they gave up and let it run before the gale.
And running under the shelter of an island called Clauda, we secured the skiff with difficulty.
When they had taken it on board, they used cables to undergird the ship; and fearing lest they should run aground on the Syrtis Sands, they struck sail and were driven.
And because we were exceedingly tempest-tossed, the next day they lightened the ship.
On the third day we threw the ship’s tackle overboard with our own hands.
Now when neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small tempest beat on us, all hope that we would be saved was finally given up.

No one had eaten for a long time. Finally, Shaul called the crew together and said, “Men, you should have listened to me in the first place and not left Crete. You would have avoided all this damage and loss.
But take courage! None of you will lose your lives, even though the ship will go down.
For last night a Malak of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me,
And the Malak said, ‘Do not be afraid, Shaul, for you will surely stand trial before Caesar! What is more, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH in His goodness has granted safety to everyone sailing with you.’
So take courage! For I believe 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. It will be just as HE said.
But we will be shipwrecked on an island.”
About midnight on the fourteenth night of the storm, as we were being driven across the Sea of Adria, the sailors sensed land was near.
And they took soundings and found it to be twenty fathoms; and when they had gone a little farther, they took soundings again and found it to be fifteen fathoms.
Then, fearing lest we should run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern, and prayed for day to come.
And as the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship, when they had let down the skiff into the sea, under pretense of putting out anchors from the prow,
Shaul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved.”
Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the skiff and let it fall off.
And as day was about to dawn, Shaul implored them all to take food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day you have waited and continued without food, and eaten nothing.
“Please eat something now for your own good. For not a hair of your heads will perish.”
Then Shaul took some bread, and gave Tudah to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH before them all, and broke off a piece and ate it.
Then everyone was encouraged and began to eat
And in all we were two hundred and seventy-six persons on the ship.
So when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship and threw out the wheat into the sea.
When morning dawned, they did not recognize the coastline, but they saw a bay with a beach and wondered if they could get to shore by running the ship aground.
So they cut off the anchors and left them in the sea. Then they lowered the rudders, raised the foresail, and headed toward shore.
But striking a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the prow stuck fast and remained immovable, but the stern was being broken up by the violence of the waves.
And the soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.
But the centurion, wanting to save Shaul, and he kept the soldiers from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should jump overboard first and get to land,
And the rest, some on boards and some on parts of the ship. And so it was that they all escaped safely to land.
After we were safe on shore, we learned that we were on the island of Malta.
The people of the island were very kind to us. It was cold and rainy, so they built a fire on the shore to welcome us.
As Shaul gathered an armful of sticks and was laying them on the fire, a poisonous snake, driven out by the heat, bit him on the hand.
The people of the island saw it hanging from his hand and said to each other, “A murderer, no doubt! Though he escaped the sea, justice will not permit him to live.”
But Shaul shook off the snake into the fire and was unharmed.
The people waited for him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But when they had waited a long time and saw that he was not harmed, they changed their minds and decided that Shaul was a deity.
Near the shore where we landed was an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and treated us kindly for three days.
And it happened that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and dysentery. Shaul went in to him and prayed, and Shaul laid his hands on him and healed him.
So when this was done, the rest of those on the island who had diseases also came and were healed.
They also honored us in many ways; and when we departed, they provided such things as were necessary.
It was three months after the shipwreck that we set sail on another ship that had wintered at the island, an Alexandrian ship with the twin idols as its figurehead.
Our first stop was Syracuse, where we stayed three days.
From there we sailed across to Rhegium. A day later a south wind began blowing, so the following day we sailed up the coast to Puteoli.
There we found some believers of Truth, who invited us to spend a week with them. And so we came to Rome.

The Achks (brothers) and Achutys (sisters) in Rome had heard we were coming, and they came to meet us at the Forum on the Appian Way. Others joined us at the three Taverns. When Shaul saw them, he was encouraged and he gave Tudah to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
When we arrived in Rome, Shaul was permitted to have his own private lodging, though he was guarded by a soldier.

Three days after Shaul’s arrival, he called together the local Yahudym leaders, he said to them, “brothers, I was arrested in Yahushalam and handed over to the Roman government, even though I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our ancestors.
The Romans tried me and wanted to release me, because they found no cause for the death sentence.
But when the Yahudym leaders protested the decision, I felt it necessary to appeal to Caesar, even though I had no desire to press charges against my own people.

I asked you to come here today so we could get acquainted and so I could explain to you that I am bound with this chain because I believe that the hope of Yashar'AL, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach has already come.
They replied, “We have had no letters from Yahudah or reports against you from anyone who has come here.
But we want to hear what you believe, for the only thing we know about this movement is that it is denounced everywhere.”

So a time was set, and on that day a large number of people came to Shaul’s lodging. He explained and testified about the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and tried to persuade them about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA from the Scriptures. Using the law of Musha and the books of the Nabyms, he spoke to them from morning until evening.
Some were persuaded by the things he said, but others did not believe.
And after they had argued back and forth among themselves, they left with this final word from Shaul: “The RUACH Ha'Qadash was right when He said to your fathers through Yashayahu the Nabym,
‘Go and say to this people: When you hear what I say, you will not understand. When you see what I do, you will not comprehend.

For the hearts of these people are hardened, and their ears cannot hear, and they have closed their eyes, so their eyes cannot see, and their ears cannot hear, and their hearts cannot understand, and they cannot turn to me and let me heal them.’
So I want you to know that this salvation from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has also been offered to the other nations, and they will accept it.”
And when he had said these words, the Yahudym departed and had a great dispute among themselves
For the next two years, Shaul lived in Rome at his own expense. He welcomed all who visited him,
boldly proclaiming the Kingdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and teaching about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach. And no one tried to stop Shaul.

books.name: Romans
chapters: This letter is from Shaul, a bondservant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach, chosen by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to be a Shaliach and sent out to preach 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s Basurah (Good news).
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH promised this Basurah (Good News) long ago through His Nabyms in the Qadash Scriptures.
The Basurah is about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s Son. In 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA‘s life in the Arath He was born into King Daud’s family line,
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was shown to be the Son of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH when He was raised from the dead by the power of the RUACH Ha'Qadash. He is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach our Savior.

Through Ha'Mashyach, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has given us the privilege and authority as Shaliach to tell the other nations everywhere what HE has done for them, so that they will believe and obey HIM, bringing kabad to His Name.
And you are included among those other nations who have been called to belong to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach.
I am writing to all of you in Rome who are loved by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH and are called to be 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s own qadash people. May 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH our ABBA and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach give you Favor and Shalum.
Let me say first that I give Tudah to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach for all of you, because your Amunah in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is being talked about all over the world.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH knows how often I pray for you. Day and night I bring you and your needs in prayer to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, whom I serve with all my heart by spreading the Basurah (Good News) about his Son.
One of the things I always pray for is the opportunity, by the Will of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that I can come to see you.
For I long to visit you so I can bring you some gifts of the RUACH that will help you grow strong in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
When we get together, I want to encourage you in your Amunah, but I also want to be encouraged by yours.

I want you to know, dear Achks (brothers) and Achutys (sisters), that I planned many times to visit you, but I was prevented until now. I want to work among you and see fruit of the RUACH, just as I have seen among some of the other nations.
For I have a great sense of obligation to people in both the civilized world and the rest of the world, to the educated and uneducated alike.
So I am eager to come to you in Rome, to preach the Basurah (Good News).
For I am not ashamed of this Basurah about Ha'Mashyach. It is the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at work, saving everyone who believes, the Yahudym first and also to the other nations.

For this Basurah tells us how 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH makes us right in HIS sight. This is accomplished from start to finish by Amunah. As the Scriptures say, “It is through Amunah that a righteous man has life.”
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH shows HIS anger from Shamaym against all sinful, wicked people who suppress the truth by their wickedness.
They know the truth about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, because HE has made it obvious to them.

For ever since the world was created, people have seen the Arath and sky. Through everything 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH made, they can clearly see 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s invisible qualities, and HIS eternal power and Divine nature. So they have no excuse for not knowing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.

Yes, they knew 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but they would not worship HIM as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH or even give Tudah to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And they began to think up foolish ideas of what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was like. As a result, their minds became dark and confused.
Claiming to be wise, they instead became utter fools.
And instead of worshiping the awesome, ever living 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH, they worshiped idols made to look like mere people and birds and animals and reptiles.
So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH abandoned them to do whatever shameful things their hearts desired. As a result, they did vile and degrading things with each other’s bodies.
They traded the truth about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for a lie. So they worshiped and served the things 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH created instead of the Creator HIMSELF, who is worthy of eternal Yadah!
That is why 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH abandoned them to their shameful desires. Even the women turned against the natural way to have sex and instead indulged in sex with each other.

And the men, instead of having normal sexual relations with women, burned with lust for each other. Men did shameful things with other men, and as a result of this sin, they suffered within themselves the penalty they deserved.
Furthermore, just as they did not think it worthwhile to retain the knowledge of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, so 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH gave them over to a depraved mind, so that they do what ought not to be done.
Their lives became full of every kind of wickedness, sin, greed, hate, envy, murder, quarreling, deception, malicious behavior, and gossip.
They are backstabbers, haters of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, insolent, proud, and boastful. They invent new ways of sinning, and they disobey their parents.
They refuse to understand, they break their promises, they are heartless, and have no mercy.
They know 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s justice requires that those who do these things deserve to die, yet they do them anyway. Worse yet, they encourage others to do them, too.
You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on someone else, for at whatever point you judge another, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
And we know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, in HIS justice, will punish anyone who does such things.
Since you judge others for doing these things, why do you think you can avoid 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s judgment when you do the same things?

Do you not see how wonderfully kind, and tolerant, and patient 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is with you? Does this mean nothing to you? Can you not see that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s kindness is intended to turn you from your sin?

But because you are stubborn and refuse to turn from your sin, you are storing up terrible punishment for yourself. For a day of anger is coming, when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s righteous judgment will be revealed.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will judge everyone according to what they have done.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will give eternal life to those who keep on doing good, seeking after the Kabad and honor and immortality that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH offers.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will pour out HIS anger and wrath on those who live for themselves, who refuse to obey the Truth and instead live lives of wickedness.
There will be trouble and calamity for everyone who keeps on doing what is evil, for the Yahudym first and also for the other nations.
But there will be Kabad and honor and Shalum from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH for all who do good, for the Yahudym first and also for the other nations.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH does not show favoritism.

When the other nations sin, they will be destroyed, even though they never had 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s written law. And the Yahudym, who do have 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Turah (law), will be judged by that law when they fail to obey it.
For merely listening to the law does not make us right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. It is obeying the Turah (law) that makes us right in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s sight.
for when the other nations, who do not have the Turah (law), by nature do the things in the Turah, these, although not having the Turah, are a Turah (law) to themselves,
They demonstrate that the law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is written in their hearts, for their own conscience and thoughts either accuse them or tell them they are doing right.
This is the message I proclaim, that the day is coming when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach, will judge everyone’s secret life.
You who call yourselves Yahudym are relying on 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Turah (law), and you boast about your special relationship with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
You know what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH wants; you know what is right because you have been taught 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s law.
You are convinced that you are a guide for the blind and a light for people who are lost in darkness.
You think you can instruct the ignorant and teach children the ways of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. For you are certain that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s law gives you complete knowledge and Truth.
Well then, if you teach others, why do you not teach yourself? You tell others not to steal, but do you steal?
You say it is wrong to commit adultery, but do you commit adultery? You condemn idolatry, but do you use items stolen from pagan temples?
You are so proud of knowing the law, but you dishonor 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by breaking it.
No wonder the Scriptures say, “The other nations blaspheme the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH because of you.”

The Yahudym ceremony of circumcision has value only if you obey the Turah (Law) of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. But if you do not obey Turah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, you are no better off than an uncircumcised man of the other nations.
Therefore, if an uncircumcised man keeps the righteous requirements of the law, will that not make an uncircumcised man be counted as circumcision?
The man who is uncircumcised physically but he keeps the Law will condemn you who break the Law, even though you have the written Law and you are circumcised.
For you are not a true Yahudym just because you were born of Yahudym parents or because you have gone through the ceremony of circumcision.

No, a true Yahudym is one whose heart is right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH. And true circumcision is not merely obeying the letter of the law; rather, it is a change of heart produced by the Ruach. And a person with a changed heart seeks praise from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, not from men.
Then what is the advantage of being a Yahudym? Is there any value in the ceremony of circumcision?
Yes, there are great benefits! First of all, the Yahudym were entrusted with the whole revelation of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
It is true that some of them were unfaithful; but just because they were unfaithful, does that mean 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will be unfaithful?
Certainly not! Indeed, let 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH be True and every man a liar. As it is written: “So that it can show that you are right in your words; and you will triumph when you are judged.

“But,” some might say, “our sinfulness serves a good purpose, for it helps people see how righteous 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is. Is it not unfair, then, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to punish us?” (This is merely a man's point of view.)
Of course not! If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH were not entirely fair, how would 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH be qualified to judge the world?
“But,” someone might still argue, “how can 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH condemn me as a sinner if my dishonesty highlights 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH‘s truthfulness and brings HIM more Kabad?”
And some people even slander us by claiming that we say, “The more we sin, the better it is!” Those who say such things deserve to be condemned.
Well then, should we conclude that we Yahudym are better than others? No, not at all, for we have already shown that all mankind, whether the Yahudym or the other nations, are under the power of sin.
As the Scriptures say, “No one is righteous, not even one.
No one is truly wise; no one is seeking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
All have turned away; all have become useless, no one does good, not a single one.”
“Their talk is foul, like the stench from an open grave. Their tongues are filled with lies. “Snake venom drips from their lips.”
“Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
“They rush to commit murder.
Destruction and misery always follow them.
They do not know where to find Shalum.”
“They have no fear of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH at all.”
Obviously, the law applies to those to whom it was given, for its purpose is to keep people from having excuses, and to show that the entire world is guilty before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
For no one can ever be made right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by doing what the law commands. The law simply shows us how sinful we are.
But now 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has shown us a way to be made right with HIM without keeping the requirements of the law, as was promised in the writings of Musha and the Nabyms long ago.
We are made right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH by placing our Amunah in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach. And this is true for everyone who believes, no matter who we are.
For everyone has sinned; we all fall short of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s righteous standard.
Yet 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH freely and mercifully declares that we are righteous. He did this through 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH freed us from the penalty for our sins.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH presented 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA as the sacrifice for sin. People are made right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH when they believe that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA sacrificed His life, shedding His blood. This sacrifice shows that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was being fair when He held back and did not punish those who sinned in times past,

for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH was looking ahead and including them in what he would do in this present time. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH did this to demonstrate His righteousness, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH HIMSELF is fair and just, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH declares sinners to be right in HIS sight when they believe in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA.
So do we have any reason to boast about ourselves? No reason at all. And why not? Because we are depending on the way of Amunah, not on what we have done in following the law.
I mean we are made right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH through Amunah, not through what we have done to follow the law. This is what we believe.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is not only the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of the Yahudym. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is also the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH of those who are not Yahudym.
There is only ONE 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will make the Yahudym right with HIM by their Amunah, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will also make the non-Yahudym right with HIM through their Amunah.
So do we destroy the law by following the way of Amunah? Not at all! In fact, Amunah causes us to be what the law actually wants.
Abraham was manly, the founder of our Yahudym nation. What did Abraham discover about being made right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH?
If Abraham's good deeds had made him acceptable to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, Abraham would have had something to boast about. But that was not 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s way.
For the Scriptures tell us, “Abraham believed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH counted Abraham as righteous because of his Amunah.”
When people work, their wages are not a gift, but something they have earned.
But people are counted as righteous, not because of their work, but because of their Amunah in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH who forgives sinners.
Daud also spoke of this when he described the happiness of those who are declared righteous without working for it:
“Oh, what joy for those whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sins are put out of sight.
Yes, what joy for those whose record 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH has cleared of sin.”

Now, is this Barakah only for the Yahudym, or is it also for the uncircumcised in the other nations? Well, we have been saying that Abraham was counted as righteous by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH because of his Amunah.
But how did this happen? Was he counted as righteous only after he was circumcised, or was it before he was circumcised Clearly, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH accepted Abraham before he was circumcised!

Circumcision was a sign that Abraham already had Amunah and that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had already accepted Abraham and declared him to be righteous, even before he was circumcised. So Abraham is the father of those who have Amunah but have not been circumcised. They are counted as righteous because of their Amunah.
And Abraham is also the father of those who have been circumcised, but only if they have the same kind of Amunah Abraham had before he was circumcised.

Clearly the promise of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH to give the whole Arath to Abraham and his descendants was based not on the obedience of Abraham to the Laws of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH, but on a right relationship with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH that comes by Amunah.
If the promise of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is only for those who obey the law, then Amunah is not necessary and the promise is pointless.
because the law brings about wrath; for where there is no law there is no transgression.

So the promise is received by Amunah. It is given as a free gift. And we are all certain to receive it, whether or not we live according to the law of Musha, if we have Amunah like Abraham. For Abraham is the father of all who believe.

That is what the Scriptures mean when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH told Abraham, “I have made you the father of many nations.” This happened because Abraham believed in the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who brings the dead back to life and who creates new things out of nothing.

Even when there was no reason for hope, Abraham kept hoping and believing that he would become the father of many nations. For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH had said to Abraham, “That Abraham will have many descendants!”
And Abraham’s Amunah did not weaken, even though, at about one hundred years of age, Abraham figured his body was as good as dead and so was Sarah’s womb.
But Abraham never wavered in believing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s promise. In fact Abraham's Amunah grew stronger, and in this Abraham brought Kabad to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Abraham was fully convinced that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH is able to do whatever he promises.
And because of Abraham’s Amunah, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH counted him as righteous.
And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH counted Abraham as righteous, it was not just for Abraham’s benefit alone. It was recorded him
And also for our benefit too, assuring us that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH will also count us as righteous if we believe in HIM, the 𐤀𐤋𐤅𐤄_ALUAH who raised 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA our Master from the dead.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was handed over to die because of our sins, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA was raised to life to make us right with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH.
Therefore, since we have been made right in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s sight by Amunah, we have Shalum with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH because of what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA Ha'Mashyach our Master has done for us.
Because of our Amunah, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA has brought us into this place of undeserved privilege where we now stand, and we confidently and joyfully look forward to sharing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH’s Kabad.
We can rejoice, too, when we run into problems and trials, for we know that they help us develop endurance.
And endurance develops strength of character, and character strengthens our confident hope of salvation.
And this hope will not lead to disappointment. For we know how dearly 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄_YAHUAH loves us, because HE has given us the RUACH Ha'Qadash to fill our hearts with His Ahaba (love).
When we were utterly helpless, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏_YAHUSHA came at just the right time and died for us sinners.
